#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>10.i/5_10.1.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
The terms &ldquo;program unit pragma&rdquo; and &ldquo;library unit pragma&rdquo; were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo; (specifically to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.15">J.15</a>) as all of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s that use these terms are now in that annex. <br />

<a id="Subclause_10.1.6"></a>

## 10.1.6  Environment-Level Visibility Rules

<MarginText>1_10.1.6</MarginText>
<p>[The normal visibility rules do not apply within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>, nor within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> that appears at the place of a compilation unit. The special visibility rules for those contexts are given here.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/2_10.1.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI95-00312-01"]} />
<p>Within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code> at the beginning of an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>, and within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0296">nonlimited_with_clause</a></code>, the only declarations that are visible are those that are explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s of the environment, and the only declarations that are directly visible are those that are explicit root <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s of the environment. Within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code>, the only declarations that are visible are those that are the implicit declaration of the limited view of a library package of the environment, and the only declarations that are directly visible are those that are the implicit declaration of the limited view of a root library package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a_10.1.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In &ldquo;<b>package</b> P.Q.R <b>is</b> ... <b>end</b> P.Q.R;&rdquo;, this rule requires P to be a root library unit, and Q to be a library unit (because those are the things that are directly visible and visible). Note that visibility does not apply between the &ldquo;<b>end</b>&rdquo; and the &ldquo;;&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>2.b_10.1.6</MarginText>
Physically nested declarations are not visible at these places.<br />

<MarginText>2.c_10.1.6</MarginText>
Although Standard is visible at these places, it is impossible to name it, since it is not directly visible, and it has no parent.<br />

<MarginText>2.c.1/2_10.1.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
Only compilation units defining limited views can be mentioned in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code>, while only compilation units defining full views (that is, the explicit declarations) can be mentioned in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0296">nonlimited_with_clause</a></code>. This resolves the conflict inherent in having two compilation units with the same defining name. <br />

<MarginText>2.d/2_10.1.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00312-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>3_10.1.6</MarginText>
<p>Within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> that is within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>, each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> mentioned in a previous <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code> is visible, and each root <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> so mentioned is directly visible. In addition, within such a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, if a given declaration is visible or directly visible, each declaration that occurs immediately within the given declaration's visible part is also visible. No other declarations are visible or directly visible. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a_10.1.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note the word &ldquo;same&rdquo;. For example, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> on a declaration mentions X, this does not make X visible in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s that are on the body. The reason for this rule is the one-pass <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>s Language Design Principle.<br />

<MarginText>3.b_10.1.6</MarginText>
Note that the second part of the rule does not mention <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>4_10.1.6</MarginText>
<p>Within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code> of a subunit, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s are visible as they are in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>; in addition, the declaration corresponding to each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0297">body_stub</a></code> in the environment is also visible. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a_10.1.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For a subprogram without a separate <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0297">body_stub</a></code> itself is the declaration. <br />

<MarginText>5_10.1.6</MarginText>
<p>Within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> that appears at the place of a compilation unit, the immediately preceding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> and each of its ancestors is visible. The ancestor root <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> is directly visible.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/2_10.1.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00312-01"]} />
<p>Notwithstanding the rules of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>, an expanded name in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> that appears at the place of a compilation unit may consist of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> that denotes a generic package and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> that denotes a child of that generic package. [(The child is necessarily a generic unit; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">10.1.1</a>.)] <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/2_10.1.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule allows <b>with</b> A.B; and <b>pragma</b> Elaborate(A.B); where A is a generic library package and B is one of its (generic) children. This is necessary because it is not normally legal to use an expanded name to reach inside a generic package. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>6.b_10.1.6</MarginText>
The special visibility rules that apply within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>, and within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> that appears at the place of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0286">compilation_unit</a></code> are clarified.<br />

<MarginText>6.c_10.1.6</MarginText>
Note that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code> is not part of any declarative region.<br />

<MarginText>6.d_10.1.6</MarginText>
We considered making the visibility rules within <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>s follow from the context of compilation. However, this attempt failed for various reasons. For example, it would require <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>s in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>s to be within the declarative region of Standard, which sounds suspiciously like a kludge. And we would still need a special rule to prevent seeing things (in our own <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>) that were with-ed by our parent, etc. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>6.e/2_10.1.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
Added separate visibility rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code>s; the existing rules apply only to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0296">nonlimited_with_clause</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>6.f/2_10.1.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00312-01"]} />
Clarified that the name of a generic child unit may appear in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>. <br />

# 10.2. Program Execution

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  87

# 10.2. Program Execution

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>An Ada <i>program</i> consists of a set of <i>partitions</i>[, which can execute in parallel with one another, possibly in a separate address space, and possibly on a separate computer.] <br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1", "AI12-0448-1"]} />
<p>A partition is a program or part of a program that can be invoked from outside the Ada implementation. [For example, on many systems, a partition can be an executable file generated by the system linker.] The user can <i>explicitly assign</i> library units to a partition. The assignment is done in an implementation-defined manner. The compilation units included in a partition are those of the explicitly assigned library units, as well as other compilation units <i>needed by</i> those library units. The compilation units needed by a given compilation unit (the <i>needed compilation units</i>) are determined as follows (unless specified otherwise via an implementation-defined <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>, or by some other implementation-defined means): <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>From a run-time point of view, an Ada 95 partition is identical to an Ada 83 program &mdash; implementations were always allowed to provide inter-program communication mechanisms. The additional semantics of partitions is that interfaces between them can be defined to obey normal language rules (as is done in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo;), whereas interfaces between separate programs had no particular semantics. <br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The manner of explicitly assigning library units to a partition.<br />

<MarginText>2.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The implementation-defined means, if any, of specifying which compilation units are needed by a given compilation unit.<br />

<MarginText>2.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There are no pragmas that &ldquo;specify otherwise&rdquo; defined by the core language. However, an implementation is allowed to provide such pragmas, and in fact <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo; defines some pragmas whose semantics includes reducing the set of compilation units described here. <br />

<MarginText>2.e/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>needed compilation unit</b> &mdash; compilation unit that is necessary to produce an executable partition, because some entity declared or defined within the unit is used elsewhere in the partition<br />

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0448-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A compilation unit is a needed compilation unit of itself;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0448-1"]} />
<li>If a compilation unit is among the needed compilation units, then so are any compilation units upon which it depends semantically;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0448-1"]} />
<li>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library_unit_declaration</a></code> is among the needed compilation units, then so is any corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0290">library_unit_body</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI12-0448-1"]} />
<li>If a compilation unit with stubs is among the needed compilation units, then so are any corresponding subunits;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that in the environment, the stubs are replaced with the corresponding <code>proper{"_"}bodies</code>. <br />

<MarginText>6.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI12-0448-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the (implicit) declaration of the limited view of a library package is among the needed compilation units, then so is the explicit declaration of the library package.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that a child unit is not included just because its parent is included &mdash; to include a child, mention it in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>6.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
A package is included in a partition even if the only reference to it is in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code>. While this isn't strictly necessary (no objects of types imported from such a unit can be created), it ensures that all incomplete types are eventually completed, and is the least surprising option. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The user can optionally designate (in an implementation-defined manner) one subprogram as the <i>main subprogram</i> for the partition. A main subprogram, if specified, shall be a subprogram. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This may seem superfluous, since it follows from the definition. But we would like to have every error message that might be generated (before run time) by an implementation correspond to some explicitly stated &ldquo;shall&rdquo; rule.<br />

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
Of course, this does not mean that the &ldquo;shall&rdquo; rules correspond one-to-one with an implementation's error messages. For example, the rule that says overload resolution &ldquo;shall&rdquo; succeed in producing a single interpretation would correspond to many error messages in a good implementation &mdash; the implementation would want to explain to the user exactly why overload resolution failed. This is especially true for the syntax rules &mdash; they are considered part of overload resolution, but in most cases, one would expect an error message based on the particular syntax rule that was violated. <br />

<MarginText>7.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The manner of designating the main subprogram of a partition.<br />

<MarginText>7.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>An implementation cannot require the user to specify, say, all of the library units to be included. It has to support, for example, perhaps the most typical case, where the user specifies just one library unit, the main program. The implementation has to do the work of tracking down all the other ones. <br />

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>Each partition has an anonymous <i>environment task</i>[, which is an implicit outermost task whose execution elaborates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s of the environment <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>, and then calls the main subprogram, if there is one. A partition's execution is that of its tasks.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>An environment task has no master; all nonenvironment tasks have masters.<br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
An implementation is allowed to support multiple concurrent executions of the same partition. <br />

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0448-1"]} />
<p>[The order of elaboration of library units is determined primarily by the <i>elaboration dependences</i>.] There is an elaboration dependence of a given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> upon another if the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> or any of its subunits depends semantically on the other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>. In addition, if a given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> or any of its subunits has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All that names another library unit, then there is an elaboration dependence of the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> upon the body of the other library unit, and, for Elaborate{"_"}All only, upon each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> that is a needed compilation unit of the declaration of the other library unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00180-01", "AI95-00256-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0107</i>{"}"} &ldquo;Mentions&rdquo; was used informally in the above rule; it was not intended to refer to the definition of <i>mentions</i> in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.2">10.1.2</a>. It was changed to &ldquo;names&rdquo; to make this clear.<br />

<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
See above for a definition of which <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s are &ldquo;needed by&rdquo; a given declaration.<br />

<MarginText>9.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
Note that elaboration dependences are among <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s, whereas the other two forms of dependence are among compilation units. Note that elaboration dependence includes semantic dependence. It's a little bit sad that the Elaborate{"_"}Body  aspect can't be folded into this mechanism. It follows from the definition that the elaboration dependence relationship is transitive. Note that the wording of the rule does not need to take into account a semantic dependence of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> or one of its subunits upon a subunit of a different library unit, because that can never happen. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>The environment task for a partition has the following structure: <br /></p>

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
task Environment{"_"}Task;{"\n"}
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
task body Environment{"_"}Task is{"\n"}    ... (1) -- The environment <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a>{"\n"}            -- (that is, the sequence of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a>s) goes here.{"\n"}begin{"\n"}    ... (2) -- Call the main subprogram, if there is one.{"\n"}end Environment{"_"}Task;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The name of the environment task is written in italics here to indicate that this task is anonymous. <br />

<MarginText>12.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The model is different for a &ldquo;passive partition&rdquo; (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.1">E.1</a>). Either there is no environment task, or its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> is an infinite loop rather than a call on a main subprogram. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>The environment <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> at (1) is a sequence of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>s consisting of copies of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s included in the partition[. The order of elaboration of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s is the order in which they appear in the environment <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>]: <br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The order of all included <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s is such that there are no forward elaboration dependences. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule is written so that if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> depends on itself, we don't require it to be elaborated before itself. See AI83-00113/12. This can happen only in pathological circumstances. For example, if a library <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> has no corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>, and one of the subunits of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> mentions the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> will depend on itself. For another example, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0290">library_unit_body</a></code> applies a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate{"_"}All to its own declaration, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0290">library_unit_body</a></code> will depend on itself. <br />

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Any included <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library_unit_declaration</a></code> for which aspect Elaborate{"_"}Body is True is immediately followed by its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0290">library_unit_body</a></code>, if included. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This implies that the body of such a library unit shall not &ldquo;with&rdquo; any of its own children, or anything else that depends semantically upon the declaration of the library unit. <br />

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>All <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s declared pure occur before any that are not declared pure.<br /></li>
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<li>All preelaborated <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s occur before any that are not preelaborated. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Normally, if two partitions contain the same compilation unit, they each contain a separate <i>copy</i> of that compilation unit. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo; for cases where two partitions share the same copy of something.<br />

<MarginText>17.b</MarginText>
There is no requirement that the main subprogram be elaborated last. In fact, it is possible to write a partition in which the main subprogram cannot be elaborated last. <br />

<MarginText>17.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> has the properties required of all environments (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.4">10.1.4</a>). However, the environment <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a partition will typically contain fewer compilation units than the environment <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> used at compile time &mdash; only the &ldquo;needed&rdquo; ones are included in the partition. <br />

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<p>There shall be a total order of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s that obeys the above rules. The order is otherwise implementation defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The only way to violate this rule is to have Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s or Elaborate{"_"}Body aspects that cause circular ordering requirements, thus preventing an order that has no forward elaboration dependences. <br />

<MarginText>18.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The order of elaboration of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>18.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>Notwithstanding what the RM says elsewhere, each rule that requires a declaration to have a corresponding completion is considered to be a Post-Compilation Rule when the declaration is that of a library unit. <br />

<MarginText>18.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Such rules may be checked at &ldquo;link time&rdquo;, for example. Rules requiring the completion to have certain properties, on the other hand, are checked at compile time of the completion. <br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<p>The full expanded names of the library units and subunits included in a given partition shall be distinct.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is a Post-Compilation Rule because making it a Legality Rule would violate the Language Design Principle labeled &ldquo;legality determinable via semantic dependences&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>20</MarginText>
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the environment task (see (2) above) consists of either: <br /></p>

<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A call to the main subprogram, if the partition has one. If the main subprogram has parameters, they are passed; where the actuals come from is implementation defined. What happens to the result of a main function is also implementation defined. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Parameter passing and function return for the main subprogram.<br />

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<p>or: <br /></p>

<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0170">null_statement</a></code>, if there is no main subprogram. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For a passive partition, either there is no environment task, or its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> is an infinite loop. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.1">E.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>24/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>The mechanisms for building and running partitions are implementation defined. [These can be combined into one operation, as, for example, in dynamic linking, or &ldquo;load-and-go&rdquo; systems.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The mechanisms for building and running partitions.<br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p>The execution of a program consists of the execution of a set of partitions. Further details are implementation defined. The execution of a partition starts with the execution of its environment task, ends when the environment task terminates, and includes the executions of all tasks of the partition. [The execution of the (implicit) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code> of the environment task acts as a master for all other tasks created as part of the execution of the partition. When the environment task completes (normally or abnormally), it waits for the termination of all such tasks, and then finalizes any remaining objects of the partition.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The &ldquo;further details&rdquo; mentioned above include, for example, program termination &mdash; it is implementation defined. There is no need to define it here; it's entirely up to the implementation whether it wants to consider the program as a whole to exist beyond the existence of individual partitions. <br />

<MarginText>25.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The details of program execution, including program termination.<br />

<MarginText>25.c</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The execution of the partition terminates (normally or abnormally) when the environment task terminates (normally or abnormally, respectively). <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>26</MarginText>
<p>Once the environment task has awaited the termination of all other tasks of the partition, any further attempt to create a task (during finalization) is a bounded error, and may result in the raising of Program{"_"}Error either upon creation or activation of the task. If such a task is activated, it is not specified whether the task is awaited prior to termination of the environment task. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>27</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall ensure that all compilation units included in a partition are consistent with one another, and are legal according to the rules of the language. <br /></p>

<MarginText>27.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The consistency requirement implies that a partition cannot contain two versions of the same compilation unit. That is, a partition cannot contain two different library units with the same full expanded name, nor two different bodies for the same program unit. For example, suppose we compile the following: <br />

<MarginText>27.b</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package A is -- Version 1.{"\n"}    ...{"\n"}end A;{"\n"}
<MarginText>27.c</MarginText>
with A;{"\n"}package B is{"\n"}end B;{"\n"}
<MarginText>27.d</MarginText>
package A is -- Version 2.{"\n"}    ...{"\n"}end A;{"\n"}
<MarginText>27.e</MarginText>
with A;{"\n"}package C is{"\n"}end C;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>27.f</MarginText>
It would be wrong for a partition containing B and C to contain both versions of A. Typically, the implementation would require the use of Version 2 of A, which might require the recompilation of B. Alternatively, the implementation might automatically recompile B when the partition is built. A third alternative would be an incremental compiler that, when Version 2 of A is compiled, automatically patches the object code for B to reflect the changes to A (if there are any relevant changes &mdash; there might not be any).<br />

<MarginText>27.g</MarginText>
An implementation that supported fancy version management might allow the use of Version 1 in some circumstances. In no case can the implementation allow the use of both versions in the same partition (unless, of course, it can prove that the two versions are semantically identical).<br />

<MarginText>27.h</MarginText>
The core language says nothing about inter-partition consistency; see also <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>28/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>The kind of partition described in this subclause is known as an <i>active</i> partition. An implementation is allowed to support other kinds of partitions, with implementation-defined semantics. <br /></p>

<MarginText>28.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The semantics of any nonactive partitions supported by the implementation.<br />

<MarginText>28.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b><a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo; defines the concept of passive partitions; they may be thought of as a partition without an environment task, or as one with a particularly simple form of environment task, having an infinite loop rather than a call on a main subprogram as its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>29</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may restrict the kinds of subprograms it supports as main subprograms. However, an implementation is required to support all main subprograms that are public parameterless library procedures. <br /></p>

<MarginText>29.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The implementation is required to support main subprograms that are procedures declared by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code>s, as well as those that are children of library units other than Standard. Generic units are, of course, not allowed to be main subprograms, since they are not subprograms.<br />

<MarginText>29.b</MarginText>
Note that renamings are irrelevant to this rule. This rules says which subprograms (not views) have to be supported. The implementation can choose any way it wants for the user to indicate which subprogram should be the main subprogram. An implementation might allow any name of any view, including those declared by renamings. Another implementation might require it to be the original name. Another implementation still might use the name of the source file or some such thing. <br />

<MarginText>30</MarginText>
<p>If the environment task completes abnormally, the implementation may abort any dependent tasks. <br /></p>

<MarginText>30.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>If the implementation does not take advantage of this permission, the normal action takes place &mdash; the environment task awaits those tasks.<br />

<MarginText>30.b</MarginText>
The possibility of aborting them is not shown in the <i>Environment{"_"}Task</i> code above, because there is nowhere to put an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> that can handle exceptions raised in both the environment <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> and the main subprogram, such that the dependent tasks can be aborted. If we put an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> in the body of the environment task, then it won't handle exceptions that occur during elaboration of the environment <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>. If we were to move those things into a nested <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code>, with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> outside that, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> would await the library tasks we are trying to abort.<br />

<MarginText>30.c</MarginText>
Furthermore, this is merely a permission, and is not fundamental to the model, so it is probably better to state it separately anyway.<br />

<MarginText>30.d</MarginText>
Note that implementations (and tools like debuggers) can have modes that provide other behaviors in addition. <br />

<MarginText>31/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 1   An implementation can provide inter-partition communication mechanism(s) via special packages and pragmas. Standard pragmas for distribution and methods for specifying inter-partition communication are defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo;. If no such mechanisms are provided, then each partition is isolated from all others, and behaves as a program in and of itself. <br />

<MarginText>31.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Not providing such mechanisms is equivalent to disallowing multi-partition programs.<br />

<MarginText>31.b</MarginText>
An implementation may provide mechanisms to facilitate checking the consistency of library units elaborated in different partitions; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo; does so. <br />

<MarginText>32/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 2   Partitions are not required to run in separate address spaces. For example, an implementation can support dynamic linking via the partition concept.<br />

<MarginText>33/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
NOTE 3   An order of elaboration of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s that is consistent with the partial ordering defined above does not always ensure that each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0290">library_unit_body</a></code> is elaborated before any other compilation unit whose elaboration necessitates that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0290">library_unit_body</a></code> be already elaborated. (In particular, there is no requirement that the body of a library unit be elaborated as soon as possible after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library_unit_declaration</a></code> is elaborated, unless the pragmas or aspects in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a> are used.)<br />

<MarginText>34/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 4   A partition (active or otherwise) does not necessarily have a main subprogram. In such a case, all the work done by the partition would be done by elaboration of various <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s, and by tasks created by that elaboration. Passive partitions, which cannot have main subprograms, are defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>34.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The environment task is the outermost semantic level defined by the language.<br />

<MarginText>34.b</MarginText>
Standard has no private part. This prevents strange implementation-dependences involving private children of Standard having visibility upon Standard's private part. It doesn't matter where the body of Standard appears in the environment, since it doesn't do anything. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Predefined Language Environment</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>34.c</MarginText>
Note that elaboration dependence is carefully defined in such a way that if (say) the body of something doesn't exist yet, then there is no elaboration dependence upon the nonexistent body. (This follows from the fact that &ldquo;needed by&rdquo; is defined that way, and the elaboration dependences caused by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All are defined in terms of &ldquo;needed by&rdquo;.) This property allows us to use the environment concept both at compile time and at partition-construction time/run time. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>34.d</MarginText>
The concept of partitions is new to Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>34.e</MarginText>
A main subprogram is now optional. The language-defined restrictions on main subprograms are relaxed. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>34.f</MarginText>
Ada 95 uses the term &ldquo;main subprogram&rdquo; instead of Ada 83's &ldquo;main program&rdquo; (which was inherited from Pascal). This is done to avoid confusion &mdash; a main subprogram is a subprogram, not a program. The program as a whole is an entirely different thing. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>34.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01"]} />
The mistaken use of &ldquo;mentions&rdquo; in the elaboration dependence rule was fixed.<br />

<MarginText>34.h/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI12-0448-1"]} />
The <i>needed</i> relationship was extended to include limited views. <br />

<a id="Subclause_10.2.1"></a>

## 10.2.1  Elaboration Control

<MarginText>1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>[ This subclause defines aspects and pragmas that help control the elaboration order of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
The rules governing preelaboration are designed to allow it to be done largely by bulk initialization of statically allocated storage from information in a &ldquo;load module&rdquo; created by a linker. Some implementations may require run-time code to be executed in some cases, but we consider these cases rare enough that we need not further complicate the rules.<br />

<MarginText>1.b_10.2.1</MarginText>
It is important that programs be able to declare data structures that are link-time initialized with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>s, and concatenations thereof. It is important to be able to write link-time evaluated expressions involving the First, Last, and Length attributes of such data structures (including variables), because they might be initialized with positional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>s, and we don't want the user to have to count the elements. There is no corresponding need for accessing discriminants, since they can be initialized with a static constant, and then the constant can be referred to elsewhere. It is important to allow link-time initialized data structures involving discriminant-dependent components. It is important to be able to write link-time evaluated expressions involving pointers (both access values and addresses) to the above-mentioned data structures.<br />

<MarginText>1.c_10.2.1</MarginText>
The rules also ensure that no Elaboration{"_"}Check need be performed for calls on library-level subprograms declared within a preelaborated package. This is true also of the Elaboration{"_"}Check on task activation for library level task types declared in a preelaborated package. However, it is not true of the Elaboration{"_"}Check on instantiations.<br />

<MarginText>1.d_10.2.1</MarginText>
A static expression should never prevent a library unit from being preelaborable.<br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 2 through 4 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<p>An elaborable construct is preelaborable unless its elaboration performs any of the following actions: <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A <i>preelaborable</i> construct can be elaborated without using any information that is available only at run time. Note that we don't try to prevent exceptions in preelaborable constructs; if the implementation wishes to generate code to raise an exception, that's OK.<br />

<MarginText>5.b_10.2.1</MarginText>
Because there is no flow of control and there are no calls (other than to predefined subprograms), these run-time properties can actually be detected at compile time. This is necessary in order to require compile-time enforcement of the rules. <br />

<MarginText>6_10.2.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> other than a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0170">null_statement</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A preelaborable construct can contain <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0171">label</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0170">null_statement</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>7/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0175-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A call to a subprogram other than: <br /></li>
<MarginText>7.1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<li>a static function;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.2/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<li>an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Conversion (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9">13.9</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.3/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<li>a function declared in System.Storage{"_"}Elements (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.7#Subclause_13.7.1">13.7.1</a>); or<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.4/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<li>the functions To{"_"}Pointer and To{"_"}Address declared in an instance of System.Address{"_"}to{"_"}Access{"_"}Conversions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.7#Subclause_13.7.2">13.7.2</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0175-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The parameters of any such function have to pass the preelaborability rules, so they typically have to be static expressions. The extra allowed functions are all forms of conversion that the compiler understands, so there should be little implementation burden. Note that such a call might raise an exception; preelaborable is not the same as elaborable with no code. <br />

<MarginText>8_10.2.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of an object, unless the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is a static expression, or statically denotes a discriminant of an enclosing type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>One can evaluate such a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, but not as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code>. For example, one can evaluate an attribute of the object. One can evaluate an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>, so long as it does not denote an object, and its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> does not disobey any of these rules. For example, Obj'Access, Obj'Unchecked{"_"}Access, and Obj'Address are generally legal in preelaborated library units. <br />

<MarginText>9/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01", "AI05-0028-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The creation of an object [(including a component)] that is initialized by default, if its type does not have preelaborable initialization. Similarly, the evaluation of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension{"_"}aggregate</a></code> with an ancestor <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype{"_"}mark</a></code> denoting a subtype of such a type.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>One can declare these kinds of types, but one cannot create objects of those types.<br />

<MarginText>9.b_10.2.1</MarginText>
It is also nonpreelaborable to create an object if that will cause the evaluation of a default expression that will call a user-defined function. This follows from the rule above forbidding nonnull statements. <br />

<MarginText>9.c/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>9.1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The elaboration of any elaborable construct that is not preelaborable. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.2/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1"]} />
<p>A generic declaration is preelaborable unless every instance would perform one of the above actions.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.d/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A generic declaration is preelaborable unless there is no instance that could be declared preelaborated. For instance, a generic package declaration that directly contains a variable initialized by a non-static function that is not a formal function is not preelaborable (and thus would be illegal if the Preelaborate aspect were applied to it). <br />

<MarginText>10/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00403-01"]} />
<p>A generic body is preelaborable only if elaboration of a corresponding instance body would not perform any such actions, presuming that: <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00403-01", "AI05-0028-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the actual for each discriminated formal derived type, formal private type, or formal private extension declared within the formal part of the generic unit is a type that does not have preelaborable initialization, unless the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect was specified for the formal type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.2/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00403-01"]} />
<li>the actual for each formal type is nonstatic;<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.3/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00403-01"]} />
<li>the actual for each formal object is nonstatic; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.4/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00403-01"]} />
<li>the actual for each formal subprogram is a user-defined subprogram. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a.1/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00403-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This is an &ldquo;assume-the-worst&rdquo; rule. The elaboration of a generic unit doesn't perform any of the actions listed above, because its sole effect is to establish that the generic can from now on be instantiated. So the elaboration of the generic itself is not the interesting part when it comes to preelaboration rules. The interesting part is what happens when you elaborate &ldquo;any instantiation&rdquo; of the generic. For instance, declaring an object of a limited formal private type might well start tasks, call functions, and do all sorts of nonpreelaborable things. We prevent these situations by assuming that the actual parameters are as badly behaved as possible. <br />

<MarginText>10.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Without this rule about generics, we would have to forbid instantiations in preelaborated library units, which would significantly reduce their usefulness. <br />

<MarginText>11/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00002-01", "AI05-0034-1", "AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0035</i>{"}"} When the library unit aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>) Preelaborate of a program unit is True, the unit is said to be <i>preelaborated</i>. When the Preelaborate aspect is specified True for a library unit, all compilation units of the library unit are preelaborated. The declaration and body of a preelaborated library unit, and all subunits that are elaborated as part of elaborating the library unit, shall be preelaborable. All compilation units of a preelaborated library unit shall depend semantically only on declared pure or preelaborated <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. [ If a library unit is preelaborated, then its declaration, if any, and body, if any, are elaborated prior to all nonpreelaborated <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s of the partition.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In a generic body, we assume the worst about formal private types and extensions.<br />

<MarginText>11.a.1/1_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00002-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0035</i>{"}"} Subunits of a preelaborated subprogram unit do not need to be preelaborable. This is needed in order to be consistent with units nested in a subprogram body, which do not need to be preelaborable even if the subprogram is preelaborated. However, such subunits cannot depend semantically on nonpreelaborated units, which is also consistent with nested units.<br />

<MarginText>11.a.2/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
If a unit is not preelaborated, the value of the Preelaborate aspect for that unit is False. <br />

<MarginText>11.b/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Preelaborate: </b>Code execution during elaboration is avoided for a given package.<br />

<MarginText>11.c/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Rules for specifying a library unit aspect (like Preelaborate) are found in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>11.1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01", "AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>The following rules specify which entities have <i>preelaborable initialization</i>, namely that the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect of the entity is True:<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.2/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0028-1", "AI12-0409-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The partial view of a private type or private extension, a protected type without <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>s, a generic formal private type, or a generic formal derived type, has preelaborable initialization if and only if the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect has been specified True for them. [A protected type with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>s or a task type never has preelaborable initialization.] The Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect of a partial view of a type may be specified as False, even if the full view of the type has preelaborable initialization. Similarly, a generic formal type may be specified with Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization False, even if the actual type in an instance has preelaborable initialization.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.3/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<li>A component (including a discriminant) of a record or protected type has preelaborable initialization if its declaration includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> whose execution does not perform any actions prohibited in preelaborable constructs as described above, or if its declaration does not include a default expression and its type has preelaborable initialization.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.4/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0028-1", "AI05-0221-1"]} />
<li>A derived type has preelaborable initialization if its parent type has preelaborable initialization and if the noninherited components all have preelaborable initialization. However, a controlled type with an Initialize procedure that is not a null procedure does not have preelaborable initialization.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.5/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01", "AI95-00345-01"]} />
<li>A view of a type has preelaborable initialization if it is an elementary type, an array type whose component type has preelaborable initialization, a record type whose components all have preelaborable initialization, or an interface type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.6/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01", "AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>The following attribute is defined for a nonformal composite subtype S declared within the visible part of a package or a generic package, or a generic formal private subtype or formal derived subtype:<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.7/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>This attribute is of Boolean type, and its value reflects whether the type of S has preelaborable initialization. The value of this attribute, the type-related Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect, may be specified for any type for which the attribute is defined. The value shall be specified by a static expression, unless the type is not a formal type but is nevertheless declared within a generic package. In this latter case, the value may also be specified by references to the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization attribute of one or more formal types visible at the point of the declaration of the composite type, conjoined with <b>and</b>.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>11.d/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>&ldquo;Formal types visible at the point of the declaration&rdquo; includes all visible formal types, including those that might have been declared in formal packages or in child packages. <br />

<MarginText>11.e/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization: </b>Declares that a type has preelaborable initialization.<br />

<MarginText>11.8/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01", "AI95-00345-01", "AI05-0028-1", "AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>If the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect is specified True for a private type or a private extension, the full view of the type shall have preelaborable initialization. If the aspect is specified True for a protected type, the protected type shall not have entries, and each component of the protected type shall have preelaborable initialization. If the aspect is specified True for a generic formal type, then in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code> the corresponding actual type shall have preelaborable initialization. If the aspect definition includes one or more Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>s, then the full view of the type shall have preelaborable initialization presuming the types mentioned in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>s all have preelaborable initialization. For any other composite type, the aspect shall be specified statically True or False only if it is confirming. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules apply also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.f/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0028-1", "AI12-0409-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The reason why we need to be allowed to specify the aspect for private types, private extensions, and protected types is fairly clear: the properties of the full view determine whether the type has preelaborable initialization or not; in order to preserve privacy we need a way to express on the partial view that the full view is well-behaved. The reason why we need to be allowed to specify the aspect for other composite types is more subtle: a nonnull override for Initialize might occur in the private part, even for a nonprivate type; in order to preserve privacy, we need a way to express on a type declared in a visible part that the private part does not contain any nasty override of Initialize. <br />

<MarginText>11.g/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Not only do protected types with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>s and task types not have preelaborable initialization, but they cannot have Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect specified True for them. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>12_10.2.1</MarginText>
<p>In an implementation, a type declared in a preelaborated package should have the same representation in every elaboration of a given version of the package, whether the elaborations occur in distinct executions of the same program, or in executions of distinct programs or partitions that include the given version. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>A type declared in a preelaborated package should have the same representation in every elaboration of a given version of the package.<br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 13 through 15 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>15.1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01", "AI05-0035-1", "AI12-0232-1"]} />
<p>A <i>pure</i> program unit is a preelaborable program unit whose elaboration does not perform any of the following actions:<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.2/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the elaboration of a variable declaration;<br /></li>
<MarginText>15.3/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<li>the evaluation of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of an access-to-variable type; for the purposes of this rule, the partial view of a type is presumed to have nonvisible components whose default initialization evaluates such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.a.1/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0004-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> would provide a backdoor way to get a global variable into a pure unit, so it is prohibited. Most such <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s are illegal anyway, as their type is required to have Storage{"_"}Size = 0 (see the next two rules). But access parameters and access discriminants don't necessarily disallow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s. However, a call is also illegal here (by the preelaboration rules), so access parameters cannot cause trouble. So this rule is really about prohibiting allocators in discriminant constraints:<br />

<MarginText>15.a.2/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Rec (Acc : access Integer) is record{"\n"}    C : Character;{"\n"}end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15.a.3/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
Not{"_"}Const : constant Rec (Acc ={">"} new Integer'(2)); -- Illegal in a pure unit.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>15.a/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0004-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
The second half of the rule is needed because aggregates can specify the default initialization of a private type or extension using {"<"}{">"} or the ancestor subtype of an extension aggregate. The subtype of a component could use an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> to initialize an access discriminant; the type still could have the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect specified. Ada 95 did not allow such private types to have preelaborable initialization, so such a default initialization could not have occurred. Thus this rule is not incompatible with Ada 95. <br />

<MarginText>15.4/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0035-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the elaboration of the declaration of a nonderived named access-to-variable type unless the Storage{"_"}Size of the type has been specified by a static expression with value zero or is defined by the language to be zero;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.b/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A remote access-to-class-wide type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2#Subclause_E.2.2">E.2.2</a>) has its Storage{"_"}Size defined to be zero. <br />

<MarginText>15.c/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We disallow most named access-to-object types because an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> has a side effect; the pool constitutes variable data. We allow access-to-subprogram types because they don't have <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s. We even allow named access-to-object types if they have an empty predefined pool (they can't have a user-defined pool as System.Storage{"_"}Pools is not pure). In this case, most attempts to use an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> are illegal, and any others (in a generic body) will raise Storage{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>15.5/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0035-1", "AI12-0232-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the elaboration of the declaration of a nonderived named access-to-constant type for which the Storage{"_"}Size has been specified by an expression other than a static expression with value zero;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.d/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We allow access-to-constant types so long as there is no user-specified nonzero Storage{"_"}Size; if there were a user-specified nonzero Storage{"_"}Size restricting the size of the storage pool, allocators would be problematic since the package is supposedly &lsquo;stateless&rsquo;, and the allocated size count for the storage pool would represent state. <br />

<MarginText>15.6/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the elaboration of any program unit that is not pure.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.7/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1"]} />
<p>A generic declaration is pure unless every instance would perform one of the above actions.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.d.1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A generic declaration is pure unless there is no instance that could be declared pure. For instance, a generic package declaration that directly contains a variable declaration is not pure (and thus would be illegal if aspect Pure is specified for it). <br />

<MarginText>15.8/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0035-1", "AI12-0232-1"]} />
<p>A generic body is pure only if elaboration of a corresponding instance body would not perform any such actions presuming any composite formal types have nonvisible components whose default initialization evaluates an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of an access-to-variable type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.9/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01", "AI12-0232-1"]} />
<p>The Storage{"_"}Size for an anonymous access-to-variable type declared at library level in a library unit that is declared pure is defined to be zero.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.e/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This makes <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s illegal for such types (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>), making a storage pool unnecessary for these types. A storage pool would represent state.<br />

<MarginText>15.f/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
Note that access discriminants and access parameters are never library-level, even when they are declared in a type or subprogram declared at library-level. That's because they have their own special accessibility rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>). <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>16/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>17/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01", "AI05-0034-1", "AI05-0035-1", "AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>When the library unit aspect Pure of a program unit is True, the unit is said to be <i>declared pure</i>. When the Pure aspect is specified True for a library unit, all compilation units of the library unit are declared pure. In addition, the limited view of any library package is declared pure. The declaration and body of a declared pure library unit, and all subunits that are elaborated as part of elaborating the library unit, shall be pure. All compilation units of a declared pure library unit shall depend semantically only on declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. Furthermore, the full view of any partial view declared in the visible part of a declared pure library unit that has any available stream attributes shall support external streaming (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>17.b_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A declared-pure package is useful for defining types to be shared between partitions with no common address space. <br />

<MarginText>17.c_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Note that generic packages are not mentioned in the list of things that can contain variable declarations. Note that the Ada 95 rules for deferred constants make them allowable in library units that are declared pure; that isn't true of Ada 83's deferred constants. <br />

<MarginText>17.d/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Anonymous access types are allowed.<br />

<MarginText>17.d.1/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1"]} />
A limited view is not a library unit, so any rule that starts &ldquo;declared pure library unit&rdquo; does not apply to a limited view. In particular, the 3rd and last sentences never apply to limited views. However, a limited view is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>, so rules that discuss &ldquo;declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s&rdquo; do include limited views.<br />

<MarginText>17.d.2/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
If a unit is not declared pure, the value of the Pure aspect for that unit is False. <br />

<MarginText>17.e/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Ada 95 didn't allow any access types as these (including access-to-subprogram types) cause trouble for <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Annex E</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/">Distributed Systems</a>&rdquo;, because such types  allow access values in a shared passive partition to designate objects in an active partition, thus allowing inter-address space references. We decided to disallow such uses in the relatively rare cases where they cause problems, rather than making life harder for the majority of users. Types declared in a pure package can be used in remote operations only if they are externally streamable. That simply means that there is a means to transport values of the type; that's automatically true for nonlimited types that don't have an access part. The only tricky part about this is to avoid privacy leakage; that was handled by ensuring that any private types (and private extensions) declared in a pure package that have available stream attributes (which include all nonlimited types by definition) have to be externally streamable. <br />

<MarginText>17.f/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Pure: </b>Side effects are avoided in the subprograms of a given package.<br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>17.1/4_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0076-1"]} />
<p>Execution is erroneous if some operation (other than the initialization or finalization of the object) modifies the value of a constant object declared at library-level in a pure package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17.g/4_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This could be accomplished via a self-referencing pointer or via squirrelling a writable pointer to a controlled object. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>18/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01", "AI05-0219-1"]} />
<p>If a library unit is declared pure, then the implementation is permitted to omit a call on a library-level subprogram of the library unit if the results are not needed after the call. In addition, the implementation may omit a call on such a subprogram and simply reuse the results produced by an earlier call on the same subprogram, provided that none of the parameters nor any object accessible via access values from the parameters have any part that is of a type whose full type is an immutably limited type, and the addresses and values of all by-reference actual parameters, the values of all by-copy-in actual parameters, and the values of all objects accessible via access values from the parameters, are the same as they were at the earlier call. [This permission applies even if the subprogram produces other side effects when called.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01", "AI05-0005-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A declared-pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> has no variable state. Hence, a call on one of its (nonnested) subprograms cannot normally have side effects. Side effects are still possible via dispatching calls and via indirect calls through access-to-subprogram values. Other mechanisms that might be used to modify variable state include machine code insertions, imported subprograms,  and unchecked conversion to an access type declared within the subprogram; this list is not exhaustive. Thus, the permissions described in this subclause may apply to a subprogram whose execution has side effects. The compiler may omit a call to such a subprogram even if  side effects exist, so the writer of such a subprogram has to keep this in mind. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>19/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The following <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s are defined with the given forms: <br /></p>

<MarginText>20_10.2.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Elaborate(<i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"{"}, <i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"}"});<br /></p>

<MarginText>21_10.2.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Elaborate{"_"}All(<i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"{"}, <i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"}"});<br /></p>

<MarginText>22/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2"><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>23_10.2.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All is only allowed within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>23.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>&ldquo;Within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>&rdquo; allows it to be the last item in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>. It can't be first, because the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> has to denote something mentioned earlier. <br />

<MarginText>24/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2"><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Hence, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All is not elaborated, not that it makes any practical difference.<br />

<MarginText>24.b_10.2.1</MarginText>
Note that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All is neither a program unit pragma, nor a library unit pragma.<br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>25/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>If the aspect Elaborate{"_"}Body is True for a declaration, then the declaration requires a completion [(a body)].<br /></p>

<MarginText>25.1/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
<p>The <i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All shall denote a nonlimited view of a library unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.b/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>These <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s are intended to prevent elaboration check failures. But a limited view does not make anything visible that has an elaboration check, so the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s cannot do anything useful. Moreover, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s would probably reintroduce the circularity that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code> was intended to break. So we make such uses illegal. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>26/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate specifies that the body of the named library unit is elaborated before the current <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate{"_"}All specifies that each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> that is needed by the named library unit declaration is elaborated before the current <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The official statement of the semantics of these <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s is given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>. <br />
