<MarginText>26.1/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>[If the Elaborate{"_"}Body aspect of a library unit is True, the body of the library unit is elaborated immediately after its declaration.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a.1/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The official statement of the semantics of this aspect is given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>. <br />

<MarginText>26.b/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The specification of the Elaborate{"_"}Body aspect simplifies the removal of unnecessary Elaboration{"_"}Checks. For a subprogram declared immediately within a library unit for which the Elaborate{"_"}Body  aspect is specified as True, the only calls that can fail the Elaboration{"_"}Check are those that occur in the library unit itself, between the declaration and body of the called subprogram; if there are no such calls (which can easily be detected at compile time if there are no <code>stub</code>s), then no Elaboration{"_"}Checks are needed for that subprogram. The same is true for Elaboration{"_"}Checks on task activations and instantiations, and for library subprograms and generic units. <br />

<MarginText>26.c_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The fact that the unit of elaboration is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> means that if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is not a completion, it is impossible for any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> to be elaborated between the declaration and the body of such a subprogram. Therefore, it is impossible for a call to such a subprogram to fail its Elaboration{"_"}Check. <br />

<MarginText>26.d_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The visibility rules imply that each <i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate or Elaborate{"_"}All has to denote a library unit mentioned by a previous <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>26.e/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Elaborate{"_"}Body: </b>A given package will have a body, and that body is elaborated immediately after the declaration.<br />

<MarginText>27/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0447-1"]} />
NOTE 1   A preelaborated library unit can have nonpreelaborable children. <br />

<MarginText>27.a/1_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00002-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0035</i>{"}"} But generally not nonpreelaborated subunits. (Nonpreelaborated subunits of subprograms are allowed as discussed above.) <br />

<MarginText>28/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0447-1"]} />
NOTE 2   A library unit that is declared pure can have impure children. <br />

<MarginText>28.a/1_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00002-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0035</i>{"}"} But generally not impure subunits. (Impure subunits of subprograms are allowed as discussed above.) <br />

<MarginText>28.b_10.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Pragma Elaborate is mainly for closely related library units, such as when two package bodies 'with' each other's declarations. In such cases, Elaborate{"_"}All sometimes won't work. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>28.c_10.2.1</MarginText>
The concepts of preelaborability and purity are new to Ada 95. The Elaborate{"_"}All, Elaborate{"_"}Body, Preelaborate, and Pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s are new to Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>28.d_10.2.1</MarginText>
Pragmas Elaborate are allowed to be mixed in with the other things in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code> &mdash; in Ada 83, they were required to appear last. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>28.e/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
The requirement that a partial view with available stream attributes be externally streamable can cause an incompatibility in rare cases. If there is a limited tagged type declared in a pure package with available attributes, and that type is used to declare a private extension in another pure package, and the full type for the private extension has a component of an explicitly limited record type, a protected type, or a type with access discriminants, then the stream attributes will have to be user-specified in the visible part of the package. That is not a requirement for Ada 95, but this combination seems very unlikely in pure packages. Note that this cannot be an incompatibility for a nonlimited type, as all of the types that are allowed in Ada 95 that would require explicitly defined stream attributes are limited (and thus cannot be used as components in a nonlimited type).<br />

<MarginText>28.f/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00403-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> Added wording to cover missing cases for preelaborated generic units. This is incompatible as a preelaborated unit could have used a formal object to initialize a library-level object; that isn't allowed in Ada 2005. But such a unit wouldn't really be preelaborable, and Ada 95 compilers can reject such units (as this is a Binding Interpretation), so such units should be very rare. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>28.g/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> The concept of preelaborable initialization and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization are new. These allow more types of objects to be created in preelaborable units, and fix holes in the old rules.<br />

<MarginText>28.h/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
Access-to-subprogram types and access-to-object types with a Storage{"_"}Size of 0 are allowed in pure units. The permission to omit calls was adjusted accordingly (which also fixes a hole in Ada 95, as access parameters are allowed, and changes in the values accessed by them must be taken into account). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>28.i/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00002-01"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> The wording was changed so that subunits of a preelaborated subprogram are also preelaborated.<br />

<MarginText>28.j/2_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
Disallowed pragma Elaborate and Elaborate{"_"}All for packages that are mentioned in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code>. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.k/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0028-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected a serious unintended incompatibility with Ada 95 in the new preelaboration wording &mdash; explicit initialization of objects of types that don't have preelaborable initialization was not allowed. Ada 2012 switches back to the Ada 95 rule in these cases. This is unlikely to occur in practice, as it is unlikely that a compiler would have implemented the more restrictive rule (it would fail many ACATS tests if it did).<br />

<MarginText>28.l/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0035-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added an assume-the-worst rule for generic bodies (else they would never be checked for purity) and added the boilerplate so that the entire generic specification is rechecked. Also fixed wording to have consistent handling for subunits for Pure and Preelaborate. An Ada 95 program could have depended on marking a generic pure that was not really pure, although this would defeat the purpose of the categorization and likely cause problems with distributed programs. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.m/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0035-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Adjusted wording so that a subunit can be pure (it is not a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>, but it is a compilation unit).<br />

<MarginText>28.n/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0035-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Adjusted wording so that the rules for access types only apply to nonderived types (derived types share their storage pool with their parent, so if the parent access type is legal, so is any derived type.)<br />

<MarginText>28.o/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
Elaborate{"_"}Body is now an aspect, so it can be specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code><br />

<MarginText>28.p/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
Pure and Preelaborate are now aspects, so they can be specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.q/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0034-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording so that a limited view is always treated as pure, no matter what categorization is used for the originating unit. This was undefined in Ada 2005.<br />

<MarginText>28.r/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0028-1", "AI05-0221-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Fixed minor issues with preelaborable initialization (PI): null Initialize procedures do not make a type non-PI; formal types with pragma PI can be assumed to have PI; formal extensions are assumed to not have PI; all composite types can have pragma PI (so that the possibility of hidden Initialize routines can be handled); added discriminants of a derived type are not considered in calculating PI.<br />

<MarginText>28.s/3_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0219-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified that the implementation permission to omit pure subprogram calls does not apply if any part of the parameters or any designated object has a part that is immutably limited. The old wording just said "limited type", which can change via visibility and thus isn't appropriate for dynamic semantics permissions. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.t/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a rule that a generic declaration is not pure if no instance could be pure (for instance, because the generic declaration would elaborates a variable.) This was legal in Ada 2012, but of course no instance could have been declared pure. A similar rule (with a similar effect) was added for preelaborable generic declarations. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.u/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0175-1"]} />
Added some intrinsic conversion functions to those allowed to be called during the elaboration of a preelaborated unit. This is necessary to allow a portable Address aspect in a preelaborated unit, important on small embedded systems.<br />

<MarginText>28.v/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
Aspect Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization is new; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization is now obsolescent. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.w/4_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0076-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Explicitly stated that modifying a library-level constant in a pure package is erroneous. We don't document this as inconsistent as implementations certainly can still do whatever they were previously doing (no change is required); moreover, this case (and many more) were erroneous in Ada 2005 and before, so we're just restoring the previous semantics.<br />

<MarginText>28.x/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0232-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Explicitly stated that the pure and preelaborate rules are recursive; that is, they apply to the contents of nested packages and generic packages.<br />

<MarginText>28.y/5_10.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
The pragmas that set aspects (Pure, Preelaborate, Elaborate{"_"}Body) are now obsolescent. <br />

# 10. Program Structure and Compilation Issues

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.mdx

sidebar_position:  85

# 10. Program Structure and Compilation Issues

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[The overall structure of programs and the facilities for separate compilation are described in this clause. A <i>program</i> is a set of <i>partitions</i>, each of which may execute in a separate address space, possibly on a separate computer. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>program</b> &mdash; set of partitions, each of which can execute in a separate address space, possibly on a separate computer<br />

<MarginText>1.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>partition</b> &mdash; part of a program, which consists of a set of interdependent library units<br />Note: Each partition can run in a separate address space, possibly on a separate computer. A program can contain just one partition, or it can be distributed across multiple partitions, which can execute concurrently.<br />

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>As explained below, a partition is constructed from <i>library units</i>. Syntactically, the declaration of a library unit is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>, as is the body of a library unit. An implementation may support a concept of a <i>program library</i> (or simply, a &ldquo;library&rdquo;), which contains <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s and their subunits. Library units may be organized into a hierarchy of children, grandchildren, and so on.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>This clause has two subclauses: <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1">10.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1">Separate Compilation</a>&rdquo; discusses compile-time issues related to separate compilation. <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">Program Execution</a>&rdquo; discusses issues related to what is traditionally known as &ldquo;link time&rdquo; and &ldquo;run time&rdquo; &mdash; building and executing partitions.<br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
We should avoid specifying details that are outside the domain of the language itself. The standard is intended (at least in part) to promote portability of Ada programs at the source level. It is not intended to standardize extra-language issues such as how one invokes the compiler (or other tools), how one's source is represented and organized, version management, the format of error messages, etc.<br />

<MarginText>3.b</MarginText>
The rules of the language should be enforced even in the presence of separate compilation. Using separate compilation should not make a program less safe.<br />

<MarginText>3.c</MarginText>
It should be possible to determine the legality of a compilation unit by looking only at the compilation unit itself and the compilation units upon which it depends semantically. As an example, it should be possible to analyze the legality of two compilation units in parallel if they do not depend semantically upon each other.<br />

<MarginText>3.d</MarginText>
On the other hand, it may be necessary to look outside that set in order to generate code &mdash; this is generally true for generic instantiation and inlining, for example. Also on the other hand, it is generally necessary to look outside that set in order to check Post-Compilation Rules.<br />

<MarginText>3.e</MarginText>
See also the &ldquo;generic contract model&rdquo; Language Design Principle of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">Generic Instantiation</a>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>3.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
The clause organization mentioned above is different from that of RM83. <br />

# 11.1. Exception Declarations

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  89

# 11.1. Exception Declarations

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code> declares a name for an exception. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>exception{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0303"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : <b>exception</b><br />   [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>Each single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code> declares a name for a different exception. If a generic unit includes an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code>s implicitly generated by different instantiations of the generic unit refer to distinct exceptions (but all have the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>). The particular exception denoted by an exception name is determined at compilation time and is the same regardless of how many times the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code> is elaborated. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We considered removing this requirement inside generic bodies, because it is an implementation burden for implementations that wish to share code among several instances. In the end, it was decided that it would introduce too much implementation dependence. <br />

<MarginText>3.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Hence, if an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code> occurs in a recursive subprogram, the exception name denotes the same exception for all invocations of the recursive subprogram. The reason for this rule is that we allow an exception occurrence to propagate out of its declaration's innermost containing master; if exceptions were created by their declarations like other entities, they would presumably be destroyed upon leaving the master; we would have to do something special to prevent them from propagating to places where they no longer exist. <br />

<MarginText>3.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Exception identities are unique across all partitions of a program. <br />

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>The <i>predefined</i> exceptions are the ones declared in the declaration of package Standard: Constraint{"_"}Error, Program{"_"}Error, Storage{"_"}Error, and Tasking{"_"}Error[; one of them is raised when a language-defined check fails.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The exceptions declared in the language-defined package IO{"_"}Exceptions, for example, are not predefined. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code> has no effect.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>The execution of any construct raises Storage{"_"}Error if there is insufficient storage for that execution. The amount of storage necessary for the execution of constructs is unspecified. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that any execution whatsoever can raise Storage{"_"}Error. This allows much implementation freedom in storage management. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of user-defined exception declarations:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Singular : exception;{"\n"}Error    : exception;{"\n"}Overflow, Underflow : exception;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 83

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
The exception Numeric{"_"}Error is now defined in the Obsolescent features Annex, as a rename of Constraint{"_"}Error. All checks that raise Numeric{"_"}Error in Ada 83 instead raise Constraint{"_"}Error in Ada 95. To increase upward compatibility, we also changed the rules to allow the same exception to be named more than once by a given handler. Thus, &ldquo;<b>when</b> Constraint{"_"}Error | Numeric{"_"}Error ={">"}&rdquo; will remain legal in Ada 95, even though Constraint{"_"}Error and Numeric{"_"}Error now denote the same exception. However, it will not be legal to have separate handlers for Constraint{"_"}Error and Numeric{"_"}Error. This change is inconsistent in the rare case that an existing program explicitly raises Numeric{"_"}Error at a point where there is a handler for Constraint{"_"}Error; the exception will now be caught by that handler. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
We explicitly define elaboration for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code>s. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>8.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

---

# 11.2. Exception Handlers

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  90

# 11.2. Exception Handlers

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[The response to one or more exceptions is specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</code><a id="S0304"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />  [<b>exception</b><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code><br />    {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>{"}"}]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>exception{"_"}handler</code><a id="S0305"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <b>when</b> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice_parameter_specification</a></code>:] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0307">exception_choice</a></code> {"{"}'|' <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0307">exception_choice</a></code>{"}"} ={">"}<br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>choice{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0306"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>exception{"_"}choice</code><a id="S0307"></a><code> ::= </code><i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> | <b>others</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>&ldquo;<i>Handler</i>&rdquo; is an abbreviation for &ldquo;<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>5.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
Within this clause, we sometimes abbreviate &ldquo;<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0307">exception_choice</a></code>&rdquo; to &ldquo;<i>choice</i>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0022-1"]} />
<p>An <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0307">exception_choice</a></code> shall denote an exception.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>A choice with an <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <i>covers</i> the named exception. A choice with <b>others</b> covers all exceptions not named by previous choices of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>. Two choices in different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>s of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> shall not cover the same exception. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0307">exception_choice</a></code>s of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> may cover the same exception. For example, given two renaming declarations in separate packages for the same exception, one may nevertheless write, for example, &ldquo;<b>when</b> Ada.Text{"_"}IO.Data{"_"}Error | My{"_"}Seq{"_"}IO.Data{"_"}Error ={">"}&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>6.b</MarginText>
An <b>others</b> choice even covers exceptions that are not visible at the place of the handler. Since exception raising is a dynamic activity, it is entirely possible for an <b>others</b> handler to handle an exception that it could not have named. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>A choice with <b>others</b> is allowed only for the last handler of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> and as the only choice of that handler.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>An <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a choice shall not denote an exception declared in a generic formal package. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is because the compiler doesn't know the identity of such an exception, and thus can't enforce the coverage rules. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice_parameter_specification</a></code> declares a <i>choice parameter</i>, which is a constant object of type Exception{"_"}Occurrence (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4#Subclause_11.4.1">11.4.1</a>). During the handling of an exception occurrence, the choice parameter, if any, of the handler represents the exception occurrence that is being handled.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>The execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> consists of the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>. [The optional handlers are used to handle any exceptions that are propagated by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>.] <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of an exception handler:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
begin{"\n"}   Open(File, In{"_"}File, "input.txt");   -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.8#Subclause_A.8.2">A.8.2</a>{"\n"}exception{"\n"}   when E : Name{"_"}Error ={">"}{"\n"}      Put("Cannot open input file : ");{"\n"}      Put{"_"}Line(Ada.Exceptions.Exception{"_"}Message(E));  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4#Subclause_11.4.1">11.4.1</a>{"\n"}      raise;{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> is modified to allow a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice_parameter_specification</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>12.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
Different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0307">exception_choice</a></code>s of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> may cover the same exception. This allows for &ldquo;when Numeric{"_"}Error | Constraint{"_"}Error ={">"}&rdquo; even though Numeric{"_"}Error is a rename of Constraint{"_"}Error. This also allows one to &ldquo;with&rdquo; two different I/O packages, and then write, for example, &ldquo;when Ada.Text{"_"}IO.Data{"_"}Error | My{"_"}Seq{"_"}IO.Data{"_"}Error ={">"}&rdquo; even though these might both be renames of the same exception. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>12.c</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> is new. These are now used in all the places where handlers are allowed. This obviates the need to explain (in Clauses <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/">5</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/">6</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/">7</a>, and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>) what portions of the program are handled by the handlers. Note that there are more such cases in Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>12.d</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice_parameter_specification</a></code> is new. <br />

---

# 11.3. Raise Statements and Raise Expressions

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  91

# 11.3. Raise Statements and Raise Expressions

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> raises an exception.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>raise{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0308"></a><code> ::= </code><b>raise</b>;<br />      | <b>raise</b> <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> [<b>with</b> <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0022-1", "AI12-0152-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>raise{"_"}expression</code><a id="S0309"></a><code> ::= </code><b>raise</b> <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> [<b>with</b> <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.2/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> appears within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of one of the following contexts, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> shall appear within a pair of parentheses within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.3/4</MarginText>
<ul>
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.4/4</MarginText>
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0043">modular_type_definition</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.5/4</MarginText>
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0045">floating_point_definition</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.6/4</MarginText>
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0048">ordinary_fixed_point_definition</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.7/4</MarginText>
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0049">decimal_fixed_point_definition</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.8/4</MarginText>
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.9/4</MarginText>
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0112">ancestor_part</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>2.a.1/4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Unlike conditional expressions, this doesn't say "immediately surrounded"; the only requirement is that it is somehow within a pair of parentheses that is part of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. We need this restriction in order that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code>s cannot be syntactically confused with immediately following constructs (such as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s). <br />

<MarginText>2.a.2/4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We only need to require that a right parenthesis appear somewhere between the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> and the surrounding context; that's all we need to specify in order to eliminate the ambiguities. Moreover, we don't care at all where the left parenthesis is (so long as it is legal, of course).<br />

<MarginText>2.a.3/4</MarginText>
For instance, the following is illegal by this rule: <br />

<MarginText>2.a.4/4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Obj : Boolean := Func{"_"}Call or else raise TBD{"_"}Error with Atomic;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.a.5/4</MarginText>
as the "<b>with</b> Atomic" could be part of the <b>raise{"_"}expression</b> or part of the object declaration. Both of the following are legal: <br />

<MarginText>2.a.6/4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Obj : Boolean := Func{"_"}Call or else (raise TBD{"_"}Error) with Atomic;{"\n"}Obj : Boolean := (Func{"_"}Call or else raise TBD{"_"}Error) with Atomic;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.a.7/4</MarginText>
and if the <b>with</b> belongs to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code>, then both of the following are legal: <br />

<MarginText>2.a.8/4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Obj : Boolean := Func{"_"}Call or else (raise TBD{"_"}Error with Atomic);{"\n"}Obj : Boolean := (Func{"_"}Call or else raise TBD{"_"}Error with Atomic);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.a.9/4</MarginText>
This rule only requires parentheses for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code>s that are part of the "top-level" of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in one of the named contexts; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> is either the entire <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, or part of a chain of logical operations. In practice, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> will almost always be last in interesting top-level <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s; anything that follows it could never be executed, so that should be rare. Other contexts such as conditional expressions, qualified expressions, aggregates, and even function calls, provide the needed parentheses. All of the following are legal, no additional parens are needed: <br />

<MarginText>2.a.10/4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Pre : Boolean  := (if not Is{"_"}Valid(Param) then raise Not{"_"}Valid{"_"}Error);{"\n"}A : A{"_"}Tagged   := (Some{"_"}Tagged'(raise TBD{"_"}Error) with Comp ={">"} 'A');{"\n"}B : Some{"_"}Array := (1, 2, 3, others ={">"} raise Not{"_"}Valid{"_"}Error);{"\n"}C : Natural    := Func (Val ={">"} raise TBD{"_"}Error);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.a.11/4</MarginText>
Parentheses that are part of the context of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> don't count. For instance, the parentheses around the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> are required in the following: <br />

<MarginText>2.a.12/4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
D : A{"_"}Tagged   := ((raise TBD{"_"}Error) with Comp ={">"} 'A');{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.a.13/4</MarginText>
as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0112">ancestor_part</a></code> is one of the contexts that triggers the rule.<br />

<MarginText>2.a.14/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
This English-language rule could have been implemented instead by adding nonterminals <code>initial{"_"}expression</code> and <code>initial{"_"}relation</code>, which are the same as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0133">choice_expression</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0134">choice_relation</a></code> except for the inclusion of membership in <code>initial{"_"}relation</code>. Then, <code>initial{"_"}expresion</code> could be used in place of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in all of the contexts noted. We did not do that because of the large amount of change required, both to the grammar and to language rules that refer to the grammar. A complete grammar is given in .<br />

<MarginText>2.a.15/4</MarginText>
The use of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> is illegal in each of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0043">modular_type_definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0045">floating_point_definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0048">ordinary_fixed_point_definition</a></code>, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0049">decimal_fixed_point_definition</a></code> as these uses are required to be static and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> is never static. We include these in this rule so that Ada text has an unambiguous syntax in these cases. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0022-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<p>The <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, if any, of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> shall denote an exception. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> with no <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (that is, a <i>re-raise statement</i>) shall be within a handler, but not within a body enclosed by that handler. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01", "AI12-0022-1", "AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>The <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, if any, of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> is expected to be of type String.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.2/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0022-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> shall be any single type. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>4/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01", "AI12-0022-1", "AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>To <i>raise an exception</i> is to raise a new occurrence of that exception[, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4">11.4</a>]. For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> with an <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, the named exception is raised. Similarly, for the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code>, the named exception is raised. [In both of these cases, if a <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is present, the expression is evaluated and its value is associated with the exception occurrence.] For the execution of a re-raise statement, the exception occurrence that caused transfer of control to the innermost enclosing handler is raised [again]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The definition of Exceptions.Exception{"_"}Message includes a statement that the string is returned (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4#Subclause_11.4.1">11.4.1</a>). We describe the use of the string here so that we don't have an unexplained parameter in this subclause. <br />

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>For a re-raise statement, the implementation does not create a new Exception{"_"}Occurrence, but instead propagates the same Exception{"_"}Occurrence value. This allows the original cause of the exception to be determined. <br />

<MarginText>4.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>raise an exception</b> &mdash; abandon normal program execution so as to draw attention to the fact that the corresponding situation has arisen<br />

<MarginText>4.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0062-1", "AI12-0152-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
NOTE   If the evaluation of a <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> raises an exception, that exception is propagated instead of the one denoted by the <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of raise statements:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
raise Ada.IO{"_"}Exceptions.Name{"_"}Error;   -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.13">A.13</a>{"\n"}raise Queue{"_"}Error with "Buffer Full"; -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.11">9.11</a>{"\n"}
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
raise;                                -- re-raise the current exception{"\n"}
<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
-- For an example of a raise expression, see the Streams Subsystem definitions in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.1">13.13.1</a>.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
The fact that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> has to denote an exception is not clear from RM83. Clearly that was the intent, since the italicized part of the syntax rules so indicate, but there was no explicit rule. RM83-1.5(11) doesn't seem to give the italicized parts of the syntax any force. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>8.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01"]} />
The syntax of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> is extended to include a string message. This is more convenient than calling Exceptions.Exception{"_"}Message (<i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>'Identity, <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>), and should encourage the use of message strings when raising exceptions. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>8.c/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0022-1", "AI12-0152-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> is new. This construct is necessary to allow conversion of existing specifications to use preconditions and predicates without changing the exceptions raised. It is considered important enough to be added to Ada 2012 rather than waiting for Ada 2022. <br />

# 11.4. Exception Handling

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  92

# 11.4. Exception Handling

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[When an exception occurrence is raised, normal program execution is abandoned and control is transferred to an applicable <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>, if any. To <i>handle</i> an exception occurrence is to respond to the exceptional event. To <i>propagate</i> an exception occurrence is to raise it again in another context; that is, to fail to respond to the exceptional event in the present context.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In other words, if the execution of a given construct raises an exception, but does not handle it, the exception is propagated to an enclosing execution (except in the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>).<br />

<MarginText>1.b/1</MarginText>
Propagation involves re-raising the same exception occurrence. For example, calling an entry of an uncallable task raises Tasking{"_"}Error; this is not propagation. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>Within a given task, if the execution of construct <i>a</i> is defined by this document to consist (in part) of the execution of construct <i>b</i>, then while <i>b</i> is executing, the execution of <i>a</i> is said to <i>dynamically enclose</i> the execution of <i>b</i>. The <i>innermost dynamically enclosing</i> execution of a given execution is the dynamically enclosing execution that started most recently. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>If the execution of <i>a</i> dynamically encloses that of <i>b</i>, then we also say that the execution of <i>b</i> is <i>included in</i> the execution of <i>a</i>. <br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Examples: The execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code> dynamically encloses the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> after the <b>if</b> (during that evaluation). (Recall that &ldquo;execution&rdquo; includes both &ldquo;elaboration&rdquo; and &ldquo;evaluation&rdquo;, as well as other executions.) The evaluation of a function call dynamically encloses the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the function <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0089">body</a></code> (during that execution). Note that, due to recursion, several simultaneous executions of the same construct can be occurring at once during the execution of a particular task.<br />

<MarginText>2.c</MarginText>
Dynamically enclosing is not defined across task boundaries; a task's execution does not include the execution of any other tasks.<br />

<MarginText>2.d</MarginText>
Dynamically enclosing is only defined for executions that are occurring at a given moment in time; if an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code> is currently executing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> after <b>then</b>, then the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> is no longer dynamically enclosed by the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code> (or anything else). <br />

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>When an exception occurrence is raised by the execution of a given construct, the rest of the execution of that construct is <i>abandoned</i>; that is, any portions of the execution that have not yet taken place are not performed. The construct is first completed, and then left, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">7.6.1</a>. Then: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the construct is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>, the exception does not propagate further; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>When an exception is raised by the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>, there is no dynamically enclosing execution, so the exception does not propagate any further. If the exception occurred during the activation of the task, then the activator raises Tasking{"_"}Error, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.2">9.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.2">Task Execution - Task Activation</a>&rdquo;, but we don't define that as propagation; it's a special rule. Otherwise (the exception occurred during the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the task), the task silently disappears. Thus, abnormal termination of tasks is not always considered to be an error. <br />

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the construct is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> that has a handler with a choice covering the exception, the occurrence is handled by that handler;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>Otherwise, the occurrence is <i>propagated</i> to the innermost dynamically enclosing execution, which means that the occurrence is raised again in that context. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>As shorthands, we refer to the <i>propagation of an exception</i>, and the <i>propagation by a construct</i>, if the execution of the construct propagates an exception occurrence. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>When an occurrence is <i>handled</i> by a given handler, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice_parameter_specification</a></code>, if any, is first elaborated, which creates the choice parameter and initializes it to the occurrence. Then, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the handler is executed; this execution replaces the abandoned portion of the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This &ldquo;replacement&rdquo; semantics implies that the handler can do pretty much anything the abandoned sequence could do; for example, in a function, the handler can execute a return statement that applies to the function. <br />

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The rules for exceptions raised in library units, main subprograms and partitions follow from the normal rules, plus the semantics of the environment task described in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/">10</a> (for example, the environment task of a partition elaborates library units and calls the main subprogram). If an exception is propagated by the main subprogram, it is propagated to the environment task, which then terminates abnormally, causing the partition to terminate abnormally. Although abnormal termination of tasks is not necessarily an error, abnormal termination of a partition due to an exception <i>is</i> an error. <br />

<MarginText>7.c/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>handle an exception</b> &mdash; perform some actions in response to the arising of an exception<br />

<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0451-1"]} />
NOTE   Exceptions raised in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a body are not handled by the handlers of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of that body. <br />

<a id="Subclause_11.4.1"></a>

## 11.4.1  The Package Exceptions

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_11.4.1</MarginText>
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_11.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00362-01", "AI95-00400-01", "AI95-00438-01", "AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1", "AI12-0399-1"]} />

<MarginText>7_11.4.1</MarginText>
<p>Each distinct exception is represented by a distinct value of type Exception{"_"}Id. Null{"_"}Id does not represent any exception, and is the default initial value of type Exception{"_"}Id. Each occurrence of an exception is represented by a value of type Exception{"_"}Occurrence. Null{"_"}Occurrence does not represent any exception occurrence, and is the default initial value of type Exception{"_"}Occurrence.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/1_11.4.1</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> E that denotes an exception, the following attribute is defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9_11.4.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>E'Identity</dt>
<dl>
<dd>E'Identity returns the unique identity of the exception. The type of this attribute is Exception{"_"}Id. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>9.a_11.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In a distributed program, the identity is unique across an entire program, not just across a single partition. Exception propagation works properly across RPC's. An exception can be propagated from one partition to another, and then back to the first, where its identity is known. <br />

<MarginText>10/2_11.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01"]} />
<p>Raise{"_"}Exception raises a new occurrence of the identified exception.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.1/4_11.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01", "AI95-00378-01", "AI05-0043-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI12-0022-1", "AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>Exception{"_"}Message returns the message associated with the given Exception{"_"}Occurrence. For an occurrence raised by a call to Raise{"_"}Exception, the message is the Message parameter passed to Raise{"_"}Exception. For the occurrence raised by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> with an <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> and a <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, the message is the <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>. For the occurrence raised by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> with an <i>exception{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> but without a <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, the message is a string giving implementation-defined information about the exception occurrence. For an occurrence originally raised in some other manner (including by the failure of a language-defined check), the message is an unspecified string. In all cases, Exception{"_"}Message returns a string with lower bound 1. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a_11.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The information returned by Exception{"_"}Message.<br />

<MarginText>10.a.1/3_11.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0043-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>There is  about the contents of this string for language-defined checks. <br />

<MarginText>10.b_11.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Given an exception E, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code>: <br />

</CodeBlock>

is equivalent to this call to Raise{"_"}Exception: <br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10.e.1/2_11.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00361-01"]} />
Similarly, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code>: <br />

<MarginText>10.e.2/2_11.4.1</MarginText>

</CodeBlock>

is equivalent to this call to Raise{"_"}Exception: <br />
