Even Ada.Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation would fail for a subtype that excludes null. Most generics would end up with comments saying that they are not intended to work for subtypes that exclude null. We would rather that this sort of requirement be reflected in the contract of the generic. <br />

<MarginText>5/3_12.5.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0239-1", "AI05-0288-1"]} />
<p>For a formal access-to-subprogram subtype, the designated profiles of the formal and the actual shall be subtype conformant. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>6_12.5.4</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of formal access types:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>7_12.5.4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
--  the formal types of the generic package {"\n"}
<MarginText>8_12.5.4</MarginText>
generic{"\n"}   type Node is private;{"\n"}   type Link is access Node;{"\n"}package P is{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9_12.5.4</MarginText>
--  can be matched by the actual types {"\n"}
<MarginText>10_12.5.4</MarginText>
type Car;{"\n"}type Car{"_"}Name is access Car;{"\n"}
<MarginText>11_12.5.4</MarginText>
type Car is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Pred, Succ : Car{"_"}Name;{"\n"}      Number     : License{"_"}Number;{"\n"}      Owner      : Person;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>12_12.5.4</MarginText>
--  in the following generic instantiation {"\n"}
<MarginText>13_12.5.4</MarginText>
package R is new P(Node ={">"} Car, Link ={">"} Car{"_"}Name);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>13.a_12.5.4</MarginText>
The check for matching of designated subtypes is changed from a runtime check to a compile-time check. The Ada 83 rule that &ldquo;If the designated type is other than a scalar type, then the designated subtypes shall be either both constrained or both unconstrained&rdquo; is removed, since it is subsumed by static matching. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>13.b_12.5.4</MarginText>
Formal access-to-subprogram subtypes and formal general access types are new concepts. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>13.c/2_12.5.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
Added a matching rule for subtypes that exclude null.<br />

<MarginText>13.d/2_12.5.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00442-01"]} />
We change to &ldquo;determines a category&rdquo; as that is the new terminology (it avoids confusion, since not all interesting properties form a class). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>13.e/3_12.5.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0288-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Matching of formal access-to-subprogram types now uses subtype conformance rather than mode conformance, which is needed to plug a hole. This could cause some instantiations legal in Ada 95 and Ada 2005 to be rejected in Ada 2012. We believe that formal access-to-subprogram types occur rarely, and actuals that are not subtype conformant are rarer still, so this should not happen often. (In addition, one popular compiler has a bug that causes such instances to be rejected, so no code compiled with that compiler could have an incompatibility.) <br />

<a id="Subclause_12.5.5"></a>

## 12.5.5  Formal Interface Types

<MarginText>1/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00442-01"]} />
<p>[The category determined for a formal interface type is the category of all interface types.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00442-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This rule follows from the rule in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5">12.5</a> that says that the category is determined by the one given in the name of the syntax production. The effect of the rule is repeated here to give a capsule summary of what this subclause is about. <br />

<MarginText>1.b/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Here we're taking advantage of our switch in terminology from &ldquo;determined class&rdquo; to &ldquo;determined category&rdquo;; by saying &ldquo;category&rdquo; rather than &ldquo;class&rdquo;, we require that any actual type be an interface type, not just some type derived from an interface type. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>formal{"_"}interface{"_"}type{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0334"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0077">interface_type_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251", "AI95-00401"]} />
<p>The actual type shall be a descendant of every progenitor of the formal type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345"]} />
<p>The actual type shall be a limited, task, protected, or synchronized interface if and only if the formal type is also, respectively, a limited, task, protected, or synchronized interface. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We require the kind of interface type to match exactly because without that it is almost impossible to properly implement the interface. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>5/5_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1", "AI12-0442-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of the use of a generic with a formal interface type, to establish a standard interface that all tasks will implement so they can be managed appropriately by an application-specific scheduler:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>6/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Root{"_"}Work{"_"}Item is tagged private;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
generic{"\n"}   type Managed{"_"}Task is task interface;{"\n"}   type Work{"_"}Item({"<"}{">"}) is new Root{"_"}Work{"_"}Item with private;{"\n"}package Server{"_"}Manager is{"\n"}   task type Server is new Managed{"_"}Task with{"\n"}      entry Start(Data : in out Work{"_"}Item);{"\n"}   end Server;{"\n"}end Server{"_"}Manager;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>8.a/2_12.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00345-01", "AI95-00401-01", "AI95-00442-01"]} />
The formal interface type is new. <br />

---

# 12.6. Formal Subprograms

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6.mdx

sidebar_position:  101

# 12.6. Formal Subprograms

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ Formal subprograms can be used to pass callable entities to a generic unit.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
Generic formal subprograms are like renames of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0318">explicit_generic_actual_parameter</a></code>. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>formal{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0335"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0336">formal_concrete_subprogram_declaration</a></code><br />    | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal_abstract_subprogram_declaration</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02", "AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>formal{"_"}concrete{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0336"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <b>with</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0196">subprogram_specification</a></code> [<b>is</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0338">subprogram_default</a></code>]<br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02", "AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0337"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <b>with</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0196">subprogram_specification</a></code> <b>is abstract</b> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0338">subprogram_default</a></code>]<br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>subprogram{"_"}default</code><a id="S0338"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0339">default_name</a></code> | {"<"}{">"} | <b>null</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>default{"_"}name</code><a id="S0339"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02", "AI95-00348-01"]} />
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0338">subprogram_default</a></code> of <b>null</b> shall not be specified for a formal function or for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal_abstract_subprogram_declaration</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>There are no null functions because the return value has to be constructed somehow. We don't allow null for abstract formal procedures, as the operation is dispatching. It doesn't seem appropriate (or useful) to say that the implementation of something is null in the formal type and all possible descendants of that type. This also would define a dispatching operation that doesn't correspond to a slot in the tag of the controlling type, which would be a new concept. Finally, additional rules would be needed to define the meaning of a dispatching null procedure (for instance, the convention of such a subprogram should be intrinsic, but that's not what the language says). It doesn't seem worth the effort. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>The expected profile for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0339">default_name</a></code>, if any, is that of the formal subprogram. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule, unlike others in this subclause, is observed at compile time of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0310">generic_declaration</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>5.b</MarginText>
The evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0339">default_name</a></code> takes place during the elaboration of each instantiation that uses the default, as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">Generic Instantiation</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>For a generic formal subprogram, the expected profile for the actual is that of the formal subprogram. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0239-1"]} />
<p>The profiles of the formal and any named default shall be mode conformant. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule, unlike others in this subclause, is checked at compile time of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0310">generic_declaration</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0239-1"]} />
<p>The profiles of the formal and actual shall be mode conformant. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00423-01"]} />
<p>For a parameter or result subtype of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code> that has an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>:<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0183-1", "AI12-0287-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>if the actual matching the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code> statically denotes a generic formal subprogram of another generic unit <i>G</i>, and the instantiation containing the actual occurs within the body of a generic unit <i>G</i> or within the body of a generic unit declared within the declarative region of the generic unit <i>G</i>, then the corresponding parameter or result type of the formal subprogram of <i>G</i> shall have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.3/2</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, the subtype of the corresponding parameter or result type of the actual matching the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code> shall exclude null. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), this rule applies also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule prevents &ldquo;lying&rdquo;. <b>Null</b> must never be the value of a parameter or result with an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>. The first bullet is an assume-the-worst rule which prevents trouble in generic bodies (including bodies of child generics) when the formal subtype excludes null implicitly. <br />

<MarginText>8.4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0204-1"]} />
<p>If the named default, if any, is a prefixed view, the prefix of that view shall denote an object for which renaming is allowed (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#Subclause_8.5.1">8.5.1</a>). Similarly, if the actual subprogram in an instantiation is a prefixed view, the prefix of that view shall denote an object for which renaming is allowed.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0204-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The prefix in such a case is essentially renamed at the point of the instantiation and passed to any calls of the formal subprogram in the generic. If the prefix isn't legal to rename, that doesn't make sense (and allowing it might end up passing a nonexistent object to some calls). <br />

<MarginText>8.5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02", "AI05-0296-1"]} />
<p>If a formal parameter of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> is of a specific tagged type <i>T</i> or of an anonymous access type designating a specific tagged type <i>T</i>, <i>T</i> is called a <i>controlling type</i> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>. Similarly, if the result of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> for a function is of a specific tagged type <i>T</i> or of an anonymous access type designating a specific tagged type <i>T</i>, <i>T</i> is called a controlling type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> shall have exactly one controlling type, and that type shall not be incomplete. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.c/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The specific tagged type could be any of a formal tagged private type, a formal derived type, a formal interface type, or a normal tagged type. While the last case doesn't seem to be very useful, there isn't any good reason for disallowing it. This rule ensures that the operation is a dispatching operation of some type, and that we unambiguously know what that type is.<br />

<MarginText>8.d/2</MarginText>
We informally call a subprogram declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> an <i>abstract formal subprogram</i>, but we do not use this term in normative wording. (We do use it often in these notes.) <br />

<MarginText>8.6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02", "AI12-0165-1"]} />
<p>The actual subprogram for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> shall be:<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.7/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a dispatching operation of the controlling type; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.8/5</MarginText>
<li>if the controlling type is a formal type, and the actual type corresponding to that formal type is a specific type <i>T</i>, a dispatching operation of type <i>T</i>; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.9/5</MarginText>
<li>if the controlling type is a formal type, and the actual type is a class-wide type <i>T</i>'Class, an implicitly declared subprogram corresponding to a primitive operation of type <i>T</i> (see Static Semantics below). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.e/2</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>We mean the controlling type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>, of course. Saying that gets unwieldy and redundant (so says at least one reviewer, anyway). <br />

<MarginText>8.e.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0165-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This means that the actual is a primitive operation of the controlling type, an abstract formal subprogram, or the implicitly available primitive operation for a class-wide type.<br />

<MarginText>8.e.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0165-1"]} />
An explicit class-wide operation cannot be used for the actual of a formal abstract subprogram. Such an operation is never primitive (only specific types have primitive subprograms).<br />

<MarginText>8.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0165-1"]} />
This could happen in a case like: <br />

<MarginText>8.g/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type T({"<"}{">"}) is tagged private;{"\n"}   with procedure Foo (Obj : in T) is abstract;{"\n"}package P ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>8.h/2</MarginText>
package New{"_"}P is new P (Something'Class, Some{"_"}Proc);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8.i/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0165-1"]} />
If Some{"_"}Proc is an explicit class-wide operation, the instantiation here is illegal, because Some{"_"}Proc is not a primitive operation of Something'Class (there are no such operations).<br />

<MarginText>8.i.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0165-1"]} />
However, if Some{"_"}Proc is a primitive operation of type Something, then the instantiation is legal; the actual is the implicitly generated subprogram described in Static Semantics below. This is not a problem, since the rules given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a> explain how this routine dispatches even though its parameter is class-wide.<br />

<MarginText>8.i.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0165-1"]} />
We allow this special case because it is possible for a class-wide operation to be primitive inside of an instance, and the contract model does not allow us to make such cases illegal. As such, it seems inconsistent to not allow the same in explicit instantiations.<br />

<MarginText>8.j/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0165-1"]} />
Specifically, since it is possible for a formal tagged type to be instantiated with a class-wide type, it is possible for the (real) controlling type to be class-wide as in the following unusual case:<br />

<MarginText>8.k/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type NT({"<"}{">"}) is new T with private;{"\n"}   -- Presume that T has the following primitive operation:{"\n"}   -- procedure Bar (Obj : in T);{"\n"}package Gr ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>8.l/2</MarginText>
package body Gr is{"\n"}   package New{"_"}P2 is new P (NT, Foo ={">"} Bar);{"\n"}end Gr;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8.m/2</MarginText>
package New{"_"}Gr is new Gr (Something'Class);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8.n/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0165-1"]} />
The instantiation of New{"_"}P2 is legal, since Bar is a dispatching operation of the actual type of the controlling type of the abstract formal subprogram Foo. Again, the rules given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a> explain how this routine dispatches.<br />

<MarginText>8.o/2</MarginText>
Note that this legality rule never needs to be rechecked in an instance (that contains a nested instantiation). The rule only talks about the actual type of the instantiation; it does not require looking further; if the actual type is in fact a formal type, we do not intend looking at the actual for that formal. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code> declares a generic formal subprogram. The types of the formal parameters and result, if any, of the formal subprogram are those determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>s given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code>; however, independent of the particular subtypes that are denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>s, the nominal subtypes of the formal parameters and result, if any, are defined to be nonstatic, and unconstrained if of an array type [(no applicable index constraint is provided in a call on a formal subprogram)]. In an instance, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code> declares a view of the actual. The profile of this view takes its subtypes and calling convention from the original profile of the actual entity, while taking the formal parameter <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default{"_"}expression</a></code>s from the profile given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>. The view is a function or procedure, never an entry. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This rule is intended to be the same as the one for renamings-as-declarations, where the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code> is analogous to a renaming-as-declaration, and the actual is analogous to the renamed view. <br />

<MarginText>9.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0071-1", "AI05-0131-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in the profile of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code> denotes a formal private or formal derived type and the actual type for this formal type is a class-wide type <i>T</i>'Class, then for the purposes of resolving the corresponding actual subprogram at the point of the instantiation, certain implicit declarations may be available as possible resolutions as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.2/3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">For each primitive subprogram of <i>T</i> that is directly visible at the point of the instantiation, and that has at least one controlling formal parameter, a corresponding implicitly declared subprogram with the same defining name, and having the same profile as the primitive subprogram except that <i>T</i> is systematically replaced by <i>T</i>'Class in the types of its profile, is potentially use-visible. The body of such a subprogram is as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a> for primitive subprograms of a formal type when the actual type is class-wide. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0071-1", "AI05-0131-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This gives the same capabilities to formal subprograms as those that primitive operations of the formal type have when the actual type is class-wide. We do not want to discourage the use of explicit declarations for (formal) subprograms! <br />

<MarginText>9.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0071-1", "AI05-0131-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Although the above wording seems to require constructing implicit versions of all of the primitive subprograms of type <i>T</i>, it should be clear that a compiler only needs to consider those that could possibly resolve to the corresponding actual subprogram. For instance, if the formal subprogram is a procedure with two parameters, and the actual subprogram name is Bar (either given explicitly or by default), the compiler need not consider primitives that are functions, that have the wrong number of parameters, that have defining names other than Bar, and so on; thus it does not need to construct implicit declarations for those primitives. <br />

<MarginText>9.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0071-1", "AI05-0131-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Functions that only have a controlling result and do not have a controlling parameter of <i>T</i> are not covered by this rule, as any call would be required to raise Program{"_"}Error by <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a>. It is better to detect the error earlier than at run time. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>If a generic unit has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0338">subprogram_default</a></code> specified by a box, and the corresponding actual parameter is omitted, then it is equivalent to an explicit actual parameter that is a usage name identical to the defining name of the formal.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />
<p>If a generic unit has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0338">subprogram_default</a></code> specified by the reserved word <b>null</b>, and the corresponding actual parameter is omitted, then it is equivalent to an explicit actual parameter that is a null procedure having the profile given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02"]} />
<p>The subprogram declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> with a controlling type <i>T</i> is a dispatching operation of type <i>T</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is necessary to trigger all of the dispatching operation rules. It otherwise would not be considered a dispatching operation, as formal subprograms are never primitive operations. <br />

<MarginText>11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 1   The matching rules for formal subprograms state requirements that are similar to those applying to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0242">subprogram_renaming_declaration</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#Subclause_8.5.4">8.5.4</a>). In particular, the name of a parameter of the formal subprogram can be different from that of the corresponding parameter of the actual subprogram; similarly, for these parameters, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s can be different.<br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
NOTE 2   The constraints that apply to a parameter of a formal subprogram are those of the corresponding formal parameter of the matching actual subprogram (not those implied by the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in the <code>{"_"}specification</code> of the formal subprogram). A similar remark applies to the result of a function. Therefore, to avoid confusion, it is recommended that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a first subtype be used in any declaration of a formal subprogram. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The subtype specified for a formal parameter of a generic formal subprogram can be any visible subtype, including a generic formal subtype of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
NOTE 4   A formal subprogram is matched by an attribute of a type if the attribute is a function with a matching specification. An enumeration literal of a given type matches a parameterless formal function whose result type is the given type.<br />

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0347-1"]} />
NOTE 5   A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0339">default_name</a></code> denotes an entity that is visible or directly visible at the place of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0310">generic_declaration</a></code>; a box used as a default is equivalent to a name that denotes an entity that is directly visible at the place of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Visibility and name resolution are applied to the equivalent explicit actual parameter. <br />

<MarginText>16/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02"]} />
NOTE 6   The actual subprogram cannot be abstract unless the formal subprogram is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.3">3.9.3</a>).<br />

<MarginText>16.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02", "AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 7   The subprogram declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> is an abstract subprogram. All calls on a subprogram declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal{"_"}abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> are limited to dispatching calls. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.3">3.9.3</a>.<br />

<MarginText>16.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />
NOTE 8   A null procedure as a subprogram default has convention Intrinsic (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>). <br />

<MarginText>16.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This is an implicitly declared subprogram, so it has convention Intrinsic as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of generic formal subprograms:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>18/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with function "+"(X, Y : Item) return Item is {"<"}{">"};{"\n"}with function Image(X : Enum) return String is Enum'Image;{"\n"}with procedure Update is Default{"_"}Update;{"\n"}with procedure Pre{"_"}Action(X : in Item) is null;  -- defaults to no action{"\n"}with procedure Write(S    : not null access Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type'Class;{"\n"}                     Desc : Descriptor){"\n"}                     is abstract Descriptor'Write;  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>{"\n"}-- Dispatching operation on Descriptor with default{"\n"}
<MarginText>19</MarginText>
--  given the generic procedure declaration {"\n"}
<MarginText>20</MarginText>
generic{"\n"}   with procedure Action (X : in Item);{"\n"}procedure Iterate(Seq : in Item{"_"}Sequence);{"\n"}
<MarginText>21</MarginText>
--  and the procedure {"\n"}
<MarginText>22</MarginText>
procedure Put{"_"}Item(X : in Item);{"\n"}
<MarginText>23</MarginText>
--  the following instantiation is possible {"\n"}
<MarginText>24</MarginText>
procedure Put{"_"}List is new Iterate(Action ={">"} Put{"_"}Item);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>24.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00260-02"]} />
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal_abstract_subprogram_declaration</a></code> is new. It allows the passing of dispatching operations to generic units.<br />

<MarginText>24.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />
The formal subprogram default of <b>null</b> is new. It allows the default of a generic procedure to do nothing, such as for passing a debugging routine. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>24.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00423-01"]} />
Added matching rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>s. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>24.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0296-1"]} />
It is now illegal to declare a formal abstract subprogram whose controlling type is incomplete. It was never intended to allow that, and such a type would have to come from outside of the generic unit in Ada 2005, so it is unlikely to be useful. Moreover, a dispatching call on the subprogram is likely to fail in many implementations. So it is very unlikely that any code will need to be changed because of this new rule. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>24.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0071-1", "AI05-0131-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added construction of implicit subprograms for primitives of class-wide actual types, to make it possible to import subprograms via formal subprograms as well as by implicit primitive operations of a formal type. (This is a <b>Correction</b> as it is very important for the usability of indefinite containers when instantiated with class-wide types; thus we want Ada 2005 implementations to support it.)<br />

<MarginText>24.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0336">formal_concrete_subprogram_declaration</a></code> and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal_abstract_subprogram_declaration</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>24.g/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0204-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a rule to ensure that for an actual subprogram that is a prefixed view, the prefix continues to exist during the life of the instantiation. If the prefix is a subcomponent that depends on discriminants, Ada 2005 and 2012 would have allowed the prefix while Ada 2022 would not. Without this change, explicit forms (renaming the object and then using that in instantiations) would be safer than directly using the prefixed view; that's inconsistent with other kinds of actual subprograms. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>24.h/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0165-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> We now allow the actual for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal_abstract_subprogram_declaration</a></code> to be an implicitly declared subprogram for a class-wide type. The rules already required a compiler to be able to construct this subprogram for use in an instantiation that occurs inside of a generic unit, so it made no sense to prevent it from being used explicitly as well (in the same way that the previous extension allows them to be used for other kinds of formal subprograms). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>24.i/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0287-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording to ensure that the object subject to a Legality Rule can be determined at compile-time. The alternative being nonsense, we treat this as a wording change. <br />

---

# 12.7. Formal Packages

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7.mdx

sidebar_position:  102

# 12.7. Formal Packages

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ Formal packages can be used to pass packages to a generic unit. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0340">formal_package_declaration</a></code> declares that the formal package is an instance of a given generic package. Upon instantiation, the actual package has to be an instance of that generic package.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>formal{"_"}package{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0340"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>with</b> <b>package</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> <b>is</b> <b>new</b> <i>generic{"_"}package{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal_package_actual_part</a></code><br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>formal{"_"}package{"_"}actual{"_"}part</code><a id="S0341"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    ([<b>others</b> ={">"}] {"<"}{">"})<br />  | [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0316">generic_actual_part</a></code>]<br />  | (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code>{"}"} [, <b>others</b> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}])<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>formal{"_"}package{"_"}association</code><a id="S0342"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0317">generic_association</a></code><br />  | <i>generic{"_"}formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<p class="Indented2">Any positional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal{"_"}package{"_"}association</a></code>s shall precede any named <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal{"_"}package{"_"}association</a></code>s. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>The <i>generic{"_"}package{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall denote a generic package (the <i>template</i> for the formal package); the formal package is an instance of the template.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0025-1"]} />
<p>The <i>generic{"_"}formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code> shall denote a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0314">generic_formal_parameter_declaration</a></code> of the template. If two or more formal subprograms of the template have the same defining name, then named associations are not allowed for the corresponding actuals.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00398-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal_package_actual_part</a></code> shall contain at most one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code> for each formal parameter. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal_package_actual_part</a></code> does not include &ldquo;<b>others</b> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}&rdquo;, each formal parameter without an association shall have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0338">subprogram_default</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0200-1"]} />
<p>The rules for matching between <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code>s and the generic formals of the template are as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.4/3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If all of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code>s are given by generic associations, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0318">explicit_generic_actual_parameter</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code>s shall be legal for an instantiation of the template.<br /></li>
<MarginText>4.5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0200-1"]} />
<li>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code> for a formal type <i>T</i> of the template is given by {"<"}{">"}, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0342">formal_package_association</a></code> for any other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0314">generic_formal_parameter_declaration</a></code> of the template that mentions <i>T</i> directly or indirectly shall also be given by {"<"}{">"}.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0200-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The above rule is simple to state, though it does not reflect the fact that the formal package functions like an instantiation of a special kind, where each box association for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0314">generic_formal_parameter_declaration</a></code> <i>F</i> is replaced with a new entity <i>F</i>' that has the same characteristics as <i>F</i>: if <i>F</i> is a formal discrete type then <i>F</i>' is a discrete type, if <i>F</i> is a formal subprogram then <i>F</i>' is a subprogram with a similar signature, etc. In practice this is achieved by making the association into a copy of the declaration of the generic formal.<br />

<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<p>The actual shall be an instance of the template. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal_package_actual_part</a></code> is ({"<"}{">"}) or (<b>others</b> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}), [then the actual may be any instance of the template]; otherwise, certain of the actual parameters of the actual instance shall match the corresponding actual parameters of the formal package, determined as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal{"_"}package{"_"}actual{"_"}part</a></code> includes <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0317">generic_association</a></code>s as well as associations with {"<"}{">"}, then only the actual parameters specified explicitly with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0317">generic_association</a></code>s are required to match;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<li>Otherwise, all actual parameters shall match[, whether any actual parameter is given explicitly or by default]. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.3/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<p>The rules for matching of actual parameters between the actual instance and the formal package are as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>For a formal object of mode <b>in</b>, the actuals match if they are static expressions with the same value, or if they statically denote the same constant, or if they are both the literal <b>null</b>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We can't simply require full conformance between the two actual parameter expressions, because the two expressions are being evaluated at different times. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a formal subtype, the actuals match if they denote statically matching subtypes. <br /></li>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<li>For other kinds of formals, the actuals match if they statically denote the same entity. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00213-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0039</i>{"}"} For the purposes of matching, any actual parameter that is the name of a formal object of mode <b>in</b> is replaced by the formal object's actual expression (recursively). <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0340">formal_package_declaration</a></code> declares a generic formal package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<p>The visible part of a formal package includes the first list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package{"_"}specification</a></code>. In addition, for each actual parameter that is not required to match, a copy of the declaration of the corresponding formal parameter of the template is included in the visible part of the formal package. If the copied declaration is for a formal type, copies of the implicit declarations of the primitive subprograms of the formal type are also included in the visible part of the formal package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal_package_actual_part</a></code> is ({"<"}{">"}), then the declarations that occur immediately within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code> of the template for the formal package are visible outside the formal package, and can be denoted by expanded names outside the formal package. If only some of the actual parameters are given by {"<"}{">"}, then the declaration corresponding to those parameters (but not the others) are made visible. <br />

<MarginText>10.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We always want either the actuals or the formals of an instance to be nameable from outside, but never both. If both were nameable, one would get some funny anomalies since they denote the same entity, but, in the case of types at least, they might have different and inconsistent sets of primitive operators due to predefined operator &ldquo;reemergence&rdquo;, Formal derived types exacerbate the difference. We want the implicit declarations of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code> as well as the explicit declarations, so we get operations on the formal types. <br />

<MarginText>10.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A generic formal package is a package, and is an instance. Hence, it is possible to pass a generic formal package as an actual to another generic formal package. <br />

<MarginText>11/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
<p>For the purposes of matching, if the actual instance <i>A</i> is itself a formal package, then the actual parameters of <i>A</i> are those specified explicitly or implicitly in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal_package_actual_part</a></code> for <i>A</i>, plus, for those not specified, the copies of the formal parameters of the template included in the visible part of <i>A</i>.<br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>12/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
<p><i>Example of a generic package with formal package parameters:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>13/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Containers.Ordered{"_"}Maps;  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.6">A.18.6</a>{"\n"}generic{"\n"}   with package Mapping{"_"}1 is new Ada.Containers.Ordered{"_"}Maps({"<"}{">"});{"\n"}   with package Mapping{"_"}2 is new Ada.Containers.Ordered{"_"}Maps{"\n"}                                    (Key{"_"}Type ={">"} Mapping{"_"}1.Element{"_"}Type,{"\n"}                                     others ={">"} {"<"}{">"});{"\n"}package Ordered{"_"}Join is{"\n"}   -- Provide a "join" between two mappings{"\n"}
<MarginText>14/2</MarginText>
   subtype Key{"_"}Type is Mapping{"_"}1.Key{"_"}Type;{"\n"}   subtype Element{"_"}Type is Mapping{"_"}2.Element{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15/2</MarginText>
   function Lookup(Key : Key{"_"}Type) return Element{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>16/2</MarginText>
   ...{"\n"}end Ordered{"_"}Join;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>17/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
<p><i>Example of an instantiation of a package with formal packages:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>18/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Containers.Ordered{"_"}Maps;{"\n"}package Symbol{"_"}Package is{"\n"}
<MarginText>19/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1"]} />
   subtype Key{"_"}String is String(1..5);{"\n"}   type String{"_"}Id is ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>20/2</MarginText>
   type Symbol{"_"}Info is ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>21/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1"]} />
   package String{"_"}Table is new Ada.Containers.Ordered{"_"}Maps{"\n"}           (Key{"_"}Type ={">"} Key{"_"}String,{"\n"}            Element{"_"}Type ={">"} String{"_"}Id);{"\n"}
<MarginText>22/2</MarginText>
   package Symbol{"_"}Table is new Ada.Containers.Ordered{"_"}Maps{"\n"}           (Key{"_"}Type ={">"} String{"_"}Id,{"\n"}            Element{"_"}Type ={">"} Symbol{"_"}Info);{"\n"}
<MarginText>23/2</MarginText>
   package String{"_"}Info is new Ordered{"_"}Join(Mapping{"_"}1 ={">"} String{"_"}Table,{"\n"}                                           Mapping{"_"}2 ={">"} Symbol{"_"}Table);{"\n"}
<MarginText>24/2</MarginText>
   Apple{"_"}Info : constant Symbol{"_"}Info := String{"_"}Info.Lookup("Apple");{"\n"}
<MarginText>25/2</MarginText>
end Symbol{"_"}Package;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>25.a</MarginText>
Formal packages are new to Ada 95. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>25.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01", "AI95-00398-01"]} />
It's now allowed to mix actuals of a formal package that are specified with those that are not specified. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>25.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00213-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0039</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected the description of formal package matching to say that formal parameters are always replaced by their actual parameters (recursively). This matches the actual practice of compilers, as the ACATS has always required this behavior.<br />

<MarginText>25.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00317-01"]} />
The description of which operations are visible in a formal package has been clarified. We also specify how matching is done when the actual is a formal package. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>25.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0025-1", "AI05-0200-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added missing rules for parameters of generic formal package that parallel those in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>, as well as some specific to {"<"}{">"} parameters. These are technically incompatibilities because generic formal package parameters that Ada 95 and Ada 2005 would have considered legal now have to be rejected. But this should not be an issue in practice as such formal parameters could not have matched any actual generics. And it is quite likely that implementations already enforce some of these rules. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>25.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0340">formal_package_declaration</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

---

# 12.8. Example of a Generic Package

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.8.mdx

sidebar_position:  103

# 12.8. Example of a Generic Package

#### Examples

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>The following example provides a possible formulation of stacks by means of a generic package. The size of each stack and the type of the stack elements are provided as generic formal parameters.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/1</MarginText>
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   Size : Positive;{"\n"}   type Item is private;{"\n"}package Stack is{"\n"}   procedure Push(E : in  Item);{"\n"}   procedure Pop (E : out Item);{"\n"}   Overflow, Underflow : exception;{"\n"}end Stack;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
package body Stack is{"\n"}
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
   type Table is array (Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Item;{"\n"}   Space : Table(1 .. Size);{"\n"}   Index : Natural := 0;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
   procedure Push(E : in Item) is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      if Index {">"}= Size then{"\n"}         raise Overflow;{"\n"}      end if;{"\n"}      Index := Index + 1;{"\n"}      Space(Index) := E;{"\n"}   end Push;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
   procedure Pop(E : out Item) is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      if Index = 0 then{"\n"}         raise Underflow;{"\n"}      end if;{"\n"}      E := Space(Index);{"\n"}      Index := Index - 1;{"\n"}   end Pop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
end Stack;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>Instances of this generic package can be obtained as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Stack{"_"}Int  is new Stack(Size ={">"} 200, Item ={">"} Integer);{"\n"}package Stack{"_"}Bool is new Stack(100, Boolean);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>Thereafter, the procedures of the instantiated packages can be called as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Stack{"_"}Int.Push(N);{"\n"}Stack{"_"}Bool.Push(True);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>Alternatively, a generic formulation of the type Stack can be given as follows (package body omitted): <br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type Item is private;{"\n"}package On{"_"}Stacks is{"\n"}   type Stack(Size : Positive) is limited private;{"\n"}   procedure Push(S : in out Stack; E : in  Item);{"\n"}   procedure Pop (S : in out Stack; E : out Item);{"\n"}   Overflow, Underflow : exception;{"\n"}private{"\n"}   type Table is array (Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Item;{"\n"}   type Stack(Size : Positive) is{"\n"}      record{"\n"}         Space : Table(1 .. Size);{"\n"}         Index : Natural := 0;{"\n"}      end record;{"\n"}end On{"_"}Stacks;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p>In order to use such a package, an instance has to be created and thereafter stacks of the corresponding type can be declared: <br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
declare{"\n"}   package Stack{"_"}Real is new On{"_"}Stacks(Real); use Stack{"_"}Real;{"\n"}   S : Stack(100);{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}   Push(S, 2.54);{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

# 12. Generic Units

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.mdx

sidebar_position:  95

# 12. Generic Units

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>A <i>generic unit</i> is a program unit that is either a generic subprogram or a generic package. A generic unit is a <i>template</i>[, which can be parameterized, and from which corresponding (nongeneric) subprograms or packages can be obtained]. The resulting program units are said to be <i>instances</i> of the original generic unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>generic unit</b> &mdash; template for a (nongeneric) program unit<br />Note 1: The template can be parameterized by objects, types, subprograms, and packages.<br />Note 2: Generic units can be used to perform the role that macros sometimes play in other languages.<br />

<MarginText>1.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>generic instance</b> &mdash; nongeneric unit created by the instantiation of a generic unit<br />

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>[A generic unit is declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0310">generic_declaration</a></code>. This form of declaration has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic{"_"}formal{"_"}part</a></code> declaring any generic formal parameters. An instance of a generic unit is obtained as the result of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code> with appropriate generic actual parameters for the generic formal parameters. An instance of a generic subprogram is a subprogram. An instance of a generic package is a package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>Generic units are templates. As templates they do not have the properties that are specific to their nongeneric counterparts. For example, a generic subprogram can be instantiated but it cannot be called. In contrast, an instance of a generic subprogram is a (nongeneric) subprogram; hence, this instance can be called but it cannot be used to produce further instances.] <br /></p>

---

# 13.1. Operational and Representation Aspects

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  105

# 13.1. Operational and Representation Aspects

<MarginText>0.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} [Two kinds of aspects of entities can be specified: representation aspects and operational aspects. Representation aspects affect how the types and other entities of the language are to be mapped onto the underlying machine. Operational aspects determine other properties of entities.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>0.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>operational aspect</b> &mdash; aspect that indicates a logical property of an entity, such as the precondition of a subprogram, or the procedure used to write a given type of object to a stream<br />

<MarginText>0.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>representation aspect</b> &mdash; aspect that indicates how an entity is mapped onto the underlying hardware, for example the size or alignment of an object<br />

<MarginText>0.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<p>[Either kind of aspect of an entity may be specified by means of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>), which is an optional element of most kinds of declarations and applies to the entity or entities being declared. Aspects may also be specified by certain other constructs occurring subsequent to the declaration of the affected entity: a representation aspect value may be specified by means of a representation item and an operational aspect value may be specified by means of an operational item.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} There are six kinds of <i>representation items</i>: <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute{"_"}definition{"_"}clause</a></code>s for representation attributes, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.4#S0350">enumeration{"_"}representation{"_"}clause</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record{"_"}representation{"_"}clause</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0353">component_clause</a></code>s, and <i>representation pragmas</i>. [ They can be provided to give more efficient representation or to interface with features that are outside the domain of the language (for example, peripheral hardware). ]<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} An <i>operational item</i> is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> for an operational attribute.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.2/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} [An operational item or a representation item applies to an entity identified by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>, which denotes an entity declared local to the current declarative region, or a library unit declared immediately preceding a representation pragma in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0285">compilation</a></code>.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} Representation aspects are intended to refer to properties that need to be known before the compiler can generate code to create or access an entity. For instance, the size of an object needs to be known before the object can be created. Conversely, operational aspects are those that only need to be known before they can be used. For instance, how an object is read from a stream only needs to be known when a stream read is executed. Thus, representation aspects have stricter rules as to when they can be specified.<br />

<MarginText>1.a.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
Confirming the value of an aspect should never change the semantics of the aspect. Thus Size = 8 (for example) means the same thing whether it was specified with a representation item or whether the compiler chose this value by default. <br />

<MarginText>1.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>aspect</b> &mdash; specifiable property of an entity<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> on the declaration of the entity. Some aspects can be queried via attributes.<br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} <code>aspect{"_"}clause</code><a id="S0343"></a><a id="S0344"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code><br />      | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.4#S0350">enumeration_representation_clause</a></code><br />      | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code><br />      | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>local{"_"}name</code><a id="S0345"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code><br />      | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>'<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code><br />      | <i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<p class="Indented2">{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} A representation pragma is allowed only at places where an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0286">compilation_unit</a></code> is allowed. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} In an operational item or representation item, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>, then it shall resolve to denote a declaration (or, in the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>, one or more declarations) that occurs immediately within the same declarative region as the item. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> has an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code>, then it shall resolve to denote an implementation-defined component (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#Subclause_13.5.1">13.5.1</a>) or a class-wide type implicitly declared immediately within the same declarative region as the item. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> that is a <i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (only permitted in a representation pragma) shall resolve to denote the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> that immediately precedes (except for other pragmas) the representation pragma. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} This is a Name Resolution Rule, because we don't want an operational or representation item for X to be ambiguous just because there's another X declared in an outer declarative region. It doesn't make much difference, since most operational or representation items are for types or subtypes, and type and subtype names can't be overloaded. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} The visibility rules imply that the declaration has to occur before the operational or representation item.<br />

<MarginText>5.c/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} For objects, this implies that operational or representation items can be applied only to stand-alone objects. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>6/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code> or representation pragma shall statically denote an entity (or, in the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>, one or more entities) declared immediately preceding it in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0285">compilation</a></code>, or within the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task{"_"}definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected{"_"}definition</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0067">record{"_"}definition</a></code> as the representation or operational item. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> denotes a [local] callable entity, it may do so through a [local] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0242">subprogram{"_"}renaming{"_"}declaration</a></code> [(as a way to resolve ambiguity in the presence of overloading)]; otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> shall not denote a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming{"_"}declaration</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The &ldquo;statically denote&rdquo; part implies that it is impossible to specify the representation of an object that is not a stand-alone object, except in the case of a representation item like pragma Atomic that is allowed inside a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> (in which case the representation item specifies the representation of components of all objects of the type). It also prevents the problem of renamings of things like &ldquo;P.<b>all</b>&rdquo; (where P is an access-to-subprogram value) or &ldquo;E(I)&rdquo; (where E is an entry family).<br />

<MarginText>6.b</MarginText>
The part about where the denoted entity has to have been declared appears twice &mdash; once as a Name Resolution Rule, and once as a Legality Rule. Suppose P renames Q, and we have a representation item in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> is P. The fact that the representation item has to appear in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> as P is a Name Resolution Rule, whereas the fact that the representation item has to appear in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> as Q is a Legality Rule. This is subtle, but it seems like the least confusing set of rules. <br />

<MarginText>6.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A separate Legality Rule applies for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0353">component_clause</a></code>s. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#Subclause_13.5.1">13.5.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#Subclause_13.5.1">Record Representation Clauses</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>The <i>representation</i> of an object consists of a certain number of bits (the <i>size</i> of the object). For an object of an elementary type, these are the bits that are normally read or updated by the machine code when loading, storing, or operating-on the value of the object. For an object of a composite type, these are the bits reserved for this object, and include bits occupied by subcomponents of the object. If the size of an object is greater than that of its subtype, the additional bits are padding bits. For an elementary object, these padding bits are normally read and updated along with the others. For a composite object, it is unspecified whether padding bits are read or updated in any given composite operation.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>Discontiguous representations are allowed, but the ones we're interested in here are generally contiguous sequences of bits. For a discontiguous representation, the size doesn't necessarily describe the &ldquo;footprint&rdquo; of the object in memory (that is, the amount of space taken in the address space for the object). <br />

<MarginText>7.a.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In the case of composite objects, we want the implementation to have the flexibility to either do operations component-by-component, or with a block operation covering all of the bits. We carefully avoid giving a preference in the wording. There is no requirement for the choice to be documented, either, as the implementation can make that choice based on many factors, and could make a different choice for different operations on the same object.<br />

<MarginText>7.a.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02"]} />
In the case of a properly aligned, contiguous object whose size is a multiple of the storage unit size, no other bits should be read or updated as part of operating on the object. We don't say this normatively because it would be difficult to normatively define &ldquo;properly aligned&rdquo; or &ldquo;contiguous&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Two objects with the same value do not necessarily have the same representation. For example, an implementation might represent False as zero and True as any odd value. Similarly, two objects (of the same type) with the same sequence of bits do not necessarily have the same value. For example, an implementation might use a biased representation in some cases but not others: <br />

<MarginText>7.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
subtype S is Integer range 1..256;{"\n"}type A is array(Natural range 1..4) of S{"\n"}   with Pack;{"\n"}X : S := 3;{"\n"}Y : A := (1, 2, 3, 4);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.d</MarginText>
The implementation might use a biased-by-1 representation for the array elements, but not for X. X and Y(3) have the same value, but different representation: the representation of X is a sequence of (say) 32 bits: 0...011, whereas the representation of Y(3) is a sequence of 8 bits: 00000010 (assuming a two's complement representation).<br />

<MarginText>7.e</MarginText>
Such tricks are not required, but are allowed. <br />

<MarginText>7.f</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The value of any padding bits is not specified by the language, though for a numeric type, it will be much harder to properly implement the predefined operations if the padding bits are not either all zero, or a sign extension. <br />

<MarginText>7.g/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, suppose S'Size = 2, and an object X is of subtype S. If the machine code typically uses a 32-bit load instruction to load the value of X, then X'Size should be 32, even though 30 bits of the value are just zeros or sign-extension bits. On the other hand, if the machine code typically masks out those 30 bits, then X'Size should be 2. Usually, such masking only happens for components of a composite type for which Pack, Component{"_"}Size, or record layout is specified.<br />

<MarginText>7.h</MarginText>
Note, however, that the formal parameter of an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Conversion is a special case. Its Size is required to be the same as that of its subtype.<br />

<MarginText>7.i</MarginText>
Note that we don't generally talk about the representation of a value. A value is considered to be an amorphous blob without any particular representation. An object is considered to be more concrete. <br />

<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0112-1", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0396-1", "AI12-0407-1"]} />
<p>A representation item <i>directly specifies</i> a <i>representation aspect</i> of the entity denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>, except in the case of a type-related representation item, whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> shall denote a first subtype, and which directly specifies an aspect of the subtype's type. A representation item that names a subtype is either <i>subtype-specific</i> (Size, Object{"_"}Size, and Alignment clauses) or <i>type-related</i> (all others).<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0407-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Some representation items directly specify more than one aspect. <br />

<MarginText>8.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For example, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Export (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.15#Subclause_J.15.5">J.15.5</a>) specifies the convention of an entity, and also specifies that it is exported. Such items are obsolescent; directly specifying the associated aspects is preferred. <br />

<MarginText>8.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Each specifiable attribute constitutes a separate aspect. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.4#S0350">enumeration_representation_clause</a></code> specifies the coding aspect. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code> (without the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8#S0369">mod_clause</a></code>) specifies the record layout aspect. Each representation pragma specifies a separate aspect. <br />

<MarginText>8.e</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We don't need to say that an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8#S0369">mod_clause</a></code> specify separate aspects, because these are equivalent to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>s. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7">J.7</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7">At Clauses</a>&rdquo;, and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8">J.8</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8">Mod Clauses</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>8.e.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0112-1"]} />
We give a default naming for representation aspects of representation pragmas so we don't have to do that for every pragma. Operational and representation attributes are given a default naming in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>. We don't want any anonymous aspects; that would make other rules more difficult to write and understand. <br />

<MarginText>8.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} An operational item <i>directly specifies</i> an <i>operational aspect</i> of the entity denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>, except in the case of a type-related operational item, whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> shall denote a first subtype, and which directly specifies an aspect of the type of the subtype. <br /></p>
