<MarginText>8.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0407-1"]} />
<p>Aspects that can be specified for types and subtypes are also classified into type-related or subtype-specific aspects. Representation aspects that can be specified for types and subtypes are considered type-related unless specified otherwise. In contrast, the classification of operational aspects are given with the definition of the aspect. Type-related aspects have the same value for all subtypes of (a view of) a type[, while subtype-specific aspects may differ for different subtypes of the same type].<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.tt/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We talk about &ldquo;type-related aspects&rdquo;, which of course include both type-related representation aspects and type-related operational aspects. Aspects Size, Object{"_"}Size, and Alignment are subtype-specific, as that is specified above. All other representation aspects are either type-related or not specifiable for a type or subtype. Unlike representation aspects, there is no default for operational aspects; whether they are type-related or subtype-specific should be part of the definition of the aspect. <br />

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0116-1", "AI12-0181-1", "AI12-0222-1"]} />
<p>A representation item or operational item that directly specifies an aspect of an entity shall appear before the entity is frozen (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.14">13.14</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI12-0222-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} The fact that a representation item (or operational item) that directly specifies an aspect of an entity is required to appear before the entity is frozen prevents changing the representation of an entity after using the entity in ways that require the representation to be known. <br />

<MarginText>9.b/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0116-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>9.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0116-1", "AI12-0222-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} A representation aspect of a subtype or type shall not be specified (whether by a representation item or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>) before the type is completely defined (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#Subclause_3.11.1">3.11.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.c/1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Unlike representation items, operational items can be specified on partial views. Since they don't affect the representation, the full declaration need not be known to determine their legality. <br />

<MarginText>9.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0116-1", "AI12-0396-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>If a representation item, operational item, library unit pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.15">J.15</a>), or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is given that directly specifies an aspect of an entity, then it is illegal to give another representation item, operational item, library unit pragma, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> that directly specifies the same aspect of the entity.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.c.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0116-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule applies to all aspects, not just those that have operational items or representation items. For instance, it applies to subtype predicates and type invariants. <br />

<MarginText>9.c.2/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0116-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>This rule is also intended to cover other ways to specify representation aspects, such as obsolescent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority. Priority is not a representation pragma, and as such is neither a representation item nor an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. Regardless, giving both a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority and an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> for Priority is illegal. We didn't want to complicate the wording solely to support obsolescent features. <br />

<MarginText>9.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0106-1", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0116-1", "AI12-0181-1"]} />
<p>Unless otherwise specified, it is illegal to specify an operational or representation aspect of a generic formal parameter. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0064-2"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Specifying an aspect on a generic formal parameter implies an added contract for a generic unit. That contract needs to be defined via generic parameter matching rules, and, as aspects vary widely, that has to be done for each such aspect. Since most aspects do not need this complexity, we avoid the complexity by saying that such contract-forming aspect specifications are banned unless the rules defining them explicitly exist. Note that the method of specification does not matter: <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s, representation items, and operational items are all covered by this rule. <br />

<MarginText>10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0109-1", "AI12-0376-1", "AI12-0427-1"]} />
<p>A <i>by-reference primitive</i> is a user-defined primitive subprogram for a type <i>T</i> that has an access result designating type <i>T</i>, or that has a formal parameter that is an access parameter designating type <i>T</i> or is aliased and of type <i>T</i>. It is illegal to specify a nonconfirming type-related representation aspect for an untagged type <i>T</i> if it is derived from a by-reference type or inherits one or more by-reference primitives, or if one or more types have been derived from <i>T</i> prior to the specification of the aspect and type <i>T</i> is a by-reference type or defines one or more by-reference primitives that are inherited by these descendants.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} On the other hand, subtype-specific representation aspects may be specified for the first subtype of such a type, as can operational aspects. <br />

<MarginText>10.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0109-1", "AI12-0376-1", "AI12-0427-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The reason for forbidding specification of type-related representation aspects on untagged by-reference types is because a change of representation is impossible when passing by reference (to an inherited subprogram). (A by-reference object cannot be copied to change its representation.) The reason for forbidding specification of type-related representation aspects on untagged types with by-reference primitives is that access parameters, access results, and aliased parameters cannot be converted as part of invoking an inherited subprogram if the representation of the designated types might be different. This rule is not needed for tagged types, because other rules prevent a type-related representation aspect from changing the representation of the parent part; we want to allow specifying a type-related representation aspect on a type extension to specify aspects of the extension part. For example, specifying aspect Pack will cause packing of the extension part, but not of the parent part. <br />

<MarginText>10.c/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0109-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>&ldquo;By-reference type&rdquo; usually cannot be used in Legality Rules, as it is privacy breaking. Our use here is privacy breaking, but we're stuck with it for compatibility reasons. Since representation aspects cannot be specified on partial views, privacy violations only can happen when a type includes a component of a private type. In that case, whether these rules are triggered depends on the full type of the private type &mdash; which is clearly privacy breaking. <br />

<MarginText>11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00117-01", "AI95-00137-01", "AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0396-1", "AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} {"{"}<i>8652/0011</i>{"}"} If a type-related aspect is defined for the partial view of a type, then it has the same definition for the full view of the type, except for certain Boolean-valued operational aspects where the language specifies that the partial view can have the value False even when the full view has the value True. Type-related aspects [cannot be specified, and] are not defined for an incomplete view of a type. Representation aspects of a generic formal parameter are the same as those of the actual. Specification of a type-related representation aspect is not allowed for a descendant of a generic formal untagged type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} Specifying representation aspects is allowed for types whose subcomponent types or index subtypes are generic formal types. Specifying operational aspects and subtype-related representation aspects is allowed on descendants of generic formal types. <br />

<MarginText>11.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Since it is not known whether a formal type has user-defined primitive subprograms, specifying type-related representation aspects for them is not allowed, unless they are tagged (in which case only the extension part is affected in any case). <br />

<MarginText>11.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>11.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0083-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Different views of an entity can have different representation and operational aspects. Most type-related aspects are the same for all views of a type; but specific aspects may have different rules. Similarly, different views of an object can have different representation aspects. For instance, an actual object passed by reference and the associated formal parameter may have different values for Alignment even though the formal parameter is merely a view of the actual object. This is necessary to maintain the language design principle that Alignments are always known at compile time. <br />

<MarginText>11.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For type-related aspects, the aspect of the partial view (if any) and full view have to be the same, with an exception for certain Boolean-valued aspects. The exception is intended for aspect Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization, where it would be wildly incompatible (as well as unfriendly) to require the (possibly implicit) state of the full view to be repeated explicitly on the partial view. Aspect Nonblocking has a similar rule for similar reasons, though it is a subtype-specific aspect. <br />

<MarginText>11.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The syntax of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#S0322">formal_incomplete_type_declaration</a></code>s do not allow for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> cannot name an incomplete type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>), so no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> can be used with an incomplete type. Similarly, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> of a representation pragma cannot name an incomplete type, so no such pragmas can be used with an incomplete type. <br />

<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<p>The specification of the Size aspect for a given subtype, or the size or storage place for an object (including a component) of a given subtype, shall allow for enough storage space to accommodate any value of the subtype.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0396-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} The specification of certain language-defined aspects is not required to be supported by all implementations; in such an implementation, the specification for such an aspect is illegal or raises an exception at run time.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is an Implementation Permission below that allows an implementation to put restrictions on any representation aspect; this rule applies if that permission is used for an aspect. This rule only applies to an operational aspect if the aspect explicitly allows the aspect to not be supported. <br />

<MarginText>13.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code> is illegal if it has one or more progenitors, and a nonconfirming value was specified for a representation aspect of an ancestor, and this conflicts with the representation of some other ancestor. The cases that cause conflicts are implementation defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.b/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The cases that cause conflicts between the representation of the ancestors of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>13.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule is needed because it may be the case that only the combination of types in a type declaration causes a conflict. Thus it is not possible, in general, to reject the original representation item or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. For instance: <br />

<MarginText>13.d/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Pkg1 is{"\n"}   type Ifc is interface;{"\n"}   type T is tagged record{"\n"}      Fld : Integer;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}   for T use record{"\n"}      Fld at 0 range 0 .. Integer'Size - 1;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}end Pkg1;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13.e/2</MarginText>
Assume the implementation uses a single tag with a default offset of zero, and that it allows the use of nondefault locations for the tag (and thus accepts representation items like the one above). The representation item will force a nondefault location for the tag (by putting a component other than the tag into the default location). Clearly, this package will be accepted by the implementation. However, other declarations could cause trouble. For instance, the implementation could reject: <br />

<MarginText>13.f/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Pkg1;{"\n"}package Pkg2 is{"\n"}   type NewT is new Pkg1.T and Pkg1.Ifc with null record;{"\n"}end Pkg2;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13.g/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
because the declarations of T and Ifc have a conflict in their representation items. This is clearly necessary (it's hard to imagine how Ifc'Class could work with the tag at a location other than the one it is expecting without introducing distributed overhead).<br />

<MarginText>13.h/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
Conflicts will usually involve implementation-defined attributes (for specifying the location of the tag, for instance), although the example above shows that doesn't have to be the case. For this reason, we didn't try to specify exactly what causes a conflict; it will depend on the implementation's implementation model and what representation aspects it allows to be changed. <br />

<MarginText>13.i/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>An implementation can only use this rule to reject <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>s where one of its ancestors had a nonconfirming representation value specified. An implementation must ensure that the default representations of ancestors cannot conflict. <br />

<MarginText>13.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0427-1"]} />
<p>When specifying an aspect that denotes a subprogram, the profile of the subprogram shall be mode conformant with the one required for the aspect, and the convention shall be Ada. Additional requirements are defined for particular aspects. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.j/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>As well as applying to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s, this rule applies to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>s for those aspects that have associated attributes.<br />

<MarginText>13.k/5</MarginText>
This rule implies, for example, that if one writes: <br />

<MarginText>13.l/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type T is ...{"\n"}   with Read ={">"} R;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13.m/5</MarginText>
R has to be a procedure with two parameters with the appropriate subtypes and modes as shown in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>14/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0059-1"]} />
<p>If two subtypes statically match, then their subtype-specific aspects (for example, Size and Alignment) are the same. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0059-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is necessary because we allow (for example) conversion between access types whose designated subtypes statically match. Note that most aspects (including the subtype-specific aspects Size and Alignment) may not be specified for a nonfirst subtype. The only language-defined exceptions to this rule are the Object{"_"}Size, Static{"_"}Predicate, and Dynamic{"_"}Predicate aspects.<br />

<MarginText>14.b</MarginText>
Consider, for example: <br />

<MarginText>14.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package P1 is{"\n"}   subtype S1 is Integer range 0..2{"*"}{"*"}16-1{"\n"}      with Size ={">"} 16; -- Illegal!{"\n"}      -- S1'Size would be 16 by default.{"\n"}   type A1 is access all S1;{"\n"}   X1: A1;{"\n"}end P1;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
package P2 is{"\n"}   subtype S2 is Integer range 0..2{"*"}{"*"}16-1{"\n"}      with Size ={">"} 32; -- Illegal!{"\n"}   type A2 is access all S2;{"\n"}   X2: A2;{"\n"}end P2;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
procedure Q is{"\n"}   use P1, P2;{"\n"}   type Array1 is array(Integer range {"<"}{">"}) of aliased S1{"\n"}      with Pack;{"\n"}   Obj1: Array1(1..100);{"\n"}   type Array2 is array(Integer range {"<"}{">"}) of aliased S2{"\n"}      with Pack;{"\n"}   Obj2: Array2(1..100);{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   X1 := Obj2(17)'Unchecked{"_"}Access;{"\n"}   X2 := Obj1(17)'Unchecked{"_"}Access;{"\n"}end Q;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14.f</MarginText>
Loads and stores through X1 would read and write 16 bits, but X1 points to a 32-bit location. Depending on the endianness of the machine, loads might load the wrong 16 bits. Stores would fail to zero the other half in any case.<br />

<MarginText>14.g</MarginText>
Loads and stores through X2 would read and write 32 bits, but X2 points to a 16-bit location. Thus, adjacent memory locations would be trashed.<br />

<MarginText>14.h</MarginText>
Hence, the above is illegal. Furthermore, the compiler is forbidden from choosing different Sizes by default, for the same reason.<br />

<MarginText>14.i/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0059-1"]} />
The same issues apply to Alignment. Similar issues apply to Object{"_"}Size, Static{"_"}Predicate, and Dynamic{"_"}Predicate, but the chosen solution is different: explicit rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9#Subclause_4.9.1">4.9.1</a> that ensure that the aspects are the same if specified.<br />

<MarginText>14.j/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0059-1"]} />
The above static matching rule combined with the definition of static matching in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9#Subclause_4.9.1">4.9.1</a> (after updating to add Object{"_"}Size) does not cause incompatibilities in existing Ada 2012 code that does not mention Object{"_"}Size. But it does constrain the implementation-defined value of Object{"_"}Size when it is not specified for a subtype; the above rule applies even in that case. (The effects noted in the example above would occur otherwise.)<br />

<MarginText>14.k/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0059-1"]} />
We need this rule even though static matching explicitly excludes confirming values of Object{"_"}Size. That's because a general access type can designate any aliased object whose subtype statically matches the designated subtype. Since the Object{"_"}Size of a subtype determines the number of bits allocated for an aliased object of the subtype, if we allowed different Object{"_"}Sizes for statically matching subtypes, we'd be allowing the access type to designate objects with differing numbers of bits. That isn't going to work. <br />

<MarginText>15/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00108-01", "AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0040</i>{"}"} A derived type inherits each type-related representation aspect of its parent type that was directly specified before the declaration of the derived type, or (in the case where the parent is derived) that was inherited by the parent type from the grandparent type. A derived subtype inherits each subtype-specific representation aspect of its parent subtype that was directly specified before the declaration of the derived type, or (in the case where the parent is derived) that was inherited by the parent subtype from the grandparent subtype, but only if the parent subtype statically matches the first subtype of the parent type. An inherited representation aspect is overridden by a subsequent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or representation item that specifies a different value for the same aspect of the type or subtype. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code> for a record extension does not override the layout of the parent part; if the layout was specified for the parent type, it is inherited by the record extension. <br />

<MarginText>15.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If a representation item for the parent appears after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived{"_"}type{"_"}definition</a></code>, then inheritance does not happen for that representation item.<br />

<MarginText>15.b.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
If an inherited aspect is confirmed by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or a later representation item for a derived type, the confirming specification does not override the inherited one. Thus the derived type has both a specified confirming value and an inherited nonconfirming representation value &mdash; this means that rules that apply only to nonconfirming representation values still apply to this type.<br />

<MarginText>15.b.2/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0109-1"]} />
If an aspect was specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> and the parent type has not yet been frozen, then the inherited aspect might not yet have been resolved and evaluated. The implementation will need to have a mechanism to handle such an aspect. <br />

<MarginText>15.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00108-01", "AI95-00444-01", "AI05-0183-1", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0040</i>{"}"} In contrast, whether type-related operational aspects are inherited by a derived type depends on each specific aspect; unless specified, an operational aspect is not inherited. When type-related operational aspects are inherited by a derived type, aspects that were directly specified by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s or operational items that are visible at any point within the immediate scope of the derived type declaration, or (in the case where the parent is derived) that were inherited by the parent type from the grandparent type, are inherited. An inherited operational aspect is overridden by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or operational item that specifies the same aspect of the type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.b.3/1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>As with representation items, if an operational item for the parent appears after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived{"_"}type{"_"}definition</a></code>, then inheritance does not happen for that operational item.<br />

<MarginText>15.b.4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
Unlike representation aspects, operational aspects can be inherited at any point in the immediate scope, and can be overridden by aspect{"_"}specifications or operational items that occur at a point before or after the inheritance takes place. <br />

<MarginText>15.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>When a type-related operational aspect is inherited, the rules for inheritance depend on the nature of the aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>). Unless otherwise specified for a given aspect, these rules are as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.3/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For an operational aspect that is a value, the inherited aspect has the same value;<br /></li>
<MarginText>15.4/5</MarginText>
<li>For an operational aspect that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>:<br /></li>
<MarginText>15.5/5</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes one or more primitive subprograms of the type, the inherited aspect is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes the corresponding primitive subprogram(s) of the derived type;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.b.6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A primitive subprogram that is declared after the end of the enclosing declaration list of a derived type (in particular, in the private part of a package if the derived type is declared in the package's visible part) is not the &ldquo;corresponding primitive subprogram&rdquo; in the sense of this rule. In a case like this, the corresponding primitive subprogram is actually the inherited subprogram. This doesn't make a difference for tagged types, because of the &ldquo;dispatching&rdquo; semantics used, which means a call on the inherited subprogram actually &ldquo;reaches&rdquo; the body of the overriding. But for untagged types, overriding an inherited subprogram of an untagged derived type in the private part is &ldquo;too late&rdquo; to have an effect on external uses of the primitive, since non-visible overridings are not generally reachable, and a call that only &ldquo;sees&rdquo; the inherited subprogram goes to the body of the parent's operation, effectively ignoring the private overriding. This same rule applies to aspects that denote an inherited subprogram of an untagged derived type &mdash; the private overriding is effectively ignored. <br />

<MarginText>15.6/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>otherwise, the inherited aspect is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes the same entity or entities as the original aspect; <br /></li>
<MarginText>15.7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1", "AI12-0423-1"]} />
<li>For an operational aspect that is an identifier specific to the aspect, the inherited aspect is the same identifier;<br /></li>
<MarginText>15.8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1", "AI12-0423-1"]} />
<li>For an operational aspect that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, the inherited aspect is a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> where each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, value, and identifier follows these same rules for inheritance.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<p>Each aspect of representation of an entity is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the aspect is <i>specified</i> for the entity, meaning that it is either directly specified or inherited, then that aspect of the entity is as specified, except in the case of Storage{"_"}Size, which specifies a minimum. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule implies that queries of the aspect return the specified value. For example, if the user writes &ldquo;<b>for</b> X'Size <b>use</b> 32;&rdquo;, then a query of X'Size will return 32. <br />

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If an aspect of representation of an entity is not specified, it is chosen by default in an unspecified manner. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} Note that specifying a representation aspect can affect the semantics of the entity.<br />

<MarginText>18.b</MarginText>
The rules forbid things like &ldquo;<b>for</b> S'Base'Alignment <b>use</b> ...&rdquo; and &ldquo;<b>for</b> S'Base <b>use</b> record ...&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>18.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The intent is that implementations will represent the components of a composite value in the same way for all subtypes of a given composite type. Hence, Component{"_"}Size and record layout are type-related aspects. <br />

<MarginText>18.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0083-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>As noted previously, in the case of an object, the entity mentioned in this text is a specific view of an object. That means that only references to the same view of an object that has a specified value for a representation aspect <i>R</i> necessarily have that value for the aspect <i>R</i>. The value of the aspect <i>R</i> for a different view of that object is unspecified. In particular, this means that the representation values for by-reference parameters is unspecified; they do not have to be the same as those of the underlying object. <br />

<MarginText>18.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00108-01", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0040</i>{"}"} If an operational aspect is <i>specified</i> for an entity (meaning that it is either directly specified or, if type-related or subtype-specific, inherited), then that aspect of the entity is as specified. Otherwise, the aspect of the entity has the default value for that aspect.[ For aspects that are neither type-related nor subtype-specific, the terms &ldquo;specified&rdquo; and &ldquo;directly specified&rdquo; are equivalent.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Aspect inheritance is only defined for types and subtypes. <br />

<MarginText>18.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or representation item that specifies a representation aspect that would have been chosen in the absence of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or representation item is said to be <i>confirming</i>. The aspect value specified in this case is said to be a <i>confirming</i> representation aspect value. Other values of the aspect are said to be <i>nonconfirming</i>, as are the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s and representation items that specified them. Similarly, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or operational item that specifies an operational aspect to be the same as the definition it would have by default is said to be <i>confirming</i>; otherwise it is <i>nonconfirming</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>As noted at the beginning of this subclause, we have a Language Design Principle that confirming aspects do not change the semantics. However, it is not a Language Design Principle principle that one can always specify a confirming aspect. Some aspects can never be confirmed. For instance, the default implementation of a stream-oriented attribute cannot be confirmed, as any subprogram that can be specified is not the same as the default subprogram, and thus is nonconfirming. Whether the effect is the same is not relevant for this purpose; it would be very difficult to formally define what it means to have the same effect. (Note that one can name any implementation for a stream-oriented attribute by using the associated attribute but specifying that by name would violate the circular aspect definition rule.) This is true for any implicitly composed aspect. Similarly, aspect Default{"_"}Value cannot be confirmed as the default is that there is no default value; any value that can be specified is not that. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>19/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} For the elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code>, any evaluable constructs within it are evaluated. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Elaboration of representation pragmas is covered by the general rules for pragmas in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8">2.8</a>. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>20/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may interpret representation aspects in an implementation-defined manner. An implementation may place implementation-defined restrictions on the specification of representation aspects. A <i>recommended level of support</i> is defined for the specification of representation aspects and related features in each subclause. These recommendations are changed to requirements for implementations that support the Systems Programming Annex (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.2">C.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.2">Required Representation Support</a>&rdquo;).<br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The interpretation of each representation aspect.<br />

<MarginText>20.b/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Any restrictions placed upon the specification of representation aspects.<br />

<MarginText>20.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Implementation-defined restrictions may be enforced either at compile time or at run time. There is no requirement that an implementation justify any such restrictions. They can be based on avoiding implementation complexity, or on avoiding excessive inefficiency, for example.<br />

<MarginText>20.c.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} There is no such permission for operational aspects. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>21/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<p>The recommended level of support for the specification of all representation aspects is qualified as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A confirming specification for a representation aspect should be supported. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>A confirming representation aspect value might not be possible for some entities. For instance, consider an unconstrained array. The size of such a type is implementation-defined, and might not actually be a representable value, or might not be static. <br />

<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>An implementation is not required to support the specification for a representation aspect that contains nonstatic expressions, unless each nonstatic expression is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that statically denotes a constant declared before the entity. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>22.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is to avoid the following sort of thing: <br />

<MarginText>22.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X : Integer := F(...){"\n"}   with Address ={">"} Y;{"\n"}Y : Address := G(...);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>22.c</MarginText>
In the above, we have to evaluate the initialization expression for X before we know where to put the result. This seems like an unreasonable implementation burden.<br />

<MarginText>22.d</MarginText>
The above code should instead be written like this: <br />

<MarginText>22.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Y : constant Address := G(...);{"\n"}X : Integer := F(...){"\n"}   with Address ={">"} Y;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>22.f</MarginText>
This allows the expression &ldquo;Y&rdquo; to be safely evaluated before X is created.<br />

<MarginText>22.g</MarginText>
The constant could be a formal parameter of mode <b>in</b>.<br />

<MarginText>22.h</MarginText>
An implementation can support other nonstatic expressions if it wants to. Expressions of type Address are hardly ever static, but their value might be known at compile time anyway in many cases. <br />

<MarginText>23/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0059-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>An implementation is not required to support a specification for the Object{"_"}Size or Size for a given composite subtype, nor the size or storage place for an object (including a component) of a given composite subtype, unless the constraints on the subtype and its composite subcomponents (if any) are all static constraints.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0059-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We don't want to require that Object{"_"}Size or Size be supported on types that might have a representation not completely specified at compile time, or are represented discontiguously, or are represented differently for different constraints. <br />

<MarginText>24/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>An implementation is not required to support specifying a nonconfirming representation aspect value if it can cause an aliased object or an object of a by-reference type to be allocated at a nonaddressable location or, when the alignment attribute of the subtype of such an object is nonzero, at an address that is not an integral multiple of that alignment. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.a/1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The intent is that access types, type System.Address, and the pointer used for a by-reference parameter should be implementable as a single machine address &mdash; bit-field pointers should not be required. (There is no requirement that this implementation be used &mdash; we just want to make sure it's feasible.) <br />

<MarginText>24.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>We want subprograms to be able to assume the properties of the types of their parameters inside of subprograms. While many objects can be copied to allow this (and thus do not need limitations), aliased or by-reference objects cannot be copied (their memory location is part of their identity). Thus, the above rule does not apply to types that merely allow by-reference parameter passing; for such types, a copy typically needs to be made at the call site when a bit-aligned component is passed as a parameter. <br />

<MarginText>25/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>An implementation is not required to support specifying a nonconfirming representation aspect value if it can cause an aliased object of an elementary type to have a size other than that which would have been chosen by default. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>25.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Since all bits of elementary objects participate in operations, aliased objects must not have a different size than that assumed by users of the access type. <br />

<MarginText>26/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>An implementation is not required to support specifying a nonconfirming representation aspect value if it can cause an aliased object of a composite type, or an object whose type is by-reference, to have a size smaller than that which would have been chosen by default. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>26.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Unlike elementary objects, there is no requirement that all bits of a composite object participate in operations. Thus, as long as the object is the same or larger in size than that expected by the access type, all is well. <br />

<MarginText>26.b/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule presumes that the implementation allocates an object of a size specified to be larger than the default size in such a way that access of the default size suffices to correctly read and write the value of the object. <br />

<MarginText>27/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>An implementation is not required to support specifying a nonconfirming subtype-specific representation aspect value for an indefinite or abstract subtype. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>27.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Representation aspects are often not well-defined for such types. <br />

<MarginText>27.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A type with the Pack aspect specified will typically not be packed so tightly as to disobey the above rules. A Component{"_"}Size clause or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code> will typically be illegal if it disobeys the above rules. Atomic components have similar restrictions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">Shared Variable Control</a>&rdquo;). <br />

<MarginText>28/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02", "AI05-0295-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>For purposes of these rules, the determination of whether specifying a representation aspect value for a type <i>can cause</i> an object to have some property is based solely on the properties of the type itself, not on any available information about how the type is used. In particular, it presumes that minimally aligned objects of this type can be declared at some point. <br /></p>

<MarginText>28.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The recommended level of support for all representation items should be followed.<br />

<MarginText>29/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
NOTE   Aspects that can be specified are defined throughout this document, and are summarized in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-K/AA-K.1">K.1</a>. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>29.a</MarginText>
It is now illegal for a representation item to cause a derived by-reference type to have a different record layout from its parent. This is necessary for by-reference parameter passing to be feasible. This only affects programs that specify the representation of types derived from types containing tasks; most by-reference types are new to Ada 95. For example, if A1 is an array of tasks, and A2 is derived from A1, it is illegal to apply a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Pack to A2. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>29.b/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} Ada 95 allows additional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code>s for objects. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>29.c/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} The syntax rule for <code>type{"_"}representation{"_"}clause</code> is removed; the right-hand side of that rule is moved up to where it was used, in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code>. There are two references to &ldquo;type representation clause&rdquo; in RM83, both in Section 13; these have been reworded. Also, the <code>representation{"_"}clause</code> has been renamed the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code> to reflect that it can be used to control more than just representation aspects.<br />

<MarginText>29.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01", "AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} We have defined a new term &ldquo;representation item&rdquo;, which includes all representation clauses and representation pragmas, as well as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0353">component_clause</a></code>s. This is convenient because the rules are almost identical for all of them. We have also defined the new terms &ldquo;operational item&rdquo; and &ldquo;operational aspects&rdquo; in order to conveniently handle new types of specifiable entities.<br />

<MarginText>29.e</MarginText>
All of the forcing occurrence stuff has been moved into its own subclause (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.14">13.14</a>), and rewritten to use the term &ldquo;freezing&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>29.f</MarginText>
RM83-13.1(10) requires implementation-defined restrictions on representation items to be enforced at compile time. However, that is impossible in some cases. If the user specifies a junk (nonstatic) address in an address clause, and the implementation chooses to detect the error (for example, using hardware memory management with protected pages), then it's clearly going to be a run-time error. It seems silly to call that &ldquo;semantics&rdquo; rather than &ldquo;a restriction&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>29.g</MarginText>
RM83-13.1(10) tries to pretend that <code>representation{"_"}clause</code>s don't affect the semantics of the program. One counter-example is the Small clause. Ada 95 has more counter-examples. We have noted the opposite above.<br />

<MarginText>29.h</MarginText>
Some of the more stringent requirements are moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.2">C.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.2">Required Representation Support</a>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>29.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> Confirming representation items are defined, and the recommended level of support is now that they always be supported. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>29.j/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added operational items in order to eliminate unnecessary restrictions and permissions on stream attributes. As part of this, <code>representation{"_"}clause</code> was renamed to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>29.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI95-00326-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added wording to say that the partial and full views have the same operational and representation aspects. Ada 2005 extends this to cover all views, including the incomplete view.<br />

<MarginText>29.l/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00108-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0040</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Changed operational items to have inheritance specified for each such aspect.<br />

<MarginText>29.m/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Added wording to allow the rejection of types with progenitors that have conflicting representation items.<br />

<MarginText>29.n/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00291-02"]} />
The description of the representation of an object was clarified (with great difficulty reaching agreement). Added wording to say that representation items on aliased and by-reference objects never need be supported if they would not be implementable without distributed overhead even if other recommended level of support says otherwise. This wording matches the rules with reality.<br />

<MarginText>29.o/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00444-01", "AI05-0005-1"]} />
Added wording so that inheritance depends on whether operational items are visible rather than whether they occur before the declaration (we don't want to look into private parts). Also limited operational inheritance to untagged types to avoid anomalies with private extensions (this is not incompatible, no existing operational attribute used this capability). Also added wording to clearly define that subprogram inheritance works like derivation of subprograms. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>29.p/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0106-1", "AI12-0064-2", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Specifying a language-defined aspect for a generic formal parameter is no longer allowed. Most aspects could not be specified on these anyway; moreover, this was not allowed in Ada 83, so it is unlikely that compilers are supporting this as a capability (and it is not likely that they have a consistent definition of what it means if it is allowed). Thus, we expect this to occur rarely in existing programs. Note: This correction is repealed in Ada 2022, as a number of aspects are allowed on formals in that later language version. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>29.q/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined that overriding of a representation aspect only happens for a nonconfirming representation item. This prevents a derived type from being considered to have only a confirming representation item when the value would be nonconfirming if given on a type that does not inherit any aspects of representation. This change just eliminates a wording confusion and ought not change any behavior.<br />

<MarginText>29.r/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined a default naming for representation aspects that are representation pragmas.<br />

<MarginText>29.s/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
Added text ensuring that the rules for representational and operational items also apply appropriately to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s; generalized operational aspects so that they can be defined for entities other than types. Any extensions are documented elsewhere.<br />

<MarginText>29.t/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
Rewrote many rules to be in terms of "specifying a representation aspect" rather than use of a "representation item". This better separates <i>how</i> an aspect is specified from <i>what</i> rules apply to the value of the aspect. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>29.u/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0109-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a rule that makes it illegal to specify a representation value after a type is derived from an untagged by-reference type. This restriction is incompatible, but since the implementation would have had to copy an object that does not allow copying in order to change the representation for any implicit or explicit conversion between the original and the derived type, it is unlikely that any program could exist without running into internal compiler errors or bogus results.<br />

<MarginText>29.v/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0181-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a rule preventing self-referencing representation or operational aspects. This is technically incompatible, but since the similar representation or operational item has been illegal since they've existed, and they don't make any sense, it's unlikely that any implementation accepted them or that they appear in any program.<br />

<MarginText>29.w/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0222-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a rule preventing giving a representation aspect on a partial view. Since this has always been prohibited for other kinds of representation items, it's unlikely that any implementation accepted them or that they appear in any program. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>29.x/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0376-1"]} />
It is now allowed to specify type-related representation aspects for an untagged derived type that has primitive operations, so long as the type is not a by-reference type. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>29.y/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0116-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that an aspect (any aspect) can be specified only once for an entity, no matter what means of specifying it are used.<br />

<MarginText>29.z/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0059-1"]} />
Added wording changes to support Object{"_"}Size.<br />

<MarginText>29.aa/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified that many of these rules only make sense for type-related aspects.<br />

<MarginText>29.bb/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1", "AI12-0419-1", "AI12-0423-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified how inheritance works for operational aspects that are not values.<br />

<MarginText>29.cc/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0427-1"]} />
Move the general requirements for aspects that are subprograms here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>. <br />

<a id="Subclause_13.1.1"></a>

## 13.1.1  Aspect Specifications

<MarginText>1/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>[Certain representation or operational aspects of an entity may be specified as part of its declaration using an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, rather than using a separate representation or operational item.] The declaration with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is termed the <i>associated declaration</i>. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>aspect{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0346"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>with</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> [={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code>] {"{"},<br />           <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> [={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code>] {"}"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>aspect{"_"}mark</code><a id="S0347"></a><code> ::= </code><i>aspect{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>['Class]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0187-1", "AI12-0285-1", "AI12-0373-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>aspect{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0348"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0209">global_aspect_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>4.a/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI05-0267-1"]} />
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is an optional element in most kinds of declarations. Here is a list of all kinds of declarations and an indication of whether or not they allow aspect clauses, and in some cases a short discussion of why ({"*"} = allowed, NO = not allowed). Kinds of declarations with no indication are followed by their subdivisions (which have indications).<br />

<MarginText>4.b/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0061-1", "AI12-0079-3", "AI12-0395-1", "AI12-0398-1"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0021">basic_declaration</a></code><br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code><br />    <code><a sense to allow specifying them.<br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#S0232">private_type_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />    <code><a aspects that may be specified<br />    -- on renames, but implementations might support some.<br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />  <code><a
