href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0039">enumeration_literal_specification</a></code>  --  NO<br />    -- The syntax would be ambiguous if this was supported directly.<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code>{"*"}<br />    -- There are no language-defined aspects that may be specified<br />    -- on discriminants, but implementations might support some.<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>  --  NO<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>  -- NO - the enclosing construct has an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code><br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>  --  NO<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0186">iterator_parameter_specification</a></code>  -- NO<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter_specification</a></code>{"*"}<br />    -- There are no language-defined aspects that may be specified<br />    -- on parameters, but implementations might support some.<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>{"*"}  --   - but language-defined aspects only if there is no explicit specification<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry_index_specification</a></code>{"*"}<br />    -- There are no language-defined aspects that may be specified<br />    -- on an entry index, but implementations might support some.<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0298">subprogram_body_stub</a></code>{"*"}  --   - but language-defined aspects only if there is no explicit specification<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice_parameter_specification</a></code>  --  NO<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0314">generic_formal_parameter_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.4#S0319">formal_object_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#S0320">formal_type_declaration</a></code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#S0321">formal_complete_type_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#S0322">formal_incomplete_type_declaration</a></code>  --  NO  - see <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code> above<br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0336">formal_concrete_subprogram_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0337">formal_abstract_subprogram_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0340">formal_package_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code>{"*"}<br />    -- There are no language-defined aspects that may be specified<br />    -- on return objects, but implementations might support some.</i><br />

<MarginText>4.c/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0169-1"]} />
-- <i>We also allow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s on all kinds of bodies, but there are no language-defined aspects</i><br />-- <i>that may be specified on a body. These are allowed for implementation-defined aspects.</i><br />-- <i>See above for subprogram bodies and stubs (as these can be declarations).</i><br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0299">package_body_stub</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0300">task_body_stub</a></code>{"*"}<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0301">protected_body_stub</a></code>{"*"}<br />

<MarginText>4.d/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0267-1"]} />
Syntactically, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s generally are located at the end of declarations. When a declaration is all in one piece such as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code> the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> goes at the end of the declaration; it is then more visible and less likely to interfere with the layout of the rest of the structure. However, we make an exception for program units (other than subprogram specifications) and bodies, in which the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> goes before the <b>is</b>. In these cases, the entity could be large and could contain other declarations that also have <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s, so it is better to put the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> toward the top of the declaration. (Some aspects &ndash; such as Pure &ndash; also affect the legality of the contents of a unit, so it would be annoying to only see those after reading the entire unit.)<br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> identifies an aspect of the entity defined by the associated declaration (the <i>associated entity</i>); the aspect denotes an object, a value, an expression, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, a subprogram, or some other kind of entity. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> identifies: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>an aspect that denotes an object, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is the type of the identified aspect of the associated entity; <br /></li>
<MarginText>7/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<li>an aspect that is a value or an expression, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is the type of the identified aspect of the associated entity;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.1/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<li>an aspect that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, the aspect definition shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, with the form of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> determined by the identified aspect;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The only requirement here is that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is syntactically an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>; there is no requirement that it resolve to some particular type or even that it should resolve like an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>. Each aspect that uses an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is responsible for specifying how the choice(s), component(s), and other contents of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> are resolved and interpreted. <br />

<MarginText>8/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>an aspect that denotes a subprogram, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>; the expected profile for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is the profile required for the aspect of the associated entity;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<li>an aspect that denotes some other kind of entity, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, and the name shall resolve to denote an entity of the appropriate kind;<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<li>an aspect that is given by an identifier specific to the aspect, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall be one of the identifiers specific to the identified aspect. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0373-1", "AI12-0427-1"]} />
<p>The usage names in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> associated with a declaration [ are not resolved at the point of the associated declaration, but rather] are resolved at the end of the immediately enclosing declaration list, or in the case of the declaration of a library unit, at the end of the visible part of the entity.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is not associated with a declaration (instead being part of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>), then it is resolved when the associated construct is resolved. <br />

<MarginText>12/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0180-1", "AI12-0220-1"]} />
<p>If the associated declaration is for a subprogram, entry,  or access-to-subprogram type, the names of the formal parameters are directly visible within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code>, as are certain attributes, as specified elsewhere in this document for the identified aspect. If the associated declaration is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>, within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> the names of any visible components, protected subprograms, and entries are directly visible, and the name of the first subtype denotes the current instance of the type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>). If the associated declaration is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0026">subtype_declaration</a></code>, within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> the name of the new subtype denotes the current instance of the subtype. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>13/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>If the first freezing point of the associated entity comes before the end of the immediately enclosing declaration list, then each usage name in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall resolve to the same entity at the first freezing point as it does at the end of the immediately enclosing declaration list.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.1/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0181-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that causes freezing of an entity shall not occur within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> that specifies a representation or operational aspect of that entity.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0181-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The rule prevents an aspect of an entity from depending (directly or indirectly) on properties of the entity itself. <br />

<MarginText>13.b/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This check needs to be deferred at least to the freezing of the entity (as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> is not resolved until then), and might be accomplished during the freezing of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> (since it is closely related). Keep in mind that multiple other entities could be involved. <br />

<MarginText>14/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>At most one occurrence of each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> is allowed within a single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. The aspect identified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> shall be an aspect that can be specified for the associated entity (or view of the entity defined by the associated declaration).<br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0116-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule prevents multiple specifications in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. Rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a> prevent multiple specifications in different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s (on different views of the same type, for instance), or between operational or representation items and an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>15/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> associated with a given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> may be omitted only when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> identifies an aspect of a boolean type, in which case it is equivalent to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> being specified as True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> includes 'Class, then the associated entity shall be a tagged type or a primitive subprogram of a tagged type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI05-0267-1", "AI12-0064-2", "AI12-0194-1", "AI12-0380-1", "AI12-0407-1"]} />
<p>Unless otherwise specified for a specific aspect, a language-defined aspect cannot be specified on a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0314">generic_formal_parameter_declaration</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0064-2"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Implementation-defined aspects can be allowed on these, of course; the implementation will need to define the semantics. In addition, the language does not define default aspect matching rules for generic formals; only the handful of aspects allowed on formals have such rules. Therefore, the implementation will need to define actual type matching rules for any aspects allowed on formal types. <br />

<MarginText>18/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI05-0267-1", "AI12-0105-1", "AI12-0380-1"]} />
<p>Unless specified otherwise, a language-defined aspect shall not be specified in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> given on a completion of a program unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Most language-defined aspects (for example, preconditions) are intended to be available to callers, and specifying them on a body that has a separate declaration hides them from callers. Specific language-defined aspects may allow this, but they have to do so explicitly (by defining an alternative Legality Rule), and provide any needed rules about visibility. Note that this rule does not apply to implementation-defined aspects, so implementers need to carefully define whether such aspects can be applied to bodies and stubs, and what happens if they are specified on both the declaration and body of a unit. <br />

<MarginText>18.1/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0138-1"]} />
<p>If an aspect of a derived type is inherited from an ancestor type and has the boolean value True, the inherited value shall not be overridden to have the value False for the derived type, unless otherwise specified in this document.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.b/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Most boolean-valued language-defined aspects are associated with a representation pragma. The existing rules for such pragmas assume that the aspect cannot be removed. For instance, if a type <i>T</i> is declared to be Atomic, then all descendants of <i>T</i> are also Atomic. This rule ensures that remains the case when using the aspect notation instead of pragmas. <br />

<MarginText>18.b.1/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This definition leaves holes for Boolean aspects that can be specified on non-first subtypes. Such aspects (for instance, Nonblocking) must have their own rules (that is, "otherwise specify" rules) that define the effects of inheriting from subtypes (both first subtypes and nonfirst subtypes). <br />

<MarginText>18.2/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>If a given aspect is type-related and inherited, then within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> for the aspect, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> resolves to denote multiple visible subprograms, all or none of the denoted subprograms shall be primitives of the associated type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.b.2/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is necessary because the inheritance rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s denoting primitive subprograms are different from those for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s denoting other entities &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>18.3/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0138-1", "AI12-0206-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
<p>Certain type-related aspects are defined to be <i>nonoverridable</i>; all such aspects are inherited by derived types according to the rules given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>. Any legality rule associated with a nonoverridable aspect is re-checked for the derived type, if the derived type is not abstract. Certain type-related and subtype-specific aspects are defined to be <i>additive</i>; such aspects are not inherited, but they can <i>apply</i> to the types derived from, or the subtypes based on, the original type or subtype, as defined for each such aspect. Finally, certain type-related aspects are <i>implicitly composed</i>; such aspects are not inherited, but rather a default implementation for a derived type is provided, as defined for each such aspect, based on that of its parent type, presuming the aspect for the parent type is available where the derived type is declared, plus those of any new components added as part of a type extension.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.4/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0138-1", "AI12-0206-1", "AI12-0211-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>If a nonoverridable aspect is directly specified for a type <i>T</i>, then any explicit specification of that aspect for any descendant of <i>T</i> (other than <i>T</i> itself) shall be <i>confirming</i>. In the case of an aspect that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, this means that the specified <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall <i>match</i> the inherited aspect in the sense that it shall denote the same declarations as would the inherited <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. Similarly, for an aspect that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, confirming means the defining <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is fully conformant (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>) with the defining <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> for the inherited aspect, with the added rule that an identifier that is specific to the aspect is the same as the corresponding identifier in the inherited aspect.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.5/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0138-1", "AI12-0396-1"]} />
<p>If a full type has a partial view, and a given nonoverridable aspect is allowed for both the full view and the partial view, then the given aspect for the partial view and the full view shall be the same: the aspect shall be directly specified only on the partial view; if the full type inherits the aspect, then a matching definition shall be specified (directly or by inheritance) for the partial view.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.c/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In order to enforce these rules without breaking privacy, we cannot allow a private type that could have a particular overridable aspect to have a hidden definition of that aspect. There is no problem if the private type does not allow the aspect (as the aspect could not be specified on descendants in that case). <br />

<MarginText>18.6/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0211-1"]} />
<p>If a type inherits a nonoverridable aspect from multiple ancestors, the value of the aspect inherited from any given ancestor shall be confirming of the values inherited from all other ancestors.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.d/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0211-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>If more than one progenitor of a type <i>T</i> specifies a nonoverridable aspect, they all have to specify the same or matching values for that aspect. Otherwise, we'd have two different values for the aspect that depend on which progenitor we inherit from. <br />

<MarginText>18.7/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0138-1", "AI12-0211-1"]} />
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules about nonoverridable aspects also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.e/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We don't need an assume-the-worst rule for most nonoverridable aspects as they only work on tagged types and deriving from formal tagged types is not allowed in generic bodies. In the case of Implicit{"_"}Dereference, a derivation in a generic body does not cause problems (the ancestor necessarily cannot have the aspect, else specifying the aspect would be illegal), as there could be no place with visibility on both aspects. In the case of Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length, it is only allowed on task and protected types, and on entries, and there are not formal versions of any of those things. In the case of No{"_"}Controlled{"_"}Parts, we defined an assume-the-worst rule with the aspect.<br />

<MarginText>18.f/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0437-1"]} />
A list of all nonoverridable aspects can be found in the index, under &ldquo;nonoverridable aspect&rdquo;. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>19/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>Depending on which aspect is identified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code>, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> specifies: <br /></p>

<MarginText>20/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a subprogram, object, or other kind of entity;<br /></li>
<MarginText>21/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0427-1"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (other than an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>), which is either evaluated to produce a single value, or which (as in a precondition) is to be evaluated at particular points during later execution;<br /></li>
<MarginText>22/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0427-1"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> specific to the aspect; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>22.1/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0427-1"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, which is positional or named, and is composed of elements of any of these four kinds of constructs. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>The identified aspect of the associated entity, or in some cases, the view of the entity defined by the declaration, is as specified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> (or by the default of True when boolean). Whether an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> <i>applies</i> to an entity or only to the particular view of the entity defined by the declaration is determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> and the kind of entity. The following aspects are view specific:<br /></p>

<MarginText>24/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>An aspect specified on an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>25/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<li>An aspect specified on a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>26/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<li>An aspect specified on a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code>.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>27/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>All other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s are associated with the entity, and <i>apply</i> to all views of the entity, unless otherwise specified in this document.<br /></p>

<MarginText>28/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0106-1"]} />
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> includes 'Class (a <i>class-wide aspect</i>), then, unless specified otherwise for a particular class-wide aspect: <br /></p>

<MarginText>29/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>if the associated entity is a tagged type, the specification <i>applies</i> to all descendants of the type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>30/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<li>if the associated entity is a primitive subprogram of a tagged type <i>T</i>, the specification <i>applies</i> to the corresponding primitive subprogram of all descendants of <i>T</i>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>31/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>All specifiable operational and representation attributes may be specified with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> instead of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>31.a/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The name of the aspect is the same as that of the attribute (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>), so the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code> of the attribute.<br />

<MarginText>31.b/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
Unless specified otherwise, all of the requirements for specifying a particular aspect with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> also apply to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> for the aspect. These are enforced at the freezing point of the entity. For example, when specifying the Size aspect of a subtype, the expression has to be a static expression with an integer type and a nonnegative value, all of the recommended level of support requirements apply if <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/">Annex C</a> is supported (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.2">C.2</a>), and so on. <br />

<MarginText>32/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0154-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>Some aspects are defined to be <i>library unit aspects</i>. Library unit aspects are of type Boolean. The expression specifying a library unit aspect shall be static. Library unit aspects are defined for all program units, but shall be specified only for library units. Notwithstanding what this document says elsewhere, the expression of a library unit aspect is resolved and evaluated at the point where it occurs in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>[, rather than the first freezing point of the associated unit].<br /></p>

<MarginText>32.a/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The name of the aspect is the same as that of the pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>), so the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code> is the name of the pragma. <br />

<MarginText>33/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>In addition, other operational and representation aspects not associated with specifiable attributes or representation pragmas may be specified, as specified elsewhere in this document.<br /></p>

<MarginText>34/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0138-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>35/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>If a Legality Rule or Static Semantics rule only applies when a particular aspect has been specified, the aspect is considered to have been specified only when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> is visible (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3">8.3</a>) at the point of the application of the rule.<br /></p>

<MarginText>35.a/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Some rules only apply when an aspect has been specified (for instance, an indexable type is one that has aspect Variable{"_"}Indexing specified). In order to prevent privacy breaking, this can only be true when the specification of the aspect is visible. In particular, if the Variable{"_"}Indexing aspect is specified on the full view of a private type, the private type is not considered an indexable type. <br />

<MarginText>36/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>Alternative legality and semantics rules may apply for particular aspects, as specified elsewhere in this document.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>37/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0355-2"]} />
<p>At the freezing point of the associated entity, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is elaborated. When appearing in a construct other than a declaration, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is elaborated as part of the execution of the construct. The elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> consists of the elaboration of each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> in an arbitrary order. The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> includes the evaluation of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that is part of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> unless the part is itself an expression. If the corresponding aspect (or part thereof) represents an expression (as in a precondition), the elaboration of that part has no effect; the expression is evaluated later at points within the execution as specified elsewhere in this document for the particular aspect. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>38/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>Implementations may support implementation-defined aspects. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> for an implementation-defined aspect may use an implementation-defined syntax for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code>, and may follow implementation-defined legality and semantics rules. <br /></p>

<MarginText>38.a/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0389-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The intent is to allow implementations to support aspects that are defined, for example, by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> rather than an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. We chose not to try to enumerate all possible <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> syntaxes, but to give implementations maximum freedom. <br />

<MarginText>38.a.1/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined aspects, including the syntax for specifying such aspects and the legality rules for such aspects.<br />

<MarginText>39/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0389-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may ignore the specification of an unrecognized aspect; if an implementation chooses to ignore such an aspect specification (as opposed to rejecting it), then it has no effect on the semantics of the program except for possibly (and this is not required) the rejection of syntax errors within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>39.a/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0389-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Identifying the textual end of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> for an unrecognized aspect may be challenging, particularly if the syntax for the unrecognized aspect's <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> is implementation-defined. It is not specified how an implementation might accomplish this. Note that an implementation is never <i>required</i> to be able to do this; if an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> for an unrecognized aspect is problematic in any way, then it can always be rejected (as opposed to being ignored). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>39.b/3_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1", "AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0267-1"]} />
Aspect specifications are new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>39.c/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0180-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Names of protected subprograms and entries are now directly visible in an aspect of a type declaration. This was always intended to be the case, but it was omitted from the Reference Manual by an editing error. In the unlikely case that a parameterless protected function has the same name and type as an entity used in a type invariant expression, the meaning would change from the outside entity which would now be hidden by the protected function. It is much more likely that a conflict (itself rather unlikely) would cause a resolution failure. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>39.d/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0154-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a clarification that aspects that correspond to library unit pragmas are resolved and evaluated immediately. This is incompatible, as a reference to an entity defined after the aspect will now be illegal. However, this would have required retroactive enforcement of such aspects, which is a new capability not available from the associated pragma, and moreover no known Ada 2012 implementation has ever allowed late evaluation of such aspects. As such, there should be no practical incompatibility.<br />

<MarginText>39.e/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0220-1"]} />
Parameters of access-to-subprogram types are now visible in aspect specifications. This can be incompatible if some entity with the same name as a parameter is used in an existing aspect specification. We believe that all such aspects require either static expressions or a subprogram that is statically denoted; since a parameter can be neither of these and hides everything else, all such cases will be caught at compile-time. In addition, we expect such cases to be very rare. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>39.f/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
An aspect can be an unresolved <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, these can be used to specify a list of entities, or to set a group of different but related properties with a single aspect.<br />

<MarginText>39.g/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0355-2"]} />
Aspect specifications can appear in, and apply to, constructs other than declarations.<br />

<MarginText>39.h/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0389-1"]} />
An unrecognized aspect specification can be ignored. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>39.i/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0105-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified the wording so that the restriction against language-defined aspects on subprogram completions includes completions that are expressions functions and null procedures.<br />

<MarginText>39.j/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0106-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Defined class-wide aspect for use in rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br />

<MarginText>39.k/4_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0138-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a definition of nonoverridable aspects. This is necessary to prevent generic contract problems with formal derived types.<br />

<MarginText>39.l/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0169-1", "AI12-0194-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> to the list of entities that don't allow any language-defined aspects. This was an oversight in  which allowed <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s on an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> in the first place.<br />

<MarginText>39.m/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0206-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Extended the definition of nonoverridable aspects to cover most kinds of aspects.<br />

<MarginText>39.n/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0211-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a rule so that the a nonoverridable aspect has to be the same for every ancestor of a type.<br />

<MarginText>39.o/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0355-2", "AI12-0427-1"]} />
Clarified when elaboration and resolution of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s not associated with a declaration occur.<br />

<MarginText>39.p/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0380-1", "AI12-0407-1"]} />
Revised the rules about entities that cannot have specified language-defined aspects. The body portion of the rule was changed to a general prohibition on specifying language-defined aspects on completions (this allows specifying aspects on bodies that act as a declaration, and eliminates the list of entities, which was a maintenance nightmare). Then the remaining entities (renamings and generic formal parameters) were revised to allow specific aspects, since Nonblocking (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>), as well as Pre and Post, are now allowed on generic formal parameters.<br />

<MarginText>39.q/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0373-1"]} />
Added the missing definition for resolution of entities found in aspects of library units.<br />

<MarginText>39.r/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0396-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined confirming for nonoverridable aspects that are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>39.s/5_13.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0419-1"]} />
Added a description of additive and implicitly composed aspects in order to explain the different inheritance mechanisms used by existing aspects. <br />

# 13.10. Unchecked Access Value Creation

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.10.mdx

sidebar_position:  114

# 13.10. Unchecked Access Value Creation

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[The attribute Unchecked{"_"}Access is used to create access values in an unsafe manner &mdash; the programmer is responsible for preventing &ldquo;dangling references&rdquo;.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The following attribute is defined for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X that denotes an aliased view of an object: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Unchecked{"_"}Access</dt>
<dl>
<dd>All rules and semantics that apply to X'Access (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>) apply also to X'Unchecked{"_"}Access, except that, for the purposes of accessibility rules and checks, it is as if X were declared immediately within a library package. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We say &ldquo;rules and semantics&rdquo; here so that library-level accessibility applies to the value created by X'Unchecked{"_"}Access as well as to the checks needed for the attribute itself. This means that any anonymous access values that inherit the accessibility of this attribute (such as access parameters) also act as if they have library-level accessibility. We don't want the "real" accessibility of the created value re-emerging at a later point &ndash; that would create hard-to-understand bugs. <br />

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0449-1"]} />
NOTE 1   This attribute is provided to support the situation where a local object is to be inserted into a global linked data structure, when the programmer knows that it will always be removed from the data structure prior to exiting the object's scope. The Access attribute would be illegal in this case (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>). <br />

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The expected type for X'Unchecked{"_"}Access is as for X'Access.<br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> with Unchecked{"_"}Access is used as the actual parameter for an access parameter, an Accessibility{"_"}Check can never fail on that access parameter. <br />

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
NOTE 2   There is no Unchecked{"_"}Access attribute for subprograms. <br />

<MarginText>5.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00254-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Such an attribute would allow unsafe &ldquo;downward closures&rdquo;, where an access value designating a more nested subprogram is passed to a less nested subprogram. (Anonymous access-to-subprogram parameters provide safe &ldquo;downward closures&rdquo;.) This requires some means of reconstructing the global environment for the more nested subprogram, so that it can do up-level references to objects. The two methods of implementing up-level references are displays and static links. If unsafe downward closures were supported, each access-to-subprogram value would have to carry the static link or display with it. We don't want to require the space and time overhead of requiring the extra information for all access-to-subprogram types, especially as including it would make interfacing to other languages (like C) harder.<br />

<MarginText>5.b</MarginText>
If desired, an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Conversion can be used to create an access value of a global access-to-subprogram type that designates a local subprogram. The semantics of using such a value are not specified by the language. In particular, it is not specified what happens if such subprograms make up-level references; even if the frame being referenced still exists, the up-level reference might go awry if the representation of a value of a global access-to-subprogram type doesn't include a static link. <br />

---

# 13.11. Storage Management

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11.mdx

sidebar_position:  115

# 13.11. Storage Management

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ Each access-to-object type has an associated storage pool. The storage allocated by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> comes from the pool; instances of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation return storage to the pool. Several access types can share the same pool.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00435-01"]} />
<p>[A storage pool is a variable of a type in the class rooted at Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool, which is an abstract limited controlled type. By default, the implementation chooses a <i>standard storage pool</i> for each access-to-object type. The user may define new pool types, and may override the choice of pool for an access-to-object type by specifying Storage{"_"}Pool for the type.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>By default, the implementation might choose to have a single global storage pool, which is used (by default) by all access types, which might mean that storage is reclaimed automatically only upon partition completion. Alternatively, it might choose to create a new pool at each accessibility level, which might mean that storage is reclaimed for an access type when leaving the appropriate scope. Other schemes are possible. <br />

<MarginText>2.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>storage pool object</b> &mdash; object associated with one or more access types from which the storage for objects created by allocators of the access type(s) is obtained<br />Note: Some storage pools can be partitioned into subpools in order to support finer-grained storage management.<br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>If Storage{"_"}Pool is specified for a given access type, Storage{"_"}Size shall not be specified for it. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The Storage{"_"}Pool determines the Storage{"_"}Size; hence it would not make sense to specify both. Note that this rule is simplified by the fact that the aspects in question cannot be specified for derived types, nor for nonfirst subtypes, so we don't have to worry about whether, say, Storage{"_"}Pool on a derived type overrides Storage{"_"}Size on the parent type. For the same reason, &ldquo;specified&rdquo; means the same thing as &ldquo;directly specified&rdquo; here. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0235-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Finalization;{"\n"}with System.Storage{"_"}Elements;{"\n"}package System.Storage{"_"}Pools {"\n"}    with Pure, Nonblocking ={">"} False is{"\n"}
<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01", "AI12-0399-1"]} />
    type Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool is{"\n"}        abstract new Ada.Finalization.Limited{"_"}Controlled with private{"\n"}        with Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
    procedure Allocate({"\n"}      Pool : in out Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool;{"\n"}      Storage{"_"}Address : out Address;{"\n"}      Size{"_"}In{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements : in Storage{"_"}Elements.Storage{"_"}Count;{"\n"}      Alignment : in Storage{"_"}Elements.Storage{"_"}Count) is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
    procedure Deallocate({"\n"}      Pool : in out Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool;{"\n"}      Storage{"_"}Address : in Address;{"\n"}      Size{"_"}In{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements : in Storage{"_"}Elements.Storage{"_"}Count;{"\n"}      Alignment : in Storage{"_"}Elements.Storage{"_"}Count) is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
    function Storage{"_"}Size(Pool : Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool){"\n"}        return Storage{"_"}Elements.Storage{"_"}Count is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
private{"\n"}   ... -- not specified by the language{"\n"}end System.Storage{"_"}Pools;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The Alignment parameter is provided to Deallocate because some allocation strategies require it. If it is not needed, it can be ignored. <br />

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>A <i>storage pool type</i> (or <i>pool type</i>) is a descendant of Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool. The <i>elements</i> of a storage pool are the objects allocated in the pool by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In most cases, an element corresponds to a single memory block allocated by Allocate. However, in some cases the implementation may choose to associate more than one memory block with a given pool element. <br />

<MarginText>12/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI95-00435-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} For every access-to-object subtype S, the following representation attributes are defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Storage{"_"}Pool</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Denotes the storage pool of the type of S. The type of this attribute is Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool'Class.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Storage{"_"}Size</dt>
<dd>Yields the result of calling Storage{"_"}Size(S'Storage{"_"}Pool)[, which is intended to be a measure of the number of storage elements reserved for the pool.] The type of this attribute is <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Storage{"_"}Size is also defined for task subtypes and objects &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br />

<MarginText>14.b</MarginText>
Storage{"_"}Size is not a measure of how much un-allocated space is left in the pool. That is, it includes both allocated and unallocated space. Implementations and users may provide a Storage{"_"}Available function for their pools, if so desired. <br />

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0319-1"]} />
<p>Storage{"_"}Size or Storage{"_"}Pool may be specified for a nonderived access-to-object type via an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute{"_"}definition{"_"}clause</a></code>; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> in a Storage{"_"}Pool clause shall denote a variable. If the nominal subtype of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> specified for Storage{"_"}Pool is nonblocking (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>), then the primitive Allocate, Deallocate, and Storage{"_"}Size subprograms of that type shall be nonblocking. Additionally, if the pool is one that supports subpools (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11#Subclause_13.11.4">13.11.4</a>), the primitive Default{"_"}Subpool{"_"}for{"_"}Pool, Allocate{"_"}From{"_"}Subpool, and Deallocate{"_"}Subpool subprograms shall be nonblocking.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Storage{"_"}Pool: </b>Pool of memory from which <b>new</b> will allocate for a given access type.<br />

<MarginText>15.b/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Storage{"_"}Size (access): </b>Sets memory size for allocations for an access type.<br />

<MarginText>15.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0319-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We need to be able to describe in contracts (especially for generic units) whether the operations of a storage pool allow blocking, and we do that with the nonblocking status of the type. We make the check when the pool is specified so we can avoid adding a special check to the declaration of a pool type &ndash; we want pool types to follow the same rules as any other type. <br />

<MarginText>16/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1", "AI05-0111-3", "AI05-0116-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of a type <i>T</i> that does not support subpools allocates storage from <i>T</i>'s storage pool. If the storage pool is a user-defined object, then the storage is allocated by calling Allocate as described below. <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">Allocator</a></code>s for types that support subpools are described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11#Subclause_13.11.4">13.11.4</a>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the implementation chooses to represent the designated subtype in multiple pieces, one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> evaluation might result in more than one call upon Allocate. In any case, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s for the access type obtain all the required storage for an object of the designated type by calling the specified Allocate procedure.<br />

<MarginText>16.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>16.b.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00103-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0111</i>{"}"} If <i>D</i> (the designated type of <i>T</i>) includes subcomponents of other access types, they will be allocated from the storage pools for those types, even if those <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s are executed as part of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of <i>T</i> (as part of the initialization of the object). For instance, an access-to-task type <i>TT</i> may allocate the data structures used to implement the task value from other storage pools. (In particular, the task stack does not necessarily need to be allocated from the storage pool for <i>TT</i>.) <br />

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p>If Storage{"_"}Pool is not specified for a type defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0080">access_to_object_definition</a></code>, then the implementation chooses a standard storage pool for it in an implementation-defined manner. In this case, the exception Storage{"_"}Error is raised by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> if there is not enough storage. It is implementation defined whether or not the implementation provides user-accessible names for the standard pool type(s). <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>17.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The manner of choosing a storage pool is covered by a Documentation Requirement below, so it is not summarized here. <br />

<MarginText>17.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Whether or not the implementation provides user-accessible names for the standard pool type(s).<br />

<MarginText>17.b.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b><b>pragma</b> Default{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11#Subclause_13.11.3">13.11.3</a>) can be used to specify a specific pool (or none at all) to be used with access types declared in a particular declaration list, rather than a standard storage pool.<br />

<MarginText>17.b.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
Although there is no language-defined user-accessible name for the standard pool type(s), the default use of a standard pool may be indicated using the identifier Standard in the <b>pragma</b> Default{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool. <br />

<MarginText>17.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>An access-to-object type defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> inherits its pool from its parent type, so all access-to-object types in the same derivation class share the same pool. Hence the &ldquo;defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0080">access_to_object_definition</a></code>&rdquo; wording above.<br />

<MarginText>17.d</MarginText>
There is no requirement that all storage pools be implemented using a contiguous block of memory (although each allocation returns a pointer to a contiguous block of memory). <br />

<MarginText>17.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0319-1", "AI12-0424-1"]} />
<p>The type(s) of the standard pool(s), and the primitive Allocate, Deallocate, and Storage{"_"}Size subprograms for the standard pool(s) are nonblocking. Concurrent invocations of these subprograms do not conflict with one another (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10">9.10</a>) when applied to standard storage pools.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17.e/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We need to specify that the type is nonblocking so that an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation is nonblocking if the object type is nonblocking (as the type is used in the contract). Ada 95 did not declare standard allocation/deallocation as potentially blocking, so these things can be used in protected types, and we want that to remain true (with static checking). <br />

<MarginText>18/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0043-1", "AI12-0319-1"]} />
<p>If Storage{"_"}Size is specified for an access type <i>T</i>, an implementation-defined pool <i>P</i> is used for the type. The Storage{"_"}Size of <i>P</i> is at least that requested, and the storage for <i>P</i> is reclaimed when the master containing the declaration of the access type is left. If the implementation cannot satisfy the request, Storage{"_"}Error is raised at the freezing point of type <i>T</i>. The storage pool <i>P</i> is used only for allocators returning type <i>T</i> or other access types specified to use <i>T</i>'Storage{"_"}Pool. Storage{"_"}Error is raised by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> returning such a type if the storage space of <i>P</i> is exhausted (additional memory is not allocated). The type of <i>P</i>, and the primitive Allocate, Deallocate, and Storage{"_"}Size subprograms of <i>P</i> are nonblocking.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0043-1"]} />
<p>If neither Storage{"_"}Pool nor Storage{"_"}Size are specified, then the meaning of Storage{"_"}Size is implementation defined.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The meaning of Storage{"_"}Size when neither the Storage{"_"}Size nor the Storage{"_"}Pool is specified for an access type.<br />

<MarginText>18.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The Storage{"_"}Size function and attribute will return the actual size, rather than the requested size. Comments about rounding up, zero, and negative on task Storage{"_"}Size apply here, as well. See also AI83-00557, AI83-00558, and AI83-00608.<br />

<MarginText>18.c</MarginText>
The expression in a Storage{"_"}Size clause need not be static.<br />

<MarginText>18.d</MarginText>
The reclamation happens after the master is finalized. <br />

<MarginText>18.e</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>For a pool allocated on the stack, normal stack cut-back can accomplish the reclamation. For a library-level pool, normal partition termination actions can accomplish the reclamation. <br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<p>If Storage{"_"}Pool is specified for an access type, then the specified pool is used.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20</MarginText>
<p>The effect of calling Allocate and Deallocate for a standard storage pool directly (rather than implicitly via an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> or an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation) is unspecified. <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> might put the pool element on a finalization list. If the user directly Deallocates it, instead of calling an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation, then the implementation would probably try to finalize the object upon master completion, which would be bad news. Therefore, the implementation should define such situations as erroneous. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p>If Storage{"_"}Pool is specified for an access type, then if Allocate can satisfy the request, it should allocate a contiguous block of memory, and return the address of the first storage element in Storage{"_"}Address. The block should contain Size{"_"}In{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements storage elements, and should be aligned according to Alignment. The allocated storage should not be used for any other purpose while the pool element remains in existence. If the request cannot be satisfied, then Allocate should propagate an exception [(such as Storage{"_"}Error)]. If Allocate behaves in any other manner, then the program execution is erroneous. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>21.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>The Allocate procedure of a user-defined storage pool object <i>P</i> may be called by the implementation only to allocate storage for a type <i>T</i> whose pool is <i>P</i>, only at the following points:<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.2/3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>During the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of type <i>T</i>;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This includes during the evaluation of the initializing expression such as an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>; this is important if the initializing expression is built in place. We need to allow allocation to be deferred until the size of the object is known. <br />

<MarginText>21.3/3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>During the execution of a return statement for a function whose result is built-in-place in the result of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of type <i>T</i>;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.b/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We need this bullet as well as the preceding one in order that exceptions that propagate from such a call to Allocate can be handled within the return statement. We don't want to require the generation of special handling code in this unusual case, as it would add overhead to most return statements of composite types. <br />

<MarginText>21.4/3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>During the execution of an assignment operation with a target of an allocated object of type <i>T</i> with a part that has an unconstrained discriminated subtype with defaults.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.c/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We allow Allocate to be called during assignment of objects with mutable parts so that mutable objects can be implemented with reallocation on assignment. (Unfortunately, the term "mutable" is only defined in the AARM, so we have to use the long-winded wording shown here.) <br />

<MarginText>21.d/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Of course, explicit calls to Allocate are also allowed and are not bound by any of the rules found here. <br />

<MarginText>21.5/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1", "AI05-0116-1", "AI05-0193-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>For each of the calls of Allocate described above, <i>P</i> (equivalent to <i>T</i>'Storage{"_"}Pool) is passed as the Pool parameter. The Size{"_"}In{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements parameter indicates the number of storage elements to be allocated, and is no more than <i>D</i>'Max{"_"}Size{"_"}In{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements, where <i>D</i> is the designated subtype of <i>T</i>. The Alignment parameter is a nonzero integral multiple of <i>D</i>'Alignment if <i>D</i> is a specific type, and otherwise is a nonzero integral multiple of the alignment of the specific type identified by the tag of the object being created; it is unspecified if there is no such value. The Alignment parameter is no more than <i>D</i>'Max{"_"}Alignment{"_"}For{"_"}Allocation. The result returned in the Storage{"_"}Address parameter is used as the address of the allocated storage, which is a contiguous block of memory of Size{"_"}In{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements storage elements. [Any exception propagated by Allocate is propagated by the construct that contained the call.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.e/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that the implementation does not turn other exceptions into Storage{"_"}Error.<br />

<MarginText>21.f/3</MarginText>
&ldquo;Nonzero integral multiple&rdquo; of an alignment includes the alignment value itself, of course. The value is unspecified if the alignment of the specific type is zero. <br />

<MarginText>21.6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>The number of calls to Allocate that will be used to implement an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> for any particular type is unspecified. The number of calls to Deallocate that will be used to implement an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11#Subclause_13.11.2">13.11.2</a>) for any particular object is the same as the number of Allocate calls for that object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.g/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This supports objects that are allocated in one or more parts. The second sentence prevents extra or missing calls to Deallocate. <br />

<MarginText>21.h/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>The number of calls to Deallocate from all sources for an object always will be the same as the number of calls to Allocate from all sources for that object. However, in unusual cases, not all of those Deallocate calls may be made by an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation. Specifically, in the unusual case of assigning to an object of a mutable variant record type such that the variant changes, some of the Deallocate calls may be made by the assignment (as may some of the Allocate calls). <br />

<MarginText>21.i/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We do not define the relative order of multiple calls used to deallocate the same object &mdash; that is, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> allocated two pieces <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>, then an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation might deallocate <i>x</i> and then <i>y</i>, or it might deallocate <i>y</i> and then <i>x</i>. <br />

<MarginText>21.7/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1"]} />
<p>The Deallocate procedure of a user-defined storage pool object <i>P</i> may be called by the implementation to deallocate storage for a type <i>T</i> whose pool is <i>P</i> only at the places when an Allocate call is allowed for <i>P</i>, during the execution of an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation for <i>T</i>, or as part of the finalization of the collection of <i>T</i>. For such a call of Deallocate, <i>P</i> (equivalent to <i>T</i>'Storage{"_"}Pool) is passed as the Pool parameter. The value of the Storage{"_"}Address parameter for a call to Deallocate is the value returned in the Storage{"_"}Address parameter of the corresponding successful call to Allocate. The values of the Size{"_"}In{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements and Alignment parameters are the same values passed to the corresponding Allocate call. Any exception propagated by Deallocate is propagated by the construct that contained the call.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.j/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We allow Deallocate to be called anywhere that Allocate is, in order to allow the recovery of storage from failed allocations (that is, those that raise exceptions); from extended return statements that exit via a goto, exit, or locally handled exception; and from objects that are reallocated when they are assigned. In each of these cases, we would have a storage leak if the implementation did not recover the storage (there is no way for the programmer to do it). We do not require such recovery, however, as it could be a serious performance drag on these operations. <br />

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>An implementation shall document the set of values that a user-defined Allocate procedure has to accept for the Alignment parameter. An implementation shall document how the standard storage pool is chosen, and how storage is allocated by standard storage pools. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>22.b/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The set of values that a user-defined Allocate procedure needs to accept for the Alignment parameter. How the standard storage pool is chosen, and how storage is allocated by standard storage pools.<br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<p>An implementation should document any cases in which it dynamically allocates heap storage for a purpose other than the evaluation of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>23.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Any cases in which heap storage is dynamically allocated other than as part of the evaluation of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> should be documented.<br />

<MarginText>23.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>This is &ldquo;&rdquo; because the term &ldquo;heap storage&rdquo; is not formally definable; therefore, it is not testable whether the implementation obeys this advice. <br />

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<p>A default (implementation-provided) storage pool for an access-to-constant type should not have overhead to support deallocation of individual objects. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>A default storage pool for an access-to-constant type should not have overhead to support deallocation of individual objects.<br />

<MarginText>24.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation is not defined for such types. If the access-to-constant type is library-level, then no deallocation (other than at partition completion) will ever be necessary, so if the size needed by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of the type is known at link-time, then the allocation should be performed statically. If, in addition, the initial value of the designated object is known at compile time, the object can be allocated to read-only memory. <br />

<MarginText>24.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>If the Storage{"_"}Size for an access type is specified, the storage pool should consist of a contiguous block of memory, possibly allocated on the stack. The pool should contain approximately this number of storage elements. These storage elements should be reserved at the place of the Storage{"_"}Size clause, so that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s cannot raise Storage{"_"}Error due to running out of pool space until the appropriate number of storage elements has been used up. This approximate (possibly rounded-up) value should be used as a maximum; the implementation should not increase the size of the pool on the fly. If the Storage{"_"}Size for an access type is specified as zero, then the pool should not take up any storage space, and any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> for the type should raise Storage{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>24.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that most of this is approximate, and so cannot be (portably) tested. That's why we make it an Implementation Note. There is no particular number of allocations that is guaranteed to succeed, and there is no particular number of allocations that is guaranteed to fail. <br />

<MarginText>25/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<p>The storage pool used for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> of an anonymous access type should be determined as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>25.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> is defining a coextension (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>) of an object being created by an outer <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>, then the storage pool used for the outer <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> should also be used for the coextension;<br /></li>
<MarginText>25.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<li>For other access discriminants and access parameters, the storage pool should be created at the point of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>, and be reclaimed when the allocated object becomes inaccessible;<br /></li>
<MarginText>25.3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0051-1"]} />
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> defines the result of a function with an access result, the storage pool is determined as though the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> were in place of the call of the function. If the call is the operand of a type conversion, the storage pool is that of the target access type of the conversion. If the call is itself defining the result of a function with an access result, this rule is applied recursively;<br /></li>
<MarginText>25.4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<li>Otherwise, a default storage pool should be created at the point where the anonymous access type is elaborated; such a storage pool may have no mechanism for the deallocation of individual objects. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>25.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Usually, a storage pool for an access discriminant or access parameter should be created at the point of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>, and be reclaimed when the designated object becomes inaccessible. For other anonymous access types, the pool should be created at the point where the type is elaborated and may have no mechanism for the deallocation of individual objects.<br />

<MarginText>25.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>For access parameters and access discriminants, the "storage pool" for an anonymous access type would not normally exist as a separate entity. Instead, the designated object of the allocator would be allocated, in the case of an access parameter, as a local aliased variable at the call site, and in the case of an access discriminant, contiguous with the object containing the discriminant. This is similar to the way storage for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s is typically managed.<br />

<MarginText>25.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
For other sorts of anonymous access types, this implementation is not possible in general, as the accessibility of the anonymous access type is that of its declaration, while the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> could be more nested. In this case, a "real" storage pool is required. Note, however, that this storage pool need not support (separate) deallocation, as it is not possible to instantiate Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation with an anonymous access type. (If deallocation is needed, the object should be allocated for a named access type and converted.) Thus, deallocation only need happen when the anonymous access type itself goes out of scope; this is similar to the case of an access-to-constant type. <br />

<MarginText>26/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 1   A user-defined storage pool type can be obtained by extending the Root{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool type, and overriding the primitive subprograms Allocate, Deallocate, and Storage{"_"}Size. A user-defined storage pool can then be obtained by declaring an object of the type extension. The user can override Initialize and Finalize if there is any desire for nontrivial initialization and finalization for a user-defined pool type. For example, Finalize can reclaim blocks of storage that are allocated separately from the pool object itself.<br />

<MarginText>27</MarginText>
