# 13.12. Pragma Restrictions and Pragma Profile

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12.mdx

sidebar_position:  116

# 13.12. Pragma Restrictions and Pragma Profile

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0246-1"]} />
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Restrictions expresses the user's intent to abide by certain restrictions. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Profile expresses the user's intent to abide by a set of Restrictions or other specified run-time policies. These may facilitate the construction of simpler run-time environments.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Restrictions is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Restrictions(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0359">restriction</a></code>{"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0359">restriction</a></code>{"}"});<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00381-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>restriction</code><a id="S0359"></a><code> ::= </code><i>restriction{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code><br />    | <i>restriction{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> ={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00381-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>restriction{"_"}parameter{"_"}argument</code><a id="S0360"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>Unless otherwise specified for a particular restriction, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is expected to be of any integer type. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>Unless otherwise specified for a particular restriction, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall be static, and its value shall be nonnegative. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<p><i>Paragraph 7 was deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0013-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Restrictions is a configuration pragma. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Restrictions applies to any compilation unit included in the partition, this may impose either (or both) of two kinds of requirements, as specified for the particular restriction:<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0013-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A restriction may impose requirements on some or all of the units comprising the partition. Unless otherwise specified for a particular restriction, such a requirement applies to all of the units comprising the partition and is enforced via a post-compilation check.<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0013-1"]} />
<li>A restriction may impose requirements on the run-time behavior of the program, as indicated by the specification of run-time behavior associated with a violation of the requirement.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a.1/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In this latter case, there is no post-compilation check needed for the requirement. <br />

<MarginText>8.3/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00130-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0042</i>{"}"} For the purpose of checking whether a partition contains constructs that violate any restriction (unless specified otherwise for a particular restriction):<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.4/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00130-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0042</i>{"}"} Generic instances are logically expanded at the point of instantiation;<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.5/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00130-01"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0042</i>{"}"} If an object of a type is declared or allocated and not explicitly initialized, then all expressions appearing in the definition for the type and any of its ancestors are presumed to be used;<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.6/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00130-01"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0042</i>{"}"} A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> for a formal parameter or a generic formal object is considered to be used if and only if the corresponding actual parameter is not provided in a given call or instantiation. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>8.7/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may provide implementation-defined restrictions; the identifier for an implementation-defined restriction shall differ from those of the language-defined restrictions. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a.2/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined restrictions allowed in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Restrictions.<br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may place limitations on the values of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that are supported, and limitations on the supported combinations of restrictions. The consequences of violating such limitations are implementation defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The consequences of violating limitations on Restrictions <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>9.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Such limitations may be enforced at compile time or at run time. Alternatively, the implementation is allowed to declare violations of the restrictions to be erroneous, and not enforce them at all. <br />

<MarginText>9.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00130-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0042</i>{"}"} An implementation is permitted to omit restriction checks for code that is recognized at compile time to be unreachable and for which no code is generated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.2/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00190-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0043</i>{"}"} Whenever enforcement of a restriction is not required prior to execution, an implementation may nevertheless enforce the restriction prior to execution of a partition to which the restriction applies, provided that every execution of the partition would violate the restriction. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>10/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00249-01", "AI05-0246-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Profile is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Profile (<i>profile{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> {"{"}, <i>profile{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0020">pragma_argument_association</a></code>{"}"});<br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00249-01", "AI05-0246-1"]} />
<p>The <i>profile{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall be the name of a usage profile. The semantics of any <i>profile{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0020">pragma{"_"}argument{"_"}association</a></code>s are defined by the usage profile specified by the <i>profile{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>13/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00249-01", "AI05-0246-1"]} />
<p>A profile is equivalent to the set of configuration pragmas that is defined for each usage profile. <br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>14/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00249-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Profile is a configuration pragma. There may be more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Profile for a partition. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>15/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may provide implementation-defined usage profiles; the identifier for an implementation-defined usage profile shall differ from those of the language-defined usage profiles.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a.1/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined usage profiles allowed in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Profile.<br />

<MarginText>16/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00347-01"]} />
NOTE 1   Restrictions intended to facilitate the construction of efficient tasking run-time systems are defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.7">D.7</a>. Restrictions intended for use when constructing high integrity systems are defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-H/AA-H.4">H.4</a>.<br />

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
NOTE 2   An implementation has to enforce the restrictions in cases where enforcement is required, even if it chooses not to take advantage of the restrictions in terms of efficiency. <br />

<MarginText>17.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>It is not the intent that an implementation will support a different run-time system for every possible combination of restrictions. An implementation might support only two run-time systems, and document a set of restrictions that is sufficient to allow use of the more efficient and safe one. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>17.b</MarginText>
Pragma Restrictions is new to Ada 95. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>17.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00249-01", "AI05-0246-1"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Profile is new; it was moved here by Ada 2012 and renamed to a "usage profile" but was otherwise unchanged. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>17.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00130-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0042</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected the wording so that restrictions are checked inside of generic instantiations and in default expressions. Since not making these checks would violate the purpose of restrictions, we are not documenting this as an incompatibility.<br />

<MarginText>17.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00190-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0043</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a permission that restrictions can be enforced at compile-time. While this is technically incompatible, documenting it as such would be unnecessarily alarming - there should not be any programs depending on the runtime failure of restrictions.<br />

<MarginText>17.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00381-01"]} />
The syntax of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> has been defined to better support restriction No{"_"}Dependence (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#Subclause_13.12.1">13.12.1</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>17.g/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0013-1"]} />
<b>Correction</b>: When restrictions are checked has been clarified. <br />

<a id="Subclause_13.12.1"></a>

## 13.12.1  Language-Defined Restrictions and Profiles

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00257-01"]} />
<p>The following <i>restriction{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s are language defined (additional restrictions are defined in the Specialized Needs Annexes):<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.1/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0241-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Aspect{"_"}Specifications </dt>
<dl>
<dd>There are no implementation-defined aspects specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>1.a/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0241-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This restriction (as well as others below) applies only to the current compilation, because it is likely that the runtime (and possibly user-written low-level code) will need to use implementation-defined aspects. But a partition-wide restriction applies everywhere, including the runtime. <br />

<MarginText>2/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00257-01"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Attributes </dt>
<dl>
<dd>There are no implementation-defined attributes. This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition. <br /></dd>
<MarginText>2.1/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0246-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Identifiers </dt>
<dd>There are no usage names that denote declarations with implementation-defined identifiers that occur within language-defined packages or instances of language-defined generic packages. Such identifiers can arise as follows: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>2.2/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The following language-defined packages and generic packages allow implementation-defined identifiers:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>2.3/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>package System (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.7">13.7</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.4/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<li>package Standard (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.1">A.1</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.5/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<li>package Ada.Command{"_"}Line (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.15">A.15</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.6/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<li>package Interfaces.C (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3">B.3</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.7/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<li>package Interfaces.C.Strings (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3#Subclause_B.3.1">B.3.1</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.8/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<li>package Interfaces.C.Pointers (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3#Subclause_B.3.2">B.3.2</a>);<br /></li>

<MarginText>2.10/3_13.12.1</MarginText>

</ul>
<MarginText>2.11/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The following language-defined packages contain only implementation-defined identifiers:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>2.12/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>package System.Machine{"_"}Code (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.8">13.8</a>);<br /></li>

<MarginText>2.14/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<li>nested Implementation packages of the Queue containers (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.28">A.18.28</a>-31);<br /></li>

<MarginText>2.16/3_13.12.1</MarginText>

</ul>
<MarginText>2.17/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>For package Standard, Standard.Long{"_"}Integer and Standard.Long{"_"}Float are considered language-defined identifiers, but identifiers such as Standard.Short{"_"}Short{"_"}Integer are considered implementation-defined.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>2.18/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<dd>This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>3/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00257-01"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Pragmas </dt>
<dd>There are no implementation-defined pragmas or pragma arguments. This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>3.1/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0242-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Units </dt>
<dd>There is no mention in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code> of any implementation-defined descendants of packages Ada, Interfaces, or System. This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>4/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00368-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Obsolescent{"_"}Features </dt>
<dd>There is no use of language features defined in Annex J. It is implementation defined whether uses of the renamings of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.1">J.1</a> and of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.15">J.15</a> are detected by this restriction. This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>4.a/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A user could compile a rename like <br />

<MarginText>4.b/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Text{"_"}IO;{"\n"}package Text{"_"}IO renames Ada.Text{"_"}IO;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4.c/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
Such a rename must not be disallowed by this restriction, nor should the compilation of such a rename be restricted by an implementation. Many implementations implement the renames of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.1">J.1</a> by compiling them normally; we do not want to require implementations to use a special mechanism to implement these renames.<br />

<MarginText>4.d/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
The pragmas have the same functionality as the corresponding aspect (unlike the typical obsolescent feature), and rejecting them could be a significant portability problem for existing code. <br />

<MarginText>5/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00381-01", "AI05-0241-1"]} />
<p>The following <i>restriction{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s are language defined:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00381-01"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Dependence </dt>
<dl>
<dd>Specifies a library unit on which there are no semantic dependences.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.1/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0241-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Specification{"_"}of{"_"}Aspect </dt>
<dd>Identifies an aspect for which no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> is given.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.2/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0272-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Use{"_"}Of{"_"}Attribute </dt>
<dd>Identifies an attribute for which no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> is given.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.3/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0272-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Use{"_"}Of{"_"}Pragma </dt>
<dd>Identifies a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> which is not to be used.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.4/5_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0389-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Unrecognized{"_"}Aspects </dt>
<dd>There are no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s having an unrecognized <i>aspect{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>. This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.a/5_13.12.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>When this restriction is in effect, unrecognized aspects cannot be ignored in the current compilation; they violate the restriction. This is true despite the Implementation Permissions of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>6.5/5_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0389-1"]} />
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Unrecognized{"_"}Pragmas </dt>
<dl>
<dd>There are no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s having an unrecognized pragma <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>. This restriction applies only to the current compilation or environment, not the entire partition.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.b/5_13.12.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>When this restriction is in effect, unrecognized pragmas cannot be ignored in the current compilation; they violate the restriction. This is true despite the rules of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8">2.8</a>. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7/5_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00381-01", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> of a No{"_"}Dependence restriction shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall have the form of a full expanded name of a library unit, but can be a name that has no corresponding unit currently present in the environment.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2_13.12.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is not resolved. <br />

<MarginText>7.1/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0241-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> of a No{"_"}Specification{"_"}of{"_"}Aspect restriction shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>; this is an identifier specific to a pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8">2.8</a>) and does not denote any declaration.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.b/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> is not resolved as it is an identifier specific to a pragma. As for No{"_"}Dependence, there is no check that the aspect <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> is meaningful; it might refer to an implementation-defined aspect on one implementation, but nothing at all on another implementation. <br />

<MarginText>7.2/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0272-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> of a No{"_"}Use{"_"}Of{"_"}Attribute restriction shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> or one of the reserved words Access, Delta, Digits, Mod, or Range; this is an identifier specific to a pragma.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.c/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> is not resolved as it is an identifier specific to a pragma. There is no check that the attribute identifier refers to a known <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code>; it might refer to an implementation-defined attribute on one implementation, but nothing at all on another implementation. <br />

<MarginText>7.3/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0272-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> of a No{"_"}Use{"_"}Of{"_"}Pragma restriction shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> or the reserved word Interface; this is an identifier specific to a pragma.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.d/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#S0360">restriction_parameter_argument</a></code> is not resolved as it is an identifier specific to a pragma. There is no check that the pragma identifier refers to a known <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>; it might refer to an implementation-defined pragma on one implementation, but nothing at all on another implementation. <br />

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>8/3_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00381-01", "AI05-0241-1"]} />
<p>No compilation unit included in the partition shall depend semantically on the library unit identified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a No{"_"}Dependence restriction.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/5_13.12.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is no requirement that the library unit actually exists. One possible use of the pragma is to prevent the use of implementation-defined units; when the program is ported to a different compiler, it is perfectly reasonable that no unit with the name exists. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<dt><br/>No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Extensions </dt>
<dl>
<dd><br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>11/3_13.12.1</MarginText>

No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Aspect{"_"}Specifications,{"\n"}No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Attributes,{"\n"}No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Identifiers,{"\n"}No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Pragmas,{"\n"}No{"_"}Implementation{"_"}Units.{"\n"}

# 13.13. Streams

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13.mdx

sidebar_position:  117

# 13.13. Streams

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>A <i>stream</i> is a sequence of elements comprising values from possibly different types and allowing sequential access to these values. A <i>stream type</i> is a type in the class whose root type is Streams.Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type. A stream type may be implemented in various ways, such as an external sequential file, an internal buffer, or a network channel. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A stream element will often be the same size as a storage element, but that is not required. <br />

<MarginText>1.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>stream</b> &mdash; sequence of elements that can be used, along with the stream-oriented attributes, to support marshalling and unmarshalling of values of most types<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>1.c</MarginText>
Streams are new in Ada 95. <br />

<a id="Subclause_13.13.1"></a>

## 13.13.1  The Streams Subsystem

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_13.13.1</MarginText>
<p>The abstract type Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type is the root type of the class of stream types. The types in this class represent different kinds of streams. A new stream type is defined by extending the root type (or some other stream type), overriding the Read and Write operations, and optionally defining additional primitive subprograms, according to the requirements of the particular kind of stream. The predefined stream-oriented attributes like T'Read and T'Write make dispatching calls on the Read and Write procedures of the Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type. (User-defined T'Read and T'Write attributes can also make such calls, or can call the Read and Write attributes of other types.)<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.1/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0293-1"]} />
<p>The library package Ada.Streams has the following declaration:<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Streams{"\n"}    with Pure, Nonblocking ={">"} False is{"\n"}
<MarginText>3/2_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01"]} />
    type Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type is abstract tagged limited private{"\n"}        with Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4/1_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00181-01"]} />
{"{"}8652/0044{"}"}     type Stream{"_"}Element is mod implementation-defined;{"\n"}    type Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset is range implementation-defined;{"\n"}    subtype Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Count is{"\n"}        Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset range 0..Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset'Last;{"\n"}    type Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array is{"\n"}        array(Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset range {"<"}{">"}) of aliased Stream{"_"}Element;{"\n"}
<MarginText>5_13.13.1</MarginText>
    procedure Read({"\n"}      Stream : in out Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type;{"\n"}      Item   : out Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array;{"\n"}      Last   : out Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset) is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6_13.13.1</MarginText>
    procedure Write({"\n"}      Stream : in out Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type;{"\n"}      Item   : in Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array) is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7_13.13.1</MarginText>
private{"\n"}   ... -- not specified by the language{"\n"}end Ada.Streams;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.a/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This package must allow blocking (Nonblocking ={">"} False) for compatibility. The purpose of this package is to provide a template for overriding user-defined routines; and such routines can only allow blocking if the root type does so. Users can still declare their overridding routines nonblocking if they wish. <br />

<MarginText>8/2_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00227-01"]} />
<p>The Read operation transfers stream elements from the specified stream to fill the array Item. Elements are transferred until Item'Length elements have been transferred, or until the end of the stream is reached. If any elements are transferred, the index of the last stream element transferred is returned in Last. Otherwise, Item'First - 1 is returned in Last. Last is less than Item'Last only if the end of the stream is reached.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9_13.13.1</MarginText>
<p>The Write operation appends Item to the specified stream.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/2_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The index subtype of Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array is Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset because we wish to allow maximum flexibility. Most Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Arrays will probably have a lower bound of 0 or 1, but other lower bounds, including negative ones, make sense in some situations.<br />

<MarginText>9.b/3_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01", "AI05-0005-1"]} />
Note that there are some language-defined subprograms that fill part of a Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array, and return the index of the last element filled as a Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset. The Read procedures declared here, Streams.Stream{"_"}IO (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.12#Subclause_A.12.1">A.12.1</a>), and System.RPC (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.5">E.5</a>) behave in this manner. These will raise Constraint{"_"}Error if the resulting Last value is not in Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset. This implies that the Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array passed to these subprograms should not have a lower bound of Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset'First, because then a read of 0 elements would always raise Constraint{"_"}Error. A better choice of lower bound is 0 or 1. <br />

<MarginText>10/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0293-1"]} />
<p>Three additional packages provide stream implementations that do not make use of any file operations. These packages provide the same operations, with Streams.Storage providing an abstract interface, and two child packages providing implementations of that interface. The difference is that for Streams.Storage.Bounded, the maximum storage is bounded.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0293-1"]} />
<p>The library package Ada.Streams.Storage has the following declaration:<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Streams.Storage{"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking is{"\n"}
<MarginText>13/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   type Storage{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type is abstract new Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type with private;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   function Element{"_"}Count (Stream : Storage{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type){"\n"}      return Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Count is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   procedure Clear (Stream : in out Storage{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type) is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>16/5_13.13.1</MarginText>

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>17/5_13.13.1</MarginText>

<p>The library package Ada.Streams.Storage.Unbounded has the following declaration:<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Streams.Storage.Unbounded{"\n"}   with Prelaborated, Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}
<MarginText>19/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   type Stream{"_"}Type is new Storage{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type with private{"\n"}      with Default{"_"}Initial{"_"}Condition ={">"}{"\n"}          Element{"_"}Count (Stream{"_"}Type) = 0;{"\n"}
<MarginText>20/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   overriding{"\n"}   procedure Read ({"\n"}      Stream : in out Stream{"_"}Type;{"\n"}      Item   : out Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array;{"\n"}      Last   : out Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset){"\n"}      with Post ={">"}{"\n"}          (declare{"\n"}              Num{"_"}Read : constant Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Count :={"\n"}                 Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Count'Min{"\n"}                    (Element{"_"}Count(Stream)'Old, Item'Length);{"\n"}           begin{"\n"}              Last = Num{"_"}Read + Item'First - 1 and{"\n"}              Element{"_"}Count (Stream) ={"\n"}                 Element{"_"}Count (Stream)'Old - Num{"_"}Read);{"\n"}

<b></b>Num{"_"}Read is the number of elements read; this is the minimum of Item'Length and the number of available elements. Last then is determined by that, and the Element{"_"}Count decreases by the number of elements read. <br />

<MarginText>21/5_13.13.1</MarginText>

<MarginText>25/5_13.13.1</MarginText>

<p>The library package Ada.Streams.Storage.Bounded has the following declaration:<br /></p>

<MarginText>26/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Streams.Storage.Bounded{"\n"}    with Pure, Nonblocking is{"\n"}
<MarginText>27/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   type Stream{"_"}Type (Max{"_"}Elements : Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Count){"\n"}      is new Storage{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type with private{"\n"}         with Default{"_"}Initial{"_"}Condition ={">"}{"\n"}            Element{"_"}Count (Stream{"_"}Type) = 0;{"\n"}

<MarginText>30/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   overriding{"\n"}   function Element{"_"}Count (Stream : Stream{"_"}Type){"\n"}      return Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Count{"\n"}      with Post ={">"} Element{"_"}Count'Result {"<"}= Stream.Max{"_"}Elements;{"\n"}
<MarginText>31/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
   overriding{"\n"}    procedure Clear (Stream : in out Stream{"_"}Type){"\n"}       with Post ={">"} Element{"_"}Count (Stream) = 0;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>33/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0293-1"]} />
<p>The Element{"_"}Count functions return the number of stream elements that are available for reading from the given stream.<br /></p>

<MarginText>34/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0293-1"]} />
<p>The Read and Write procedures behave as described for package Ada.Streams above. Stream elements are read in FIFO (first-in, first-out) order; stream elements are available for reading immediately after they are written.<br /></p>

<MarginText>35/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0293-1"]} />
<p>The Clear procedures remove any available stream elements from the given stream.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>36/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00181-01", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0044</i>{"}"} If Stream{"_"}Element'Size is not a multiple of System.Storage{"_"}Unit, then the components of Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array will not be aliased. <br /></p>

<MarginText>36.a/2_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the Stream{"_"}Element'Size is less than the size of System.Storage{"_"}Unit, then components of Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Array need not be aliased. This is necessary as the components of type Stream{"_"}Element size might not be addressable on the target architecture. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>37/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0293-1"]} />
<p>Streams.Storage.Bounded.Stream{"_"}Type objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation.<br /></p>

<MarginText>37.a.1/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Streams.Storage.Bounded.Stream{"_"}Type objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation.<br />

<MarginText>37.a/5_13.13.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The Streams.Storage.Bounded package is provided in order to make available an alternative to the Streams.Storage.Unbounded package which gives more predictable memory usage. <br />

<MarginText>38_13.13.1</MarginText>
NOTE 1   See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.12#Subclause_A.12.1">A.12.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.12#Subclause_A.12.1">The Package Streams.Stream_IO</a>&rdquo; for an example of extending type Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type.<br />

<MarginText>39/2_13.13.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00227-01"]} />
NOTE 2   If the end of stream has been reached, and Item'First is Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset'First, Read will raise Constraint{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>39.a/2_13.13.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Thus, Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Arrays should start at 0 or 1, not Stream{"_"}Element{"_"}Offset'First. <br />

<a id="Subclause_13.13.2"></a>

## 13.13.2  Stream-Oriented Attributes

<MarginText>1/3_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01", "AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} The type-related operational attributes Write, Read, Output, and Input convert values to a stream of elements and reconstruct values from a stream. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1.1/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00270-01"]} />
<p>For every subtype S of an elementary type <i>T</i>, the following representation attribute is defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.2/3_13.13.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Stream{"_"}Size</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00270-01", "AI05-0194-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>Denotes the number of bits read from or written to a stream by the default implementations of S'Read and S'Write. Hence, the number of stream elements required per item of elementary type <i>T</i> is:<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>1.3/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
T'Stream{"_"}Size / Ada.Streams.Stream{"_"}Element'Size{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>1.4/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>The value of this attribute is of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i> and is a multiple of Stream{"_"}Element'Size.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>1.5/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<dd>Stream{"_"}Size may be specified for first subtypes via an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of such a clause shall be static, nonnegative, and a multiple of Stream{"_"}Element'Size.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>1.a/3_13.13.2</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Stream{"_"}Size: </b>Size in bits used to represent elementary objects in a stream.<br />

<MarginText>1.b/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Stream{"_"}Size is a type-related attribute (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>). <br />

<MarginText>1.c/3_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0194-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The value of S'Stream{"_"}Size is unaffected by the presence or absence of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s specifying the Read or Write attributes of any ancestor of S. S'Stream{"_"}Size is defined in terms of the behavior of the default implementations of S'Read and S'Write even if those default implementations are overridden. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>1.6/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00270-01"]} />
<p>If not specified, the value of Stream{"_"}Size for an elementary type should be the number of bits that corresponds to the minimum number of stream elements required by the first subtype of the type, rounded up to the nearest factor or multiple of the word size that is also a multiple of the stream element size. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.d/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If not specified, the value of Stream{"_"}Size for an elementary type should be the number of bits that corresponds to the minimum number of stream elements required by the first subtype of the type, rounded up to the nearest factor or multiple of the word size that is also a multiple of the stream element size.<br />

<MarginText>1.e/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00270-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>This is  because we want to allow implementations to remain compatible with their Ada 95 implementations, which may have a different handling of the number of stream elements. Users can always specify Stream{"_"}Size if they need a specific number of stream elements. <br />

<MarginText>1.7/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00270-01"]} />
<p>The recommended level of support for the Stream{"_"}Size attribute is: <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.8/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00270-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>A Stream{"_"}Size clause should be supported for a discrete or fixed point type <i>T</i> if the specified Stream{"_"}Size is a multiple of Stream{"_"}Element'Size and is no less than the size of the first subtype of <i>T</i>, and no greater than the size of the largest type of the same elementary class (signed integer, modular integer, enumeration, ordinary fixed point, or decimal fixed point). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>1.f/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The recommended level of support for the Stream{"_"}Size attribute should be followed.<br />

<MarginText>1.g/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There are no requirements beyond supporting confirming Stream{"_"}Size clauses for floating point and access types. Floating point and access types usually only have a handful of defined formats, streaming anything else makes no sense for them.<br />

<MarginText>1.h/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
For discrete and fixed point types, this may require support for sizes other than the &ldquo;natural&rdquo; ones. For instance, on a typical machine with 32-bit integers and a Stream{"_"}Element'Size of 8, setting Stream{"_"}Size to 24 must be supported. This is required as such formats can be useful for interoperability with unusual machines, and there is no difficulty with the implementation (drop extra bits on output, sign extend on input). <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<p>For every subtype S of a specific type <i>T</i>, the following attributes are defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3_13.13.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Write</dt>
<dl>
<dd>S'Write denotes a procedure with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>4/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00441-01"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure S'Write({"\n"}   Stream : not null access Ada.Streams.Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type'Class;{"\n"}   Item : in T){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5_13.13.2</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>S'Write writes the value of <i>Item</i> to <i>Stream</i>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6_13.13.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Read</dt>
<dd>S'Read denotes a procedure with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>7/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00441-01"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure S'Read({"\n"}   Stream : not null access Ada.Streams.Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type'Class;{"\n"}   Item : out T){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8_13.13.2</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>S'Read reads the value of <i>Item</i> from <i>Stream</i>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>8.1/5_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00108-01", "AI95-00444-01", "AI05-0192-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i>{"{"}<i>8652/0040</i>{"}"} <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.2/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00444-01"]} />
<p>The default implementations of the Write and Read attributes, where available, execute as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00108-01", "AI95-00195-01", "AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00270-01", "AI05-0139-2", "AI12-0191-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0040</i>{"}"} For nonderived elementary types, Read reads (and Write writes) the number of stream elements implied by the Stream{"_"}Size for the type <i>T</i>; the representation of those stream elements is implementation defined. For nonderived composite types, the Write or Read attribute for each component (excluding those, if any, that are not components of the nominal type of the object) is called in canonical order, which is last dimension varying fastest for an array (unless the convention of the array is Fortran, in which case it is first dimension varying fastest), and positional aggregate order for a record. Bounds are not included in the stream if <i>T</i> is an array type. If <i>T</i> is a discriminated type, discriminants are included only if they have defaults. If <i>T</i> is a tagged type, the tag is not included. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The contents of the stream elements read and written by the Read and Write attributes of elementary types.<br />

<MarginText>9.1/5_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0419-1"]} />
<p>For type extensions, the Write or Read attribute for the parent type is called, followed by the Write or Read attribute of each component of the extension part, in canonical order. For a limited type extension, if the attribute of the parent type or any progenitor type of <i>T</i> is available anywhere within the immediate scope of <i>T</i>, and the attribute of the parent type or the type of any of the extension components is not available at the freezing point of <i>T</i>, then the attribute of <i>T</i> shall be directly specified. For untagged derived types, the Write (resp. Read) attribute invokes the corresponding attribute of the parent type, if the attribute is available for the parent type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a.1/5_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0419-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The default implementation of a stream-oriented attribute might not be well-defined in cases where the attribute is never available anywhere in the scope of the type. In such cases, the attribute cannot be called and is defined (far below) to raise Program{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>9.2/5_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0023-1", "AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
<p>If <i>T</i> is a discriminated type and its discriminants have defaults, then S'Read first reads the discriminants from the stream without modifying <i>Item</i>. S'Read then creates an object of type <i>T</i> constrained by these discriminants. The value of this object is then converted to the subtype of <i>Item</i> and is assigned to <i>Item</i>. Finally, the Read attribute for each nondiscriminant component of <i>Item</i> is called in canonical order as described above. Normal default initialization and finalization take place for the created object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.b_13.13.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A discriminant with a default value is treated simply as a component of the object. On the other hand, an array bound or a discriminant without a default value, is treated as &ldquo;descriptor&rdquo; or &ldquo;dope&rdquo; that must be provided in order to create the object and thus is logically separate from the regular components. Such &ldquo;descriptor&rdquo; data are written by 'Output and produced as part of the delivered result by the 'Input function, but they are not written by 'Write nor read by 'Read. A tag is like a discriminant without a default.<br />

<MarginText>9.b.1/1_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00108-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0040</i>{"}"} For limited type extensions, we must have a definition of 'Read and 'Write if the parent type has one, as it is possible to make a dispatching call through the attributes. The rule is designed to automatically do the right thing in as many cases as possible.<br />

<MarginText>9.b.2/1_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Similarly, a type that has a progenitor with an available attribute must also have that attribute, for the same reason.<br />

<MarginText>9.b.3/3_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0023-1"]} />
The semantics of S'Read for a discriminated type with defaults involves an anonymous object so that the point of required initialization and finalization is well-defined, especially for objects that change shape and have controlled components. The creation of this anonymous object often can be omitted (see the Implementation Permissions below). <br />

<MarginText>9.c/2_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00195-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For a composite object, the subprogram denoted by the Write or Read attribute of each component is called, whether it is the default or is user-specified. Implementations are allowed to optimize these calls (see below), presuming the properties of the attributes are preserved. <br />

<MarginText>9.3/5_13.13.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00270-01", "AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
<p>Constraint{"_"}Error is raised by the predefined Write attribute if the value of the elementary item is outside the range of values representable using Stream{"_"}Size bits. For a signed integer type, an enumeration type, or a fixed point type, the range is unsigned only if the integer code for the lower bound of the first subtype is nonnegative, and a (symmetric) signed range that covers all values of the first subtype would require more than Stream{"_"}Size bits; otherwise, the range is signed.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10_13.13.2</MarginText>

procedure S'Class'Write({"\n"}   Stream : not null access Ada.Streams.Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type'Class;{"\n"}   Item   : in T'Class){"\n"}
