# 3.1. Declarations

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  19

# 3.1. Declarations

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0373-1"]} />
<p>The language defines several kinds of named <i>entities</i> that are declared by declarations. The entity's <i>name</i> is defined by the declaration, usually by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining{"_"}identifier</a></code>, but sometimes by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0040">defining{"_"}character{"_"}literal</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0203">defining{"_"}operator{"_"}symbol</a></code>. There are also entities that are not directly declared; some of these are elements of other entities, or are allocated dynamically. Such entities can be denoted using <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>, or dereference <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0373-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Some entities are always anonymous. For instance, a type is never named (the name represents the first subtype). We don't mention those here as this paragraph is about <i>named</i> entities. <br />

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>There are several forms of declaration. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0021">basic_declaration</a></code> is a form of declaration defined as follows. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01", "AI05-0177-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>basic{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0021"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0026">subtype_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0076">abstract_subprogram_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code>	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression_function_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code>	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.1#S0303">exception_declaration</a></code>	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0310">generic_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>defining{"_"}identifier</code><a id="S0022"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>A <i>declaration</i> is a language construct that associates a name with (a view of) an entity. A declaration may appear explicitly in the program text (an <i>explicit</i> declaration), or may be supposed to occur at a given place in the text as a consequence of the semantics of another construct (an <i>implicit</i> declaration). <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>An implicit declaration generally declares a predefined or inherited operation associated with the definition of a type. This term is used primarily when allowing explicit declarations to override implicit declarations, as part of a type declaration. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>declaration</b> &mdash; language construct that associates a name with (a view of) an entity<br />Note: A declaration can appear explicitly in the program text (an explicit declaration), or can be supposed to occur at a given place in the text as a consequence of the semantics of another construct (an implicit declaration).<br />

<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0255-1", "AI05-0277-1", "AI12-0061-1", "AI12-0308-1"]} />
<p>Each of the following is defined to be a declaration: any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0021">basic{"_"}declaration</a></code>; an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0039">enumeration{"_"}literal{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component{"_"}declaration</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0119">iterated{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk{"_"}specification</a></code>; an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0186">iterator{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram{"_"}body</a></code>; an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended{"_"}return{"_"}object{"_"}declaration</a></code>; an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code>; an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry{"_"}index{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0314">generic{"_"}formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}declaration</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This list (when <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0021">basic_declaration</a></code> is expanded out) contains all syntactic categories that end in "{"_"}declaration" or "{"_"}specification", except for program unit {"_"}specifications. Moreover, it contains <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is a declaration, whether or not it completes a previous declaration. This is a bit strange, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is not part of the syntax of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0021">basic_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library_unit_declaration</a></code>. A renaming-as-body is considered a declaration. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is not considered a declaration. Completions are sometimes declarations, and sometimes not. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>All declarations contain a <i>definition</i> for a <i>view</i> of an entity. A view consists of an identification of the entity (the entity <i>of</i> the view), plus view-specific characteristics that affect the use of the entity through that view (such as mode of access to an object, formal parameter names and defaults for a subprogram, or visibility to components of a type). In most cases, a declaration also contains the definition for the entity itself (a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> is an example of a declaration that does not define a new entity, but instead defines a view of an existing entity (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5">8.5</a>)).<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a.1/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>view of an entity</b> &mdash; representation of an entity that reveals some or all of the properties of the entity<br />Note: A single entity can have multiple views.<br />

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Most declarations define a view (of some entity) whose view-specific characteristics are unchanging for the life of the view. However, subtypes are somewhat unusual in that they inherit characteristics from whatever view of their type is currently visible. Hence, a subtype is not a <i>view</i> of a type; it is more of an indirect reference. By contrast, a private type provides a single, unchanging (partial) view of its full type. <br />

<MarginText>7.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0080-1"]} />
<p>When it is clear from context, the term <i>object</i> is used in place of <i>view of an object</i>. Similarly, the terms <i>type</i> and <i>subtype</i> are used in place of <i>view of a type</i> and <i>view of a subtype</i>, respectively.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.b/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Rules interpreted at compile time generally refer to views of entities, rather than the entities themselves. This is necessary to preserve privacy; characteristics that are not visible should not be used in compile-time rules. Thus, Static Semantics and Legality Rules generally implicitly have &ldquo;view of&rdquo;. Legality Rules that need to look into the private part are the exception to this interpretation.<br />

<MarginText>7.c/3</MarginText>
On the other hand, run-time rules can work either way, so &ldquo;view of&rdquo; should not be assumed in Dynamic Semantics rules.<br />

<MarginText>7.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0191-1"]} />
For example, a reference to the components of an object in a rule that is interpreted at compile time would not apply to components that are not visible. On the other hand, a reference to the components of an object in a dynamic semantics rule would apply to all components of the object, visible or not, including (for tagged objects) components which are not components of the nominal type of the object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a>). Other terms, such as &ldquo;subcomponent&rdquo; and &ldquo;part&rdquo;, are interpreted analogously. <br />

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>For each declaration, the language rules define a certain region of text called the <i>scope</i> of the declaration (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.2">8.2</a>). Most declarations associate an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> with a declared entity. Within its scope, and only there, there are places where it is possible to use the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> to refer to the declaration, the view it defines, and the associated entity; these places are defined by the visibility rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3">8.3</a>). At such places the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> is said to be a <i>name</i> of the entity (the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>); the name is said to <i>denote</i> the declaration, the view, and the associated entity (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>). The declaration is said to <i>declare</i> the name, the view, and in most cases, the entity itself.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>As an alternative to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, an enumeration literal can be declared with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code> as its name (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.1">3.5.1</a>), and a function can be declared with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> as its name (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>The syntax rules use the terms <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0040">defining{"_"}character{"_"}literal</a></code>, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0203">defining{"_"}operator{"_"}symbol</a></code> for the defining occurrence of a name; these are collectively called <i>defining names</i>. The terms <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> are used for usage occurrences of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>s. These are collectively called <i>usage names</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The terms <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> are used directly in contexts where the normal visibility rules do not apply (such as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> that appears after the <b>end</b> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>). Analogous conventions apply to the use of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0199">designator</a></code>, which is the collective term for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>The process by which a construct achieves its run-time effect is called <i>execution</i>. This process is also called <i>elaboration</i> for declarations and <i>evaluation</i> for expressions. One of the terms execution, elaboration, or evaluation is defined by this Reference Manual for each construct that has a run-time effect. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a.1/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>execution</b> &mdash; process by which a construct achieves its run-time effect<br />Note: Execution of a declaration is also called elaboration. Execution of an expression is also called evaluation.<br />

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The term elaboration is also used for the execution of certain constructs that are not declarations, and the term evaluation is used for the execution of certain constructs that are not expressions. For example, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>s are elaborated, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>s are evaluated.<br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
For bodies, execution and elaboration are both explicitly defined. When we refer specifically to the execution of a body, we mean the explicit definition of execution for that kind of body, not its elaboration. <br />

<MarginText>11.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Technically, "the execution of a declaration" and "the elaboration of a declaration" are synonymous. We use the term "elaboration" of a construct when we know the construct is elaborable. When we are talking about more arbitrary constructs, we use the term "execution". For example, we use the term "erroneous execution", to refer to any erroneous execution, including erroneous elaboration or evaluation.<br />

<MarginText>11.d</MarginText>
When we explicitly define evaluation or elaboration for a construct, we are implicitly defining execution of that construct.<br />

<MarginText>11.e</MarginText>
We also use the term "execution" for things like <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s, which are executable, but neither elaborable nor evaluable. We considered using the term "execution" only for nonelaborable, nonevaluable constructs, and defining the term "action" to mean what we have defined "execution" to mean. We rejected this idea because we thought three terms that mean the same thing was enough &mdash; four would be overkill. Thus, the term "action" is used only informally in the standard (except where it is defined as part of a larger term, such as "protected action"). <br />

<MarginText>11.e.1/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>elaboration</b> &mdash; process by which a declaration achieves its run-time effect<br />Note: Elaboration is one of the forms of execution.<br />

<MarginText>11.e.2/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>evaluation</b> &mdash; process by which an expression achieves its run-time effect<br />Note: Evaluation is one of the forms of execution.<br />

<MarginText>11.f</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>A construct is <i>elaborable</i> if elaboration is defined for it. A construct is <i>evaluable</i> if evaluation is defined for it. A construct is <i>executable</i> if execution is defined for it. <br />

<MarginText>11.g</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Don't confuse &ldquo;elaborable&rdquo; with &ldquo;preelaborable&rdquo; (defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>11.h/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
Evaluation of an evaluable construct produces a result that is either a value, a denotation, or a range. The following are evaluable: expression; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry_index_specification</a></code>; and possibly <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>. The last one is curious &mdash; RM83 uses the term &ldquo;evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>&rdquo;, but never defines it. One might presume that the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> consists of the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>, depending on what it is. But <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>s are not evaluated; they are elaborated.<br />

<MarginText>11.i</MarginText>
Intuitively, an <i>executable</i> construct is one that has a defined run-time effect (which may be null). Since execution includes elaboration and evaluation as special cases, all elaborable and all evaluable constructs are also executable. Hence, most constructs in Ada are executable. An important exception is that the constructs inside a generic unit are not executable directly, but rather are used as a template for (generally) executable constructs in instances of the generic. <br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
NOTE   At compile time, the declaration of an entity <i>declares</i> the entity. At run time, the elaboration of the declaration <i>creates</i> the entity. <br />

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Syntactic categories for declarations are named either <i>entity{"_"}</i><code>declaration</code> (if they include a trailing semicolon) or <i>entity{"_"}</i><code>specification</code> (if not).<br />

<MarginText>12.b</MarginText>
The various kinds of named entities that can be declared are as follows: an object (including components and parameters), a named number, a type (the name always refers to its first subtype), a subtype, a subprogram (including enumeration literals and operators), a single entry, an entry family, a package, a protected or task unit (which corresponds to either a type or a single object), an exception, a generic unit, a label, and the name of a statement.<br />

<MarginText>12.c</MarginText>
Identifiers are also associated with names of pragmas, arguments to pragmas, and with attributes, but these are not user-definable. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>12.d</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> is new. It is used for the defining occurrence of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>. Usage occurrences use the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> syntactic categories. Each occurrence of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> (or <code>simple{"_"}name</code>), <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> in the Ada 83 syntax rules is handled as follows in Ada 95: <br />

<MarginText>12.e</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>It becomes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0040">defining_character_literal</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0203">defining_operator_symbol</a></code> (or some syntactic category composed of these), to indicate a defining occurrence;<br /></li>
<MarginText>12.f</MarginText>
<li>It becomes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>, in usage occurrences where the usage is required (in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/">8</a> to be directly visible;<br /></li>
<MarginText>12.g</MarginText>
<li>It becomes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>, in usage occurrences where the usage is required (in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/">8</a>) to be visible but not necessarily directly visible;<br /></li>
<MarginText>12.h</MarginText>
<li>It remains an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>, in cases where the visibility rules do not apply (such as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0199">designator</a></code> that appears after the <b>end</b> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.i</MarginText>
For declarations that come in &ldquo;two parts&rdquo; (program unit declaration plus body, private or incomplete type plus full type, deferred constant plus full constant), we consider both to be defining occurrences. Thus, for example, the syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> uses <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> after the reserved word <b>body</b>, as opposed to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>12.j</MarginText>
The defining occurrence of a statement name is in its implicit declaration, not where it appears in the program text. Considering the statement name itself to be the defining occurrence would complicate the visibility rules.<br />

<MarginText>12.k</MarginText>
The phrase &ldquo;visible by selection&rdquo; is not used in Ada 95. It is subsumed by simply &ldquo;visible&rdquo; and the Name Resolution Rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>12.l/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
(Note that in Ada 95, a declaration is visible at all places where one could have used a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>, not just at places where a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> was actually used. Thus, the places where a declaration is directly visible are a subset of the places where it is visible. See Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/">8</a> for details.)<br />

<MarginText>12.m</MarginText>
We use the term &ldquo;declaration&rdquo; to cover <code>{"_"}specification</code>s that declare (views of) objects, such as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter_specification</a></code>s. In Ada 83, these are referred to as a &ldquo;form of declaration&rdquo;, but it is not entirely clear that they are considered simply &ldquo;declarations&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>12.n/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
RM83 contains an incomplete definition of "elaborated" in this subclause: it defines "elaborated" for declarations, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0286">compilation_unit</a></code>s, but "elaboration" is defined elsewhere for various other constructs. To make matters worse, Ada 95 has a different set of elaborable constructs. Instead of correcting the list, it is more maintainable to refer to the term "elaborable," which is defined in a distributed manner.<br />

<MarginText>12.o</MarginText>
RM83 uses the term &ldquo;has no other effect&rdquo; to describe an elaboration that doesn't do anything except change the state from not-yet-elaborated to elaborated. This was a confusing wording, because the answer to &ldquo;other than what?&rdquo; was to be found many pages away. In Ada 95, we change this wording to &ldquo;has no effect&rdquo; (for things that truly do nothing at run time), and &ldquo;has no effect other than to establish that so-and-so can happen without failing the Elaboration{"_"}Check&rdquo; (for things where it matters).<br />

<MarginText>12.p</MarginText>
We make it clearer that the term "execution" covers elaboration and evaluation as special cases. This was implied in RM83. For example, "erroneous execution" can include any execution, and RM83-9.4(3) has, "The task designated by any other task object depends on the master whose execution creates the task object;" the elaboration of the master's <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> is doing the task creation. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>12.q/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
Added <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> to the list of declarations.<br />

<MarginText>12.r/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />
Added null procedures (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7">6.7</a>) to the syntax. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>12.s/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
Added expression functions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8">6.8</a>) to the syntax. <br />

# 3.10. Access Types

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10.mdx

sidebar_position:  28

# 3.10. Access Types

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>A value of an access type (an <i>access value</i>) provides indirect access to the object or subprogram it <i>designates</i>. Depending on its type, an access value can designate either subprograms, objects created by allocators (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>), or more generally <i>aliased</i> objects of an appropriate type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <i>denotes</i> an entity; an access value <i>designates</i> an entity. The &ldquo;dereference&rdquo; of an access value X, written &ldquo;X.<b>all</b>&rdquo;, is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes the entity designated by X. <br />

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
Access values should always be well defined (barring uses of certain unchecked features of Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/">13</a>). In particular, uninitialized access variables should be prevented by compile-time rules. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>access{"_"}type{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0079"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0080">access_to_object_definition</a></code><br />  | [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0082">access_to_subprogram_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>access{"_"}to{"_"}object{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0080"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>access</b> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0081">general_access_modifier</a></code>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

</CodeBlock>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>7/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00062-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0012</i>{"}"} There are two kinds of access types, <i>access-to-object</i> types, whose values designate objects, and <i>access-to-subprogram</i> types, whose values designate subprograms. Associated with an access-to-object type is a <i>storage pool</i>; several access types may share the same storage pool. All descendants of an access type share the same storage pool. A storage pool is an area of storage used to hold dynamically allocated objects (called <i>pool elements</i>) created by allocators[; storage pools are described further in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">Storage Management</a>&rdquo;].<br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>Access-to-object types are further subdivided into <i>pool-specific</i> access types, whose values can designate only the elements of their associated storage pool, and <i>general</i> access types, whose values can designate the elements of any storage pool, as well as aliased objects created by declarations rather than allocators, and aliased subcomponents of other objects. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The value of an access type will typically be a machine address. However, a value of a pool-specific access type can be represented as an offset (or index) relative to its storage pool, since it can point only to the elements of that pool. <br />

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00225-01", "AI95-00363-01", "AI05-0053-1", "AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0277-1", "AI12-0228-1", "AI12-0324-1"]} />
<p>A view of an object is defined to be <i>aliased</i> if it is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object{"_"}declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component{"_"}definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> with the reserved word <b>aliased</b>, or by a renaming of an aliased view. In addition, the dereference of an access-to-object value denotes an aliased view, as does a view conversion (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>) of an aliased view. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> denotes an aliased view when the operand denotes an aliased view. The current instance of an immutably limited type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>) is defined to be aliased. Finally, a formal parameter or generic formal object of a tagged type is defined to be aliased. [Aliased views are the ones that can be designated by an access value.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>aliased view</b> &mdash; view of an object that can be designated by an access value<br />Note: Objects allocated by allocators are aliased. Objects can also be explicitly declared as aliased with the reserved word aliased. The Access attribute can be used to create an access value designating an aliased object.<br />

<MarginText>9.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The current instance of a nonlimited type is not aliased.<br />

<MarginText>9.c</MarginText>
The object created by an allocator is aliased, but not its subcomponents, except of course for those that themselves have <b>aliased</b> in their <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>9.d</MarginText>
The renaming of an aliased object is aliased.<br />

<MarginText>9.e</MarginText>
Slices are never aliased. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.2">4.1.2</a> for more discussion. <br />

<MarginText>9.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00225-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The current instance of a limited type is defined to be aliased so that an access discriminant of a component can be initialized with T'Access inside the definition of T. Note that we don't want this to apply to a type that could become nonlimited later within its immediate scope, so we require the full definition to be limited.<br />

<MarginText>9.g</MarginText>
A formal parameter of a tagged type is defined to be aliased so that a (tagged) parameter X may be passed to an access parameter P by using P ={">"} X'Access. Access parameters are most important for tagged types because of dispatching-on-access-parameters (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>). By restricting this to formal parameters, we minimize problems associated with allowing components that are not declared aliased to be pointed-to from within the same record.<br />

<MarginText>9.h</MarginText>
A view conversion of an aliased view is aliased so that the type of an access parameter can be changed without first converting to a named access type. For example: <br />

<MarginText>9.i</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type T1 is tagged ...;{"\n"}procedure P(X : access T1);{"\n"}
<MarginText>9.j</MarginText>
type T2 is new T1 with ...;{"\n"}procedure P(X : access T2) is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}    P(T1(X.all)'Access);  -- hand off to T1's P{"\n"}    . . .     -- now do extra T2-specific processing{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>9.l/2</MarginText>
We considered making more kinds of objects aliased by default. In particular, any object of a by-reference type will pretty much have to be allocated at an addressable location, so it can be passed by reference without using bit-field pointers. Therefore, one might wish to allow the Access and Unchecked{"_"}Access attributes for such objects. However, private parts are transparent to the definition of &ldquo;by-reference type&rdquo;, so if we made all objects of a by-reference type aliased, we would be violating the privacy of private parts. Instead, we would have to define a concept of &ldquo;visibly by-reference&rdquo; and base the rule on that. This seemed to complicate the rules more than it was worth, especially since there is no way to declare an untagged limited private type to be by-reference, since the full type might by nonlimited. <br />

<MarginText>9.m</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that we do not use the term &ldquo;aliased&rdquo; to refer to formal parameters that are referenced through multiple access paths (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.2">6.2</a>). <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0080">access_to_object_definition</a></code> defines an access-to-object type and its first subtype; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> defines the <i>designated subtype</i> of the access type. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0081">general{"_"}access{"_"}modifier</a></code> appears, then the access type is a general access type. If the modifier is the reserved word <b>constant</b>, then the type is an <i>access-to-constant type</i>[; a designated object cannot be updated through a value of such a type]. If the modifier is the reserved word <b>all</b>, then the type is an <i>access-to-variable type</i>[; a designated object can be both read and updated through a value of such a type]. If no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0081">general{"_"}access{"_"}modifier</a></code> appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0080">access{"_"}to{"_"}object{"_"}definition</a></code>, the access type is a pool-specific access-to-variable type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The type of the designated subtype is called the <i>designated type</i>. <br />

<MarginText>10.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The modifier <b>all</b> was picked to suggest that values of a general access type could point into &ldquo;all&rdquo; storage pools, as well as to objects declared aliased, and that &ldquo;all&rdquo; access (both read and update) to the designated object was provided. We couldn't think of any use for pool-specific access-to-constant types, so any access type defined with the modifier <b>constant</b> is considered a general access type, and can point into any storage pool or at other (appropriate) aliased objects. <br />

<MarginText>10.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The predefined generic Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation can be instantiated for any named access-to-variable type. There is no (language-defined) support for deallocating objects designated by a value of an access-to-constant type. Because of this, an allocator for an access-to-constant type can allocate out of a storage pool with no support for deallocation. Frequently, the allocation can be done at link-time, if the size and initial value are known then. <br />

<MarginText>10.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For the purpose of generic formal type matching, the relevant subclasses of access types are access-to-subprogram types, access-to-constant types, and (named) access-to-variable types, with its subclass (named) general access-to-variable types. Pool-specific access-to-variable types are not a separately matchable subclass of types, since they don't have any &ldquo;extra&rdquo; operations relative to all (named) access-to-variable types. <br />

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0082">access_to_subprogram_definition</a></code> defines an access-to-subprogram type and its first subtype; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0204">parameter_profile</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0205">parameter_and_result_profile</a></code> defines the <i>designated profile</i> of the access type. There is a <i>calling convention</i> associated with the designated profile[; only subprograms with this calling convention can be designated by values of the access type.] By default, the calling convention is &ldquo;<i>protected</i>&rdquo; if the reserved word <b>protected</b> appears, and &ldquo;Ada&rdquo; otherwise. [See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/">Annex B</a> for how to override this default.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The calling convention <i>protected</i> is in italics to emphasize that it cannot be specified explicitly by the user. This is a consequence of it being a reserved word. <br />

<MarginText>11.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00254-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>For a named access-to-subprogram type, the representation of an access value might include implementation-defined information needed to support up-level references &mdash; for example, a static link. The accessibility rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>) ensure that in a "global-display-based" implementation model (as opposed to a static-link-based model), a named access-to-(unprotected)-subprogram value need consist only of the address of the subprogram. The global display is guaranteed to be properly set up any time the designated subprogram is called. Even in a static-link-based model, the only time a static link is definitely required is for an access-to-subprogram type declared in a scope nested at least two levels deep within subprogram or task bodies, since values of such a type might designate subprograms nested a smaller number of levels. For the normal case of a named access-to-subprogram type declared at the outermost (library) level, a code address by itself should be sufficient to represent the access value in many implementations.<br />

<MarginText>11.c</MarginText>
For access-to-protected-subprogram, the access values will necessarily include both an address (or other identification) of the code of the subprogram, as well as the address of the associated protected object. This could be thought of as a static link, but it will be needed even for global-display-based implementation models. It corresponds to the value of the &ldquo;implicit parameter&rdquo; that is passed into every call of a protected operation, to identify the current instance of the protected type on which they are to operate.<br />

<MarginText>11.d</MarginText>
Any Elaboration{"_"}Check is performed when a call is made through an access value, rather than when the access value is first "created" via a 'Access. For implementation models that normally put that check at the call-site, an access value will have to point to a separate entry point that does the check. Alternatively, the access value could point to a "subprogram descriptor" that consisted of two words (or perhaps more), the first being the address of the code, the second being the elaboration bit. Or perhaps more efficiently, just the address of the code, but using the trick that the descriptor is initialized to point to a Raise-Program-Error routine initially, and then set to point to the "real" code when the body is elaborated.<br />

<MarginText>11.e</MarginText>
For implementations that share code between generic instantiations, the extra level of indirection suggested above to support Elaboration{"_"}Checks could also be used to provide a pointer to the per-instance data area normally required when calling shared code. The trick would be to put a pointer to the per-instance data area into the subprogram descriptor, and then make sure that the address of the subprogram descriptor is loaded into a "known" register whenever an indirect call is performed. Once inside the shared code, the address of the per-instance data area can be retrieved out of the subprogram descriptor, by indexing off the "known" register.<br />

<MarginText>11.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00344-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>11.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00254-01"]} />
Note that access parameters of an anonymous access-to-subprogram type are permitted. Such parameters represent full &ldquo;downward&rdquo; closures, meaning that in an implementation that uses a per-task (global) display, the display will have to be passed as a hidden parameter, and reconstructed at the point of call. <br />

<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00231-01", "AI95-00254-01", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> defines an anonymous general access type or an anonymous access-to-subprogram type. For a general access type, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes its <i>designated subtype</i>; if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0081">general{"_"}access{"_"}modifier</a></code> <b>constant</b> appears, the type is an access-to-constant type; otherwise, it is an access-to-variable type. For an access-to-subprogram type, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0204">parameter{"_"}profile</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0205">parameter{"_"}and{"_"}result{"_"}profile</a></code> denotes its <i>designated profile</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00231-01"]} />
<p>For each access type, there is a null access value designating no entity at all, which can be obtained by (implicitly) converting the literal <b>null</b> to the access type. [The null value of an access type is the default initial value of the type.] Nonnull values of an access-to-object type are obtained by evaluating an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>[, which returns an access value designating a newly created object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>)], or in the case of a general access-to-object type, evaluating an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> for the Access or Unchecked{"_"}Access attribute of an aliased view of an object. Nonnull values of an access-to-subprogram type are obtained by evaluating an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> for the Access attribute of a nonintrinsic subprogram.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>13.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>13.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> in a construct specifies that the null value does not belong to the access subtype defined by the construct, that is, the access subtype <i>excludes null</i>. In addition, the anonymous access subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> for a controlling access parameter (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>) excludes null. Finally, for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>, the subtype denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> excludes null if and only if the subtype denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> excludes null. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> used in a controlling parameter excludes null because it is necessary to read the tag to dispatch, and null has no tag. We would have preferred to require <b>not null</b> to be specified for such parameters, but that would have been too incompatible with Ada 95 code to require.<br />

<MarginText>13.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01"]} />
Note that we considered imposing a similar implicit null exclusion for controlling access results, but chose not to do that, because there is no Ada 95 compatibility issue, and there is no automatic null check inherent in the use of a controlling access result. If a null check is necessary, it is because there is a dereference of the result, or because the value is passed to a parameter whose subtype excludes null. If there is no dereference of the result, a null return value is perfectly acceptable, and can be a useful indication of a particular status of the call. <br />

<MarginText>14/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00012-01", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0013</i>{"}"} [All subtypes of an access-to-subprogram type are constrained.] The first subtype of a type defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0080">access_to_object_definition</a></code> is unconstrained if the designated subtype is an unconstrained array or discriminated subtype; otherwise, it is constrained. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The Legality Rules on <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range_constraint</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>) do not permit the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> to denote an access-to-scalar type, only a scalar type. The Legality Rules on <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.1">3.6.1</a>) and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#Subclause_3.7.1">3.7.1</a>) both permit access-to-composite types in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> with such {"_"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code>s. Note that an access-to-access-to-composite is never permitted in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>14.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Only <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0031">composite_constraint</a></code>s are permitted for an access type, and only on access-to-composite types. A constraint on an access-to-scalar or access-to-access type might be violated due to assignments via other access paths that were not so constrained. By contrast, if the designated subtype is an array or discriminated type without defaults, the constraint could not be violated by unconstrained assignments, since array objects are always constrained, and  discriminated objects are also constrained when the type does not have defaults for its discriminants. Constraints are not allowed on general access-to-unconstrained discriminated types if the type has defaults for its discriminants; constraints on pool-specific access types are usually allowed because allocated objects are usually constrained by their initial value. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>14.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0205">parameter{"_"}and{"_"}result{"_"}profile</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object{"_"}renaming{"_"}declaration</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.4#S0319">formal{"_"}object{"_"}declaration</a></code> has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null{"_"}exclusion</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype{"_"}mark</a></code> in that construct shall denote an access subtype that does not exclude null. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>This means &ldquo;directly allowed in&rdquo;; we are not talking about a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> that occurs in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> in one of these constructs (for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is not restricted). <br />

<MarginText>14.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is similar to doubly constraining a composite subtype, which we also don't allow. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>15/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0031">composite_constraint</a></code> is <i>compatible</i> with an unconstrained access subtype if it is compatible with the designated subtype. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> is compatible with any access subtype that does not exclude null. An access value <i>satisfies</i> a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0031">composite_constraint</a></code> of an access subtype if it equals the null value of its type or if it designates an object whose value satisfies the constraint. An access value satisfies an exclusion of the null value if it does not equal the null value of its type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0079">access_type_definition</a></code> creates the access type and its first subtype. For an access-to-object type, this elaboration includes the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>, which creates the designated subtype.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00254-01"]} />
<p>The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> creates an anonymous access type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
NOTE 1   Access values are called &ldquo;pointers&rdquo; or &ldquo;references&rdquo; in some other languages.<br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
NOTE 2   Each access-to-object type has an associated storage pool; several access types can share the same pool. An object can be created in the storage pool of an access type by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>) for the access type. A storage pool (roughly) corresponds to what some other languages call a &ldquo;heap&rdquo;. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a> for a discussion of pools.<br />

<MarginText>20</MarginText>
NOTE 3   Only <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>s can be applied to access types (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.1">3.6.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#Subclause_3.7.1">3.7.1</a>). <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of access-to-object types:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>22/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01", "AI12-0056-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Frame is access Matrix;  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>{"\n"}type Peripheral{"_"}Ref is not null access Peripheral;  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>{"\n"}type Binop{"_"}Ptr is access all Binary{"_"}Operation'Class;{"\n"}                              -- general access-to-class-wide, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of an access subtype:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
subtype Drum{"_"}Ref is Peripheral{"_"}Ref(Drum); -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of an access-to-subprogram type:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>26</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Message{"_"}Procedure is access procedure (M : in String := "Error!");{"\n"}procedure Default{"_"}Message{"_"}Procedure(M : in String);{"\n"}Give{"_"}Message : Message{"_"}Procedure := Default{"_"}Message{"_"}Procedure'Access;{"\n"}...{"\n"}procedure Other{"_"}Procedure(M : in String);{"\n"}...{"\n"}Give{"_"}Message := Other{"_"}Procedure'Access;{"\n"}...{"\n"}Give{"_"}Message("File not found.");{"\n"}                         -- call with parameter (.all is optional){"\n"}Give{"_"}Message.all;        -- call with no parameters{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>26.a</MarginText>
The syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0079">access_type_definition</a></code> is changed to support general access types (including access-to-constants) and access-to-subprograms. The syntax rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0081">general_access_modifier</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> are new. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>26.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
We use the term "storage pool" to talk about the data area from which allocation takes place. The term "collection" is only used for finalization. ("Collection" and "storage pool" are not the same thing because multiple unrelated access types can share the same storage pool; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a> for more discussion.) <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 95

<MarginText>26.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
Access discriminants and noncontrolling access parameters no longer exclude null. A program which passed <b>null</b> to such an access discriminant or access parameter and expected it to raise Constraint{"_"}Error may fail when compiled with Ada 2005. One hopes that there no such programs outside of the ACATS. (Of course, a program which actually wants to pass <b>null</b> will work, which is far more likely.)<br />

<MarginText>26.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
Most unconstrained aliased objects with defaulted discriminants are no longer constrained by their initial values. This means that a program that raised Constraint{"_"}Error from an attempt to change the discriminants will no longer do so. The change only affects programs that depended on the raising of Constraint{"_"}Error in this case, so the inconsistency is unlikely to occur outside of the ACATS. This change may however cause compilers to implement these objects differently, possibly taking additional memory or time. This is unlikely to be worse than the differences caused by any major compiler upgrade. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>26.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00225-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> The rule defining when a current instance of a limited type is considered to be aliased has been tightened to apply only to types that cannot become nonlimited. A program that attempts to take 'Access of the current instance of a limited type that can become nonlimited will be illegal in Ada 2005. While original Ada 95 allowed the current instance of any limited type to be treated as aliased, this was inconsistently implemented in compilers, and was likely to not work as expected for types that are ultimately nonlimited.<br />

<MarginText>26.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0289-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Static matching (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9#Subclause_4.9.1">4.9.1</a>) requires that both anonymous access types exclude null; and full conformance requires statically matching subtypes. Because of the definition of &ldquo;excludes null&rdquo; given in this subclause, an access parameter that designates an untagged private type P (which does not exclude null) does not match its completion if P is completed with a tagged type (in that case, the parameter is controlling and thus excludes null, regardless of whether there is an explicit null exclusion on the body). Similar considerations apply in contexts where mode conformance and subtype conformance are required (for instance, subprogram renaming). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>26.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> is new. It can be used in both anonymous and named access type definitions. It is most useful to declare that parameters cannot be <b>null</b>, thus eliminating the need for checks on use.<br />

<MarginText>26.h/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI95-00254-01", "AI95-00404-01"]} />
The kinds of anonymous access types allowed were increased by adding anonymous access-to-constant and anonymous access-to-subprogram types. Anonymous access-to-subprogram types used as parameters allow passing of subprograms at any level. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>26.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00062-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0012</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added accidentally-omitted wording that says that a derived access type shares its storage pool with its parent type. This was clearly intended, both because of a note in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4">3.4</a>, and because anything else would have been incompatible with Ada 83.<br />

<MarginText>26.j/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00012-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0013</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Fixed typographical errors in the description of when access types are constrained.<br />

<MarginText>26.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
The wording was fixed to allow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s and the literal <b>null</b> for anonymous access types. The former was clearly intended by Ada 95; see the  in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>.<br />

<MarginText>26.l/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
The rules about aliased objects being constrained by their initial values now apply only to allocated objects, and thus have been moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">Allocators</a>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.m/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0053-1", "AI05-0277-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The rule about a current instance being aliased now is worded in terms of immutably limited types. Wording was also added to make extended return object declarations that have the keyword <b>aliased</b> be considered aliased. This latter was a significant oversight in Ada 2005 &mdash; technically, the keyword <b>aliased</b> had no effect. But of course implementations followed the intent, not the letter of the Reference Manual.<br />

<MarginText>26.n/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
Explicitly aliased parameters (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>) are defined to be aliased. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.o/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0228-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> of an aliased object is now also aliased. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.10.1"></a>

## 3.10.1  Incomplete Type Declarations

<MarginText>1_3.10.1</MarginText>
<p>There are no particular limitations on the designated type of an access type. In particular, the type of a component of the designated type can be another access type, or even the same access type. This permits mutually dependent and recursive access types. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code> can be used to introduce a type to be used as a designated type, while deferring its full definition to a subsequent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0085"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>type</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code>] [<b>is tagged</b>];<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2.1/4_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI12-0137-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code> declares an <i>incomplete view</i> of a type and its first subtype; the first subtype is unconstrained if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code> appears. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> includes the reserved word <b>tagged</b>, it declares a <i>tagged incomplete view</i>. If <i>T</i> denotes a tagged incomplete view, then <i>T</i>'Class denotes a tagged incomplete view. [An incomplete view of a type is a limited view of the type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>).]<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.2/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<p>Given an access type <i>A</i> whose designated type <i>T</i> is an incomplete view, a dereference of a value of type <i>A</i> also has this incomplete view except when: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0208-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Whether the designated type is an incomplete view (and thus whether this set of rules applies) is determined by the view of the type at the declaration of the access type; it does not change during the life of the type. <br />

<MarginText>2.3/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>it occurs within the immediate scope of the completion of <i>T</i>, or<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.4/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0208-1"]} />
<li>it occurs within the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0296">nonlimited_with_clause</a></code> that mentions a library package in whose visible part the completion of <i>T</i> is declared, or<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.5/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0208-1"]} />
<li>it occurs within the scope of the completion of <i>T</i> and <i>T</i> is an incomplete view declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>2.6/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0162-1"]} />
<p>In these cases, the dereference has the view of <i>T</i> visible at the point of the dereference. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.b/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We need the &ldquo;in whose visible part&rdquo; rule so that the second rule doesn't trigger in the body of a package with a <b>with</b> of a child unit: <br />

<MarginText>2.c/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package P is{"\n"}private{"\n"}   type T;{"\n"}   type PtrT is access T;{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>2.d/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
private package P.C is{"\n"}   Ptr : PtrT;{"\n"}end P.C;{"\n"}
<MarginText>2.e/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
with P.C;{"\n"}package body P is{"\n"}    -- Ptr.all'Size is not legal here, but we are within the scope{"\n"}    -- of a <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0296">nonlimited_with_clause</a> for P.{"\n"}type T is ...{"\n"}    --  Ptr.all'Size is legal here.{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.7/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00412-01", "AI05-0162-1", "AI05-0208-1"]} />
<p>Similarly, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0026">subtype_declaration</a></code> defining a subtype of an incomplete view <i>T</i>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes an incomplete view except under the same three circumstances given above, in which case it denotes the view of <i>T</i> visible at the point of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0162-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> requires a completion, which shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type{"_"}declaration</a></code> other than an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code>. [If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> occurs immediately within either the visible part of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package{"_"}specification</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type{"_"}declaration</a></code> shall occur later and immediately within this visible part or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code>. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> occurs immediately within the private part of a given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package{"_"}specification</a></code>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type{"_"}declaration</a></code> shall occur later and immediately within either the private part itself, or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code> of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package{"_"}body</a></code>.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a_3.10.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This is implied by the next AARM-only rule, plus the rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#Subclause_3.11.1">3.11.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#Subclause_3.11.1">Completions of Declarations</a>&rdquo; which require a completion to appear later and immediately within the same declarative region. <br />

<MarginText>3.b_3.10.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code> occurs immediately within the visible part of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, then the completing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type{"_"}declaration</a></code> shall occur immediately within this visible part. <br />

<MarginText>3.c_3.10.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>If the implementation supports it, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code> can be imported (using aspect Import, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>), in which case no explicit completion is allowed. <br />

<MarginText>4/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0162-1"]} />
<p>If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> includes the reserved word <b>tagged</b>, then a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type{"_"}declaration</a></code> that completes it shall declare a tagged type. If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</a></code>, then a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type{"_"}declaration</a></code> that completes it shall have a fully conforming (explicit) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>). [If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> has no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code> (or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</a></code>), then a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type{"_"}declaration</a></code> is nevertheless allowed to have discriminants, either explicitly, or inherited via derivation.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes an incomplete view of a type may be used as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0098-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0080">access{"_"}to{"_"}object{"_"}definition</a></code>; [the only form of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> allowed in this <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code> [(a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> is not allowed)];] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a_3.10.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>We now allow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>s even if the full type is deferred to the package body. However, there is no particular implementation burden because we have dropped the concept of the dependent compatibility check. In other words, we have effectively repealed AI83-00007. <br />

<MarginText>7/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI95-00412-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0026">subtype_declaration</a></code>; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> shall not have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null{"_"}exclusion</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code>; <br /></li>
<MarginText>8/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0151-1"]} />
<li>as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> for an access-to-object type; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>This does not mean any random <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in a construct that makes up an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, such as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code>, just the one given directly in the syntax of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>8.1/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0151-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> defining the subtype of a parameter or result in a profile occurring within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0021">basic_declaration</a></code>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.b/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>But not in the profile for a body or entry. <br />

<MarginText>8.2/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0213-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>as a generic actual parameter whose corresponding generic formal parameter is a formal incomplete type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.3/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<p>If such a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes a tagged incomplete view, it may also be used:<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.4/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0151-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> defining the subtype of a parameter in the profile for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<li>as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute{"_"}designator</a></code> is Class; such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute{"_"}reference</a></code> is restricted to the uses allowed here; it denotes a tagged incomplete view. <br /></li>
</ul>

<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />

<MarginText>9.1/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0151-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>9.2/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0098-1", "AI05-0151-1"]} />
<ul>
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.b/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>9.3/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<p>If any of the above uses occurs as part of the declaration of a primitive subprogram of the incomplete view, and the declaration occurs immediately within the private part of a package, then the completion of the incomplete view shall also occur immediately within the private part; it shall not be deferred to the package body. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.c/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This fixes a hole in Ada 95 where a dispatching operation with an access parameter could be declared in a private part and a dispatching call on it could occur in a child even though there is no visibility on the full type, requiring access to the controlling tag without access to the representation of the type. <br />

<MarginText>9.4/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<p>No other uses of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes an incomplete view of a type are allowed.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0151-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> that denotes an object shall not be of an incomplete view. An actual parameter in a call shall not be of an untagged incomplete view. The result object of a function call shall not be of an incomplete view. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> shall not denote a subprogram having a formal parameter of an untagged incomplete view, nor a return type that is an incomplete view. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We used to disallow all dereferences of an incomplete type. Now we only disallow such dereferences when used as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>. Dereferences used in other contexts do not pose a problem since normal type matching will preclude their use except when the full type is &ldquo;nearby&rdquo; as context (for example, as the expected type).<br />

<MarginText>10.b/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
This also disallows <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es that are directly of an incomplete view. For instance, a parameter <i>P</i> can be declared of a tagged incomplete type, but we don't want to allow <i>P</i>'Size, <i>P</i>'Alignment, or the like, as representation values aren't known for an incomplete view.<br />

<MarginText>10.c/2_3.10.1</MarginText>
We say &ldquo;denotes an object&rdquo; so that prefixes that directly name an incomplete view are not covered; the previous rules cover such cases, and we certainly don't want to ban Incomp'Class.<br />

<MarginText>10.d/3_3.10.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0151-1"]} />
