<b></b>We assume the worst in a generic body whether or not a formal subtype has a constrained partial view; specifically, in a generic body a discriminated subtype is considered to have a constrained partial view if it is a descendant of an untagged generic formal private or derived type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a> for the formal definition of this rule). <br />

<MarginText>28/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0041-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The accessibility level of the view shall not be statically deeper than that of the access type <i>A</i>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>28.a_3.10.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In an instance body, a runtime check applies.<br />

<MarginText>28.b/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
If <i>A</i> is an anonymous access-to-object type of an access parameter, then the view can never have a deeper accessibility level than <i>A</i>. The same is true for an anonymous access-to-object type of an access discriminant, except when X'Access is used to initialize an access discriminant of an object created by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>. The latter case is illegal if the accessibility level of X is statically deeper than that of the access type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>; a runtime check is needed in the case where the initial value comes from an access parameter. Other anonymous access-to-object types have "normal" accessibility checks. <br />

<MarginText>28.b.1/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Additional restrictions exist in the specialized needs annexes. For instance, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a> includes additional restrictions on atomic and volatile <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es of the Access attribute. <br />

<MarginText>28.1/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0041-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these requirements apply also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29_3.10.2</MarginText>
<dd>A check is made that the accessibility level of X is not deeper than that of the access type <i>A</i>. If this check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>29.a/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The check is needed for access parameters  of an access-to-object type and in instance bodies.<br />

<MarginText>29.a.1/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0024-1"]} />
Because there are no access parameters permitted for task entries, the accessibility levels are always comparable. We would have to switch to the terminology used in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a> based on inclusion within masters if we relax this restriction. That might introduce unacceptable distributed overhead. <br />

<MarginText>29.b/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0148-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This check requires that some indication of lifetime is passed as an implicit parameter along with access parameters of an access-to-object type. A similar indication is required for stand-alone objects of anonymous access-to-object types.No such requirement applies to other anonymous access types, since the checks associated with them are all compile-time checks. <br />

<MarginText>30/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>If the nominal subtype of X does not statically match the designated subtype of <i>A</i>, a view conversion of X to the designated subtype is evaluated (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>) and the value of X'Access designates that view. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>31_3.10.2</MarginText>
<p>The following attribute is defined for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> P that denotes a subprogram: <br /></p>

<MarginText>32/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>P'Access</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00229-01", "AI95-00254-01", "AI05-0239-1", "AI12-0064-2"]} />
<dl>
<dd>P'Access yields an access value that designates the subprogram denoted by P. The type of P'Access is an access-to-subprogram type (<i>S</i>), as determined by the expected type. The accessibility level of P shall not be statically deeper than that of <i>S</i>. If <i>S</i> is nonblocking, P shall be nonblocking. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules apply also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. The profile of P shall be subtype conformant with the designated profile of <i>S</i>, and shall not be Intrinsic. If the subprogram denoted by P is declared within a generic unit, and the expression P'Access occurs within the body of that generic unit or within the body of a generic unit declared within the declarative region of the generic unit, then the ultimate ancestor of <i>S</i> shall be either a nonformal type declared within the generic unit or an anonymous access type of an access parameter.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>32.a/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00229-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The part about generic bodies is worded in terms of the denoted subprogram, not the denoted view; this implies that renaming is invisible to this part of the rule. &ldquo;Declared within the declarative region of the generic&rdquo; is referring to child and nested generic units. This rule is partly to prevent contract model problems with respect to the accessibility rules, and partly to ease shared-generic-body implementations, in which a subprogram declared in an instance needs to have a different calling convention from other subprograms with the same profile.<br />

<MarginText>32.b_3.10.2</MarginText>
Overload resolution ensures only that the profile is type conformant. This rule specifies that subtype conformance is required (which also requires matching calling conventions). P cannot denote an entry because access-to-subprogram types never have the <i>entry</i> calling convention. P cannot denote an enumeration literal or an attribute function because these have intrinsic calling conventions. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>32.1/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is said to have <i>distributed accessibility</i> if it is<br /></p>

<MarginText>32.2/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.7">4.5.7</a>); or<br /></li>
<MarginText>32.3/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.9">4.5.9</a>) whose <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> has distributed accessibility; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>32.4/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<li>a view conversion, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>, or parenthesized expression whose operand has distributed accessibility. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>32.5/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>The statically deeper relationship does not apply to the accessibility level of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> having distributed accessibility; that is, such an accessibility level is not considered to be statically deeper, nor statically shallower, than any other.<br /></p>

<MarginText>32.6/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>Any static accessibility requirement that is imposed on an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that has distributed accessibility (or on its type) is instead imposed on the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s of the underlying <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>. This rule is applied recursively if a <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> also has distributed accessibility.<br /></p>

<MarginText>32.c/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This means that any Legality Rule requiring that the accessibility level of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (or that of the type of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>) shall or shall not be statically deeper than some other level also applies, in the case where the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> has distributed accessibility, to each <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the underlying <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>33_3.10.2</MarginText>
NOTE 1   The Unchecked{"_"}Access attribute yields the same result as the Access attribute for objects, but has fewer restrictions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.10">13.10</a>). There are other predefined operations that yield access values: an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> can be used to create an object, and return an access value that designates it (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>); evaluating the literal <b>null</b> yields a null access value that designates no entity at all (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2">4.2</a>).<br />

<MarginText>34/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
NOTE 2   The predefined operations of an access type also include the assignment operation, qualification, and membership tests. Explicit conversion is allowed between general access types with matching designated subtypes; explicit conversion is allowed between access-to-subprogram types with subtype conformant profiles (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>). Named access types have predefined equality operators; anonymous access types do not, but they can use the predefined equality operators for <i>universal{"_"}access</i> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.2">4.5.2</a>). <br />

<MarginText>34.a/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Anonymous access types can use the universal access equality operators declared in Standard, while named access types cannot for compatibility reasons. By not having equality operators for anonymous access types, we eliminate the need to specify exactly where the predefined operators for anonymous access types would be defined, as well as the need for an implementer to insert an implicit declaration for "=", etc. at the appropriate place in their symbol table. Note that ":=", 'Access, and ".<b>all</b>" are defined. <br />

<MarginText>35_3.10.2</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The object or subprogram designated by an access value can be named with a dereference, either an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0094">explicit{"_"}dereference</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0095">implicit_dereference</a></code>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a>.<br />

<MarginText>36_3.10.2</MarginText>
NOTE 4   A call through the dereference of an access-to-subprogram value is never a dispatching call. <br />

<MarginText>36.a_3.10.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>. <br />

<MarginText>37/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00254-01", "AI12-0440-1", "AI12-0451-1"]} />
NOTE 5   The Access attribute for subprograms and parameters of an anonymous access-to-subprogram type can be used together to implement &ldquo;downward closures&rdquo; &mdash; that is, to pass a more-nested subprogram as a parameter to a less-nested subprogram, as can be appropriate for an iterator abstraction or numerical integration. Downward closures can also be implemented using generic formal subprograms (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6">12.6</a>). Unlike for objects, there is no Unchecked{"_"}Access attribute for subprograms.<br />

<MarginText>38/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0451-1"]} />
NOTE 6   Using an access-to-class-wide tagged type with a dispatching operation is a potentially more structured alternative to using an access-to-subprogram type.<br />

<MarginText>39/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 7   An implementation can consider two access-to-subprogram values to be unequal, even though they designate the same subprogram. For instance, this can happen because one points directly to the subprogram, while the other points to a special prologue that performs an Elaboration{"_"}Check and then jumps to the subprogram. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.2">4.5.2</a>. <br />

<MarginText>39.a_3.10.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If equality of access-to-subprogram values is important to the logic of a program, a reference to the Access attribute of a subprogram should be evaluated only once and stored in a global constant for subsequent use and equality comparison. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>40_3.10.2</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of use of the Access attribute:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>41/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Becky : Person{"_"}Name := new Person(F);       -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}Cars  : array (1..2) of aliased Car;{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}Becky.Vehicle := Cars(1)'Access;{"\n"}Casey.Vehicle := Cars(2)'Access;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>41.a_3.10.2</MarginText>
We no longer make things like 'Last and ".component" (basic) operations of an access type that need to be "declared" somewhere. Instead, implicit dereference in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> takes care of them all. This means that there should never be a case when X.<b>all</b>'Last is legal while X'Last is not. See AI83-00154. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>41.b/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
 Aliased variables are not necessarily constrained in Ada 2005 (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>). Therefore, a subcomponent of an aliased variable may disappear or change shape, and taking 'Access of such a subcomponent thus is illegal, while the same operation would have been legal in Ada 95. Note that most allocated objects are still constrained by their initial value (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>), and thus legality of 'Access didn't change for them. For example: <br />

<MarginText>41.c/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type T1 (D1 : Boolean := False) is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      case D1 is{"\n"}         when False ={">"}{"\n"}            C1 : aliased Integer;{"\n"}         when True ={">"}{"\n"}            null;{"\n"}      end case;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}type Acc{"_"}Int is access all Integer;{"\n"}
<MarginText>41.d/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
A{"_"}T : aliased T1;{"\n"}Ptr : Acc{"_"}Int := A{"_"}T.C1'Access; -- Illegal in Ada 2005, legal in Ada 95{"\n"}A{"_"}T := (D1 ={">"} True);            -- Raised Constraint{"_"}Error in Ada 95, but does not{"\n"}                                -- in Ada 2005, so Ptr would become invalid when this{"\n"}                                -- is assigned (thus Ptr is illegal).{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>41.e/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
If a discriminated full type has a partial view (private type) that is constrained, we do not allow 'Access on objects to create a value of an object of an access-to-unconstrained type. Ada 95 allowed this attribute and various access subtypes, requiring that the heap object be constrained and thus making details of the implementation of the private type visible to the client of the private type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a> for more on this topic.<br />

<MarginText>41.f/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00229-01", "AI95-00254-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> Taking 'Access of a subprogram declared in a generic unit in the body of that generic is no longer allowed. Such references can easily be used to create dangling pointers, as Legality Rules are not rechecked in instance bodies. At the same time, the rules were loosened a bit where that is harmless, and also to allow any routine to be passed to an access parameter of an access-to-subprogram type. The now illegal uses of 'Access can almost always be moved to the private part of the generic unit, where they are still legal (and rechecked upon instantiation for possibly dangling pointers). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>41.g/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00127-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0010</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Access attributes of objects of class-wide types can be used as the controlling parameter in a dispatching calls (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>). This was an oversight in Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>41.h/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00235-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> The type of the prefix can now be used in resolving Access attributes. This allows more uses of the Access attribute to resolve. For example: <br />

<MarginText>41.i/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Int{"_"}Ptr is access all Integer;{"\n"}type Float{"_"}Ptr is access all Float;{"\n"}
<MarginText>41.j/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
function Zap (Val : Int{"_"}Ptr) return Float;{"\n"}function Zap (Val : Float{"_"}Ptr) return Float;{"\n"}
<MarginText>41.k/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
Value : aliased Integer := 10;{"\n"}
<MarginText>41.l/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
Result1 : Float := Zap (Value'access); -- Ambiguous in Ada 95; resolves in Ada 2005.{"\n"}Result2 : Float := Zap (Int{"_"}Ptr'(Value'access)); -- Resolves in Ada 95 and Ada 2005.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>41.m/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
This change is upward compatible; any expression that does not resolve by the new rules would have failed a Legality Rule. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>41.n/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01"]} />
Adjusted the wording to reflect the fact that expressions and function calls are masters.<br />

<MarginText>41.o/2_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00254-01", "AI95-00318-02", "AI95-00385-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
Defined the accessibility of the various new kinds and uses of anonymous access types. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>41.p/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Simplified the description of when a discriminant-dependent component is allowed as the prefix of 'Access to when the object is known to be constrained. This fixes a confusion as to whether a subcomponent of an object that is not certain to be constrained can be used as a prefix of 'Access. The fix introduces an incompatibility, as the rule did not apply in Ada 95 if the prefix was a constant; but it now applies no matter what kind of object is involved. The incompatibility is not too bad, since most kinds of constants are known to be constrained.<br />

<MarginText>41.q/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0041-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the checks for the constrainedness of the prefix of the Access attribute so that assume-the-worst is used in generic bodies. This may make some programs illegal, but those programs were at risk having objects disappear while valid access values still pointed at them. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>41.r/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0082-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Eliminated the static accessibility definition for generic formal types, as the actual can be more or less nested than the generic itself. This allows programs that were illegal for Ada 95 and for Ada 2005.<br />

<MarginText>41.s/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0148-1", "AI05-0253-1"]} />
Eliminate the static accessibility definition for stand-alone objects of anonymous access-to-object types. This allows such objects to be used as temporaries without causing accessibility problems. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>41.t/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0014-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the rules so that the accessibility of the object designated by an access object is that of the access type, even when no dereference is given. The accessibility was not specified in the past. This correction applies to both Ada 95 and Ada 2005.<br />

<MarginText>41.u/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0024-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected accessibility rules for access discriminants so that no cases are omitted.<br />

<MarginText>41.v/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0051-1", "AI05-0234-1", "AI05-0235-1", "AI05-0284-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected accessibility rules for anonymous access return types and access discriminants in return statements.<br />

<MarginText>41.w/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0066-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Changed coextension rules so that coextensions that belong to an anonymous object are transfered to the ultimate object.<br />

<MarginText>41.x/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0188-1", "AI05-0235-1"]} />
Defined the accessibility of explicitly aliased parameters (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>) and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.7">4.5.7</a>).<br />

<MarginText>41.y/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0234-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined the term &ldquo;master of the call&rdquo; to simplify other wording, especially that for the accessibility checks associated with return statements and explicitly aliased parameters.<br />

<MarginText>41.z/3_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0270-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined the (omitted) accessibility level of null values when those are passed as the actual of an access-to-object parameter. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>41.aa/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0278-1", "AI12-0390-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined that the accessibility of a function that returns an anonymous access type is the same for implicit and explicit conversions. This could cause code involving implicit conversions to named access types that is legal and does not raise an exception in original Ada 2012 to become illegal or raise Program{"_"}Error because of an accessibility failure in Ada 2022. This is more likely to prevent a dangling pointer bug than to prevent something useful.<br />

<MarginText>41.bb/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0345-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Tightened the cases where an explicitly aliased parameter has special accessibility, to avoid needing to pass the required dynamic accessibility to functions that have explicitly aliased parameters. The changes affects programs that use the dynamic accessibility of an explicitly aliased parameter within a return statement of a function (typically using anonymous access types). This can mean that a program that would have been legal and worked in Ada 2012 as defined would raise Program{"_"}Error or be rejected in Ada 2022. One such example is: <br />

<MarginText>41.cc/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Rec is record{"\n"}    Comp : aliased Integer;{"\n"}    ...{"\n"}end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>41.dd/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
function F1 (A : aliased in out Rec) return access Integer is{"\n"}   function F2 (B : access Integer) return access Integer{"\n"}      is (B); -- (1){"\n"}begin{"\n"}   return F2 (A.Comp'Access); -- (2){"\n"}end F1;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>41.ee/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
At (2), there is a check that the dynamic accessibility level of B is not deeper than the master of the call for F2 (which is defined to be the master of the call for F1). In Ada 2012, since the reference is inside of a return statement, the dynamic accessibility of A.Comp'Access is the master of the call for F1 - meaning the check at (2) should pass. In Ada 2022, the dynamic accessibility of A.Comp'Access is local for for F1 - meaning the check at (2) should fail and raise Program{"_"}Error.<br />

<MarginText>41.ff/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
We're not aware of any Ada 2012 compilers that correctly implemented the rule as written (because of the overhead that is implied), so the practical effect of this change is to make the rules more consistent with actual practice.<br />

<MarginText>41.gg/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0345-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Adjusted the rules so that using a part of a return object in a return expression does not break the connection between the inner and outer function calls. This means that some cases that (unnecessarily) failed an accessibility check in Ada 2012 will not do so in Ada 2022. This change will mostly remove latent problems from Ada code; very little code depends on an accessibility check failing. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>41.hh/4_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0027-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Defined the accessibility of a value conversion, so that it is treated like an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> built at the point of the conversion. This was previously unspecified, so this change might be incompatible if an Ada implementation treated the accessibility of such conversions as that of the operand type; in that case, previous legal conversions probably will become illegal as the lifetime of the conversion is very short. However, code that could tell this difference is fairly rare (taking 'Access of a component of a result of a type conversion), code depending on this accessibility was not portable, and such code could have created an immediately dangling pointer if the conversion actually made a copy (which is necessary in some instances).<br />

<MarginText>41.ii/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0371-1"]} />
The accessibility of a renaming of a formal subprogram in a generic package specification has changed to reflect the fact that a wrapper may be needed for the formal subprogram. Thus, 'Access of such a renaming found in an instance that is not library-level may become illegal. We think this case is unlikely to occur in practice, and a simple workaround is available (rename the actual at the point of the instance, use that rename as the prefix of 'Access). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>41.jj/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0402-1"]} />
Adjusted the special accessibility for functions initializing objects to only apply to composite types. This makes some function calls of functions that return elementary types and have aliased parameters legal that otherwise would be illegal. Such a function cannot return a part of a parameter, and thus one does not need parameter checks to make that possible. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>41.kk/4_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0067-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected so that it is clear that explicitly aliased parameters in procedures have the same accessibility as other parameters. Only explicitly aliased parameters in functions are special.<br />

<MarginText>41.ll/4_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0070-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> The accessibility of an anonymous access type of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> is defined here rather than in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a> so that all accessibility rules are here.<br />

<MarginText>41.mm/4_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0089-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected a number of rules so that they clearly apply to generic functions as well as functions. (Remember, a generic function is not a function.)<br />

<MarginText>41.nn/4_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0095-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Moved the assume the worst rule about constrainedness of the prefix of attribute Access to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a>, as a number of places in the Reference Manual need this rule.<br />

<MarginText>41.oo/4_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0157-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Ensured that the statically deeper relationship applies within the return expression of an expression function. (Dynamic properties apply by equivalence, but static properties are handled separately.)<br />

<MarginText>41.pp/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0064-2"]} />
Added Nonblocking (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>) matching to P'Access.<br />

<MarginText>41.qq/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0156-1"]} />
Added text to define the accessibility of anonymous access types declaring a loop parameter.<br />

<MarginText>41.rr/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
Added <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code>s to the accessibility rules.<br />

<MarginText>41.ss/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0277-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified the static level of explicitly aliased parameters.<br />

<MarginText>41.tt/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0372-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Redefined the statically deeper relationship for the master of a function call and locals of that call. This might cause programs to be rejected that were previously legal, but any such program should have failed a dynamic accessibility check. Thus this is not an incompatibility as it is changing the detection of an error from runtime to compile-time.<br />

<MarginText>41.uu/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording to clarify that the accessibility of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> does not need any static checks (it is considered to match any accessibility required).<br />

<MarginText>41.vv/5_3.10.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0406-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Used the new term &ldquo;master construct&rdquo;, to put static accessibility rules on a firmer basis, including ensuring that those rules apply inside of generic bodies. <br />

# 3.11. Declarative Parts

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11.mdx

sidebar_position:  29

# 3.11. Declarative Parts

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> contains <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>s (possibly none).] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>declarative{"_"}part</code><a id="S0086"></a><code> ::= </code>{"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>{"}"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>declarative{"_"}item</code><a id="S0087"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0089">body</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} <code>basic{"_"}declarative{"_"}item</code><a id="S0088"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0021">basic_declaration</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>body</code><a id="S0089"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0090">proper_body</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0297">body_stub</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>proper{"_"}body</code><a id="S0090"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00420-01"]} />
<p>The list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> is called the <i>declaration list</i> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>s, if any, in the order in which they are given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>An elaborable construct is in the <i>elaborated</i> state after the normal completion of its elaboration. Prior to that, it is <i>not yet elaborated</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The elaborated state is only important for bodies; certain uses of a body raise an exception if the body is not yet elaborated.<br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
Note that "prior" implies before the start of elaboration, as well as during elaboration.<br />

<MarginText>8.c</MarginText>
The use of the term "normal completion" implies that if the elaboration propagates an exception or is aborted, the declaration is not elaborated. RM83 missed the aborted case. <br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>For a construct that attempts to use a body, a check (Elaboration{"_"}Check) is performed, as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>10/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00064-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0014</i>{"}"} For a call to a (non-protected) subprogram that has an explicit body, a check is made that the body is already elaborated. This check and the evaluations of any actual parameters of the call are done in an arbitrary order. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>AI83-00180 specifies that there is no elaboration check for a subprogram defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Interface (or equivalently, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import). AI83-00430 specifies that there is no elaboration check for an enumeration literal. AI83-00406 specifies that the evaluation of parameters and the elaboration check occur in an arbitrary order. AI83-00406 applies to generic instantiation as well (see below).<br />

<MarginText>10.a.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00064-01", "AI05-0177-1"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0014</i>{"}"} A subprogram can be completed by a renaming-as-body, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code>, or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression_function_declaration</a></code>, and we need to make an elaboration check on such a body, so we use &ldquo;body&rdquo; rather than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> above. <br />

<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For a call to a protected operation of a protected type (that has a body &mdash; no check is performed if  the protected type is imported &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>), a check is made that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code> is already elaborated. This check and the evaluations of any actual parameters of the call are done in an arbitrary order. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A protected type has only one elaboration &ldquo;bit&rdquo;, rather than one for each operation, because one call may result in evaluating the barriers of other entries, and because there are no elaborable declarations between the bodies of the operations. In fact, the elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code> does not elaborate the enclosed bodies, since they are not considered independently elaborable.<br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
Note that there is no elaboration check when calling a task entry. Task entry calls are permitted even before the associated <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code> has been seen. Such calls are simply queued until the task is activated and reaches a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>. We considered a similar rule for protected entries &mdash; simply queuing all calls until the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code> was seen, but felt it was not worth the possible implementation overhead, particularly given that there might be multiple instances of the protected type. <br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For the activation of a task, a check is made by the activator that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code> is already elaborated. If two or more tasks are being activated together (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.2">9.2</a>), as the result of the elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> or the initialization for the object created by an allocator, this check is done for all of them before activating any of them. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>As specified by AI83-00149, the check is done by the activator, rather than by the task itself. If it were done by the task itself, it would be turned into a Tasking{"_"}Error in the activator, and the other tasks would still be activated. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For the instantiation of a generic unit that has a body, a check is made that this body is already elaborated. This check and the evaluation of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0318">explicit_generic_actual_parameter</a></code>s of the instantiation are done in an arbitrary order. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>The exception Program{"_"}Error is raised if any of these checks fails. <br /></p>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>14.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
The syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> is modified to remove the ordering restrictions of Ada 83; that is, the distinction between <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s and <code>later{"_"}declarative{"_"}item</code>s within <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>s is removed. This means that things like <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>s can be freely intermixed with things like bodies.<br />

<MarginText>14.b</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0090">proper_body</a></code> now allows a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code>, and the rules for elaboration checks now cover calls on protected operations. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>14.c</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code>later{"_"}declarative{"_"}item</code> is removed; the syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code> is new.<br />

<MarginText>14.d</MarginText>
RM83 defines &ldquo;elaborated&rdquo; and &ldquo;not yet elaborated&rdquo; for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>s here, and for other things in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1">3.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1">Declarations</a>&rdquo;. That's no longer necessary, since these terms are fully defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1">3.1</a>.<br />

<MarginText>14.e</MarginText>
In RM83, all uses of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> are optional (except for the one in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> with a <b>declare</b>) which is sort of strange, since a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> can be empty, according to the syntax. That is, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>s are sort of &ldquo;doubly optional&rdquo;. In Ada 95, these <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>s are always required (but can still be empty). To simplify description, we go further and say (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6">5.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6">Block Statements</a>&rdquo;) that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> without an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> is equivalent to one with an empty one. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>14.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Changed representation clauses to aspect clauses to reflect that they are used for more than just representation.<br />

<MarginText>14.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00064-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0014</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that the elaboration check applies to all kinds of subprogram bodies.<br />

<MarginText>14.h/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00420-01"]} />
Defined &ldquo;declaration list&rdquo; to avoid confusion for various rules. Other kinds of declaration list are defined elsewhere. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.11.1"></a>

## 3.11.1  Completions of Declarations

<MarginText>1/3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00064-01", "AI05-0177-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0014</i>{"}"} Declarations sometimes come in two parts. A declaration that requires a second part is said to <i>require completion</i>. The second part is called the <i>completion</i> of the declaration (and of the entity declared), and is either another declaration, a body, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>. A <i>body</i> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0089">body</a></code>, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression_function_declaration</a></code> that completes another declaration, or a renaming-as-body (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#Subclause_8.5.4">8.5.4</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a_3.11.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Throughout the RM95, there are rules about completions that define the following: <br />

<MarginText>1.b_3.11.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Which declarations require a corresponding completion.<br /></li>
<MarginText>1.c_3.11.1</MarginText>
<li>Which constructs can only serve as the completion of a declaration.<br /></li>
<MarginText>1.d_3.11.1</MarginText>
<li>Where the completion of a declaration is allowed to be.<br /></li>
<MarginText>1.e_3.11.1</MarginText>
<li>What kinds of completions are allowed to correspond to each kind of declaration that allows one. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>1.f_3.11.1</MarginText>
Don't confuse this compile-time concept with the run-time concept of completion defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">7.6.1</a>.<br />

<MarginText>1.g_3.11.1</MarginText>
Note that the declaration of a private type (if limited) can be completed with the declaration of a task type, which is then completed with a body. Thus, a declaration can actually come in <i>three</i> parts.<br />

<MarginText>1.h/3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI05-0162-1"]} />
An incomplete type (whether declared in the limited view of a package or not) may be completed by a private type declaration, so we can in fact have <i>four</i> parts.<br />

<MarginText>1.i/3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
In Ada 2012, there are no language-defined pragmas that act as completions. Pragma Import (which is obsolescent) has the effect of setting aspect Import to True; such an aspect makes giving a completion illegal. The wording that allows pragmas as completions was left as it is harmless and appears in many places in this Reference Manual. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>2_3.11.1</MarginText>
<p>A construct that can be a completion is interpreted as the completion of a prior declaration only if: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The declaration and the completion occur immediately within the same declarative region;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4_3.11.1</MarginText>
<li>The defining name or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0201">defining_program_unit_name</a></code> in the completion is the same as in the declaration, or in the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies to the declaration;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5_3.11.1</MarginText>
<li>If the declaration is overloadable, then the completion either has a type-conformant profile, or is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>6/3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An implicit declaration shall not have a completion. For any explicit declaration that is specified to <i>require completion</i>, there shall be a corresponding explicit completion, unless the declared entity is imported (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a.1/2_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>The implicit declarations occurring in a limited view do have a completion (the explicit declaration occurring in the full view) but that's a special case, since the implicit declarations are actually built from the explicit ones. So they do not <i>require</i> a completion, they have one by <i>fiat</i>. <br />

<MarginText>6.a_3.11.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The implicit declarations of predefined operators are not allowed to have a completion. Enumeration literals, although they are subprograms, are not allowed to have a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. That's because the completion rules are described in terms of constructs (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>s) and not entities (subprograms). When a completion is required, it has to be explicit; the implicit null <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> that Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/">7</a> talks about cannot serve as the completion of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code> if a completion is required. <br />

<MarginText>7_3.11.1</MarginText>
<p>At most one completion is allowed for a given declaration. Additional requirements on completions appear where each kind of completion is defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a_3.11.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A subunit is not a completion; the stub is.<br />

<MarginText>7.b_3.11.1</MarginText>
If the completion of a declaration is also a declaration, then <i>that</i> declaration might have a completion, too. For example, a limited private type can be completed with a task type, which can then be completed with a task body. This is not a violation of the &ldquo;at most one completion&rdquo; rule. <br />

<MarginText>8_3.11.1</MarginText>
<p>A type is <i>completely defined</i> at a place that is after its full type definition (if it has one) and after all of its subcomponent types are completely defined. A type shall be completely defined before it is frozen (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.14">13.14</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3">7.3</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a_3.11.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Index types are always completely defined &mdash; no need to mention them. There is no way for a completely defined type to depend on the value of a (still) deferred constant. <br />

<MarginText>9/3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
NOTE 1   Completions are in principle allowed for any kind of explicit declaration. However, for some kinds of declaration, the only allowed completion is an implementation-defined pragma, and implementations are not required to have any such pragmas. <br />

<MarginText>9.a/3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>10/5_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0449-1"]} />
NOTE 2   There are rules that prevent premature uses of declarations that have a corresponding completion. The Elaboration{"_"}Checks of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11">3.11</a> prevent such uses at run time for subprograms, protected operations, tasks, and generic units. The freezing rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.14">13.14</a>) prevent, at compile time, premature uses of other entities such as private types and deferred constants. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>10.a_3.11.1</MarginText>
This subclause is new. It is intended to cover all kinds of completions of declarations, be they a body for a spec, a full type for an incomplete or private type, a full constant declaration for a deferred constant declaration, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import for any kind of entity. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>10.b/2_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00064-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0014</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a definition of <i>body</i>, which is different than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0089">body</a></code> or <b>body</b>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>10.c/3_3.11.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-0177-1"]} />
Added null procedures and expression functions that are completions to the definition of <i>body</i>. <br />
