An object can be created and initialized as part of elaborating a declaration, evaluating an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>, or passing a parameter by copy. Prior to reclaiming the storage for an object, it is finalized if necessary (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">7.6.1</a>).] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>All of the following are objects: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>object</b> &mdash; entity that contains a value, and is either a constant or a variable<br /><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> or by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>. A formal parameter is (a view of) an object. A subcomponent of an object is an object.<br />

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the entity declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<li>a formal parameter of a subprogram, entry, or generic subprogram;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<li>a generic formal object;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>a loop parameter;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0061-1"]} />
<li>the index parameter of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0119">iterated_component_association</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0308-1"]} />
<li>the chunk parameter of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<li>a choice parameter of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<li>an entry index of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<li>the result of dereferencing an access-to-object value (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0015-1"]} />
<li>the return object of a function;<br /></li>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<li>the result of evaluating an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0003-1", "AI12-0226-1"]} />
<li>a value conversion or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> whose operand denotes an object;<br /></li>
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<li>a component, slice, or view conversion of another object. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0054-2"]} />
<p>An object is either a <i>constant</i> object or a <i>variable</i> object. Similarly, a view of an object is either a <i>constant</i> or a <i>variable</i>. All views of a constant elementary object are constant. All views of a constant composite object are constant, except for parts that are of controlled or immutably limited types; variable views of those parts and their subcomponents may exist. In this sense, objects of controlled and immutably limited types are <i>inherently mutable</i>. A constant view of an object cannot be used to modify its value. The terms constant and variable by themselves refer to constant and variable views of objects.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0422-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If some part of an object has a variable view, then the object as a whole has a variable view, and not all views of the object are constant. That's true even if only a subcomponent has a variable view. <br />

<MarginText>13.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0422-1"]} />
<p>A constant object is <i>known to have no variable views</i> if it does not have a part that is immutably limited, or of a controlled type, private type, or private extension.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0422-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This definition can be used in Legality Rules as it respects privacy. It is an assume-the-worst rule, as all private types and private extensions might have a controlled component. <br />

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>The value of an object is <i>read</i> when the value of any part of the object is evaluated, or when the value of an enclosing object is evaluated. The value of a variable is <i>updated</i> when an assignment is performed to any part of the variable, or when an assignment is performed to an enclosing object. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Reading and updating are intended to include read/write references of any kind, even if they are not associated with the evaluation of a particular construct. Consider, for example, the expression &ldquo;X.<b>all</b>(F)&rdquo;, where X is an access-to-array object, and F is a function. The implementation is allowed to first evaluate &ldquo;X.<b>all</b>&rdquo; and then F. Finally, a read is performed to get the value of the F'th component of the array. Note that the array is not necessarily read as part of the evaluation of &ldquo;X.<b>all</b>&rdquo;. This is important, because if F were to free X using Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation, we want the execution of the final read to be erroneous. <br />

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<p>Whether a view of an object is constant or variable is determined by the definition of the view. The following (and no others) represent variables: <br /></p>

<MarginText>16/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>an object declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> without the reserved word <b>constant</b>;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00385-01"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>We mean the word <b>constant</b> as defined by the grammar for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>, not some random word <b>constant</b>. Thus, <br />

<MarginText>16.b/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X : access constant T;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16.c/2</MarginText>
is not a constant. <br />

<MarginText>17/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>a formal parameter of mode <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>17.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>a generic formal object of mode <b>in out</b>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>18/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>a non-discriminant component of a variable;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This includes both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>18.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0097">slice</a></code> of a variable;<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>a loop parameter that is specified to be a variable for a generalized loop (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>19/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>a view conversion of a variable;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>a dereference of an access-to-variable value;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0015-1", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>the return object declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> without the reserved word <b>constant</b>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>21/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0015-1", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>the current instance of a type other than a protected type[, if the current instance is an object and not a value (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>)];<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We exclude current instances of protected types as they are protected units and the next bullet applies. <br />

<MarginText>21.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This list of bullets only applies to views of objects, so current instances that are not objects are not considered here. <br />

<MarginText>21.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0003-1", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<ul>
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
<MarginText>21.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0120-1", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>the current instance of a protected unit except within the body of a protected function of that protected unit, or within a function declared immediately within the body of the protected unit;<br /></li>
<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> where the attribute is defined to denote a variable (for example, the Storage{"_"}Pool attribute &ndash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>).<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>22.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In particular, this implies that the following are not variables: <br />

<MarginText>22.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0226-1", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the result of evaluating a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, a value conversion, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code>, or a parenthesized expression;<br /></li>
<MarginText>22.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3"]} />
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#Subclause_5.2.1">5.2.1</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>22.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0061-1"]} />
<li>the index parameter of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0119">iterated_component_association</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>22.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<li>a choice parameter or entry index;<br /></li>
<MarginText>22.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0308-1"]} />
<li>a chunk parameter of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>22.g/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
This list of constructs that yield constant views is not exhaustive. <br />

<MarginText>23/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0191-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
<p>At the place where a view of an object is defined, a <i>nominal subtype</i> is associated with the view. The <i>nominal type</i> of a view is the type of the nominal subtype of the view. The object's <i>actual subtype</i> (that is, its subtype) can be more restrictive than the nominal subtype of the view; it always is more restrictive if the nominal subtype is an <i>indefinite subtype</i>. A subtype is an indefinite subtype if it is an unconstrained array subtype, or if it has unknown discriminants or unconstrained discriminants without defaults (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7">3.7</a>); otherwise, the subtype is a <i>definite</i> subtype [(all elementary subtypes are definite subtypes)]. [A class-wide subtype is defined to have unknown discriminants, and is therefore an indefinite subtype. An indefinite subtype does not by itself provide enough information to create an object; an additional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> or explicit initialization <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is necessary (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>). A component cannot have an indefinite nominal subtype.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>23.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>nominal subtype</b> &mdash; subtype specified when a view of an object is defined<br />

<MarginText>23.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1"]} />
<p>A view of a composite object is <i>known to be constrained</i> if:<br /></p>

<MarginText>23.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0401-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>its nominal subtype is constrained and not an untagged partial view, and it is neither a value conversion nor a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.3/3</MarginText>
<li>its nominal subtype is indefinite; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1", "AI05-0093-1"]} />
<li>its type is immutably limited (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>); or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.5/3</MarginText>
<li>it is part of a stand-alone constant (including a generic formal object of mode <b>in</b>); or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.6/3</MarginText>
<li>it is part of a formal parameter of mode <b>in</b>; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.7/3</MarginText>
<li>it is part of the object denoted by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0226-1", "AI12-0228-1"]} />
<li>it is a value conversion or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> where the operand denotes a view of a composite object that is known to be constrained; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0228-1"]} />
<li>it is part of a constant return object of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1", "AI05-0041-1", "AI12-0228-1"]} />
<li>it is a dereference of a pool-specific access type, and there is no ancestor of its type that has a constrained partial view.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23.b/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We do not include dereferences of general access types because they might denote stand-alone aliased unconstrained variables. That's true even for access-to-constant types (the denoted object does not have to be a constant).<br />

<MarginText>23.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1", "AI05-0008-1", "AI12-0228-1"]} />
We don't mention view conversions as there are no mutable tagged types (discriminant defaults are allowed only if the type is immutably limited), so all tagged view conversions are either of an indefinite type (if it has discriminants without defaults), an immutably limited type (if the discriminants do have defaults), or constrained (if there are no discriminants). This matches the first three bullets here, so all tagged view conversions are known to be constrained without needing to mention them explicitly. Untagged view conversions only can occur in parameter passing (as actuals to <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> parameters), and "known to be constrained" is not used there.<br />

<MarginText>23.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0228-1"]} />
We don't need to mention the current instance of a (sub)type, either. If a current instance of a type or subtype appears in an aspect specification, it represents a value, so whether or not it is known to be constrained is irrelevant (the term is only defined for composite objects). Otherwise, the current instance of a type can only be used in an immutably limited type, so all such instances are known to be constrained by the third bullet. <br />

<MarginText>23.11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1", "AI05-0041-1", "AI12-0228-1"]} />
<p>For the purposes of determining within a generic body whether an object is known to be constrained: <br /></p>

<MarginText>23.12/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>if a subtype is a descendant of an untagged generic formal private or derived type, and the subtype is not an unconstrained array subtype, it is not considered indefinite and is considered to have a constrained partial view;<br /></li>
<MarginText>23.13/5</MarginText>
<li>if a subtype is a descendant of a formal access type, it is not considered pool-specific.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<p>A <i>named number</i> provides a name for a numeric value known at compile time. It is declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
NOTE 1   A constant cannot be the target of an assignment operation, nor be passed as an <b>in</b> <b>out</b> or <b>out</b> parameter, between its initialization and finalization, if any.<br />

<MarginText>25.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0054-2"]} />
NOTE 2   The value of a constant object cannot be changed after its initialization, except in some cases where the object has a controlled or immutably limited part (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>, and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9#Subclause_13.9.1">13.9.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>26/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
NOTE 3   The nominal and actual subtypes of an elementary object are always the same. For a discriminated or array object, if the nominal subtype is constrained, then so is the actual subtype. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>26.a</MarginText>
There are additional kinds of objects (choice parameters and entry indices of entry bodies).<br />

<MarginText>26.b</MarginText>
The result of a function and of evaluating an aggregate are considered (constant) objects. This is necessary to explain the action of finalization on such things. Because a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> is also syntactically a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a>), the result of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> can be renamed, thereby allowing repeated use of the result without calling the function again. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>26.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause now follows the subclauses on types and subtypes, to cut down on the number of forward references.<br />

<MarginText>26.d</MarginText>
The term nominal subtype is new. It is used to distinguish what is known at compile time about an object's constraint, versus what its "true" run-time constraint is.<br />

<MarginText>26.e</MarginText>
The terms definite and indefinite (which apply to subtypes) are new. They are used to aid in the description of generic formal type matching, and to specify when an explicit initial value is required in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>26.f</MarginText>
We have moved the syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code> down into their respective subclauses, to keep the syntax close to the description of the associated semantics.<br />

<MarginText>26.g</MarginText>
We talk about variables and constants here, since the discussion is not specific to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>s, and it seems better to have the list of the kinds of constants juxtaposed with the kinds of objects.<br />

<MarginText>26.h</MarginText>
We no longer talk about indirect updating due to parameter passing. Parameter passing is handled in 6.2 and 6.4.1 in a way that there is no need to mention it here in the definition of read and update. Reading and updating now includes the case of evaluating or assigning to an enclosing object. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>26.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01"]} />
Clarified that the return object is the object created by a function call. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0015-1"]} />
Added wording to allow return objects to be declared as constants, and corrected the definition of return objects as objects. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.k/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1", "AI05-0041-1", "AI05-0093-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a definition of <i>known to be constrained</i>, for use in other rules.<br />

<MarginText>26.l/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0054-2"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> We now recognize the fact that not all declared constant objects are immutable; for those that a variable view can be constructed, they can be changed via that view.<br />

<MarginText>26.m/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0120-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added the current instance of a protected object to the list of constant views; since the list claims to include all possibilities, it had better include that one.<br />

<MarginText>26.n/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0003-1"]} />
The result of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> is defined to be a constant view and is defined to be an object if the operand of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> is an object. These definitions, combined with some grammar changes, allow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>s to be used in more places. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a> for details. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.o/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0401-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the definition of &ldquo;known to be constrained&rdquo; so that the status of the operand of value conversions and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>s is always used to determine whether the property exists. As the rules are <b>or</b>ed together, a value conversion or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> with a constrained nominal subtype would have always met the requirements in Ada 2012, regardless of the operand. This change will mean that some conversions or qualifications (mostly of variables) will no longer be considered &ldquo;known to be constrained&rdquo; and therefore 'Access and renaming of such <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es will now be illegal. This is necessary to meet the design goal that subsequent execution cannot cause a renaming or 'Access to cause erroneous execution. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.p/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0228-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> of an object that is known to be constrained is now also known to be constrained. This allows qualification to be used to disambiguate a function call used as a prefix in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> without making the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> illegal.<br />

<MarginText>26.q/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0226-1"]} />
A value conversion of an object is an object; this makes value conversions consistent with qualified expressions. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.r/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0392-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Changed from a list of constants to a list of variables. This makes the default to be a constant, which is the more common case, and eliminates issues caused by omissions from the list (such as parenthesized expressions).<br />

<MarginText>26.s/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0422-1"]} />
Added the term &ldquo;known to have no variable views&rdquo; in order to have a definition that can be used in Legality Rules without breaking privacy. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.3.1"></a>

## 3.3.1  Object Declarations

<MarginText>1/3_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> declares a <i>stand-alone</i> object with a given nominal subtype and, optionally, an explicit initial value given by an initialization expression. For an array, access, task, or protected object, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> may include the definition of the (anonymous) type of the object. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00385-01", "AI95-00406-01", "AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>object{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0032"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : [<b>aliased</b>] [<b>constant</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> [:= <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]<br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : [<b>aliased</b>] [<b>constant</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> [:= <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]<br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : [<b>aliased</b>] [<b>constant</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> [:= <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]<br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single_task_declaration</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single_protected_declaration</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_3.3.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>defining{"_"}identifier{"_"}list</code><a id="S0033"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>{"}"}<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>4_3.3.1</MarginText>
<p>For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> following the compound delimiter :=, the type expected for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is that of the object. This <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is called the <i>initialization expression</i>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> without the reserved word <b>constant</b> declares a variable object. If it has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> that defines an indefinite subtype, then there shall be an initialization expression. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1", "AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> with the reserved word <b>constant</b> declares a constant object. If it has an initialization expression, then it is called a <i>full constant declaration</i>. Otherwise, it is called a <i>deferred constant declaration</i>. The rules for deferred constant declarations are given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.4">7.4</a>. The rules for full constant declarations are given in this subclause.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7_3.3.1</MarginText>
<p>Any declaration that includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> with more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> is equivalent to a series of declarations each containing one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> from the list, with the rest of the text of the declaration copied for each declaration in the series, in the same order as the list. The remainder of this Reference Manual relies on this equivalence; explanations are given for declarations with a single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00385-01"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, or full type definition of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> defines the nominal subtype of the object. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> declares an object of the type of the nominal subtype. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00385-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The phrase &ldquo;full type definition&rdquo; here includes the case of an anonymous array, access, task, or protected type. <br />

<MarginText>8.1/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01", "AI12-0192-1"]} />
<p>A component of an object is said to <i>require late initialization</i> if: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.2/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0192-1", "AI12-0404-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>it has an access discriminant value constrained by a per-object expression; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.3/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0192-1"]} />
<li>it has an initialization expression that includes a name denoting an access discriminant; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.4/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0192-1"]} />
<li>it has an initialization expression that includes a reference to the current instance of the type either by name or implicitly as the target object of a call. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.b/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Such components can depend on the values of other components of the object. We want to initialize them as late and as reproducibly as possible. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>9/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<p>If a composite object declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> has an unconstrained nominal subtype, then if this subtype is indefinite or the object is constant the actual subtype of this object is constrained. The constraint is determined by the bounds or discriminants (if any) of its initial value; the object is said to be <i>constrained by its initial value</i>. When not constrained by its initial value, the actual and nominal subtypes of the object are the same. If its actual subtype is constrained, the object is called a <i>constrained object</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10_3.3.1</MarginText>
<p>For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> without an initialization expression, any initial values for the object or its subcomponents are determined by the <i>implicit initial values</i> defined for its nominal subtype, as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>11_3.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The implicit initial value for an access subtype is the null value of the access type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.1/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<li>The implicit initial value for a scalar subtype that has the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified is the value of that aspect converted to the nominal subtype (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">Type Conversions</a>&rdquo;);<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a.1/3_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This is a Dynamic Semantics rule, so the visibility of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is not relevant &mdash; if the full type for a private type has the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified, partial views of the type also have this implicit initial value. <br />

<MarginText>12_3.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The implicit initial (and only) value for each discriminant of a constrained discriminated subtype is defined by the subtype.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<li>For a (definite) composite subtype, the implicit initial value of each component with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> is obtained by evaluation of this expression and conversion to the component's nominal subtype (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error), unless the component is a discriminant of a constrained subtype (the previous case), or is in an excluded <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>). For each component that does not have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>, if the composite subtype has the Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value aspect specified, the implicit initial value is the value of that aspect converted to the component's nominal subtype; otherwise, any implicit initial values are those determined by the component's nominal subtype.<br /></li>
<MarginText>14_3.3.1</MarginText>
<li>For a protected or task subtype, there is an implicit component (an entry queue) corresponding to each entry, with its implicit initial value being an empty queue. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The implementation may add implicit components for its own use, which might have implicit initial values. For a task subtype, such components might represent the state of the associated thread of control. For a type with dynamic-sized components, such implicit components might be used to hold the offset to some explicit component. <br />

<MarginText>15_3.3.1</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> proceeds in the following sequence of steps: <br /></p>

<MarginText>16/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00385-01"]} />
<dl>
<dd>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access{"_"}definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array{"_"}type{"_"}definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single{"_"}task{"_"}declaration</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single{"_"}protected{"_"}declaration</a></code> is first elaborated. This creates the nominal subtype (and the anonymous type in the last four cases).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>17/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<dd>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> includes an initialization expression, the (explicit) initial value is obtained by evaluating the expression and converting it to the nominal subtype (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>). <br /></dd>
<MarginText>18/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01", "AI95-00373-01"]} />
<dd>{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} The object is created, and, if there is not an initialization expression, the object is <i>initialized by default</i>. When an object is initialized by default, any per-object constraints (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8">3.8</a>) are elaborated and any implicit initial values for the object or for its subcomponents are obtained as determined by the nominal subtype. Any initial values (whether explicit or implicit) are assigned to the object or to the corresponding subcomponents. As described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2">5.2</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>, Initialize and Adjust procedures can be called. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>18.a_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For a per-object constraint that contains some per-object expressions and some non-per-object expressions, the values used for the constraint consist of the values of the non-per-object expressions evaluated at the point of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>, and the values of the per-object expressions evaluated at the point of the creation of the object.<br />

<MarginText>18.b_3.3.1</MarginText>
The elaboration of per-object constraints was presumably performed as part of the dependent compatibility check in Ada 83. If the object is of a limited type with an access discriminant, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is elaborated at this time (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7">3.7</a>). <br />

<MarginText>18.c_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The reason we say that evaluating an explicit initialization expression happens before creating the object is that in some cases it is impossible to know the size of the object being created until its initial value is known, as in &ldquo;X: String := Func{"_"}Call(...);&rdquo;. The implementation can create the object early in the common case where the size can be known early, since this optimization is semantically neutral. <br />

<MarginText>19/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/></dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01"]} />
<dl>
<dd><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>19.a_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Since the initial values have already been converted to the appropriate nominal subtype, the only Constraint{"_"}Errors that might occur as part of these assignments are for values outside their base range that are used to initialize unconstrained numeric subcomponents. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>. <br />

<MarginText>20/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01"]} />
<p>For the third step above, evaluations and assignments are performed in an arbitrary order subject to the following restrictions: <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.1/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>Assignment to any part of the object is preceded by the evaluation of the value that is to be assigned. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a.1/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Duh. But we ought to say it. Note that, like any rule in the Reference Manual, it doesn't prevent an &ldquo;as-if&rdquo; optimization; as long as the semantics as observed from the program are correct, the compiler can generate any code it wants. <br />

<MarginText>20.2/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> that includes the name of a discriminant is preceded by the assignment to that discriminant. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a.2/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Duh again. But we have to say this, too. It's odd that Ada 95 only required the default expressions to be evaluated before the discriminant is used; it says nothing about discriminant values that come from <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>20.3/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> for any component that depends on a discriminant is preceded by the assignment to that discriminant. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>For example: <br />

<MarginText>20.b_3.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type R(D : Integer := F) is{"\n"}    record{"\n"}        S : String(1..D) := (others ={">"} G);{"\n"}    end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>20.c_3.3.1</MarginText>
X : R;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>20.d_3.3.1</MarginText>
For the elaboration of the declaration of X, it is important that F be evaluated before the aggregate. <br />

<MarginText>20.4/3_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01", "AI05-0092-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The assignments to any components, including implicit components, not requiring late initialization precede the initial value evaluations for any components requiring late initialization; if two components both require late initialization, then assignments to parts of the component occurring earlier in the order of the component declarations precede the initial value evaluations of the component occurring later. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.e/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Components that require late initialization can refer to the entire object during their initialization. We want them to be initialized as late as possible to reduce the chance that their initialization depends on uninitialized components. For instance: <br />

<MarginText>20.f/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type T (D : Natural) is{"\n"}  limited record{"\n"}    C1 : T1 (T'Access);{"\n"}    C2 : Natural := F (D);{"\n"}    C3 : String (1 .. D) := (others ={">"} ' ');{"\n"}  end record;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>20.g/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
Component C1 requires late initialization. The initialization could depend on the values of any component of T, including D, C2, or C3. Therefore, we want to it to be initialized last. Note that C2 and C3 do not require late initialization; they only have to be initialized after D.<br />

<MarginText>20.h/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
It is possible for there to be more than one component that requires late initialization. In this case, the language can't prevent problems, because all of the components can't be the last one initialized. In this case, we specify the order of initialization for components requiring late initialization; by doing so, programmers can arrange their code to avoid accessing uninitialized components, and such arrangements are portable. Note that if the program accesses an uninitialized component, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9#Subclause_13.9.1">13.9.1</a> defines the execution to be erroneous. <br />

<MarginText>21/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>[There is no implicit initial value defined for a scalar subtype unless the Default{"_"}Value aspect has been specified for the type.] In the absence of an explicit initialization or the specification of the Default{"_"}Value aspect, a newly created scalar object can have a value that does not belong to its subtype (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9#Subclause_13.9.1">13.9.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-H/AA-H.1">H.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a_3.3.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>It could even be represented by a bit pattern that doesn't actually represent any value of the type at all, such as an invalid internal code for an enumeration type, or a NaN for a floating point type. It is a generally a bounded error to reference scalar objects with such &ldquo;invalid representations&rdquo;, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9#Subclause_13.9.1">13.9.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9#Subclause_13.9.1">Data Validity</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>21.b_3.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is no requirement that two objects of the same scalar subtype have the same implicit initial &ldquo;value&rdquo; (or representation). It might even be the case that two elaborations of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> produce two different initial values. However, any particular uninitialized object is default-initialized to a single value (or invalid representation). Thus, multiple reads of such an uninitialized object will produce the same value each time (if the implementation chooses not to detect the error). <br />

<MarginText>22_3.3.1</MarginText>
NOTE 1   Implicit initial values are not defined for an indefinite subtype, because if an object's nominal subtype is indefinite, an explicit initial value is required.<br />

<MarginText>23/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0092-1", "AI05-0255-1", "AI12-0061-1", "AI12-0308-1"]} />
NOTE 2   As indicated above, a stand-alone object is an object declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>. Similar definitions apply to &ldquo;stand-alone constant&rdquo; and &ldquo;stand-alone variable&rdquo;. A subcomponent of an object is not a stand-alone object, nor is an object that is created by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>. An object declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0119">iterated{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry{"_"}index{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.4#S0319">formal{"_"}object{"_"}declaration</a></code> of mode <b>in out</b> is not considered a stand-alone object.<br />

<MarginText>24_3.3.1</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The type of a stand-alone object cannot be abstract (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.3">3.9.3</a>). <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>25_3.3.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a multiple object declaration:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>26_3.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
-- the multiple object declaration{"\n"}
<MarginText>27/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
John, Paul : not null Person{"_"}Name := new Person(Sex ={">"} M); -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}
<MarginText>28_3.3.1</MarginText>
-- is equivalent to the two single object declarations in the order given{"\n"}
<MarginText>29/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
John : not null Person{"_"}Name := new Person(Sex ={">"} M);{"\n"}Paul : not null Person{"_"}Name := new Person(Sex ={">"} M);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>30_3.3.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of variable declarations:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>31/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01", "AI12-0430-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Count, Sum  : Integer;{"\n"}Size        : Integer range 0 .. 10{"_"}000 := 0;{"\n"}Sorted      : Boolean := False;{"\n"}Color{"_"}Table : array(1 .. Max) of Color;{"\n"}Option      : Bit{"_"}Vector(1 .. 10) := (others ={">"} True); -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>{"\n"}Hello       : aliased String := "Hi, world.";{"\n"}&#952;, &#966;        : Float range -&pi; .. +&pi;;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>32_3.3.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of constant declarations:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>33/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01", "AI12-0425-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Limit     : constant Integer := 10{"_"}000;{"\n"}Low{"_"}Limit : constant Integer := Limit/10;{"\n"}Tolerance : constant Real := Dispersion(1.15);{"\n"}A{"_"}String  : constant String := "A";{"\n"}Hello{"_"}Msg : constant access String := Hello'Access; -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>33.a_3.3.1</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> is modified to allow the <b>aliased</b> reserved word.<br />

<MarginText>33.b_3.3.1</MarginText>
A variable declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> can be constrained by its initial value; that is, a variable of a nominally unconstrained array subtype, or discriminated type without defaults, can be declared so long as it has an explicit initial value. In Ada 83, this was permitted for constants, and for variables created by allocators, but not for variables declared by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>s. This is particularly important for tagged class-wide types, since there is no way to constrain them explicitly, and so an initial value is the only way to provide a constraint. It is also important for generic formal private types with unknown discriminants.<br />

<MarginText>33.c_3.3.1</MarginText>
We now allow an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0052">unconstrained_array_definition</a></code> in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>. This allows an object of an anonymous array type to have its bounds determined by its initial value. This is for uniformity: If one can write &ldquo;X: <b>constant</b> <b>array</b>(Integer <b>range</b> 1..10) <b>of</b> Integer := ...;&rdquo; then it makes sense to also allow &ldquo;X: <b>constant</b> <b>array</b>(Integer <b>range</b> {"<"}{">"}) <b>of</b> Integer := ...;&rdquo;. (Note that if anonymous array types are ever sensible, a common situation is for a table implemented as an array. Tables are often constant, and for constants, there's usually no point in forcing the user to count the number of elements in the value.) <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>33.d_3.3.1</MarginText>
We have moved the syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>s into this subclause.<br />

<MarginText>33.e_3.3.1</MarginText>
Deferred constants no longer have a separate syntax rule, but rather are incorporated in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> as constants declared without an initialization expression. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 95

<MarginText>33.f/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
Unconstrained aliased objects of types with discriminants with defaults are no longer constrained by their initial values. This means that a program that raised Constraint{"_"}Error from an attempt to change the discriminants will no longer do so. The change only affects programs that depended on the raising of Constraint{"_"}Error in this case, so the inconsistency is unlikely to occur outside of the ACATS. This change may however cause compilers to implement these objects differently, possibly taking additional memory or time. This is unlikely to be worse than the differences caused by any major compiler upgrade. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>33.g/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
A constant may have a limited type; the initialization <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> has to be built-in-place (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>).<br />

<MarginText>33.h/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00385-01", "AI95-00406-01"]} />
A stand-alone object may have an anonymous access type. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>33.i/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected wording to say that per-object constraints are elaborated (not evaluated).<br />

<MarginText>33.j/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01"]} />
The rules for evaluating default initialization have been tightened. In particular, components whose default initialization can refer to the rest of the object are required to be initialized last.<br />

<MarginText>33.k/2_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
Added examples of various new constructs. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>33.l/3_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>33.m/3_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1"]} />
Implicit initial values can now be given for scalar types and for scalar array components, using the Default{"_"}Value (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>) and Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>) aspects; the extension is documented there. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>33.n/5_3.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0192-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Components of a protected type require late initialization if their initialization includes (implicitly) the current instance of the type. This means that the components could end up being initialized in a different order. In most cases, this will have no visible effect, or will even fix bugs. Most code for which this is an issue depends on the (unspecified) order of initialization, so it is at risk of failing with a new compiler version regardless of Ada rule changes. However, there do exist very unlikely cases where legal, portable Ada 2012 code would become erroneous. (See the discussion section of  for an example.) These are so unlikely that it is expected that they only exist in the minds of Ada lawyers. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.3.2"></a>

## 3.3.2  Number Declarations

<MarginText>1_3.3.2</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code> declares a named number. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5_3.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>If a value or other property of a construct is required to be <i>static</i> that means it is required to be determined prior to execution. A <i>static</i> expression is an expression whose value is computed at compile time and is usable in contexts where the actual value might affect the legality of the construct. This is fully defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9">4.9</a>. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_3.3.2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>number{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0034"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : <b>constant</b> := <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>;<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3_3.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> given for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code> is expected to be of any numeric type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.1/5_3.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0394-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code> is interpreted as a value of a universal type, unless the expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is a non-numeric type with an Integer{"_"}Literal or Real{"_"}Literal aspect, in which case it is interpreted to be of its expected type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/5_3.3.2</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>This is only a Name Resolution Rule; all named numbers are values of a universal type (see the Static Semantics below). We need this rule so that named numbers can match types with user-defined literals; we need the other rules so the value of the named number is well-defined in all cases. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_3.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>The <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> given for a number declaration shall be a static expression, as defined by <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9">4.9</a>. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5_3.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The named number denotes a value of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i> if the type of the <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is an integer type. The named number denotes a value of type <i>universal{"_"}real</i> if the type of the <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is a real type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6_3.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The value denoted by the named number is the value of the <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, converted to the corresponding universal type. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7_3.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code> has no effect. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a_3.3.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Since the <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> was evaluated at compile time. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>8_3.3.2</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of number declarations:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>9_3.3.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Two{"_"}Pi        : constant := 2.0{"*"}Ada.Numerics.Pi; {"\n"}                                          -- a real number (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5">A.5</a>){"\n"}
<MarginText>10/2_3.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
Max           : constant := 500;          -- an integer number{"\n"}Max{"_"}Line{"_"}Size : constant := Max/6;        -- the integer 83{"\n"}Power{"_"}16      : constant := 2{"*"}{"*"}16;        -- the integer 65{"_"}536{"\n"}One, Un, Eins : constant := 1;            -- three different names for 1{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>10.a_3.3.2</MarginText>
We now allow a static expression of any numeric type to initialize a named number. For integer types, it was possible in Ada 83 to use 'Pos to define a named number, but there was no way to use a static expression of some nonuniversal real type to define a named number. This change is upward compatible because of the preference rule for the operators of the root numeric types. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>10.b_3.3.2</MarginText>
We have moved the syntax rule into this subclause.<br />

<MarginText>10.c_3.3.2</MarginText>
AI83-00263 describes the elaboration of a number declaration in words similar to that of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>. However, since there is no expression to be evaluated and no object to be created, it seems simpler to say that the elaboration has no effect. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>10.d/5_3.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0394-1"]} />
Named numbers now can be used with (non-numeric) types that define user-defined literals (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>). <br />

---

# 3.4. Derived Types and Classes

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  22

# 3.4. Derived Types and Classes

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00401-01", "AI95-00419-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> defines a <i>derived type</i> (and its first subtype) whose characteristics are <i>derived</i> from those of a parent type, and possibly from progenitor types. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>derived type</b> &mdash; type defined in terms of a parent type and zero or more progenitor types given in a derived type definition<br />Note 1: A derived type inherits properties such as components and primitive operations from its parent and progenitors.<br />Note 2: A type together with the types derived from it (directly or indirectly) form a derivation class.<br />

<MarginText>1.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00442-01"]} />
<p>A <i>class of types</i> is a set of types that is closed under derivation; that is, if the parent or a progenitor type of a derived type belongs to a class, then so does the derived type. By saying that a particular group of types forms a class, we are saying that all derivatives of a type in the set inherit the characteristics that define that set. The more general term <i>category of types</i> is used for a set of types whose defining characteristics are not necessarily inherited by derivatives; for example, limited, abstract, and interface are all categories of types, but not classes of types.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.b/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A class of types is also a category of types. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00419-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>derived{"_"}type{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0035"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    [<b>abstract</b>] [<b>limited</b>] <b>new</b> <i>parent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> [[<b>and</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0078">interface_list</a></code>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00401-01", "AI95-00419-01"]} />
<p>The <i>parent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> defines the <i>parent subtype</i>; its type is the <i>parent type</i>. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0078">interface_list</a></code> defines the progenitor types (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.4">3.9.4</a>). A derived type has one parent type and zero or more progenitor types.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>parent of a derived type</b> &mdash; first ancestor type given in the definition of the derived type<br />Note: The parent can be almost any kind of type, including an interface type.<br />

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>A type shall be completely defined (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#Subclause_3.11.1">3.11.1</a>) prior to being specified as the parent type in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> &mdash; [the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>s for the parent type and any of its subcomponents have to precede the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This restriction does not apply to the ancestor type of a private extension &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3">7.3</a>; such a type need not be completely defined prior to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#S0233">private_extension_declaration</a></code>. However, the restriction does apply to record extensions, so the ancestor type will have to be completely defined prior to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> corresponding to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#S0233">private_extension_declaration</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We originally hoped we could relax this restriction. However, we found it too complex to specify the rules for a type derived from an incompletely defined limited type that subsequently became nonlimited. <br />

<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00401-01"]} />
<p>If there is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code>, the derived type is called a <i>record extension</i> of the parent type. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code> shall be provided if and only if the parent type is a tagged type. [An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0078">interface_list</a></code> shall be provided only if the parent type is a tagged type.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00401-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The syntax only allows an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0078">interface_list</a></code> to appear with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code>, and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code> can only be provided if the parent type is a tagged type. We give the last sentence anyway for completeness. <br />

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>We allow a record extension to inherit discriminants; an early version of Ada 9X did not. If the parent subtype is unconstrained, it can be implemented as though its discriminants were repeated in a new <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> and then used to constrain the old ones one-for-one. However, in an extension aggregate, the discriminants in this case do not appear in the component association list. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule needs to be rechecked in the visible part of an instance of a generic unit because of the &ldquo;only if&rdquo; part of the rule. For example: <br />

<MarginText>5.c/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type T is private;{"\n"}package P is{"\n"}   type Der is new T;{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>5.d/2</MarginText>
package I is new P (Some{"_"}Tagged{"_"}Type); -- illegal{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
The instantiation is illegal because a tagged type is being extended in the visible part without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code>. Note that this is legal in the private part or body of an instance, both to avoid a contract model violation, and because no code that can see that the type is actually tagged can also see the derived type declaration.<br />

<MarginText>5.f/2</MarginText>
No recheck is needed for derived types with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code>, as that has to be derived from something that is known to be tagged (otherwise the template is illegal). <br />

<MarginText>5.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00419-01", "AI05-0096-1"]} />
<p>If the reserved word <b>limited</b> appears in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>, the parent type shall be a limited type. If the parent type is a tagged formal type, then in addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), this rule applies also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.g/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We allow <b>limited</b> because we don't inherit limitedness from interfaces, so we must have a way to derive a limited type from interfaces. The word <b>limited</b> has to be legal when the parent <i>could be</i> an interface, and that includes generic formal abstract types. Since we have to allow it in this case, we might as well allow it everywhere as documentation, to make it explicit that the type is limited.<br />

<MarginText>5.h/2</MarginText>
However, we do not want to allow <b>limited</b> when the parent is nonlimited: limitedness cannot change in a derivation tree.<br />

<MarginText>5.i/3</MarginText>
If the parent type is an untagged limited formal type with an actual type that is nonlimited, we allow derivation as a limited type in the private part or body as no place could have visibility on the resulting type where it was known to be nonlimited (outside of the instance). (See the previous paragraph's annotations for an explanation of this.) However, if the parent type is a tagged limited formal type with an actual type that is nonlimited, it would be possible to pass a value of the limited type extension to a class-wide type of the parent, which would be nonlimited. That's too weird to allow (even though all of the extension components would have to be nonlimited because the rules of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a> are rechecked), so we have a special rule to prevent that in the private part (type extension from a formal type is illegal in a generic package body). <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>The first subtype of the derived type is unconstrained if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> is provided in the declaration of the derived type, or if the parent subtype is unconstrained. Otherwise, the constraint of the first subtype <i>corresponds</i> to that of the parent subtype in the following sense: it is the same as that of the parent subtype except that for a range constraint (implicit or explicit), the value of each bound of its range is replaced by the corresponding value of the derived type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> for a decimal fixed point subtype always imposes a range constraint, implicitly if there is no explicit one given. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.9">3.5.9</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.9">Fixed Point Types</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>6.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<p>The first subtype of the derived type excludes null (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10">3.10</a>) if and only if the parent subtype excludes null.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0110-1"]} />
<p>The <i>characteristics</i> and implicitly declared primitive subprograms of the derived type are defined as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0110-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The characteristics of a type do not include its primitive subprograms (primitive subprograms include predefined operators). The rules governing availability/visibility and inheritance of characteristics are separate from those for primitive subprograms. <br />

<MarginText>8/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00401-01", "AI95-00442-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>[If the parent type or a progenitor type belongs to a class of types, then the derived type also belongs to that class.] The following sets of types, as well as any higher-level sets composed from them, are classes in this sense[, and hence the characteristics defining these classes are inherited by derived types from their parent or progenitor types]: signed integer, modular integer, ordinary fixed, decimal fixed, floating point, enumeration, boolean, character, access-to-constant, general access-to-variable, pool-specific access-to-variable, access-to-subprogram, array, string, non-array composite, nonlimited, untagged record, tagged, task, protected, and synchronized tagged. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This is inherent in our notion of a &ldquo;class&rdquo; of types. It is not mentioned in the initial definition of &ldquo;class&rdquo; since at that point type derivation has not been defined. In any case, this rule ensures that every class of types is closed under derivation. <br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the parent type is an elementary type or an array type, then the set of possible values of the derived type is a copy of the set of possible values of the parent type. For a scalar type, the base range of the derived type is the same as that of the parent type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The base range of a type defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0041">integer_type_definition</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0044">real_type_definition</a></code> is determined by the <code>{"_"}definition</code>, and is not necessarily the same as that of the corresponding root numeric type from which the newly defined type is implicitly derived. Treating numerics types as implicitly derived from one of the two root numeric types is simply to link them into a type hierarchy; such an implicit derivation does not follow all the rules given here for an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the parent type is a composite type other than an array type, then the components, protected subprograms, and entries that are declared for the derived type are as follows: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The discriminants specified by a new <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code>, if there is one; otherwise, each discriminant of the parent type (implicitly declared in the same order with the same specifications) &mdash; in the latter case, the discriminants are said to be <i>inherited</i>, or if unknown in the parent, are also unknown in the derived type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<li>Each nondiscriminant component, entry, and protected subprogram of the parent type, implicitly declared in the same order with the same declarations; these components, entries, and protected subprograms are said to be <i>inherited</i>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The profiles of entries and protected subprograms do not change upon type derivation, although the type of the &ldquo;implicit&rdquo; parameter identified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> in a call does.<br />

<MarginText>12.b</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Any name in the parent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code> that denotes the current instance of the type is replaced with a name denoting the current instance of the derived type, converted to the parent type.<br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Each component declared in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code>, if any. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Declarations of components, protected subprograms, and entries, whether implicit or explicit, occur immediately within the declarative region of the type, in the order indicated above, following the parent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The order of declarations within the region matters for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>14.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In most cases, these things are implicitly declared <i>immediately</i> following the parent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>. However, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">7.3.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">Private Operations</a>&rdquo; defines some cases in which they are implicitly declared later, and some cases in which the are not declared at all. <br />

<MarginText>14.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The place of the implicit declarations of inherited components matters for visibility &mdash; they are not visible in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> nor in the parent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>, but are usually visible within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code>, if any (although there are restrictions on their use). Note that a discriminant specified in a new <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> is not considered &ldquo;inherited&rdquo; even if it has the same name and subtype as a discriminant of the parent type. <br />

<MarginText>15/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00419-01"]} />
<ul>
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<li>[For each predefined operator of the parent type, there is a corresponding predefined operator of the derived type.] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This is a ramification of the fact that each class that includes the parent type also includes the derived type, and the fact that the set of predefined operators that is defined for a type, as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5">4.5</a>, is determined by the classes to which it belongs. <br />

<MarginText>16.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Predefined operators are handled separately because they follow a slightly different rule than user-defined primitive subprograms. In particular the systematic replacement described below does not apply fully to the relational operators for Boolean and the exponentiation operator for Integer. The relational operators for a type derived from Boolean still return Standard.Boolean. The exponentiation operator for a type derived from Integer still expects Standard.Integer for the right operand. In addition, predefined operators "reemerge" when a type is the actual type corresponding to a generic formal type, so they need to be well defined even if hidden by user-defined primitive subprograms. <br />

<MarginText>17/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00401-01"]} />
<ul>
