#### Inconsistencies With Ada 83

<MarginText>28.a_3.5.9</MarginText>
In Ada 95, S'Small always equals S'Base'Small, so if an implementation chooses a <i>small</i> for a fixed point type smaller than required by the <i>delta</i>, the value of S'Small in Ada 95 might not be the same as it was in Ada 83. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>28.b/3_3.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
Decimal fixed point types are new, though their capabilities are essentially similar to that available in Ada 83 with a fixed point type whose <i>small</i> equals its <i>delta</i> and both are a power of 10. However, in the Information Systems Annex, additional requirements are placed on the support of decimal fixed point types (e.g. a minimum of 18 digits of precision). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>28.c_3.5.9</MarginText>
The syntax rules for <code>fixed{"_"}point{"_"}constraint</code> and <code>fixed{"_"}accuracy{"_"}definition</code> are removed. The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0047">fixed_point_definition</a></code> is new. A syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> is included in the Obsolescent features (to be compatible with Ada 83's <code>fixed{"_"}point{"_"}constraint</code>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>28.d/2_3.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00100-01"]} />
Added wording to define the machine numbers of fixed point types; this is needed by the static evaluation rules. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.e/4_3.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Changed the syntax so that the value following <b>digits</b> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>. This is compatible with one very unlikely exception: if the <b>digits</b> expression is a static expression of a modular type using an unparenthesized logical operator (like <b>and</b> or <b>or</b>). Parenthesizing the expression will make it legal in that case. The change is necessary to eliminate syntax ambguities in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>s. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.f/4_3.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0159-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum</b>:Added wording to define the expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code>. This was missing since Ada 95, but as it is obvious and unchanged from Ada 83, we don't consider it an incompatibility. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.5.10"></a>

## 3.5.10  Operations of Fixed Point Types

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_3.5.10</MarginText>
<p>The following attributes are defined for every fixed point subtype S: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Small</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00054-01", "AI12-0367-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>{"{"}<i>8652/0005</i>{"}"} S'Small denotes the <i>small</i> of the type of S. The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}real</i>. Small may be specified for nonderived ordinary fixed point types via an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute{"_"}definition{"_"}clause</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>); the expression of such a clause shall be static and positive.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>2.a/3_3.5.10</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Small: </b>Scale factor for a fixed point type.<br />

<MarginText>3_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Delta</dt>
<dl>
<dd>S'Delta denotes the <i>delta</i> of the fixed point subtype S. The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}real</i>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.a_3.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The <i>delta</i> is associated with the <i>sub</i>type as opposed to the type, because of the possibility of an (obsolescent) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>4_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Fore</dt>
<dl>
<dd>S'Fore yields the minimum number of characters needed before the decimal point for the decimal representation of any value of the subtype S, assuming that the representation does not include an exponent, but includes a one-character prefix that is either a minus sign or a space. (This minimum number does not include superfluous zeros or underlines, and is at least 2.) The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>5_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Aft</dt>
<dd>S'Aft yields the number of decimal digits needed after the decimal point to accommodate the <i>delta</i> of the subtype S, unless the <i>delta</i> of the subtype S is greater than 0.1, in which case the attribute yields the value one. [(S'Aft is the smallest positive integer N for which (10{"*"}{"*"}N){"*"}S'Delta is greater than or equal to one.)] The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6_3.5.10</MarginText>
<p>The following additional attributes are defined for every decimal fixed point subtype S: <br /></p>

<MarginText>7_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Digits</dt>
<dl>
<dd>S'Digits denotes the <i>digits</i> of the decimal fixed point subtype S, which corresponds to the number of decimal digits that are representable in objects of the subtype. The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. Its value is determined as follows: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>8_3.5.10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a first subtype or a subtype defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code>, the digits is the value of the expression given after the reserved word <b>digits</b>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/5_3.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0426-1"]} />
<li>For a subtype defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code>, the digits of the subtype is the same as that of the subtype denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a_3.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Although a decimal subtype can be both range-constrained and digits-constrained, the digits constraint is intended to control the Size attribute of the subtype. For decimal types, Size can be important because input/output of decimal types is so common. <br />

<MarginText>10_3.5.10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The digits of a base subtype is the largest integer <i>D</i> such that the range &ndash;(10{"*"}{"*"}<i>D</i>&ndash;1){"*"}<i>delta</i> .. +(10{"*"}{"*"}<i>D</i>&ndash;1){"*"}<i>delta</i> is included in the base range of the type.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Scale</dt>
<dl>
<dd>S'Scale denotes the <i>scale</i> of the subtype S, defined as the value N such that S'Delta = 10.0{"*"}{"*"}(&ndash;N). [The scale indicates the position of the point relative to the rightmost significant digits of values of subtype S.] The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>11.a_3.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>S'Scale is negative if S'Delta is greater than one. By contrast, S'Aft is always positive. <br />

<MarginText>12_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Round</dt>
<dl>
<dd>S'Round denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>13_3.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Round(X : universal{"_"}real){"\n"}  return S'Base{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14_3.5.10</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>The function returns the value obtained by rounding X (away from 0, if X is midway between two values of the type of S). <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>15_3.5.10</MarginText>
NOTE 1   All subtypes of a fixed point type will have the same value for the Delta attribute, in the absence of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3">J.3</a>).<br />

<MarginText>16_3.5.10</MarginText>
NOTE 2   S'Scale is not always the same as S'Aft for a decimal subtype; for example, if S'Delta = 1.0 then S'Aft is 1 while S'Scale is 0.<br />

<MarginText>17_3.5.10</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The predefined operations of a fixed point type include the assignment operation, qualification, the membership tests, and explicit conversion to and from other numeric types. They also include the relational operators and the following predefined arithmetic operators: the binary and unary adding operators &ndash; and +, multiplying operators, and the unary operator <b>abs</b>.<br />

<MarginText>18_3.5.10</MarginText>
NOTE 4   As for all types, objects of a fixed point type have Size and Address attributes (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>). Other attributes of fixed point types are defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.4">A.5.4</a>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>18.a/2_3.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00054-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0005</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that <i>small</i> may be specified only for ordinary fixed point types. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>18.b/5_3.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0367-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified that <i>small</i> may be specified only with positive values. <br />

# 3.6. Array Types

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6.mdx

sidebar_position:  24

# 3.6. Array Types

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>An <i>array</i> object is a composite object consisting of components which all have the same subtype. The name for a component of an array uses one or more index values belonging to specified discrete types. The value of an array object is a composite value consisting of the values of the components. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>array{"_"}type{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0051"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0052">unconstrained_array_definition</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0054">constrained_array_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>unconstrained{"_"}array{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0052"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>array</b>(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0053">index_subtype_definition</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0053">index_subtype_definition</a></code>{"}"}) <b>of</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>index{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0053"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> <b>range</b> {"<"}{">"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>constrained{"_"}array{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0054"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>array</b> (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>{"}"}) <b>of</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0055"></a><code> ::= </code><i>discrete{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00406-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>component{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0056"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<b>aliased</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code><br /> | [<b>aliased</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> shall resolve to be of some specific discrete type[; which discrete type shall be determined without using any context other than the bounds of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> itself (plus the preference for <i>root{"_"}integer</i> &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>).] <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>Each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0053">index_subtype_definition</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> defines an <i>index subtype</i>; its type (the <i>index type</i>) shall be discrete. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>An <i>index</i> is a discrete quantity used to select along a given dimension of an array. A component is selected by specifying corresponding values for each of the indices. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>The subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> (the <i>component subtype</i>) shall be a definite subtype. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This applies to all uses of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code>, including in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0066">record_type_definition</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>11/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>An array is characterized by the number of indices (the <i>dimensionality</i> of the array), the type and position of each index, the lower and upper bounds for each index, and the subtype of the components. The order of the indices is significant.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>A one-dimensional array has a distinct component for each possible index value. A multidimensional array has a distinct component for each possible sequence of index values that can be formed by selecting one value for each index position (in the given order). The possible values for a given index are all the values between the lower and upper bounds, inclusive; this range of values is called the <i>index range</i>. The <i>bounds</i> of an array are the bounds of its index ranges. The <i>length</i> of a dimension of an array is the number of values of the index range of the dimension (zero for a null range). The <i>length</i> of a one-dimensional array is the length of its only dimension.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> defines an array type and its first subtype. For each object of this array type, the number of indices, the type and position of each index, and the subtype of the components are as in the type definition[; the values of the lower and upper bounds for each index belong to the corresponding index subtype of its type, except for null arrays (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.1">3.6.1</a>)].<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0052">unconstrained_array_definition</a></code> defines an array type with an unconstrained first subtype. Each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0053">index{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> defines the corresponding index subtype to be the subtype denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype{"_"}mark</a></code>. [ The compound delimiter {"<"}{">"} (called a <i>box</i>) of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0053">index_subtype_definition</a></code> stands for an undefined range (different objects of the type can have different bounds).]<br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0054">constrained_array_definition</a></code> defines an array type with a constrained first subtype. Each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> defines the corresponding index subtype, as well as the corresponding index range for the constrained first subtype. The <i>constraint</i> of the first subtype consists of the bounds of the index ranges. <br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Although there is no nameable unconstrained array subtype in this case, the predefined slicing and concatenation operations can operate on and yield values that do not necessarily belong to the first array subtype. This is also true for Ada 83. <br />

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p>The discrete subtype defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> is either that defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>, or a subtype determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> resolves to <i>root{"_"}integer</i>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> defines a subtype of the predefined type Integer with bounds given by a conversion to Integer of the bounds of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that indexing over the discrete subtype can be performed with regular Integers, rather than only <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>s. <br />

<MarginText>18.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We considered doing this by simply creating a &ldquo;preference&rdquo; for Integer when resolving the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>. However, this can introduce <i>Beaujolais</i> effects when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>s involve calls on functions visible due to <b>use</b> clauses. <br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> defines a subtype of the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>, with the bounds given by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20</MarginText>
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> defines the nominal subtype of the components. If the reserved word <b>aliased</b> appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code>, then each component of the array is aliased (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10">3.10</a>). <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> creates the array type and its first subtype, and consists of the elaboration of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>s and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component{"_"}definition</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01", "AI95-00230-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> that does not contain any per-object expressions creates the discrete subtype, and consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> or the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>. The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> that contains one or more per-object expressions is defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8">3.8</a>. The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component{"_"}definition</a></code> in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array{"_"}type{"_"}definition</a></code> consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>. The elaboration of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>s and the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component{"_"}definition</a></code> are performed in an arbitrary order. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>22.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1"]} />
<p>For an array type with a scalar component type, the following language-defined representation aspect may be specified with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>): <br /></p>

<MarginText>22.2/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect shall be specified by a static expression, and that expression shall be explicit, even if the aspect has a boolean type. Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value shall be specified only on a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>22.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The part about requiring an explicit expression is to disallow omitting the value for this aspect, which would otherwise be allowed by the rules of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>.<br />

<MarginText>22.b/3</MarginText>
This is a representation attribute in order to disallow specifying it on a derived type that has inherited primitive subprograms; that is necessary as the sizes of <b>out</b> parameters could be different whether or not a Default{"_"}Value is specified (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>). <br />

<MarginText>22.c/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value: </b>Default value for the components of an array-of-scalar subtype.<br />

<MarginText>22.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1", "AI12-0427-1"]} />
<p>If a derived type inherits a boolean Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value aspect, the aspect may be specified to have any value for the derived type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22.d/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This overrides the <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a> rule that says that a boolean aspect with a value True cannot be changed. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>22.4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> specified for the Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value aspect is the component type of the array type defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> on which it appears. <br /></p>

<MarginText>23</MarginText>
NOTE 1   All components of an array have the same subtype. In particular, for an array of components that are one-dimensional arrays, this means that all components have the same bounds and hence the same length.<br />

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
NOTE 2   Each elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> creates a distinct array type. A consequence of this is that each object whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> contains an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0051">array_type_definition</a></code> is of its own unique type. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of type declarations with unconstrained array definitions:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>26</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Vector     is array(Integer  range {"<"}{">"}) of Real;{"\n"}type Matrix     is array(Integer  range {"<"}{">"}, Integer range {"<"}{">"}) of Real;{"\n"}type Bit{"_"}Vector is array(Integer  range {"<"}{">"}) of Boolean;{"\n"}type Roman      is array(Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Roman{"_"}Digit; -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.2">3.5.2</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>27</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of type declarations with constrained array definitions:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>28</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Table    is array(1 .. 10) of Integer;{"\n"}type Schedule is array(Day) of Boolean;{"\n"}type Line     is array(1 .. Max{"_"}Line{"_"}Size) of Character;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>29</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of object declarations with array type definitions:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>30/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Grid      : array(1 .. 80, 1 .. 100) of Boolean;{"\n"}Mix       : array(Color range Red .. Green) of Boolean;{"\n"}Msg{"_"}Table : constant array(Error{"_"}Code) of access constant String :={"\n"}      (Too{"_"}Big ={">"} new String'("Result too big"), Too{"_"}Small ={">"} ...);{"\n"}Page      : array(Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Line := -- an array of arrays{"\n"}  (1 | 50  ={">"} Line'(1 | Line'Last ={">"} '+', others ={">"} '-'), -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.3">4.3.3</a>{"\n"}   2 .. 49 ={">"} Line'(1 | Line'Last ={">"} '|', others ={">"} ' '));{"\n"}    -- Page is constrained by its initial value to (1..50){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>30.a</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> is modified to allow the reserved word <b>aliased</b>.<br />

<MarginText>30.b</MarginText>
The syntax rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0052">unconstrained_array_definition</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0054">constrained_array_definition</a></code> are modified to use <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> (instead of <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>). The effect of this change is to allow the reserved word <b>aliased</b> before the component <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>30.c</MarginText>
A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> may use arbitrary universal expressions for each bound (e.g. &ndash;1 .. 3+5), rather than strictly "implicitly convertible" operands. The subtype defined will still be a subtype of Integer. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>30.d</MarginText>
We introduce a new syntactic category, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>, as distinct from <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>. These two constructs have the same syntax, but their semantics are quite different (one defines a subtype, with a preference for Integer subtypes, while the other just selects a subrange of an existing subtype). We use this new syntactic category in <b>for</b> loops and entry families.<br />

<MarginText>30.e</MarginText>
The syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> have been moved to their own subclause, since they are no longer used here.<br />

<MarginText>30.f</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> (formerly <code>component{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</code>) is moved here from RM83-3.7. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>30.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00406-01"]} />
Array components can have an anonymous access type.<br />

<MarginText>30.h/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
The prohibition against unconstrained discriminated aliased components has been lifted. It has been replaced by a prohibition against the actual troublemakers: general access discriminant constraints (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#Subclause_3.7.1">3.7.1</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>30.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added wording to allow the elaboration of per-object constraints for constrained arrays. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>30.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1"]} />
The new aspect Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value allows defining implicit initial values (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>) for arrays of scalar types. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.6.1"></a>

## 3.6.1  Index Constraints and Discrete Ranges

<MarginText>1_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> determines the range of possible values for every index of an array subtype, and thereby the corresponding array bounds. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_3.6.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>index{"_"}constraint</code><a id="S0057"></a><code> ::= </code> (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>{"}"})<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_3.6.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>discrete{"_"}range</code><a id="S0058"></a><code> ::= </code><i>discrete{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>4_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p>The type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> is the type of the subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>, or the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>. For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code>, each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> shall resolve to be of the type of the corresponding index. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a_3.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In Ada 95, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code>s only appear in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>; they no longer appear in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0054">constrained_array_definition</a></code>s. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> shall appear only in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes either an unconstrained array subtype, or an unconstrained access subtype whose designated subtype is an unconstrained array subtype; in either case, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> shall provide a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> for each index of the array type. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> defines a range whose bounds are given by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>, or by the range of the subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> is <i>compatible</i> with an unconstrained array subtype if and only if the index range defined by each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> is compatible (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>) with the corresponding index subtype. If any of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>s defines a null range, any array thus constrained is a <i>null array</i>, having no components. An array value <i>satisfies</i> an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> if at each index position the array value and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> have the same index bounds. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a_3.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is no need to define compatibility with a constrained array subtype, because one is not allowed to constrain it again.<br />

<MarginText>8_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> consists of the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>(s), in an arbitrary order. The evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> or the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9_3.6.1</MarginText>
NOTE 1   The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> consisting of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> followed by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> checks the compatibility of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.2">3.2.2</a>).<br />

<MarginText>10_3.6.1</MarginText>
NOTE 2   Even if an array value does not satisfy the index constraint of an array subtype, Constraint{"_"}Error is not raised on conversion to the array subtype, so long as the length of each dimension of the array value and the array subtype match. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>11_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of array declarations including an index constraint:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_3.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Board     : Matrix(1 .. 8,  1 .. 8);  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>{"\n"}Rectangle : Matrix(1 .. 20, 1 .. 30);{"\n"}Inverse   : Matrix(1 .. N,  1 .. N);  -- N can be nonstatic{"\n"}
<MarginText>13/5_3.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI125-0430-1"]} />
Filter    : Bit{"_"}Vector(0 .. 31);      -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of array declaration with a constrained array subtype:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>15_3.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
My{"_"}Schedule : Schedule;  -- all arrays of type Schedule have the same bounds{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16_3.6.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of record type with a component that is an array:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>17_3.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Var{"_"}Line(Length : Natural) is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Image : String(1 .. Length);{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>18_3.6.1</MarginText>
Null{"_"}Line : Var{"_"}Line(0);  -- Null{"_"}Line.Image is a null array{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>18.a_3.6.1</MarginText>
We allow the declaration of a variable with a nominally unconstrained array subtype, so long as it has an initialization expression to determine its bounds. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>18.b_3.6.1</MarginText>
We have moved the syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> here since they are no longer used in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0054">constrained_array_definition</a></code>s. We therefore also no longer have to describe the (special) semantics of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0057">index_constraint</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>s that appear in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0054">constrained_array_definition</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>18.c_3.6.1</MarginText>
The rules given in RM83-3.6.1(5,7-10), which define the bounds of an array object, are redundant with rules given elsewhere, and so are not repeated here. RM83-3.6.1(6), which requires that the (nominal) subtype of an array variable be constrained, no longer applies, so long as the variable is explicitly initialized. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.6.2"></a>

## 3.6.2  Operations of Array Types

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>1_3.6.2</MarginText>
<p>[The argument N used in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code>s for the N-th dimension of an array shall be a static <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of some integer type.] The value of N shall be positive (nonzero) and no greater than the dimensionality of the array. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/1_3.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00030-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0006</i>{"}"} The following attributes are defined for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> A that is of an array type [(after any implicit dereference)], or denotes a constrained array subtype: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a_3.6.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>These attributes are not defined if A is a subtype-mark for an access-to-array subtype. They are defined (by implicit dereference) for access-to-array values.<br />

<MarginText>3_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'First</dt>
<dl>
<dd>A'First denotes the lower bound of the first index range; its type is the corresponding index type.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>4_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'First(N)</dt>
<dd>A'First(N) denotes the lower bound of the N-th index range; its type is the corresponding index type.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>5_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Last</dt>
<dd>A'Last denotes the upper bound of the first index range; its type is the corresponding index type.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Last(N)</dt>
<dd>A'Last(N) denotes the upper bound of the N-th index range; its type is the corresponding index type.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>7_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Range</dt>
<dd>A'Range is equivalent to the range A'First .. A'Last, except that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> A is only evaluated once.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>8_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Range(N)</dt>
<dd>A'Range(N) is equivalent to the range A'First(N) .. A'Last(N), except that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> A is only evaluated once.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>9_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Length</dt>
<dd>A'Length denotes the number of values of the first index range (zero for a null range); its type is <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>10_3.6.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Length(N)</dt>
<dd>A'Length(N) denotes the number of values of the N-th index range (zero for a null range); its type is <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. <br /></dd>
</dl>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>11/3_3.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An implementation should normally represent multidimensional arrays in row-major order, consistent with the notation used for multidimensional array aggregates (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.3">4.3.3</a>). However, if convention Fortran is specified for a multidimensional array type, then column-major order should be used instead (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.5">B.5</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.5">Interfacing with Fortran</a>&rdquo;). <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/2_3.6.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Multidimensional arrays should be represented in row-major order, unless the array has convention Fortran.<br />

<MarginText>12_3.6.2</MarginText>
NOTE 1   The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>s A'First and A'First(1) denote the same value. A similar relation exists for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>s A'Last, A'Range, and A'Length. The following relation is satisfied (except for a null array) by the above attributes if the index type is an integer type: <br />

<MarginText>13_3.6.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   A'Length(N) = A'Last(N) - A'First(N) + 1{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14_3.6.2</MarginText>
NOTE 2   An array type is limited if its component type is limited (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>).<br />

<MarginText>15_3.6.2</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The predefined operations of an array type include the membership tests, qualification, and explicit conversion. If the array type is not limited, they also include assignment and the predefined equality operators. For a one-dimensional array type, they include the predefined concatenation operators (if nonlimited) and, if the component type is discrete, the predefined relational operators; if the component type is boolean, the predefined logical operators are also included.<br />

<MarginText>16/2_3.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
NOTE 4   A component of an array can be named with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>. A value of an array type can be specified with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code>. For a one-dimensional array type, a slice of the array can be named; also, string literals are defined if the component type is a character type. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>17/5_3.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p><i>Examples (using arrays declared in the examples of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.1">3.6.1</a>):</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>18_3.6.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
-- Filter'First      =  0   Filter'Last       = 31   Filter'Length = 32{"\n"}-- Rectangle'Last(1) = 20   Rectangle'Last(2) = 30{"\n"}
<a id="Subclause_3.6.3"></a>

</CodeBlock>

## 3.6.3  String Types

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_3.6.3</MarginText>
<p>A one-dimensional array type whose component type is a character type is called a <i>string type</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/2_3.6.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
<p>[There are three predefined string types, String, Wide{"_"}String, and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String, each indexed by values of the predefined subtype Positive; these are declared in the visible part of package Standard:] <br /></p>

<MarginText>3_3.6.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
[subtype Positive is Integer range 1 .. Integer'Last;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4/2_3.6.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
type String is array(Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Character;{"\n"}type Wide{"_"}String is array(Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Wide{"_"}Character;{"\n"}type Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String is array(Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Character;{"\n"}]{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5_3.6.3</MarginText>
NOTE   String literals (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6">2.6</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2">4.2</a>) are defined for all string types. The concatenation operator & is predefined for string types, as for all nonlimited one-dimensional array types. The ordering operators {"<"}, {"<"}=, {">"}, and {">"}= are predefined for string types, as for all one-dimensional discrete array types; these ordering operators correspond to lexicographic order (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.2">4.5.2</a>).<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>6_3.6.3</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of string objects:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>7_3.6.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Stars      : String(1 .. 120) := (1 .. 120 ={">"} '{"*"}' );{"\n"}Question   : constant String  := "How many characters?";{"\n"}                      -- Question'First = 1, Question'Last = 20{"\n"}                      -- Question'Length = 20 (the number of characters){"\n"}
<MarginText>8_3.6.3</MarginText>
Ask{"_"}Twice  : String  := Question & Question; -- constrained to (1..40){"\n"}Ninety{"_"}Six : constant Roman   := "XCVI";     -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.2">3.5.2</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 83

<MarginText>8.a_3.6.3</MarginText>
The declaration of Wide{"_"}String in Standard hides a use-visible declaration with the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>. In rare cases, this might result in an inconsistency between Ada 83 and Ada 95. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>8.b_3.6.3</MarginText>
Because both String and Wide{"_"}String are always directly visible, an expression like <br />

<MarginText>8.c_3.6.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
"a" {"<"} "bc"{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8.d_3.6.3</MarginText>
is now ambiguous, whereas in Ada 83 both string literals could be resolved to type String. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>8.e_3.6.3</MarginText>
The type Wide{"_"}String is new (though it was approved by ARG for Ada 83 compilers as well). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>8.f_3.6.3</MarginText>
We define the term <i>string type</i> as a natural analogy to the term <i>character type</i>. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 95

<MarginText>8.g/2_3.6.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
The declaration of Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String in Standard hides a use-visible declaration with the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>. In the (very) unlikely event that an Ada 95 program had depended on such a use-visible declaration, and the program remains legal after the substitution of Standard.Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String, the meaning of the program will be different. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>8.h/2_3.6.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
The type Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String is new. <br />

---

# 3.7. Discriminants

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7.mdx

sidebar_position:  25

# 3.7. Discriminants

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00326-01"]} />
<p>[ A composite type (other than an array or interface type) can have discriminants, which parameterize the type. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> specifies the discriminants of a composite type. A discriminant of an object is a component of the object, and is either of a discrete type or an access type. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code> in the declaration of a view of a type specifies that the discriminants of the type are unknown for the given view; all subtypes of such a view are indefinite subtypes.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>discriminant</b> &mdash; parameter for a composite type, which can control, for example, the bounds of a component that is an array<br />Note: A discriminant for a task type can be used to pass data to a task of the type upon its creation.<br />

<MarginText>1.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A view of a type, and all subtypes of the view, have <i>unknown discriminants</i> when the number or names of the discriminants, if any, are unknown at the point of the type declaration for the view. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code> of ({"<"}{">"}) is used to indicate unknown discriminants. <br />

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00402-01"]} />
When an access discriminant is initialized at the time of object creation with an allocator of an anonymous type, the allocated object and the object with the discriminant are tied together for their lifetime. They should be allocated out of the same storage pool, and then at the end of the lifetime of the enclosing object, finalized and reclaimed together. In this case, the allocated object is called a coextension (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>). <br />

<MarginText>1.d/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The above principle when applied to a nonlimited type implies that such an object may be copied only to a shorter-lived object, because attempting to assign it to a longer-lived object would fail because the access discriminants would not match. In a copy, the lifetime connection between the enclosing object and the allocated object does not exist. The allocated object is tied in the above sense only to the original object. Other copies have only secondary references to it.<br />

<MarginText>1.e/2</MarginText>
Note that when an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> appears as a constraint on an access discriminant in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> that is elaborated independently from object creation, no such connection exists. For example, if a named constrained subtype is declared via "<b>subtype</b> Constr <b>is</b> Rec(Acc{"_"}Discrim ={">"} <b>new</b> T);" or if such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> for a component, the allocator is evaluated when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> is elaborated, and hence its lifetime is typically longer than the objects or components that will later be subject to the constraint. In these cases, the allocated object should not be reclaimed until the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> goes out of scope. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>unknown{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</code><a id="S0060"></a><code> ::= </code>({"<"}{">"})<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>known{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</code><a id="S0061"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code> {"{"}; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code>{"}"})<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI12-0398-1"]} />

<code>discriminant{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0062"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> [:= <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>]<br />      [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <br /> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> [:= <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>]<br />      [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0398-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Only implementation-defined aspects are allowed on discriminants in Ada 2022. Implementers are cautioned that any aspect allowed on a discriminant will need conformance rules. If, for instance, an aspect changed the representation of a discriminant, rules would be needed to ensure that the representation is the same for all views of the type (partial and full). <br />

<MarginText>6</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>default{"_"}expression</code><a id="S0063"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code> is that of the corresponding discriminant. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>8/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00098-01", "AI95-00251-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0007</i>{"}"} A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code> is only permitted in a declaration for a composite type that is not an array or interface type [(this includes generic formal types)]. A type declared with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> is called a <i>discriminated</i> type, as is a type that inherits (known) discriminants. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Discriminants on array types were considered, but were omitted to ease (existing) implementations. <br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that the above definition for &ldquo;discriminated type&rdquo; does not include types declared with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code>. This seems consistent with Ada 83, where such types (in a generic formal part) would not be considered discriminated types. Furthermore, the full type for a type with unknown discriminants need not even be composite, much less have any discriminants.<br />

<MarginText>8.b.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00098-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0007</i>{"}"} On the other hand, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code>s cannot be applied to type declarations that cannot have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code>. There is no point in having unknown discriminants on a type that can never have discriminants (for instance, a formal modular type), even when these are allowed syntactically. <br />

<MarginText>9/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI95-00254-01"]} />
<p>The subtype of a discriminant may be defined by an optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>, in which case the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> shall denote a discrete or access subtype, or it may be defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>. A discriminant that is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is called an <i>access discriminant</i> and is of an anonymous access type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>9.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Note that discriminants of a named access type are not considered &ldquo;access discriminants&rdquo;. Similarly, &ldquo;access parameter&rdquo; only refers to a formal parameter defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>9.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00402-01", "AI05-0214-1"]} />
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">Default_expression</a></code>s shall be provided either for all or for none of the discriminants of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</a></code>. No <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default{"_"}expression</a></code>s are permitted in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</a></code> in a declaration of a nonlimited tagged type [or a generic formal type].<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.c/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The all-or-none rule is related to the rule that a discriminant constraint shall specify values for all discriminants. One could imagine a different rule that allowed a constraint to specify only some of the discriminants, with the others provided by default. Having defaults for discriminants has a special significance &mdash; it allows objects of the type to be unconstrained, with the discriminants alterable as part of assigning to the object.<br />

<MarginText>9.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0214-1"]} />
Defaults for discriminants of tagged types are disallowed so that every object of a nonlimited tagged type is constrained, either by an explicit constraint, or by its initial discriminant values. This substantially simplifies the semantic rules and the implementation of inherited dispatching operations. We don't need this rule for limited tagged types, as the discriminants of such objects cannot be changed after the object is created in any case &mdash; no full-object assignment is supported, and that is required to change discriminant values. For generic formal types, the restriction simplifies the type matching rules. If one simply wants a "default" value for the discriminants, a constrained subtype can be declared for future use. <br />

<MarginText>10/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00402-01", "AI95-00419-01", "AI05-0063-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code> for an access discriminant may have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> only in the declaration for an immutably limited type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>). In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), this rule applies also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This rule implies that a type can have a default for an access discriminant if the type is limited, but not if the only reason it's limited is because of a limited component. Compare the definition of limited type and immutably limited type in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>. <br />

<MarginText>10.b/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A (nonformal) limited private type can always have a default for an access discriminant, because having the default itself makes the type immutably limited. Such a private type must necessarily have a full type with the same access discriminant with a default, and thus the full type will always be immutably limited (if legal). <br />

<MarginText>10.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We considered the following rules for access discriminants: <br />

<MarginText>10.d</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If a type has an access discriminant, this automatically makes it limited, just like having a limited component automatically makes a type limited. This was rejected because it decreases program readability, and because it seemed error prone (two bugs in a previous version of the RM9X were attributable to this rule).<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.e/2</MarginText>
<li>A type with an access discriminant shall be limited. This is equivalent to the rule we actually chose for Ada 95, except that it allows a type to have an access discriminant if it is limited just because of a limited component. For example, any record containing a task would be allowed to have an access discriminant, whereas the actual rule requires &ldquo;<b>limited</b> <b>record</b>&rdquo;. This rule was also rejected due to readability concerns, and because would interact badly with the rules for limited types that &ldquo;become nonlimited&rdquo;.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.e.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0063-1"]} />
<li>A type may have an access discriminant if it is an immutably limited type. This was the rule chosen for Ada 95.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.f/2</MarginText>
<li>Any type may have an access discriminant. For nonlimited type, there is no special accessibility for access discriminants; they're the same as any other anonymous access component. For a limited type, they have the special accessibility of Ada 95. However, this doesn't work because a limited partial view can have a nonlimited full view -- giving the two views different accessibility.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.f.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0063-1"]} />
<li>Any type may have an access discriminant, as above. However, special accessibility rules only apply to types that are immutably limited (task, protected, and explicitly limited records). However, this breaks privacy; worse, Legality Rules depend on the definition of accessibility.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.f.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0063-1"]} />
<li>Any type may have an access discriminant, as above. Limited types have special accessibility, while nonlimited types have normal accessibility. However, a limited partial view with an access discriminant can only be completed by an immutably limited type. That prevents accessibility from changing. A runtime accessibility check is required on generic formal types with access discriminants. However, changing between limited and nonlimited types would have far-reaching consequences for access discriminants &mdash; which is uncomfortable.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.g/2</MarginText>
<li>Any type may have an access discriminant. All types have special accessibility. This was considered early during the Ada 9X process, but was dropped for &ldquo;unpleasant complexities&rdquo;, which unfortunately aren't recorded. It does seem that an accessibility check would be needed on assignment of such a type, to avoid copying an object with a discriminant pointing to a local object into a more global object (and thus creating a dangling pointer).<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.h/2</MarginText>
<li>Any type may have an access discriminant, but access discriminants cannot have defaults. All types have special accessibility. This gets rid of the problems on assignment (you couldn't change such a discriminant), but it would be horribly incompatible with Ada 95.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.h.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0063-1"]} />
<li>Any type may have an access discriminant, but access discriminants may have defaults only if they are of an immutably limited type. This is the rule chosen for Ada 2005, as it is not incompatible, and it doesn't require weird accessibility checks. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00402-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>For a type defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> is provided in its declaration, then: <br /></p>

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The parent subtype shall be constrained;<br /></li>
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<li>If the parent type is not a tagged type, then each discriminant of the derived type shall be used in the constraint defining the parent subtype;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This ensures that the new discriminant can share storage with an existing discriminant.<br />

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If a discriminant is used in the constraint defining the parent subtype, the subtype of the discriminant shall be statically compatible (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9#Subclause_4.9.1">4.9.1</a>) with the subtype of the corresponding parent discriminant. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that on conversion (or extension via an extension aggregate) to a distantly related type, if the discriminants satisfy the target type's requirements they satisfy all the intermediate types' requirements as well. <br />

<MarginText>15.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is no requirement that the new discriminant have the same (or any) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> as the parent's discriminant. <br />

<MarginText>16/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0102-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/3</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code> declares a discriminant; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes its subtype unless it is an access discriminant, in which case the discriminant's subtype is the anonymous access-to-variable subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<p>[For a type defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>, each discriminant of the parent type is either inherited, constrained to equal some new discriminant of the derived type, or constrained to the value of an expression.] When inherited or constrained to equal some new discriminant, the parent discriminant and the discriminant of the derived type are said to <i>correspond</i>. Two discriminants also correspond if there is some common discriminant to which they both correspond. A discriminant corresponds to itself as well. If a discriminant of a parent type is constrained to a specific value by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>, then that discriminant is said to be <i>specified</i> by that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The correspondence relationship is transitive, symmetric, and reflexive. That is, if A corresponds to B, and B corresponds to C, then A, B, and C each corresponds to A, B, and C in all combinations.<br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> that appears within the definition of a discriminated type <i>depends on a discriminant</i> of the type if it names the discriminant as a bound or discriminant value. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> depends on a discriminant if its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> depends on the discriminant, or on a discriminant that corresponds to it. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code> is not considered to <i>depend</i> on a discriminant of the task type, even if it names it. It is only the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code>s in the type definition itself that are considered dependents. Similarly for protected types. <br />

<MarginText>20</MarginText>
<p>A component <i>depends on a discriminant</i> if: <br /></p>

<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> depends on the discriminant; or <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A component does <i>not</i> depend on a discriminant just because its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> refers to the discriminant.<br />

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>It is declared in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> that is governed by the discriminant; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<li>It is a component inherited as part of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> of the <i>parent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> depends on the discriminant; or <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>When the parent subtype depends on a discriminant, the parent part of the derived type is treated like a discriminant-dependent component. <br />

<MarginText>23.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Because of this rule, we don't really need to worry about &ldquo;corresponding&rdquo; discriminants, since all the inherited components will be discriminant-dependent if there is a new <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> whose discriminants are used to constrain the old discriminants. <br />

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>It is a subcomponent of a component that depends on the discriminant. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The concept of discriminant-dependent (sub)components is primarily used in various rules that disallow renaming or 'Access, or specify that certain discriminant-changing assignments are erroneous. The goal is to allow implementations to move around or change the size of discriminant-dependent subcomponents upon a discriminant-changing assignment to an enclosing object. The above definition specifies that all subcomponents of a discriminant-dependent component or parent part are themselves discriminant-dependent, even though their presence or size does not in fact depend on a discriminant. This is because it is likely that they will move in a discriminant-changing assignment if they are a component of one of several discriminant-dependent parts of the same record. <br />

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p>Each value of a discriminated type includes a value for each component of the type that does not depend on a discriminant[; this includes the discriminants themselves]. The values of discriminants determine which other component values are present in the value of the discriminated type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Which values are present might depend on discriminants of some ancestor type that are constrained in an intervening <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>. That's why we say "values of discriminants" instead of "values of <i>the</i> discriminants" &mdash; a subtle point.<br />

<MarginText>26</MarginText>
<p>A type declared with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> is said to have <i>known discriminants</i>; its first subtype is unconstrained. A type declared with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code> is said to have <i>unknown discriminants</i>. A type declared without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code> has no discriminants, unless it is a derived type; if derived, such a type has the same sort of discriminants (known, unknown, or none) as its parent (or ancestor) type. A tagged class-wide type also has unknown discriminants. [Any subtype of a type with unknown discriminants is an unconstrained and indefinite subtype (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2">3.2</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3">3.3</a>).] <br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code> &ldquo;({"<"}{">"})&rdquo; is only permitted in the declaration of a (generic or nongeneric) private type, private extension, incomplete type, or formal derived type. Hence, only such types, descendants thereof, and class-wide types can have unknown discriminants. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code> is used to indicate that the corresponding actual or full type might have discriminants without defaults, or be an unconstrained array subtype. Tagged class-wide types are also considered to have unknown discriminants because discriminants can be added by type extensions, so the total number of discriminants of any given value of a tagged class-wide type is not known at compile time.<br />

<MarginText>26.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
A subtype with unknown discriminants is indefinite, and hence an object of such a subtype needs explicit initialization. A limited private type with unknown discriminants is &ldquo;extremely&rdquo; limited; objects of such a type  can be initialized only by subprograms (either procedures with a parameter of the type, or a function returning the type) declared in the package. Subprograms declared elsewhere can operate on and even return the type, but they can only initialize the object by calling (ultimately) a subprogram in the package declaring the type. Such a type is useful for keeping complete control over object creation within the package declaring the type.<br />

<MarginText>26.c</MarginText>
A partial view of a type might have unknown discriminants, while the full view of the same type might have known, unknown, or no discriminants. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>27/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
<p>For an access discriminant, its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is elaborated when the value of the access discriminant is defined: by evaluation of its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>, by elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>, or by an assignment that initializes the enclosing object. <br /></p>

<MarginText>27.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The conversion of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> defining the access discriminant to the anonymous access type raises Program{"_"}Error for an object created by an allocator of an access type T, if the initial value is an access parameter that designates a view whose accessibility level is deeper than that of T. <br />

<MarginText>28</MarginText>
NOTE 1   If a discriminated type has <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s for its discriminants, then unconstrained variables of the type are permitted, and the values of the discriminants can be changed by an assignment to such a variable. If defaults are not provided for the discriminants, then all variables of the type are constrained, either by explicit constraint or by their initial value; the values of the discriminants of such a variable cannot be changed after initialization. <br />

<MarginText>28.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This connection between discriminant defaults and unconstrained variables can be a source of confusion. For Ada 95, we considered various ways to break the connection between defaults and unconstrainedness, but ultimately gave up for lack of a sufficiently simple and intuitive alternative.<br />

<MarginText>28.b</MarginText>
An unconstrained discriminated subtype with defaults is called a <i>mutable</i> subtype, and a variable of such a subtype is called a mutable variable, because the discriminants of such a variable can change. There are no mutable arrays (that is, the bounds of an array object can never change), because there is no way in the language to define default values for the bounds. Similarly, there are no mutable class-wide subtypes, because there is no way to define the default tag, and defaults for discriminants are not allowed in the tagged case. Mutable tags would also require a way for the maximum possible size of such a class-wide subtype to be known. (In some implementations, all mutable variables are allocated with the maximum possible size. This approach is appropriate for real-time applications where implicit use of the heap is inappropriate.)<br />

<MarginText>29</MarginText>
NOTE 2   The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> for a discriminant of a type is evaluated when an object of an unconstrained subtype of the type is created.<br />

<MarginText>30</MarginText>
NOTE 3   Assignment to a discriminant of an object (after its initialization) is not allowed, since the name of a discriminant is a constant; neither <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>s nor assignments inherent in passing as an <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> parameter are allowed. Note however that the value of a discriminant can be changed by assigning to the enclosing object, presuming it is an unconstrained variable. <br />

<MarginText>30.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code> is permitted only in the declaration of a private type (including generic formal private), private extension, incomplete type, or generic formal derived type. These are the things that will have a corresponding completion or generic actual, which will either define the discriminants, or say there are none. The ({"<"}{">"}) indicates that the actual/full subtype might be an indefinite subtype. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code> is not permitted in a normal untagged derived type declaration, because there is no separate full type declaration for such a type. Note that ({"<"}{">"}) allows unconstrained array bounds; those are somewhat like undefaulted discriminants.<br />

<MarginText>30.b</MarginText>
For a derived type, either the discriminants are inherited as is, or completely respecified in a new <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code>.
