In this latter case, each discriminant of the parent type shall be constrained, either to a specific value, or to equal one of the new discriminants. Constraining a parent type's discriminant to equal one of the new discriminants is like a renaming of the discriminant, except that the subtype of the new discriminant can be more restrictive than that of the parent's one. In any case, the new discriminant can share storage with the parent's discriminant. <br />

<MarginText>31</MarginText>
NOTE 4   A discriminant that is of a named access type is not called an access discriminant; that term is used only for discriminants defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>32</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of discriminated types:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>33</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Buffer(Size : Buffer{"_"}Size := 100)  is        -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.4">3.5.4</a>{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Pos   : Buffer{"_"}Size := 0;{"\n"}      Value : String(1 .. Size);{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>34</MarginText>
type Matrix{"_"}Rec(Rows, Columns : Integer) is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Mat : Matrix(1 .. Rows, 1 .. Columns);       -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>35</MarginText>
type Square(Side : Integer) is new{"\n"}   Matrix{"_"}Rec(Rows ={">"} Side, Columns ={">"} Side);{"\n"}
<MarginText>36</MarginText>
type Double{"_"}Square(Number : Integer) is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Left  : Square(Number);{"\n"}      Right : Square(Number);{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>37/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
task type Worker(Prio : System.Priority; Buf : access Buffer){"\n"}   with Priority ={">"} Prio is -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>{"\n"}   -- discriminants used to parameterize the task type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1">9.1</a>){"\n"}   entry Fill;{"\n"}   entry Drain;{"\n"}end Worker;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>37.a</MarginText>
The syntax for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code> is modified to allow an <i>access discriminant</i>, with a type specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10">3.10</a>).<br />

<MarginText>37.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Discriminants are allowed on all composite types other than array and interface types.<br />

<MarginText>37.c</MarginText>
Discriminants may be of an access type. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>37.d</MarginText>
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">Discriminant_part</a></code>s are not elaborated, though an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is elaborated when the discriminant is initialized.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>37.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00402-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
Access discriminants (anonymous access types used as a discriminant) can be used on any type allowing discriminants. Defaults aren't allowed on discriminants of nonlimited types, however, so that accessibility problems don't happen on assignment.<br />

<MarginText>37.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> can be used in the declaration of a discriminant. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>37.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00098-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0007</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> The wording was clarified so that types that cannot have discriminants cannot have an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>37.h/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Added wording to prevent interfaces from having discriminants. We don't want interfaces to have any components.<br />

<MarginText>37.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00254-01"]} />
Removed wording which implied or required an access discriminant to have an access-to-object type (anonymous access types can now be access-to-subprogram types as well).<br />

<MarginText>37.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
Fixed the wording of the introduction to this subclause to reflect that both incomplete and partial views can have unknown discriminants. That was always true, but for some reason this wording specified partial views.<br />

<MarginText>37.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00419-01"]} />
Changed the wording to use the new term &ldquo;explicitly limited record&rdquo;, which makes the intent much clearer (and eliminates confusion with derived types that happen to contain the reserved word <b>limited</b>). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>37.l/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0063-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Changed the rules for when access discriminants can have defaults to depend on the new definition for immutably limited types; this will help ensure that unusual corner cases are properly handled. Note that the Ada 2005 rule was unintentionally incompatible with the Ada 95 rule (as enforced by the ACATS); this change brings it back into alignment with actual practice. So there should be no practical incompatibility. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>37.m/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0214-1"]} />
A limited tagged type may now have defaults for its discriminants. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>37.n/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0102-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Moved implicit conversion Legality Rule to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>37.o/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0398-1"]} />
Discriminants now can have an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, allowing the specification of (implementation-defined) aspects for individual discriminants. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.7.1"></a>

## 3.7.1  Discriminant Constraints

<MarginText>1_3.7.1</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code> specifies the values of the discriminants for a given discriminated type. <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a/3_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
The rules in this subclause are intentionally parallel to those given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.1">4.3.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.1">Record Aggregates</a>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_3.7.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>discriminant{"_"}constraint</code><a id="S0064"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0065">discriminant_association</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0065">discriminant_association</a></code>{"}"})<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>discriminant{"_"}association</code><a id="S0065"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<i>discriminant{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> {"{"}'|' <i>discriminant{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>{"}"} ={">"}] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4_3.7.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0065">discriminant_association</a></code> is said to be <i>named</i> if it has one or more <i>discriminant{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>s; it is otherwise said to be <i>positional</i>. In a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>, any positional associations shall precede any named associations. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5_3.7.1</MarginText>
<p>Each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> of a named <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0065">discriminant{"_"}association</a></code> shall resolve to denote a discriminant of the subtype being constrained; the discriminants so named are the <i>associated discriminants</i> of the named association. For a positional association, the <i>associated discriminant</i> is the one whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant{"_"}specification</a></code> occurred in the corresponding position in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known{"_"}discriminant{"_"}part</a></code> that defined the discriminants of the subtype being constrained.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6_3.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0065">discriminant_association</a></code> is that of the associated discriminant(s). <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7/3_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00168-01", "AI95-00363-01", "AI05-0041-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0008</i>{"}"} A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code> is only allowed in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes either an unconstrained discriminated subtype, or an unconstrained access subtype whose designated subtype is an unconstrained discriminated subtype. However, in the case of an access subtype, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant{"_"}constraint</a></code> is legal only if any dereference of a value of the access type is known to be constrained (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3">3.3</a>). In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules apply also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a.1/2_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00168-01", "AI95-00363-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i>{"{"}<i>8652/0008</i>{"}"} <br />

<MarginText>7.a/2_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The second rule is necessary to prevent objects from changing so that they no longer match their constraint. In Ada 95, we attempted to prevent this by banning every case where an aliased object could be unconstrained or be changed by an enclosing assignment. New ways to cause this problem were being discovered frequently, meaning that new rules had to be dreamed up to cover them. Meanwhile, aliased objects and components were getting more and more limited. In Ada 2005, we sweep away all of that cruft and replace it by a simple rule &ldquo;thou shalt not create an access subtype that can point to an item whose discriminants can be changed by assignment&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>7.b/3_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0041-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The second rule will only use the indefinite or dereference bullets in the definition of &ldquo;known to be constrained&rdquo;. The rule is worded in terms of &ldquo;known to be constrained&rdquo; in order to capture the special rules that apply in generic bodies (rather than repeating them and getting them subtly wrong). <br />

<MarginText>8_3.7.1</MarginText>
<p>A named <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0065">discriminant_association</a></code> with more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> is allowed only if the named discriminants are all of the same type. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code> shall provide exactly one value for each discriminant of the subtype being constrained.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/3_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0102-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/3_3.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In addition, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a> requires that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> associated with an access discriminant is convertible (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>) to the anonymous access type. This implies both convertibility of designated types, and static accessibility. This implies that if an object of type T with an access discriminant is created by an allocator for an access type A, then it requires that the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> associated with the access discriminant have an accessibility level that is not statically deeper than that of A. This is to avoid dangling references.<br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10_3.7.1</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code> is <i>compatible</i> with an unconstrained discriminated subtype if each discriminant value belongs to the subtype of the corresponding discriminant. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a_3.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The "dependent compatibility check" has been eliminated in Ada 95. Any checking on subcomponents is performed when (and if) an object is created.<br />

<MarginText>10.b_3.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There is no need to define compatibility with a constrained discriminated subtype, because one is not allowed to constrain it again.<br />

<MarginText>11_3.7.1</MarginText>
<p>A composite value <i>satisfies</i> a discriminant constraint if and only if each discriminant of the composite value has the value imposed by the discriminant constraint.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>For the elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0065">discriminant_association</a></code>s are evaluated in an arbitrary order and converted to the type of the associated discriminant (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>); the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a named association is evaluated (and converted) once for each associated discriminant. The result of each evaluation and conversion is the value imposed by the constraint for the associated discriminant. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a_3.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We convert to the type, not the subtype, so that the definition of compatibility of discriminant constraints is not vacuous.<br />

<MarginText>13_3.7.1</MarginText>
NOTE   The rules of the language ensure that a discriminant of an object always has a value, either from explicit or implicit initialization. <br />

<MarginText>13.a_3.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Although it is illegal to constrain a class-wide tagged subtype, it is possible to have a partially constrained class-wide subtype: If the subtype S is defined by T(A ={">"} B), then S'Class is partially constrained in the sense that objects of subtype S'Class have to have discriminants corresponding to A equal to B, but there can be other discriminants defined in extensions that are not constrained to any particular value. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>14/5_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p><i>Examples (using types declared above in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7">3.7</a>):</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>15_3.7.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Large   : Buffer(200);  --  constrained, always 200 characters{"\n"}                        --   (explicit discriminant value){"\n"}Message : Buffer;       --  unconstrained, initially 100 characters{"\n"}                        --   (default discriminant value){"\n"}Basis   : Square(5);    --  constrained, always 5 by 5{"\n"}Illegal : Square;       --  illegal, a Square has to be constrained{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 83

<MarginText>15.a_3.7.1</MarginText>
Dependent compatibility checks are no longer performed on subtype declaration. Instead they are deferred until object creation (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>). This is upward compatible for a program that does not raise Constraint{"_"}Error. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>15.b_3.7.1</MarginText>
Everything in RM83-3.7.2(7-12), which specifies the initial values for discriminants, is now redundant with 3.3.1, 6.4.1, 8.5.1, and 12.4. Therefore, we don't repeat it here. Since the material is largely intuitive, but nevertheless complicated to state formally, it doesn't seem worth putting it in a "NOTE". <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>15.c/2_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00168-01", "AI95-00363-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0008</i>{"}"} The Corrigendum added a restriction on <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>s for general access subtypes. Such constraints are prohibited if the designated type can be treated as constrained somewhere in the program. Ada 2005 goes further and prohibits such <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>s if the designated type has (or might have, in the case of a formal type) defaults for its discriminants. The use of general access subtypes is rare, and this eliminates a boatload of problems that required many restrictions on the use of aliased objects and components (now lifted). Similarly, Ada 2005 prohibits <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0064">discriminant_constraint</a></code>s on any access type whose designated type has a partial view that is constrained. Such a type will not be constrained in the heap to avoid privacy problems. Again, the use of such subtypes is rare (they can only happen within the package and its child units). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>15.d/3_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0041-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Revised the rules on access subtypes having discriminant constraints to depend on the &ldquo;known to be constrained&rdquo; rules. This centralizes the rules so that future fixes need to be made in only one place, as well as fixing bugs in obscure cases.<br />

<MarginText>15.e/3_3.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0102-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Moved implicit conversion Legality Rule to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.7.2"></a>

## 3.7.2  Operations of Discriminated Types

<MarginText>1_3.7.2</MarginText>
<p>[If a discriminated type has <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s for its discriminants, then unconstrained variables of the type are permitted, and the discriminants of such a variable can be changed by assignment to the variable. For a formal parameter of such a type, an attribute is provided to determine whether the corresponding actual parameter is constrained or unconstrained.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2_3.7.2</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> A that is of a discriminated type [(after any implicit dereference)], the following attribute is defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_3.7.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Constrained</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0214-1", "AI12-0183-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>Yields the value True if A denotes a constant, a value, a tagged object, or a constrained variable, and False otherwise. The value of this attribute is of the predefined type Boolean. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.a/3_3.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0214-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This attribute is primarily used on parameters, to determine whether the discriminants can be changed as part of an assignment. The Constrained attribute is statically True for <b>in</b> parameters. For <b>in out</b> and <b>out</b> parameters of a discriminated type, the value of this attribute needs to be passed as an implicit parameter, in general. However, if the type is tagged or does not have defaults for its discriminants, the attribute is statically True, so no implicit parameter is needed. Parameters of a limited untagged type with defaulted discriminants need this implicit parameter, unless there are no nonlimited views, because they might be passed to a subprogram whose body has visibility on a nonlimited view of the type, and hence might be able to assign to the object and change its discriminants. <br />

<MarginText>3.b/4_3.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0214-1", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>All tagged objects are known to be constrained (as nonlimited tagged types cannot have discriminant defaults, and limited tagged objects are immutably limited), and are always considered constrained by this attribute to avoid distributed overhead for parameters of limited class-wide types, as limited tagged objects may technically be unconstrained if they use defaulted discriminants. Such objects still cannot have their discriminants changed, as assignment is not supported for them, so there is no use for this attribute that would justify the overhead of passing it with all class-wide parameters. <br />

<MarginText>3.c/3_3.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1", "AI05-0214-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>If the type of A is a type derived from an untagged partial view of a tagged type such that it is not a tagged type, then A is not considered a tagged object, and A'Constrained can return either True or False depending on the nature of the object. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>4_3.7.2</MarginText>
<p>The execution of a construct is erroneous if the construct has a constituent that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denoting a subcomponent that depends on discriminants, and the value of any of these discriminants is changed by this execution between evaluating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> and the last use (within this execution) of the subcomponent denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a_3.7.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule applies to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>s, calls (except when the discriminant-dependent subcomponent is an <b>in</b> parameter passed by copy), <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0097">slice</a></code>s. Ada 83 only covered the first two cases. AI83-00585 pointed out the situation with the last two cases. The cases of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object_renaming_declaration</a></code>s and generic formal <b>in out</b> objects are handled differently, by disallowing the situation at compile time. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>4.b/1_3.7.2</MarginText>
For consistency with other attributes, we are allowing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of Constrained to be a value as well as an object of a discriminated type, and also an implicit dereference. These extensions are not important capabilities, but there seems no reason to make this attribute different from other similar attributes. We are curious what most Ada 83 compilers do with F(1).X'Constrained.<br />

<MarginText>4.c_3.7.2</MarginText>
We now handle in a general way the cases of erroneousness identified by AI83-00585, where the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0097">slice</a></code> is discriminant-dependent, and the evaluation of the index or discrete range changes the value of a discriminant. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>4.d_3.7.2</MarginText>
We have moved all discussion of erroneous use of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s that denote discriminant-dependent subcomponents to this subclause. In Ada 83, it used to appear separately under <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>s and subprogram calls. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>4.e/3_3.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0214-1"]} />
A'Constrained is now defined to return True for any A that is a tagged object. This doesn't change the result for any A allowed by previous versions of Ada; the change is necessary to avoid unnecessary overhead for limited tagged parameters. <br />

---

# 3.8. Record Types

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8.mdx

sidebar_position:  26

# 3.8. Record Types

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>A record object is a composite object consisting of named components. The value of a record object is a composite value consisting of the values of the components. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>record{"_"}type{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0066"></a><code> ::= </code>[[<b>abstract</b>] <b>tagged</b>] [<b>limited</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0067">record_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0213-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>record{"_"}definition</code><a id="S0067"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>record</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code><br />    <b>end</b> <b>record</b> [<i>record{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>]<br />  | <b>null record</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>component{"_"}list</code><a id="S0068"></a><code> ::= </code><br />      <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0069">component_item</a></code> {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0069">component_item</a></code>{"}"}<br />   | {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0069">component_item</a></code>{"}"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code><br />   |  <b>null</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} <code>component{"_"}item</code><a id="S0069"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>component{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0070"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> : <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> [:= <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>]<br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0213-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">If a <i>record{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> appears at the end of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0067">record_definition</a></code>, it shall repeat the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> of the enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>, if any, in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> is the type of the component. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>8/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>9/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
<p>Each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> declares a component of the record type. Besides components declared by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>s, the components of a record type include any components declared by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code>s of the record type declaration. [The identifiers of all components of a record type shall be distinct.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The identifiers of all components of a record type have to be distinct because they are all declared immediately within the same declarative region. See Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/">8</a>. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>Within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a component, protected subprogram, or entry of the type is allowed only in the following cases:<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0004-1", "AI05-0295-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes any component, protected subprogram, or entry is allowed within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, an operational item, or a representation item that occurs within the declaration of the composite type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a noninherited discriminant is allowed within the declaration of the type, but not within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code>. If the discriminant is used to define the constraint of a component, the bounds of an entry family, or the constraint of the parent subtype in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>, then its name shall appear alone as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> (not as part of a larger expression or expanded name). A discriminant shall not be used to define the constraint of a scalar component. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The penultimate restriction simplifies implementation, and allows the outer discriminant and the inner discriminant or bound to possibly share storage. <br />

<MarginText>12.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Other rules prevent such a discriminant from being an inherited one. <br />

<MarginText>12.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The last restriction is inherited from Ada 83. The restriction is not really necessary from a language design point of view, but we did not remove it, in order to avoid unnecessary changes to existing compilers. <br />

<MarginText>12.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that a discriminant can be used to define the constraint for a component that is of an access-to-composite type. <br />

<MarginText>12.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00373-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The above rules, and a similar one in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a> for formal parameters, are intended to allow initializations of components or parameters to occur in a (nearly) arbitrary order &mdash; whatever order is most efficient (subject to the restrictions of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>), since one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> cannot depend on the value of another one. They also prevent circularities. <br />

<MarginText>12.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0295-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Inherited discriminants are not allowed to be denoted, except within <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s and representation items. However, the <i>discriminant{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> of the parent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> is allowed to denote a discriminant of the parent. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>If the name of the current instance of a type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>) is used to define the constraint of a component, then it shall appear as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> that is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> whose result is of an access type, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> shall appear alone. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule allows T'Access or T'Unchecked{"_"}Access, but disallows, for example, a range constraint (1..T'Size). Allowing things like (1..T'Size) would mean that a per-object constraint could affect the size of the object, which would be bad. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>13.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0004-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0066">record_type_definition</a></code> includes the reserved word <b>limited</b>, the type is called an <i>explicitly limited record</i> type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> defines the (nominal) subtype of the component. If the reserved word <b>aliased</b> appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code>, then the component is aliased (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10">3.10</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> of a record type is defined by the reserved word <b>null</b> and there are no discriminants, then the record type has no components and all records of the type are <i>null records</i>. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0067">record_definition</a></code> of <b>null record</b> is equivalent to <b>record null; end record</b>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0426-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This shorthand is available both for declaring a record type and a record extension &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a>. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0066">record_type_definition</a></code> creates the record type and its first subtype, and consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0067">record_definition</a></code>. The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0067">record_definition</a></code> consists of the elaboration of its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code>, if any.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0069">component_item</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>, if any, in the order in which they appear. The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0033">defining_identifier_list</a></code> has more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>, we presume here that the transformation explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a> has already taken place. Alternatively, we could say that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> is elaborated once for each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> in the list. <br />

<MarginText>18/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01", "AI95-00230-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} Within the definition of a composite type, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.2">9.5.2</a>) includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a discriminant of the type, or that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> denotes the current instance of the type, the expression containing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is called a <i>per-object expression</i>, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> being defined is called a <i>per-object constraint</i>. For the elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> for an entry family (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.2">9.5.2</a>), if the component subtype is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> or if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> is not a per-object constraint, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> is elaborated. On the other hand, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> is a per-object constraint, then the elaboration consists of the evaluation of any included expression that is not part of a per-object expression. Each such expression is evaluated once unless it is part of a named association in a discriminant constraint, in which case it is evaluated once for each associated discriminant.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} When a per-object constraint is elaborated [(as part of creating an object)], each per-object expression of the constraint is evaluated. For other expressions, the values determined during the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component{"_"}definition</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> are used. Any checks associated with the enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> are performed[, including the subtype compatibility check (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.2">3.2.2</a>),] and the associated subtype is created. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The evaluation of other expressions that appear in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>s is performed when the type definition is elaborated. The evaluation of expressions that appear as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s is postponed until an object is created. Expressions in representation items that appear within a composite type definition are evaluated according to the rules of the particular representation item. <br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
NOTE 1   A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> with several identifiers is equivalent to a sequence of single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>s, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>.<br />

<MarginText>20</MarginText>
NOTE 2   The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> of a record component is only evaluated upon the creation of a default-initialized object of the record type (presuming the object has the component, if it is in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>21</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The subtype defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>) has to be a definite subtype.<br />

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
NOTE 4   If a record type does not have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>, then the same components are present in all values of the type.<br />

<MarginText>23</MarginText>
NOTE 5   A record type is limited if it has the reserved word <b>limited</b> in its definition, or if any of its components are limited (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>).<br />

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
NOTE 6   The predefined operations of a record type include membership tests, qualification, and explicit conversion. If the record type is nonlimited, they also include assignment and the predefined equality operators.<br />

<MarginText>25/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
NOTE 7   A component of a record can be named with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>. A value of a record can be specified with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code>.<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>26</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of record type declarations:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>27/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0430-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Date is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Day   : Integer range 1 .. 31;{"\n"}      Month : Month{"_"}Name;                  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.1">3.5.1</a>{"\n"}      Year  : Integer range 0 .. 4000;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>28/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0213-1"]} />
type Complex is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Re : Real := 0.0;{"\n"}      Im : Real := 0.0;{"\n"}   end record Complex;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>29</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of record variables:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>30</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Tomorrow, Yesterday : Date;{"\n"}A, B, C : Complex;{"\n"}
<MarginText>31</MarginText>
-- both components of A, B, and C are implicitly initialized to zero {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>31.a</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> is modified to use <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0056">component_definition</a></code> (instead of <code>component{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</code>). The effect of this change is to allow the reserved word <b>aliased</b> before the <code>component{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</code>.<br />

<MarginText>31.b</MarginText>
A short-hand is provided for defining a null record type (and a null record extension), as these will be more common for abstract root types (and derived types without additional components).<br />

<MarginText>31.c</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0066">record_type_definition</a></code> is modified to allow the reserved words <b>tagged</b> and <b>limited</b>. Tagging is new. Limitedness is now orthogonal to privateness. In Ada 83 the syntax implied that limited private was sort of more private than private. However, limitedness really has nothing to do with privateness; limitedness simply indicates the lack of assignment capabilities, and makes perfect sense for nonprivate types such as record types. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>31.d/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} The syntax rules now allow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code>s to appear in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0067">record_definition</a></code>. This is not a language extension, because Legality Rules prevent all language-defined representation clauses from appearing there. However, an implementation-defined <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> could appear there. The reason for this change is to allow the rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0343">aspect_clause</a></code>s and representation pragmas to be as similar as possible. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>31.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
Record components can have an anonymous access type.<br />

<MarginText>31.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
Limited components can be initialized, so long as the expression is one that allows building the object in place (such as an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>31.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Improved the description of the elaboration of per-object constraints.<br />

<MarginText>31.h/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00137-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0009</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Changed representation clauses to aspect clauses to reflect that they are used for more than just representation.<br />

<MarginText>31.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
Defined <i>explicitly limited record</i> type to use in other rules. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>31.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>31.k/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0213-1"]} />
The <i>record{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> following <b>end record</b> is new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_3.8.1"></a>

## 3.8.1  Variant Parts and Discrete Choices

<MarginText>1_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>A record type with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> specifies alternative lists of components. Each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> defines the components for the value or values of the discriminant covered by its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a_3.8.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">Discrete_choice_list</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s are said to <i>cover</i> values as defined below; which <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> covers a value determines which of various alternatives is chosen. These are used in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>s. <br />

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.b_3.8.1</MarginText>
The definition of &ldquo;cover&rdquo; in this subclause and the rules about discrete choices are designed so that they are also appropriate for array aggregates and case statements.<br />

<MarginText>1.c_3.8.1</MarginText>
The rules of this subclause intentionally parallel those for case statements. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_3.8.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>variant{"_"}part</code><a id="S0071"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>case</b> <i>discriminant{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> <b>is</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code><br />      {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>{"}"}<br />   <b>end</b> <b>case</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_3.8.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>variant</code><a id="S0072"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>when</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> ={">"}<br />      <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/5_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>discrete{"_"}choice{"_"}list</code><a id="S0073"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> {"{"}'|' <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>{"}"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0158-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>discrete{"_"}choice</code><a id="S0074"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0133">choice_expression</a></code> | <i>discrete{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> | <b>others</b><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>6_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>The <i>discriminant{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> shall resolve to denote a discriminant (called the <i>discriminant of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code></i>) specified in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>. The expected type for each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> is the type of the discriminant of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a_3.8.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> has to have a (new) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code>; the discriminant of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> cannot be an inherited discriminant. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>The discriminant of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> shall be of a discrete type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a_3.8.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>It shall not be of an access type, named or anonymous.<br />

<MarginText>8/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0133">choice_expression</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>s given as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> shall be static. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> <b>others</b> shall appear alone in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>, and such a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>, if it appears, shall be the last one in the enclosing construct.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> is defined to <i>cover a value</i> in the following cases: <br /></p>

<MarginText>10/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0133">choice_expression</a></code> covers a value if the value equals the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0133">choice_expression</a></code> converted to the expected type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.1/4_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0071-1"]} />
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> covers all values (possibly none) that belong to the subtype and that satisfy the static predicates of the subtype (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>).<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A dynamic predicate is never allowed in this case (for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>s, a subtype with a dynamic predicate isn't static and thus isn't allowed in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>, and for a choice in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code>, a dynamic predicate is explicitly disallowed &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>). <br />

<MarginText>11/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
<ul>
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> covers all values (possibly none) that belong to the range.<br /></li>
<MarginText>12_3.8.1</MarginText>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> <b>others</b> covers all values of its expected type that are not covered by previous <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>s of the same construct. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a_3.8.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>s, this includes values outside the range of the static subtype (if any) to be covered by the choices. It even includes values outside the base range of the case expression's type, since values of numeric types (and undefined values of any scalar type?) can be outside their base range. <br />

<MarginText>13_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> covers a value if one of its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s covers the value.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>The possible values of the discriminant of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> shall be covered as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>15/4_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0188-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0071-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the discriminant is of a static constrained scalar subtype then, except within an instance of a generic unit, each non-<b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete{"_"}choice</a></code> shall cover only values in that subtype that satisfy its predicates, and each value of that subtype that satisfies its predicates shall be covered by some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete{"_"}choice</a></code> [(either explicitly or by <b>others</b>)];<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.a/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The exemption for a discriminated type declared in an instance allows the following example: <br />

<MarginText>15.b/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type T is new Integer;{"\n"}package G is{"\n"}   type Rec (Discrim : T) is record{"\n"}      case Discrim is{"\n"}         when -10 .. -1 ={">"}{"\n"}            Foo : Float;{"\n"}         when others ={">"}{"\n"}            null;{"\n"}      end case;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}end G;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15.c/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
package I is new G (Natural); -- Legal{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the type of the discriminant is a descendant of a generic formal scalar type, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> shall have an <b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16.a_3.8.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The base range is not known statically in this case. <br />

<MarginText>17_3.8.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Otherwise, each value of the base range of the type of the discriminant shall be covered [(either explicitly or by <b>others</b>)]. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>Two distinct <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> shall not cover the same value.<br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>19_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> is specified by <b>null</b>, the variant has no components.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>The discriminant of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> is said to <i>govern</i> the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> and its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>s. In addition, the discriminant of a derived type governs a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> and its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>s if it corresponds (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7">3.7</a>) to the discriminant of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>21_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>A record value contains the values of the components of a particular <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> only if the value of the discriminant governing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> is covered by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>. This rule applies in turn to any further <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> that is, itself, included in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> of the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.1/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0290-1"]} />
<p>When an object of a discriminated type <i>T</i> is initialized by default, Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> of <i>T</i> covers the value of the discriminant that governs the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>. When a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> of another <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> <i>V</i>, this test is only applied if the value of the discriminant governing <i>V</i> is covered by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> of <i>V</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This is not a &ldquo;check&rdquo;; it cannot be suppressed. However, in most cases it is not necessary to generate any code to raise this exception. A test is needed (and can fail) in the case where the discriminant subtype has a Static{"_"}Predicate specified, it also has predicate checking disabled, and the discriminant governs a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> which lacks a <b>when others</b> choice.<br />

<MarginText>21.b/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
The test also could fail for a static discriminant subtype with range checking suppressed and the discriminant governs a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> which lacks a <b>when others</b> choice. But execution is erroneous if a range check that would have failed is suppressed (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.5">11.5</a>), so an implementation does not have to generate code to check this case. (An unchecked failed predicate does not cause erroneous execution, so the test is required in that case.)<br />

<MarginText>21.c/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
Like the checks associated with a per-object constraint, this test is not made during the elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>22_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> of each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> in the order in which they appear. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>23_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of record type with a variant part: </i><br /></p>

<MarginText>24_3.8.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Device is (Printer, Disk, Drum);{"\n"}type State  is (Open, Closed);{"\n"}
<MarginText>25_3.8.1</MarginText>
type Peripheral(Unit : Device := Disk) is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Status : State;{"\n"}      case Unit is{"\n"}         when Printer ={">"}{"\n"}            Line{"_"}Count : Integer range 1 .. Page{"_"}Size;{"\n"}         when others ={">"}{"\n"}            Cylinder   : Cylinder{"_"}Index;{"\n"}            Track      : Track{"_"}Number;{"\n"}      end case;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>26_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of record subtypes:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>27_3.8.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
subtype Drum{"_"}Unit is Peripheral(Drum);{"\n"}subtype Disk{"_"}Unit is Peripheral(Disk);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>28_3.8.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of constrained record variables:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>29_3.8.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Writer   : Peripheral(Unit  ={">"} Printer);{"\n"}Archive  : Disk{"_"}Unit;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>29.a_3.8.1</MarginText>
In Ada 83, the discriminant of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> is not allowed to be of a generic formal type. This restriction is removed in Ada 95; an <b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> is required in this case. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>29.b_3.8.1</MarginText>
The syntactic category <code>choice</code> is removed. The syntax rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code>, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> now use <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> instead. The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> now defines its own syntax for named associations.<br />

<MarginText>29.c/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
We have added the term Discrete Choice to the title since this is where they are talked about. This is analogous to the name of the subclause "Index Constraints and Discrete Ranges" in the subclause on Array Types.<br />

<MarginText>29.d_3.8.1</MarginText>
The rule requiring that the discriminant denote a discriminant of the type being defined seems to have been left implicit in RM83. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>29.e/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1"]} />
Membership tests are no longer allowed as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>, in order that those tests can be expanded to allow multiple tests in a single expression without ambiguity. Since a membership test has a boolean type, they are very unlikely to be used as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>29.f/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
Subtypes with static predicates can be used in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s, and the coverage rules are modified to respect the predicates.<br />

<MarginText>29.g/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
Variants in generic specifications are no longer rejected if the subtype of the actual type does not include all of the case choices. This probably isn't useful, but it is consistent with the treatment of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>s. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>29.h/3_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0290-1"]} />
Added a test that some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> covers the value of a discriminant that governs a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>. This is similar to the test that some case limb covers the value of the <i>Selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>. This test cannot change the behavior of any nonerroneous Ada 2005 program, so it is not an inconsistency. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>29.i/4_3.8.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0071-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Updated wording of the coverage rules to use the new term "satisfies the predicates" (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>). <br />

# 3.9. Tagged Types and Type Extensions

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9.mdx

sidebar_position:  27

# 3.9. Tagged Types and Type Extensions

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ Tagged types and type extensions support object-oriented programming, based on inheritance with extension and run-time polymorphism via <i>dispatching operations</i>. ]<br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
The intended implementation model is for the static portion of a tag to be represented as a pointer to a statically allocated and link-time initialized type descriptor. The type descriptor contains the address of the code for each primitive operation of the type. It probably also contains other information, such as might make membership tests convenient and efficient. Tags for nested type extensions must also have a dynamic part that identifies the particular elaboration of the type.<br />

<MarginText>1.b</MarginText>
The primitive operations of a tagged type are known at its first freezing point; the type descriptor is laid out at that point. It contains linker symbols for each primitive operation; the linker fills in the actual addresses.<br />

<MarginText>1.b.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Primitive operations of type extensions that are declared at a level deeper than the level of the ultimate ancestor from which they are derived can be represented by wrappers that use the dynamic part of the tag to call the actual primitive operation. The dynamic part would generally be some way to represent the static link or display necessary for making a nested call. One implementation strategy would be to store that information in the extension part of such nested type extensions, and use the dynamic part of the tag to point at it. (That way, the &ldquo;dynamic&rdquo; part of the tag could be static, at the cost of indirect access.)<br />

<MarginText>1.b.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
If the tagged type is descended from any interface types, it also will need to include &ldquo;subtags&rdquo; (one for each interface) that describe the mapping of the primitive operations of the interface to the primitives of the type. These subtags could directly reference the primitive operations (for faster performance), or simply provide the tag &ldquo;slot&rdquo; numbers for the primitive operations (for easier derivation). In either case, the subtags would be used for calls that dispatch through a class-wide type of the interface.<br />

<MarginText>1.c</MarginText>
Other implementation models are possible.<br />

<MarginText>1.d</MarginText>
The rules ensure that &ldquo;dangling dispatching&rdquo; is impossible; that is, when a dispatching call is made, there is always a body to execute. This is different from some other object-oriented languages, such as Smalltalk, where it is possible to get a run-time error from a missing method.<br />

<MarginText>1.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Dispatching calls should be efficient, and should have a bounded worst-case execution time. This is important in a language intended for real-time applications. In the intended implementation model, a dispatching call involves calling indirect through the appropriate slot in the dispatch table. No complicated "method lookup" is involved although a call which is dispatching on an interface may require a lookup of the appropriate interface subtag.<br />

<MarginText>1.f</MarginText>
The programmer should have the choice at each call site of a dispatching operation whether to do a dispatching call or a statically determined call (i.e. whether the body executed should be determined at run time or at compile time).<br />

<MarginText>1.g</MarginText>
The same body should be executed for a call where the tag is statically determined to be T'Tag as for a dispatching call where the tag is found at run time to be T'Tag. This allows one to test a given tagged type with statically determined calls, with some confidence that run-time dispatching will produce the same behavior.<br />

<MarginText>1.h</MarginText>
All views of a type should share the same type descriptor and the same tag.<br />

<MarginText>1.i</MarginText>
The visibility rules determine what is legal at compile time; they have nothing to do with what bodies can be executed at run time. Thus, it is possible to dispatch to a subprogram whose declaration is not visible at the call site. In fact, this is one of the primary facts that gives object-oriented programming its power. The subprogram that ends up being dispatched to by a given call might even be designed long after the call site has been coded and compiled.<br />

<MarginText>1.j</MarginText>
Given that Ada has overloading, determining whether a given subprogram overrides another is based both on the names and the type profiles of the operations.<br />

<MarginText>1.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00401-01"]} />
When a type extension is declared, if there is any place within its immediate scope where a certain subprogram of the parent or progenitor is visible, then a matching subprogram should override. If there is no such place, then a matching subprogram should be totally unrelated, and occupy a different slot in the type descriptor. This is important to preserve the privacy of private parts; when an operation declared in a private part is inherited, the inherited version can be overridden only in that private part, in the package body, and in any children of the package.<br />

<MarginText>1.l</MarginText>
If an implementation shares code for instances of generic bodies, it should be allowed to share type descriptors of tagged types declared in the generic body, so long as they are not extensions of types declared in the specification of the generic unit. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<p>A record type or private type that has the reserved word <b>tagged</b> in its declaration is called a <i>tagged</i> type. In addition, an interface type is a tagged type, as is a task or protected type derived from an interface (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.4">3.9.4</a>). [When deriving from a tagged type, as for any derived type, additional primitive subprograms may be defined, and inherited primitive subprograms may be overridden.] The derived type is called an <i>extension</i> of its ancestor types, or simply a <i>type extension</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<p>Every type extension is also a tagged type, and is a <i>record extension</i> or a <i>private extension</i> of some other tagged type, or a noninterface synchronized tagged type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.4">3.9.4</a>). A record extension is defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a>)[, which may include the definition of additional components]. A private extension, which is a partial view of a record extension or of a synchronized tagged type, can be declared in the visible part of a package (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3">7.3</a>) or in a generic formal part (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>tagged type</b> &mdash; type whose objects each have a run-time type tag, which indicates the specific type for which the object was originally created<br />Note: Tagged types can be extended with additional components.<br />

<MarginText>2.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If a tagged type is declared other than in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, it is impossible to add new primitive subprograms for that type, although it can inherit primitive subprograms, and those can be overridden. If the user incorrectly thinks a certain subprogram is primitive when it is not, and tries to call it with a dispatching call, an error message will be given at the call site. Similarly, by using an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>), the user can declare that a subprogram is intended to be overriding, and get an error message when they made a mistake. The use of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>s is highly recommended in new code that does not need to be compatible with Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>An object of a tagged type has an associated (run-time) <i>tag</i> that identifies the specific tagged type used to create the object originally. [ The tag of an operand of a class-wide tagged type <i>T</i>'Class controls which subprogram body is to be executed when a primitive subprogram of type <i>T</i> is applied to the operand (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>); using a tag to control which body to execute is called <i>dispatching</i>.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00344-01"]} />
<p>The tag of a specific tagged type identifies the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> of the type, and for a type extension, is sufficient to uniquely identify the type among all descendants of the same ancestor. If a declaration for a tagged type occurs within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0312">generic_package_declaration</a></code>, then the corresponding type declarations in distinct instances of the generic package are associated with distinct tags. For a tagged type that is local to a generic package body and with all of its ancestors (if any) also local to the generic body, the language does not specify whether repeated instantiations of the generic body result in distinct tags. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00344-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>4.a.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00344-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>In most cases, a tag need only identify a particular tagged type declaration, and can therefore be a simple link-time-known address. However, for tag checks (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>) it is essential that each descendant (that currently exists) of a given type have a unique tag. Hence, for types declared in shared generic bodies where an ancestor comes from outside the generic, or for types declared at a deeper level than an ancestor, the tag needs to be augmented with some kind of dynamic descriptor (which may be a static link, global display, instance descriptor pointer, or combination). This implies that type Tag may need to be two words, the second of which is normally null, but in these identified special cases needs to include a static link or equivalent.
