[ 1 ={">"} [ 1 ={">"} [ 123 ={">"} True,  124 ={">"} False]{"\n"}         2 ={">"} [ 123 ={">"} False,  124 ={">"} False]],{"\n"}  2 ={">"} [ 1 ={">"} [ 123 ={">"} True,  124 ={">"} True],{"\n"}         2 ={">"} [ 123 ={">"} True,  124 ={">"} False]]]{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>19.c/5</MarginText>
although perhaps with different white space and/or line breaking. <br />

<MarginText>20/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The case of a null array is handled specially, using ranges for index bounds and "{"<"}{">"}" as a syntactic component-value placeholder.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This might generate an image such as "[ 1 ..  3 ={">"} [ 1 ..  0 ={">"} [ 1 .. 5 ={">"} {"<"}{">"}]]]", where the use of "{"<"}{">"}" (among other things) indicates that the overall array is a null array and has no actual elements. <br />

<MarginText>21/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For a record type (or, as indicated above, a type extension with no noninterface ancestor specifying Put{"_"}Image), or a protected type, the default implementation of T'Put{"_"}Image generates an image based on named (not positional) record aggregate syntax (except that for a protected type, the initial left parenthesis is followed by "PROTECTED with "). Component names are displayed in upper case, following the rules for the image of an enumeration value. Component values are displayed via calls to the component type's Put{"_"}Image procedure.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This might generate an image such as: <br />

<MarginText>21.b/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
"(FOO ={">"} [1 ={">"} 'c',  2 ={">"} 'a',  3 ={">"} 't'], BAR ={">"} TRUE)"{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The image written out for a record having no components (including any interface type) is "(NULL RECORD)". The image written out for a componentless protected type is "(PROTECTED NULL RECORD)". In the case of a protected type T, a call to the default implementation of T'Put{"_"}Image begins only one protected (read-only) action.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>22.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The expected, but not required, implementation model for generating the image of a protected record involves the compiler producing a "helper" protected function which T'Put{"_"}Image would call. The result type of this function might be a null record; it is only a function because it does not need a write-lock, not because it returns a meaningful result.<br />

<MarginText>22.b/5</MarginText>
The assertion in the following example should succeed: <br />

<MarginText>22.c/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type T1 (D1, D2 : Positive) is record ... end record; -- untagged{"\n"}type T2 (D : Positive) is new T1 (D1 ={">"} D, D2 ={">"} D);{"\n"}X : T2 (D ={">"} 123) := ... ;{"\n"}pragma Assert (X'Image /= T1(X)'Image);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>23/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For an undiscriminated task type, the default implementation of T'Put{"_"}Image generates an image of the form "(TASK {"<"}task{"_"}id{"_"}image{">"})" where {"<"}task{"_"}id{"_"}image{">"} is the result obtained by calling Task{"_"}Identification.Image with the id of the given task and then passing that String to Characters.Conversions.To{"_"}Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String.<br /></li>
<MarginText>24/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1"]} />
<li>For a discriminated task type, the default implementation of T'Put{"_"}Image also includes discriminant values, as in: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>25/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
"(TASK {"<"}task{"_"}id{"_"}image{">"} with D1 ={">"}  123, D2 ={">"}  456)"{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>26/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0384-2"]} />
<p>For a class-wide type, the default implementation of T'Put{"_"}Image generates an image based on qualified expression syntax. Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Put is called with Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Expanded{"_"}Name of <i>Arg</i>'Tag. Then S'Put{"_"}Image is called, where S is the specific type identified by <i>Arg</i>'Tag.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This will typically require a dispatching call. <br />

<MarginText>26.b/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This might generate an image such as: <br />

<MarginText>26.c/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
SOME{"_"}PACKAGE.SOME{"_"}TAGGED{"_"}TYPE'{"\n"}   (COMPONENT{"_"}1 ={">"}  123, COMPONENT{"_"}2 ={">"} 456){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>26.d/5</MarginText>
The parentheses in this case are generated by the call to Some{"_"}Tagged{"_"}Type'Put{"_"}Image. <br />

<MarginText>27/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0384-2"]} />
<p>[T'Put{"_"}Image is the same for both the partial view and full view of T, if T has a partial view.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>27.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0384-2"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>A type-related operational aspect is the same for the full view and partial view of a type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>28/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0435-1"]} />
<p>In the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0205">parameter_and_result_profile</a></code> for the default implementation of Put{"_"}Image, the subtype of the <i>Arg</i> parameter is the base subtype of <i>T</i> if <i>T</i> is a scalar type, and the first subtype otherwise. For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> specifying Put{"_"}Image, the subprogram name shall denote a nonabstract procedure whose second parameter is either of the first subtype of <i>T</i>, or as an option when <i>T</i> is scalar, the base subtype of <i>T</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>28.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Put{"_"}Image is never an abstract routine, even for an abstract type. Thus, Put{"_"}Image and Image can be called for any type. <br />

<MarginText>29/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1"]} />
<p>For every subtype S of a type T, the following attributes are defined:<br /></p>

<MarginText>30/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0340-1", "AI12-0384-2"]} />
<dl>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>30.1/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image(Arg : S'Base){"\n"}  return Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>30.2/5</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image calls S'Put{"_"}Image passing <i>Arg</i> (which will typically store a sequence of character values in a text buffer) and then returns the result of retrieving the contents of that buffer with function Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Get. The lower bound of the result is one. [Any exception propagated by the call of S'Put{"_"}Image is propagated.]<br /></dd>
<MarginText>31/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Wide{"_"}Image</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0340-1", "AI12-0384-2"]} />
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Image denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>32/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Wide{"_"}Image(Arg : S'Base){"\n"}  return Wide{"_"}String{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>33/5</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Image calls S'Put{"_"}Image passing <i>Arg</i> (which will typically store a sequence of character values in a text buffer) and then returns the result of retrieving the contents of that buffer with function Wide{"_"}Get. The lower bound of the result is one. [Any exception propagated by the call of S'Put{"_"}Image is propagated.]<br /></dd>
<MarginText>34/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Image</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0340-1", "AI12-0384-2"]} />
<dd>S'Image denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>35/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Image(Arg : S'Base){"\n"}  return String{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>36/5</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>S'Image calls S'Put{"_"}Image passing <i>Arg</i> (which will typically store a sequence of character values in a text buffer) and then returns the result of retrieving the contents of that buffer with function Get. The lower bound of the result is one. [Any exception propagated by the call of S'Put{"_"}Image is propagated.]<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>37/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0124-1", "AI12-0315-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X of a type T other than <i>universal{"_"}real</i> or <i>universal{"_"}fixed</i>, the following attributes are defined:<br /></p>

<MarginText>38/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0124-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>X'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image denotes the result of calling function S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image with <i>Arg</i> being X, where S is the nominal subtype of X.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>39/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Wide{"_"}Image</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0124-1"]} />
<dd>X'Wide{"_"}Image denotes the result of calling function S'Wide{"_"}Image with <i>Arg</i> being X, where S is the nominal subtype of X.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>40/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Image</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0124-1"]} />
<dd>X'Image denotes the result of calling function S'Image with <i>Arg</i> being X, where S is the nominal subtype of X. <br /></dd>
</dl>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>41/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may transform the image generated by the default implementation of S'Put{"_"}Image for a composite subtype S in the following ways:<br /></p>

<MarginText>42/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If S is a composite subtype, the leading character of the image <i>M</i> of a component value or index value is a space, and the immediately preceding character (if any) is an open parenthesis, open bracket, or space, then the leading space of the image <i>M</i> may be omitted. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>42.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This means that it is permitted to generate "[1 ={">"} 123, 2 ={">"} 456]" instead of "[ 1 ={">"}  123,  2 ={">"}  456]". <br />

<MarginText>43/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If S is an array subtype, the low bound of the array in each dimension equals the low bound of the corresponding index subtype, and the array value is not a null array value, then positional array aggregate syntax may be used.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>43.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This means that it is permitted to generate "[TRUE, TRUE, FALSE]" instead of "[ 1 ={">"} TRUE,  2 ={">"} TRUE,  3 ={">"} FALSE]" if the low bound of the index subtype is one. <br />

<MarginText>44/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If S is an array subtype and the given value can be displayed using <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0116">named_array_aggregate</a></code> syntax where some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> identifies more than one index value by identifying a sequence of one or more ranges and values separated by vertical bars, then this image may be generated instead; this may involve the reordering of component values.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>44.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This means that it is permitted to generate "[ 1 ..  2 |  5 ={">"} TRUE,  3 ..  4 ={">"} FALSE]" instead of "[ 1 ={">"} TRUE,  2 ={">"} TRUE,  3 ={">"} FALSE,  4 ={">"} FALSE,  5 ={">"} TRUE]". <br />

<MarginText>45/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Similarly, if S is a record subtype (or a discriminated type) and the given value can be displayed using named component association syntax where the length of some component{"_"}choice{"_"}list is greater than one, then this image may be generated instead; this may involve the reordering of component values.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>45.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This means that it is permitted to generate "(F1 | F2 ={">"} TRUE)" instead of "(F1 ={">"} TRUE, F2 ={">"} TRUE)". <br />

<MarginText>46/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0340-1", "AI12-0384-2"]} />
<ul>
<li>Additional spaces (Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Characters with position 32), and calls to the New{"_"}Line operation of a text buffer, may be inserted to improve readability of the generated image, with the spaces inserted directly or via use of the Increase{"_"}Indent and Decrease{"_"}Indent procedures.<br /></li>
<MarginText>47/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0384-2"]} />
<li>For a string type, implementations may produce an image corresponding to a string literal.<br /></li>
<MarginText>48/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0384-2"]} />
<li>For an unchecked union type, implementations may raise Program{"_"}Error or produce some recognizable image (such as "(UNCHECKED UNION)") that does not require reading the discriminants. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>49/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0304-1"]} />
<p>For each language-defined nonscalar type T, T'Put{"_"}Image may be specified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>49.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This permission applies, in particular, to nonscalar types declared in language-defined generic packages, and to any language-defined private type, even if an implementation chooses to complete it as a scalar type. <br />

<MarginText>49.b/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For any language-defined scalar type T, T'Put{"_"}Image should not be specified; the Image attribute needs to return the language-defined image for such types. This is important for compatibility: the Image attribute has been available for scalar types for many Ada revisions, and programs can (and do!) depend on its behavior. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>50/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0304-1"]} />
<p>For each language-defined container type T (that is, each of the Vector, List, Map, Set, Tree, and Holder types defined in the various children of Ada.Containers), T'Put{"_"}Image shall be specified so that T'Image produces a result consistent with array aggregate syntax (using '[' and ']' as delimiters) as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>51/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Vector images shall be consistent with the default image of an array type with the same index and component types.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>51.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In particular, this means that the format is 	that of a named array aggregate. We have no recommendation on how to 	handle empty elements; if the implementation can identify them, it may 	wish to display them specially, but otherwise, they're just 	uninitialized elements. <br />

<MarginText>52/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Map images shall be consistent with named array aggregate syntax, using key value images in place of discrete choice names. For example, [Key1 ={">"} Value1, Key2 ={">"} Value2].<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>52.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There is no recommendation about the order in which key/element pairs occur within a map image. In the case of multiple key values whose corresponding element values have the same image, there is no recommendation about factoring (that is, generating Key1 | Key2 ={">"} Some{"_"}Value instead of Key1 ={">"} Some{"_"}Value, Key2 ={">"} Some{"_"}Value). <br />

<MarginText>53/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Set, List, and Holder images shall be consistent with positional array aggregate syntax. List elements shall occur in order within an image of a list. The image of an empty holder shall be [].<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>53.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There is no recommendation about the order in which set elements occur within the image of a set. <br />

<MarginText>54/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Tree images (and images of subtrees of trees) shall be consistent with positional array aggregate syntax. For example, [[1, 2], [111, 222, 333]].<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>55/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0304-1"]} />
<p>For each language-defined nonscalar type T that has a primitive language-defined Image function whose profile is type conformant with that of T'Image (for example, Ada.Numerics.Float{"_"}Random.State has such an Image function), T'Put{"_"}Image shall be specified so that T'Image yields the same result as that Image function.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>56/5</MarginText>
<p>For each language-defined private type T, T'Image should generate an image that would be meaningful based only on the relevant public interfaces, as opposed to requiring knowledge of the implementation of the private type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>56.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>For each language-defined private type T, T'Image should generate an image that would be meaningful based only on the relevant public interfaces.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>56.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0020-1", "AI12-0315-1", "AI12-0340-1", "AI12-0384-2", "AI12-0419-1", "AI12-0427-1", "AI12-0435-1"]} />
Attribute Put{"_"}Image is new. Attributes Image, Wide{"_"}Image, and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image now can be used with any type, and are defined in terms of Put{"_"}Image so that they can be redefined. <br />

---

# 4.2. Literals

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  32

# 4.2. Literals

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ A <i>literal</i> represents a value literally, that is, by means of notation suited to its kind.] A literal is either a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.4#S0006">numeric_literal</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, the literal <b>null</b>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>An enumeration literal that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> rather than a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code> is not considered a <i>literal</i> in the above sense, because it involves no special notation &ldquo;suited to its kind&rdquo;. It might more properly be called an <code>enumeration{"_"}identifier</code>, except for historical reasons. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that consists of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, either its expected type shall be a single character type, in which case it is interpreted as a parameterless <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> that yields the corresponding value of the character type, or its expected profile shall correspond to a parameterless function with a character result type, in which case it is interpreted as the name of the corresponding parameterless function declared as part of the character type's definition (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.1">3.5.1</a>). In either case, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code> denotes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0039">enumeration_literal_specification</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a> for the resolution rules for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0325-1", "AI12-0373-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> shall be a single string type or a type with a specified String{"_"}Literal aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>). In either case, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> is interpreted to be of its expected type. If the expected type of an integer literal is a type with a specified Integer{"_"}Literal aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>), the literal is interpreted to be of its expected type; otherwise it is interpreted to be of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. If the expected type of a real literal is a type with a specified Real{"_"}Literal aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>), it is interpreted to be of its expected type; otherwise, it is interpreted to be of type <i>universal{"_"}real</i>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall correspond to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0040">defining_character_literal</a></code> of the expected type, or of the result type of the expected profile.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0295-1", "AI12-0325-1"]} />
<p>If the expected type for a string{"_"}literal is a string type, then for each character of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> there shall be a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0040">defining_character_literal</a></code> of the component type of the expected string type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00231-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI12-0373-1"]} />
<p>The literal <b>null</b> is of type <i>universal{"_"}access</i>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1"]} />
<p>If its expected type is a numeric type, the evaluation of a numeric literal yields the represented value. [In other cases, the effect of evaluating a numeric literal is determined by the Integer{"_"}Literal or Real{"_"}Literal aspect that applies (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>).]<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1"]} />
<p>The evaluation of the literal <b>null</b> yields the null value of the expected type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0295-1", "AI12-0325-1"]} />
<p>The evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> and has an expected type that is a string type, yields an array value containing the value of each character of the sequence of characters of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>, as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6">2.6</a>. The bounds of this array value are determined according to the rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0114">positional_array_aggregate</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.3">4.3.3</a>), except that for a null string literal, the upper bound is the predecessor of the lower bound. [In other cases, the effect of evaluating a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> is determined by the String{"_"}Literal aspect that applies (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>).]<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0295-1", "AI12-0325-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> of a string type <i>T</i>, a check is made that the value of each character of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> belongs to the component subtype of <i>T</i>. For the evaluation of a null string literal of a string type, a check is made that its lower bound is greater than the lower bound of the base range of the index type. The exception Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if either of these checks fails. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If no predicates apply to the component subtype, the checks on the characters need not involve more than two checks altogether, since one need only check the characters of the string with the lowest and highest position numbers against the range of the component subtype. <br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
NOTE   Enumeration literals that are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s rather than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s follow the normal rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s when used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>). <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">Character_literal</a></code>s used as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>s follow the normal rules for expanded names (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>). <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of literals:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
3.14159{"_"}26536 	--  a real literal{"\n"}1{"_"}345 	--  an integer literal{"\n"}'A' 	--  a character literal{"\n"}"Some Text" 	--  a string literal {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
Because <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s are now treated like other literals, in that they are resolved using context rather than depending on direct visibility, additional qualification might be necessary when passing a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code> to an overloaded subprogram. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>14.b</MarginText>
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">Character_literal</a></code>s are now treated analogously to <b>null</b> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>s, in that they are resolved using context, rather than their content; the declaration of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0040">defining_character_literal</a></code> need not be directly visible. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>14.c</MarginText>
Name Resolution rules for enumeration literals that are not <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s are not included anymore, since they are neither syntactically nor semantically "literals" but are rather names of parameterless functions. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>14.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00231-01"]} />
<b>Null</b> now has type <i>universal{"_"}access</i>, which is similar to other literals. <b>Null</b> can be used with anonymous access types. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>14.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0295-1"]} />
The rules in this subclause are adjusted to allow for the possibility of user-defined literals. These are fully documented in the next subclause. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.2.1"></a>

## 4.2.1  User-Defined Literals

<MarginText>1/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1"]} />
<p>Using one or more of the aspects defined below, a type may be specified to allow the use of one or more kinds of literals as values of the type. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0342-1"]} />
<p>The following type-related operational aspects (collectively known as <i>user-defined literal aspects</i>) may be specified for a type <i>T</i>:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0373-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Integer{"_"}Literal</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is specified by a <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that statically denotes a function with a result type of <i>T</i> and one <b>in</b> parameter that is of type String and is not explicitly aliased.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.a/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Integer{"_"}Literal: </b>Defines a function to implement user-defined integer literals.<br />

<MarginText>4/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0373-1", "AI12-0394-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Real{"_"}Literal</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is specified by a <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that statically denotes a function with a result type of <i>T</i> and one <b>in</b> parameter that is of type String and is not explicitly aliased, and optionally a second function [(overloading the first) ]with a result type of <i>T</i> and two <b>in</b> parameters of type String that are not explicitly aliased.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>4.a/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Real{"_"}Literal: </b>Defines a function or functions to implement user-defined real literals.<br />

<MarginText>5/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0295-1", "AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0373-1"]} />
<dt><br/>String{"_"}Literal</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is specified by a <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that statically denotes a function with a result type of <i>T</i> and one <b>in</b> parameter that is of type Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String and is not explicitly aliased.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>5.a/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>String{"_"}Literal: </b>Defines a function to implement user-defined string literals.<br />

<MarginText>5.b/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The following example is legal because the resolution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> for an aspect that is defined to be a subprogram is based on the profile required for that aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>): <br />

<MarginText>5.c/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Pkg1 is{"\n"}   type T is record X, Y : Integer; end record{"\n"}     with Integer{"_"}Literal ={">"} Int{"_"}Lit;{"\n"}   function Int{"_"}Lit (X, Y : T) return Duration;    -- Wrong profile.{"\n"}   function Int{"_"}Lit (Lit{"_"}Image : String) return T; -- Right profile.{"\n"}end Pkg1;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
<p>User-defined literal aspects are nonoverridable (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This means that in this example<br />

<MarginText>6.b/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Pkg2 is{"\n"}   type T1 is record{"\n"}      X, Y : Integer;{"\n"}   end record with Integer{"_"}Literal ={">"} I{"_"}L;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6.c/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
   function I{"_"}L (S : String) return T1 is ((0, 0));{"\n"}
<MarginText>6.d/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
   type T2 is new T1;{"\n"}   function I{"_"}L (S : String) return T2 is ((1, 1));{"\n"}   X : T2 := 123;{"\n"}end Pkg2;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.e/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0419-1"]} />
the initial value of Pkg2.X is (1,1), not (0,0). <br />

<MarginText>7/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0427-1"]} />
<p>When a numeric literal is interpreted as a value of a non-numeric type <i>T</i> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> is interpreted as a value of a type <i>T</i> that is not a string type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2">4.2</a>), it is equivalent to a call to the subprogram denoted by the corresponding aspect of <i>T</i>: the Integer{"_"}Literal aspect for an integer literal, the Real{"_"}Literal aspect for a real literal, and the String{"_"}Literal aspect for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>. The actual parameter of this notional call is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> representing a sequence of characters that is the same as the sequence of characters in the original numeric literal, or the sequence represented by the original string literal.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This equivalence defines, for example, the nominal type, the nominal subtype, and the accessibility level of a user-defined literal. It also has the consequence that a user-defined literal shall not be of an abstract type (because that would be equivalent to a nondispatching call to an abstract function). This equivalence also defines the Dynamic Semantics of evaluating a user-defined literal.<br />

<MarginText>7.b/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
The (sub)type of the actual parameter to this call is determined by the profile of the appropriate aspect, and the bounds of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code> are defined by the usual rules for the bounds of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>8/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1"]} />
<p>Such a literal is said to be a <i>user-defined literal</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0394-1"]} />
<p>When a named number that denotes a value of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i> is interpreted as a value of a non-numeric type <i>T</i>, it is equivalent to a call to the function denoted by the Integer{"_"}Literal aspect of <i>T</i>. The actual parameter of this notional call is a String having a textual representation of a decimal integer literal optionally preceded by a minus sign, representing the same value as the named number.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0394-1"]} />
<p>When a named number that denotes a value of type <i>universal{"_"}real</i> is interpreted as a value of a non-numeric type <i>T</i>, it is equivalent to a call to the two-parameter function denoted by the Real{"_"}Literal aspect of <i>T</i>, if any. The actual parameters of this notional call are each a String with the textual representation of a decimal integer literal, with the first optionally preceded by a minus sign, where the first String represents the same value as the numerator, and the second the same value as the denominator, of the named number when represented as a rational number in lowest terms, with a positive denominator.<br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>11/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0295-1", "AI12-0325-1", "AI12-0342-1"]} />
<p>The Integer{"_"}Literal or Real{"_"}Literal aspect shall not be specified for a type <i>T</i> if the full view of <i>T</i> is a numeric type. The String{"_"}Literal aspect shall not be specified for a type <i>T</i> if the full view of <i>T</i> is a string type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1"]} />
<p>For a nonabstract type, the function directly specified for a user-defined literal aspect shall not be abstract.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1"]} />
<p>For a tagged type with a partial view, a user-defined literal aspect shall not be directly specified on the full type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0394-1"]} />
<p>If a nonabstract tagged type inherits any user-defined literal aspect, then each inherited aspect shall be directly specified as a nonabstract function for the type unless the inherited aspect denotes a nonabstract function, or functions, and the type is a null extension.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0394-1"]} />
<p>If a named number that denotes a value of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i> is interpreted as a value of a non-numeric type <i>T</i>, <i>T</i> shall have an Integer{"_"}Literal aspect. If a named number that denotes a value of type <i>universal{"_"}real</i> is interpreted as a value of a non-numeric type <i>T</i>, <i>T</i> shall have a Real{"_"}Literal aspect, and the aspect shall denote a function that has two <b>in</b> parameters, both of type String, with result of type <i>T</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0342-1"]} />
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>17/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0325-1", "AI12-0342-1", "AI12-0394-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error if the evaluation of a literal or named number that has an expected type with a specified user-defined literal aspect propagates an exception. Either Program{"_"}Error or the exception propagated by the evaluation is raised at the point of use of the value of the literal or named number. If it is recognized prior to run time that evaluation of such a literal or named number will inevitably (if executed) result in such a bounded error, then this may be reported as an error prior to run time.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>As always, an implementation may apply "as-if" optimizations (those that result in the same external effects in the absence of erroneous execution) to the function calls associated with user-defined literals. In particular, if the function associated with a user-defined literal aspect has a Global aspect that indicates no references to global variables, then a number of optimizations are available to the implementation: <br />

<MarginText>17.b/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The implementation can evaluate a user-defined literal function at compile-time if it has access to the body of the function (for example, if it is inlined), and that body doesn't reference anything evaluated at runtime. If the compile-time evaluation results in an exception, this bounded error allows the compilation unit to be rejected.<br /></li>
<MarginText>17.c/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<li>Implementations can use existing permissions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#Subclause_6.1.2">6.1.2</a>) to avoid evaluating the function associated with a user-defined literal more than once for a particular literal value. This evaluation can be "hoisted" (done once per compilation unit during the elaboration of the unit) if the compiler can prove that the function doesn't depend on any constants or locals with a runtime value not yet elaborated.<br /></li>
<MarginText>17.d/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<li>If the literal value is not needed by the execution of the program, the function call can be omitted even if it might have side-effects (again, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#Subclause_6.1.2">6.1.2</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Examples

<MarginText>18/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Examples of the specification and use of user-defined literals:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>19/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
subtype Roman{"_"}Character is Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Character{"\n"}   with Static{"_"}Predicate ={">"}{"\n"}      Roman{"_"}Character in 'I' | 'V' | 'X' | 'L' | 'C' | 'D' | 'M';{"\n"}
<MarginText>20/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
Max{"_"}Roman{"_"}Number : constant := 3{"_"}999;  -- MMMCMXCIX{"\n"}
<MarginText>21/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
type Roman{"_"}Number is range 1 .. Max{"_"}Roman{"_"}Number{"\n"}   with String{"_"}Literal ={">"} To{"_"}Roman{"_"}Number;{"\n"}
<MarginText>22/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
function To{"_"}Roman{"_"}Number (S : Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String) return Roman{"_"}Number{"\n"}   with Pre ={">"} S'Length {">"} 0 and then{"\n"}      (for all Char of S ={">"} Char in Roman{"_"}Character);{"\n"}
<MarginText>23/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1", "AI12-0386-1"]} />
function To{"_"}Roman{"_"}Number (S : Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String) return Roman{"_"}Number is{"\n"}   (declare{"\n"}      R : constant array (Integer range {"<"}{">"}) of Roman{"_"}Number :={"\n"}         (for D in S'Range ={">"} Roman{"_"}Digit'Enum{"_"}Rep{"\n"}             (Roman{"_"}Digit'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value (''' & S(D) & ''')));{"\n"}                     -- See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.2">3.5.2</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.4">13.4</a>{"\n"}    begin{"\n"}      [for I in R'Range ={">"}{"\n"}         (if I {"<"} R'Last and then R(I) {"<"} R(I + 1) then -1 else 1) {"*"} R(I)]{"\n"}            'Reduce("+", 0){"\n"}   );{"\n"}
<MarginText>24/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
X : Roman{"_"}Number := "III" {"*"} "IV" {"*"} "XII"; -- 144 (that is, CXLIV){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>24.a/5_4.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0249-1", "AI12-0295-1", "AI12-0325-1", "AI12-0342-1"]} />
The user-defined literal aspects Integer{"_"}Literal, Real{"_"}Literal, and String{"_"}Literal are new. <br />

# 4.3. Aggregates

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  33

# 4.3. Aggregates

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ An <i>aggregate</i> combines component values into a composite value of an array type, record type, or record extension.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>aggregate</b> &mdash; construct used to define a value of a composite type by specifying the values of the components of the type<br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1", "AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>aggregate</code><a id="S0106"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0120">delta_aggregate</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01", "AI12-0127-1", "AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0307-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> shall be a single array type, a single type with the Aggregate aspect specified, or a single descendant of a record type or of a record extension. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">The Context of Overload Resolution</a>&rdquo; for the meaning of &ldquo;shall be a single ... type&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>3.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There are additional rules for each kind of aggregate. These aggregate rules are additive; a legal expression needs to satisfy all of the applicable rules. That means the rule given here must be satisfied even when it is syntactically possible to tell which specific kind of aggregate is being used. <br />

<MarginText>3.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0127-1", "AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0307-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Generally, we don't want to look in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s to resolve them. For instance, Ada 95 allowed array types to match <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>s, even though those have to be record types. Thus, we allow any record type with any visible (nondiscriminant) components to match an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, even though only <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0120">delta_aggregate</a></code>s allow private types or private extensions. Similarly, we allow any container type to match an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, even though only <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code>s allow container types. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code> shall not be of a class-wide type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>When the expected type in some context is class-wide, an aggregate has to be explicitly qualified by the specific type of value to be created, so that the expected type for the aggregate itself is specific. <br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We used to disallow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s of a type with unknown discriminants. However, that was unnecessarily restrictive in the case of an extension aggregate, and irrelevant to a record aggregate (since a type that is legal for a record aggregate could not possibly have unknown discriminants) and to an array aggregate (the only specific types that can have unknown discriminants are private types, private extensions, and types derived from them). <br />

<MarginText>4.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We don't mention <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0120">delta_aggregate</a></code>s, as those can get the specific type from the object represented by the <i>base{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (possibly at run time). We don't mention <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code>s, as those cannot even be of a tagged type, so being class-wide is impossible. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>For the evaluation of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, an anonymous object is created and values for the components or ancestor part are obtained (as described in the subsequent subclause for each kind of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>) and assigned into the corresponding components or ancestor part of the anonymous object. Obtaining the values and the assignments occur in an arbitrary order. The value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is the value of this object. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The ancestor part is the set of components inherited from the ancestor type. The syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0112">ancestor_part</a></code> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> that specifies how the ancestor part of the anonymous object should be initialized. <br />

<MarginText>5.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The assignment operations do the necessary value adjustment, as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>. Note that the value as a whole is not adjusted &mdash; just the subcomponents (and ancestor part, if any). <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a> also describes when this anonymous object is finalized.<br />

<MarginText>5.c</MarginText>
If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0112">ancestor_part</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> the Initialize procedure for the ancestor type is applied to the ancestor part after default-initializing it, unless the procedure is abstract, as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>. The Adjust procedure for the ancestor type is not called in this case, since there is no assignment to the ancestor part as a whole. <br />

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is of a tagged type, a check is made that its value belongs to the first subtype of the type. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This check ensures that no values of a tagged type are ever outside the first subtype, as required for inherited dispatching operations to work properly (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4">3.4</a>). This check will always succeed if the first subtype is unconstrained. This check is not extended to untagged types to preserve upward compatibility. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>6.b</MarginText>
We now allow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>s. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>6.c</MarginText>
We have adopted new wording for expressing the rule that the type of an aggregate shall be determinable from the outside, though using the fact that it is nonlimited record (extension) or array.<br />

<MarginText>6.d</MarginText>
An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> now creates an anonymous object. This is necessary so that controlled types will work (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>6.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
In Ada 95, a limited type is not considered when resolving an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>. Since Ada 2005 now allows limited <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s, we can have incompatibilities. For example: <br />

<MarginText>6.f/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Lim is limited{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Comp: Integer;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6.g/2</MarginText>
type Not{"_"}Lim is{"\n"}   record{"\n"}      Comp: Integer;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6.h/2</MarginText>
procedure P(X: Lim);{"\n"}procedure P(X: Not{"_"}Lim);{"\n"}
<MarginText>6.i/2</MarginText>
P((Comp ={">"} 123)); -- Illegal in Ada 2005, legal in Ada 95{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.j/2</MarginText>
The call to P is ambiguous in Ada 2005, while it would not be ambiguous in Ada 95 as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> could not have a limited type. Qualifying the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> will eliminate any ambiguity. This construction would be rather confusing to a maintenance programmer, so it should be avoided, and thus we expect it to be rare. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>6.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">Aggregate</a></code>s can be of a limited type. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>6.l/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0127-1", "AI12-0212-1"]} />
We now allow types with the Aggregate aspect specified ("container types"), as well as private types and extensions descended from a record type or extension, to match all forms of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>. These types are only allowed for new types of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code>s for the Aggregate aspect, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0120">delta_aggregate</a></code>s for private types), but, consistent with other forms of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, we do not look at the form of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> to determine resolution. This can be incompatible in usually unlikely cases, where overloading of a container or private type with a type that was previously allowed in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s makes an existing call ambiguous. Unfortunately, Ada.Containers.Vectors has a number of such overloadings for Insert, Append, Prepend, and "&", so the problem may appear for any element type of a Vector that allows aggregates. For instance, if My{"_"}Vector is an instance of Ada.Containers.Vectors with an element type of Not{"_"}Lim as defined above, and V is an object of My{"_"}Vector.Vector, then My{"_"}Vector.Append (V, (Comp ={">"} 123)); will be illegal in Ada 2022 and legal in Ada 2012. This can easily be fixed by qualifying the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> with the correct type. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.3.1"></a>

## 4.3.1  Record Aggregates

<MarginText>1_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p>[In a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code>, a value is specified for each component of the record or record extension value, using either a named or a positional association.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_4.3.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>record{"_"}aggregate</code><a id="S0107"></a><code> ::= </code>(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record_component_association_list</a></code>)<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_4.3.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>record{"_"}component{"_"}association{"_"}list</code><a id="S0108"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code>{"}"}<br />  | <b>null record</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/2_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>record{"_"}component{"_"}association</code><a id="S0109"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0110">component_choice_list</a></code> ={">"}] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0110">component_choice_list</a></code> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>component{"_"}choice{"_"}list</code><a id="S0110"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> {"{"}'|' <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>{"}"}<br />   | <b>others</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code> is a <i>named component association</i> if it has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0110">component_choice_list</a></code>; otherwise, it is a <i>positional component association</i>. Any positional component associations shall precede any named component associations. If there is a named association with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0110">component_choice_list</a></code> of <b>others</b>, it shall come last. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>These rules were implied by the BNF in an early version of the RM9X, but it made the grammar harder to read, and was inconsistent with how we handle discriminant constraints. Note that for array aggregates we still express some of the rules in the grammar, but array aggregates are significantly different because an array aggregate is either all positional (with a possible <b>others</b> at the end), or all named. <br />

<MarginText>7_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">In the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record{"_"}component{"_"}association{"_"}list</a></code> for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record{"_"}aggregate</a></code>, if there is only one association, it shall be a named association. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Otherwise, the construct would be interpreted as a parenthesized expression. This is considered a syntax rule, since it is relevant to overload resolution. We choose not to express it with BNF so we can share the definition of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record_component_association_list</a></code> in both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>7.b_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record_component_association_list</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code> does not have such a restriction. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8/2_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> shall be a single record type or record extension. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule is used to resolve whether an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code>. The presence of a <b>with</b> is used to resolve between a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> and an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>9/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>For the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record{"_"}component{"_"}association{"_"}list</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record{"_"}aggregate</a></code>, all components of the composite value defined by the aggregate are <i>needed</i>[; for the association list of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>, only those components not determined by the ancestor expression or subtype are needed (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.2">4.3.2</a>).] Each <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector{"_"}name</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code> shall denote a needed component [(including possibly a discriminant)]. Each <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0121">record_delta_aggregate</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.4">4.3.4</a>) shall denote a nondiscriminant component of the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For the association list of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code>, &ldquo;needed components&rdquo; includes every component of the composite value, but does not include those in unchosen <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>s (see AI83-309). If there are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>s, then the value specified for the discriminant that governs them determines which <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> is chosen, and hence which components are needed.<br />

<MarginText>9.b_4.3.1</MarginText>
If an extension defines a new <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code>, then all of its discriminants are needed in the component association list of an extension aggregate for that type, even if the discriminants have the same names and types as discriminants of the type of the ancestor expression. This is necessary to ensure that the positions in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record{"_"}component{"_"}association{"_"}list</a></code> are well defined, and that discriminants that govern <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>s can be given by static expressions. <br />

<MarginText>9.c/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We don't define &ldquo;needed&rdquo; for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0121">record_delta_aggregate</a></code>s so that there is no completeness requirement. But that means that we need to ensure that the rules using &ldquo;needed&rdquo; doesn't appear to apply to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0121">record_delta_aggregate</a></code>s, and we also need Legality Rules to prevent giving the same component twice and giving components from two different variants. <br />

<MarginText>9.d/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>needed component</b> &mdash; component of a record type or record extension that is required to have its value specified within a given aggregate<br />

<MarginText>10_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code> is the type of the <i>associated</i> component(s); the associated component(s) are as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>11_4.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a positional association, the component [(including possibly a discriminant)] in the corresponding relative position (in the declarative region of the type), counting only the needed components; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This means that for an association list of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>, only noninherited components are counted to determine the position.<br />

<MarginText>11.b/3_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
For a derived type (including type extensions), the order of declaration is defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4">3.4</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4">Derived Types and Classes</a>&rdquo;. In particular, all discriminants come first, regardless of whether they are defined for the parent type or are newly added to the derived type. <br />

<MarginText>12_4.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a named association with one or more <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>s, the named component(s);<br /></li>
<MarginText>13_4.3.1</MarginText>
<li>For a named association with the reserved word <b>others</b>, all needed components that are not associated with some previous association. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>14_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p>If the type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> is a record extension, then it shall be a descendant of a record type, through one or more record extensions (and no private extensions).<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0016-1", "AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record_component_association_list</a></code> shall be <b>null record</b> only if the list occurs in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>, and there are no components needed for that list.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, "(<b>null record</b>)" is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> for a null record type. Similarly, "(T'(A) <b>with null record</b>)" is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code> for a type defined as a null record extension of T.<br />

<MarginText>15.b/3_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0016-1"]} />
If no components are needed and <b>null record</b> is not used, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code> must necessarily be <b>others</b> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}, as that is the only <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code> that does not require an associated component. <br />

<MarginText>16/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01", "AI05-0199-1", "AI12-0046-1", "AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>, each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> other than an <b>others</b> choice with a {"<"}{">"} shall have at least one associated component, and each needed component shall be associated with exactly one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record{"_"}component{"_"}association</a></code>. For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0121">record_delta_aggregate</a></code>, each <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> of each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0110">component_choice_list</a></code> shall denote a distinct nondiscriminant component of the type of the aggregate.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/2_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>These rules apply to an association with an <b>others</b> choice with an expression. An <b>others</b> choice with a {"<"}{">"} can match zero components or several components with different types. <br />

<MarginText>16.b/2_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Without these rules, there would be no way to know what was the expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the association. Note that some of the rules do not apply to {"<"}{">"} associations, as we do not need to resolve anything. We allow <b>others</b> ={">"} {"<"}{">"} to match no components as this is similar to array aggregates. That means that (<b>others</b> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}) always represents a default-initialized record or array value. <br />

<MarginText>16.c/4_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0046-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>16.d_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The rule that requires at least one associated component for each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> implies that there can be no extra associations for components that don't exist in the composite value, or that are already determined by the ancestor expression or subtype of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>16.e_4.3.1</MarginText>
The second part of the first sentence ensures that no needed components are left out, nor specified twice. <br />

<MarginText>16.1/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0046-1", "AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> has two or more associated components, all of them shall be of the same type, or all of them shall be of anonymous access types whose subtypes statically match. In addition, Legality Rules are enforced separately for each associated component.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.f/4_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0046-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>AI83-00244 also requires that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall be legal for each associated component. Ada 95 omitted this wording, as it was thought that all cases of difference had been eliminated. That probably was true, but Ada 2005 reintroduced cases where the types match but the legality differs. For example:<br />

<MarginText>16.g/4_4.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Rec (D : access Integer) is record{"\n"}          F : access Integer;{"\n"}end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>16.h/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
begin{"\n"}   declare{"\n"}      X : aliased Integer;{"\n"}      R : Rec := (D | F ={">"} X'Access); -- Legal for D, illegal for F{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16.i/4_4.3.1</MarginText>
There are additional ways for this to happen; because of cases like the above we require that the Legality Rules are checked individually for each associated component. <br />

<MarginText>17/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0220-1", "AI12-0086-1", "AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> <i>P</i> is nested within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code> <i>V</i> that is not selected by the discriminant value governing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> enclosing <i>V</i>, then there is no restriction on the discriminant governing <i>P</i>. Otherwise, the value of the discriminant that governs <i>P</i> shall be given by a static expression, or by a nonstatic expression having a constrained static nominal subtype. In this latter case of a nonstatic expression, there shall be exactly one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> of <i>P</i> that covers each value that belongs to the nominal subtype and satisfies the predicates of the subtype, and there shall be at least one such value. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This expression might either be given within the aggregate itself, or in a constraint on the parent subtype in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> for some ancestor of the type of the aggregate.<br />

<MarginText>17.a.1/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0086-1"]} />
This means that in the nonstatic value case, the (static) subtype cannot have a null range. <br />

<MarginText>17.1/2_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> for a discriminant without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> shall have an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> rather than {"<"}{">"}. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.b/2_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A discriminant must always have a defined value, but {"<"}{">"} means uninitialized for a discrete type unless the component has a default value. <br />

<MarginText>17.2/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record_component_association_list</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0121">record_delta_aggregate</a></code> shall not:<br /></p>

<MarginText>17.3/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0418-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>use the box compound delimiter {"<"}{">"} rather than an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>17.4/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<li>have an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a limited type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>17.5/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<li>omit the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0110">component_choice_list</a></code>; or<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17.c/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0121">record_delta_aggregate</a></code> cannot use positional notation; all choices shall be named choices. <br />

<MarginText>17.6/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0110">component_choice_list</a></code> that is an <b>others</b> choice. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17.7/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0121">record_delta_aggregate</a></code>, no two <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>s shall denote components declared within different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>s of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>18_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p>The evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> consists of the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record{"_"}component{"_"}association{"_"}list</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0086-1", "AI12-0451-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0108">record{"_"}component{"_"}association{"_"}list</a></code>, any per-object constraints (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8">3.8</a>) for components specified in the association list are elaborated and any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s are evaluated and converted to the subtype of the associated component. Any constraint elaborations and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> evaluations (and conversions) occur in an arbitrary order, except that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> for a discriminant is evaluated (and converted) prior to the elaboration of any per-object constraint that depends on it, which in turn occurs prior to the evaluation and conversion of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> for the component with the per-object constraint. If the value of a discriminant that governs a selected <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> is given by a nonstatic <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, and the evaluation of that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> yields a value that does not belong to the nominal subtype of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, then Constraint{"_"}Error is raised.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The conversion in the first rule might raise Constraint{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>19.b_4.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This check in the first rule presumably happened as part of the dependent compatibility check in Ada 83. <br />

<MarginText>19.c/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0086-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The test on the value of the discriminant can only fail if the value is outside the base range of its type, does not satisfy the (static) predicates of the subtype (possible when the predicate is disabled), or is an invalid representation. This is a rule similar to that used for case statements. As with case statements, this is not a &ldquo;check&rdquo;; it cannot be Suppressed. <br />

<MarginText>19.1/2_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> defines the value for the associated component(s). For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> with {"<"}{">"}, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>, that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> defines the value for the associated component(s); otherwise, the associated component(s) are initialized by default as for a stand-alone object of the component subtype (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>20_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> is evaluated (and converted) once for each associated component.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a/3_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We don't need similar language for {"<"}{">"}, as we're considering the value of {"<"}{">"} for each individual component. Each component has its own default expression or its own default initialization (they can be different for each component; the components even could have different types), and each one has to be evaluated. So there is no need to repeat that. <br />

<MarginText>21/5_4.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0447-1"]} />
NOTE   By the rules given above, for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0107">record_aggregate</a></code> with positional associations, expressions specifying discriminant values appear first and in the same order as their corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code>s, since the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> occurs first in the declaration of the type. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>22_4.3.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a record aggregate with positional associations:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>23_4.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
