</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>29/5_4.3.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1", "AI12-0379-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example where the base expression is class-wide:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>30/5_4.3.4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Translate (P : Point'Class; X, Y : Real) return Point'Class is{"\n"}   (P with delta X ={">"} P.X + X,{"\n"}                 Y ={">"} P.Y + Y); -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9">3.9</a> for declaration of type Point{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>30.a/5_4.3.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0127-1"]} />
Delta aggregates are new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.3.5"></a>

## 4.3.5  Container Aggregates

<MarginText>1/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>In a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code>, values are specified for elements of a container; for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0125">positional_container_aggregate</a></code>, the elements are given sequentially; for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code>, the elements are specified by a sequence of key/value pairs, or using an iterator. The Aggregate aspect of the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> determines how the elements are combined to form the container.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>container aggregate</b> &mdash; construct used to define a value of a type that represents a collection of elements, by explicitly specifying the elements in the collection<br />

<MarginText>2/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>For a type other than an array type, the following type-related operational aspect may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Aggregate</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> of the form:<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Aggregate: </b>Mechanism to define user-defined aggregates.<br />

<MarginText>4/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented8">   (Empty ={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>[,<br />    Add{"_"}Named ={">"} <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>][,<br />    Add{"_"}Unnamed ={">"} <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>][,<br />    New{"_"}Indexed ={">"} <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>,<br />    Assign{"_"}Indexed ={">"} <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>])<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI22-0020-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>As this aspect is described with syntax, it has to be given exactly as specified here. That means it cannot be given as a positional aggregate, nor can the order of the elements be changed. For instance, New{"_"}Indexed always has to occur before Assign{"_"}Indexed, and Empty always has to be first. <br />

<MarginText>5/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>The type for which this aspect is specified is known as the <i>container type</i> of the Aggregate aspect. A <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall be specified for at least one of Add{"_"}Named, Add{"_"}Unnamed, or Assign{"_"}Indexed. If Add{"_"}Named is specified, neither Add{"_"}Unnamed nor Assign{"_"}Indexed shall be specified. Either both or neither of New{"_"}Indexed and Assign{"_"}Indexed shall be specified.<br /></dd>
</dl>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>6/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> specified for Empty for an Aggregate aspect shall denote a constant of the container type, or denote exactly one function with a result type of the container type that has no parameters, or that has one <b>in</b> parameter of a signed integer type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>In the function case, the parameter, if present may be used to specify an initial size for the container, in anticipation of adding elements to it. For a positional aggregate, or a named aggregate that doesn't use an iterator, it will be initialized with the number of elements. For a named aggregate that uses an iterator, the implementation is permitted to estimate the number of elements that the iterator will produce, but it is not required to do so. <br />

<MarginText>7/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0437-1"]} />
<p>The <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> specified for Add{"_"}Unnamed for an Aggregate aspect shall denote exactly one procedure that has two parameters, the first an <b>in out</b> parameter of the container type, and the second an <b>in</b> parameter of some nonlimited type, called the <i>element type</i> of the container type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0437-1"]} />
<p>The <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> specified for New{"_"}Indexed for an Aggregate aspect shall denote exactly one function with a result type of the container type, and two parameters of the same discrete type, with that type being the <i>key type</i> of the container type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The New{"_"}Indexed function is used instead of Empty as the first step of creating an aggregate that is initialized using the Assign{"_"}Indexed procedure. <br />

<MarginText>9/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0437-1"]} />
<p>The <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> specified for Add{"_"}Named or Assign{"_"}Indexed for an Aggregate aspect shall denote exactly one procedure that has three parameters, the first an <b>in out</b> parameter of the container type, the second an <b>in</b> parameter of a nonlimited type (the <i>key type</i> of the container type), and the third, an <b>in</b> parameter of a nonlimited type that is called the <i>element type</i> of the container type.<br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>10/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>If the container type of an Aggregate aspect is a private type, the full type of the container type shall not be an array type. If the container type is limited, the name specified for Empty shall denote a function rather than a constant object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>For an Aggregate aspect, the key type of Assign{"_"}Indexed shall be the same type as that of the parameters of New{"_"}Indexed. Additionally, if both Add{"_"}Unnamed and Assign{"_"}Indexed are specified, the final parameters shall be of the same type &mdash; the element type of the container type.<br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>12/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0388-1"]} />
<p>The Aggregate aspect is nonoverridable (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>). <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>13/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>container{"_"}aggregate</code><a id="S0123"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0124">null_container_aggregate</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0125">positional_container_aggregate</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>null{"_"}container{"_"}aggregate</code><a id="S0124"></a><code> ::= </code>'[' ']'<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>15/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>positional{"_"}container{"_"}aggregate</code><a id="S0125"></a><code> ::= </code>'[' <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>{"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>{"}"} ']'<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>named{"_"}container{"_"}aggregate</code><a id="S0126"></a><code> ::= </code>'[' <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0127">container_element_association_list</a></code> ']'<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Unlike other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s, container aggregates have to be surrounded with brackets rather than parentheses. Using brackets allows writing zero- and one-element positional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s. (Were we to use parentheses, a one-element positional aggregate would look the same as and would always be interpreted as a parenthesized expression.) Unlike the case for arrays, where it is always possible to give bounds to work around this gap, such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> could not be written at all for a sequence type (such as a list) where there is no index or key to use. <br />

<MarginText>17/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>container{"_"}element{"_"}association{"_"}list</code><a id="S0127"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code>{"}"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>18/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>container{"_"}element{"_"}association</code><a id="S0128"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code> ={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code> ={">"} {"<"}{">"}<br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>19/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>key{"_"}choice{"_"}list</code><a id="S0129"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code> {"{"}'|' <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code>{"}"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>20/5_4.3.5</MarginText>

<code>key{"_"}choice</code><a id="S0130"></a><code> ::= </code><i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iterated{"_"}element{"_"}association</code><a id="S0131"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>[ <b>use</b> <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>] ={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />  | <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>[ <b>use</b> <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>] ={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>22/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0437-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code> shall be a single type for which the Aggregate aspect has been specified. The expected type for each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code> is the element type of the expected type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>23/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code>, is the key type of the expected type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>.<br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>24/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0125">positional_container_aggregate</a></code> shall have an Aggregate aspect that includes a specification for an Add{"_"}Unnamed procedure or an Assign{"_"}Indexed procedure. The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> that contains one or more <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>s with a <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall have an Aggregate aspect that includes a specification for the Add{"_"}Named procedure. The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> that contains one or more <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code>s shall have an Aggregate aspect that includes a specification for the Add{"_"}Named or Assign{"_"}Indexed procedure. [A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0124">null_container_aggregate</a></code> can be of any type with an Aggregate aspect.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>25/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>A non-null container aggregate is called an <i>indexed aggregate</i> if the expected type <i>T</i> of the aggregate specifies an Assign{"_"}Indexed procedure in its Aggregate aspect, and either there is no Add{"_"}Unnamed procedure specified for the type, or the aggregate is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code> that contains a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>. The key type of an indexed aggregate is also called the <i>index type</i> of the aggregate.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code> with a {"<"}{">"} rather than an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, or with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0058">discrete_range</a></code>, is permitted only in an indexed aggregate.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Only an element of an indexed aggregate can be left uninitialized, because the compiler can simply omit producing an Assign{"_"}Indexed operation for the given index. For other kinds of aggregates, there are no operations that add an element without giving it a value. We could have defined such (optional) operations, but they would have added significant complication to an already complex feature without adding much additional expressive power. Note that, to be consistent with array aggregates, we do not support specifying {"<"}{">"} in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>27/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> without a <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is an indexed aggregate or the expected type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> specifies an Add{"_"}Named procedure in its Aggregate aspect, then the type of the loop parameter of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> shall be the same as the key type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If there is a <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>, it determines the key of each added key/value pair, rather than the loop parameter. But if there is no <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, the loop parameter itself is used as the key. <br />

<MarginText>28/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0250-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> that is an indexed aggregate, all <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code>s shall contain either a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> without a <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code>. Furthermore, for such an aggregate, either: <br /></p>

<MarginText>29/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>all <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code>s shall be static expressions or static ranges, and every <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> shall have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> that defines a non-null static range, and the set of values of the index type covered by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code>s and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>s shall form a contiguous range of values with no duplications; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>30/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>there shall be exactly one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code>, and if it has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code>, the list shall have exactly one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>30.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The above is trying to mimic the rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0116">named_array_aggregate</a></code>s, without <b>others</b>. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>31/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>The evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code> starts by creating an anonymous object <i>A</i> of the expected type <i>T</i>, initialized as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>32/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is an indexed aggregate, from the result of a call on the New{"_"}Indexed function; the actual parameters in this call represent the lower and upper bound of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, and are determined as follows: <br /></li>
<MarginText>33/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0125">positional_container_aggregate</a></code>, the lower bound is the low bound of the subtype of the key parameter of the Add{"_"}Indexed procedure, and the upper bound has a position number that is the sum of the position number of the lower bound and one less than the number of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>34/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code>, the lower bound is the lowest value covered by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code> or is the low bound of a range defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>; the upper bound is the highest value covered by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code> or is the high bound of a range defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>. <br /></li>
<MarginText>35/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> is not an indexed aggregate, by assignment from the Empty constant, or from a call on the Empty function specified in the Aggregate aspect. In the case of an Empty function with a formal parameter, the actual parameter has the following value:<br /></li>
<MarginText>36/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0124">null_container_aggregate</a></code>, the value zero;<br /></li>
<MarginText>37/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0125">positional_container_aggregate</a></code>, the number of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s;<br /></li>
<MarginText>38/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> without an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>, the number of <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s;<br /></li>
<MarginText>39/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> where every <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> contains a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>, the total number of elements specified by all of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code>s;<br /></li>
<MarginText>40/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, to an implementation-defined value.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>40.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This value ought to be an estimate for the number of elements in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, if one is available. If not, it is suggested to use the default value for the parameter if one exists, and zero otherwise. <br />

<MarginText>40.b/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The value of the parameter to Empty for some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0123">container_aggregate</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>41/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
<p>The evaluation then proceeds as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>42/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0124">null_container_aggregate</a></code>, the anonymous object <i>A</i> is the result;<br /></li>
<MarginText>43/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0125">positional_container_aggregate</a></code> of a type with a specified Add{"_"}Unnamed procedure, each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is evaluated in an arbitrary order, and the Add{"_"}Unnamed procedure is invoked in sequence with the anonymous object <i>A</i> as the first parameter and the result of evaluating each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> as the second parameter, in the order of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s;<br /></li>
<MarginText>44/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0125">positional_container_aggregate</a></code> that is an indexed aggregate, each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is evaluated in an arbitrary order, and the Assign{"_"}Indexed procedure is invoked in sequence with the anonymous object <i>A</i> as the first parameter, the key value as the second parameter, computed by starting with the low bound of the subtype of the key formal parameter of the Assign{"_"}Indexed procedure and taking the successor of this value for each successive <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, and the result of evaluating each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> as the third parameter;<br /></li>
<MarginText>45/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> for a type with an Add{"_"}Named procedure in its Aggregate aspect, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code>s are evaluated in an arbitrary order: <br /></li>
<MarginText>46/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0129">key_choice_list</a></code>, for each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code> of the list in an arbitrary order, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code> is evaluated as is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code> (in an arbitrary order), and the Add{"_"}Named procedure is invoked once for each value covered by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code>, with the anonymous object <i>A</i> as the first parameter, the value from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0130">key_choice</a></code> as the second parameter, and the result of evaluating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> as the third parameter;<br /></li>
<MarginText>47/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0327-1"]} />
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>, first the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> is elaborated, then an iteration is performed, and for each value conditionally produced by the iteration (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>) the Add{"_"}Named procedure is invoked with the anonymous object <i>A</i> as the first parameter, the result of evaluating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> as the third parameter, and:<br /></li>
<MarginText>48/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>if there is a <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, the result of evaluating the <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> as the second parameter;<br /></li>
<MarginText>49/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, with the loop parameter as the second parameter;<br /></li>
<MarginText>50/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code> that is an indexed aggregate, the evaluation proceeds as above for the case of Add{"_"}Named, but with the Assign{"_"}Indexed procedure being invoked instead of Add{"_"}Named; in the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code> with a {"<"}{">"} rather than an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, the corresponding call on Assign{"_"}Indexed is not performed, leaving the component as it was upon return from the New{"_"}Indexed function;<br /></li>
<MarginText>51/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<li>for any other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0126">named_container_aggregate</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0128">container_element_association</a></code>s (which are necessarily <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>s) are evaluated in the order given; each such evaluation comprises two steps: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>52/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> is elaborated;<br /></dd>
<MarginText>53/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0327-1"]} />
<dd>an iteration is performed, and for each value conditionally produced by the iteration (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>) the Add{"_"}Unnamed procedure is invoked, with the anonymous object <i>A</i> as the first parameter and the result of evaluating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> as the second parameter.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>53.a/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In this case, the value of the loop parameter is not directly relevant, though presumably it appears within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>54/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Examples of specifying the Aggregate aspect for a Set{"_"}Type, a Map{"_"}Type, and a Vector{"_"}Type:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>55/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   --  Set{"_"}Type is a set-like container type.{"\n"}   type Set{"_"}Type is private{"\n"}      with Aggregate ={">"} (Empty       ={">"} Empty{"_"}Set,{"\n"}                         Add{"_"}Unnamed ={">"} Include);{"\n"}   function Empty{"_"}Set return Set{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>56/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   subtype Small{"_"}Int is Integer range -1000..1000;{"\n"}
<MarginText>57/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   procedure Include (S : in out Set{"_"}Type; N : in Small{"_"}Int);{"\n"}
<MarginText>58/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   --  Map{"_"}Type is a map-like container type.{"\n"}   type Map{"_"}Type is private{"\n"}      with Aggregate ={">"}  (Empty     ={">"} Empty{"_"}Map,{"\n"}                          Add{"_"}Named ={">"} Add{"_"}To{"_"}Map);{"\n"}
<MarginText>59/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   procedure Add{"_"}To{"_"}Map (M     : in out Map{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                         Key   : in Integer;{"\n"}                         Value : in String);{"\n"}
<MarginText>60/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   Empty{"_"}Map : constant Map{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>61/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   --  Vector{"_"}Type is an extensible array-like container type.{"\n"}   type Vector{"_"}Type is private{"\n"}      with Aggregate ={">"} (Empty          ={">"} Empty{"_"}Vector,{"\n"}                         Add{"_"}Unnamed    ={">"} Append{"_"}One,{"\n"}                         New{"_"}Indexed    ={">"} New{"_"}Vector,{"\n"}                         Assign{"_"}Indexed ={">"} Assign{"_"}Element);{"\n"}
<MarginText>62/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   function Empty{"_"}Vector (Capacity : Integer := 0) return Vector{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>63/5_4.3.5</MarginText>
   procedure Append{"_"}One (V : in out Vector{"_"}Type; New{"_"}Item : in String);{"\n"}
<MarginText>64/5_4.3.5</MarginText>

# 4.4. Expressions

# 4.4. Expressions

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0158-1", "AI05-0176-1"]} />
<p>An <i>expression</i> is a formula that defines the computation or retrieval of a value. In this Reference Manual, the term &ldquo;expression&rdquo; refers to a construct of the syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or of any of the following categories: <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0133">choice_expression</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0134">choice_relation</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0139">term</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0140">factor</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>expression</code><a id="S0132"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code> {"{"}<b>and</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>{"}"} 	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code> {"{"}<b>and</b> <b>then</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>{"}"}<br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code> {"{"}<b>or</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>{"}"} 	| <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code> {"{"}<b>or</b> <b>else</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>{"}"}<br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code> {"{"}<b>xor</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>{"}"}<br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> used as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> shall resolve to denote an object or a value. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This replaces RM83-4.4(3). We don't need to mention named numbers explicitly, because the name of a named number denotes a value. We don't need to mention attributes explicitly, because attributes now denote (rather than yield) values in general. Also, the new wording allows attributes that denote objects, which should always have been allowed (in case the implementation chose to have such a thing). <br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>It might seem odd that this is an overload resolution rule, but it is relevant during overload resolution. For example, it helps ensure that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that consists of only the identifier of a parameterless function is interpreted as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> rather than directly as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>Each expression has a type; it specifies the computation or retrieval of a value of that type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0317-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> surrounded by ( and ) is known as a <i>parenthesized expression</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0317-1"]} />
<p>Every <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> consists of one or more <i>operative constituent</i> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s, only one of which is evaluated as part of evaluating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (the <i>evaluated operative constituent</i>). The operative constituents are determined as follows, according to the form of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>):<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.3/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>, the operative constituents of its <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.4/5</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>) is a parenthesized expression, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>, or a view conversion, the operative constituent(s) of its operand;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.5/5</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code>, the operative constituent(s) of its <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.6/5</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>) itself. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0317-1"]} />
<p>In certain contexts, we specify that an operative constituent shall (or shall not) be <i>newly constructed</i>. This means the operative constituent shall (or shall not) be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>; in either case, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> is permitted.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code> does not have an <b>else</b> clause, "True" is an operative constituent of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and it can be the evaluated operative constituent. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>The value of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denoting an object is the value of the object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0227-1"]} />
<p>An expression of a numeric universal type is evaluated as if it has type <i>root{"_"}integer</i> (for <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>) or <i>root{"_"}real</i> (otherwise) unless the context identifies a specific type (in which case that type is used).<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This has no effect for a static expression; its value may be arbitrarily small or large since no specific type is expected for any expression for which this rule specifies one of the root types. The only effect of this rule is to allow Constraint{"_"}Error to be raised if the value is outside of the base range of <i>root{"_"}integer</i> or <i>root{"_"}real</i> when the expression is not static. <br />

<MarginText>10.b/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule means that implementations don't have to support unlimited range math at run time for universal expressions. Note that universal expressions for which the context doesn't specify a specific type are quite rare; attribute prefixes and results are the only known cases. (For operators, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a> already specifies that the operator of a root type be used, which provides a specific type.) <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denoting an object of an unconstrained numeric subtype, if the value of the object is outside the base range of its type, the implementation may either raise Constraint{"_"}Error or return the value of the object. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This means that if extra-range intermediates are used to hold the value of an object of an unconstrained numeric subtype, a Constraint{"_"}Error can be raised on a read of the object, rather than only on an assignment to it. Similarly, it means that computing the value of an object of such a subtype can be deferred until the first read of the object (presuming no side effects other than failing an Overflow{"_"}Check are possible). This permission is over and above that provided by <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.6">11.6</a>, since this allows the Constraint{"_"}Error to move to a different handler. <br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This permission is intended to allow extra-range registers to be used efficiently to hold parameters and local variables, even if they might need to be transferred into smaller registers for performing certain predefined operations. <br />

<MarginText>11.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There is no need to mention other kinds of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code>s, since any Constraint{"_"}Error to be raised can be &ldquo;charged&rdquo; to the evaluation of the particular kind of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of primaries:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
4.0                -- real literal{"\n"}Pi                 -- named number{"\n"}(1 .. 10 ={">"} 0)     -- array aggregate{"\n"}Sum                -- variable{"\n"}Integer'Last       -- attribute{"\n"}Sine(X)            -- function call{"\n"}Color'(Blue)       -- qualified expression{"\n"}Real(M{"*"}N)          -- conversion{"\n"}(Line{"_"}Count + 10)  -- parenthesized expression {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of expressions:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>15/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Volume                      -- primary{"\n"}not Destroyed               -- factor{"\n"}2{"*"}Line{"_"}Count                -- term{"\n"}-4.0                        -- simple expression{"\n"}-4.0 + A                    -- simple expression{"\n"}B{"*"}{"*"}2 - 4.0{"*"}A{"*"}C              -- simple expression{"\n"}R{"*"}Sin(&#952;){"*"}Cos(&#966;)             -- simple expression{"\n"}Password(1 .. 3) = "Bwv"    -- relation{"\n"}Count in Small{"_"}Int          -- relation{"\n"}Count not in Small{"_"}Int      -- relation{"\n"}Index = 0 or Item{"_"}Hit       -- expression{"\n"}(Cold and Sunny) or Warm    -- expression (parentheses are required){"\n"}A{"*"}{"*"}(B{"*"}{"*"}C)                   -- expression (parentheses are required){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
In Ada 83, <b>out</b> parameters and their nondiscriminant subcomponents are not allowed as <code>primaries</code>. These restrictions are eliminated in Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>15.b</MarginText>
In various contexts throughout the language where Ada 83 syntax rules had <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, the corresponding Ada 95 syntax rule has <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> instead. This reflects the inclusion of modular integer types, which makes the logical operators "<b>and</b>", "<b>or</b>", and "<b>xor</b>" more useful in expressions of an integer type. Requiring parentheses to use these operators in such contexts seemed unnecessary and potentially confusing. Note that the bounds of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> still have to be specified by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>s, since otherwise <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s involving membership tests might be ambiguous. Essentially, the operation ".." is of higher precedence than the logical operators, and hence uses of logical operators still have to be parenthesized when used in a bound of a range. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>15.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0003-1"]} />
Moved <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> from <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a>). This allows the use of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>s in more places.<br />

<MarginText>15.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0176-1"]} />
Added <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>15.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1"]} />
Expanded membership test syntax (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.2">4.5.2</a>). <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>15.f/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0039-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Revised membership syntax to eliminate ambiguities. In some cases, previously ambiguous membership expressions will now have an unambiguous meaning. If an Ada 2012 implementation chose the "wrong" meaning, the expression could silently change meaning. Virtually all such expressions will become illegal because of type mismatches (and thus be incompatible, not inconsistent). However, if the choices are all of a Boolean type, resolution might succeed. For instance, A <b>in</b> B | C <b>and</b> D now always means (A <b>in</b> B | C) <b>and</b> D, but the original Ada 2012 syntax would have allowed it to mean A <b>in</b> B | (C <b>and</b> D). If a compiler allowed the expression and interpreted it as the latter, the meaning of the expression would silently change. We expect this to be extremely rare as membership operations on Boolean types are unlikely (and this can happen only in code written for Ada 2012). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>15.g/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0039-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> The revised membership syntax will require parentheses in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0136">membership_choice_list</a></code>s in some cases where the Ada 2012 grammar did not require them. For instance, A <b>in</b> B <b>in</b> C | D is now illegal. However, such expressions can be interpreted in multiple ways (either A <b>in</b> (B <b>in</b> C) | D or A <b>in</b> (B <b>in</b> C | D) for this example), so using such expressions is likely to be dangerous (another compiler might interpret the expression differently). In addition, all such expressions occur only in Ada 2012 syntax; so they should be rare. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>15.h/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0227-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording so that universal expressions evaluated at run time can raise Constraint{"_"}Error if the value is outside of the range of <i>root{"_"}integer</i> or <i>root{"_"}real</i>. We don't document this as an inconsistency because the rule requires no implementation to change (as Constraint{"_"}Error is not required); it just allows implementations that already raise Constraint{"_"}Error (which is all of them surveyed) to be considered correct.<br />

<MarginText>15.i/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
Added <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code>. It shares the rules about parentheses with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>15.j/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0317-1"]} />
Added the definitions of &ldquo;operative constituent&rdquo; and &ldquo;newly constructed&rdquo; to centralize definitions that are needed for various rules and definitions across the Reference Manual. In particular, <i>operative constituent</i> is often used when we want the semantics or legality to be unchanged by the presence of parens, qualification, or view conversions. Examples are found in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.2">4.3.2</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.2">6.2</a>, and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>. <br />

# 4.5. Operators and Expression Evaluation

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5.mdx

sidebar_position:  35

# 4.5. Operators and Expression Evaluation

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ The language defines the following six categories of operators (given in order of increasing precedence). The corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>s, and only those, can be used as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0199">designator</a></code>s in declarations of functions for user-defined operators. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.6">6.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.6">Overloading of Operators</a>&rdquo;.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>logical{"_"}operator</code><a id="S0142"></a><code> ::= </code>	 <b>and</b> | <b>or</b>  | <b>xor</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>relational{"_"}operator</code><a id="S0143"></a><code> ::= </code>	 =   | /=  | {"<"}   | {"<"}= | {">"} | {">"}=<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>binary{"_"}adding{"_"}operator</code><a id="S0144"></a><code> ::= </code>	 +   | &ndash;   | &<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>unary{"_"}adding{"_"}operator</code><a id="S0145"></a><code> ::= </code>	 +   | &ndash;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>multiplying{"_"}operator</code><a id="S0146"></a><code> ::= </code>	 {"*"}   | /   | <b>mod</b> | <b>rem</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>highest{"_"}precedence{"_"}operator</code><a id="S0147"></a><code> ::= </code>	 {"*"}{"*"}  | <b>abs</b> | <b>not</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Some of the above syntactic categories are not used in other syntax rules. They are just used for classification. The others are used for both classification and parsing. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>For a sequence of operators of the same precedence level, the operators are associated with their operands in textual order from left to right. Parentheses can be used to impose specific associations. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The left-associativity is not directly inherent in the grammar of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4">4.4</a>, though in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.4">1.1.4</a> the definition of the metasymbols <b>{"{"}{"}"}</b> implies left associativity. So this could be seen as redundant, depending on how literally one interprets the definition of the <b>{"{"}{"}"}</b> metasymbols.<br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
See the Implementation Permissions below regarding flexibility in reassociating operators of the same precedence. <br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>For each form of type definition, certain of the above operators are <i>predefined</i>; that is, they are implicitly declared immediately after the type definition. For each such implicit operator declaration, the parameters are called Left and Right for <i>binary</i> operators; the single parameter is called Right for <i>unary</i> operators. [An expression of the form X op Y, where op is a binary operator, is equivalent to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> of the form "op"(X, Y). An expression of the form op Y, where op is a unary operator, is equivalent to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> of the form "op"(Y). The predefined operators and their effects are described in subclauses <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.1">4.5.1</a> through <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.6">4.5.6</a>.] <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>[ The predefined operations on integer types either yield the mathematically correct result or raise the exception Constraint{"_"}Error. For implementations that support the Numerics Annex, the predefined operations on real types yield results whose accuracy is defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/">Annex G</a>, or raise the exception Constraint{"_"}Error. ]<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Predefined operations on real types can &ldquo;silently&rdquo; give wrong results when the Machine{"_"}Overflows attribute is false, and the computation overflows. <br />

<MarginText>10.b/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>For integer types, this is normatively stated in the Dynamic Semantics of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.4">3.5.4</a>. For floating point types, this is normatively stated at the end of the Implementation Requirements of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.1">G.2.1</a>. For fixed point types, this is normatively stated at the end of the Implementation Requirements of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.3">G.2.3</a>. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>The implementation of a predefined operator that delivers a result of an integer or fixed point type may raise Constraint{"_"}Error only if the result is outside the base range of the result type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>The implementation of a predefined operator that delivers a result of a floating point type may raise Constraint{"_"}Error only if the result is outside the safe range of the result type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>An exception is made for exponentiation by a negative exponent in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.6">4.5.6</a>.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>For a sequence of predefined operators of the same precedence level (and in the absence of parentheses imposing a specific association), an implementation may impose any association of the operators with operands so long as the result produced is an allowed result for the left-to-right association, but ignoring the potential for failure of language-defined checks in either the left-to-right or chosen order of association. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that the permission to reassociate the operands in any way subject to producing a result allowed for the left-to-right association is not much help for most floating point operators, since reassociation may introduce significantly different round-off errors, delivering a result that is outside the model interval for the left-to-right association. Similar problems arise for division with integer or fixed point operands.<br />

<MarginText>13.b</MarginText>
Note that this permission does not apply to user-defined operators. <br />

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
NOTE   The two operands of an expression of the form X op Y, where op is a binary operator, are evaluated in an arbitrary order, as for any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4">6.4</a>).<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of precedence:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
not Sunny or Warm    -- same as (not Sunny) or Warm{"\n"}X {">"} 4.0 and Y {">"} 0.0  -- same as (X {">"} 4.0) and (Y {">"} 0.0){"\n"}
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
-4.0{"*"}A{"*"}{"*"}2            -- same as &ndash;(4.0 {"*"} (A{"*"}{"*"}2)){"\n"}abs(1 + A) + B       -- same as (abs (1 + A)) + B{"\n"}Y{"*"}{"*"}(-3)              -- parentheses are necessary{"\n"}A / B {"*"} C            -- same as (A/B){"*"}C{"\n"}A + (B + C)          -- evaluate B + C before adding it to A {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>17.a</MarginText>
We don't give a detailed definition of precedence, since it is all implicit in the syntax rules anyway.<br />

<MarginText>17.b</MarginText>
The permission to reassociate is moved here from RM83-11.6(5), so it is closer to the rules defining operator association. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.1"></a>

## 4.5.1  Logical Operators and Short-circuit Control Forms

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>1_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> consisting of two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>s connected by <b>and then</b> or <b>or else</b> (a <i>short-circuit control form</i>) shall resolve to be of some boolean type; the expected type for both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code>s is that same boolean type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a_4.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule is written this way so that overload resolution treats the two operands symmetrically; the resolution of overloading present in either one can benefit from the resolution of the other. Furthermore, the type expected by context can help. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p>The following logical operators are predefined for every boolean type <i>T</i>, for every modular type <i>T</i>, and for every one-dimensional array type <i>T</i> whose component type is a boolean type: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3_4.5.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "and"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "or" (Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "xor"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.a/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00145-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>3.b/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00145-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For these operators, we are talking about the type without any (interesting) subtype, and not some subtype with a constraint or exclusion. Since it's possible that there is no name for the &ldquo;uninteresting&rdquo; subtype, we denote the type with an italicized <i>T</i>. This applies to the italicized <i>T</i> in many other predefined operators and attributes as well.<br />

<MarginText>3.c/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00145-01"]} />
In many cases, there is a subtype with the correct properties available. The italicized <i>T</i> means: <br />

<MarginText>3.d/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li><i>T</i>'Base, for scalars;<br /></li>
<MarginText>3.e/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
<li>the first subtype of <i>T</i>, for tagged types;<br /></li>
<MarginText>3.f/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
<li>a subtype of the type <i>T</i> without any constraint or null exclusion, in other cases. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>3.g/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
Note that &ldquo;without a constraint&rdquo; is not the same as unconstrained. For instance, a record type with no discriminant part is considered constrained; no subtype of it has a constraint, but the subtype is still constrained.<br />

<MarginText>3.h/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
Thus, the last case often is the same as the first subtype of <i>T</i>, but that isn't the case for constrained array types (where the correct subtype is unconstrained) and for access types with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> (where the correct subtype does not exclude null).<br />

<MarginText>3.i/2_4.5.1</MarginText>
This italicized <i>T</i> is used for defining operators and attributes of the language. The meaning is intended to be as described here. <br />

<MarginText>4_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p>For boolean types, the predefined logical operators <b>and</b>, <b>or</b>, and <b>xor</b> perform the conventional operations of conjunction, inclusive disjunction, and exclusive disjunction, respectively.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p>For modular types, the predefined logical operators are defined on a bit-by-bit basis, using the binary representation of the value of the operands to yield a binary representation for the result, where zero represents False and one represents True. If this result is outside the base range of the type, a final subtraction by the modulus is performed to bring the result into the base range of the type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p>The logical operators on arrays are performed on a component-by-component basis on matching components (as for equality &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.2">4.5.2</a>), using the predefined logical operator for the component type. The bounds of the resulting array are those of the left operand.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p>The short-circuit control forms <b>and then</b> and <b>or else</b> deliver the same result as the corresponding predefined <b>and</b> and <b>or</b> operators for boolean types, except that the left operand is always evaluated first, and the right operand is not evaluated if the value of the left operand determines the result.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p>For the logical operators on arrays, a check is made that for each component of the left operand there is a matching component of the right operand, and vice versa. Also, a check is made that each component of the result belongs to the component subtype. The exception Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if either of the above checks fails. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a_4.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The check against the component subtype is per AI83-00535. <br />

<MarginText>9_4.5.1</MarginText>
NOTE   The conventional meaning of the logical operators is given by the following truth table: <br />

<MarginText>10_4.5.1</MarginText>
	  A	  B	(A <b>and</b> B)	(A <b>or</b> B)	(A <b>xor</b> B)<br /><br />	True  	True  	True  	True  	False<br />	True  	False 	False 	True  	True<br />	False 	True  	False 	True  	True<br />	False 	False 	False 	False 	False<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>11_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of logical operators:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>12_4.5.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Sunny or Warm{"\n"}Filter(1 .. 10) and Filter(15 .. 24)   -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.1">3.6.1</a> {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13_4.5.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of short-circuit control forms:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>14_4.5.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Next{"_"}Car.Owner /= null and then Next{"_"}Car.Owner.Age {">"} 25   -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}N = 0 or else A(N) = Hit{"_"}Value{"\n"}
<a id="Subclause_4.5.2"></a>

</CodeBlock>

## 4.5.2  Relational Operators and Membership Tests

<MarginText>1_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>[ The <i>equality operators</i> = (equals) and /= (not equals) are predefined for nonlimited types. The other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0143">relational_operator</a></code>s are the <i>ordering operators</i> {"<"} (less than), {"<"}= (less than or equal), {">"} (greater than), and {">"}= (greater than or equal). The ordering operators are predefined for scalar types, and for <i>discrete array types</i>, that is, one-dimensional array types whose components are of a discrete type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The equality operators are not defined for <i>every</i> nonlimited type &mdash; see below for the exact rule. <br />

<MarginText>2/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>A <i>membership test</i>, using <b>in</b> or <b>not in</b>, determines whether or not a value belongs to any given subtype or range, is equal to any given value, has a tag that identifies a type that is covered by a given type, or is convertible to and has an accessibility level appropriate for a given access type. Membership tests are allowed for all types.]<br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI05-0158-1"]} />
<p>The <i>tested type</i> of a membership test is determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0136">membership_choice_list</a></code>. Either all <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0136">membership_choice_list</a></code> shall resolve to the same type, which is the tested type; or each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code> shall be of an elementary type, and the tested type shall be covered by each of these elementary types.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.1/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>If the tested type is tagged, then the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> shall resolve to be of a type that is convertible (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>) to the tested type; if untagged, the expected type of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is the tested type. The expected type of a <i>choice{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>, and of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>, is the tested type of the membership operation.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The part of the rule for untagged types is stated in a way that ensures that operands like a string literal are still legal as operands of a membership test.<br />

<MarginText>3.b/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
The significance of &ldquo;is convertible to&rdquo; is that we allow the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> to be of any class-wide type that could be converted to the tested type, not just the one rooted at the tested type. This includes any class-wide type that covers the tested type, along with class-wide interfaces in some cases.<br />

<MarginText>3.c/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1"]} />
The special rule for determining the tested type for elementary types is to allow numeric literals in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0136">membership_choice_list</a></code>s. Without the rule, A <b>in</b> B | 1 would be illegal as B and 1 would have different types (the literal having type <i>universal integer</i>). <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0039-1"]} />
<p>For a membership test, if the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is of a tagged class-wide type, then the tested type shall be (visibly) tagged. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Untagged types covered by the tagged class-wide type are not permitted. Such types can exist if they are descendants of a private type whose full type is tagged. This rule is intended to avoid confusion since such derivatives don't have their &ldquo;own&rdquo; tag, and hence are indistinguishable from one another at run time once converted to a covering class-wide type. <br />

<MarginText>4.1/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1", "AI12-0328-1"]} />
<p>If a membership test includes one or more <i>choice{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>s and the tested type of the membership test is limited, then the tested type of the membership test shall have a visible primitive equality operator; if the tested type of the membership test is nonlimited with a user-defined primitive equality operator that is defined at a point where the type is limited, the tested type shall be a record type or record extension. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.b/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A visible equality operator is required in order to avoid breaking privacy; that is, we don't want to depend on a hidden equality operator.<br />

<MarginText>4.c/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0328-1"]} />
We make the membership test on the nonlimited view of a type illegal if it would use a different equality operator than what would be used for a limited view of the same type (and such a limited view is known to exist). <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>The result type of a membership test is the predefined type Boolean.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>The equality operators are predefined for every specific type <i>T</i> that is not limited, and not an anonymous access type, with the following specifications: <br /></p>

<MarginText>7_4.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "=" (Left, Right : T) return Boolean{"\n"}function "/="(Left, Right : T) return Boolean{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.1/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<p>The following additional equality operators for the <i>universal{"_"}access</i> type are declared in package Standard for use with anonymous access types: <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.2/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "=" (Left, Right : universal{"_"}access) return Boolean{"\n"}function "/="(Left, Right : universal{"_"}access) return Boolean{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>The ordering operators are predefined for every specific scalar type <i>T</i>, and for every discrete array type <i>T</i>, with the following specifications: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9_4.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"<"}" (Left, Right : T) return Boolean{"\n"}function "{"<"}="(Left, Right : T) return Boolean{"\n"}function "{">"}" (Left, Right : T) return Boolean{"\n"}function "{">"}="(Left, Right : T) return Boolean{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>9.1/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00420-01"]} />
<p>At least one of the operands of an equality operator for <i>universal{"_"}access</i> shall be of a specific anonymous access type. Unless the predefined equality operator is identified using an expanded name with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> denoting the package Standard, neither operand shall be of an access-to-object type whose designated type is <i>D</i> or <i>D</i>'Class, where <i>D</i> has a user-defined primitive equality operator such that: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.2/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>its result type is Boolean;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.3/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0020-1"]} />
<li>it is declared immediately within the same declaration list as <i>D</i> or any partial or incomplete view of <i>D</i>; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.4/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>at least one of its operands is an access parameter with designated type <i>D</i>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The first sentence prevents compatibility problems by ensuring that these operators are not used for named access types. Also, universal access types do not count for the purposes of this rule. Otherwise, equality expressions like (X = <b>null</b>) would be ambiguous for normal access types.<br />

<MarginText>9.b/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
The rest of the rule makes it possible to call (including a dispatching call) user-defined "=" operators for anonymous access-to-object types (they'd be hidden otherwise), and to write user-defined "=" operations for anonymous access types (by making it possible to see the universal operator using the Standard prefix). <br />

<MarginText>9.c/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We don't need a similar rule for anonymous access-to-subprogram types because they can't be primitive for any type. Note that any nonprimitive user-defined equality operators still are hidden by the universal operators; they'll have to be called with a package prefix, but they are likely to be very uncommon. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>9.5/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<p>At least one of the operands of the equality operators for <i>universal{"_"}access</i> shall be of type <i>universal{"_"}access</i>, or both shall be of access-to-object types, or both shall be of access-to-subprogram types. Further: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.6/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>When both are of access-to-object types, the designated types shall be the same or one shall cover the other, and if the designated types are elementary or array types, then the designated subtypes shall statically match;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.7/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>When both are of access-to-subprogram types, the designated profiles shall be subtype conformant. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.d/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We don't want to allow completely arbitrary comparisons, as we don't want to insist that all access types are represented in ways that are convertible to one another. For instance, a compiler could use completely separate address spaces or incompatible representations. Instead, we allow compares if there exists an access parameter to which both operands could be converted. Since the user could write such an subprogram, and any reasonable meaning for "=" would allow using it in such a subprogram, this doesn't impose any further restrictions on Ada implementations. <br />

<MarginText>9.8/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1", "AI12-0101-1", "AI12-0352-1"]} />
<p>If the profile of an explicitly declared primitive equality operator of an untagged record type is type conformant with that of the corresponding predefined equality operator, the declaration shall occur before the type is frozen. In addition, no type shall have been derived from the untagged record type before the declaration of the primitive equality operator. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), this rule applies also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>For discrete types, the predefined relational operators are defined in terms of corresponding mathematical operations on the position numbers of the values of the operands.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>For real types, the predefined relational operators are defined in terms of the corresponding mathematical operations on the values of the operands, subject to the accuracy of the type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For floating point types, the results of comparing <i>nearly</i> equal values depends on the accuracy of the implementation (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.1">G.2.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.1">Model of Floating Point Arithmetic</a>&rdquo; for implementations that support the Numerics Annex). <br />

<MarginText>11.b_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>On a machine with signed zeros, if the generated code generates both plus zero and minus zero, plus and minus zero must be equal by the predefined equality operators. <br />

<MarginText>12_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>Two access-to-object values are equal if they designate the same object, or if both are equal to the null value of the access type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>Two access-to-subprogram values are equal if they are the result of the same evaluation of an Access <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>, or if both are equal to the null value of the access type. Two access-to-subprogram values are unequal if they designate different subprograms. [It is unspecified whether two access values that designate the same subprogram but are the result of distinct evaluations of Access <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>s are equal or unequal.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This allows each Access <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> for a subprogram to designate a distinct &ldquo;wrapper&rdquo; subprogram if necessary to support an indirect call. <br />

<MarginText>14/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
<p>For a type extension, predefined equality is defined in terms of the primitive [(possibly user-defined)] equals operator for the parent type and for any components that have a record type in the extension part, and predefined equality for any other components not inherited from the parent type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Two values of a type extension are not equal if there is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> in the extension part and the two values have different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0072">variant</a></code>s present. This is a ramification of the requirement that a discriminant governing such a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code> has to be a &ldquo;new&rdquo; discriminant, and so has to be equal in the two values for the values to be equal. Note that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>s in the parent part need not match if the primitive equals operator for the parent type considers them equal.<br />

<MarginText>14.b/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00349-01"]} />
The full type extension's operation is used for a private extension. This follows as only full types have parent types; the type specified in a private extension is an ancestor, but not necessarily the parent type. For instance, in: <br />
