<MarginText>14.c/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Pak1;{"\n"}package Pak2 is{"\n"}   type Typ3 is new Pak1.Typ1 with private;{"\n"}private{"\n"}   type Typ3 is new Pak1.Typ2 with null record;{"\n"}end Pak2;{"\n"}  {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14.d/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
the parent type is Pak1.Typ2, not Pak1.Typ1, and the equality operator of Pak1.Typ2 is used to create predefined equality for Typ3. <br />

<MarginText>15/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1", "AI12-0328-1"]} />
<p>For a private type, if its full type is a record type or a record extension, predefined equality is defined in terms of the primitive equals operator of the full type; otherwise, predefined equality for the private type is that of its full type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>For other composite types, the predefined equality operators [(and certain other predefined operations on composite types &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.1">4.5.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>)] are defined in terms of the corresponding operation on <i>matching components</i>, defined as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>17_4.5.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For two composite objects or values of the same non-array type, matching components are those that correspond to the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant_specification</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>18_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>For two one-dimensional arrays of the same type, matching components are those (if any) whose index values match in the following sense: the lower bounds of the index ranges are defined to match, and the successors of matching indices are defined to match;<br /></li>
<MarginText>19_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>For two multidimensional arrays of the same type, matching components are those whose index values match in successive index positions. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>The analogous definitions apply if the types of the two objects or values are convertible, rather than being the same. <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Ada 83 seems to omit this part of the definition, though it is used in array type conversions. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>. <br />

<MarginText>21_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>Given the above definition of matching components, the result of the predefined equals operator for composite types (other than for those composite types covered earlier) is defined as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>22_4.5.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If there are no components, the result is defined to be True;<br /></li>
<MarginText>23_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>If there are unmatched components, the result is defined to be False;<br /></li>
<MarginText>24/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
<li>Otherwise, the result is defined in terms of the primitive equals operator for any matching components that are records, and the predefined equals for any other matching components. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.a/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This asymmetry between components with and without a record type is necessary to preserve most upward compatibility and corresponds with the corresponding situation with generics, where the predefined operations &ldquo;reemerge&rdquo; in a generic for non-record types, but do not for record types. Also, only tagged types support user-defined assignment (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>), so only tagged types can fully handle levels of indirection in the implementation of the type. For untagged types, one reason for a user-defined equals operator might be to allow values with different bounds or discriminants to compare equal in certain cases. When such values are matching components, the bounds or discriminants will necessarily match anyway if the discriminants of the enclosing values match. <br />

<MarginText>24.b_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Two null arrays of the same type are always equal; two null records of the same type are always equal.<br />

<MarginText>24.c/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
Note that if a composite object has a component of a floating point type, and the floating point type has both a plus and minus zero, which are considered equal by the predefined equality, then a block compare cannot be used for the predefined composite equality. Of course, with user-defined equals operators for components that are records, a block compare breaks down anyway, so this is not the only special case that requires component-by-component comparisons. On a one's complement machine, a similar situation might occur for integer types, since one's complement machines typically have both a plus and minus (integer) zero. <br />

<MarginText>24.d/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>For a component with an anonymous access type, &ldquo;predefined equality&rdquo; is that defined for the <i>universal{"_"}access</i> type (anonymous access types have no equality operators of their own).<br />

<MarginText>24.e/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
For a component with a record type <i>T</i>, &ldquo;the primitive equals operator&rdquo; is the one with two parameters of <i>T</i> which returns Boolean. We're not talking about some random other primitive function named "=". <br />

<MarginText>24.1/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1", "AI12-0413-1"]} />
<p>If the primitive equals operator for an untagged record type is abstract, then Program{"_"}Error is raised at the point of any call to that abstract subprogram[, implicitly as part of an equality operation on an enclosing composite object, or in an instance of a generic with a formal private type where the actual type is a record type with an abstract "="]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.f/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0413-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>An explicit call to an abstract subprogram is generally illegal. This rule is needed in order to define the effect of a call in an instance of a generic body, or an implicit call such as a call that is part of the predefined equality operation for an enclosing composite type that has a component of an untagged record type that has an abstract primitive equals operator. For tagged types, an abstract primitive equals operator is only allowed for an abstract type, and abstract types cannot be components, so this case does not occur. <br />

<MarginText>24.2/1_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00123-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0016</i>{"}"} For any composite type, the order in which "=" is called for components is unspecified. Furthermore, if the result can be determined before calling "=" on some components, it is unspecified whether "=" is called on those components.<br /></p>

<MarginText>25_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>The predefined "/=" operator gives the complementary result to the predefined "=" operator. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Furthermore, if the user defines an "=" operator that returns Boolean, then a "/=" operator is implicitly declared in terms of the user-defined "=" operator so as to give the complementary result. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.6">6.6</a>. <br />

<MarginText>26/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>For a discrete array type, the predefined ordering operators correspond to <i>lexicographic order</i> using the predefined order relation of the component type: A null array is lexicographically less than any array having at least one component. In the case of nonnull arrays, the left operand is lexicographically less than the right operand if the first component of the left operand is less than that of the right; otherwise, the left operand is lexicographically less than the right operand only if their first components are equal and the tail of the left operand is lexicographically less than that of the right (the <i>tail</i> consists of the remaining components beyond the first and can be null).<br /></p>

<MarginText>26.1/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>An <i>individual membership test</i> is the membership test of a single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a membership test using <b>in</b> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0136">membership_choice_list</a></code> has a single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>, the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code> are evaluated in an arbitrary order; the result is the result of the individual membership test for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27.1/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a membership test using <b>in</b> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0136">membership_choice_list</a></code> has more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>, the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> of the membership test is evaluated first and the result of the operation is equivalent to that of a sequence consisting of an individual membership test on each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code> combined with the short-circuit control form <b>or else</b>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27.a.1/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This equivalence includes the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>s; evaluation stops as soon as an individual choice evaluates to True. <br />

<MarginText>28/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>An individual membership test yields the result True if: <br /></p>

<MarginText>28.1/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1", "AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0039-1", "AI12-0328-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code> is a <i>choice{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, and the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is equal to the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>. If the tested type is a record type or a record extension, or is limited at the point where the membership test occurs, the test uses the primitive equality for the type; otherwise, the test uses predefined equality.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>28.a/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We use the predefined equality operator if the membership test occurs where the type is nonlimited if the type is not a record type or record extension. However, to avoid confusion, cases where a membership test could use different equality operators based on the view are illegal. <br />

<MarginText>28.2/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> and the value of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> belongs to the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>29/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1", "AI12-0071-1"]} />
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>, the tested type is scalar, the value of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> belongs to the range of the named subtype, and the value satisfies the predicates of the named subtype. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>29.a/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The scalar membership test only does a range check and a predicate check. It does not perform any other check, such as whether a value falls in a &ldquo;hole&rdquo; of a &ldquo;holey&rdquo; enumeration type. The Pos attribute function can be used for that purpose.<br />

<MarginText>29.b_4.5.2</MarginText>
Even though Standard.Float is an unconstrained subtype, the test &ldquo;X in Float&rdquo; will still return False (presuming the evaluation of X does not raise Constraint{"_"}Error) when X is outside Float'Range. <br />

<MarginText>30/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1", "AI12-0071-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>, the tested type is not scalar, the value of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> satisfies any constraints of the named subtype, the value satisfies the predicates of the named subtype, and: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>30.1/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>if the type of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is class-wide, the value has a tag that identifies a type covered by the tested type; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>30.a/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0039-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that the tag is not checked if the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is of a specific type. <br />

<MarginText>30.2/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI05-0149-1", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>if the tested type is an access type and the named subtype excludes null, the value of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is not null;<br /></li>
<MarginText>30.3/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0149-1", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
<li>if the tested type is a general access-to-object type, the type of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is convertible to the tested type and its accessibility level is no deeper than that of the tested type; further, if the designated type of the tested type is tagged and the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is nonnull, the tag of the object designated by the value of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is covered by the designated type of the tested type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>30.b/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>In some of these cases, the bulleted checks need to pass before any predicate check is executed. Otherwise, a predicate check could be performed on an object of the wrong type. Consider:<br />

<MarginText>30.c/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Root is tagged null record;{"\n"}type Ext is new Root with record Data : Integer; end record;{"\n"}function Is{"_"}Even (Param : Ext) return Boolean is{"\n"}   (Param.Data mod 2 = 0);{"\n"}subtype Even{"_"}Ext is Ext{"\n"}  with Dynamic{"_"}Predicate ={">"} Is{"_"}Even (Even{"_"}Ext);{"\n"}function F (X : Root'Class) return Boolean is{"\n"}   (X in Even{"_"}Ext);{"\n"}Flag : Boolean := F (Root'(null record));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>30.d/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
If the predicate check is performed before the tag check or regardless of the result of that check, Is{"_"}Even would be called on an object that does not have a Data component. Similar cases can be constructed for general access types. <br />

<MarginText>31/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>Otherwise, the test yields the result False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>32_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p>A membership test using <b>not in</b> gives the complementary result to the corresponding membership test using <b>in</b>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>32.a/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1", "AI12-0039-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b><i>X</i> <b>not in</b> <i>A</i> | <i>B</i> | <i>C</i> is intended to be exactly equivalent to <b>not</b> (<i>X</i> <b>in</b> <i>A</i> | <i>B</i> | <i>C</i>), including the order of evaluation of the <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0137">membership_choice</a></code>s. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>32.1/1_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00123-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0016</i>{"}"} For all nonlimited types declared in language-defined packages, the "=" and "/=" operators of the type shall behave as if they were the predefined equality operators for the purposes of the equality of composite types and generic formal types. <br /></p>

<MarginText>32.a.1/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00123-01", "AI05-0123-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If any language-defined types are implemented with a user-defined "=" operator, then either the full type must be a record type, or the compiler must use &ldquo;magic&rdquo; to implement equality for this type. A normal user-defined "=" operator for a non-record type does <i>not</i> meet this requirement. <br />

<MarginText>33/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>34_4.5.2</MarginText>
NOTE   If a composite type has components that depend on discriminants, two values of this type have matching components if and only if their discriminants are equal. Two nonnull arrays have matching components if and only if the length of each dimension is the same for both. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>35_4.5.2</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of expressions involving relational operators and membership tests:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>36_4.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X /= Y{"\n"}
<MarginText>37/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1", "AI12-0425-1"]} />
A{"_"}String = "A"                        -- True (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>){"\n"}"" {"<"} A{"_"}String and A{"_"}String {"<"} "Aa"     -- True{"\n"}A{"_"}String {"<"} "Bb" and A{"_"}String {"<"} "A  "  -- True{"\n"}
<MarginText>38/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
My{"_"}Car = null        -- True if My{"_"}Car has been set to null (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>){"\n"}My{"_"}Car = Your{"_"}Car           -- True if we both share the same car{"\n"}My{"_"}Car.all = Your{"_"}Car.all   -- True if the two cars are identical{"\n"}
<MarginText>39/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1"]} />
N not in 1 .. 10            -- range membership test{"\n"}Today in Mon .. Fri         -- range membership test{"\n"}Today in Weekday            -- subtype membership test (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.1">3.5.1</a>){"\n"}Card in Clubs | Spades      -- list membership test (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.1">3.5.1</a>){"\n"}Archive in Disk{"_"}Unit        -- subtype membership test (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>){"\n"}Tree.all in Addition'Class  -- class membership test (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a>){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>39.a_4.5.2</MarginText>
Membership tests can be used to test the tag of a class-wide value.<br />

<MarginText>39.b_4.5.2</MarginText>
Predefined equality for a composite type is defined in terms of the primitive equals operator for tagged components or the parent part. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>39.c_4.5.2</MarginText>
The term &ldquo;membership test&rdquo; refers to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0135">relation</a></code> "X in S" rather to simply the reserved word <b>in</b> or <b>not in</b>.<br />

<MarginText>39.d_4.5.2</MarginText>
We use the term &ldquo;equality operator&rdquo; to refer to both the = (equals) and /= (not equals) operators. Ada 83 referred to = as <i>the</i> equality operator, and /= as the inequality operator. The new wording is more consistent with the ISO 10646 name for "=" (equals sign) and provides a category similar to &ldquo;ordering operator&rdquo; to refer to both = and /=.<br />

<MarginText>39.e_4.5.2</MarginText>
We have changed the term &ldquo;catenate&rdquo; to &ldquo;concatenate&rdquo;. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>39.f/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00420-01"]} />
The <i>universal{"_"}access</i> equality operators are new. They provide equality operations (most importantly, testing against <b>null</b>) for anonymous access types. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>39.g/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00123-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0016</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Wording was added to clarify that the order of calls (and whether the calls are made at all) on "=" for components is unspecified. Also clarified that "=" must compose properly for language-defined types.<br />

<MarginText>39.h/2_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Memberships were adjusted to allow interfaces which don't cover the tested type, in order to be consistent with type conversions. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2005

<MarginText>39.i/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
User-defined untagged record equality is now defined to compose and be used in generics. Any code which assumes that the predefined equality reemerges in generics and in predefined equals for composite types could fail. However, it is much more likely that this change will fix bugs, as the behavior that would be expected (the user-defined "=" is used) will be true in more cases.<br />

<MarginText>39.j/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
If a composite type contains a component of an untagged record type with an abstract equality operation, calling "=" on the composite type will raise Program{"_"}Error, while in the past a result will be returned using the predefined equality. This is quite possible in ASIS programs; it will detect a bug in such programs but of course the programs will need to be fixed before they will work. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>39.k/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0123-1"]} />
Late and hidden overriding of equality for untagged record types is now prohibited. This is necessary to make composition of equality predictable. It should always be possible to move the overriding to an earlier spot where it will be legal. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>39.l/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0149-1"]} />
Membership tests for valid accessibility levels and tag coverage by the designated type for general access types are new.<br />

<MarginText>39.m/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
Membership tests now include a predicate check.<br />

<MarginText>39.n/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0158-1"]} />
Membership tests now allow multiple choices. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>39.o/3_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0020-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Wording was added to clarify that <i>universal{"_"}access</i> "=" does not apply if an appropriate operator is declared for a partial or incomplete view of the designated type. Otherwise, adding a partial or incomplete view could make some "=" operators ambiguous. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>39.p/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0101-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Removed the incompatible rule preventing the declaration of "=" in the private part of a package specification for an untagged record type that completes a private type. Any code that calls the predefined "=" on the private type will now execute the body for the redefined "=" instead for the predefined "=". Eliminating the rule eliminates an unnecessary incompatibility (especially for programs that never call the predefined "="). Moreover, (like the composition of untagged record "=" in Ada 2012) this is more likely to fix bugs than cause them (who defines an "=" with a presumably different result and does not want clients to use it?). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>39.q/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0328-1"]} />
A membership test is now illegal if all of the following are True: <br />

<MarginText>39.r/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The membership test has one or more <i>choice{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>s;<br /></li>
<MarginText>39.s/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>The membership test occurs in a place where the tested type is nonlimited;<br /></li>
<MarginText>39.t/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>The tested type has a limited view with a primitive "=" operator;<br /></li>
<MarginText>39.u/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<li>The full type of the tested type is not a record type or a record extension. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>39.v/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
In such a case, the limited and nonlimited views would use different equality operators, which would be confusing and would cause various semantic difficulties. We believe such cases to be quite rare, especially as such membership tests are new to Ada 2012. The workaround is to replace such memberships with equality tests (assuming that the primitive "=" is intended; the predefined "=" is hidden in such cases and an extra type is needed to make it accessible). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>39.w/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0039-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Reworded membership tests to use the syntax items <i>tested{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> and <i>choice{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>. This was necessary to eliminate wording ambiguities introduced when the grammar was corrected to eliminate syntax ambiguities. (Both of the above are now <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>s, so merely talking about a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is insufficient.)<br />

<MarginText>39.x/4_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0071-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Updated wording of the membership tests to use the new term "satisfies the predicates" (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>).<br />

<MarginText>39.y/5_4.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0413-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified that a call to an abstract equality in an instance body raises Program{"_"}Error. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.3"></a>

## 4.5.3  Binary Adding Operators

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_4.5.3</MarginText>
<p>The binary adding operators + (addition) and &ndash; (subtraction) are predefined for every specific numeric type <i>T</i> with their conventional meaning. They have the following specifications: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_4.5.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "+"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "-"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_4.5.3</MarginText>
<p>The concatenation operators & are predefined for every nonlimited, one-dimensional array type <i>T</i> with component type <i>C</i>. They have the following specifications: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4_4.5.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "&"(Left : T; Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "&"(Left : T; Right : C) return T{"\n"}function "&"(Left : C; Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "&"(Left : C; Right : C) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5_4.5.3</MarginText>
<p>For the evaluation of a concatenation with result type <i>T</i>, if both operands are of type <i>T</i>, the result of the concatenation is a one-dimensional array whose length is the sum of the lengths of its operands, and whose components comprise the components of the left operand followed by the components of the right operand. If the left operand is a null array, the result of the concatenation is the right operand. Otherwise, the lower bound of the result is determined as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6_4.5.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the ultimate ancestor of the array type was defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0054">constrained_array_definition</a></code>, then the lower bound of the result is that of the index subtype; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a_4.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule avoids Constraint{"_"}Error when using concatenation on an array type whose first subtype is constrained. <br />

<MarginText>7_4.5.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the ultimate ancestor of the array type was defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0052">unconstrained_array_definition</a></code>, then the lower bound of the result is that of the left operand. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8_4.5.3</MarginText>
<p>[The upper bound is determined by the lower bound and the length.] A check is made that the upper bound of the result of the concatenation belongs to the range of the index subtype, unless the result is a null array. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9_4.5.3</MarginText>
<p>If either operand is of the component type <i>C</i>, the result of the concatenation is given by the above rules, using in place of such an operand an array having this operand as its only component (converted to the component subtype) and having the lower bound of the index subtype of the array type as its lower bound. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a_4.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The conversion might raise Constraint{"_"}Error. The conversion provides &ldquo;sliding&rdquo; for the component in the case of an array-of-arrays, consistent with the normal Ada 95 rules that allow sliding during parameter passing. <br />

<MarginText>10_4.5.3</MarginText>
<p>The result of a concatenation is defined in terms of an assignment to an anonymous object, as for any function call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a_4.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This implies that value adjustment is performed as appropriate &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>. We don't bother saying this for other predefined operators, even though they are all function calls, because this is the only one where it matters. It is the only one that can return a value having controlled parts. <br />

<MarginText>11_4.5.3</MarginText>
NOTE   As for all predefined operators on modular types, the binary adding operators + and &ndash; on modular types include a final reduction modulo the modulus if the result is outside the base range of the type. <br />

<MarginText>11.a_4.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>A full "modulus" operation need not be performed after addition or subtraction of modular types. For binary moduli, a simple mask is sufficient. For nonbinary moduli, a check after addition to see if the value is greater than the high bound of the base range can be followed by a conditional subtraction of the modulus. Conversely, a check after subtraction to see if a "borrow" was performed can be followed by a conditional addition of the modulus. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>12_4.5.3</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of expressions involving binary adding operators:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>13_4.5.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Z + 0.1     -- Z has to be of a real type {"\n"}
<MarginText>14_4.5.3</MarginText>
"A" & "BCD" -- concatenation of two string literals{"\n"}'A' & "BCD" -- concatenation of a character literal and a string literal{"\n"}'A' & 'A'   -- concatenation of two character literals {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 83

<MarginText>14.a_4.5.3</MarginText>
The lower bound of the result of concatenation, for a type whose first subtype is constrained, is now that of the index subtype. This is inconsistent with Ada 83, but generally only for Ada 83 programs that raise Constraint{"_"}Error. For example, the concatenation operator in <br />

<MarginText>14.b_4.5.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X : array(1..10) of Integer;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}X := X(6..10) & X(1..5);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14.c_4.5.3</MarginText>
would raise Constraint{"_"}Error in Ada 83 (because the bounds of the result of the concatenation would be 6..15, which is outside of 1..10), but would succeed and swap the halves of X (as expected) in Ada 95. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>14.d_4.5.3</MarginText>
Concatenation is now useful for array types whose first subtype is constrained. When the result type of a concatenation is such an array type, Constraint{"_"}Error is avoided by effectively first sliding the left operand (if nonnull) so that its lower bound is that of the index subtype. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.4"></a>

## 4.5.4  Unary Adding Operators

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_4.5.4</MarginText>
<p>The unary adding operators + (identity) and &ndash; (negation) are predefined for every specific numeric type <i>T</i> with their conventional meaning. They have the following specifications: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_4.5.4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "+"(Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "-"(Right : T) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_4.5.4</MarginText>
NOTE   For modular integer types, the unary adding operator &ndash;, when given a nonzero operand, returns the result of subtracting the value of the operand from the modulus; for a zero operand, the result is zero. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.5"></a>

## 4.5.5  Multiplying Operators

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>The multiplying operators {"*"} (multiplication), / (division), <b>mod</b> (modulus), and <b>rem</b> (remainder) are predefined for every specific integer type <i>T</i>: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"*"}"  (Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "/"  (Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "mod"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "rem"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>Signed integer multiplication has its conventional meaning.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>Signed integer division and remainder are defined by the relation: <br /></p>

<MarginText>5_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
A = (A/B){"*"}B + (A rem B){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>where (A <b>rem</b> B) has the sign of A and an absolute value less than the absolute value of B. Signed integer division satisfies the identity: <br /></p>

<MarginText>7_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
(-A)/B = -(A/B) = A/(-B){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8/3_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0260-1"]} />
<p>The signed integer modulus operator is defined such that the result of A <b>mod</b> B is either zero, or has the sign of B and an absolute value less than the absolute value of B; in addition, for some signed integer value N, this result satisfies the relation: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
A = B{"*"}N + (A mod B){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>The multiplying operators on modular types are defined in terms of the corresponding signed integer operators[, followed by a reduction modulo the modulus if the result is outside the base range of the type] [(which is only possible for the "{"*"}" operator)]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a_4.5.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The above identity satisfied by signed integer division is not satisfied by modular division because of the difference in effect of negation. <br />

<MarginText>11_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>Multiplication and division operators are predefined for every specific floating point type <i>T</i>: <br /></p>

<MarginText>12_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"*"}"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "/"(Left, Right : T) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>The following multiplication and division operators, with an operand of the predefined type Integer, are predefined for every specific fixed point type <i>T</i>: <br /></p>

<MarginText>14_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"*"}"(Left : T; Right : Integer) return T{"\n"}function "{"*"}"(Left : Integer; Right : T) return T{"\n"}function "/"(Left : T; Right : Integer) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>15_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>[All of the above multiplying operators are usable with an operand of an appropriate universal numeric type.] The following additional multiplying operators for <i>root{"_"}real</i> are predefined[, and are usable when both operands are of an appropriate universal or root numeric type, and the result is allowed to be of type <i>root{"_"}real</i>, as in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0034">number_declaration</a></code>]: <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a_4.5.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>These operators are analogous to the multiplying operators involving fixed or floating point types where <i>root{"_"}real</i> substitutes for the fixed or floating point type, and <i>root{"_"}integer</i> substitutes for Integer. Only values of the corresponding universal numeric types are implicitly convertible to these root numeric types, so these operators are really restricted to use with operands of a universal type, or the specified root numeric types. <br />

<MarginText>16_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"*"}"(Left, Right : root{"_"}real) return root{"_"}real{"\n"}function "/"(Left, Right : root{"_"}real) return root{"_"}real{"\n"}
<MarginText>17_4.5.5</MarginText>
function "{"*"}"(Left : root{"_"}real; Right : root{"_"}integer) return root{"_"}real{"\n"}function "{"*"}"(Left : root{"_"}integer; Right : root{"_"}real) return root{"_"}real{"\n"}function "/"(Left : root{"_"}real; Right : root{"_"}integer) return root{"_"}real{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>18_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>Multiplication and division between any two fixed point types are provided by the following two predefined operators: <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a/3_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b><i>Universal{"_"}fixed</i> is the universal type for the class of fixed point types, meaning that these operators take operands of any fixed point type (not necessarily the same) and return a result that is implicitly (or explicitly) convertible to any fixed point type. <br />

<MarginText>19_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"*"}"(Left, Right : universal{"_"}fixed) return universal{"_"}fixed{"\n"}function "/"(Left, Right : universal{"_"}fixed) return universal{"_"}fixed{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>19.1/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00364-01", "AI95-00420-01"]} />
<p>The above two fixed-fixed multiplying operators shall not be used in a context where the expected type for the result is itself <i>universal{"_"}fixed</i> [&mdash; the context has to identify some other numeric type to which the result is to be converted, either explicitly or implicitly]. Unless the predefined universal operator is identified using an expanded name with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> denoting the package Standard, an explicit conversion is required on the result when using the above fixed-fixed multiplication operator if either operand is of a type having a user-defined primitive multiplication operator such that: <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.2/3_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0020-1", "AI05-0209-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>it is declared immediately within the same declaration list as the type or any partial or incomplete view thereof; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>19.3/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<li>both of its formal parameters are of a fixed-point type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>19.4/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00364-01", "AI95-00420-01"]} />
<p>A corresponding requirement applies to the universal fixed-fixed division operator.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The <i>small</i> of <i>universal{"_"}fixed</i> is infinitesimal; no loss of precision is permitted. However, fixed-fixed division is impractical to implement when an exact result is required, and multiplication will sometimes result in unanticipated overflows in such circumstances, so we require an explicit conversion to be inserted in expressions like A {"*"} B {"*"} C if A, B, and C are each of some fixed point type.<br />

<MarginText>19.b/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
On the other hand, X := A {"*"} B; is permitted by this rule, even if X, A, and B are all of different fixed point types, since the expected type for the result of the multiplication is the type of X, which is necessarily not <i>universal{"_"}fixed</i>.<br />

<MarginText>19.c/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00364-01", "AI95-00420-01"]} />
We have made these into Name Resolution rules to ensure that user-defined primitive fixed-fixed operators are not made unusable due to the presence of these universal fixed-fixed operators. But we do allow these operators to be used if prefixed by package Standard, so that they can be used in the definitions of user-defined operators. <br />

<p><i>Paragraph 20 was deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>21_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>The multiplication and division operators for real types have their conventional meaning. [For floating point types, the accuracy of the result is determined by the precision of the result type. For decimal fixed point types, the result is truncated toward zero if the mathematical result is between two multiples of the <i>small</i> of the specific result type (possibly determined by context); for ordinary fixed point types, if the mathematical result is between two multiples of the <i>small</i>, it is unspecified which of the two is the result. ]<br /></p>

<MarginText>22_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p>The exception Constraint{"_"}Error is raised by integer division, <b>rem</b>, and <b>mod</b> if the right operand is zero. [Similarly, for a real type <i>T</i> with <i>T'</i>Machine{"_"}Overflows True, division by zero raises Constraint{"_"}Error.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>23_4.5.5</MarginText>
NOTE 1   For positive A and B, A/B is the quotient and A <b>rem</b> B is the remainder when A is divided by B. The following relations are satisfied by the rem operator: <br />

<MarginText>24_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
     A  rem (-B) =   A rem B{"\n"}   (-A) rem   B  = -(A rem B){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>25_4.5.5</MarginText>
NOTE 2   For any signed integer K, the following identity holds: <br />

<MarginText>26_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   A mod B   =   (A + K{"*"}B) mod B{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>27_4.5.5</MarginText>
The relations between signed integer division, remainder, and modulus are illustrated by the following table: <br />

<MarginText>28_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   A      B   A/B   A rem B  A mod B     A     B    A/B   A rem B   A mod B{"\n"}
<MarginText>29_4.5.5</MarginText>
   10     5    2       0        0       -10    5    -2       0         0{"\n"}   11     5    2       1        1       -11    5    -2      -1         4{"\n"}   12     5    2       2        2       -12    5    -2      -2         3{"\n"}   13     5    2       3        3       -13    5    -2      -3         2{"\n"}   14     5    2       4        4       -14    5    -2      -4         1{"\n"}
<MarginText>30_4.5.5</MarginText>
   A      B   A/B   A rem B  A mod B     A     B    A/B   A rem B   A mod B{"\n"}{"\n"}   10    -5   -2       0        0       -10   -5     2       0         0{"\n"}   11    -5   -2       1       -4       -11   -5     2      -1        -1{"\n"}   12    -5   -2       2       -3       -12   -5     2      -2        -2{"\n"}   13    -5   -2       3       -2       -13   -5     2      -3        -3{"\n"}   14    -5   -2       4       -1       -14   -5     2      -4        -4{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Examples

<MarginText>31_4.5.5</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of expressions involving multiplying operators:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>32_4.5.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
I : Integer := 1;{"\n"}J : Integer := 2;{"\n"}K : Integer := 3;{"\n"}
<MarginText>33_4.5.5</MarginText>
X : Real := 1.0;                      -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.7">3.5.7</a>{"\n"}Y : Real := 2.0;{"\n"}
<MarginText>34_4.5.5</MarginText>
F : Fraction := 0.25;                 -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.9">3.5.9</a>{"\n"}G : Fraction := 0.5;{"\n"}
<MarginText>35_4.5.5</MarginText>
Expression  	Value  	Result Type{"\n"}{"\n"}I{"*"}J            	2      	same as I and J, that is, Integer{"\n"}K/J            	1      	same as K and J, that is, Integer{"\n"}K mod J  	1      	same as K and J, that is, Integer{"\n"}{"\n"}X/Y            	0.5    	same as X and Y, that is, Real{"\n"}F/2            	0.125  	same as F, that is, Fraction{"\n"}{"\n"}3{"*"}F            	0.75   	same as F, that is, Fraction{"\n"}0.75{"*"}G         	0.375  	universal{"_"}fixed, implicitly convertible{"\n"}               	       	to any fixed point type{"\n"}Fraction(F{"*"}G)  	0.125  	Fraction, as stated by the conversion{"\n"}Real(J){"*"}Y      	4.0    	Real, the type of both operands after{"\n"}               	       	conversion of J{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>35.a.1/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00364-01", "AI95-00420-01"]} />
The universal fixed-fixed multiplying operators are now directly available (see below). Any attempt to use user-defined fixed-fixed multiplying operators will be ambiguous with the universal ones. The only way to use the user-defined operators is to fully qualify them in a prefix call. This problem was not documented during the design of Ada 95, and has been mitigated by Ada 2005. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>35.a_4.5.5</MarginText>
Explicit conversion of the result of multiplying or dividing two fixed point numbers is no longer required, provided the context uniquely determines some specific fixed point result type. This is to improve support for decimal fixed point, where requiring explicit conversion on every fixed-fixed multiply or divide was felt to be inappropriate.<br />

<MarginText>35.b_4.5.5</MarginText>
The type <i>universal{"_"}fixed</i> is covered by <i>universal{"_"}real</i>, so real literals and fixed point operands may be multiplied or divided directly, without any explicit conversions required. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>35.c_4.5.5</MarginText>
We have used the normal syntax for function definition rather than a tabular format. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>35.d/2_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00364-01"]} />
We have changed the resolution rules for the universal fixed-fixed multiplying operators to remove the incompatibility with Ada 83 discussed above. The solution is to hide the universal operators in some circumstances. As a result, some legal Ada 95 programs will require the insertion of an explicit conversion around a fixed-fixed multiply operator. This change is likely to catch as many bugs as it causes, since it is unlikely that the user wanted to use predefined operators when they had defined user-defined versions. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>35.e/3_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0020-1", "AI05-0209-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Wording was added to clarify that <i>universal{"_"}fixed</i> "{"*"}" and "/" does not apply if an appropriate operator is declared for a partial (or incomplete) view of the designated type. Otherwise, adding a partial (or incomplete) view could make some "{"*"}" and "/" operators ambiguous.<br />

<MarginText>35.f/3_4.5.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0260-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The wording for the <b>mod</b> operator was corrected so that a result of 0 does not have to have "the sign of B" (which is impossible if B is negative). <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.6"></a>

## 4.5.6  Highest Precedence Operators

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_4.5.6</MarginText>
<p>The highest precedence unary operator <b>abs</b> (absolute value) is predefined for every specific numeric type <i>T</i>, with the following specification: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_4.5.6</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "abs"(Right : T) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_4.5.6</MarginText>
<p>The highest precedence unary operator <b>not</b> (logical negation) is predefined for every boolean type <i>T</i>, every modular type <i>T</i>, and for every one-dimensional array type <i>T</i> whose components are of a boolean type, with the following specification: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4_4.5.6</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "not"(Right : T) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5_4.5.6</MarginText>
<p>The result of the operator <b>not</b> for a modular type is defined as the difference between the high bound of the base range of the type and the value of the operand. [For a binary modulus, this corresponds to a bit-wise complement of the binary representation of the value of the operand.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>6_4.5.6</MarginText>
<p>The operator <b>not</b> that applies to a one-dimensional array of boolean components yields a one-dimensional boolean array with the same bounds; each component of the result is obtained by logical negation of the corresponding component of the operand (that is, the component that has the same index value). A check is made that each component of the result belongs to the component subtype; the exception Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a_4.5.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The check against the component subtype is per AI83-00535. <br />

<MarginText>7_4.5.6</MarginText>
<p>The highest precedence <i>exponentiation</i> operator {"*"}{"*"} is predefined for every specific integer type <i>T</i> with the following specification: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8_4.5.6</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"*"}{"*"}"(Left : T; Right : Natural) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9_4.5.6</MarginText>
<p>Exponentiation is also predefined for every specific floating point type as well as <i>root{"_"}real</i>, with the following specification (where <i>T</i> is <i>root{"_"}real</i> or the floating point type): <br /></p>

<MarginText>10_4.5.6</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "{"*"}{"*"}"(Left : T; Right : Integer'Base) return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>11/3_4.5.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0088-1"]} />
<p>The right operand of an exponentiation is the <i>exponent</i>. The value of X{"*"}{"*"}N with the value of the exponent N positive is the same as the value of X{"*"}X{"*"}...X (with N&ndash;1 multiplications) except that the multiplications are associated in an arbitrary order. With N equal to zero, the result is one. With the value of N negative [(only defined for a floating point operand)], the result is the reciprocal of the result using the absolute value of N as the exponent. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a_4.5.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The language does not specify the order of association of the multiplications inherent in an exponentiation. For a floating point type, the accuracy of the result might depend on the particular association order chosen. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>12_4.5.6</MarginText>
<p>The implementation of exponentiation for the case of a negative exponent is allowed to raise Constraint{"_"}Error if the intermediate result of the repeated multiplications is outside the safe range of the type, even though the final result (after taking the reciprocal) would not be. (The best machine approximation to the final result in this case would generally be 0.0.) <br /></p>

<MarginText>13_4.5.6</MarginText>
NOTE   As implied by the specification given above for exponentiation of an integer type, a check is made that the exponent is not negative. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 83

<MarginText>13.a.1/1_4.5.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00018-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0100</i>{"}"} The definition of "{"*"}{"*"}" allows arbitrary association of the multiplications which make up the result. Ada 83 required left-to-right associations (confirmed by AI83-00137). Thus it is possible that "{"*"}{"*"}" would provide a slightly different (and more potentially accurate) answer in Ada 95 than in the same Ada 83 program. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>13.a_4.5.6</MarginText>
We now show the specification for "{"*"}{"*"}" for integer types with a parameter subtype of Natural rather than Integer for the exponent. This reflects the fact that Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if a negative value is provided for the exponent. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>13.b/3_4.5.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0088-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The equivalence definition for "{"*"}{"*"}" was corrected so that it does not imply that the operands are evaluated multiple times. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.7"></a>

## 4.5.7  Conditional Expressions

<MarginText>1/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0188-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> selects for evaluation at most one of the enclosed <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s, depending on a decision among the alternatives. One kind of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code>, which selects for evaluation a <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> depending on the value of one or more corresponding conditions. The other kind of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>, which selects for evaluation one of a number of alternative <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s; the chosen alternative is determined by the value of a <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
As previously noted, there are two kinds of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>s. Whenever possible, we have written the rules in terms of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s to avoid duplication.<br />

<MarginText>1.b/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
The rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s have been designed as much as possible to work similarly to a parenthesized expression. The intent is that as much as possible, wherever a parenthesized expression would be allowed, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> would be allowed, and it should work the same way. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>conditional{"_"}expression</code><a id="S0148"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0188-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>if{"_"}expression</code><a id="S0149"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>if</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> <b>then</b> <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />   {"{"}<b>elsif</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> <b>then</b> <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>{"}"}<br />   [<b>else</b> <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>condition</code><a id="S0150"></a><code> ::= </code><i>boolean{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>case{"_"}expression</code><a id="S0151"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>case</b> <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> <b>is</b><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0152">case_expression_alternative</a></code> {"{"},<br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0152">case_expression_alternative</a></code>{"}"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>case{"_"}expression{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0152"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>when</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> ={">"}<br />        <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">Wherever the Syntax Rules allow an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> may be used in place of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, so long as it is immediately surrounded by parentheses.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> appears only as a primary that is parenthesized. The above rule allows it to additionally be used in other contexts where it would be directly surrounded by parentheses.<br />

<MarginText>7.b/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
The grammar makes the following directly legal:<br />

<MarginText>7.c/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
A := (if X then Y else Z); -- parentheses required{"\n"}A := B + (if X then Y else Z) + C; -- parentheses required{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.d/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
The following procedure calls are syntactically legal; the first uses the above rule to eliminate the redundant parentheses found in the second:<br />

<MarginText>7.e/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
P(if X then Y else Z);{"\n"}P((if X then Y else Z)); -- redundant parentheses{"\n"}
<MarginText>7.f/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
P((if X then Y else Z), Some{"_"}Other{"_"}Param);{"\n"}P(Some{"_"}Other{"_"}Param, (if X then Y else Z));{"\n"}P(Formal ={">"} (if X then Y else Z));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.g/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
whereas the following are illegal:<br />

<MarginText>7.h/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
P(if X then Y else Z, Some{"_"}Other{"_"}Param);{"\n"}P(Some{"_"}Other{"_"}Param, if X then Y else Z);{"\n"}P(Formal ={">"} if X then Y else Z);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.i/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
because in these latter cases, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is not immediately surrounded by parentheses (which means on both sides!).<br />

<MarginText>7.j/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
The English-language rule applies in all places that could surround an expression with parentheses, including pragma arguments, type conversion and qualified expression operands, and array index expressions.<br />

<MarginText>7.k/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
This English-language rule could have been implemented instead by adding a nonterminal <code>expression{"_"}within{"_"}parentheses</code>, which would consist of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s. Then, that could be used in all of the syntax which could consist of parens directly around an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. We did not do that because of the large amount of change required. A complete grammar is given in . <br />

<MarginText>7.l/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Implementers are cautioned to consider error detection when implementing the syntax for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code> and an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code> are very similar syntactically, (as are a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code> and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>) and simple mistakes can appear to change one into the other, potentially causing errors to be moved far away from their actual location. The absence of <b>end if</b> to terminate an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code> (and <b>end case</b> for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>) also may make error handling harder. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is expected to be of a type <i>T</i>, then each <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is expected to be of type <i>T</i>. Similarly, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is expected to be of some class of types, then each <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is subject to the same expectation. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> shall resolve to be of a type <i>T</i>, then each <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall resolve to be of type <i>T</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
<p>The possible types of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> are further determined as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is the operand of a type conversion, the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is the target type of the conversion; otherwise,<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule distributes an enclosing type conversion to the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s. This means that <br />

<MarginText>10.b/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
T(if C then A else B){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10.c/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
has the same semantics as <br />

<MarginText>10.d/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
(if C then T(A) else T(B)){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>11/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If all of the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s are of the same type, the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is that type; otherwise,<br /></li>
<MarginText>12/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<li>If a <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is of an elementary type, the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> shall be covered by that type; otherwise,<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule supports the use of numeric literals and universal expressions within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>13/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is expected to be of type <i>T</i> or shall resolve to type <i>T</i>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is of type <i>T</i>.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> cannot be determined by one of these rules, then Name Resolution has failed for that expression, even if the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s would resolve individually. <br />

<MarginText>14/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> is expected to be of any boolean type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s are as for case statements (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4">5.4</a>). <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>16/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>All of the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s shall be convertible (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>) to the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0188-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>If the expected type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is a specific tagged type, all of the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> shall be dynamically tagged, or none shall be dynamically tagged. In this case, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code> is dynamically tagged if all of the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s are dynamically tagged, is tag-indeterminate if all of the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s are tag-indeterminate, and is statically tagged otherwise.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>If there is no <b>else</b> <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code> shall be of a boolean type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>All Legality Rules that apply to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4">5.4</a>) also apply to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code> except within an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The exemption for a case expression that occurs in an instance allows the following example: <br />

<MarginText>19.b/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   with function Int{"_"}Func return Integer;{"\n"}package G is{"\n"}   X : Float := (case Int{"_"}Func is{"\n"}                  when Integer'First .. -1 ={">"} -1.0,{"\n"}                  when 0 ={">"} 0.0,{"\n"}                  when Positive ={">"} 1.0);{"\n"}end G;{"\n"}
<MarginText>19.c/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
function Nat{"_"}Func return Natural is (123);{"\n"}
<MarginText>19.d/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
package I is new G (Int{"_"}Func ={">"} Nat{"_"}Func); -- Legal{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>19.e/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
Note that the Legality Rules still apply in the generic unit itself; they are just not enforced in an instance of the unit. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>20/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1", "AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> specified after <b>if</b>, and any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>s specified after <b>elsif</b>, are evaluated in succession (treating a final <b>else</b> as <b>elsif</b> True <b>then</b>), until one evaluates to True or all <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>s are evaluated and yield False. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> evaluates to True, the associated <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is evaluated, converted to the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code>, and the resulting value is the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code>. Otherwise (when there is no <b>else</b> clause), the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code> is True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b><b>Else</b> is required unless the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code> has a boolean type, so the last sentence can only apply to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code>s with a boolean type. <br />

<MarginText>21/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>, the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is first evaluated. If the value of the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is covered by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> of some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0152">case_expression_alternative</a></code>, then the <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0152">case_expression_alternative</a></code> is evaluated, converted to the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>, and the resulting value is the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>. Otherwise (the value is not covered by any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>, perhaps due to being outside the base range), Constraint{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>22/5_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of use of an</i> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0149">if_expression</a></code><i>:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>23/5_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Put{"_"}Line ("Casey is " &{"\n"}      (if Casey.Sex = M then "Male" else "Female")); -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>24/5_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of use of a</i> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code><i>:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>25/5_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Card{"_"}Color (Card : Suit) return Color is -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.1">3.5.1</a>{"\n"}  (case Card is{"\n"}      when Clubs  | Spades   ={">"} Black,{"\n"}      when Hearts | Diamonds ={">"} Red);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>25.a/3_4.5.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
If expressions and case expressions are new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.8"></a>

## 4.5.8  Quantified Expressions

<MarginText>0.1/4_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0158-1"]} />
<p>Quantified expressions provide a way to write universally and existentially quantified predicates over containers and arrays. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>quantified{"_"}expression</code><a id="S0153"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0154">quantifier</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> ={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code><br />  | <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0154">quantifier</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> ={">"} <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2/3_4.5.8</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>quantifier</code><a id="S0154"></a><code> ::= </code><b>all</b> | <b>some</b><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/3_4.5.8</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>predicate</code><a id="S0155"></a><code> ::= </code><i>boolean{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">Wherever the Syntax Rules allow an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> may be used in place of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, so long as it is immediately surrounded by parentheses.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> appears only as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is parenthesized. The above rule allows it to additionally be used in other contexts where it would be directly surrounded by parentheses. This is the same rule that is used for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.7">4.5.7</a> for a detailed discussion of the meaning and effects of this rule. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1"]} />
<p>The expected type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> is any Boolean type. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> is expected to be of the same type. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6/5_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1", "AI12-0158-1", "AI12-0327-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is first elaborated. The evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> then performs an iteration, and evaluates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code> for each value conditionally produced by the iteration (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/5_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0327-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The order of evaluation of the predicates is that in which the values are produced, as specified in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a> or <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>. <br />

<MarginText>7/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1"]} />
<p>The value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> is determined as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/4_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0158-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0154">quantifier</a></code> is <b>all</b>, the expression is False if the evaluation of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code> yields False; evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> stops at that point. Otherwise (every predicate has been evaluated and yielded True), the expression is True.
