Any exception raised by evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code> is propagated.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is True if the domain contains no values. <br />

<MarginText>9/4_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0158-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0154">quantifier</a></code> is <b>some</b>, the expression is True if the evaluation of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code> yields True; evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code> stops at that point. Otherwise (every predicate has been evaluated and yielded False), the expression is False. Any exception raised by evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0155">predicate</a></code> is propagated.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is False if the domain contains no values. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>10/5_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a quantified expression as a postcondition for a sorting routine on an array A with an index subtype T:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>11/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Post ={">"} (A'Length {"<"} 2 or else{"\n"}   (for all I in A'First .. T'Pred(A'Last) ={">"} A (I) {"<"}= A (T'Succ (I)))){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12/5_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1", "AI12-0429-1", "AI12-0430-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of use of a quantified expression as an assertion that a positive number N is composite (as opposed to prime):</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
pragma Assert (for some X in 2 .. N when X {"*"} X {"<"}= N ={">"} N mod X = 0);{"\n"}   -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a> in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>13.a/3_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0176-1"]} />
Quantified expressions are new. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>13.b/4_4.5.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0158-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Revised the wording to make it clear that the semantics is short-circuited, and what the result is when there are no values for the loop parameter. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.9"></a>

## 4.5.9  Declare Expressions

<MarginText>1/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<p>Declare expressions provide a way to declare local constants and object renamings in an expression context. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>declare{"_"}expression</code><a id="S0156"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>declare</b> {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0157">declare_item</a></code>{"}"}<br />    <b>begin</b> <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>declare{"_"}item</code><a id="S0157"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object_renaming_declaration</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.a/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We allow (<b>declare begin</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>) with no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0157">declare_item</a></code>s, for uniformity with block statements, which also allow a pointless <b>declare</b>. <br />

<MarginText>4/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">Wherever the Syntax Rules allow an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> may be used in place of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, so long as it is immediately surrounded by parentheses.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> appears only as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is parenthesized. The above rule allows it to additionally be used in other contexts where it would be directly surrounded by parentheses. This is the same rule that is used for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>s; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.7">4.5.7</a> for a detailed discussion of the meaning and effects of this rule. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0157">declare_item</a></code> that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> shall declare a constant of a nonlimited type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We disallow limited objects to avoid the horror of task waiting in the middle of an expression. The solution used for controlled objects (wait until the entire expression is finished) isn't appropriate for tasks. This restriction also eliminates build-in-place complexities and the need to activate tasks found in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0157">declare_item</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>6/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1", "AI12-0317-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0157">declare_item</a></code> that is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object_renaming_declaration</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#Subclause_8.5.1">8.5.1</a>) shall not rename an object of a limited type if any operative constituent of the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is a value conversion or is newly constructed (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4">4.4</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We disallow renaming limited temporary objects (like the result of a function call) for the same reasons as for stand-alone objects. We do allow renaming existing limited objects because these don't cause any problems. Note that one cannot directly rename an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, parenthesized expression, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> (these are not <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s), but any of these can appear inside of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> (which are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s and thus can be renamed). <br />

<MarginText>7/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<p>The following are not allowed within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code>: a declaration containing the reserved word <b>aliased</b>; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code> Access or Unchecked{"_"}Access; or an anonymous access type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We do not want to define accessibility rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0157">declare_item</a></code>s, as nested <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code>s cause complexities or usage warts. We want to keep this feature simple to use, understand, and implement. Thus, we do not allow any of the features that would require accessibility rules. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> is expected to be of a type <i>T</i>, then the <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is expected to be of type <i>T</i>. Similarly, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> is expected to be of some class of types, then the <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is subject to the same expectation. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> shall resolve to be of a type <i>T</i>, then the <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall resolve to be of type <i>T</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<p>The type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> is the type of the <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0157">declare_item</a></code>s are elaborated in order, and then the <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is evaluated. The value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> is that of the <i>body{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>11/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of use of a declare expression as a replacement postcondition for Ada.Containers.Vectors."&" (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a>):</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Post ={">"}{"\n"}   (declare{"\n"}      Result renames Vectors."&"'Result;{"\n"}      Length : constant Count{"_"}Type := Left.Length + Right.Length;{"\n"}    begin{"\n"}      Result.Length = Length and then{"\n"}      not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited (Result) and then{"\n"}      not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited (Result) and then{"\n"}      Result.Capacity {">"}= Length){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>12.a/5_4.5.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
Declare expressions are new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_4.5.10"></a>

## 4.5.10  Reduction Expressions

<MarginText>1/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p>Reduction expressions provide a way to map or transform a collection of values into a new set of values, and then summarize the values produced by applying an operation to reduce the set to a single value result. A reduction expression is represented as an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> of the reduction attributes Reduce or Parallel{"_"}Reduce.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>reduction expression</b> &mdash; expression that defines how to map or transform a collection of values into a new set of values, and then summarize the values by applying an operation to reduce the set to a single value<br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0262-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>reduction{"_"}attribute{"_"}reference</code><a id="S0158"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code>'<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0160">reduction_attribute_designator</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>'<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0160">reduction_attribute_designator</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0355-2"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>value{"_"}sequence</code><a id="S0159"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    '[' [<b>parallel</b>[(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>)] [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>]]<br />        <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> ']'<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>reduction{"_"}attribute{"_"}designator</code><a id="S0160"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <i>reduction{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0161">reduction_specification</a></code>)<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>reduction{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0161"></a><code> ::= </code><i>reducer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, <i>initial{"_"}value{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> shall not have a <i>key{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, nor shall it have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> that has the reserved word <b>reverse</b>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The intent is that the syntax matches as closely as possible array or container aggregate notation. Syntax that matches a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> with the <b>reverse</b> reserved word would not be permitted in an array aggregate, so we disallow that here. <br />

<MarginText>7/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, if any, of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> shall be an <i>integer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>.<br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code> shall be a single nonlimited type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p>In the remainder of this subclause, we will refer to nonlimited subtypes <i>Value{"_"}Type</i> and <i>Accum{"_"}Type</i> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code>. These subtypes and interpretations of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code> are determined by the following rules:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b><i>Accum{"_"}Type</i> represents the result of the reduction (the <i>accumulator</i> type), and <i>Value{"_"}Type</i> represents the type of the input values to the reduction. <br />

<MarginText>10/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<ul>
<li><i>Accum{"_"}Type</i> is a subtype of the expected type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<li>A <i>reducer subprogram</i> is subtype conformant with one of the following specifications:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   function Reducer(Accumulator : Accum{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                    Value : Value{"_"}Type) return Accum{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>13/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
   procedure Reducer(Accumulator : in out Accum{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                     Value : in Value{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The <i>reducer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0161">reduction_specification</a></code> denotes a reducer subprogram.<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<li>The expected type of an <i>initial{"_"}value{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0161">reduction_specification</a></code> is that of subtype <i>Accum{"_"}Type</i>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>16/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0262-1"]} />
<li>The expected type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> is that of subtype <i>Value{"_"}Type</i>. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>17/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code> has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> with the reserved word <b>parallel</b>, the subtypes <i>Accum{"_"}Type</i> and <i>Value{"_"}Type</i> shall statically match.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0160">reduction_attribute_designator</a></code> is Parallel{"_"}Reduce, the subtypes <i>Accum{"_"}Type</i> and <i>Value{"_"}Type</i> shall statically match.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> that does not have the reserved word <b>parallel</b> or has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0160">reduction_attribute_designator</a></code> is Reduce, the subtypes <i>Accum{"_"}Type</i> and <i>Value{"_"}Type</i> can be different because only one logical thread of control is presumed so there is no need to combine multiple results. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>19/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code> denotes a value, with its nominal subtype being the subtype of the first parameter of the subprogram denoted by the <i>reducer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>20/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0327-1", "AI12-0355-2"]} />
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, if any, are elaborated in an arbitrary order. Next an iteration is performed, and for each value conditionally produced by the iteration (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>), the associated <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is evaluated with the loop parameter having this value, which produces a result that is converted to Value{"_"}Type and is used to define the next value in the sequence.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> does not have the reserved word <b>parallel</b>, it is produced as a single sequence of values by a single logical thread of control. If the reserved word <b>parallel</b> is present in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code>, the enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code> is a parallel construct, and the sequence of values is generated by a parallel iteration (as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.1">5.5.1</a>, and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>), as a set of non-empty, non-overlapping contiguous chunks (<i>subsequences</i>) with one logical thread of control (see Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>) associated with each subsequence. If there is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, it determines the maximum number of chunks, as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>; otherwise the maximum number of chunks is implementation defined.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The maximum number of chunks for a parallel reduction expression without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>22/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> V, the following attribute is defined:<br /></p>

<MarginText>23/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>V'Reduce(Reducer, Initial{"_"}Value)</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>This attribute represents a <i>reduction expression</i>, and is in the form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code>. <br /></dd>
<MarginText>24/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dd>The evaluation of a use of this attribute begins by evaluating the parts of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0160">reduction_attribute_designator</a></code> (the <i>reducer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> Reducer and the <i>initial{"_"}value{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> Initial{"_"}Value), in an arbitrary order. It then initializes the <i>accumulator</i> of the reduction expression to the value of the <i>initial{"_"}value{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (the <i>initial value</i>).  The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> V is then evaluated.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>25/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dd>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> does not have the reserved word <b>parallel</b>, each value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> is passed, in order, as the second (Value) parameter to a call on Reducer, with the first (Accumulator) parameter being the prior value of the accumulator, saving the result as the new value of the accumulator. The reduction expression yields the final value of the accumulator.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>26/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<dd>If the reserved word <b>parallel</b> is present in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code>, then the (parallel) reduction expression is a parallel construct and the sequence has been partitioned into one or more subsequences (see above) each with its own separate logical thread of control.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>27/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dd>Each logical thread of control creates a local accumulator for processing its subsequence. The accumulator for a subsequence is initialized to the first value of the subsequence, and calls on Reducer start with the second value of the subsequence (if any). The result for the subsequence is the final value of its local accumulator.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>28/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dd>After all logical threads of control of a parallel reduction expression have completed, Reducer is called for each subsequence, in the original sequence order, passing the local accumulator for that subsequence as the second (Value) parameter, and the overall accumulator [(initialized above to the initial value)] as the first (Accumulator) parameter, with the result saved back in the overall accumulator. The parallel reduction expression yields the final value of the overall accumulator.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<dd>If the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> yields an empty sequence of values, the reduction expression yields the initial value.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>30/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dd>If an exception is propagated by one of the calls on Reducer, that exception is propagated from the reduction expression. If different exceptions are propagated in different logical threads of control, one is chosen arbitrarily to be propagated from the reduction expression as a whole.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>30.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0158">reduction_attribute_reference</a></code> that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code> without the reserved word <b>parallel</b> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> where the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0160">reduction_attribute_designator</a></code> is Reduce (see below), generally the compiler can still choose to execute the reduction in parallel, presuming doing so would not change the results. However sequential execution is necessary if the subtypes of the parameters of Reducer do not statically match, since there is no subprogram identified in the construct that could be used for combining the results in parallel. <br />

<MarginText>30.b/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We say the calls to Reducer that combine the results of parallel execution are sequentially ordered in increasing order because certain reductions, such as vector concatenation, can be non-commutative (but still associative) operations. In order to return a deterministic result for parallel execution that is consistent with sequential execution, we need to specify an order for the iteration, and for the combination of results from the logical threads of control. It is also necessary that combining calls to Reducer are issued sequentially with respect to each other, which may require extra synchronization if the calls to Reducer are being executed by different logical threads of control. <br />

<MarginText>31/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X of an array type[ (after any implicit dereference)], or that denotes an iterable container object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.1">5.5.1</a>), the following attributes are defined:<br /></p>

<MarginText>32/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Reduce(Reducer, Initial{"_"}Value)</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>X'Reduce is a reduction expression that yields a result equivalent to replacing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the attribute with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code>: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>32.1/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
[for Item of X ={">"} Item]{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>33/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Parallel{"_"}Reduce(Reducer, Initial{"_"}Value)</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>X'Parallel{"_"}Reduce is a reduction expression that yields a result equivalent to replacing the attribute <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> with Reduce and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the attribute with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0159">value_sequence</a></code>: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>33.1/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
[parallel for Item of X ={">"} Item]{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>34/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
<p>For a parallel reduction expression, it is a bounded error if the reducer subprogram is not associative. That is, for any arbitrary values of subtype <i>Value{"_"}Type</i> <i>A</i>, <i>B</i>, <i>C</i> and a reducer function <i>R</i>, the result of <i>R</i> (<i>A</i>, <i>R</i> (<i>B</i>, <i>C</i>)) should produce a result equal to <i>R</i> (<i>R</i> (<i>A</i>, <i>B</i>), <i>C</i>)); it is a bounded error if <i>R</i> does not. The possible consequences are Program{"_"}Error, or a result that does not match the equivalent sequential reduction expression due to the order of calls on the reducer subprogram being unspecified in the overall reduction. Analogous rules apply in the case of a reduction procedure.<br /></p>

<MarginText>34.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>In a sequential reduction expression, the reducer subprogram is called in a left-to-right order, whereas in a parallel reduction expression, the reducer subprogram is called in an order that depends on the number of logical threads of control that execute the reduction and on the elements/components given to each chunk. If the reducer is associative, this order does not matter, but in other cases, very different results are possible. While one can specify the <i>maximum</i> number of chunks, the actual number of chunks is unspecified. Similarly, the split of elements has only weak requirements. Thus, to get a consistent and portable result, an associative reducer is required for a parallel reduction. We define this as a Bounded (Run-Time) Errors to provide a stern warning about the required nature of the reducer subprogram and to let compilers detect the problem when possible. <br />

<MarginText>34.b/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>In this rule, &ldquo;equal&rdquo; means semantically equal. We don't care if the bit patterns differ but that the results mean the same thing. In particular, if the primitive equal is user-defined, that equality would be the one used to determine if this rule is violated. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>35/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of an expression function that returns its result as a reduction expression:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>36/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Factorial(N : Natural) return Natural is{"\n"}   ([for J in 1..N ={">"} J]'Reduce("{"*"}", 1));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>37/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a reduction expression that computes the Sine of X using a Taylor expansion:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>38/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Sine (X : Float; Num{"_"}Terms : Positive := 5) return Float is{"\n"}   ([for I in 1..Num{"_"}Terms ={">"}{"\n"}      (-1.0){"*"}{"*"}(I-1) {"*"} X{"*"}{"*"}(2{"*"}I-1)/Float(Factorial(2{"*"}I-1))]{"\n"}         'Reduce("+", 0.0));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>39/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0379-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a reduction expression that outputs the sum of squares:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>40/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Put{"_"}Line ("Sum of Squares is" &{"\n"}          Integer'Image([for I in 1 .. 10 ={">"} I{"*"}{"*"}2]'Reduce("+", 0)));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>41/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0379-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a reduction expression used to compute the value of Pi:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>42/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
--  See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.7">3.5.7</a>.{"\n"}function Pi (Number{"_"}Of{"_"}Steps : Natural := 10{"_"}000) return Real is{"\n"}  (1.0 / Real (Number{"_"}Of{"_"}Steps) {"*"}{"\n"}    [for I in 1 .. Number{"_"}Of{"_"}Steps ={">"}{"\n"}        (4.0 / (1.0 + ((Real (I) - 0.5) {"*"}{"\n"}           (1.0 / Real (Number{"_"}Of{"_"}Steps))){"*"}{"*"}2))]{"\n"}              'Reduce("+", 0.0));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>43/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a reduction expression used to calculate the sum of elements of an array of integers:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>44/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
A'Reduce("+",0)  -- See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.3">4.3.3</a>.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>45/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a reduction expression used to determine if all elements in a two-dimensional array of booleans are set to true:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>46/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Grid'Reduce("and", True)  -- See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>47/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a reduction expression used to calculate the minimum value of an array of integers in parallel:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>48/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
A'Parallel{"_"}Reduce(Integer'Min, Integer'Last){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>49/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a parallel reduction expression used to calculate the mean of the elements of a two-dimensional array of subtype Matrix (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>) that are greater than 100.0:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>50/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Accumulator is record{"\n"}   Sum   : Real; -- See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.7">3.5.7</a>.{"\n"}   Count : Integer;{"\n"}end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>51/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
function Accumulate (L, R : Accumulator) return Accumulator is{"\n"}  (Sum   ={">"} L.Sum   + R.Sum,{"\n"}   Count ={">"} L.Count + R.Count);{"\n"}
<MarginText>52/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
function Average{"_"}of{"_"}Values{"_"}Greater{"_"}Than{"_"}100 (M : Matrix) return Real is{"\n"}   (declare{"\n"}       Acc : constant Accumulator :={"\n"}          [parallel for Val of M when Val {">"} 100.0 ={">"} (Val, 1)]{"\n"}             'Reduce(Accumulate, (Sum ={">"} 0, Count ={">"} 0));{"\n"}    begin{"\n"}       Acc.Sum / Real(Acc.Count));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>52.a/5_4.5.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0242-1", "AI12-0262-1", "AI12-0348-1"]} />
Reduction expressions and the associated attributes are new. <br />

# 4.6. Type Conversions

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6.mdx

sidebar_position:  36

# 4.6. Type Conversions

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[Explicit type conversions, both value conversions and view conversions, are allowed between closely related types as defined below. This subclause also defines rules for value and view conversions to a particular subtype of a type, both explicit ones and those implicit in other constructs. ]<br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>type{"_"}conversion</code><a id="S0162"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>)<br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>)<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The <i>target subtype</i> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> is the subtype denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>. The <i>operand</i> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> within the parentheses; its type is the <i>operand type</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>One type is <i>convertible</i> to a second type if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> with the first type as operand type and the second type as target type is legal according to the rules of this subclause. Two types are convertible if each is convertible to the other. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that &ldquo;convertible&rdquo; is defined in terms of legality of the conversion. Whether the conversion would raise an exception at run time is irrelevant to this definition. <br />

<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00184-01", "AI95-00330-01", "AI12-0392-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0017</i>{"}"} A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> is called a <i>view conversion</i> if both its target type and operand type are tagged, or if it appears in a call as an actual parameter of mode <b>out</b> or <b>in out</b>; other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>s are called <i>value conversions</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A view conversion to a tagged type can appear in any context that requires an object <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, including in an object renaming, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>, and if the operand is a variable, on the left side of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>. View conversions to other types only occur as actual parameters. Allowing view conversions of untagged types in all contexts seemed to incur an undue implementation burden.<br />

<MarginText>5.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00330-01"]} />
A type conversion appearing as an <b>in out</b> parameter in a generic instantiation is not a view conversion; the second part of the rule only applies to subprogram calls, not instantiations. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>The operand of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> is expected to be of any type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This replaces the &ldquo;must be determinable&rdquo; wording of Ada 83. This is equivalent to (but hopefully more intuitive than) saying that the operand of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> is a &ldquo;complete context&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The operand of a view conversion is interpreted only as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>; the operand of a value conversion is interpreted as an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This formally resolves the syntactic ambiguity between the two forms of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>. This matters because an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is evaluated and represents a value while a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> by itself can be an object; we want a view conversion to be an object. <br />

<MarginText>7.b/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This wording uses "interpreted as" rather than "shall be" so that this rule is not used to resolve overloading; it is solely about evaluation as described above. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>8/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<p>In a view conversion for an untagged type, the target type shall be convertible (back) to the operand type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Untagged view conversions appear only as [<b>in</b>] <b>out</b> parameters. Hence, the reverse conversion must be legal as well. The forward conversion must be legal even for an <b>out</b> parameter, because (for example) actual parameters of an access type are always copied in anyway. <br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 9 through 20 were reorganized and moved below.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The entire Legality Rules section has been reorganized to eliminate an unintentional incompatibility with Ada 83. In rare cases, a type conversion between two types related by derivation is not allowed by Ada 95, while it is allowed in Ada 83. The reorganization fixes this. Much of the wording of the legality section is unchanged, but it is reordered and reformatted. Because of the limitations of our tools, we had to delete and replace nearly the entire section. The text of Ada 95 paragraphs 8 through 12, 14, 15, 17, 19, 20, and 24 are unchanged (just moved); these are now 24.1 through 24.5, 24.12, 24.13, 24.17, 24.19, 24.20, and 8. <br />

<MarginText>21/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI05-0115-1"]} />
<p>If there is a type (other than a root numeric type) that is an ancestor of both the target type and the operand type, or both types are class-wide types, then at least one of the following rules shall apply: <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The target type shall be untagged; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<li>The operand type shall be covered by or descended from the target type; or <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>22.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This is a conversion toward the root, which is always safe. <br />

<MarginText>23/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The operand type shall be a class-wide type that covers the target type; or <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This is a conversion of a class-wide type toward the leaves, which requires a tag check. See Dynamic Semantics.<br />

<MarginText>23.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
These two rules imply that a conversion from an ancestor type to a type extension is not permitted, as this would require specifying the values for additional components, in general, and changing the tag. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code> has to be used instead, constructing a new value, rather than converting an existing value. However, a conversion from the class-wide type rooted at an ancestor type is permitted; such a conversion just verifies that the operand's tag is a descendant of the target. <br />

<MarginText>23.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The operand and target types shall both be class-wide types and the specific type associated with at least one of them shall be an interface type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23.c/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We allow converting any class-wide type T'Class to or from a class-wide interface type even if the specific type T does not have an appropriate interface ancestor, because some extension of T might have the needed ancestor. This is similar to a conversion of a class-wide type toward the leaves of the tree, and we need to be consistent. Of course, there is a runtime check that the actual object has the needed interface. <br />

<MarginText>24/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI05-0115-1"]} />
<p>If there is no type (other than a root numeric type) that is the ancestor of both the target type and the operand type, and they are not both class-wide types, one of the following rules shall apply: <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type is a numeric type, then the operand type shall be a numeric type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<li>If the target type is an array type, then the operand type shall be an array type. Further:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.3/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The types shall have the same dimensionality;<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.4/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<li>Corresponding index types shall be convertible; <br /></li>
<MarginText>24.5/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<li>The component subtypes shall statically match; <br /></li>
<MarginText>24.6/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00392-01"]} />
<li>If the component types are anonymous access types, then the accessibility level of the operand type shall not be statically deeper than that of the target type; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.b/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>For unrelated array types, the component types could have different accessibility, and we had better not allow a conversion of a local type into a global type, in case the local type points at local objects. We don't need a check for other types of components; such components necessarily are for related types, and either have the same accessibility or (for access discriminants) cannot be changed so the discriminant check will prevent problems. <br />

<MarginText>24.7/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00246-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>Neither the target type nor the operand type shall be limited; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.c/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We cannot allow conversions between unrelated limited types, as they may have different representations, and (since the types are limited), a copy cannot be made to reconcile the representations. <br />

<MarginText>24.8/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00363-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type of a view conversion has aliased components, then so shall the operand type; and <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We cannot allow a view conversion from an object with unaliased components to an object with aliased components, because that would effectively allow pointers to unaliased components. This rule was missing from Ada 95. <br />

<MarginText>24.9/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00246-01", "AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The operand type of a view conversion shall not have a tagged, private, or volatile subcomponent. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00246-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We cannot allow view conversions between unrelated might-be-by-reference types, as they may have different representations, and a copy cannot be made to reconcile the representations. <br />

<MarginText>24.f/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>These rules only apply to unrelated array conversions; different (weaker) rules apply to conversions between related types. <br />

<MarginText>24.10/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type is <i>universal{"_"}access</i>, then the operand type shall be an access type.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.g/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Such a conversion cannot be written explicitly, of course, but it can be implicit (see below). <br />

<MarginText>24.11/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type is a general access-to-object type, then the operand type shall be <i>universal{"_"}access</i> or an access-to-object type. Further, if the operand type is not <i>universal{"_"}access</i>:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.h/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The Legality Rules and Dynamic Semantics are worded so that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> T(X) (where T is an access type) is (almost) equivalent to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> X.<b>all</b>'Access, where the result is of type T. The only difference is that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> accepts a null value, whereas the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> would raise Constraint{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>24.12/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type is an access-to-variable type, then the operand type shall be an access-to-variable type; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.i/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the target type is an access-to-constant type, then the operand type can be access-to-constant or access-to-variable. <br />

<MarginText>24.13/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target designated type is tagged, then the operand designated type shall be convertible to the target designated type; <br /></li>
<MarginText>24.14/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI95-00363-01"]} />
<li>If the target designated type is not tagged, then the designated types shall be the same, and either:<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.15/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<li>the designated subtypes shall statically match; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.16/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01", "AI95-00384-01"]} />
<li>the designated type shall be discriminated in its full view and unconstrained in any partial view, and one of the designated subtypes shall be unconstrained;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.j/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This does not require that types have a partial view in order to allow the conversion, simply that any partial view that does exist is unconstrained.<br />

<MarginText>24.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00384-01"]} />
This allows conversions both ways (either subtype can be unconstrained); while Ada 95 only allowed the conversion if the target subtype is unconstrained. We generally want type conversions to be symmetric; which type is the target shouldn't matter for legality. <br />

<MarginText>24.l/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>If the visible partial view is constrained, we do not allow conversion between unconstrained and constrained subtypes. This means that whether the full type had discriminants is not visible to clients of the partial view. <br />

<MarginText>24.l.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0095-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We assume the worst in a generic body about whether or not a formal subtype has a constrained partial view; specifically, in a generic body a discriminated subtype is considered to have a constrained partial view if it is a descendant of an untagged generic formal private or derived type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a> for the formal definition of this rule). <br />

<MarginText>24.m/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>These rules are designed to ensure that aliased array objects only <i>need</i> "dope" if their nominal subtype is unconstrained, but they can always <i>have</i> dope if required by the run-time model (since no sliding is permitted as part of access type conversion). By contrast, aliased discriminated objects will always <i>need</i> their discriminants stored with them, even if nominally constrained. (Here, we are assuming an implementation that represents an access value as a single pointer.) <br />

<MarginText>24.17/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI05-0148-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI12-0027-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The accessibility level of the operand type shall not be statically deeper than that of the target type, unless the target type is an anonymous access type of a stand-alone object. If the target type is that of such a stand-alone object, the accessibility level of the operand type shall not be statically deeper than that of the declaration of the stand-alone object. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.n/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0148-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The access parameter case is handled by a run-time check. runtime checks are also done in instance bodies, and for stand-alone objects of anonymous access types. <br />

<MarginText>24.n.1/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We prohibit storing accesses to objects deeper than a stand-alone object of an anonymous access-to-object (even while we allow storing all other accesses) in order to prevent dangling accesses. <br />

<MarginText>24.18/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type is a pool-specific access-to-object type, then the operand type shall be <i>universal{"_"}access</i>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.o/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This allows <b>null</b> to be converted to pool-specific types. Without it, <b>null</b> could be converted to general access types but not pool-specific ones, which would be too inconsistent. Remember that these rules only apply to unrelated types, so we don't have to talk about conversions to derived or other related types. <br />

<MarginText>24.19/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type is an access-to-subprogram type, then the operand type shall be <i>universal{"_"}access</i> or an access-to-subprogram type. Further, if the operand type is not <i>universal{"_"}access</i>:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.20/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI05-0239-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The designated profiles shall be subtype conformant. <br /></li>
<MarginText>24.21/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI12-0027-1"]} />
<li>The accessibility level of the operand type shall not be statically deeper than that of the target type. If the operand type is declared within a generic body, the target type shall be declared within the generic body.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.p/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The reason it is illegal to convert from an access-to-subprogram type declared in a generic body to one declared outside that body is that in an implementation that shares generic bodies, subprograms declared inside the generic need to have a different calling convention &mdash; they need an extra parameter pointing to the data declared in the current instance. For subprograms declared in the spec, that's OK, because the compiler can know about them at compile time of the instantiation. <br />

<MarginText>24.22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0380-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the target type has a Global aspect other than <b>in out all</b> or Unspecified, then each mode of the Global aspect of the operand type shall identify a subset of the variables identified by the corresponding mode of the target type Global aspect, or by the <b>in out</b> mode of the target type Global aspect.<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.23/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0064-2"]} />
<li>If the target type is nonblocking, the operand type shall be nonblocking. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.24/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0027-1"]} />
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules apply also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.q/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This applies to <i>all</i> of the Legality Rules in this section. It won't matter for the majority of these rules, but in any case that it does, we want to apply the same rules in the private part. (Ada got the default wrong for these, as there is only one known case where we don't want to recheck in the private part, see derivations without record extensions in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4">3.4</a>.) <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> that is a value conversion denotes the value that is the result of converting the value of the operand to the target subtype.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> that is a view conversion denotes a view of the object denoted by the operand. This view is a variable of the target type if the operand denotes a variable; otherwise, it is a constant of the target type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27</MarginText>
<p>The nominal subtype of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> is its target subtype. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>28</MarginText>
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> that is a value conversion, the operand is evaluated, and then the value of the operand is <i>converted</i> to a <i>corresponding</i> value of the target type, if any. If there is no value of the target type that corresponds to the operand value, Constraint{"_"}Error is raised[; this can only happen on conversion to a modular type, and only when the operand value is outside the base range of the modular type.] Additional rules follow: <br /></p>

<MarginText>29</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Numeric Type Conversion <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>30</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the target and the operand types are both integer types, then the result is the value of the target type that corresponds to the same mathematical integer as the operand.<br /></li>
<MarginText>31</MarginText>
<li>If the target type is a decimal fixed point type, then the result is truncated (toward 0) if the value of the operand is not a multiple of the <i>small</i> of the target type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>32</MarginText>
<li>If the target type is some other real type, then the result is within the accuracy of the target type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2">G.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2">Numeric Performance Requirements</a>&rdquo;, for implementations that support the Numerics Annex). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>32.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>An integer type might have more bits of precision than a real type, so on conversion (of a large integer), some precision might be lost. <br />

<MarginText>33</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the target type is an integer type and the operand type is real, the result is rounded to the nearest integer (away from zero if exactly halfway between two integers). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>33.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00267-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This was implementation defined in Ada 83. There seems no reason to preserve the nonportability in Ada 95. Round-away-from-zero is the conventional definition of rounding, and standard Fortran and COBOL both specify rounding away from zero, so for interoperability, it seems important to pick this. This is also the most easily &ldquo;undone&rdquo; by hand. Round-to-nearest-even is an alternative, but that is quite complicated if not supported by the hardware. In any case, this operation is not usually part of an inner loop, so predictability and portability are judged most important. A floating point attribute function Unbiased{"_"}Rounding is provided (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>) for those applications that require round-to-nearest-even, and a floating point attribute function Machine{"_"}Rounding (also see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>) is provided for those applications that require the highest possible performance. &ldquo;Deterministic&rdquo; rounding is required for static conversions to integer as well. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9">4.9</a>. <br />

<MarginText>34</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Enumeration Type Conversion <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>35</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The result is the value of the target type with the same position number as that of the operand value. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>36</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Array Type Conversion <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>37</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the target subtype is a constrained array subtype, then a check is made that the length of each dimension of the value of the operand equals the length of the corresponding dimension of the target subtype. The bounds of the result are those of the target subtype.<br /></li>
<MarginText>38</MarginText>
<li>If the target subtype is an unconstrained array subtype, then the bounds of the result are obtained by converting each bound of the value of the operand to the corresponding index type of the target type. For each nonnull index range, a check is made that the bounds of the range belong to the corresponding index subtype. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>38.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Only nonnull index ranges are checked, per AI83-00313. <br />

<MarginText>39</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>In either array case, the value of each component of the result is that of the matching component of the operand value (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.2">4.5.2</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>39.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This applies whether or not the component is initialized. <br />

<MarginText>39.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00392-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the component types of the array types are anonymous access types, then a check is made that the accessibility level of the operand type is not deeper than that of the target type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>39.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This check is needed for operands that are in instance bodies. Other cases are handled by the legality rule given previously. <br />

<MarginText>40</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Composite (Non-Array) Type Conversion <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>41</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The value of each nondiscriminant component of the result is that of the matching component of the operand value. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>41.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This applies whether or not the component is initialized. <br />

<MarginText>42</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>[The tag of the result is that of the operand.] If the operand type is class-wide, a check is made that the tag of the operand identifies a (specific) type that is covered by or descended from the target type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>42.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This check is certain to succeed if the operand type is itself covered by or descended from the target type. <br />

<MarginText>42.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The fact that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> preserves the tag is stated officially in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9">3.9</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9">Tagged Types and Type Extensions</a>&rdquo; <br />

<MarginText>43</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For each discriminant of the target type that corresponds to a discriminant of the operand type, its value is that of the corresponding discriminant of the operand value; if it corresponds to more than one discriminant of the operand type, a check is made that all these discriminants are equal in the operand value.<br /></li>
<MarginText>44</MarginText>
<li>For each discriminant of the target type that corresponds to a discriminant that is specified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> for some ancestor of the operand type (or if class-wide, some ancestor of the specific type identified by the tag of the operand), its value in the result is that specified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>44.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>It is a ramification of the rules for the discriminants of derived types that each discriminant of the result is covered either by this paragraph or the previous one. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7">3.7</a>. <br />

<MarginText>45</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For each discriminant of the operand type that corresponds to a discriminant that is specified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> for some ancestor of the target type, a check is made that in the operand value it equals the value specified for it.<br /></li>
<MarginText>46</MarginText>
<li>For each discriminant of the result, a check is made that its value belongs to its subtype. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>47</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Access Type Conversion <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>48/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0148-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For an access-to-object type, a check is made that the accessibility level of the operand type is not deeper than that of the target type, unless the target type is an anonymous access type of a stand-alone object. If the target type is that of such a stand-alone object, a check is made that the accessibility level of the operand type is not deeper than that of the declaration of the stand-alone object[; then if the check succeeds, the accessibility level of the target type becomes that of the operand type]. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>48.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0148-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This check is needed for operands that are access parameters, for stand-alone anonymous access objects, and in instance bodies.<br />

<MarginText>48.b</MarginText>
Note that this check can never fail for the implicit conversion to the anonymous type of an access parameter that is done when calling a subprogram with an access parameter. <br />

<MarginText>49/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00231-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the operand value is null, the result of the conversion is the null value of the target type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>49.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A conversion to an anonymous access type happens implicitly as part of initializing or assigning to an anonymous access object. <br />

<MarginText>50</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the operand value is not null, then the result designates the same object (or subprogram) as is designated by the operand value, but viewed as being of the target designated subtype (or profile); any checks associated with evaluating a conversion to the target designated subtype are performed. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>50.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The checks are certain to succeed if the target and operand designated subtypes statically match. <br />

<MarginText>51/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0290-1", "AI12-0071-1", "AI12-0333-1"]} />
<p>After conversion of the value to the target type, if the target subtype is constrained, a check is performed that the value satisfies this constraint. If the target subtype excludes null, then a check is made that the value is not null. If predicate checks are enabled for the target subtype (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>), a check is performed that the value satisfies the predicates of the target subtype, unless the conversion is:. <br /></p>

<MarginText>51.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The first check above is a Range{"_"}Check for scalar subtypes, a Discriminant{"_"}Check or Index{"_"}Check for access subtypes, and a Discriminant{"_"}Check for discriminated subtypes. The Length{"_"}Check for an array conversion is performed as part of the conversion to the target type. The check for exclusion of null is an Access{"_"}Check. <br />

<MarginText>51.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0333-1", "AI12-0432-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>a view conversion that is the target of an assignment statement and is not referenced with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code>, or an actual parameter of mode <b>out</b>; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>51.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0333-1"]} />
<li>an implicit subtype conversion of an actual parameter of mode <b>out</b> to the nominal subtype of its formal parameter. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>51.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0333-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The reverse conversion applied to by-copy <b>out</b> parameters is <i>not</i> a view conversion and it is to the nominal subtype of the <i>actual</i> parameter, therefore any enabled predicate checks <i>are</i> performed. <br />

<MarginText>52</MarginText>
<p>For the evaluation of a view conversion, the operand <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is evaluated, and a new view of the object denoted by the operand is created, whose type is the target type; if the target type is composite, checks are performed as above for a value conversion.<br /></p>

<MarginText>53</MarginText>
<p>The properties of this new view are as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>54/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00184-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0017</i>{"}"} If the target type is composite, the bounds or discriminants (if any) of the view are as defined above for a value conversion; each nondiscriminant component of the view denotes the matching component of the operand object; the subtype of the view is constrained if either the target subtype or the operand object is constrained, or if the target subtype is indefinite, or if the operand type is a descendant of the target type and has discriminants that were not inherited from the target type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>55/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<li>If the target type is tagged, then an assignment to the view assigns to the corresponding part of the object denoted by the operand; otherwise, an assignment to the view assigns to the object, after converting the assigned value to the subtype of the object (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error); <br /></li>
<MarginText>56/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0074-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<li>Reading the value of the view yields the result of converting the value of the operand object to the target subtype (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error), except if the object is of an elementary type and the view conversion is passed as an <b>out</b> parameter; in this latter case, the value of the operand object may be used to initialize the formal parameter without checking against any constraint of the target subtype (as described more precisely in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>56.a/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0074-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that even an <b>out</b> parameter of an elementary type is initialized reasonably. <br />

<MarginText>57/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0290-1", "AI12-0096-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>If an Accessibility{"_"}Check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. If a predicate check fails, the effect is as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>. Any other check associated with a conversion raises Constraint{"_"}Error if it fails.<br /></p>

<MarginText>58</MarginText>
<p>Conversion to a type is the same as conversion to an unconstrained subtype of the type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>58.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This definition is needed because the semantics of various constructs involves converting to a type, whereas an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> actually converts to a subtype. For example, the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> is defined to convert the values of the expressions to the type of the range. <br />

<MarginText>58.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A conversion to a scalar type, or, equivalently, to an unconstrained scalar subtype, can raise Constraint{"_"}Error if the value is outside the base range of the type. <br />

<MarginText>58.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0027-1", "AI12-0226-1"]} />
<p>Evaluation of a value conversion of an object either creates a new anonymous object[ (similar to the object created by the evaluation of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or a function call)] or yields a new view of the operand object without creating a new object:<br /></p>

<MarginText>58.2/4</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the target type is a by-reference type and there is a type that is an ancestor of both the target type and the operand type then no new object is created;<br /></li>
<MarginText>58.3/4</MarginText>
<li>If the target type is an array type having aliased components and the operand type is an array type having unaliased components, then a new object is created;<br /></li>
<MarginText>58.4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0226-1"]} />
<li>If the target type is an elementary type, then a new object is created;<br /></li>
<MarginText>58.5/5</MarginText>
<li>Otherwise, it is unspecified whether a new object is created. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>58.6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0027-1"]} />
<p>If a new object is created, then the initialization of that object is an assignment operation.<br /></p>

<MarginText>58.c/4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This makes a difference in the case of converting from an array type with unaliased components to one with aliased components if the element type has a controlled part.<br />

<MarginText>58.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0226-1"]} />
For an elementary type, the representation might change so we require a new object to avoid problems. <br />

<MarginText>58.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0226-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The temporary object need not be materialized in most cases; it should be handled like the return object of a predefined operator. Generally, whether the object exists can only be detected if it is renamed (unless a part of the type is controlled). <br />

<MarginText>58.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0226-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This set of rules does not apply in those cases where the operand is not an object (such as a value conversion of a named number); in such cases, the result isn't an object, so it isn't necessary to describe what that means. The rules cover all value conversions of composite types (since there aren't any values of composite types separate from objects). <br />

<MarginText>59</MarginText>
NOTE 1   In addition to explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>s, type conversions are performed implicitly in situations where the expected type and the actual type of a construct differ, as is permitted by the type resolution rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>). For example, an integer literal is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>, and is implicitly converted when assigned to a target of some specific integer type. Similarly, an actual parameter of a specific tagged type is implicitly converted when the corresponding formal parameter is of a class-wide type.<br />

<MarginText>60</MarginText>
Even when the expected and actual types are the same, implicit subtype conversions are performed to adjust the array bounds (if any) of an operand to match the desired target subtype, or to raise Constraint{"_"}Error if the (possibly adjusted) value does not satisfy the constraints of the target subtype.<br />

<MarginText>61/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01"]} />
NOTE 2   A ramification of the overload resolution rules is that the operand of an (explicit) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> cannot be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> for an Access or Unchecked{"_"}Access attribute. Similarly, such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> enclosed by parentheses is not allowed. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7">4.7</a>) can be used instead of such a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>62</MarginText>
