# 5.2. Assignment Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  43

# 5.2. Assignment Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> replaces the current value of a variable with the result of evaluating an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>assignment{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0173"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> := <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> includes the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and the <i>assignment</i> of the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> into the <i>target</i>. [An assignment operation (as opposed to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment{"_"}statement</a></code>) is performed in other contexts as well, including object initialization and by-copy parameter passing.] The <i>target</i> of an assignment operation is the view of the object to which a value is being assigned; the target of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment{"_"}statement</a></code> is the variable denoted by the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Don't confuse this notion of the &ldquo;target&rdquo; of an assignment with the notion of the &ldquo;target object&rdquo; of an entry call or requeue.<br />

<MarginText>3.b</MarginText>
Don't confuse the term &ldquo;assignment operation&rdquo; with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>. The assignment operation is just one part of the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>. The assignment operation is also a part of the execution of various other constructs; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">7.6.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">Completion and Finalization</a>&rdquo; for a complete list. Note that when we say, &ldquo;such-and-such is assigned to so-and-so&rdquo;, we mean that the assignment operation is being applied, and that so-and-so is the target of the assignment operation. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<p>The <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> is expected to be of any type. The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is the type of the target. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> as a whole is a &ldquo;complete context&rdquo;, so if the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> is overloaded, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> can be used to help disambiguate it. For example: <br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
  type P1 is access R1;{"\n"}  type P2 is access R2;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.c</MarginText>
  function F return P1;{"\n"}  function F return P2;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.d</MarginText>
  X : R1;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}  F.all := X;  -- Right hand side helps resolve left hand side{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<p>The target [denoted by the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>] shall be a variable of a nonlimited type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>If the target is of a tagged class-wide type <i>T</i>'Class, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall either be dynamically tagged, or of type <i>T</i> and tag-indeterminate (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is consistent with the general rule that a single dispatching operation shall not have both dynamically tagged and statically tagged operands. Note that for an object initialization (as opposed to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>), a statically tagged initialization expression is permitted, since there is no chance for confusion (or Tag{"_"}Check failure). Also, in an object initialization, tag-indeterminate expressions of any type covered by <i>T</i>'Class would be allowed, but with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>, that might not work if the tag of the target was for a type that didn't have one of the dispatching operations in the tag-indeterminate expression. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>, the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> are first evaluated in an arbitrary order. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Other rules of the language may require that the bounds of the variable be determined prior to evaluating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, but that does not necessarily require evaluation of the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, as pointed out by the ACID. <br />

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>When the type of the target is class-wide: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is tag-indeterminate (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>), then the controlling tag value for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is the tag of the target; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">Dispatching Operations of Tagged Types</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Otherwise [(the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is dynamically tagged)], a check is made that the tag of the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is the same as that of the target; if this check fails, Constraint{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>The value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is converted to the subtype of the target. [The conversion can raise an exception (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>).] <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">Type Conversions</a>&rdquo; defines what actions and checks are associated with subtype conversion. For non-array subtypes, it is just a constraint check presuming the types match. For array subtypes, it checks the lengths and slides if the target is constrained. &ldquo;Sliding&rdquo; means the array doesn't have to have the same bounds, so long as it is the same length. <br />

<MarginText>12/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>In cases involving controlled types, the target is finalized, and an anonymous object can be used as an intermediate in the assignment, as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">7.6.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">Completion and Finalization</a>&rdquo;. In any case, the converted value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is then <i>assigned</i> to the target, which consists of the following two steps: <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6#Subclause_7.6.1">7.6.1</a> actually says that finalization happens always, but unless controlled types are involved, this finalization during an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> does nothing. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The value of the target becomes the converted value.<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<li>If any part of the target is controlled, its value is adjusted as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If any parts of the object are controlled, abort is deferred during the assignment operation itself, but not during the rest of the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
NOTE   The tag of an object never changes; in particular, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> does not change the tag of the target.<br />

<MarginText>16/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00363-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>16.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The implicit subtype conversion described above for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>s is performed only for the value of the right-hand side expression as a whole; it is not performed for subcomponents of the value.<br />

<MarginText>16.b</MarginText>
The determination of the type of the variable of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> may require consideration of the expression if the variable name can be interpreted as the name of a variable designated by the access value returned by a function call, and similarly, as a component or slice of such a variable (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">The Context of Overload Resolution</a>&rdquo;). <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of assignment statements:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Value := Max{"_"}Value - 1;{"\n"}Shade := Blue;{"\n"}
<MarginText>19</MarginText>
Next{"_"}Frame(F)(M, N) := 2.5;        -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.1">4.1.1</a>{"\n"}U := Dot{"_"}Product(V, W);            -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3">6.3</a>{"\n"}
<MarginText>20/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0056-1"]} />
Writer := (Status ={">"} Open, Unit ={">"} Printer, Line{"_"}Count ={">"} 60);{"\n"}                                   -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>{"\n"}Next.all := (72074, null, Head);   -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples involving scalar subtype conversions:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
I, J : Integer range 1 .. 10 := 5;{"\n"}K    : Integer range 1 .. 20 := 15;{"\n"} ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>23</MarginText>
I := J;  -- identical ranges{"\n"}K := J;  -- compatible ranges{"\n"}J := K;  -- will raise Constraint{"_"}Error if K {">"} 10{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples involving array subtype conversions:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
A : String(1 .. 31);{"\n"}B : String(3 .. 33);{"\n"} ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>26</MarginText>
A := B;  -- same number of components{"\n"}
<MarginText>27</MarginText>
A(1 .. 9)  := "tar sauce";{"\n"}A(4 .. 12) := A(1 .. 9);  -- A(1 .. 12) = "tartar sauce"{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>28/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0452-1"]} />
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">Assignment_statement</a></code>s are well-defined even in the case of overlapping slices of the same array, because the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> are both evaluated before copying the value into the variable. In the above example, an implementation yielding A(1 .. 12) = "tartartartar" would be incorrect.<br /></p>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>29.a</MarginText>
We now allow user-defined finalization and value adjustment actions as part of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">Assignment and Finalization</a>&rdquo;). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>29.b</MarginText>
The special case of array assignment is subsumed by the concept of a subtype conversion, which is applied for all kinds of types, not just arrays. For arrays it provides &ldquo;sliding&rdquo;. For numeric types it provides conversion of a value of a universal type to the specific type of the target. For other types, it generally has no run-time effect, other than a constraint check.<br />

<MarginText>29.c</MarginText>
We now cover in a general way in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#Subclause_3.7.2">3.7.2</a> the erroneous execution possible due to changing the value of a discriminant when the variable in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> is a subcomponent that depends on discriminants. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>29.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
The change of the limited check from a resolution rule to a legality rule is not quite upward compatible. For example <br />

<MarginText>29.e/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type AccNonLim is access NonLim;{"\n"}function Foo (Arg : in Integer) return AccNonLim;{"\n"}type AccLim is access Lim;{"\n"}function Foo (Arg : in Integer) return AccLim;{"\n"}Foo(2).all := Foo(1).all;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>29.f/2</MarginText>
where NonLim is a nonlimited type and Lim is a limited type. The assignment is legal in Ada 95 (only the first Foo would be considered), and is ambiguous in Ada 2005. We made the change because we want limited types to be as similar to nonlimited types as possible. Limited expressions are now allowed in all other contexts (with a similar incompatibility), and it would be odd if assignments had different resolution rules (which would eliminate ambiguities in some cases). Moreover, examples like this one are rare, as they depend on assigning into overloaded function calls. <br />

<a id="Subclause_5.2.1"></a>

## 5.2.1  Target Name Symbols

<MarginText>1/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3"]} />
<p>@, known as the <i>target name</i> of an assignment statement, provides an abbreviation to avoid repetition of potentially long names in assignment statements. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>target{"_"}name</code><a id="S0174"></a><code> ::= </code>@<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3"]} />
<p>[If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code> occurs in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> <i>A</i>, the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <i>V</i> of <i>A</i> is a complete context. The target name is a constant view of <i>V</i>, having the nominal subtype of <i>V</i>.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3", "AI12-0322-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The complete context rule is formally given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>. The constant view rule is formally given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3">3.3</a>; the nominal subtype is a property taken from the target object as described below in Dynamic Semantics. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3", "AI12-0322-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code> shall appear only in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3", "AI12-0322-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> with one or more <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code>s appearing in its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <i>V</i> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> is evaluated first to determine the object denoted by <i>V</i>, and then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> is evaluated with the evaluation of each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code> yielding a constant view of the target whose properties are otherwise identical to those of the view provided by <i>V</i>. The remainder of the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> is as given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2">5.2</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The properties here include static properties like whether the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code> is aliased and the nominal subtype of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code>. It was too weird to give separate rules for static and dynamic properties that said almost the same thing. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0322-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Use of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code> can be erroneous if the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <i>V</i> is a discriminant-dependent component, and some other constituent of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> modifies the discriminant governing the component <i>V</i>. The assignment probably would be erroneous anyway, but the use of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0174">target_name</a></code> eliminates the possibility that a later evaluation of <i>V</i> raises an exception before any erroneous execution occurs. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#Subclause_3.7.2">3.7.2</a>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>6/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Examples of the use of target name symbols:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>7/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3", "AI12-0379-1", "AI12-0442-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Board(1, 1) := @ + 1.0;{"\n"}            -- An abbreviation for Board(1, 1) := Board(1, 1) + 1.0;{"\n"}            -- (Board is declared in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.1">3.6.1</a>).{"\n"}
<MarginText>8/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3"]} />
My{"_"}Complex{"_"}Array : array (1 .. Max) of Complex; -- See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.2">3.3.2</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8">3.8</a>.{"\n"}...{"\n"}-- Square the element in the Count (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>) position:{"\n"}My{"_"}Complex{"_"}Array (Count) := (Re ={">"} @.Re{"*"}{"*"}2 - @.Im{"*"}{"*"}2,{"\n"}                             Im ={">"} 2.0 {"*"} @.Re {"*"} @.Im);{"\n"}   -- A target{"_"}name can be used multiple times and{"\n"}   -- as a prefix if desired.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>8.a/5_5.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0125-3", "AI12-0322-1"]} />
The target name symbol @ is new. <br />

# 5.3. If Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  44

# 5.3. If Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code> selects for execution at most one of the enclosed <code>sequences{"_"}of{"_"}statements</code>, depending on the (truth) value of one or more corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>s.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>if{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0175"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>if</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> <b>then</b><br />      <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />   {"{"}<b>elsif</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> <b>then</b><br />      <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>{"}"}<br />   [<b>else</b><br />      <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>]<br />    <b>end</b> <b>if</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<p><i>Paragraphs 3 and 4 were deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> specified after <b>if</b>, and any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>s specified after <b>elsif</b>, are evaluated in succession (treating a final <b>else</b> as <b>elsif</b> True <b>then</b>), until one evaluates to True or all <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>s are evaluated and yield False. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> evaluates to True, then the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> is executed; otherwise, none of them is executed. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The part about all evaluating to False can't happen if there is an <b>else</b>, since that is herein considered equivalent to <b>elsif</b> True <b>then</b>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of if statements:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
if Month = December and Day = 31 then{"\n"}   Month := January;{"\n"}   Day   := 1;{"\n"}   Year  := Year + 1;{"\n"}end if;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
if Line{"_"}Too{"_"}Short then{"\n"}   raise Layout{"_"}Error;{"\n"}elsif Line{"_"}Full then{"\n"}   New{"_"}Line;{"\n"}   Put(Item);{"\n"}else{"\n"}   Put(Item);{"\n"}end if;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
if My{"_"}Car.Owner.Vehicle /= My{"_"}Car then            -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}   Report ("Incorrect data");{"\n"}end if;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>9.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0147-1"]} />
Moved definition of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.7">4.5.7</a> in order to eliminate a forward reference. <br />

# 5.4. Case Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  45

# 5.4. Case Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> selects for execution one of a number of alternative <code>sequences{"_"}of{"_"}statements</code>; the chosen alternative is defined by the value of an expression.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>case{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0176"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>case</b> <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> <b>is</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0177">case_statement_alternative</a></code><br />      {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0177">case_statement_alternative</a></code>{"}"}<br />   <b>end case</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>case{"_"}statement{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0177"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>when</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> ={">"}<br />      <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>The <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is expected to be of any discrete type. The expected type for each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> is the type of the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0133">choice_expression</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>s given as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> shall be static. [A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> <b>others</b>, if present, shall appear alone and in the last <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1", "AI05-0240-1"]} />
<p>The possible values of the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall be covered (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>) as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0240-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The meaning of "covered" here and in the following rules is that of the term "cover a value" that is defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>7/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0003-1", "AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0188-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0071-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> [(including a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>)] having a static and constrained nominal subtype, then each non-<b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> shall cover only values in that subtype that satisfy its predicates (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>), and each value of that subtype that satisfies its predicates shall be covered by some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> [(either explicitly or by <b>others</b>)]. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Although not official <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s of objects, a value conversion still has a defined nominal subtype, namely its target subtype. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>. <br />

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the type of the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is <i>root{"_"}integer</i>, <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>, or a descendant of a formal scalar type, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> shall have an <b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is because the base range is implementation defined for <i>root{"_"}integer</i> and <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>, and not known statically in the case of a formal scalar type. <br />

<MarginText>9/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Otherwise, each value of the base range of the type of the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall be covered [(either explicitly or by <b>others</b>)]. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>Two distinct <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> shall not cover the same value. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The goal of these coverage rules is that any possible value of the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> should be covered by exactly one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>, and that this should be checked at compile time. The goal is achieved in most cases, but there are two minor loopholes: <br />

<MarginText>10.b</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the expression reads an object with an invalid representation (e.g. an uninitialized object), then the value can be outside the covered range. This can happen for static constrained subtypes, as well as nonstatic or unconstrained subtypes. It cannot, however, happen if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> has the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> <b>others</b>, because <b>others</b> covers all values, even those outside the subtype.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01", "AI05-0188-1"]} />
<li>If the compiler chooses to represent the value of an expression of an unconstrained subtype in a way that includes values outside the bounds of the subtype, then those values can be outside the covered range. For example, if X: Integer := Integer'Last;, and the case <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is X+1, then the implementation might choose to produce the correct value, which is outside the bounds of Integer. (It might raise Constraint{"_"}Error instead.) This case can only happen for nongeneric subtypes that are either unconstrained or nonstatic (or both). It can only happen if there is no <b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.d</MarginText>
In the uninitialized variable case, the value might be anything; hence, any alternative can be chosen, or Constraint{"_"}Error can be raised. (We intend to prevent, however, jumping to random memory locations and the like.) In the out-of-range case, the behavior is more sensible: if there is an <b>others</b>, then the implementation may choose to raise Constraint{"_"}Error on the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (as usual), or it may choose to correctly evaluate the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and therefore choose the <b>others</b> alternative. Otherwise (no <b>others</b>), Constraint{"_"}Error is raised either way &mdash; on the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> evaluation, or for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> itself.<br />

<MarginText>10.e</MarginText>
For an enumeration type with a discontiguous set of internal codes (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.4">13.4</a>), the only way to get values in between the proper values is via an object with an invalid representation; there is no &ldquo;out-of-range&rdquo; situation that can produce them. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>, the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is first evaluated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<p>If the value of the <i>selecting{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is covered by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete{"_"}choice{"_"}list</a></code> of some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0177">case{"_"}statement{"_"}alternative</a></code>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code>{"_"}alternative</code> is executed.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>Otherwise (the value is not covered by any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>, perhaps due to being outside the base range), Constraint{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In this case, the value fails to satisfy its (static) predicate (possible when the predicate is disabled), is outside the base range of its type, or is an invalid representation.<br />

<MarginText>14/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE   The execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> chooses one and only one alternative. Qualification of the expression of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> by a static subtype can often be used to limit the number of choices that can be given explicitly. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of case statements:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
case Sensor is{"\n"}   when Elevation	={">"} Record{"_"}Elevation(Sensor{"_"}Value);{"\n"}   when Azimuth	={">"} Record{"_"}Azimuth  (Sensor{"_"}Value);{"\n"}   when Distance	={">"} Record{"_"}Distance (Sensor{"_"}Value);{"\n"}   when others	={">"} null;{"\n"}end case;{"\n"}
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
case Today is{"\n"}   when Mon	={">"} Compute{"_"}Initial{"_"}Balance;{"\n"}   when Fri	={">"} Compute{"_"}Closing{"_"}Balance;{"\n"}   when Tue .. Thu	={">"} Generate{"_"}Report(Today);{"\n"}   when Sat .. Sun	={">"} null;{"\n"}end case;{"\n"}
<MarginText>18</MarginText>
case Bin{"_"}Number(Count) is{"\n"}   when 1	={">"} Update{"_"}Bin(1);{"\n"}   when 2	={">"} Update{"_"}Bin(2);{"\n"}   when 3 | 4	={">"}{"\n"}      Empty{"_"}Bin(1);{"\n"}      Empty{"_"}Bin(2);{"\n"}   when others	={">"} raise Error;{"\n"}end case;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>18.a.1/1</MarginText>
In Ada 95, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>s are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s, whereas in Ada 83, they were <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s. Therefore, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>, and the result subtype is static, it is illegal to specify a choice outside the bounds of the subtype. For this case in Ada 83 choices only are required to be in the base range of the type.<br />

<MarginText>18.a.2/1</MarginText>
In addition, the rule about which choices must be covered is unchanged in Ada 95. Therefore, for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>, Ada 83 required covering all choices in the base range, while Ada 95 only requires covering choices in the bounds of the subtype. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> does not include an <b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>, then a legal Ada 83 <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> will be illegal in Ada 95 if the bounds of the subtype are different than the bounds of the base type. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>18.a</MarginText>
In Ada 83, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> is not allowed to be of a generic formal type. This restriction is removed in Ada 95; an <b>others</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> is required instead.<br />

<MarginText>18.b</MarginText>
In Ada 95, a function call is the name of an object; this was not true in Ada 83 (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">4.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1">Names</a>&rdquo;). This change makes the following <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> legal: <br />

<MarginText>18.c</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
subtype S is Integer range 1..2;{"\n"}function F return S;{"\n"}case F is{"\n"}   when 1 ={">"} ...;{"\n"}   when 2 ={">"} ...;{"\n"}   -- No others needed.{"\n"}end case;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>18.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
Note that the result subtype given in a function <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> is ignored; for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code> whose expression calls a such a function, the full coverage rules are checked using the result subtype of the original function. Note that predefined operators such as "+" have an unconstrained result subtype (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.1">4.5.1</a>). Note that generic formal functions do not have static result subtypes. Note that the result subtype of an inherited subprogram need not correspond to any nameable subtype; there is still a perfectly good result subtype, though. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>18.e</MarginText>
Ada 83 forgot to say what happens for &ldquo;legally&rdquo; out-of-bounds values.<br />

<MarginText>18.f</MarginText>
We take advantage of rules and terms (e.g. <i>cover a value</i>) defined for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code>s in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">Variant Parts and Discrete Choices</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>18.g</MarginText>
In the Name Resolution Rule for the case expression, we no longer need RM83-5.4(3)'s &ldquo;which must be determinable independently of the context in which the expression occurs, but using the fact that the expression must be of a discrete type&rdquo;, because the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is now a complete context. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">The Context of Overload Resolution</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>18.h</MarginText>
Since <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>s are now defined as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s, their coverage rule is now covered under the general rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s, rather than being separated out along with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code>s. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>18.i/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0003-1"]} />
Rewording to reflect that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> is now a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>18.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
Revised for changes to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code>s made to allow static predicates (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>) as case choices (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#Subclause_3.8.1">3.8.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>18.k/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
Added the <i>selecting{"_"}</i> prefix to make this wording consistent with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0151">case_expression</a></code>, and to clarify which <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is being talked about in the wording. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>18.l/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0071-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Updated wording of case coverage to use the new term "satisfies the predicates" (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>). <br />

# 5.5. Loop Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5.mdx

sidebar_position:  46

# 5.5. Loop Statements

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> that is to be executed repeatedly, zero or more times with the iterations running sequentially or concurrently with one another.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>loop{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0178"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<i>loop{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0172">statement_identifier</a></code>:]<br />      [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code>] <b>loop</b><br />         <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />       <b>end</b> <b>loop</b> [<i>loop{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0251-1", "AI12-0266-1", "AI12-0326-2", "AI12-0355-2"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iteration{"_"}scheme</code><a id="S0179"></a><code> ::= </code><b>while</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code><br />   | <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code><br />   | <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code><br />   | [<b>parallel</b> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>]]<br />     <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code><br />   | <b>parallel</b> [(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>)] [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>]<br />     <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code><br />   | <b>parallel</b> [(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>)] [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>]<br />     <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0251-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>chunk{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0180"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <i>integer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> <b>in</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0181"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> <b>in</b> [<b>reverse</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code><br />     [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iterator{"_"}filter</code><a id="S0182"></a><code> ::= </code><b>when</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> has a <i>loop{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0172">statement_identifier</a></code>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall be repeated after the <b>end loop</b>; otherwise, there shall not be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> after the <b>end loop</b>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> that begins with the reserved word <b>parallel</b> shall not have the reserved word <b>reverse</b> in its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0251-1"]} />
<p>In a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> that is an <i>integer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, the <i>integer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is expected to be of any integer type. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0061-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> declares a <i>loop parameter</i>, which is an object whose subtype (and nominal subtype) is that defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0251-1"]} />
<p>In a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> declares a <i>chunk parameter</i> object whose subtype (and nominal subtype) is that defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0327-1"]} />
<p>The <i>filter</i> of an <i>iterator construct</i> (a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code>) is defined to be <i>satisfied</i> when there is no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code> for the iterator construct, or when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code> evaluates to True for a given iteration of the iterator construct.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>iterator filter</b> &mdash; construct that is used to restrict the elements produced by an iteration to those for which a boolean condition evaluates to True<br />

<MarginText>6.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0327-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with an iterator construct is said to be <i>conditionally executed</i>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s are executed only when the filter of the iterator construct is satisfied.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0327-1"]} />
<p>The loop iterators <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> can also be used in contexts other than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>s (for example, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.5">4.3.5</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.8">4.5.8</a>). In such a context, the iterator <i>conditionally produces</i> values in the order specified for the associated construct below or in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>. The values produced are the values given to the loop parameter when the filter of the iterator construct is satisfied for that value. [No value is produced when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code> evaluates to False.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> is executed zero or more times, until the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> is complete. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> is complete when a transfer of control occurs that transfers control out of the loop, or, in the case of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code>, as specified below.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with a <b>while</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code>, the condition is evaluated before each execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>; if the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> is True, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> is executed; if False, the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code> is complete.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0251-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
<p>If the reserved word <b>parallel</b> is present in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> (a <i>parallel loop</i>), the iterations are partitioned into one or more <i>chunks</i>, each with its own separate logical thread of control (see Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>). If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> is present in a parallel loop, it is elaborated first, and the result of the elaboration determines the maximum number of chunks used for the parallel loop. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> is an <i>integer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>, the elaboration evaluates the expression, and the value of the expression determines the maximum number of chunks. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> is present, the elaboration elaborates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>, which defines the subtype of the chunk parameter, and the number of values in this subtype determines the maximum number of chunks. After elaborating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, a check is made that the determined maximum number of chunks is greater than zero. If this check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0071-1", "AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0251-1", "AI12-0294-1", "AI12-0355-2", "AI12-0416-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> that has an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> including a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>, after elaborating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, if any, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</a></code> is elaborated. This elaborates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>, which defines the subtype of the loop parameter. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> defines a subtype with a null range, the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> is complete. Otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> is conditionally executed once for each value of the discrete subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> that satisfies the predicates of the subtype (or until the loop is left as a consequence of a transfer of control). Prior to each such iteration, the corresponding value of the discrete subtype is assigned to the loop parameter associated with the given iteration. If the loop is a parallel loop, each chunk has its own logical thread of control with its own copy of the loop parameter; otherwise (a <i>sequential loop</i>), a single logical thread of control performs the loop, and there is a single copy of the loop parameter. Each logical thread of control handles a distinct subrange of the values of the subtype of the loop parameter such that all values are covered with no overlaps. Within each logical thread of control, the values are assigned to the loop parameter in increasing order unless the reserved word <b>reverse</b> is present, in which case the values are assigned in decreasing order. In the absence of a transfer of control, the associated parallel construct of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> is complete when all of its logical threads of control are complete. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0294-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>This wording does not describe when the loop parameter object(s) are created. That creation has no side-effects (other than possibly raising Storage{"_"}Error, but anything can do that), so we simplified the wording by leaving it out. Each object has to be created before any iteration that depends on it starts, but we do not (for instance) require that the objects are all created at once at the start of the loop, nor that the objects are created after the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>9.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0294-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>9.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The predicate (if any) necessarily has to be a static predicate as a dynamic predicate is explicitly disallowed &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>. <br />

<MarginText>9.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>If there is a predicate, the loop still visits the values in the order of the underlying base type; the order of the values in the predicate is irrelevant. This is the case so that the following loops have the same sequence of calls and parameters on procedure Call for any subtype S: <br />

<MarginText>9.d</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for I in S loop{"\n"}   Call (I);{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9.e</MarginText>
for I in S'Base loop{"\n"}   if I in S then{"\n"}      Call (I);{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0416-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The rules for completing a parallel construct when there is a transfer of control are given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1">5.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0251-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> is present, then the logical thread of control associated with a given chunk has its own copy of the chunk parameter initialized with a distinct value from the discrete subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>. The values of the chunk parameters are assigned such that they increase with increasing values of the ranges covered by the corresponding loop parameters.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0251-1"]} />
<p>Whether or not a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> is present in a parallel loop, the total number of iterations of the loop represents an upper bound on the number of logical threads of control devoted to the loop.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>[For details about the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> including an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>. For details relating to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code>, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.3">5.5.3</a>.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1"]} />
NOTE 1   A loop parameter declared by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> is a constant; it cannot be updated within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the loop (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3">3.3</a>).<br />

<MarginText>14/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 2   No separate <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> is expected for a loop parameter, since the loop parameter is automatically declared by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>. The scope of a loop parameter extends from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> to the end of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>, and the visibility rules are such that a loop parameter is only visible within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the loop. <br />

<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>An implementation could give a warning if a variable is hidden by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> of a for loop is elaborated just once. Use of the reserved word <b>reverse</b> does not alter the discrete subtype defined, so that the following <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code>s are not equivalent; the first has a null range. <br />

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for J in reverse 1 .. 0{"\n"}for J in 0 .. 1{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code> has a static discrete range, the subtype of the loop parameter is static. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a loop statement without an iteration scheme:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
loop{"\n"}   Get(Current{"_"}Character);{"\n"}   exit when Current{"_"}Character = '{"*"}';{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a loop statement with a <b>while</b> iteration scheme:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>20</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
while Bid(N).Price {"<"} Cut{"_"}Off.Price loop{"\n"}   Record{"_"}Bid(Bid(N).Price);{"\n"}   N := N + 1;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a loop statement with a <b>for</b> iteration scheme:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for J in Buffer'Range loop     --  works even with a null range{"\n"}   if Buffer(J) /= Space then{"\n"}      Put(Buffer(J));{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a loop statement with a name:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Summation:{"\n"}   while Next /= Head loop       -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}      Sum  := Sum + Next.Value;{"\n"}      Next := Next.Succ;{"\n"}   end loop Summation;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>25/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0312-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a simple parallel loop:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>26/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
-- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>{"\n"}parallel{"\n"}for I in Grid'Range(1) loop{"\n"}   Grid(I, 1) := (for all J in Grid'Range(2) ={">"} Grid(I,J) = True);{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>27/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a parallel loop with a chunk specification:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>28/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
declare{"\n"}   subtype Chunk{"_"}Number is Natural range 1 .. 8;{"\n"}
<MarginText>29/5</MarginText>
   Partial{"_"}Sum,{"\n"}   Partial{"_"}Max : array (Chunk{"_"}Number) of Natural := (others ={">"} 0);{"\n"}   Partial{"_"}Min : array (Chunk{"_"}Number) of Natural :={"\n"}                       (others ={">"} Natural'Last);{"\n"}
<MarginText>30/5</MarginText>
begin{"\n"}   parallel (Chunk in Chunk{"_"}Number){"\n"}   for I in Grid'Range(1) loop{"\n"}      declare{"\n"}         True{"_"}Count : constant Natural :={"\n"}           [for J in Grid'Range(2) ={">"}{"\n"}              (if Grid (I, J) then 1 else 0)]'Reduce("+",0);{"\n"}      begin{"\n"}         Partial{"_"}Sum (Chunk) := @ + True{"_"}Count;{"\n"}         Partial{"_"}Min (Chunk) := Natural'Min(@, True{"_"}Count);{"\n"}         Partial{"_"}Max (Chunk) := Natural'Max(@, True{"_"}Count);{"\n"}      end;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>31/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0386-1"]} />
   Put{"_"}Line{"\n"}     ("Total=" & Partial{"_"}Sum'Reduce("+", 0)'Image &{"\n"}      ", Min=" & Partial{"_"}Min'Reduce(Natural'Min, Natural'Last)'Image &{"\n"}      ", Max=" & Partial{"_"}Max'Reduce(Natural'Max, 0)'Image);{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>32/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0312-1"]} />
<p><i>For an example of an</i> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code><i>, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.8">4.5.8</a>.</i> <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>32.a</MarginText>
The constant-ness of loop parameters is specified in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3">3.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3">Objects and Named Numbers</a>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>32.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0262-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
Generalized <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>s are allowed in <b>for</b> loops; these are documented as an extension in the appropriate subclause. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>32.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0251-1", "AI12-0266-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
Parallel loops are new.<br />

<MarginText>32.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1"]} />
An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code> is now allowed on <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0181">loop_parameter_specification</a></code>s. This is mainly for consistency with aggregate and reduction iterators, where it eliminates the need for temporary objects. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>32.e/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0071-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Updated wording of loop execution to use the new term "satisfies the predicates" (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>).<br />

<MarginText>32.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0061-1"]} />
Added text so that the nominal subtype of a loop parameter is clearly defined. <br />

<a id="Subclause_5.5.1"></a>

## 5.5.1  User-Defined Iterator Types

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2"]} />
<p>The following language-defined generic library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type Cursor;{"\n"}   with function Has{"_"}Element (Position : Cursor) return Boolean;{"\n"}package Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces{"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking ={">"} False is{"\n"}
<MarginText>3/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
   type Forward{"_"}Iterator is limited interface;{"\n"}   function First (Object : Forward{"_"}Iterator) return Cursor is abstract;{"\n"}   function Next (Object : Forward{"_"}Iterator; Position : Cursor){"\n"}      return Cursor is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
   type Reversible{"_"}Iterator is limited interface and Forward{"_"}Iterator;{"\n"}   function Last (Object : Reversible{"_"}Iterator) return Cursor is abstract;{"\n"}   function Previous (Object : Reversible{"_"}Iterator; Position : Cursor){"\n"}      return Cursor is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.1/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   type Parallel{"_"}Iterator is limited interface and Forward{"_"}Iterator;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.2/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   subtype Chunk{"_"}Index is Positive;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.3/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   function Is{"_"}Split (Object : Parallel{"_"}Iterator){"\n"}      return Boolean is abstract;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.4/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   procedure Split{"_"}Into{"_"}Chunks (Object     : in out Parallel{"_"}Iterator;{"\n"}                                Max{"_"}Chunks : in     Chunk{"_"}Index) is abstract{"\n"}      with Pre'Class   ={">"} not Object.Is{"_"}Split or else raise Program{"_"}Error,{"\n"}           Post'Class  ={">"} Object.Is{"_"}Split and then{"\n"}                          Object.Chunk{"_"}Count {"<"}= Max{"_"}Chunks;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.5/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   function Chunk{"_"}Count (Object : Parallel{"_"}Iterator){"\n"}      return Chunk{"_"}Index is abstract{"\n"}      with Pre'Class   ={">"} Object.Is{"_"}Split or else raise Program{"_"}Error;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.6/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   function First (Object : Parallel{"_"}Iterator;{"\n"}                   Chunk  : Chunk{"_"}Index) return Cursor is abstract{"\n"}      with Pre'Class   ={">"} (Object.Is{"_"}Split and then{"\n"}                              Chunk {"<"}= Object.Chunk{"_"}Count){"\n"}                           or else raise Program{"_"}Error;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.7/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   function Next (Object   : Parallel{"_"}Iterator;{"\n"}                  Position : Cursor;{"\n"}                  Chunk    : Chunk{"_"}Index) return Cursor is abstract{"\n"}      with Pre'Class   ={">"} (Object.Is{"_"}Split and then{"\n"}                              Chunk {"<"}= Object.Chunk{"_"}Count){"\n"}                           or else raise Program{"_"}Error;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.8/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
   type Parallel{"_"}Reversible{"_"}Iterator is limited interface{"\n"}      and Parallel{"_"}Iterator and Reversible{"_"}Iterator;{"\n"}
<MarginText>5/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
end Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.a/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This package must allow blocking (Nonblocking ={">"} False) for compatibility. The purpose of this package is to provide a template for overriding user-defined routines; and such routines can only allow blocking if the root type does so. Users can still declare their overridding routines nonblocking if they wish. <br />

<MarginText>6/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>An <i>iterator type</i> is a type descended from the Forward{"_"}Iterator interface from some instance of Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces. A <i>reversible iterator type</i> is a type descended from the Reversible{"_"}Iterator interface from some instance of Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces. A <i>parallel iterator type</i> is a type descended from the Parallel{"_"}Iterator interface from some instance of Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces. A type descended from the Parallel{"_"}Reversible{"_"}Iterator interface from some instance of Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces is both a parallel iterator type and a reversible iterator type. An <i>iterator object</i> is an object of an iterator type. A <i>reversible iterator object</i> is an object of a reversible iterator type. A <i>parallel iterator object</i> is an object of a parallel iterator type. The formal subtype Cursor from the associated instance of Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces is the <i>iteration cursor subtype</i> for the iterator type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1"]} />
<p>The following type-related operational aspects may be specified for an indexable container type <i>T</i> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.6">4.1.6</a>):<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0428-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Default{"_"}Iterator</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is specified by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes exactly one function declared immediately within the same declaration list in which <i>T</i>, or the declaration completed by <i>T</i>, is declared, whose first parameter is of type <i>T</i> or <i>T</i>'Class or an access parameter whose designated type is type <i>T</i> or <i>T</i>'Class, whose other parameters, if any, have default expressions, and whose result type is an iterator type. This function is the <i>default iterator function</i> for <i>T</i>. Its result subtype is the <i>default iterator subtype</i> for <i>T</i>. The iteration cursor subtype for the default iterator subtype is the <i>default cursor subtype</i> for <i>T</i>. This aspect is inherited by descendants of type <i>T</i> (including <i>T</i>'Class).<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>8.a/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Default{"_"}Iterator: </b>Default iterator to be used in <b>for</b> loops.<br />

<MarginText>9/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Iterator{"_"}Element</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is specified by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a subtype. This is the <i>default element subtype</i> for <i>T</i>. This aspect is inherited by descendants of type <i>T</i> (including <i>T</i>'Class).<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>9.a/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Iterator{"_"}Element: </b>Element type to be used for user-defined iterators.<br />

<MarginText>9.1/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Iterator{"_"}View</dt>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is specified by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a type <i>T2</i> with the following properties:<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>9.2/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li><i>T2</i> is declared in the same compilation unit as <i>T</i>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.3/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<li><i>T2</i> is an iterable container type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.4/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<li><i>T2</i> has a single discriminant which is an access discriminant designating <i>T</i>; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.5/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<li>The default iterator subtypes for <i>T</i> and <i>T2</i> statically match. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.6/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>This aspect is never inherited[, even by <i>T</i>'Class].<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>9.b/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Iterator{"_"}View allows specifying an alternative type to be automatically used by container element iterators; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>. This allows setting state for an iteration only once rather than for each individual reference. <br />

<MarginText>9.c/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Since Iterator{"_"}View is not inherited, it does not apply to <i>T</i>'Class. Otherwise, the type of the iterator object would not be known at compile-time (since it necessarily has to be different for each descendant). <br />

<MarginText>9.d/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Iterator{"_"}View: </b>An alternative type to used for container element iterators.<br />

<MarginText>10/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>An <i>iterable container type</i> is an indexable container type with specified Default{"_"}Iterator and Iterator{"_"}Element aspects. A <i>reversible iterable container type</i> is an iterable container type with the default iterator type being a reversible iterator type. A <i>parallel iterable container type</i> is an iterable container type with the default iterator type being a parallel iterator type. An <i>iterable container object</i> is an object of an iterable container type. A <i>reversible iterable container object</i> is an object of a reversible iterable container type. A <i>parallel iterable container object</i> is an object of a parallel iterable container type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>iterable container type</b> &mdash; type that has user-defined behavior for iteration, via the Default{"_"}Iterator and Iterator{"_"}Element aspects<br />

<MarginText>11.1/4_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0138-1"]} />
<p>The Default{"_"}Iterator and Iterator{"_"}Element aspects are nonoverridable (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.b/4_5.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that all descendants of an iterable container type have aspects with the same properties. This prevents generic contract problems with formal derived types. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>12/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1"]} />
<p>The Constant{"_"}Indexing aspect (if any) of an iterable container type <i>T</i> shall denote exactly one function with the following properties:<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the result type of the function is covered by the default element type of <i>T</i> or is a reference type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.5">4.1.5</a>) with an access discriminant designating a type covered by the default element type of <i>T</i>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<li>the type of the second parameter of the function covers the default cursor type for <i>T</i>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<li>if there are more than two parameters, the additional parameters all have default expressions.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<p>This function (if any) is the <i>default constant indexing function</i> for <i>T</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This does not mean that Constant{"_"}Indexing has to designate only one subprogram, only that there is only one routine that meets all of these properties. There can be other routines designated by Constant{"_"}Indexing, but they cannot have the profile described above. For instance, map containers have a version of Constant{"_"}Indexing that takes a key instead of a cursor; this is allowed. <br />

<MarginText>17/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1"]} />
<p>The Variable{"_"}Indexing aspect (if any) of an iterable container type <i>T</i> shall denote exactly one function with the following properties:<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the result type of the function is a reference type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.5">4.1.5</a>) with an access discriminant designating a type covered by the default element type of <i>T</i>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>19/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<li>the type of the second parameter of the function covers the default cursor type for <i>T</i>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<li>if there are more than two parameters, the additional parameters all have default expressions.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
