<p>This function (if any) is the <i>default variable indexing function</i> for <i>T</i>.<br /></p>

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>22/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0354-1"]} />
<p>A call on the First or Next operation on a given Parallel{"_"}Iterator object with a given Chunk value, which does not propagate an exception, should return a Cursor value that either yields False when passed to Has{"_"}Element, or that identifies an element distinct from any Cursor value returned by a call on a First or Next operation on the same Parallel{"_"}Iterator object with a different Chunk value. If the First or Next operations with a Chunk parameter behave in any other manner, execution is erroneous. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This describes the expectations from a user-written parallel iterator. If the expectations are not met, execution is erroneous so that implementations do not need to go to heroic efforts to avoid problems caused by bad iterators. This is similar to the handling of storage pools, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>22.b/3_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2"]} />
User-defined iterator types are new in Ada 2012. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>22.c/4_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0138-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Defined Default{"_"}Iterator and Iterator{"_"}Element to be nonoveridable, which makes redefinitions and hiding of these aspects illegal. It's possible that some program could violate one of these new restrictions, but in most cases this can easily be worked around by using overriding rather than redefinition.<br />

<MarginText>22.d/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
Various new types and subprograms are newly added to Ada.Iterator{"_"}Interfaces. Therefore, a use clause conflict is possible; see the introduction of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a> for more on this topic. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>22.e/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
Aspect Iterator{"_"}View is new; it allows container element iterators to set the tampering state once rather than for each use of the element.<br />

<MarginText>22.f/5_5.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1", "AI12-0354-1"]} />
Parallel iterator interfaces are new; they allow user-defined parallel loops to be defined. <br />

<a id="Subclause_5.5.2"></a>

## 5.5.2  Generalized Loop Iteration

<MarginText>1/3_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2"]} />
<p>Generalized forms of loop iteration are provided by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1", "AI12-0156-1", "AI12-0250-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iterator{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0183"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> [: <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop_parameter_subtype_indication</a></code>] <b>in</b> [<b>reverse</b>] <i>iterator{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />      [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code>]<br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> [: <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop_parameter_subtype_indication</a></code>] <b>of</b> [<b>reverse</b>] <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />      [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.1/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0156-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</code><a id="S0184"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.2/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is for a parallel construct, the reserved word <b>reverse</b> shall not appear in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/3_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1"]} />
<p>For the first form of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>, called a <i>generalized iterator</i>, the expected type for the <i>iterator{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is any iterator type. For the second form of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>, the expected type for the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is any array or iterable container type. If the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes an array object, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is called an <i>array component iterator</i>; otherwise it is called a <i>container element iterator</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>iterator</b> &mdash; construct that is used to loop over the elements of an array or container<br />Note: Iterators can be user defined, and can perform arbitrary computations to access elements from a container.<br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>If the reserved word <b>reverse</b> appears, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is a <i>reverse iterator</i>. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is for a parallel construct, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is a <i>parallel iterator</i>. Otherwise, it is a <i>forward iterator</i>. Forward and reverse iterators are collectively called <i>sequential</i> iterators. In a reverse generalized iterator, the <i>iterator{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall be of a reversible iterator type. In a parallel generalized iterator, the <i>iterator{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall be of a parallel iterator type. In a reverse container element iterator, the default iterator type for the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall be a reversible iterator type. In a parallel container element iterator, the default iterator type for the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall be of a parallel iterator type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI12-0151-1", "AI12-0156-1", "AI12-0183-1"]} />
<p>The subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>, if any, of a generalized iterator shall statically match the iteration cursor subtype. The subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>, if any, of an array component iterator shall statically match the component subtype of the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. The subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop{"_"}parameter{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>, if any, of a container element iterator shall statically match the default element subtype for the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2"]} />
<p>In a container element iterator whose <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> has type <i>T</i>, if the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes a constant or the Variable{"_"}Indexing aspect is not specified for <i>T</i>, then the Constant{"_"}Indexing aspect shall be specified for <i>T</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.1/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0047-1"]} />
<p>The <i>iterator{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> shall not denote a subcomponent that depends on discriminants of an object whose nominal subtype is unconstrained, unless the object is known to be constrained.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is the same rule that applies to renames; it serves the same purpose of preventing the object from disappearing while the iterator is still using it. <br />

<MarginText>6.2/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0120-1"]} />
<p>A container element iterator is illegal if the call of the default iterator function that creates the loop iterator (see below) is illegal.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.b/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This can happen if the parameter to the default iterator function is <b>in out</b> and the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is a constant. The wording applies to any reason that the call would be illegal, as it's possible that one of the default parameters would be illegal, or that some accessibility check would fail. <br />

<MarginText>6.3/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0120-1"]} />
<p>A generalized iterator is illegal if the iteration cursor subtype of the <i>iterator{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is a limited type at the point of the generalized iterator. A container element iterator is illegal if the default cursor subtype of the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is a limited type at the point of the container element iterator.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.c/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>If the cursor type is limited, the assignment to the loop parameter for a generalized iterator would be illegal. The same is true for a container element iterator. We have to say "at the point of the iterator" as the limitedness of a type can change due to visibility. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>7/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0269-1", "AI05-0292-1", "AI12-0156-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> declares a <i>loop parameter</i>. In a generalized iterator, an array component iterator, or a container element iterator, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop_parameter_subtype_indication</a></code> is present, it determines the nominal subtype of the loop parameter. In a generalized iterator, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop_parameter_subtype_indication</a></code> is not present, the nominal subtype of the loop parameter is the iteration cursor subtype. In an array component iterator, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop_parameter_subtype_indication</a></code> is not present, the nominal subtype of the loop parameter is the component subtype of the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. In a container element iterator, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop_parameter_subtype_indication</a></code> is not present, the nominal subtype of the loop parameter is the default element subtype for the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/3_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1"]} />
<p>In a generalized iterator, the loop parameter is a constant. In an array component iterator, the loop parameter is a constant if the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes a constant; otherwise it denotes a variable. In a container element iterator, the loop parameter is a constant if the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes a constant, or if the Variable{"_"}Indexing aspect is not specified for the type of the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>; otherwise it is a variable.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0093-1", "AI12-0156-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The loop parameter of a generalized iterator has the same accessibility as the loop statement. This means that the loop parameter object is finalized when the loop statement is left. (It also may be finalized as part of assigning a new value to the loop parameter.) For array component iterators, the loop parameter directly denotes an element of the array and has the accessibility of the associated array. For container element iterators, the loop parameter denotes the result of the indexing function call (in the case of a constant indexing) or a generalized reference thereof (in the case of a variable indexing). Roughly speaking, the loop parameter has the accessibility level of a single iteration of the loop. More precisely, the function result (or the generalized reference thereof) is considered to be renamed in the declarative part of a notional block statement which immediately encloses the loop's <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>; the accessibility of the loop parameter is that of the block statement. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>9/3_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2"]} />
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is first elaborated. This elaboration elaborates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>, if any.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>For a sequential generalized iterator, the loop parameter is created, the <i>iterator{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is evaluated, and the denoted iterator object becomes the <i>loop iterator</i>. In a forward generalized iterator, the operation First of the iterator type is called on the loop iterator, to produce the initial value for the loop parameter. If the result of calling Has{"_"}Element on the initial value is False, then the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> is complete. Otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> is conditionally executed and then the Next operation of the iterator type is called with the loop iterator and the current value of the loop parameter to produce the next value to be assigned to the loop parameter. This repeats until the result of calling Has{"_"}Element on the loop parameter is False, or the loop is left as a consequence of a transfer of control. For a reverse generalized iterator, the operations Last and Previous are called rather than First and Next.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0093-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The loop parameter of a generalized iterator is a variable of which the user only has a constant view. It follows the normal rules for a variable of its nominal subtype. In particular, if the nominal subtype is indefinite, the variable is constrained by its initial value. Similarly, if the nominal subtype is class-wide, the variable (like all variables) has the tag of the initial value. Constraint{"_"}Error may be raised by a subsequent iteration if Next or Previous return an object with a different tag or constraint. <br />

<MarginText>10.1/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>For a parallel generalized iterator, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, if any, of the associated parallel construct, is first elaborated, to determine the maximum number of chunks (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>), and then the operation Split{"_"}Into{"_"}Chunks of the iterator type is called, with the determined maximum passed as the Max{"_"}Chunks parameter, specifying the upper bound for the number of loop parameter objects (and the number of logical threads of control) to be associated with the iterator. In the absence of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, the maximum number of chunks is determined in an implementation-defined manner.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.b/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The maximum number of chunks for a parallel generalized iterator without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>10.c/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The Max{"_"}Chunks parameter of the Split{"_"}Into{"_"}Chunks procedure is an upper bound for the number of chunks to be associated with a loop. A container implementation may opt for a lower value for the number of chunks if a more optimal split can be determined. For instance, a tree-based container might create the split based on the number of branches at the top levels of the tree. <br />

<MarginText>10.2/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0266-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>Upon return from Split{"_"}Into{"_"}Chunks, the actual number of chunks for the loop is determined by calling the Chunk{"_"}Count operation of the iterator, at which point one logical thread of control is initiated for each chunk, with an associated chunk index in the range from one to the actual number of chunks.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.3/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0266-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>Within each logical thread of control, a loop parameter is created. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> is present in the associated parallel construct, then a chunk parameter is created and initialized with a value from the discrete subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>, so that the order of the chosen chunk parameter values correspond to the order of the chunk indices associated with the logical threads of control. The operation First of the iterator type that has a Chunk parameter is called on the loop iterator, with Chunk initialized from the corresponding chunk index, to produce the initial value for the loop parameter. If the result of calling Has{"_"}Element on this initial value is False, then the execution of the logical thread of control is complete. Otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> is conditionally executed, and then the Next operation of the iterator type that has a Chunk parameter is called with the loop iterator, the current value of the loop parameter, and the corresponding chunk index, to produce the next value to be assigned to the loop parameter. This repeats until the result of calling Has{"_"}Element on the loop parameter is False, or the associated parallel construct is left as a consequence of a transfer of control.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.4/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0266-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>In the absence of a transfer of control, the associated parallel construct of a parallel generalized iterator is complete when all of its logical threads of control are complete.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1", "AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>For an array component iterator, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> of the associated parallel construct, if any, is first elaborated to determine the maximum number of chunks (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>), and then the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is evaluated and the denoted array object becomes the <i>array for the loop</i>. If the array for the loop is a null array, then the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> is complete. Otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> is conditionally executed with the loop parameter denoting each component of the array for the loop, using a <i>canonical</i> order of components, which is last dimension varying fastest (unless the array has convention Fortran, in which case it is first dimension varying fastest). For a forward array component iterator, the iteration starts with the component whose index values are each the first in their index range, and continues in the canonical order. For a reverse array component iterator, the iteration starts with the component whose index values are each the last in their index range, and continues in the reverse of the canonical order. For a parallel array component iterator, the iteration is broken up into contiguous chunks of the canonical order, such that all components are covered with no overlaps; each chunk has its own logical thread of control with its own loop parameter and iteration within each chunk is in the canonical order. The number of chunks is implementation defined, but is limited in the presence of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> to the determined maximum. The loop iteration proceeds until the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> has been conditionally executed for each component of the array for the loop, or until the loop is left as a consequence of a transfer of control.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The number of chunks for an array component iterator.<br />

<MarginText>11.1/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> is present in the associated parallel construct, then the logical thread of control associated with a given chunk has a chunk parameter initialized with a distinct value from the discrete subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>. The values of the chunk parameters are assigned such that they increase in the canonical order of the starting array components for the chunks.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1", "AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>For a container element iterator, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> of the associated parallel construct, if any, is first elaborated to determine the maximum number of chunks (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>), and then the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is evaluated. If the container type has Iterator{"_"}View specified, an object of the Iterator{"_"}View type is created with the discriminant referencing the iterable container object denoted by the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. This is the <i>iterable container object for the loop</i>. Otherwise, the iterable container object denoted by the <i>iterable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> becomes the iterable container object for the loop. The default iterator function for the type of the iterable container object for the loop is called on the iterable container object and the result is the <i>loop iterator</i>. For a sequential container element iterator, an object of the default cursor subtype is created (the <i>loop cursor</i>). For a parallel container element iterator, each chunk of iterations will have its own loop cursor, again of the default cursor subtype.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>If Iterator{"_"}View is specified, we add an extra object and use that object for this iteration. This allows these iterators to automatically use the stable view (defined in each of the language-defined containers) to do the iteration. That eliminates the need to set and clear the tampering with elements indication each time Reference is called; that eliminates substantial overhead as finalization is typically used to implement the tampering reset. <br />

<MarginText>13/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2", "AI05-0292-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p>A container element iterator then proceeds as described above for a generalized iterator, except that each reference to a loop parameter is replaced by a reference to the corresponding loop cursor. For a container element iterator, the loop parameter for each iteration instead denotes an indexing (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.6">4.1.6</a>) into the iterable container object for the loop, with the only parameter to the indexing being the value of the loop cursor for the given iteration. If the loop parameter is a constant (see above), then the indexing uses the default constant indexing function for the type of the iterable container object for the loop; otherwise it uses the default variable indexing function.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0120-1"]} />
<p>Any exception propagated by the execution of a generalized iterator or container element iterator is propagated by the immediately enclosing loop statement.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This text covers exceptions raised by called functions that make up the execution of the iterator as well as exceptions raised by the assignment to the loop parameter or cursor. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>15/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a parallel generalized loop over an array:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>16/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0269-1", "AI12-0266-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
parallel{"\n"}for Element of Board loop  -- See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.1">3.6.1</a>.{"\n"}   Element := Element {"*"} 2.0; -- Double each element of Board, a two-dimensional array.{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>17/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0268-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>For examples of use of generalized iterators, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.33">A.18.33</a> and the corresponding container packages in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.3">A.18.3</a>.</i><br /></p>

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>17.a/3_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0139-2"]} />
Generalized forms of loop iteration are new. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.b/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0047-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a rule to ensure that the object being iterated cannot be a component that could disappear before the loop completes. This could be incompatible by making a loop that was legal (and worked correctly, so long as the enclosing object is not modified during the loop) from the original Ada 2012 illegal in corrected Ada 2012. Such loops should be pretty rare, especially as these iterator forms are new to Ada 2012.<br />

<MarginText>17.c/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0120-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added rules to reject loops if the call to the default iterator function for a container element iterator is illegal, or if the cursor type of an iterator is limited. These are formally incompatible with original Ada 2012, but as it's unlikely that any Ada 2012 compiler ever allowed the illegal usages in an expansion of a loop (it's much more likely that they would have just caused an internal error in the compiler), this should have no effect in practice.<br />

<MarginText>17.d/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0151-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a requirement that the given subtype statically match the subtype of the element or component for a component element iterator or array component iterator. Original Ada 2012 text allowed any type that covered the subtype of the element or component, but that led to questions of what the meaning was if they are different. In this case, the element is essentially a renaming of the container element, and it doesn't make sense for the constraints to be different. Ignoring explicitly defined constraints in renames is a mistake that we don't want to continue, thus we require static matching. This means that some programs might be illegal, but those programs were misleading at best, and potentially would raise unexpected exceptions because the element values might have been invalid or abnormal with respect to the declared constraint. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.e/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0156-1"]} />
For consistency, we now allow a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> on a generalized iterator, and anonymous access types on all forms of iterator. We introduced a new syntax non-terminal, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0184">loop_parameter_subtype_indication</a></code> to simplfy the wording.<br />

<MarginText>17.f/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1"]} />
An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code> is now allowed on <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>s. This is mainly for consistency with aggregate and reduction iterators, where it eliminates the need for temporary objects. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.g/4_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0120-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added wording to specify that a loop propagates any exceptions propagated by the execution of an iterator. Since that's what naturally would happen from a macro-style expansion of the parts of an iterator, and no other interpretation makes sense given the way the rest of Ada works, we consider it so unlikely that any Ada 2012 implementation ever did anything else that we don't document this as a possible inconsistency.<br />

<MarginText>17.h/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
Added wording to include the use of the iterator view in a container element iterator.<br />

<MarginText>17.i/5_5.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
Added wording to describe the execution of parallel iterators. <br />

<a id="Subclause_5.5.3"></a>

## 5.5.3  Procedural Iterators

<MarginText>1/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> invokes a user-defined procedure, passing in the body of the enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> as a parameter of an anonymous access-to-procedure type, to allow the loop body to be executed repeatedly as part of the invocation of the user-defined procedure. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0250-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>procedural{"_"}iterator</code><a id="S0185"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0186">iterator_parameter_specification</a></code> <b>of</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code><br />       [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0308-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iterator{"_"}parameter{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0186"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code><br />   | (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>{"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>{"}"})<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iterator{"_"}procedure{"_"}call</code><a id="S0187"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />   | <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0188">iterator_actual_parameter_part</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iterator{"_"}actual{"_"}parameter{"_"}part</code><a id="S0188"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0189">iterator_parameter_association</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0189">iterator_parameter_association</a></code>{"}"})<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>iterator{"_"}parameter{"_"}association</code><a id="S0189"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0190">parameter_association_with_box</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>parameter{"_"}association{"_"}with{"_"}box</code><a id="S0190"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [ <i>formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> ={">"} ] {"<"}{">"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">At most one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0189">iterator_parameter_association</a></code> within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0188">iterator_actual_parameter_part</a></code> shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0190">parameter_association_with_box</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>9/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0292-1", "AI12-0326-2"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> given in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> shall resolve to denote a callable entity <i>C</i> (the <i>iterating procedure</i>) that is a procedure, or an entry renamed as (viewed as) a procedure. [When there is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0188">iterator_actual_parameter_part</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> can be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0095">implicit_dereference</a></code> of an access-to-subprogram value.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0190">parameter_association_with_box</a></code> is equivalent to one with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0188">iterator_actual_parameter_part</a></code> with an additional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0190">parameter_association_with_box</a></code> at the end, with the <i>formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> identifying the last formal parameter of the callable entity denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0320-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> shall contain at most one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0189">iterator_parameter_association</a></code> for each formal parameter of the callable entity <i>C</i>. Each formal parameter without an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0189">iterator_parameter_association</a></code> shall have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> (in the profile of the view of <i>C</i> denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1"]} />
<p>The formal parameter of the callable entity <i>C</i> associated with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0190">parameter_association_with_box</a></code> shall be of an anonymous access-to-procedure type <i>A</i>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>13/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0308-1"]} />
<p>The anonymous access-to-procedure type <i>A</i> shall have at least one formal parameter in its parameter profile. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0186">iterator_parameter_specification</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code>, then this <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code> shall be mode conformant with that of <i>A</i>. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0186">iterator_parameter_specification</a></code> is a list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>s, the number of formal parameters of <i>A</i> shall be the same as the length of this list.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0292-1"]} />
<p>[If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> given in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> denotes an abstract subprogram, the subprogram shall be a dispatching subprogram.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0320-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This is stated normatively in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.3">3.9.3</a>. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>15/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0250-1", "AI12-0308-1", "AI12-0326-2"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> is equivalent to a local declaration of a procedure P followed by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">procedure_call_statement</a></code> that is formed from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> by replacing the {"<"}{">"} of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0190">parameter_association_with_box</a></code> with P'Access. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code> of the locally declared procedure P is formed from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code> of the anonymous access-to-procedure type <i>A</i>, by replacing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of each formal parameter of this <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code> with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of the corresponding formal parameter or element of the list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>s given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0186">iterator_parameter_specification</a></code>. The body of <i>P</i> consists of the conditionally executed <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>. The procedure P is called the <i>loop body procedure</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0250-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a></code>, the body of the routine would be something like:<br />

<MarginText>15.b/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure P ... is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   if <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0182">iterator_filter</a> then{"\n"}      <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a>{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0344-1"]} />
<p>In a procedural iterator, the Parallel{"_"}Calls aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10#Subclause_9.10.1">9.10.1</a>) of the loop body procedure is True if the reserved word <b>parallel</b> occurs in the corresponding loop statement, and False otherwise.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0326-2", "AI12-0344-1"]} />
<p>The following aspects may be specified for a callable entity <i>S</i> that has exactly one formal parameter of an anonymous access-to-subprogram type:<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Allows{"_"}Exit</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The Allows{"_"}Exit aspect is of type Boolean. The specified value shall be static. The Allows{"_"}Exit aspect of an inherited primitive subprogram is True if Allows{"_"}Exit is True either for the corresponding subprogram of the progenitor type or for any other inherited subprogram that it overrides. If not specified or inherited as True, the Allows{"_"}Exit aspect of a callable entity is False. For an entry, only a confirming specification of False is permitted for the Allows{"_"}Exit aspect.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>18.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>An entry does not allow exit, because implementing a transfer of control out of a task or protected entry creates unnecessarily complex dynamic semantics. <br />

<MarginText>19/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>Specifying the Allows{"_"}Exit aspect to be True for a subprogram indicates that the subprogram <i>allows exit</i>, meaning that it is prepared to be completed by arbitrary transfers of control from the loop body procedure[, including propagation of exceptions. A subprogram for which Allows{"_"}Exit is True should use finalization as appropriate rather than exception handling to recover resources and make any necessary final updates to data structures].<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>19.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Allows{"_"}Exit: </b>An indication of whether a subprogram will operate correctly for arbitrary transfers of control.<br />

<MarginText>19.b/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A subprogram that does not need cleanup satisfies the requirements, and thus can specify Allows{"_"}Exit as True. If a subprogram <i>S</i> allows exit, it cannot expect to get control other than via finalization if the loop body procedure initiates a transfer of control as part of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code>. In particular, exception handlers in <i>S</i>, even <b>when others</b> handlers, will not be executed when a transfer of control occurs. The mechanism that the implementation uses to implement such transfers of control needs to avoid triggering exception handlers. <br />

<MarginText>20/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Parallel{"_"}Iterator</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect is of type Boolean. The specified value shall be static. The Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect of an inherited primitive subprogram is True if Parallel{"_"}Iterator is True either for the corresponding subprogram of the progenitor type or for any other inherited subprogram that it overrides. If not specified or inherited as True, the Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect of a callable entity is False.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>21/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0442-1"]} />
<dd>Specifying the Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect to be True for a callable entity indicates that the entity is allowed to invoke the loop body procedure from multiple distinct logical threads of control. The Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect for a subprogram shall be statically False if the subprogram allows exit.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>21.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Parallel{"_"}Iterator: </b>An indication of whether a subprogram may use multiple threads of control to invoke a loop body procedure.<br />

<MarginText>21.b/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Permitting exit from a parallel procedural iterator introduces additional semantic and implementation complexity. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>22/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0326-2"]} />
<p>If a callable entity overrides an inherited dispatching subprogram that allows exit, the overriding callable entity also shall allow exit. If a callable entity overrides an inherited dispatching subprogram that has a True Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect, the overriding callable entity also shall have a True Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Since an entry never allows exit, attempting to implement an allows exit subprogram with a task or protected entry is always illegal. However, the Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect can be applied to an entry, so a subprogram with the Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect True can be implemented by an entry. <br />

<MarginText>23/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0326-2"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> as its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> shall begin with the reserved word <b>parallel</b> if and only if the callable entity identified in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> has a Parallel{"_"}iterator aspect of True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>24/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0326-2"]} />
<p>If the actual parameter of an anonymous access-to-subprogram type, passed in an explicit call of a subprogram for which the Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspect is True, is of the form <i>P</i>'Access, the designated subprogram <i>P</i> shall have a Parallel{"_"}Calls aspect True (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10#Subclause_9.10.1">9.10.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>25/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0326-2"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> as its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> shall contain an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code>, return statement, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0265">requeue_statement</a></code> that leaves the loop only if the callable entity associated with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> allows exit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0294-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> as its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> shall not contain an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> occurs outside the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is not allowed in a procedure (see 9.5.2), it has to be directly in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>. Since the loop body here is implemented as  a procedure, we can't allow <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s there, either, even if the loop itself is directly in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>26.b/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This includes cases where the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is part of another construct, for instance, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select_statement</a></code>. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>27/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0326-2", "AI12-0355-2", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>[For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code>, the procedure denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> (the <i>iterating procedure</i>) is invoked, passing an access value designating the loop body procedure as a parameter. The iterating procedure then calls the loop body procedure zero or more times and returns, whereupon the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> is complete. If the <b>parallel</b> reserved word is present, the iterating procedure is allowed to invoke the loop body procedure from multiple distinct logical threads of control.] The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, if any, is elaborated prior to the invocation of the iterating procedure.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The stated dynamic semantics are implied by the static semantics given above and the bounded errors given below. <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>28/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0326-2", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>If the callable entity identified in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0187">iterator_procedure_call</a></code> allows exit, then it is a bounded error for a call of the loop body procedure to be performed from within an abort-deferred operation (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8">9.8</a>), unless the entire <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> was within the same abort-deferred operation. If detected, Program{"_"}Error is raised at the point of the call; otherwise, a transfer of control from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> will not necessarily terminate the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>, and the loop body procedure can be called again.<br /></p>

<MarginText>29/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0326-2", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> with the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0185">procedural_iterator</a></code> as its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0179">iteration_scheme</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>) does not begin with the reserved word <b>parallel</b>, it is a bounded error if the loop body procedure is invoked from a different logical thread of control than the one that initiates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>. If detected, Program{"_"}Error is raised; otherwise, conflicts associated with concurrent executions of the loop body procedure can occur without being detected by the applicable conflict check policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10#Subclause_9.10.1">9.10.1</a>). Furthermore, propagating an exception or making an attempt to exit in the presence of multiple threads of control will not necessarily terminate the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>, deadlock can occur, or the loop body procedure can be called again.<br /></p>

<MarginText>29.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0326-2"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Other Ada rules are still in effect for the allows exit subprogram <i>A</i>, of course. For instance, if a transfer of control causes finalization which raises an exception, Program{"_"}Error will be propagated by <i>A</i> (rather than the transfer of control). In such a case, the bounded error above would still apply. Another example is the case where an unrelated task is waiting on the normal completion of the loop body procedure call in <i>A</i>. Such a task might end up waiting forever if a transfer of control happens (this is a deadlock situation). This case does not require additional wording, as the same thing would happen if an exception is propagated from the loop body procedure or if <i>A</i> executed a transfer of control (such as a return statement). <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>30/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0379-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of iterating over a map from My{"_"}Key{"_"}Type to My{"_"}Element{"_"}Type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.4">A.18.4</a>):</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>31/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for (C : Cursor) of My{"_"}Map.Iterate loop{"\n"}   Put{"_"}Line (My{"_"}Key{"_"}Type'Image (Key (C)) & " ={">"} " &{"\n"}      My{"_"}Element{"_"}Type'Image (Element (C)));{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>32/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
-- The above is equivalent to:{"\n"}
<MarginText>33/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
declare{"\n"}   procedure P (C : Cursor) is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      Put{"_"}Line (My{"_"}Key{"_"}Type'Image (Key (c)) & " ={">"} " &{"\n"}         My{"_"}Element{"_"}Type'Image (Element (C)));{"\n"}   end P;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   My{"_"}Map.Iterate (P'Access);{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>34/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of iterating over the environment variables (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.17">A.17</a>):</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>35/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for (Name, Val) of Ada.Environment{"_"}Variables.Iterate({"<"}{">"}) loop{"\n"}   --  "({"<"}{">"})" is optional because it is the last parameter{"\n"}   Put{"_"}Line (Name & " ={">"} " & Val);{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>36/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
-- The above is equivalent to:{"\n"}
<MarginText>37/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
declare{"\n"}   procedure P (Name : String; Val : String) is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      Put{"_"}Line (Name & " ={">"} " & Val);{"\n"}   end P;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   Ada.Environment{"_"}Variables.Iterate (P'Access);{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>37.a/5_5.5.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0189-1", "AI12-0292-1", "AI12-0294-1", "AI12-0326-2", "AI12-0344-1"]} />
Procedural iterators, and the Allows{"_"}Exit and Parallel{"_"}Iterator aspects are new in Ada 2022. <br />

# 5.6. Block Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6.mdx

sidebar_position:  47

# 5.6. Block Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> encloses a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> optionally preceded by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>block{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0191"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<i>block{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0172">statement_identifier</a></code>:]<br />       [<b>declare</b><br />            <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>]<br />        <b>begin</b><br />            <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />        <b>end</b> [<i>block{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> has a <i>block{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0172">statement_identifier</a></code>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall be repeated after the <b>end</b>; otherwise, there shall not be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> after the <b>end</b>. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> that has no explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> has an implicit empty <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Thus, other rules can always refer to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code>. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>The execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> consists of the elaboration of its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> followed by the execution of its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a block statement with a local variable:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Swap:{"\n"}   declare{"\n"}      Temp : Integer;{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      Temp := V; V := U; U := Temp;{"\n"}   end Swap;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If task objects are declared within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> whose execution is completed, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> is not left until all its dependent tasks are terminated (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>). This rule applies to completion caused by a transfer of control.<br />

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
Within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code>, the block name can be used in expanded names denoting local entities such as Swap.Temp in the above example (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>7.c</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> now uses the syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>. <br />

<a id="Subclause_5.6.1"></a>

## 5.6.1  Parallel Block Statements

<MarginText>1/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0436-1"]} />
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0192">parallel_block_statement</a></code> comprises two or more <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> separated by <b>and</b> where each represents an independent activity that is intended to proceed concurrently with the others.]<br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0427-1", "AI12-0436-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>parallel{"_"}block{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0192"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>parallel</b> [(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>)] [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <b>do</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />    <b>and</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />   {"{"}<b>and</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>{"}"}<br />    <b>end do</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0427-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, if any, of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0192">parallel_block_statement</a></code> shall be an <i>integer{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>4/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0427-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0192">parallel_block_statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code> and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, if any, are elaborated in an arbitrary order. After elaborating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, if any, a check is made that the determined maximum number of chunks is greater than zero. If this check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0427-1", "AI12-0436-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>Then, the various <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> are grouped into one or more <i>chunks</i>, each with its own logical thread of control (see Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>), up to the maximum number of chunks specified by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0180">chunk_specification</a></code>, if any. Within each chunk every <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the chunk is executed in turn, in an arbitrary order. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0192">parallel_block_statement</a></code> is complete once every one of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> has completed, either by reaching the end of its execution, or due to a transfer of control out of the construct by one of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1">5.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0436-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Although each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of a parallel block represents a separate logical thread of control, the implementation may choose to combine two or more such logical threads of control into a single physical thread of control to reduce the cost of creating numerous physical threads of control. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>6/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a parallel block used to walk a binary tree in parallel:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>7/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0404-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Traverse (T : Expr{"_"}Ptr) is -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a>{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   if T /= null and then{"\n"}      T.all in Binary{"_"}Operation'Class -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.1">3.9.1</a>{"\n"}   then -- recurse down the binary tree{"\n"}      parallel do{"\n"}         Traverse (T.Left);{"\n"}      and{"\n"}         Traverse (T.Right);{"\n"}      and{"\n"}         Ada.Text{"_"}IO.Put{"_"}Line{"\n"}            ("Processing " & Ada.Tags.Expanded{"_"}Name (T'Tag));{"\n"}      end do;{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end Traverse;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a parallel block used to search two halves of a string in parallel:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Search (S : String; Char : Character) return Boolean is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   if S'Length {"<"}= 1000 then{"\n"}       -- Sequential scan{"\n"}       return (for some C of S ={">"} C = Char);{"\n"}   else{"\n"}       -- Parallel divide and conquer{"\n"}       declare{"\n"}          Mid : constant Positive := S'First + S'Length/2 - 1;{"\n"}       begin{"\n"}          parallel do{"\n"}             for C of S(S'First .. Mid) loop{"\n"}                if C = Char then{"\n"}                   return True;  -- Terminates enclosing do{"\n"}                end if;{"\n"}             end loop;{"\n"}          and{"\n"}             for C of S(Mid + 1 .. S'Last) loop{"\n"}                if C = Char then{"\n"}                   return True;  -- Terminates enclosing do{"\n"}                end if;{"\n"}             end loop;{"\n"}          end do;{"\n"}          -- Not found{"\n"}          return False;{"\n"}       end;{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end Search;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>9.a/5_5.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0427-1", "AI12-0436-1"]} />
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0192">parallel_block_statement</a></code> is new. <br />

---

# 5.7. Exit Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7.mdx

sidebar_position:  48

# 5.7. Exit Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code> is used to complete the execution of an enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>; the completion is conditional if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code> includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>exit{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0193"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>exit</b> [<i>loop{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>] [<b>when</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The <i>loop{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, if any, in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code> shall resolve to denote a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>Each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit{"_"}statement</a></code> <i>applies to</i> a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code>; this is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code> being exited. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit{"_"}statement</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is only allowed within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code> denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, and applies to that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code>. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit{"_"}statement</a></code> without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is only allowed within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code>, and applies to the innermost enclosing one. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit{"_"}statement</a></code> that applies to a given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code> shall not appear within a body or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code>, if this construct is itself enclosed by the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>, if present, is first evaluated. If the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> is True, or if there is no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>, a transfer of control is done to complete the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop{"_"}statement</a></code>. If the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> is False, no transfer of control takes place. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
NOTE   Several nested loops can be exited by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code> that names the outer loop. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of loops with exit statements:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for N in 1 .. Max{"_"}Num{"_"}Items loop{"\n"}   Get{"_"}New{"_"}Item(New{"_"}Item);{"\n"}   Merge{"_"}Item(New{"_"}Item, Storage{"_"}File);{"\n"}   exit when New{"_"}Item = Terminal{"_"}Item;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
Main{"_"}Cycle:{"\n"}   loop{"\n"}      --  initial statements{"\n"}      exit Main{"_"}Cycle when Found;{"\n"}      --  final statements{"\n"}   end loop Main{"_"}Cycle;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

---

# 5.8. Goto Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8.mdx

sidebar_position:  49

# 5.8. Goto Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> specifies an explicit transfer of control from this <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> to a target statement with a given label.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>goto{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0194"></a><code> ::= </code><b>goto</b> <i>label{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>;<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The <i>label{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall resolve to denote a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0171">label</a></code>; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> with that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0171">label</a></code> is the <i>target statement</i>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>The innermost <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> that encloses the target statement shall also enclose the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code>. Furthermore, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> is enclosed by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> or a body, then the target statement shall not be outside this enclosing construct. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> can be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> of an inner <code>sequence{"_"}</code>.<br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
It follows from the second rule that if the target <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> is enclosed by such a construct, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> cannot be outside. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>The execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> transfers control to the target statement, completing the execution of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0169">compound_statement</a></code> that encloses the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> but does not enclose the target. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
NOTE   The above rules allow transfer of control to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> of an enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> but not the reverse. Similarly, they prohibit transfers of control such as between alternatives of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.4#S0176">case_statement</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select_statement</a></code>; between <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>s; or from an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> back to its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a loop containing a goto statement:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
{"<"}{"<"}Sort{">"}{">"}{"\n"}for I in 1 .. N-1 loop{"\n"}   if A(I) {">"} A(I+1) then{"\n"}      Exchange(A(I), A(I+1));{"\n"}      goto Sort;{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

# 5. Statements

# 5. Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code> defines an action to be performed upon its execution.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>[This clause describes the general rules applicable to all <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s. Some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s are discussed in later clauses: <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">Procedure{"_"}call{"_"}statement</a></code>s and return statements are described in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/">6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/">Subprograms</a>&rdquo;. <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0264">Entry{"_"}call{"_"}statement</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0265">requeue{"_"}statement</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay{"_"}statement</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select{"_"}statement</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort{"_"}statement</a></code>s are described in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">Tasks and Synchronization</a>&rdquo;. <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">Raise{"_"}statement</a></code>s are described in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/">11</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/">Exceptions</a>&rdquo;, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.8#S0357">code{"_"}statement</a></code>s in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/">13</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/">Representation Issues</a>&rdquo;. The remaining forms of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s are presented in this clause.] <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>2.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
The description of return statements has been moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">Return Statements</a>&rdquo;, so that it is closer to the description of subprograms. <br />

# 6.1. Subprogram Declarations

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> declares a procedure or function.] <br /></p>

<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03", "AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>subprogram{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0195"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>]<br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0196">subprogram_specification</a></code><br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>operator{"_"}symbol</code><a id="S0202"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6#S0016">string_literal</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00395-01", "AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The sequence of characters in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> shall form a reserved word, a delimiter, or compound delimiter that corresponds to an operator belonging to one of the six categories of operators defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5">4.5</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00395-01", "AI05-0090-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The &ldquo;sequence of characters&rdquo; of the string literal of the operator is a technical term (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.6">2.6</a>), and does not include the surrounding quote characters. As defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.2">2.2</a>, lexical elements are &ldquo;formed&rdquo; from a sequence of characters. Spaces are not allowed, and upper and lower case is not significant. <br />

<MarginText>11</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>defining{"_"}operator{"_"}symbol</code><a id="S0203"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>parameter{"_"}profile</code><a id="S0204"></a><code> ::= </code>[<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI95-00318-02"]} />

<CodeBlock>
