# 6.2. Formal Parameter Modes

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  52

# 6.2. Formal Parameter Modes

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter_specification</a></code> declares a formal parameter of mode <b>in</b>, <b>in out</b>, or <b>out</b>.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>A parameter is passed either <i>by copy</i> or <i>by reference</i>. [When a parameter is passed by copy, the formal parameter denotes a separate object from the actual parameter, and any information transfer between the two occurs only before and after executing the subprogram. When a parameter is passed by reference, the formal parameter denotes (a view of) the object denoted by the actual parameter; reads and updates of the formal parameter directly reference the actual parameter object.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>A type is a <i>by-copy type</i> if it is an elementary type, or if it is a descendant of a private type whose full type is a by-copy type. A parameter of a by-copy type is passed by copy, unless the formal parameter is explicitly aliased.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>A type is a <i>by-reference type</i> if it is a descendant of one of the following: <br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a tagged type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>a task or protected type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0096-1"]} />
<li>an explicitly limited record type; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0096-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a composite type with a subcomponent of a by-reference type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<li>a private type whose full type is a by-reference type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0188-1", "AI12-0027-1", "AI12-0236-1", "AI12-0317-1"]} />
<p>A parameter of a by-reference type is passed by reference, as is an explicitly aliased parameter of any type. Each value of a by-reference type has an associated object. For a value conversion, the associated object is the anonymous result object if such an object is created (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>); otherwise it is the associated object of the operand. In other cases, the object associated with the evaluated operative constituent of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4">4.4</a>) determines its associated object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>By-reference parameter passing makes sense only if there is an object to reference; hence, we define such an object for each case.<br />

<MarginText>10.b</MarginText>
Since tagged types are by-reference types, this implies that every value of a tagged type has an associated object. This simplifies things, because we can define the tag to be a property of the object, and not of the value of the object, which makes it clearer that object tags never change.<br />

<MarginText>10.b.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0317-1"]} />
A construct like parenthesized expression or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.7#S0163">qualified_expression</a></code> is ignored for the purposes of determining the associated object; for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0148">conditional_expression</a></code>, it is relevant only in that it determines which <i>dependent{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> defines the associated object.<br />

<MarginText>10.c</MarginText>
We considered simplifying things even more by making every value (and therefore every expression) have an associated object. After all, there is little semantic difference between a constant object and a value. However, this would cause problems for untagged types. In particular, we would have to do a constraint check on every read of a type conversion (or a renaming thereof) in certain cases.<br />

<MarginText>10.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
We do not want this definition to depend on the view of the type; privateness is essentially ignored for this definition. Otherwise, things would be confusing (does the rule apply at the call site, at the site of the declaration of the subprogram, at the site of the return statement?), and requiring different calls to use different mechanisms would be an implementation burden.<br />

<MarginText>10.e</MarginText>
<a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">Shared Variable Control</a>&rdquo; says that a composite type with an atomic or volatile subcomponent is a by-reference type, among other things.<br />

<MarginText>10.f</MarginText>
Every value of a limited by-reference type is the value of one and only one limited object. The <i>associated object</i> of a value of a limited by-reference type is the object whose value it represents. Two values of a limited by-reference type are the <i>same</i> if and only if they represent the value of the same object.<br />

<MarginText>10.g</MarginText>
We say &ldquo;by-reference&rdquo; above because these statements are not always true for limited private types whose underlying type is nonlimited (unfortunately). <br />

<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0240-1"]} />
<p>For other parameters, it is unspecified whether the parameter is passed by copy or by reference. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There is no need to incorporate the discussion of AI83-00178, which requires pass-by-copy for certain kinds of actual parameters, while allowing pass-by-reference for others. This is because we explicitly indicate that a function creates an anonymous constant object for its result (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a>). We also provide a special dispensation for instances of Unchecked{"_"}Conversion to return by reference (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9">13.9</a>). <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0240-1"]} />
<p>If one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes a part of a formal parameter, and a second <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes a part of a distinct formal parameter or an object that is not part of a formal parameter, then the two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are considered <i>distinct access paths</i>. If an object is of a type for which the parameter passing mechanism is not specified and is not an explicitly aliased parameter, then it is a bounded error to assign to the object via one access path, and then read the value of the object via a distinct access path, unless the first access path denotes a part of a formal parameter that no longer exists at the point of the second access [(due to leaving the corresponding callable construct).] The possible consequences are that Program{"_"}Error is raised, or the newly assigned value is read, or some old value of the object is read. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For example, if we call &ldquo;P(X ={">"} Global{"_"}Variable, Y ={">"} Global{"_"}Variable)&rdquo;, then within P, the names &ldquo;X&rdquo;, &ldquo;Y&rdquo;, and &ldquo;Global{"_"}Variable&rdquo; are all distinct access paths. If Global{"_"}Variable's type is neither pass-by-copy nor pass-by-reference, then it is a bounded error to assign to Global{"_"}Variable and then read X or Y, since the language does not specify whether the old or the new value would be read. On the other hand, if Global{"_"}Variable's type is pass-by-copy, then the old value would always be read, and there is no error. Similarly, if Global{"_"}Variable's type is defined by the language to be pass-by-reference, then the new value would always be read, and again there is no error. <br />

<MarginText>12.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We are saying <i>assign</i> here, not <i>update</i>, because updating any subcomponent is considered to update the enclosing object.<br />

<MarginText>12.c</MarginText>
The &ldquo;still exists&rdquo; part is so that a read after the subprogram returns is OK.<br />

<MarginText>12.d</MarginText>
If the parameter is of a by-copy type, then there is no issue here &mdash; the formal is not a view of the actual. If the parameter is of a by-reference type, then the programmer may depend on updates through one access path being visible through some other access path, just as if the parameter were of an access type. <br />

<MarginText>12.e</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The implementation can keep a copy in a register of a parameter whose parameter-passing mechanism is not specified. If a different access path is used to update the object (creating a bounded error situation), then the implementation can still use the value of the register, even though the in-memory version of the object has been changed. However, to keep the error properly bounded, if the implementation chooses to read the in-memory version, it has to be consistent -- it cannot then assume that something it has proven about the register is true of the memory location. For example, suppose the formal parameter is L, the value of L(6) is now in a register, and L(6) is used in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code> as in &ldquo;A(L(6)) := 99;&rdquo;, where A has bounds 1..3. If the implementation can prove that the value for L(6) in the register is in the range 1..3, then it need not perform the constraint check if it uses the register value. However, if the memory value of L(6) has been changed to 4, and the implementation uses that memory value, then it had better not alter memory outside of A.<br />

<MarginText>12.f</MarginText>
Note that the rule allows the implementation to pass a parameter by reference and then keep just part of it in a register, or, equivalently, to pass part of the parameter by reference and another part by copy. <br />

<MarginText>12.g</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We do not want to go so far as to say that the mere presence of aliasing is wrong. We wish to be able to write the following sorts of things in standard Ada: <br />

<MarginText>12.h</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Move ( Source  : in  String;{"\n"}                 Target  : out String;{"\n"}                 Drop    : in  Truncation := Error;{"\n"}                 Justify : in  Alignment  := Left;{"\n"}                 Pad     : in  Character  := Space);{"\n"}-- Copies elements from Source to Target (safely if they overlap){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12.i</MarginText>
This is from the standard string handling package. It would be embarrassing if this couldn't be written in Ada!<br />

<MarginText>12.j</MarginText>
The &ldquo;then&rdquo; before &ldquo;read&rdquo; in the rule implies that the implementation can move a read to an earlier place in the code, but not to a later place after a potentially aliased assignment. Thus, if the subprogram reads one of its parameters into a local variable, and then updates another potentially aliased one, the local copy is safe &mdash; it is known to have the old value. For example, the above-mentioned Move subprogram can be implemented by copying Source into a local variable before assigning into Target.<br />

<MarginText>12.k</MarginText>
For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> assigning one array parameter to another, the implementation has to check which direction to copy at run time, in general, in case the actual parameters are overlapping slices. For example: <br />

<MarginText>12.l</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Copy(X : in out String; Y: String) is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}    X := Y;{"\n"}end Copy;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12.m</MarginText>
It would be wrong for the compiler to assume that X and Y do not overlap (unless, of course, it can prove otherwise). <br />

<MarginText>13/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0056-1"]} />
NOTE 1   The mode of a formal parameter describes the direction of information transfer to or from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>14/4</MarginText>
NOTE 2   A formal parameter of mode <b>in</b> is a constant view (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3">3.3</a>); it cannot be updated within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0056-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 3   A formal parameter of mode <b>out</b> can be uninitialized at the start of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
The value of an <b>out</b> parameter may be read. An <b>out</b> parameter is treated like a declared variable without an explicit initial expression. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>15.b</MarginText>
Discussion of copy-in for parts of out parameters is now covered in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">Parameter Associations</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>15.c</MarginText>
The concept of a by-reference type is new to Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>15.d</MarginText>
We now cover in a general way in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#Subclause_3.7.2">3.7.2</a> the rule regarding erroneous execution when a discriminant is changed and one of the parameters depends on the discriminant. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>15.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0096-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected so that limited derived types are by-reference only if their parent is.<br />

<MarginText>15.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
Defined that explicitly aliased parameters (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>) are always passed by reference. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>15.g/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0027-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected so that value conversions that are copies are the &ldquo;associated object&rdquo; for parameter passing of by-reference types. This can only happen if the conversion is between unrelated non-limited types, and it is necessary just so the correct object is defined. <br />

---

# 6.3. Subprogram Bodies

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  53

# 6.3. Subprogram Bodies

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> specifies the execution of a subprogram.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03", "AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>subprogram{"_"}body</code><a id="S0216"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>]<br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0196">subprogram_specification</a></code><br />       [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <b>is</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code><br />    <b>begin</b><br />        <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />    <b>end</b> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0199">designator</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0199">designator</a></code> appears at the end of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, it shall repeat the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0200">defining_designator</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0196">subprogram_specification</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>[In contrast to other bodies,] a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is allowed to be defined without it being the completion of a previous declaration[, in which case the body declares the subprogram]. If the body is a completion, it shall be the completion of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0311">generic_subprogram_declaration</a></code>. The profile of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> that completes a declaration shall conform fully to that of the declaration. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is considered a declaration. It can either complete a previous declaration, or itself be the initial declaration of the subprogram. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a nongeneric <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> has no other effect than to establish that the subprogram can from then on be called without failing the Elaboration{"_"}Check. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.2">12.2</a> for elaboration of a generic body. Note that protected <code>subprogram{"_"}bodies</code> never get elaborated; the elaboration of the containing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code> allows them to be called without failing the Elaboration{"_"}Check. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>[The execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is invoked by a subprogram call.] For this execution the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> is elaborated, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> is then executed. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of procedure body:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Push(E : in Element{"_"}Type; S : in out Stack) is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   if S.Index = S.Size then{"\n"}      raise Stack{"_"}Overflow;{"\n"}   else{"\n"}      S.Index := S.Index + 1;{"\n"}      S.Space(S.Index) := E;{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end Push;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a function body:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Dot{"_"}Product(Left, Right : Vector) return Real is{"\n"}   Sum : Real := 0.0;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   Check(Left'First = Right'First and Left'Last = Right'Last);{"\n"}   for J in Left'Range loop{"\n"}      Sum := Sum + Left(J){"*"}Right(J);{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}   return Sum;{"\n"}end Dot{"_"}Product;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> may be used instead of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> now uses the syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>11.c</MarginText>
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is now required; that doesn't make any real difference, because a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> can be empty.<br />

<MarginText>11.d</MarginText>
We have incorporated some rules from RM83-6.5 here.<br />

<MarginText>11.e</MarginText>
RM83 forgot to restrict the definition of elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> to nongenerics. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>11.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">Overriding_indicator</a></code> is added to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>11.g/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

<a id="Subclause_6.3.1"></a>

## 6.3.1  Conformance Rules

<MarginText>1_6.3.1</MarginText>
<p>[When subprogram profiles are given in more than one place, they are required to conform in one of four ways: type conformance, mode conformance, subtype conformance, or full conformance.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00117-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0011</i>{"}"} [As explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">Interfacing Aspects</a>&rdquo;, a <i>convention</i> can be specified for an entity.] Unless this document states otherwise, the default convention of an entity is Ada. [For a callable entity or access-to-subprogram type, the convention is called the <i>calling convention</i>.] The following conventions are defined by the language: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The default calling convention for any subprogram not listed below is <i>Ada</i>. [The Convention aspect may be specified to override the default calling convention (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>)]. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>3.a_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>See also the rule about renamings-as-body in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#Subclause_8.5.4">8.5.4</a>. <br />

<MarginText>4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The <i>Intrinsic</i> calling convention represents subprograms that are &ldquo;built in&rdquo; to the compiler. The default calling convention is Intrinsic for the following: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>an enumeration literal;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6_6.3.1</MarginText>
<li>a "/=" operator declared implicitly due to the declaration of "=" (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.6">6.6</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>7_6.3.1</MarginText>
<li>any other implicitly declared subprogram unless it is a dispatching operation of a tagged type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>8_6.3.1</MarginText>
<li>an inherited subprogram of a generic formal tagged type with unknown discriminants; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a.1/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Consider: <br />

<MarginText>8.a.2/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package P is{"\n"}    type Root is tagged null record;{"\n"}    procedure Proc(X: Root);{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8.a.3/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
generic{"\n"}    type Formal({"<"}{">"}) is new Root with private;{"\n"}package G is{"\n"}    ...{"\n"}end G;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8.a.4/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
package body G is{"\n"}    ...{"\n"}    X: Formal := ...;{"\n"}    ...{"\n"}    Proc(X); -- This is a dispatching call in Instance, because{"\n"}             -- the actual type for Formal is class-wide.{"\n"}    ...{"\n"}    -- Proc'Access would be illegal here, because it is of{"\n"}    -- convention Intrinsic, by the above rule.{"\n"}end G;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8.a.5/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
type Actual is new Root with ...;{"\n"}procedure Proc(X: Actual);{"\n"}package Instance is new G(Formal ={">"} Actual'Class);{"\n"}    -- It is legal to pass in a class-wide actual, because Formal{"\n"}    -- has unknown discriminants.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8.a.6/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
Within Instance, all calls to Proc will be dispatching calls, so Proc doesn't really exist in machine code, so we wish to avoid taking 'Access of it. This rule applies to those cases where the actual type might be class-wide, and makes these Intrinsic, thus forbidding 'Access. <br />

<MarginText>9_6.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>an attribute that is a subprogram;<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00252-01"]} />
<li>a subprogram declared immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.1/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00252-01", "AI95-00407-01", "AI12-0107-1"]} />
<li>any prefixed view of a subprogram (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>) without synchronization kind (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>) By{"_"}Entry or By{"_"}Protected{"_"}Procedure. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The profile of a prefixed view is different from the &ldquo;real&rdquo; profile of the subprogram (it doesn't have the first parameter), so we don't want to be able to take 'Access of it, as that would require generating a wrapper of some sort.<br />

<MarginText>10.b/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0107-1"]} />
We except prefixed views that have synchronization kind By{"_"}Protected{"_"}Procedure so that they can be used with an access-to-protected-procedure type. These don't require special wrappers (this is the normal form for a protected subprogram call). The By{"_"}Entry part is just for consistency (there is no access-to-entry type in Ada). <br />

<MarginText>11_6.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>[The Access attribute is not allowed for Intrinsic subprograms.] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The Intrinsic calling convention really represents any number of calling conventions at the machine code level; the compiler might have a different instruction sequence for each intrinsic. That's why the Access attribute is disallowed. We do not wish to require the implementation to generate an out of line body for an intrinsic.<br />

<MarginText>11.b/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
Whenever we wish to disallow the Access attribute in order to ease implementation, we make the subprogram Intrinsic. Several language-defined subprograms have &ldquo;<b>with</b> Convention ={">"} Intrinsic;&rdquo;. An implementation might actually implement this as &ldquo;<b>with</b> Import ={">"} True, Convention ={">"} Intrinsic;&rdquo;, if there is really no body, and the implementation of the subprogram is built into the code generator.<br />

<MarginText>11.c_6.3.1</MarginText>
Subprograms declared in <code>protected{"_"}bodies</code> will generally have a special calling convention so as to pass along the identification of the current instance of the protected type. The convention is not <i>protected</i> since such local subprograms need not contain any &ldquo;locking&rdquo; logic since they are not callable via &ldquo;external&rdquo; calls; this rule prevents an access value designating such a subprogram from being passed outside the protected unit.<br />

<MarginText>11.d_6.3.1</MarginText>
The &ldquo;implicitly declared subprogram&rdquo; above refers to predefined operators (other than the "=" of a tagged type) and the inherited subprograms of untagged types. <br />

<MarginText>12/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0107-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The default calling convention is <i>protected</i> for a protected subprogram, for a prefixed view of a subprogram with a synchronization kind of By{"_"}Protected{"_"}Procedure, and for an access-to-subprogram type with the reserved word <b>protected</b> in its definition.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0107-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<li>The default calling convention is <i>entry</i> for an entry and for a prefixed view of a subprogram with a synchronization kind of By{"_"}Entry.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.1/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00254-01", "AI95-00409-01", "AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0207-1"]} />
<li>The calling convention for an anonymous access-to-subprogram parameter or anonymous access-to-subprogram result is <i>protected</i> if the reserved word <b>protected</b> appears in its definition; otherwise, it is the convention of the entity that has the parameter or result, unless that entity has convention <i>protected</i>, <i>entry</i>, or Intrinsic, in which case the convention is Ada. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The calling convention for other anonymous access-to-subprogram types is Ada. <br />

<MarginText>13.2/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00117-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0011</i>{"}"} [If not specified above as Intrinsic, the calling convention for any inherited or overriding dispatching operation of a tagged type is that of the corresponding subprogram of the parent type.] The default calling convention for a new dispatching operation of a tagged type is the convention of the type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a.1/1_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The first rule is officially stated in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>. The second is intended to make interfacing to foreign OOP languages easier, by making the default be that the type and operations all have the same convention. <br />

<MarginText>14/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>Of these four conventions, only Ada and Intrinsic are allowed as a <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> in the specification of a Convention aspect. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The names of the <i>protected</i> and <i>entry</i> calling conventions cannot be used in the specification of Convention. Note that <b>protected</b> and <b>entry</b> are reserved words. <br />

<MarginText>15/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00409-01"]} />
<p>Two profiles are <i>type conformant</i> if they have the same number of parameters, and both have a result if either does, and corresponding parameter and result types are the same, or, for access parameters or access results, corresponding designated types are the same, or corresponding designated profiles are type conformant. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00409-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For anonymous access-to-object parameters, the designated types have to be the same for type conformance, not the access types, since in general each access parameter has its own anonymous access type, created when the subprogram is called. Of course, corresponding parameters have to be either both access parameters or both not access parameters.<br />

<MarginText>15.b/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00409-01"]} />
Similarly, for anonymous access-to-subprogram parameters, the designated profiles of the types, not the types themselves, have to be conformant. <br />

<MarginText>16/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI95-00409-01", "AI05-0142-4"]} />
<p>Two profiles are <i>mode conformant</i> if:<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.1/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>they are type conformant; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>16.2/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
<li>corresponding parameters have identical modes and both or neither are explicitly aliased parameters; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>16.3/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0207-1"]} />
<li>for corresponding access parameters and any access result type, the designated subtypes statically match and either both or neither are access-to-constant, or the designated profiles are subtype conformant. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0239-1"]} />
<p>Two profiles are <i>subtype conformant</i> if they are mode conformant, corresponding subtypes of the profile statically match, and the associated calling conventions are the same. The profile of a generic formal subprogram is not subtype conformant with any other profile. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b><br />

<MarginText>18/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0134-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>Two profiles are <i>fully conformant</i> if they are subtype conformant, if they have access-to-subprogram results whose designated profiles are fully conformant, and for corresponding parameters: <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.1/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>they have the same names; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.2/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0046-1"]} />
<li>both or neither have <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>s; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.3/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<li>neither have <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s, or they both have <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s that are fully conformant with one another; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.4/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0134-1"]} />
<li>for access-to-subprogram parameters, the designated profiles are fully conformant. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.a_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Full conformance requires subtype conformance, which requires the same calling conventions. However, the calling convention of the declaration and body of a subprogram or entry are always the same by definition. <br />

<MarginText>18.b/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0046-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The part about <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>s is necessary to prevent controlling parameters from having different exclusions, as such a parameter is defined to exclude null whether or not an exclusion is given.<br />

<MarginText>18.c/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0134-1"]} />
The parts about access-to-subprogram parameters and results is necessary to prevent such types from having different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s in the specification and body of a subprogram. If that was allowed, it would be undefined which <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> was used in a call of an access-to-subprogram parameter. <br />

<MarginText>19_6.3.1</MarginText>
<p>Two expressions are <i>fully conformant</i> if, [after replacing each use of an operator with the equivalent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>:] <br /></p>

<MarginText>20_6.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>each constituent construct of one corresponds to an instance of the same syntactic category in the other, except that an expanded name may correspond to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> (or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>) or to a different expanded name in the other; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.1/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0050-1"]} />
<li>corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>s occurring within the two expressions are the same; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>21/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0050-1"]} />
<li>each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> that is not part of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an expanded name in one denotes the same declaration as the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> in the other, or they denote corresponding declarations occurring within the two expressions; and <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21.a/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0300-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that it doesn't say &ldquo;respectively&rdquo; because a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> can correspond to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>, and vice versa, by the previous bullet. This rule allows the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an expanded name to be removed, or replaced with a different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> that denotes a renaming of the same entity. However, it does not allow a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> to be replaced with one denoting a distinct renaming (except for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>s in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es of expanded names). Note that calls using operator notation are equivalent to calls using prefix notation.<br />

<MarginText>21.b_6.3.1</MarginText>
Given the following declarations: <br />

<MarginText>21.c_6.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package A is{"\n"}    function F(X : Integer := 1) return Boolean;{"\n"}end A;{"\n"}
<MarginText>21.c.1/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
with A;{"\n"}package B is{"\n"}    package A{"_"}View renames A;{"\n"}    function F{"_"}View(X : Integer := 9999) return Boolean renames A.F;{"\n"}end B;{"\n"}
<MarginText>21.d_6.3.1</MarginText>
with A, B; use A, B;{"\n"}procedure Main is ...{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21.e_6.3.1</MarginText>
Within Main, the expressions &ldquo;F&rdquo;, &ldquo;A.F&rdquo;, &ldquo;B.A{"_"}View.F&rdquo;, and &ldquo;A{"_"}View.F&rdquo; are all fully conformant with one another. However, &ldquo;F&rdquo; and &ldquo;F{"_"}View&rdquo; are not fully conformant. If they were, it would be bad news, since the two denoted views have different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>21.f/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0050-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We talk about <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>s and "corresponding declarations" because of the possibility of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code>s occurring within the expressions; each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> is a separate declaration, which we need to allow, but we do want to require that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>s are the same. <br />

<MarginText>21.1/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00175-01", "AI05-0092-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0018</i>{"}"} each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code> in one is the same as the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code> in the other; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>22/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1"]} />
<li>each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0141">primary</a></code> that is a literal in one is a user-defined literal if and only if the corresponding literal in the other is also a user-defined literal. Furthermore, if neither are user-defined literals then they shall have the same values[, but they may have differing textual representations]; if both are user-defined literals then they shall have the same textual representation.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>22.a/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule applies to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s, so even though other rules would allow a rename of a character literal to conform to the literal, this rule prevents that. <br />

<MarginText>22.b_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that the above definition makes full conformance a transitive relation. <br />

<MarginText>23_6.3.1</MarginText>
<p>Two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code>s are <i>fully conformant</i> if they have the same number of discriminants, and discriminants in the same positions have the same names, statically matching subtypes, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s that are fully conformant with one another. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24_6.3.1</MarginText>
<p>Two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>s are <i>fully conformant</i> if they are both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>s or are both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>s, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>s (if any) denote the same subtype, and the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>s (if any) fully conform. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> case, any ranges have to <i>be</i> corresponding; that is, two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>s cannot conform unless both or neither has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>24.b_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This definition is used in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.2">9.5.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.2">Entries and Accept Statements</a>&rdquo; for the conformance required between the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>s of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> for a family of entries and the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry_index_specification</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>24.1/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01", "AI95-00397-01"]} />
<p>The <i>prefixed view profile</i> of a subprogram is the profile obtained by omitting the first parameter of that subprogram. There is no prefixed view profile for a parameterless subprogram. For the purposes of defining subtype and mode conformance, the convention of a prefixed view profile is considered to match that of either an entry or a protected operation.<br /></p>

<MarginText>24.c/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This definition is used to define how primitive subprograms of interfaces match operations in task and protected type definitions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1">9.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4">9.4</a>). <br />

<MarginText>24.d/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The weird rule about conventions is pretty much required for synchronized interfaces to make any sense. There will be wrappers all over the place for interfaces anyway. Of course, this doesn't imply that entries have the same convention as protected operations. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>25_6.3.1</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may declare an operator declared in a language-defined library unit to be intrinsic. <br /></p>

<MarginText>26/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0398-1"]} />
NOTE   Any conformance requirements between <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s that are part of a profile or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0061">known_discriminant_part</a></code> are defined by the semantics of each particular aspect. In particular, there is no general requirement for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>s to match in conforming profiles or discriminant parts. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>26.a_6.3.1</MarginText>
The rules for full conformance are relaxed &mdash; they are now based on the structure of constructs, rather than the sequence of lexical elements. This implies, for example, that "(X, Y: T)" conforms fully with "(X: T; Y: T)", and "(X: T)" conforms fully with "(X: <b>in</b> T)". <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>26.b/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00117-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0011</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that the default convention is Ada. Also clarified that the convention of a primitive operation of a tagged type is the same as that of the type.<br />

<MarginText>26.c/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00175-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0018</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added wording to ensure that two attributes conform only if they have the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>26.d/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00252-01", "AI95-00254-01", "AI95-00407-01"]} />
Defined the calling convention for anonymous access-to-subprogram types and for prefixed views of subprograms (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>).<br />

<MarginText>26.e/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
Defined the conformance of access result types (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>26.f/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01", "AI95-00397-01"]} />
Defined the prefixed view profile of subprograms for later use.<br />

<MarginText>26.g/2_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00409-01"]} />
Defined the conformance of anonymous access-to-subprogram parameters. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.h/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0046-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Now require <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>s to match for full conformance. While this is technically incompatible with Ada 2005 as defined by Amendment 1, it is a new Ada 2005 feature and it is unlikely that users have been intentionally taking advantage of the ability to write mismatching exclusions. In any case, it is easy to fix: add a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> where needed for conformance.<br />

<MarginText>26.i/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0134-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Now require full conformance of anonymous access-to-subprogram parameters and results for full conformance. This is necessary so that there is no confusion about the default expression that is used for a call. While this is technically incompatible with Ada 2005 as defined by Amendment 1, it is a new Ada 2005 feature and it is unlikely that users have been intentionally taking advantage and writing different default expressions. In any case, it is easy to fix: change any default expressions that don't conform so that they do conform.<br />

<MarginText>26.j/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0207-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Now include the presence or absence of <b>constant</b> in access parameters to be considered when checking mode conformance. This is necessary to prevent modification of constants. While this is technically incompatible with Ada 2005 as defined by Amendment 1, it is a new Ada 2005 feature and it is unlikely that users have been intentionally taking advantage and writing mismatching access types. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.k/3_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
Explicitly aliased parameters are included as part of mode conformance (since it affects the parameter passing mechanism). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.l/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0207-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The convention of an anonymous access-to-subprogram parameter of a protected entry or subprogram is Ada; if one wants it to be <i>protected</i> it can be declared with the keyword <b>protected</b>. This is incompatible, but only in a very rare case; usually the intent is to pass a normal subprogram to a protected subprogram (and this was impossible in Ada 2012). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.m/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0107-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> We now define that a prefixed view of a subprogram with synchronization kind By{"_"}Protected{"_"}Procedure can be used as the prefix of 'Access for an access-to-protected type. We consider this a correction as it certainly appears that it ought to work, but in original Ada 2012 it would have had a convention mismatch. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.n/4_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0050-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> We now define how two expressions containing quantified expressions can fully conform. This isn't incompatible, as the original Ada 2012 never allowed such expressions to conform (the declarations in each formally being different). Neither is it an extension as one would expect these to conform.<br />

<MarginText>26.o/5_6.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0342-1"]} />
The conformance of literals is tightened up to not assume anything about the value of a user-defined literal. <br />

<a id="Subclause_6.3.2"></a>

## 6.3.2  Inline Expansion of Subprograms

<MarginText>1_6.3.2</MarginText>
<p>[Subprograms may be expanded in line at the call site.] <br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraphs 2 through 4 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For a callable entity or a generic subprogram, the following language-defined representation aspect may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.1/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Inline</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Inline is Boolean. When aspect Inline is True for a callable entity, inline expansion is desired for all calls to that entity. When aspect Inline is True for a generic subprogram, inline expansion is desired for all calls to all instances of that generic subprogram.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>5.2/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<dd>If directly specified, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a static expression. [This aspect is never inherited;] if not directly specified, the aspect is False.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>5.a/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Inline: </b>For efficiency, Inline calls are requested for a subprogram.<br />

<MarginText>5.b/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>5.c/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
This paragraph was deleted.{"\n"}
<MarginText>5.d/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
This paragraph was deleted.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.e/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The meaning of a subprogram can be changed by inline expansion as requested by aspect Inline only in the presence of failing checks (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.6">11.6</a>). <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>6/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For each call, an implementation is free to follow or to ignore the recommendation determined by the Inline aspect. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a_6.3.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note, in particular, that the recommendation cannot always be followed for a recursive call, and is often infeasible for entries. Note also that the implementation can inline calls even when no such desire was expressed via the Inline aspect, so long as the semantics of the program remains unchanged. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>7.a/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00309-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>7.b/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>7.c/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00309-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>7.d/3_6.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
Aspect Inline is new; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Inline is now obsolescent. <br />

# 6.4. Subprogram Calls

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  54

# 6.4. Subprogram Calls

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>A <i>subprogram call</i> is either a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">procedure_call_statement</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>; [it invokes the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. The call specifies the association of the actual parameters, if any, with formal parameters of the subprogram.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>procedure{"_"}call{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0217"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>;<br />  | <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0219">actual_parameter_part</a></code>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>function{"_"}call</code><a id="S0218"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />  | <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0219">actual_parameter_part</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>For the purpose of non-syntax rules, infix operator calls are considered <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>s. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.6">6.6</a>. <br />

<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>actual{"_"}parameter{"_"}part</code><a id="S0219"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code>{"}"})<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>parameter{"_"}association</code><a id="S0220"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<i>formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> ={">"}] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0221">explicit_actual_parameter</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>explicit{"_"}actual{"_"}parameter</code><a id="S0221"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> | <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0416-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code> is <i>named</i> or <i>positional</i> according to whether or not the <i>formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector{"_"}name</a></code> is specified. For the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code>s of a single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0219">actual_parameter_part</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0188">iterator_actual_parameter_part</a></code>, any positional associations shall precede any named associations. Named associations are not allowed if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> in a subprogram call is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute{"_"}reference</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This means that the formal parameter names used in describing predefined attributes are to aid presentation of their semantics, but are not intended for use in actual calls. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00310-01"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> given in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">procedure_call_statement</a></code> shall resolve to denote a callable entity that is a procedure, or an entry renamed as (viewed as) a procedure. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> given in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> shall resolve to denote a callable entity that is a function. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> shall not resolve to denote an abstract subprogram unless it is also a dispatching subprogram. [When there is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0219">actual{"_"}parameter{"_"}part</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> can be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0095">implicit{"_"}dereference</a></code> of an access-to-subprogram value.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00310-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This rule is talking about dispatching operations (which is a static concept) and not about dispatching calls (which is a dynamic concept). <br />

<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The function can be an operator, enumeration literal, attribute that is a function, etc. <br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>A subprogram call shall contain at most one association for each formal parameter. Each formal parameter without an association shall have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> (in the profile of the view denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>). [This rule is an overloading rule (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>).] <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0240-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>All Name Resolution Rules are overloading rules, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00407-01", "AI12-0416-1"]} />
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of a subprogram call denotes a prefixed view (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>), the subprogram call is equivalent to a call on the underlying subprogram, with the first actual parameter being provided by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the prefixed view (or the Access attribute of this <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> if the first formal parameter is an access parameter), and the remaining actual parameters given by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0219">actual_parameter_part</a></code>, if any. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<p>For the execution of a subprogram call, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the call is evaluated, and each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter{"_"}association</a></code> is evaluated (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>). If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default{"_"}expression</a></code> is used, an implicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter{"_"}association</a></code> is assumed for this rule. These evaluations are done in an arbitrary order. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram{"_"}body</a></code> is then executed, or a call on an entry or protected subprogram is performed (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>). Finally, if the subprogram completes normally, then after it is left, any necessary assigning back of formal to actual parameters occurs (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The implicit association for a default is only for this run-time rule. At compile time, the visibility rules are applied to the default at the place where it occurs, not at the place of a call. <br />

<MarginText>10.b</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>If the subprogram is inherited, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4">3.4</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4">Derived Types and Classes</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>10.c</MarginText>
If the subprogram is protected, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.1">9.5.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.1">Protected Subprograms and Protected Actions</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>10.d</MarginText>
If the subprogram is really a renaming of an entry, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">Entry Calls</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>10.d.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
If the subprogram is implemented by an entry or protected subprogram, it will be treated as a dispatching call to the corresponding entry (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">Entry Calls</a>&rdquo;) or protected subprogram (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.1">9.5.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.1">Protected Subprograms and Protected Actions</a>&rdquo;).<br />

<MarginText>10.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />
Normally, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> that is executed by the above rule is the one for the subprogram being called. For an enumeration literal, implicitly declared (but noninherited) subprogram, null procedure, or an attribute that is a subprogram, an implicit body is assumed. For a dispatching call, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">Dispatching Operations of Tagged Types</a>&rdquo; defines which <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> is executed. <br />

<MarginText>11/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<p>The exception Program{"_"}Error is raised at the point of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> if the function completes normally without executing a return statement. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We are committing to raising the exception at the point of call, for uniformity &mdash; see AI83-00152. This happens after the function is left, of course.<br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
Note that there is no name for suppressing this check, since the check imposes no time overhead and minimal space overhead (since it can usually be statically eliminated as dead code). <br />

<MarginText>12/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> denotes a constant, as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a>; the nominal subtype of the constant is given by the nominal subtype of the function result. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of procedure calls:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Traverse{"_"}Tree;                                               --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>{"\n"}Print{"_"}Header(128, Title, True);                              --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>{"\n"}
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
Switch(From ={">"} X, To ={">"} Next);                               --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>{"\n"}Print{"_"}Header(128, Header ={">"} Title, Center ={">"} True);          --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>{"\n"}Print{"_"}Header(Header ={">"} Title, Center ={">"} True, Pages ={">"} 128); --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of function calls:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Dot{"_"}Product(U, V)   --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3">6.3</a>{"\n"}Clock               --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6">9.6</a>{"\n"}F.all               --  presuming F is of an access-to-subprogram type &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10">3.10</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of procedures with default expressions:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Activate(Process : in Process{"_"}Name;{"\n"}                   After   : in Process{"_"}Name := No{"_"}Process;{"\n"}                   Wait    : in Duration := 0.0;{"\n"}                   Prior   : in Boolean := False);{"\n"}
<MarginText>20/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
procedure Pair(Left, Right : in Person{"_"}Name := new Person(M));   --  see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a>{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of their calls:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Activate(X);{"\n"}Activate(X, After ={">"} Y);{"\n"}Activate(X, Wait ={">"} 60.0, Prior ={">"} True);{"\n"}Activate(X, Y, 10.0, False);{"\n"}
<MarginText>23/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
Pair;{"\n"}Pair(Left ={">"} new Person(F), Right ={">"} new Person(M));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>24</MarginText>
NOTE   If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> is used for two or more parameters in a multiple <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default{"_"}expression</a></code> is evaluated once for each omitted parameter. Hence in the above examples, the two calls of Pair are equivalent. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of overloaded subprograms:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>26</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Put(X : in Integer);{"\n"}procedure Put(X : in String);{"\n"}
<MarginText>27</MarginText>
procedure Set(Tint   : in Color);{"\n"}procedure Set(Signal : in Light);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>28</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of their calls:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>29</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Put(28);{"\n"}Put("no possible ambiguity here");{"\n"}
<MarginText>30</MarginText>
Set(Tint   ={">"} Red);{"\n"}Set(Signal ={">"} Red);{"\n"}Set(Color'(Red));{"\n"}
<MarginText>31/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
--  Set(Red) would be ambiguous since Red can{"\n"}--  denote a value either of type Color or of type Light{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>31.a</MarginText>
We have gotten rid of parameters &ldquo;of the form of a type conversion&rdquo; (see RM83-6.4.1(3)). The new view semantics of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>s allows us to use normal <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>s instead.<br />

<MarginText>31.b</MarginText>
We have moved wording about run-time semantics of parameter associations to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>.<br />

<MarginText>31.c</MarginText>
We have moved wording about raising Program{"_"}Error for a function that falls off the end to here from RM83-6.5. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>31.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00310-01"]} />
Nondispatching abstract operations are no longer considered when resolving a subprogram call. That makes it possible to use <b>abstract</b> to &ldquo;undefine&rdquo; a predefined operation for an untagged type. That's especially helpful when defining custom arithmetic packages. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>31.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
Changed the definition of the nominal subtype of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> to use the nominal subtype wording of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>, to take into account <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>s and access result types.<br />

<MarginText>31.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
Added wording to clarify that the meaning of a call on a subprogram &ldquo;implemented by&rdquo; an entry or protected operation is defined by <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>.<br />

<MarginText>31.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00407-01"]} />
Defined the meaning of a call on a prefixed view of a subprogram (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>31.h/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0416-1"]} />
Moved the equivalence definition for a prefixed view to Static Semantics, in order that it is clear Legality Rules that apply to calls and the parameters of calls apply to prefixed views (including the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>). <br />

<a id="Subclause_6.4.1"></a>

## 6.4.1  Parameter Associations

<MarginText>1_6.4.1</MarginText>
<p>[ A parameter association defines the association between an actual parameter and a formal parameter.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a_6.4.1</MarginText>
The parameter passing rules for <b>out</b> parameters are designed to ensure that the parts of a type that have implicit initial values (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>) don't become &ldquo;de-initialized&rdquo; by being passed as an <b>out</b> parameter.<br />

<MarginText>1.b/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
For explicitly aliased parameters of functions, we will ensure at the call site that a part of the parameter can be returned as part of the function result without creating a dangling pointer. We do this with accessibility checks at the call site that all actual objects of explicitly aliased parameters live at least as long as the function result; then we can allow them to be returned as access discriminants or anonymous access results, as those have the master of the function result. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>2/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0118-1"]} />
<p>The <i>formal{"_"}parameter{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> of a named <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter{"_"}association</a></code> shall resolve to denote a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code> of the view being called; this is the formal parameter of the association. The formal parameter for a positional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter{"_"}association</a></code> is the parameter with the corresponding position in the formal part of the view being called.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0118-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>For positional parameters, the &ldquo;corresponding position&rdquo; is calculated after any transformation of prefixed views. <br />

<MarginText>3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<p>The <i>actual parameter</i> is either the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0221">explicit_actual_parameter</a></code> given in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code> for a given formal parameter, or the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> if no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code> is given for the formal parameter. The expected type for an actual parameter is the type of the corresponding formal parameter. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a_6.4.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> is the one of the corresponding formal parameter in the profile of the view denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the call. <br />

<MarginText>4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<p>If the mode is <b>in</b>, the actual is interpreted as an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>; otherwise, the actual is interpreted only as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, if possible. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This formally resolves the ambiguity present in the syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0221">explicit_actual_parameter</a></code>. This matters as an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is evaluated and represents a value while a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> by itself can be an object; if the mode is not <b>in</b>, we want the parameter to interpreted as an object. Note that we don't actually require that the actual be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> if the mode is not <b>in</b>; we do that below.<br />

<MarginText>4.b/4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
This wording uses "interpreted as" rather than "shall be" so that this rule is not used to resolve overloading; it is solely about evaluation as described above. We definitely do not want to allow oddities like the presence of parentheses requiring the selection of an <b>in</b> formal parameter as opposed to an otherwise matching <b>in out</b> parameter. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<p>If the mode is <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b>, the actual shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes a variable. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We no longer need &ldquo;or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> whose argument is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a variable&rdquo;, because a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code> is now a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, and a view conversion of a variable is a variable while any other conversion (which should not be legal here) is a constant. <br />

<MarginText>5.b_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The requirement that the actual be a (variable) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is not an overload resolution rule, since we don't want the difference between <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> to be used to resolve overloading. For example: <br />

<MarginText>5.c_6.4.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Print(X : in Integer; Y : in Boolean := True);{"\n"}procedure Print(Z : in out Integer);{"\n"}. . .{"\n"}Print(3); -- Ambiguous!{"\n"}  {"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.d_6.4.1</MarginText>
The above call to Print is ambiguous even though the call is not compatible with the second Print which requires an actual that is a (variable) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (&ldquo;3&rdquo; is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, not a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>). This requirement is a legality rule, so overload resolution fails before it is considered, meaning that the call is ambiguous. <br />

<MarginText>5.1/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0074-1", "AI12-0159-1", "AI12-0377-1"]} />
<p>If the mode is <b>out</b>, the actual parameter is a view conversion, and the type of the formal parameter is a scalar type, then <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.2/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>neither the target type nor the operand type has the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.3/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>both the target type and the operand type shall have the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified, and there shall exist a type (other than a root numeric type) that is an ancestor of both the target type and the operand type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.4/4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0074-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.e/4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>These rules are needed in order to ensure that a well-defined parameter value is passed. <br />

<MarginText>6/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0102-1", "AI05-0142-4"]} />
