<p>If the formal parameter is an explicitly aliased parameter, the type of the actual parameter shall be tagged or the actual parameter shall be an aliased view of an object. Further, if the formal parameter subtype <i>F</i> is untagged:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.1/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the subtype <i>F</i> shall statically match the nominal subtype of the actual object; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.2/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>the subtype <i>F</i> shall be unconstrained, discriminated in its full view, and unconstrained in any partial view. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Tagged objects (and tagged <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s for <b>in</b> parameters) do not need to be aliased. This matches the behavior of unaliased formal parameters of tagged types, which allow 'Access to be taken of the formal parameter regardless of the form of the actual parameter. <br />

<MarginText>6.b/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We need the subtype check on untagged actual parameters so that the requirements of 'Access are not lost. 'Access makes its checks against the nominal subtype of its prefix, and parameter passing can change that subtype. But we don't want this parameter passing to change the objects that would be allowed as the prefix of 'Access. This is particularly important for arrays, where we don't want to require any additional implementation burden. <br />

<MarginText>6.b.1/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0095-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We assume the worst in a generic body regarding whether a formal subtype has a constrained partial view; specifically, in a generic body a discriminated subtype is considered to have a constrained partial view if it is a descendant of an untagged generic formal private or derived type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a> for the formal definition of this rule). <br />

<MarginText>6.3/4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0095-1"]} />
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.4/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0234-1"]} />
<p>In a function call, the accessibility level of the actual object for each explicitly aliased parameter shall not be statically deeper than the accessibility level of the master of the call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.c/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Since explicitly aliased parameters are either tagged or required to be objects, there is always an object (possibly anonymous) to talk about. This is discussing the static accessibility level of the actual object; it does not depend on any runtime information (for instance when the actual object is a formal parameter of another subprogram, it does not depend on the actual parameter of that other subprogram). <br />

<MarginText>6.d/4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0095-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This accessibility check (and its dynamic cousin as well) can only fail if the master of the function call (which is defined in the Heart of Darkness, or <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a> if you prefer) is different than the master directly enclosing the call. The most likely place where this will occur is in the initializer of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>; in almost all other cases this check will always pass. <br />

<MarginText>6.5/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0144-2"]} />
<p>Two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are <i>known to denote the same object</i> if:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.6/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s statically denote the same stand-alone object or parameter; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.7/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>s, their <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es are known to denote the same object, and their <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>s denote the same component; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.8/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are dereferences (implicit or explicit) and the dereferenced <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are known to denote the same object; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.9/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>s, their <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es are known to denote the same object, and each of the pairs of corresponding index values are either both static expressions with the same static value or both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s that are known to denote the same object; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.10/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0097">slice</a></code>s, their <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es are known to denote the same object, and the two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0097">slice</a></code>s have statically matching index constraints; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.11/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>one of the two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s statically denotes a renaming declaration whose renamed <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is known to denote the same object as the other, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of any dereference within the renamed <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is not a variable, and any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> within the renamed <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> contains no references to variables nor calls on nonstatic functions. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.e/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This exposes known renamings of slices, indexing, and so on to this definition. In particular, if we have <br />

<MarginText>6.f/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
C : Character renames S(1);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.g/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
then C and S(1) are known to denote the same object.<br />

<MarginText>6.h/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
We need the requirement that no variables occur in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es of dereferences and in (index) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s of the renamed object in order to avoid problems from later changes to those parts of renamed names. Consider:<br />

<MarginText>6.i/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   type Ref is access Some{"_"}Type;{"\n"}   Ptr : Ref := new Some{"_"}Type'(...);{"\n"}   X : Some{"_"}Type renames Ptr.all;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   Ptr := new Some{"_"}Type'(...);{"\n"}   P (Func{"_"}With{"_"}Out{"_"}Params (Ptr.all), X);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.j/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
X and Ptr.<b>all</b> should not be known to denote the same object, since they denote different allocated objects (and this is not an unreasonable thing to do). <br />

<MarginText>6.k/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The exclusion of variables from renamed object{"_"}names is not enough to prevent altering the value of the name or expression by another access path. For instance, both <b>in</b> parameters passed by reference and access-to-constant values can designate variables. For the intended use of "known to be the same object", this is OK; the modification via another access path is very tricky and it is OK to reject code that would be buggy except for the tricky code. Assuming Element is an elementary type, consider the following example: <br />

<MarginText>6.l/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Global : Tagged{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6.m/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
procedure Foo (Param : in Tagged{"_"}Type := Global) is{"\n"}   X : Element renames Some{"_"}Global{"_"}Array (Param.C);{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   Global.C := Global.C + 1;{"\n"}   Swap (X, Some{"_"}Global{"_"}Array (Param.C));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.n/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
The rules will flag the call of procedure Swap as illegal, since X and Some{"_"}Global{"_"}Array (Parameter.C) are known to denote the same object (even though they will actually represent different objects if Param = Global). But this is only incorrect if the parameter actually is Global and not some other value; the error could exist for some calls. So this flagging seems harmless.<br />

<MarginText>6.o/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
Similar examples can be constructed using stand-alone composite constants with controlled or immutably limited components, and (as previously noted) with dereferences of access-to-constant values. Even when these examples flag a call incorrectly, that call depends on very tricky code (modifying the value of a constant); the code is likely to confuse future maintainers as well and thus we do not mind rejecting it. <br />

<MarginText>6.p/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Whether or not <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>es are known to denote the same object is determined statically. If the name contains some dynamic portion other than a dereference, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0097">slice</a></code>, it is not "known to denote the same object".<br />

<MarginText>6.q/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
These rules make no attempt to handle slices of objects that are known to be the same when the slices have dynamic bounds (other than the trivial case of bounds being defined by the same subtype), even when the bounds could be proven to be the same, as it is just too complex to get right and these rules are intended to be conservative. <br />

<MarginText>6.r/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>"Known to denote the same object" is intended to be an equivalence relationship, that is, it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. We believe this follows from the rules. For instance, given the following declarations: <br />

<MarginText>6.s/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
S   : String(1..10);{"\n"}ONE : constant Natural := 1;{"\n"}R   : Character renames S(1);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.t/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
the names R and S(1) are known to denote the same object by the sixth bullet, and S(1) and S(ONE) are known to denote the same object by the fourth bullet, so using the sixth bullet on R and S(ONE), we simply have to test S(1) vs. S(ONE), which we already know denote the same object. <br />

<MarginText>6.12/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0144-2"]} />
<p>Two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are <i>known to refer to the same object</i> if <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.13/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are known to denote the same object; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.14/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>One of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0097">slice</a></code> and its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> is known to refer to the same object as the other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.15/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>One of the two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s statically denotes a renaming declaration whose renamed <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is known to refer to the same object as the other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.u/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that names Prefix.Comp and Prefix are known to refer to the same object for the purposes of the rules below. This intentionally does not include dereferences; we only want to worry about accesses to the same object, and a dereference changes the object in question. (There is nothing shared between an access value and the object it designates.) <br />

<MarginText>6.16/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0144-2"]} />
<p>If a call <i>C</i> has two or more parameters of mode <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> that are of an elementary type, then the call is legal only if:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.17/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0216-1", "AI12-0324-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> <i>N</i> denoting an object of an elementary type that is passed as a parameter of mode <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> to the call <i>C</i>, there is no other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> among the other parameters of mode <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> to <i>C</i> that is known to denote the same object.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.v/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>This means <i>visibly</i> an elementary type; it does not include partial views of elementary types (partial views are always composite). That's necessary to avoid having Legality Rules depend on the contents of the private part. <br />

<MarginText>6.18/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0144-2"]} />
<p>If a construct <i>C</i> has two or more direct constituents that are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s whose evaluation may occur in an arbitrary order, at least one of which contains a function call with an <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> parameter, then the construct is legal only if:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.w/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>All of the places where the language allows an arbitrary order can be found by looking in the index under "arbitrary order, allowed". Note that this listing includes places that don't involve <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s (such as checks or finalization). <br />

<MarginText>6.19/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For each name <i>N</i> that is passed as a parameter of mode <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> to some inner function call <i>C2</i> (not including the construct <i>C</i> itself), there is no other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> anywhere within a direct constituent of the construct <i>C</i> other than the one containing <i>C2</i>, that is known to refer to the same object. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.x/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This requirement cannot fail for a procedure or entry call alone; there must be at least one function with an <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> parameter called as part of a parameter expression of the call in order for it to fail. <br />

<MarginText>6.y/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>These rules prevent obvious cases of dependence on the order of evaluation of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s. Such dependence is usually a bug, and in any case, is not portable to another implementation (or even another optimization setting).<br />

<MarginText>6.z/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
In the case that the top-level construct C is a call, these rules do not require checks for most <b>in out</b> parameters, as the rules about evaluation of calls prevent problems. Similarly, we do not need checks for short circuit operations or other operations with a defined order of evaluation. The rules about arbitrary order (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.4">1.1.4</a>) allow evaluating parameters and writing parameters back in an arbitrary order, but not interleaving of evaluating parameters of one call with writing parameters back from another &mdash; that would not correspond to any allowed sequential order. <br />

<MarginText>6.20/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0144-2"]} />
<p>For the purposes of checking this rule:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.21/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For an array <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> associated with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0073">discrete_choice_list</a></code> that has two or more discrete choices, or that has a nonstatic range, is considered as two or more separate occurrences of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.22/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>For a record <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.23/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> is considered to occur once for each associated component; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.24/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> for each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0109">record_component_association</a></code> with {"<"}{">"} for which the associated component has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> is considered part of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.25/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a call, any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code> evaluated as part of the call is considered part of the call. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.aa/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We do not check expressions that are evaluated only because of a component initialized by default in an aggregate (via {"<"}{">"}). <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7_6.4.1</MarginText>
<p>For the evaluation of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code>: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The actual parameter is first evaluated.<br /></li>
<MarginText>9_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>For an access parameter, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is elaborated, which creates the anonymous access type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10_6.4.1</MarginText>
<li>For a parameter [(of any mode)] that is passed by reference (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.2">6.2</a>), a view conversion of the actual parameter to the nominal subtype of the formal parameter is evaluated, and the formal parameter denotes that conversion. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We are always allowing sliding, even for [<b>in</b>] <b>out</b> by-reference parameters. <br />

<MarginText>11_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For an <b>in</b> or <b>in out</b> parameter that is passed by copy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.2">6.2</a>), the formal parameter object is created, and the value of the actual parameter is converted to the nominal subtype of the formal parameter and assigned to the formal. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The conversion mentioned here is a value conversion. <br />

<MarginText>12_6.4.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For an <b>out</b> parameter that is passed by copy, the formal parameter object is created, and: <br /></li>
<MarginText>13/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0196-1", "AI12-0378-1"]} />
<li>For an access type, the formal parameter is initialized from the value of the actual, without checking whether the value satisfies any constraints, predicates, or null exclusions, but including any[ dynamic] accessibility checks associated with a conversion to the type of the formal parameter.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This preserves the Language Design Principle that an object of an access type is always initialized with a &ldquo;reasonable&rdquo; value. <br />

<MarginText>13.b/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0378-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The permission to pass <b>null</b> (see below) can be used in any case where an accessibility check could fail, rather than making a check. <br />

<MarginText>13.1/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3", "AI05-0228-1", "AI12-0074-1", "AI12-0159-1", "AI12-0377-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For a scalar type that has the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified, the formal parameter is initialized from the value of the actual, without checking that the value satisfies any constraint or any predicate.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.c/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This preserves the Language Design Principle that all objects of a type with an implicit initial value are initialized. This is important so that a programmer can guarantee that all objects of a scalar type have a valid value with a carefully chosen Default{"_"}Value. <br />

<MarginText>13.d/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This rule means that <b>out</b> parameters of a subtype <i>T</i> with a specified Default{"_"}Value need to be large enough to support any possible value of the base type of <i>T</i>. In contrast, a type that does not have a Default{"_"}Value only need support the size of the subtype (since no values are passed in). <br />

<MarginText>14/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0333-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For a composite type with discriminants or that has implicit initial values for any subcomponents (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>), the behavior is as for an <b>in out</b> parameter passed by copy[, except that no predicate check is performed]. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that no part of an object of such a type can become &ldquo;de-initialized&rdquo; by being part of an <b>out</b> parameter. <br />

<MarginText>14.b_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This includes an array type whose component type is an access type, and a record type with a component that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>, among other things. <br />

<MarginText>14.c/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0333-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>No predicate check follows from the definition of subtype conversion in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>. <br />

<MarginText>15/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>For any other type, the formal parameter is uninitialized. If composite, a view conversion of the actual parameter to the nominal subtype of the formal is evaluated [(which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error)], and the actual subtype of the formal is that of the view conversion. If elementary, the actual subtype of the formal is given by its nominal subtype. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.a/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0228-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This case covers scalar types that do not have Default{"_"}Value specified, and composite types whose subcomponent's subtypes do not have any implicit initial values. The view conversion for composite types ensures that if the lengths don't match between an actual and a formal array parameter, the Constraint{"_"}Error is raised before the call, rather than after. <br />

<MarginText>15.1/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0377-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Furthermore, if the type is a scalar type, and the actual parameter is a view conversion, then Program{"_"}Error is raised if either the target or the operand type has the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified, unless they both have the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified, and there is a type (other than a root numeric type) that is an ancestor of both the target type and the operand type.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.b/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This can only occur in the body of an instance of a generic unit. Legality Rules will catch all other cases. Implementations that macro-expand generics can always detect this case when the enclosing instance body is expanded. <br />

<MarginText>15.2/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0234-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>In a function call, for each explicitly aliased parameter, a check is made that the accessibility level of the master of the actual object is not deeper than that of the master of the call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.c/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the actual object to a call <i>C</i> is a formal parameter of some function call <i>F</i>, no dynamic check against the master of the actual parameter of <i>F</i> is necessary. Any case which could fail the dynamic check is already statically illegal (either at the call site of <i>F</i>, or at the call site <i>C</i>). This is important, as it would require nasty distributed overhead to accurately know the dynamic accessibility of a formal parameter (all tagged and explicitly aliased parameters would have to carry accessibility levels). <br />

<MarginText>16_6.4.1</MarginText>
<p>A formal parameter of mode <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> with discriminants is constrained if either its nominal subtype or the actual parameter is constrained.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17_6.4.1</MarginText>
<p>After normal completion and leaving of a subprogram, for each <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> parameter that is passed by copy, the value of the formal parameter is converted to the subtype of the variable given as the actual parameter and assigned to it. These conversions and assignments occur in an arbitrary order. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The conversions mentioned above during parameter passing might raise Constraint{"_"}Error &mdash; (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>). <br />

<MarginText>17.b_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If any conversion or assignment as part of parameter passing propagates an exception, the exception is raised at the place of the subprogram call; that is, it cannot be handled inside the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>17.c_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Since these checks happen before or after executing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> does not dynamically enclose them, so it can't handle the exceptions. <br />

<MarginText>17.d_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The variable we're talking about is the one denoted by the <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> given as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0221">explicit_actual_parameter</a></code>. If this <i>variable{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>, then the rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a> for assigning to a view conversion apply. That is, if X is of subtype S1, and the actual is S2(X), the above-mentioned conversion will convert to S2, and the one mentioned in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a> will convert to S1. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>18/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1"]} />
<p>If the nominal subtype of a formal parameter with discriminants is constrained or indefinite, and the parameter is passed by reference, then the execution of the call is erroneous if the value of any discriminant of the actual is changed while the formal parameter exists (that is, before leaving the corresponding callable construct). <br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>19/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0378-1"]} />
<p>If the actual parameter in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0220">parameter_association</a></code> with mode <b>out</b> is a view conversion between two access types that do not share a common ancestor type, the implementation may pass in the null value of the type of the formal parameter instead of the value of the actual parameter. It is implementation-defined under what circumstances the implementation passes in the null value. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The circumstances in which the implementation passes in the null value for a view conversion of an access type used as an <b>out</b> parameter.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>19.b_6.4.1</MarginText>
In Ada 95, a program can rely on the fact that passing an object as an <b>out</b> parameter does not &ldquo;de-initialize&rdquo; any parts of the object whose subtypes have implicit initial values. (This generalizes the RM83 rule that required copy-in for parts that were discriminants or of an access type.) <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>19.c/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
We have eliminated the subclause on Default Parameters, as it is subsumed by earlier subclauses. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2005

<MarginText>19.d/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0196-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified that <b>out</b> parameters of an access type are not checked for null exclusions when they are passed in (which is similar to the behavior for constraints). This was unspecified in Ada 2005, so a program which depends on the behavior of an implementation which does check the exclusion may malfunction. But a program depending on an exception being raised is unlikely. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>19.e/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0144-2"]} />
Additional rules have been added to make illegal passing the same elementary object to more than one <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> parameters of the same call. In this case, the result in the object could depend on the compiler version, optimization settings, and potentially the phase of the moon, so this check will mostly reject programs that are nonportable and could fail with any change. Even when the result is expected to be the same in both parameters, the code is unnecessarily tricky. Programs which fail this new check should be rare and are easily fixed by adding a temporary object. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>19.f/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0008-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> A missing rule was added to cover cases that were missed in Ada 95 and Ada 2005; specifically, that an <b>in</b> parameter passed by reference might have its discriminants changed via another path. Such cases are erroneous as requiring compilers to detect such errors would be expensive, and requiring such cases to work would be a major change of the user model (<b>in</b> parameters with discriminants could no longer be assumed constant). This is not an inconsistency, as compilers are not required to change any current behavior.<br />

<MarginText>19.g/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0102-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Moved implicit conversion Legality Rule to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>.<br />

<MarginText>19.h/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0118-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a definition for positional parameters, as this is missing from Ada 95 and later.<br />

<MarginText>19.i/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
Rules have been added defining the legality and dynamic checks needed for explicitly aliased parameters (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>19.j/3_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0144-2"]} />
Additional rules have been added such that passing an object to an <b>in out</b> or <b>out</b> parameter of a function is illegal if it is used elsewhere in a construct which allows evaluation in an arbitrary order. Such calls are not portable (since the results may depend on the evaluation order), and the results could even vary because of optimization settings and the like. Thus they've been banned. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>19.k/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0378-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a permission to pass <b>null</b> so that value passed into an <b>out</b> parameter for access types is well-defined in the case of a view conversion. <b>Null</b> may be passed for any view conversion between unrelated access types; this is important for conversions that may have problematic accessibility or tags. If the permission is used and the <b>out</b> parameter is read before it is written (perhaps to read a bound or discriminant), Constraint{"_"}Error may be raised by Ada 2022 when it would not have been in Ada 2012. Additionally, if the called subprogram does not write the <b>out</b> parameter at all, the actual object will be overwritten with <b>null</b> (and possibly raise Constraint{"_"}Error if the object is null excluding), while the object would be unchanged in Ada 2012. Such cases are thought to be rare, as most <b>out</b> parameters of access types are overwritten before being read. In addition, at least one widely-used Ada compiler already passes <b>null</b> in these cases. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>19.l/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0074-1", "AI12-0159-1", "AI12-0377-1", "AI12-0378-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added rules to ensure that the value passed into an <b>out</b> parameter for scalar types is well-defined in the case of a view conversion. The new rules can be incompatible. View conversions from/to an unrelated type with the Default{"_"}Value aspect specified are unlikely to occur in existing code, as the aspect is new in Ada 2012. Declaring and passing a temporary rather than a view conversion will eliminate the problem.<br />

<MarginText>19.m/4_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0095-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Because of a rule added in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a>, the checks for the passing of an object to an explicitly aliased parameter in a generic body were strengthened to use an assume the worst rule. This case is rather unlikely as a formal private or derived type with discriminants is required along with an explicitly aliased parameter whose type doesn't statically match the formal type. Such a program is very unlikely, especially as explicitly aliased parameters are a new Ada 2012 feature. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>19.n/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0216-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The <b>in out</b> parameter rule only applies to actual parameters of elementary types. While this allows additional programs (and thus could be considered an extension), it is unlikely to change anything in a real program (it could only matter in a call with 4 or more parameters, and then only if two composite parameters have matching actuals). Thus we document it as a wording change.<br />

<MarginText>19.o/5_6.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0333-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Predicate checks are not made for inbound <b>out</b> parameters. The actual rule change that has this effect is found in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a> and is documented there. <br />

---

# 6.5. Return Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5.mdx

sidebar_position:  55

# 6.5. Return Statements

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> (collectively called a <i>return statement</i>) is used to complete the execution of the innermost enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram{"_"}body</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry{"_"}body</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0222"></a><a id="S0223"></a><code> ::= </code><b>return</b> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0277-1", "AI12-0398-1", "AI12-0446-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>extended{"_"}return{"_"}object{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0224"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> : [<b>aliased</b>] [<b>constant</b>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return_subtype_indication</a></code> [:= <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]<br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0015-1", "AI05-0053-1", "AI05-0277-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0225"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>return</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> [<b>do</b><br />        <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />    <b>end</b> <b>return</b>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.3/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>return{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</code><a id="S0226"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI12-0173-1"]} />
<p>The <i>result subtype</i> of a function is the subtype denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>, or defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, after the reserved word <b>return</b> in the profile of the function. The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, if any, of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> is the result type of the corresponding function. The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> is that of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The same applies to generic functions. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<p>A return statement shall be within a callable construct, and it <i>applies to</i> the innermost callable construct or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> that contains it. A return statement shall not be within a body that is within the construct to which the return statement applies.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0089-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>The above also applies to generic subprograms, even though they are not callable constructs. (An instance of a generic subprogram is a callable construct, but not a generic subprogram itself.) <br />

<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0015-1", "AI12-0173-1"]} />
<p>A function body shall contain at least one return statement that applies to the function body, unless the function contains <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.8#S0357">code_statement</a></code>s. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> shall include an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> if and only if it applies to a function body. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> shall apply to a function body. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> with the reserved word <b>constant</b> shall include an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI12-0022-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The requirement that a function body has to have at least one return statement is a &ldquo;helpful&rdquo; restriction. There has been some interest in lifting this restriction, or allowing a raise statement to substitute for the return statement. However, there was enough interest in leaving it as is that we decided not to change it. Note that for Ada 2012, Corrigendum 1, a return statement whose expression is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> can be given in <i>any</i> function body (the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code> will match any type), so there is much less need to eliminate this rule. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A return statement can apply to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>, so a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> without an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> can be given in one. However, neither <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> nor an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> can be given inside an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>, as they must apply (directly) to a function body.<br />

<MarginText>5.b.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0089-1"]} />
Since a "function body" includes a generic function body, this rule and all of the following Legality Rules apply to generic function bodies as well as non-generic function bodies. This is true even though a generic function is not a function. <br />

<MarginText>5.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0173-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>The <i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code></i> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (if any) of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.b.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0173-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The <i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a return statement</i> is either the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code> or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> as defined above. <br />

<MarginText>5.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<p>For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> that applies to a function body:<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0032-1", "AI05-0103-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the result subtype of the function is defined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>. The type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> shall be covered by the result type of the function. The subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> shall be statically compatible with the result subtype of the function; if the result type of the function is elementary, the two subtypes shall statically match. If the result subtype of the function is indefinite, then the subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> shall be a definite subtype, or there shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<li>If the result subtype of the function is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>. The subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> shall statically match the result subtype of the function. [The accessibility level of this anonymous access subtype is that of the result subtype.] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.b.3/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0070-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The accessibility of such anonymous access types is defined in the Heart of Darkness (aka <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>). <br />

<MarginText>5.5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0032-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the result subtype of the function is class-wide, the accessibility level of the type of the subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return_subtype_indication</a></code> shall not be statically deeper than that of the master that elaborated the function body. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.b.4/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>In this case, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return_subtype_indication</a></code> could be a specific type initialized by default; in that case there is no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> to check. <br />

<MarginText>5.6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0032-1"]} />
<p>For any return statement that applies to a function body:<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0188-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>[If the result subtype of the function is limited, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the return statement (if any) shall meet the restrictions described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>.] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0188-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>5.8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0032-1", "AI05-0051-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the result subtype of the function is class-wide, the accessibility level of the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (if any) of the return statement shall not be statically deeper than that of the master that elaborated the function body.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.d/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0032-1", "AI05-0051-1", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>If the result type is class-wide, then there must be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the return statement unless this is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return_subtype_indication</a></code> is a specific type. We have a separate rule to cover that case. Note that if an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> has an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, then both this rule and the next one must be satisfied. <br />

<MarginText>5.9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0051-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the subtype determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code> or by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return_subtype_indication</a></code> has one or more access discriminants, the accessibility level of the anonymous access type of each access discriminant shall not be statically deeper than that of the master that elaborated the function body.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.d.1/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We use the type used by the return statement rather than from the function return type since we want to check whenever the return object has access discriminants, even if the function return type doesn't have any (mostly for a class-wide type). <br />

<MarginText>5.10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0277-1", "AI12-0426-1"]} />
<p>If the reserved word <b>aliased</b> is present in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code>, the type of the extended return object shall be immutably limited. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5.11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0015-1", "AI05-0144-2"]} />
<p>Within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>, the <i>return object</i> is declared with the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>, with the nominal subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code>. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> with the reserved word <b>constant</b> is a full constant declaration that declares the return object to be a constant object. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5.12/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0032-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is elaborated. This creates the nominal subtype of the return object. If there is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, it is evaluated and converted to the nominal subtype (which can raise Constraint{"_"}Error &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>); the return object is created and the converted value is assigned to the return object. Otherwise, the return object is created and initialized by default as for a stand-alone object of its nominal subtype (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>). If the nominal subtype is indefinite, the return object is constrained by its initial value. A check is made that the value of the return object belongs to the function result subtype. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.e/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the result type is controlled or has a controlled part, appropriate calls on Initialize or Adjust are performed prior to executing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>, except when the initial expression is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> (which requires build-in-place with no call on Adjust).<br />

<MarginText>5.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
If the return statement is left without resulting in a return (for example, due to an exception propagated from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>, or a goto out of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>), if the return object has been created, it is finalized prior to leaving the return statement. If it has not been created when the return statement is left, it is not created or finalized.<br />

<MarginText>5.g/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0032-1"]} />
Other rules ensure that the check required by this rule cannot fail unless the function has a class-wide result subtype where the associated specific subtype is constrained. In other cases, either the subtypes have to match or the function's subtype is unconstrained and needs no checking. <br />

<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> (if any) is first evaluated, converted to the result subtype, and then is assigned to the anonymous <i>return object</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The conversion might raise Constraint{"_"}Error &mdash; (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>). <br />

<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
<p>[If the return object has any parts that are tasks, the activation of those tasks does not occur until after the function returns (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.2">9.2</a>).] <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This is specified by the rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.2">9.2</a>. <br />

<MarginText>7.b/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Only the caller can know when task activations should take place, as it depends on the context of the call. If the function is being used to initialize the component of some larger object, then that entire object must be initialized before any task activations. Even after the outer object is fully initialized, task activations are still postponed until the <b>begin</b> at the end of the declarative part if the function is being used to initialize part of a declared object. <br />

<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI95-00344-01", "AI05-0024-1", "AI05-0032-1", "AI12-0097-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>If the result type of a function is a specific tagged type, the tag of the return object is that of the result type. If the result type is class-wide, the tag of the return object is that of the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the return statement, unless the return object is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> that is specific, in which case it is that of the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code>. A check is made that the master of the type identified by the tag of the result includes the elaboration of the master that elaborated the function body. If this check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The first sentence is true even if the tag of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is different, which could happen if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> were a view conversion or a dereference of an access value. Note that for a limited type, because of the restriction to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s and function calls (and no conversions), the tag will already match. <br />

<MarginText>8.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The first rule ensures that a function whose result type is a specific tagged type always returns an object whose tag is that of the result type. This is important for dispatching on controlling result, and allows the caller to allocate the appropriate amount of space to hold the value being returned (assuming there are no discriminants).<br />

<MarginText>8.c/3</MarginText>
The master check prevents the returned object from outliving its type. Note that this check cannot fail for a specific tagged type, as the tag represents the function's type, which necessarily must be declared outside of the function.<br />

<MarginText>8.d/3</MarginText>
We can't use the normal accessibility level &ldquo;deeper than&rdquo; check here because we may have &ldquo;incomparable&rdquo; levels if the masters belong to two different tasks. This can happen when an accept statement calls a function declared in the enclosing task body, and the function returns an object passed to it from the accept statement, and this object was itself a parameter to the accept statement. <br />

<MarginText>8.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0058-1", "AI12-0343-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> is executed. Within this <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>, the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> that applies to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> causes a transfer of control that completes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code>. Upon completion of a return statement that applies to a callable construct by the normal completion of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code> or by reaching the <b>end return</b> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code>, a transfer of control is performed which completes the execution of the callable construct, and returns to the caller.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0058-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A transfer of control that completes an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> (such as an exit or goto) does not cause a return to the caller unless it is caused by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code> (that is, triggers the second sentence of this paragraph). The return to the caller occurs for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code> that applies to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> because the last sentence says &ldquo;the normal completion of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code>&rdquo;, which includes the one nested in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>8.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0343-1"]} />
The check on the tag of the object occurs when the object is created (before any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>); the checks which follow occur after the execution of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>. This is implicit in the order of definition of these Dynamic Semantics. <br />

<MarginText>8.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0073-1", "AI12-0343-1"]} />
<p>If the result subtype of the function is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> designating a specific tagged type <i>T</i>, a check is made that the result value is null or the tag of the object designated by the result value identifies <i>T</i>. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.g/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This check is needed so that dispatching on controlling access results works for tag-indeterminate functions. If it was not made, it would be possible for such functions to return an access to a descendant type, meaning the function could return an object with a tag different than the one assumed by the dispatching rules. <br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 9 through 20 were deleted.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>21/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI95-00402-01", "AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0051-1"]} />
<p>If any part of the specific type of the return object of a function (or coextension thereof) has one or more access discriminants whose value is not constrained by the result subtype of the function, a check is made that the accessibility level of the anonymous access type of each access discriminant, as determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> of the return statement, is not deeper than the level of the master of the call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>). If this check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>21.b/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The check prevents the returned object (for a nonlimited type) from outliving the object designated by one of its discriminants. The check is made on the values of the discriminants, which may come from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return{"_"}subtype{"_"}indication</a></code> (if constrained), or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, but it is never necessary to check both. <br />

<MarginText>21.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0234-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The reason for saying &ldquo;any part of the specific type&rdquo; is to simplify implementation. In the case of class-wide result objects, this allows the testing of a simple flag in the tagged type descriptor that indicates whether the specific type has any parts with access discriminants. By basing the test on the type of the object rather than the object itself, we avoid concerns about whether subcomponents in variant parts and of arrays (which might be empty) are present. <br />

<MarginText>21.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0234-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For a function with a class-wide result type, the access values that need to be checked are determined by the tag of the return object. In order to implement this accessibility check in the case where the tag of the result is not known statically at the point of the return statement, an implementation may need to somehow associate with the tag of a specific tagged type an indication of whether the type has unconstrained access discriminants (explicit or inherited) or has any subcomponents with such discriminants. If an implementation is already maintaining a statically initialized descriptor of some kind for each specific tagged type, then an additional Boolean could be added to this descriptor.<br />

<MarginText>21.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1", "AI05-0234-1"]} />
Note that the flag should only be queried in the case where the result object might have access discriminants that might have subtypes with "bad" accessibility levels (as determined by the rules of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a> for determining the accessibility level of the type of an access discriminant in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return_subtype_indication</a></code> of a return statement).<br />

<MarginText>21.f/3</MarginText>
Thus, in a case like<br />

<MarginText>21.g/3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Global is access T'Class;{"\n"}function F (Ptr : Global) return T'Class is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   return Ptr.all;{"\n"}end F;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21.h/3</MarginText>
there is no need for a run-time accessibility check. While an object of T'Class "might have" access discriminants, the accessibility of those potential discriminants cannot be bad. The setting of the bit doesn't matter and there is no need to query it.<br />

<MarginText>21.i/3</MarginText>
On the other hand, given <br />

<MarginText>21.j/3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function F return T'Class is{"\n"}   Local : T'Class := ... ;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   return Local;{"\n"}end F;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21.k/3</MarginText>
In this case, a check would typically be required.<br />

<MarginText>21.l/3</MarginText>
The need for including subcomponents in this check is illustrated by the following example: <br />

<MarginText>21.m/3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X : aliased Integer;{"\n"}
<MarginText>21.n/3</MarginText>
type Component{"_"}Type (Discrim : access Integer := X'Access){"\n"}   is limited null record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>21.o/3</MarginText>
type Undiscriminated is record{"\n"}   Fld : Component{"_"}Type;{"\n"}end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>21.p/3</MarginText>
function F return Undiscriminated is{"\n"}   Local : aliased Integer;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   return X : Undiscriminated := (Fld ={">"} (Discrim ={">"} Local'Access)) do{"\n"}      Foo;{"\n"}   end return;{"\n"}   -- raises Program{"_"}Error after calling Foo.{"\n"}end F;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>21.q/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0234-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In the case where the tag of the result is not known statically at the point of the return statement and the run-time accessibility check is needed, discriminant values and array bounds play no role in performing this check. That is, array components are assumed to have nonzero length and components declared within variant parts are assumed to be present. Thus, the check may be implemented simply by testing the aforementioned descriptor bit and conditionally raising Program{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI05-0058-1", "AI12-0343-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>A check is performed that the return value satisfies the predicates of the return subtype. If this check fails, the effect is as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0058-1", "AI12-0343-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>22.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0343-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The subtype conversion of the return expression for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code> performs this same check. The permissions of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4#Subclause_11.4.2">11.4.2</a> ensure that duplicate evaluation of a predicate at a single point is not required (other than pathological, not portable cases), so a single evaluation of the predicate is enough in this case. <br />

<MarginText>23/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<p>In the case of a function, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> denotes a constant view of the return object. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>24/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0050-1"]} />
<p>For a function call used to initialize a composite object with a constrained nominal subtype or used to initialize a return object that is built in place into such an object:<br /></p>

<MarginText>24.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0050-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the result subtype of the function is constrained, and conversion of an object of this subtype to the subtype of the object being initialized would raise Constraint{"_"}Error, then Constraint{"_"}Error may be raised before calling the function.<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0050-1"]} />
<li>If the result subtype of the function is unconstrained, and a return statement is executed such that the return object is known to be constrained, and conversion of the return object to the subtype of the object being initialized would raise Constraint{"_"}Error, then Constraint{"_"}Error may be raised at the point of the call (after abandoning the execution of the function body). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0050-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Without such a permission, it would be very difficult to implement &ldquo;built-in-place&rdquo; semantics. The intention is that the exception is raised at the same point that it would have been raised without the permission; it should not change handlers if the implementation switches between return-by-copy and built-in-place. This means that the exception is not handleable within the function, because in the return-by-copy case, the constraint check to verify that the result satisfies the constraints of the object being initialized happens after the function returns. This implies further that upon detecting such a situation, the implementation may need to simulate a goto to a point outside any local exception handlers prior to raising the exception. <br />

<MarginText>24.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0050-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>These permissions do not apply in the case of an extended return object with mutable discriminants. That's necessary because in that case a return object can be created with the &ldquo;wrong&rdquo; discriminants and then changed to the &ldquo;right&rdquo; discriminants later (but before returning). We don't want this case raising an exception when the canonical semantics will not do so.<br />

<MarginText>24.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0050-1"]} />
It's still possible to write a program that will raise an exception using this permission that would not in the canonical semantics. That could happen if a return statement with the &ldquo;wrong&rdquo; discriminants or bounds is abandoned (via an exception, or for an extended{"_"}return{"_"}statement, via an exit or goto statement), and then a return statement with the &ldquo;right&rdquo; discriminants or bounds is executed. The only solution for this problem is to not have the permission at all, but this is too unusual of a case to worry about the effects of the permission, especially given the implementation difficulties for built-in-place objects that this permission is intended to ease.<br />

<MarginText>24.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0050-1"]} />
Note that the mutable-discriminant case only happens when built-in-place initialization is optional. This means that any difficulties associated with implementing built-in-place initialization without these permissions can be sidestepped by not building in place.<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of return statements:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>26/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
return;                         -- in a procedure body, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a>,{"\n"}                                -- <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a>, or <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a>{"\n"}
<MarginText>27</MarginText>
return Key{"_"}Value(Last{"_"}Index);   -- in a function body{"\n"}
<MarginText>28/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
return Node : Cell do           -- in a function body, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.1">3.10.1</a> for Cell{"\n"}   Node.Value := Result;{"\n"}   Node.Succ := Next{"_"}Node;{"\n"}end return;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>28.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
In Ada 95, if the result type of a function has a part that is a task, then an attempt to return a local variable will raise Program{"_"}Error. This is illegal in Ada 2005, see below. In Ada 83, if a function returns a local variable containing a task, execution is erroneous according to AI83-00867. However, there are other situations where functions that return tasks (or that return a variant record only one of whose variants includes a task) are correct in Ada 83 but will raise Program{"_"}Error according to the new rules.<br />

<MarginText>28.b</MarginText>
The rule change was made because there will be more types (protected types, limited controlled types) in Ada 95 for which it will be meaningless to return a local variable, and making all of these erroneous is unacceptable. The current rule was felt to be the simplest that kept upward incompatibilities to situations involving returning tasks, which are quite rare. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>28.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause has been moved here from chapter 5, since it has mainly to do with subprograms.<br />

<MarginText>28.d</MarginText>
A function now creates an anonymous object. This is necessary so that controlled types will work.<br />

<MarginText>28.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
We have clarified that a return statement applies to a callable construct, not to a callable entity.<br />

<MarginText>28.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
There is no need to mention generics in the rules about where a return statement can appear and what it applies to; the phrase &ldquo;body of a subprogram or generic subprogram&rdquo; is syntactic, and refers exactly to &ldquo;<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>&rdquo;. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 95

<MarginText>28.f.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-0416-1", "AI05-0005-1", "AI05-0050-1"]} />
Added an Implementation Permission allowing early raising of Constraint{"_"}Error if the result cannot fit in the ultimate object. This gives implementations more flexibility to do built-in-place returns, and is essential for limited types (which cannot be built in a temporary). However, it allows raising Constraint{"_"}Error in some cases where it would not be raised if the permission was not used. See Inconsistencies With Ada 2005 for additional changes. This case is potentially inconsistent with Ada 95, but a compiler does not have to take advantage of these permissions for any Ada 95 code, so there should be little practical impact. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>28.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
 The entire business about return-by-reference types has been dropped. Instead, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a return statement of a limited type can only be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>). This means that returning a global object or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>, legal in Ada 95, is now illegal. Such functions can be converted to use anonymous access return types by adding <b>access</b> in the function definition and return statement, adding .<b>all</b> in uses, and adding <b>aliased</b> in the object declarations. This has the advantage of making the reference return semantics much clearer to the casual reader.<br />

<MarginText>28.h/2</MarginText>
We changed these rules so that functions, combined with the new rules for limited types (<a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a>), can be used as build-in-place constructors for limited types. This reduces the differences between limited and nonlimited types, which will make limited types useful in more circumstances. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>28.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> is new. This provides a name for the object being returned, which reduces the copying needed to return complex objects (including no copying at all for limited objects). It also allows component-by-component construction of the return object. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>28.j/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
The wording was updated to support anonymous access return subtypes.<br />

<MarginText>28.k/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
The term &ldquo;return expression&rdquo; was dropped because reviewers found it confusing when applied to the default <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>28.l/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00344-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
