Added accessibility checks to class-wide return statements. These checks could not fail in Ada 95 (as all of the types had to be declared at the same level, so the tagged type would necessarily have been at the same level as the type of the object).<br />

<MarginText>28.m/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00402-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
Added accessibility checks to return statements for types with access discriminants. Since such types have to be limited in Ada 95, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a return statement would have been illegal in order for this check to fail. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.n/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0050-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The Implementation Permission allowing early raising of Constraint{"_"}Error was modified to remove the most common of these cases from the permission (returning an object with mutable discriminants, where the return object is created with one set of discriminants and then changed to another). (The permission was also widened to allow the early check for constrained functions when that constraint is wrong.) However, there still is an unlikely case where the permission would allow an exception to be raised when none would be raised by the canonical semantics (when a return statement is abandoned). These changes can only remove the raising of an exception (or change the place where it is raised) compared to Ada 2005, so programs that depend on the previous behavior should be very rare.<br />

<MarginText>28.o/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0051-1", "AI05-0234-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Accessibility checks for access discriminants now depend on the master of the call rather than the point of declaration of the function. This will result in cases that used to raise Program{"_"}Error now running without raising any exception. This is technically inconsistent with Ada 2005 (as defined by Amendment 1), but it is unlikely that any real code depends on the raising of this exception.<br />

<MarginText>28.p/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0073-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a tag check for functions returning anonymous access-to-tagged types, so that dispatching of tag-indeterminate function works as expected. This is technically inconsistent with Ada 2005 (as defined by Amendment 1), but as the feature in question was newly added to Ada 2005, there should be little code that depends on the behavior that now raises an exception. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.q/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0053-1", "AI05-0277-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The <b>aliased</b> keyword can now only appear on extended return objects with an immutably limited type. Other types would provide a way to get an aliased view of an object that is not necessarily aliased, which would be very bad. This is incompatible, but since the feature was added in Ada 2005, the keyword had no defined meaning in Ada 2005 (a significant oversight), and most sensible uses involve immutably limited types, it is unlikely that it appears meaningfully in existing programs.<br />

<MarginText>28.r/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0103-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording to require static matching for unconstrained access types in extended return statements. This disallows adding or omitting null exclusions, and adding access constraints, in the declaration of the return object. While this is incompatible, the incompatible cases in question are either useless (access constraints &ndash; the constraint can be given on an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> if necessary, and still must be given there even if given on the return object) or wrong (null exclusions &ndash; null could be returned from a function declared to be null excluding), so we expect them to be extremely rare in practice. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.s/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0015-1", "AI05-0144-2"]} />
The return object of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> can be declared constant; this works similarly to a constant object declaration.<br />

<MarginText>28.t/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0032-1"]} />
Added wording to allow the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0226">return_subtype_indication</a></code> to have a specific type if the return subtype of the function is class-wide. Specifying the (specific) type of the return object is awkward without this change, and this is consistent with the way <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s work. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.u/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0024-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the master check for tags since the masters may be for different tasks and thus incomparable.<br />

<MarginText>28.v/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0058-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the wording defining returns for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>s, since leaving by an exit or goto is considered &ldquo;normal&rdquo; completion of the statement.<br />

<MarginText>28.w/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0205-1", "AI05-0277-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> to make other rules easier to write and eliminate the problem described in AI05-0205-1. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.x/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0343-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Reordered the checks associated with return statements to clarify when they happen relative to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>, and to add an additional predicate check on the returned value. This latter check can fail if the value to be returned is changed in the statements of an extended return. Thus, the following function now raises Assertion{"_"}Error, while no exception would be raised in Ada 2012: <br />

<MarginText>28.y/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Rec is record{"\n"}  Count, Max : Natural;{"\n"}end record with Dynamic{"_"}Predicate ={">"} Rec.Count {"<"}= Rec.Max;{"\n"}
<MarginText>28.z/5</MarginText>
function Foo return Rec is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}    return Result : Rec := (Count ={">"} 5, Max ={">"} 10) do{"\n"}       Result.Max := 0;{"\n"}    end return;{"\n"}end Foo;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>28.aa/5</MarginText>
This will detect a program bug (returning a value that does not meet the predicate of the return subtype) rather than leaving it hidden, so the inconsistency is tolerable. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.bb/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0398-1"]} />
Extended return objects now can have an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>, allowing the specification of (implementation-defined) aspects for return objects. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>28.cc/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0097-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified the wording so that it is clear where the tag of the return object comes from. While a literal reading of the original Ada 2012 rule could have caused some weird results (by using some nearby <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> to provide the tag in the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code>), such a reading would be so unlike the rest of the language that we do not believe anyone would ever have thought it was intended. As such, we do not believe any implementation ever did this wrong (at least because of the old wording), and thus do not document this as a possible inconsistency.<br />

<MarginText>28.dd/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0173-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a definition of the term <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>. That wording was commonly used before the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0224">extended_return_object_declaration</a></code> was split into a separate syntax production, leaving the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code> without any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of its own. Moreover, the wording often just uses &ldquo;<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a return statement&rdquo; to cover both kinds of return statement. Changing the wording in more than a dozen places was unappealing, and some of the changes would be awkward to read, so we defined the term and left the majority of the wording unchanged. <br />

<a id="Subclause_6.5.1"></a>

## 6.5.1  Nonreturning Subprograms

<MarginText>1/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00329-01", "AI95-00414-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0269-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>Specifying aspect No{"_"}Return to have the value True indicates that a subprogram cannot return normally[; it may, for example, propagate an exception or loop forever]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Aspect No{"_"}Deposit will have to wait for Ada 2028. :-) <br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 2 and 3 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3.1/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p>For a subprogram or generic subprogram, the following language-defined representation aspect may be specified: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.2/3_6.5.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>No{"_"}Return</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect No{"_"}Return is Boolean. When aspect No{"_"}Return is True for an entity, the entity is said to be <i>nonreturning</i>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>3.3/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0423-1"]} />
<dd>If directly specified, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a static expression. When not directly specified, if the subprogram is a primitive subprogram inherited by a derived type, then the aspect is True if any corresponding subprogram of the parent or progenitor types is nonreturning. Otherwise, the aspect is False.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.a/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>No{"_"}Return: </b>A subprogram will not return normally.<br />

<MarginText>3.4/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p>If a generic subprogram is nonreturning, then so are its instances. If a subprogram declared within a generic unit is nonreturning, then so are the corresponding copies of that subprogram in instances.<br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/3_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00329-01", "AI95-00414-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>Aspect No{"_"}Return shall not be specified for a null procedure nor an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/2_6.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A null procedure cannot have the appropriate nonreturning semantics, as it does not raise an exception or loop forever. <br />

<MarginText>4.b/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0269-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The procedure can be abstract. If a nonreturning subprogram is renamed (anywhere) calls through the new name still have the nonreturning semantics. <br />

<MarginText>5/2_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00329-01", "AI95-00414-01"]} />
<p>A return statement shall not apply to a nonreturning procedure or generic procedure.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.1/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p>Any return statement that applies to a nonreturning function or generic function shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code> with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0309">raise_expression</a></code>, a call on a nonreturning function, or a parenthesized <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of one of these.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We still require at least one return statement in a function; we just require that all such return statements don't actually return a value. <br />

<MarginText>6/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00414-01", "AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p>A subprogram shall be nonreturning if it overrides a dispatching nonreturning subprogram. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), this rule applies also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that dispatching calls to nonreturning subprograms will, in fact, not return. <br />

<MarginText>7/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00414-01", "AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p>If a renaming-as-body completes a nonreturning subprogram declaration, then the renamed subprogram shall be nonreturning.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2_6.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that no extra code is needed to implement the renames (that is, no wrapper is needed) as the body has the same property. <br />

<p><i>Paragraph 8 was deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>9/2_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00329-01", "AI95-00414-01"]} />
<p>If the body of a nonreturning procedure completes normally, Program{"_"}Error is raised at the point of the call. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0269-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that there is no name for suppressing this check, since the check represents a bug, imposes no time overhead, and minimal space overhead (since it can usually be statically eliminated as dead code). We don't need a similar rule for nonreturning functions as this is standard semantics for all functions that normally complete without a transfer of control (such as a return statement). <br />

<MarginText>9.b/2_6.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>If a nonreturning procedure tries to return, we raise Program{"_"}Error. This is stated as happening at the call site, because we do not wish to allow the procedure to handle the exception (and then, perhaps, try to return again!). However, the expected run-time model is that the compiler will generate <b>raise</b> Program{"_"}Error at the end of the procedure body (but not handleable by the procedure itself), as opposed to doing it at the call site. (This is just like the typical run-time model for functions that fall off the end without returning a value). The reason is indirect calls: in P.<b>all</b>(...);, the compiler cannot know whether P designates a nonreturning procedure or a normal one. Putting the <b>raise</b> Program{"_"}Error in the procedure's generated code solves this problem neatly.<br />

<MarginText>9.c/2_6.5.1</MarginText>
Similarly, if one passes a nonreturning procedure to a generic formal parameter, the compiler cannot know this at call sites (in shared code implementations); the raise-in-body solution deals with this neatly. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>10/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a specification of a No{"_"}Return aspect:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>11/3_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Fail(Msg : String)  -- raises Fatal{"_"}Error exception{"\n"}   with No{"_"}Return;{"\n"}   -- Inform compiler and reader that procedure never returns normally{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>11.a/2_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00329-01", "AI95-00414-01"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> No{"_"}Return is new. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>11.b/3_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
Aspect No{"_"}Return is new; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> No{"_"}Return is now obsolescent. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>11.c/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0423-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified that the nonreturning property is inherited by derivation. A literal implementation of the Ada 2012 would mean that no overriding would ever be rejected, as the inherited routine would never be nonreturning. Ada 2022 requires overridings of dispatching nonreturning subprograms to be rejected. This is formally incompatible, but practically such overridings have been rejected in practice. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>11.d/5_6.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0269-1"]} />
Aspect No{"_"}Return can now be applied to functions as well as procedures. <br />

---

# 6.6. Overloading of Operators

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.6.mdx

sidebar_position:  56

# 6.6. Overloading of Operators

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>An <i>operator</i> is a function whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0199">designator</a></code> is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>. [Operators, like other functions, may be overloaded.] <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>Each use of a unary or binary operator is equivalent to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> with <i>function{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> being the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>, and with (respectively) one or two positional actual parameters being the operand(s) of the operator (in order). <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>We also use the term operator (in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/">4</a> and in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>) to refer to one of the syntactic categories defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5">4.5</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5">Operators and Expression Evaluation</a>&rdquo; whose names end with &ldquo;{"_"}operator:&rdquo; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0142">logical{"_"}operator</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0143">relational{"_"}operator</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0144">binary{"_"}adding{"_"}operator</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0145">unary{"_"}adding{"_"}operator</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0146">multiplying{"_"}operator</a></code>, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0147">highest{"_"}precedence{"_"}operator</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>2.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This equivalence extends to uses of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> in most other language rules. However, as often happens, the equivalence is not perfect, as operator calls are not a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, while a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. Thus, operator calls cannot be used in contexts that require a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (such as a rename of an object). A direct fix for this problem would be very disruptive, and thus we have not done that. However, qualifying an operator call can be used as a workaround in contexts that require a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0143-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0196">subprogram_specification</a></code> of a unary or binary operator shall have one or two parameters, respectively. The parameters shall be of mode <b>in</b>. A generic function instantiation whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0199">designator</a></code> is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> is only allowed if the specification of the generic function has the corresponding number of parameters, and they are all of mode <b>in</b>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">Default_expression</a></code>s are not allowed for the parameters of an operator (whether the operator is declared with an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0196">subprogram_specification</a></code> or by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>An explicit declaration of "/=" shall not have a result type of the predefined type Boolean. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0128-1"]} />
<p>An explicit declaration of "=" whose result type is Boolean implicitly declares an operator "/=" that gives the complementary result. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0128-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A "/=" defined by this rule is considered user-defined, which means that it will be inherited by a derived type. &ldquo;User-defined&rdquo; means &ldquo;not language-defined&rdquo; for the purposes of inheritance, that is anything other than predefined operators. <br />

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE   The operators "+" and "&ndash;" are both unary and binary operators, and hence can be overloaded with both one- and two-parameter functions. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of user-defined operators:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "+" (Left, Right : Matrix) return Matrix;{"\n"}function "+" (Left, Right : Vector) return Vector;{"\n"}{"\n"}--  assuming that A, B, and C are of the type Vector{"\n"}--  the following two statements are equivalent:{"\n"}{"\n"}A := B + C;{"\n"}A := "+"(B, C);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
Explicit declarations of "=" are now permitted for any combination of parameter and result types.<br />

<MarginText>9.b</MarginText>
Explicit declarations of "/=" are now permitted, so long as the result type is not Boolean. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>9.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0128-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the wording so that only explicit declarations of "=" cause an implicit declaration of "/="; otherwise, we could get multiple implicit definitions of "/=" without an obvious way to chose between them.<br />

<MarginText>9.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0143-1"]} />
Added wording so that operators only allow parameters of mode <b>in</b>. This was made necessary by the elimination elsewhere of the restriction that function parameters be only of mode <b>in</b>. <br />

---

# 6.7. Null Procedures

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7.mdx

sidebar_position:  57

# 6.7. Null Procedures

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> provides a shorthand to declare a procedure with an empty body. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01", "AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>null{"_"}procedure{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0227"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>]<br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0197">procedure_specification</a></code> <b>is</b> <b>null</b><br />       [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>2.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> is a completion, it shall be the completion of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0311">generic_subprogram_declaration</a></code>. The profile of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> that completes a declaration shall conform fully to that of the declaration. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01", "AI05-0177-1", "AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0408-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> that is not a completion declares a <i>null procedure</i>. A completion is not allowed for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code>; however, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> can complete a previous declaration. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>There are no null functions because the return value has to be constructed somehow; a function that always raises Program{"_"}Error doesn't seem very useful or worth the complication. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01", "AI12-0408-1"]} />
<p>The execution of a null procedure is invoked by a subprogram call. For the execution of a subprogram call on a null procedure, or on a procedure completed with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code>, the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> has no effect. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Thus, a null procedure is equivalent to the body <br />

<MarginText>4.b/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
begin{"\n"}   null;{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4.c/2</MarginText>
with the exception that a null procedure can be used in place of a procedure specification. <br />

<MarginText>5/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01", "AI05-0177-1"]} />
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> has no other effect than to establish that the null procedure can be called without failing the Elaboration{"_"}Check. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of the declaration of a null procedure:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Simplify(Expr : in out Expression) is null; -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9">3.9</a>{"\n"}-- By default, Simplify does nothing, but it can be overridden in extensions of Expression{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>7.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00348-01"]} />
Null procedures are new. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>7.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code> can now be a completion.<br />

<MarginText>7.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null_procedure_declaration</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>7.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0408-1"]} />
Clarified the term &ldquo;null procedure&rdquo; so it matches the meaning expected in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>. <br />

---

# 6.8. Expression Functions

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8.mdx

sidebar_position:  58

# 6.8. Expression Functions

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression_function_declaration</a></code> provides a shorthand to declare a function whose body consists of a single return statement. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-0177-1", "AI12-0157-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0228"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>]<br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0198">function_specification</a></code> <b>is</b><br />       (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>)<br />       [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br /> | [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>]<br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0198">function_specification</a></code> <b>is</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code><br />       [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1", "AI12-0157-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code> is the result type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a>) of the function. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1", "AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0075-1", "AI12-0157-1", "AI12-0408-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code> that is not a completion declares an <i>expression function</i>. The <i>return expression of an expression function</i> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression_function_declaration</a></code>. A completion is not allowed for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code>; however, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code> can complete a previous declaration.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0075-1"]} />
<p>A <i>potentially static expression</i> is defined in the same way as a static expression except that<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.3/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a name denoting a formal parameter of an expression function is a potentially static expression; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>3.4/5</MarginText>
<li>each use of &ldquo;static expression&rdquo; in the definition of &ldquo;static expression&rdquo; is replaced with a corresponding use of &ldquo;potentially static expression&rdquo; in the definition of &ldquo;potentially static expression&rdquo;. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>3.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>These uses occur in the definition of &ldquo;static expression&rdquo; in the cases of function calls, type conversions, qualified expressions, membership tests, short circuit control forms, conditional expressions, and parenthesized expressions. <br />

<MarginText>3.5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0075-1"]} />
<p>The following language-defined representation aspect may be specified for an expression function:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.6/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Static</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Static is Boolean. When aspect Static is True for an expression function, the function is a <i>static expression function</i>. If directly specified, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a static expression.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Static: </b>Specifies that an associated expression function can be used in static expressions.<br />

<MarginText>3.7/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/></dt>
<dl>
<dd>The Static value for an inherited function is True if some corresponding primitive function of the parent or progenitor type is a static expression function; otherwise, if not directly specified, the aspect is False. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0075-1"]} />
<p>[A static expression function is a static function; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9">4.9</a>.] <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
<p>If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code> is a completion, it shall be the completion of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0311">generic_subprogram_declaration</a></code>. The profile of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code> that completes a declaration shall conform fully to that of the declaration.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1", "AI12-0157-1"]} />
<p>If the result subtype has one or more unconstrained access discriminants, the accessibility level of the anonymous access type of each access discriminant, as determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code>, shall not be statically deeper than that of the master that elaborated the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This can only fail if the discriminant is an access to a part of a nonaliased parameter, as there can be no local declarations here. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We don't need to repeat any of the other Legality Rules for return statements since none of them can fail here: the implicit return statement has to apply to this function (and isn't nested in something), there clearly is a return statement in this function, and the static class-wide accessibility check cannot fail as a tagged type cannot be declared locally in an expression function. <br />

<MarginText>5.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0075-1"]} />
<p>Aspect Static shall be specified to have the value True only if the associated <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code>:<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.2/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>is not a completion;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.3/5</MarginText>
<li>has an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that is a potentially static expression;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.4/5</MarginText>
<li>contains no calls to itself;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.5/5</MarginText>
<li>each parameter (if any) is of mode <b>in</b> and is of a static subtype;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.6/5</MarginText>
<li>has a result subtype that is a static subtype;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.7/5</MarginText>
<li>has no applicable precondition or postcondition expression; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>5.8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0075-1", "AI12-0191-1"]} />
<li>for result type <i>R</i>, if the function is a boundary entity for type <i>R</i> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.2">7.3.2</a>), no type invariant applies to type <i>R</i>; if <i>R</i> has a component type <i>C</i>, a similar rule applies to <i>C</i>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.c/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Since a string subtype can be static, this allows an expression function of a string type to be static. <br />

<p><i>Paragraph 6 was deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0157-1", "AI12-0408-1"]} />
<p>The execution of an expression function is invoked by a subprogram call. For the execution of a subprogram call on an expression function, or on a function completed with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code>, the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> executes an implicit function body containing only a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple_return_statement</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is the return expression of the expression function.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The last sentence effectively means that all of the dynamic wording in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a> applies as needed, and we don't have to repeat it here. <br />

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
<p>The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code> has no other effect than to establish that the expression function can be called without failing the Elaboration{"_"}Check. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of an expression function:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>10/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Is{"_"}Origin (P : in Point) return Boolean is -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9">3.9</a>{"\n"}   (P.X = 0.0 and P.Y = 0.0);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>10.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1"]} />
Expression functions are new in Ada 2012. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>10.b/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0157-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> can directly be the return expression of an expression function. This eliminates the double parentheses that otherwise would be necessary.<br />

<MarginText>10.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0075-1"]} />
Aspect Static is new; it allows using suitable expression functions in static expressions. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>10.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0408-1"]} />
Clarified the term &ldquo;expression function&rdquo; so it matches the meaning expected in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>. <br />

---

# 6. Subprograms

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.mdx

sidebar_position:  50

# 6. Subprograms

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>A subprogram is a program unit or intrinsic operation whose execution is invoked by a subprogram call. There are two forms of subprogram: procedures and functions. A procedure call is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>; a function call is an expression and returns a value. The definition of a subprogram can be given in two parts: a subprogram declaration defining its interface, and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> defining its execution. [Operators and enumeration literals are functions.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>A function call is an expression, but more specifically it is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>1.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>subprogram</b> &mdash; unit of a program that can be brought into execution in various contexts, with the invocation being a subprogram call that can parameterize the effect of the subprogram through the passing of operands<br />Note: There are two forms of subprograms: functions, which return values, and procedures, which do not.<br />

<MarginText>1.c/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>function</b> &mdash; form of subprogram that returns a result and can be called as part of an expression<br />

<MarginText>1.d/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>procedure</b> &mdash; form of subprogram that does not return a result and can only be invoked by a statement<br />

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>A <i>callable entity</i> is a subprogram or entry (see Section 9). A callable entity is invoked by a <i>call</i>; that is, a subprogram call or entry call. A <i>callable construct</i> is a construct that defines the action of a call upon a callable entity: a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that &ldquo;callable entity&rdquo; includes predefined operators, enumeration literals, and abstract subprograms. &ldquo;Call&rdquo; includes calls of these things. They do not have callable constructs, since they don't have completions. <br />

---

# 7.1. Package Specifications and Declarations

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  60

# 7.1. Package Specifications and Declarations

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A package is generally provided in two parts: a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code> and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>. Every package has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, but not all packages have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>package{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0229"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>package{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0230"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>package</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0201">defining_program_unit_name</a></code><br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <b>is</b><br />      {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>{"}"}<br />   [<b>private</b><br />      {"{"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>{"}"}]<br />    <b>end</b> [[<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code>.]<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code>.<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> appears at the end of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, then this sequence of lexical elements shall repeat the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0201">defining_program_unit_name</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0312">generic_package_declaration</a></code> requires a completion [(a body)] if it contains any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code> that requires a completion, but whose completion is not in its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>If an implementation supports it, the body of a package or generic package may be imported (using aspect Import, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>), in which case no explicit body is allowed. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00420-01", "AI95-00434-01"]} />
<p>The first list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code> of a package other than a generic formal package is called the <i>visible part</i> of the package. [ The optional list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s after the reserved word <b>private</b> (of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>) is called the <i>private part</i> of the package. If the reserved word <b>private</b> does not appear, the package has an implicit empty private part.] Each list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code> forms a <i>declaration list</i> of the package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This definition of visible part does not apply to generic formal packages &mdash; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7">12.7</a> defines the visible part of a generic formal package.<br />

<MarginText>6.b</MarginText>
The implicit empty private part is important because certain implicit declarations occur there if the package is a child package, and it defines types in its visible part that are derived from, or contain as components, private types declared within the parent package. These implicit declarations are visible in children of the child package. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">10.1.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>[An entity declared in the private part of a package is visible only within the declarative region of the package itself (including any child units &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">10.1.1</a>). In contrast, expanded names denoting entities declared in the visible part can be used even outside the package; furthermore, direct visibility of such entities can be achieved by means of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4">8.4</a>).] <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code> consists of the elaboration of its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s in the given order. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
NOTE 1   The visible part of a package contains all the information that another program unit is able to know about the package.<br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
NOTE 2   If a declaration occurs immediately within the specification of a package, and the declaration has a corresponding completion that is a body, then that body has to occur immediately within the body of the package. <br />

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This follows from the fact that the declaration and completion are required to occur immediately within the same declarative region, and the fact that <code>bodies</code> are disallowed (by the Syntax Rules) in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>s. This does not apply to instances of generic units, whose bodies can occur in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>s. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a package declaration:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Rational{"_"}Numbers is{"\n"}
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
   type Rational is{"\n"}      record{"\n"}         Numerator   : Integer;{"\n"}         Denominator : Positive;{"\n"}      end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
   function "="(X,Y : Rational) return Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
   function "/"  (X,Y : Integer)  return Rational;  --  to construct a rational number{"\n"}
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
   function "+"  (X,Y : Rational) return Rational;{"\n"}   function "-"  (X,Y : Rational) return Rational;{"\n"}   function "{"*"}"  (X,Y : Rational) return Rational;{"\n"}   function "/"  (X,Y : Rational) return Rational;{"\n"}end Rational{"_"}Numbers;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p>There are also many examples of package declarations in the predefined language environment (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a>). <br /></p>

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>17.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
In Ada 83, a library package is allowed to have a body even if it doesn't need one. In Ada 95, a library package body is either required or forbidden &mdash; never optional. The workaround is to add aspect Elaborate{"_"}Body, or something else requiring a body, to each library package that has a body that isn't otherwise required. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>17.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
We have moved the syntax into this subclause and the next subclause from RM83-7.1, &ldquo;Package Structure&rdquo;, which we have removed.<br />

<MarginText>17.c</MarginText>
RM83 was unclear on the rules about when a package requires a body. For example, RM83-7.1(4) and RM83-7.1(8) clearly forgot about the case of an incomplete type declared in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code> but completed in the body. In addition, RM83 forgot to make this rule apply to a generic package. We have corrected these rules. Finally, since we now allow a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import for any explicit declaration, the completion rules need to take this into account as well. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>17.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00420-01"]} />
Defined &ldquo;declaration list&rdquo; to avoid ambiguity in other rules as to whether packages are included. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>17.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />

---

# 7.2. Package Bodies

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  61

# 7.2. Package Bodies

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[In contrast to the entities declared in the visible part of a package, the entities declared in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> are visible only within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> itself. As a consequence, a package with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> can be used for the construction of a group of related subprograms in which the logical operations available to clients are clearly isolated from the internal entities.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0267-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>package{"_"}body</code><a id="S0231"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>package</b> <b>body</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0201">defining_program_unit_name</a></code><br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <b>is</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code><br />   [<b>begin</b><br />        <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>]<br />    <b>end</b> [[<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code>.]<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code>.<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> appears at the end of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>, then this sequence of lexical elements shall repeat the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0201">defining_program_unit_name</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> shall be the completion of a previous <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package{"_"}declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0312">generic{"_"}package{"_"}declaration</a></code>. A library <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package{"_"}declaration</a></code> or library <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0312">generic{"_"}package{"_"}declaration</a></code> shall not have a body unless it requires a body[; the Elaborate{"_"}Body aspect can be used to require a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library{"_"}unit{"_"}declaration</a></code> to have a body (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>) if it would not otherwise require one]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The first part of the rule forbids a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> from standing alone &mdash; it has to belong to some previous <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0312">generic_package_declaration</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
A nonlibrary <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code> or nonlibrary <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0312">generic_package_declaration</a></code> that does not require a completion may have a corresponding body anyway. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>In any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> without <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s there is an implicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0170">null{"_"}statement</a></code>. For any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package{"_"}declaration</a></code> without an explicit completion, there is an implicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package{"_"}body</a></code> containing a single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0170">null_statement</a></code>. For a noninstance, nonlibrary package, this body occurs at the end of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code> of the innermost enclosing program unit or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block{"_"}statement</a></code>; if there are several such packages, the order of the implicit <code>package{"_"}bodies</code> is unspecified. [(For an instance, the implicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package{"_"}body</a></code> occurs at the place of the instantiation (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>). For a library package, the place is partially determined by the elaboration dependences (see Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/">10</a>).)] <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Thus, for example, we can refer to something happening just after the <b>begin</b> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>, and we can refer to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>, without worrying about all the optional pieces. The place of the implicit body makes a difference for tasks activated by the package. See also RM83-9.3(5).<br />

<MarginText>5.b</MarginText>
The implicit body would be illegal if explicit in the case of a library package that does not require (and therefore does not allow) a body. This is a bit strange, but not harmful. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>For the elaboration of a nongeneric <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>, its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code> is first elaborated, and its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> is then executed. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
NOTE 1   A variable declared in the body of a package is only visible within this body and, consequently, its value can only be changed within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>. In the absence of local tasks, the value of such a variable remains unchanged between calls issued from outside the package to subprograms declared in the visible part. The properties of such a variable are similar to those of a &ldquo;static&rdquo; variable of C.<br />

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
NOTE 2   The elaboration of the body of a subprogram explicitly declared in the visible part of a package is caused by the elaboration of the body of the package. Hence a call of such a subprogram by an outside program unit raises the exception Program{"_"}Error if the call takes place before the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11">3.11</a>). <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a package body (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1">7.1</a>):</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package body Rational{"_"}Numbers is{"\n"}
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
   procedure Same{"_"}Denominator (X,Y : in out Rational) is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      --  reduces X and Y to the same denominator:{"\n"}      ...{"\n"}   end Same{"_"}Denominator;{"\n"}
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
   function "="(X,Y : Rational) return Boolean is{"\n"}      U : Rational := X;{"\n"}      V : Rational := Y;{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      Same{"_"}Denominator (U,V);{"\n"}      return U.Numerator = V.Numerator;{"\n"}   end "=";{"\n"}
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
   function "/" (X,Y : Integer) return Rational is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      if Y {">"} 0 then{"\n"}         return (Numerator ={">"} X,  Denominator ={">"} Y);{"\n"}      else{"\n"}         return (Numerator ={">"} -X, Denominator ={">"} -Y);{"\n"}      end if;{"\n"}   end "/";{"\n"}
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
   function "+" (X,Y : Rational) return Rational is ... end "+";{"\n"}   function "-" (X,Y : Rational) return Rational is ... end "-";{"\n"}   function "{"*"}" (X,Y : Rational) return Rational is ... end "{"*"}";{"\n"}   function "/" (X,Y : Rational) return Rational is ... end "/";{"\n"}
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
end Rational{"_"}Numbers;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
The syntax rule for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> now uses the syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>15.b</MarginText>
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> is now required; that doesn't make any real difference, since a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> can be empty.<br />

<MarginText>15.c</MarginText>
RM83 seems to have forgotten to say that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code> can't stand alone, without a previous declaration. We state that rule here.<br />

<MarginText>15.d</MarginText>
RM83 forgot to restrict the definition of elaboration of <code>package{"_"}bodies</code> to nongeneric ones. We have corrected that omission.<br />

<MarginText>15.e</MarginText>
The rule about implicit bodies (from RM83-9.3(5)) is moved here, since it is more generally applicable. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>15.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0267-1"]} />
An optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> can be used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>. This is described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>. <br />
