<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the &ldquo;needs finalization&rdquo; rules to include class-wide types, as a future extension can include a part that needs finalization.<br />

<MarginText>27.o/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0026-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Corrected the &ldquo;needs finalization&rdquo; rules to clearly say that they ignore privacy.<br />

<MarginText>27.p/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0067-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Changed &ldquo;built in place&rdquo; to Dynamic Semantics and centralized the rules here. This eliminates the fiction that built in place is just a combination of a permission and a requirement; it clearly has noticeable semantic effects. This wording change is not intended to change the semantics of any correct Ada program. <br />

<a id="Subclause_7.6.1"></a>

## 7.6.1  Completion and Finalization

<MarginText>1_7.6.1</MarginText>
<p>[This subclause defines <i>completion</i> and <i>leaving</i> of the execution of constructs and entities. A <i>master</i> is the execution of a construct that includes finalization of local objects after it is complete (and after waiting for any local tasks &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.3">9.3</a>), but before leaving. Other constructs and entities are left immediately upon completion. ]<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>2/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<p>The execution of a construct or entity is <i>complete</i> when the end of that execution has been reached, or when a transfer of control (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1">5.1</a>) causes it to be abandoned. Completion due to reaching the end of execution, or due to the transfer of control of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code>, return statement, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0265">requeue_statement</a></code> or of the selection of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code> is <i>normal completion</i>. Completion is <i>abnormal</i> otherwise [&mdash; when control is transferred out of a construct due to abort or the raising of an exception]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Don't confuse the run-time concept of completion with the compile-time concept of completion defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#Subclause_3.11.1">3.11.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>3/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01", "AI95-00416-01", "AI12-0406-1"]} />
<p>After execution of a construct or entity is complete, it is <i>left</i>, meaning that execution continues with the next action, as defined for the execution that is taking place. Leaving an execution happens immediately after its completion, except in the case of the execution of a <i>master construct</i>: a body other than a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.2#S0231">package_body</a></code>; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>; or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code> that is not part of an enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0037">range</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0168">simple{"_"}statement</a></code> other than a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0222">simple{"_"}return{"_"}statement</a></code>. The term <i>master</i> by itself refers to the execution of a master construct. A master is finalized after it is complete, and before it is left.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">Expression</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s are masters so that objects created by subprogram calls (in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s for anonymous access-to-object types, and so on) are finalized and have their tasks awaited before the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s are left. Note that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s like the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.3#S0175">if_statement</a></code> are masters, because they are not enclosed by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0168">simple_statement</a></code>. Similarly, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> which is renamed is a master, as it is not in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0168">simple{"_"}statement</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>3.b/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01"]} />
We have to include <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>s in the contexts that do not cause masters to occur so that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s contained in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> (that is not part of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0168">simple_statement</a></code>) do not individually become masters. We certainly do not want the parameter <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> to be separate masters, as they would then be finalized before the function is called. <br />

<MarginText>3.c/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The fact that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> is a master does not change the accessibility of the return object denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>; that depends on the use of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code> is the master of any short-lived entities (such as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s used as parameters of types with task or controlled parts). <br />

<MarginText>3.d/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>master</b> &mdash; execution of a master construct<br />Note: Each object and task is associated with a master. When a master is left, associated tasks are awaited and associated objects are finalized.<br />

<MarginText>3.e/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>master construct</b> &mdash; one of certain executable constructs for which there can be objects or tasks whose lifetime ends when the construct completes<br />Note: Execution of a master construct is a master, with which objects and tasks are associated for the purposes of waiting and finalization.<br />

<MarginText>4_7.6.1</MarginText>
<p>For the <i>finalization</i> of a master, dependent tasks are first awaited, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.3">9.3</a>. Then each object whose accessibility level is the same as that of the master is finalized if the object was successfully initialized and still exists. [These actions are performed whether the master is left by reaching the last statement or via a transfer of control.] When a transfer of control causes completion of an execution, each included master is finalized in order, from innermost outward. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>As explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>, the set of objects with the same accessibility level as that of the master includes objects declared immediately within the master, objects declared in nested packages, objects created by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s (if the ultimate ancestor access type is declared in one of those places) and subcomponents of all of these things. If an object was already finalized by Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation, then it is not finalized again when the master is left.<br />

<MarginText>4.b_7.6.1</MarginText>
Note that any object whose accessibility level is deeper than that of the master would no longer exist; those objects would have been finalized by some inner master. Thus, after leaving a master, the only objects yet to be finalized are those whose accessibility level is less deep than that of the master.<br />

<MarginText>4.c_7.6.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Subcomponents of objects due to be finalized are not finalized by the finalization of the master; they are finalized by the finalization of the containing object. <br />

<MarginText>4.d_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We need to finalize subcomponents of objects even if the containing object is not going to get finalized because it was not fully initialized. But if the containing object is finalized, we don't want to require repeated finalization of the subcomponents, as might normally be implied by the recursion in finalization of a master and the recursion in finalization of an object. <br />

<MarginText>4.e_7.6.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Formally, completion and leaving refer to executions of constructs or entities. However, the standard sometimes (informally) refers to the constructs or entities whose executions are being completed. Thus, for example, &ldquo;the subprogram call or task is complete&rdquo; really means &ldquo;<i>the execution of</i> the subprogram call or task is complete&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<p>For the <i>finalization</i> of an object: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0099-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the full type of the object is an elementary type, finalization has no effect; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0099-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We say &ldquo;full type&rdquo; in this and the following bullets as privacy is ignored for the purpose of determining the finalization actions of an object; that is as expected for Dynamic Semantics rules. <br />

<MarginText>7/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0099-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the full type of the object is a tagged type, and the tag of the object identifies a controlled type, the Finalize procedure of that controlled type is called;<br /></li>
<MarginText>8/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0099-1"]} />
<li>If the full type of the object is a protected type, or if the full type of the object is a tagged type and the tag of the object identifies a protected type, the actions defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4">9.4</a> are performed;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01", "AI05-0099-1"]} />
<li>If the full type of the object is a composite type, then after performing the above actions, if any, every component of the object is finalized in an arbitrary order, except as follows: if the object has a component with an access discriminant constrained by a per-object expression, this component is finalized before any components that do not have such discriminants; for an object with several components with such a discriminant, they are finalized in the reverse of the order of their <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>s; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This allows the finalization of a component with an access discriminant to refer to other components of the enclosing object prior to their being finalized. <br />

<MarginText>9.b/4_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0099-1", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>The components discussed here are all of the components that the object actually has, not just those components that are statically identified by the type of the object. These can be different if the object has a class-wide type. <br />

<MarginText>9.1/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If the object has coextensions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>), each coextension is finalized after the object whose access discriminant designates it.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.c/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0066-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In the case of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call that is used (in its entirety) to directly initialize a part of an object, the coextensions of the result of evaluating the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call are transfered to become coextensions of the object being initialized and are not finalized until the object being initialized is ultimately finalized, even if an anonymous object is created as part of the operation. <br />

<MarginText>10_7.6.1</MarginText>
<p>Immediately before an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation reclaims the storage of an object, the object is finalized. [If an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation is never applied to an object created by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>, the object will still exist when the corresponding master completes, and it will be finalized then.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00280-01", "AI05-0051-1", "AI05-0190-1"]} />
<p>The finalization of a master performs finalization of objects created by declarations in the master in the reverse order of their creation. After the finalization of a master is complete, the objects finalized as part of its finalization cease to <i>exist</i>, as do any types and subtypes defined and created within the master. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>11.b/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>11.c/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>11.d/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>11.e_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that a deferred constant declaration does not create the constant; the full constant declaration creates it. Therefore, the order of finalization depends on where the full constant declaration occurs, not the deferred constant declaration.<br />

<MarginText>11.f_7.6.1</MarginText>
An imported object is not created by its declaration. It is neither initialized nor finalized. <br />

<MarginText>11.g_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>An implementation has to ensure that the storage for an object is not reclaimed when references to the object are still possible (unless, of course, the user explicitly requests reclamation via an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation). This implies, in general, that objects cannot be deallocated one by one as they are finalized; a subsequent finalization might reference an object that has been finalized, and that object had better be in its (well-defined) finalized state. <br />

<MarginText>11.1/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<p>Each nonderived access type <i>T</i> has an associated <i>collection</i>, which is the set of objects created by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s of <i>T</i>, or of types derived from <i>T</i>. Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation removes an object from its collection. Finalization of a collection consists of finalization of each object in the collection, in an arbitrary order. The collection of an access type is an object implicitly declared at the following place:<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.h/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The place of the implicit declaration determines when allocated objects are finalized. For multiple collections declared at the same place, we do not define the order of their implicit declarations.<br />

<MarginText>11.i/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
Finalization of allocated objects is done according to the (ultimate ancestor) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> type, not according to the storage pool in which they are allocated. Pool finalization might reclaim storage (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">Storage Management</a>&rdquo;), but has nothing (directly) to do with finalization of the pool elements.<br />

<MarginText>11.j/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
Note that finalization is done only for objects that still exist; if an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation has already gotten rid of a given pool element, that pool element will not be finalized when the master is left. <br />

<MarginText>11.k/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Note that we talk about the type of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> here. There may be access values of a (general) access type pointing at objects created by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s for some other type; these are not (necessarily) finalized at this point. <br />

<MarginText>11.2/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a named access type, the first freezing point (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.14">13.14</a>) of the type.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.l/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0190-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The freezing point of the ultimate ancestor access type is chosen because before that point, pool elements cannot be created, and after that point, access values designating (parts of) the pool elements can be created. This is also the point after which the pool object cannot have been declared. We don't want to finalize the pool elements until after anything finalizing objects that contain access values designating them. Nor do we want to finalize pool elements after finalizing the pool object itself. <br />

<MarginText>11.3/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For the type of an access parameter, the call that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.4/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<li>For the type of an access result, within the master of the call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.m/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1", "AI05-0190-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>We mean at a place within the master consistent with the execution of the call within the master. We don't say that normatively, as it is difficult to explain that when the master of the call need not be the master that immediately includes the call (such as when an anonymous result is converted to a named access type). <br />

<MarginText>11.5/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For any other anonymous access type, the first freezing point of the innermost enclosing declaration. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01"]} />
<p>The target of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> is finalized before copying in the new value, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01", "AI95-00182-01", "AI05-0066-1", "AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0021</i>{"}"} The master of an object is the master enclosing its creation whose accessibility level (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>) is equal to that of the object, except in the case of an anonymous object representing the result of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call. If such an anonymous object is part of the result of evaluating the actual parameter expression for an explicitly aliased parameter of a function call, the master of the object is the innermost master enclosing the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call, excluding the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call itself. Otherwise, the master of such an anonymous object is the innermost master enclosing the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call, which may be the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call itself. <br /></p>

<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>13.b/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13.c/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>13.d/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This effectively imports all of the special rules for the accessibility level of renames, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s, and so on, and applies them to determine where objects created in them are finalized. For instance, the master of a rename of a subprogram is that of the renamed subprogram.<br />

<MarginText>13.e/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0066-1"]} />
In <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a> we assign an accessibility level to the result of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call that is used to directly initialize a part of an object based on the object being initialized. This is important to ensure that any access discriminants denote objects that live at least as long as the object being initialized. However, if the result of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or function call is not built directly in the target object, but instead is built in an anonymous object that is then assigned to the target, the anonymous object needs to be finalized after the assignment rather than persisting until the target object is finalized (but not its coextensions). (Note than an implementation is never required to create such an anonymous object, and in some cases is required to <i>not</i> have such a separate object, but rather to build the result directly in the target.)<br />

<MarginText>13.f/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
The special case for explicitly aliased parameters of functions is needed for the same reason, as access discriminants of the returned object may designate one of these parameters. In that case, we want to lengthen the lifetime of the anonymous objects as long as the possible lifetime of the result.<br />

<MarginText>13.g/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
We don't do a similar change for other kinds of calls, because the extended lifetime of the parameters adds no value, but could constitute a storage leak. For instance, such an anonymous object created by a procedure call in the elaboration part of a package body would have to live until the end of the program, even though it could not be used after the procedure returns (other than via Unchecked{"_"}Access). <br />

<MarginText>13.h/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that the lifetime of the master given to anonymous objects in explicitly aliased parameters of functions is not necessarily as long as the lifetime of the master of the object being initialized (if the function call is used to initialize an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>, for instance). In that case, the accessibility check on explicitly aliased parameters will necessarily fail if any such anonymous objects exist. This is necessary to avoid requiring the objects to live as long as the access type or having the implementation complexity of an implicit coextension. <br />

<MarginText>13.1/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01", "AI95-00169-01", "AI05-0066-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0023</i>{"}"} In the case of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> that is a master, finalization of any (anonymous) objects occurs after completing evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and all use of the objects, prior to starting the execution of any subsequent construct.<br /></p>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>14/1_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00169-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0023</i>{"}"} It is a bounded error for a call on Finalize or Adjust that occurs as part of object finalization or assignment to propagate an exception. The possible consequences depend on what action invoked the Finalize or Adjust operation: <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>It is not a bounded error for Initialize to propagate an exception. If Initialize propagates an exception, then no further calls on Initialize are performed, and those components that have already been initialized (either explicitly or by default) are finalized in the usual way.<br />

<MarginText>14.a.1/1_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00169-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0023</i>{"}"} It also is not a bounded error for an explicit call to Finalize or Adjust to propagate an exception. We do not want implementations to have to treat explicit calls to these routines specially. <br />

<MarginText>15_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a Finalize invoked as part of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>, Program{"_"}Error is raised at that point.<br /></li>
<MarginText>16/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00193-01", "AI95-00256-01", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0024</i>{"}"} For an Adjust invoked as part of assignment operations other than those invoked as part of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>, some of the adjustments due to be performed can be performed, and then Program{"_"}Error is raised. During its propagation, finalization may be applied to objects whose Adjust failed. For an Adjust invoked as part of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>, any other adjustments due to be performed are performed, and then Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16.a/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00193-01", "AI95-00256-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0024</i>{"}"} In the case of assignments that are part of initialization, there is no need to complete all adjustments if one propagates an exception, as the object will immediately be finalized. So long as a subcomponent is not going to be finalized, it need not be adjusted, even if it is initialized as part of an enclosing composite assignment operation for which some adjustments are performed. However, there is no harm in an implementation making additional Adjust calls (as long as any additional components that are adjusted are also finalized), so we allow the implementation flexibility here. On the other hand, for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>, it is important that all adjustments be performed, even if one fails, because all controlled subcomponents are going to be finalized. Other kinds of assignment are more like initialization than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>s, so we include them as well in the permission. <br />

<MarginText>16.a.1/1_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00193-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0024</i>{"}"} Even if an Adjust invoked as part of the initialization of a controlled object propagates an exception, objects whose initialization (including any Adjust or Initialize calls) successfully completed will be finalized. The permission above only applies to objects whose Adjust failed. Objects for which Adjust was never even invoked must not be finalized. <br />

<MarginText>17_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a Finalize invoked as part of a call on an instance of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation, any other finalizations due to be performed are performed, and then Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17.a.1/1_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00179-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0104</i>{"}"} The standard does not specify if storage is recovered in this case. If storage is not recovered (and the object continues to exist), Finalize may be called on the object again (when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>'s master is finalized). <br />

<MarginText>17.1/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00169-01", "AI05-0064-1"]} />
<ul>
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i>{"{"}<i>8652/0023</i>{"}"} <br /></li>
<MarginText>17.2/1_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00169-01"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0023</i>{"}"} For a Finalize invoked due to reaching the end of the execution of a master, any other finalizations associated with the master are performed, and Program{"_"}Error is raised immediately after leaving the master.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17.a/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0064-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This rule covers both ordinary objects created by a declaration, and anonymous objects created as part of evaluating an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. All contexts that create objects that need finalization are defined to be masters. <br />

<MarginText>18/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<ul>
<li>For a Finalize invoked by the transfer of control of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.7#S0193">exit_statement</a></code>, return statement, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0265">requeue{"_"}statement</a></code>, Program{"_"}Error is raised no earlier than after the finalization of the master being finalized when the exception occurred, and no later than the point where normal execution would have continued. Any other finalizations due to be performed up to that point are performed before raising Program{"_"}Error. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, upon leaving a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code> due to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code>, the Program{"_"}Error would be raised at the point of the target statement denoted by the label, or else in some more dynamically nested place, but not so nested as to allow an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> that has visibility upon the finalized object to handle it. For example, <br />

<MarginText>18.b_7.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Main is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}    {"<"}{"<"}The{"_"}Label{">"}{">"}{"\n"}    Outer{"_"}Block{"_"}Statement : declare{"\n"}        X : Some{"_"}Controlled{"_"}Type;{"\n"}    begin{"\n"}        Inner{"_"}Block{"_"}Statement : declare{"\n"}            Y : Some{"_"}Controlled{"_"}Type;{"\n"}            Z : Some{"_"}Controlled{"_"}Type;{"\n"}        begin{"\n"}            goto The{"_"}Label;{"\n"}        exception{"\n"}            when Program{"_"}Error ={">"} ... -- Handler number 1.{"\n"}        end;{"\n"}    exception{"\n"}        when Program{"_"}Error ={">"} ... -- Handler number 2.{"\n"}    end;{"\n"}exception{"\n"}    when Program{"_"}Error ={">"} ... -- Handler number 3.{"\n"}end Main;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>18.c/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> will first cause Finalize(Z) to be called. Suppose that Finalize(Z) propagates an exception. Program{"_"}Error will be raised after leaving Inner{"_"}Block{"_"}Statement, but before leaving Main. Thus, handler number 1 cannot handle this Program{"_"}Error; it will be handled either by handler number 2 or handler number 3. If it is handled by handler number 2, then Finalize(Y) will be done before executing the handler. If it is handled by handler number 3, then Finalize(Y) and Finalize(X) will both be done before executing the handler. <br />

<MarginText>19_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a Finalize invoked by a transfer of control that is due to raising an exception, any other finalizations due to be performed for the same master are performed; Program{"_"}Error is raised immediately after leaving the master. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>19.a/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If, in the above example, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.8#S0194">goto_statement</a></code> were replaced by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.3#S0308">raise_statement</a></code>, then the Program{"_"}Error would be handled by handler number 2, and Finalize(Y) would be done before executing the handler. <br />

<MarginText>19.b_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We considered treating this case in the same way as the others, but that would render certain <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>s useless. For example, suppose the only <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> is one for <b>others</b> in the main subprogram. If some deeply nested call raises an exception, causing some Finalize operation to be called, which then raises an exception, then normal execution &ldquo;would have continued&rdquo; at the beginning of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>. Raising Program{"_"}Error at that point would cause that handler's code to be skipped. One would need two nested <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>s to be sure of catching such cases!<br />

<MarginText>19.c_7.6.1</MarginText>
On the other hand, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> for a given master should not be allowed to handle exceptions raised during finalization of that master. <br />

<MarginText>20_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a Finalize invoked by a transfer of control due to an abort or selection of a terminate alternative, the exception is ignored; any other finalizations due to be performed are performed. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This case includes an asynchronous transfer of control. <br />

<MarginText>20.b_7.6.1</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>This violates the general principle that it is always possible for a bounded error to raise Program{"_"}Error (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.5">1.1.5</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.5">Classification of Errors</a>&rdquo;). <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>20.1/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1"]} />
<p>If the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> propagates an exception, any parts of the allocated object that were successfully initialized may be finalized as part of the finalization of the innermost master enclosing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20.c/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This allows deallocating the memory for the allocated object at the innermost master, preventing a storage leak. Otherwise, the object would have to stay around until the finalization of the collection that it belongs to, which could be the entire life of the program if the associated access type is library level. <br />

<MarginText>20.2/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0111-3", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>The implementation may finalize objects created by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s for an access type whose storage pool supports subpools (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11#Subclause_13.11.4">13.11.4</a>) as if the objects were created (in an arbitrary order) at the point where the storage pool was elaborated instead of at the first freezing point of the access type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20.d/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This allows the finalization of such objects to occur later than they otherwise would, but still as part of the finalization of the same master. Accessibility rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11#Subclause_13.11.4">13.11.4</a> ensure that it is the same master (usually that of the environment task). <br />

<MarginText>20.e/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This permission is intended to allow the allocated objects to "belong" to the subpool objects and to allow those objects to be finalized at the time that the storage pool is finalized (if they are not finalized earlier). This is expected to ease implementation, as the remaining yet-to-be deallocated objects will only need to be accessible at run time from the subpool header and not also from the overall access type collection header. That is, they only need to belong to a single list, rather than two. <br />

<MarginText>21/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
NOTE 1   The rules of Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/">10</a> imply that immediately prior to partition termination, Finalize operations are applied to library-level controlled objects (including those created by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s of library-level access types, except those already finalized). This occurs after waiting for library-level tasks to terminate. <br />

<MarginText>21.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We considered defining a pragma that would apply to a controlled type that would suppress Finalize operations for library-level objects of the type upon partition termination. This would be useful for types whose finalization actions consist of simply reclaiming global heap storage, when this is already provided automatically by the environment upon program termination. <br />

<MarginText>22_7.6.1</MarginText>
NOTE 2   A constant is only constant between its initialization and finalization. Both initialization and finalization are allowed to change the value of a constant.<br />

<MarginText>23_7.6.1</MarginText>
NOTE 3   Abort is deferred during certain operations related to controlled types, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8">9.8</a>. Those rules prevent an abort from causing a controlled object to be left in an ill-defined state.<br />

<MarginText>24_7.6.1</MarginText>
NOTE 4   The Finalize procedure is called upon finalization of a controlled object, even if Finalize was called earlier, either explicitly or as part of an assignment; hence, if a controlled type is visibly controlled (implying that its Finalize primitive is directly callable), or is nonlimited (implying that assignment is allowed), its Finalize procedure is ideally designed to have no ill effect if it is applied a second time to the same object. <br />

<MarginText>24.a_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Or equivalently, a Finalize procedure should be &ldquo;idempotent&rdquo;; applying it twice to the same object should be equivalent to applying it once. <br />

<MarginText>24.b_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A user-written Finalize procedure should be idempotent since it can be called explicitly by a client (at least if the type is "visibly" controlled). Also, Finalize is used implicitly as part of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> if the type is nonlimited, and an abort is permitted to disrupt an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> between finalizing the left-hand side and assigning the new value to it (an abort is not permitted to disrupt an assignment operation between copying in the new value and adjusting it). <br />

<MarginText>24.c/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Either Initialize or Adjust, but not both, is applied to (almost) every controlled object when it is created: Initialize is done when no initial value is assigned to the object, whereas Adjust is done as part of assigning the initial value. The one exception is the object initialized by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> (both the anonymous object created for an aggregate, or an object initialized by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> that is built-in-place); Initialize is not applied to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> as a whole, nor is the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> or object adjusted.<br />

<MarginText>24.d_7.6.1</MarginText>
All of the following use the assignment operation, and thus perform value adjustment: <br />

<MarginText>24.e_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2">5.2</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.f_7.6.1</MarginText>
<li>explicit initialization of a stand-alone object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>) or of a pool element (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.g_7.6.1</MarginText>
<li>default initialization of a component of a stand-alone object or pool element (in this case, the value of each component is assigned, and therefore adjusted, but the value of the object as a whole is not adjusted);<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.h/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<li>function return, when the result is not built-in-place (adjustment of the result happens before finalization of the function);<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.i_7.6.1</MarginText>
<li>predefined operators (although the only one that matters is concatenation; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#Subclause_4.5.3">4.5.3</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.j_7.6.1</MarginText>
<li>generic formal objects of mode <b>in</b> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.4">12.4</a>); these are defined in terms of constant declarations; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.k/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
<li><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3">4.3</a>), when the result is not built-in-place (in this case, the value of each component, and the ancestor part, for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0111">extension_aggregate</a></code>, is assigned, and therefore adjusted, but the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> as a whole is not adjusted; neither is Initialize called); <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.l_7.6.1</MarginText>
The following also use the assignment operation, but adjustment never does anything interesting in these cases: <br />

<MarginText>24.m_7.6.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>By-copy parameter passing uses the assignment operation (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>), but controlled objects are always passed by reference, so the assignment operation never does anything interesting in this case. If we were to allow by-copy parameter passing for controlled objects, we would need to make sure that the actual is finalized before doing the copy back for [<b>in</b>] <b>out</b> parameters. The finalization of the parameter itself needs to happen after the copy back (if any), similar to the finalization of an anonymous function return object or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> object.<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.n_7.6.1</MarginText>
<li><b>For</b> loops use the assignment operation (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5">5.5</a>), but since the type of the loop parameter is never controlled, nothing interesting happens there, either.<br /></li>
<MarginText>24.n.1/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<li>Objects initialized by function results and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code>s that are built-in-place. In this case, the assignment operation is never executed, and no adjustment takes place. While built-in-place is always allowed, it is required for some types &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.5">7.5</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a> &mdash; and that's important since limited types have no Adjust to call. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>24.o/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00287-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>24.p_7.6.1</MarginText>
Finalization of the parts of a protected object are not done as protected actions. It is possible (in pathological cases) to create tasks during finalization that access these parts in parallel with the finalization itself. This is an erroneous use of shared variables. <br />

<MarginText>24.q_7.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>One implementation technique for finalization is to chain the controlled objects together on a per-task list. When leaving a master, the list can be walked up to a marked place. The links needed to implement the list can be declared (privately) in types Controlled and Limited{"_"}Controlled, so they will be inherited by all controlled types.<br />

<MarginText>24.r_7.6.1</MarginText>
Another implementation technique, which we refer to as the &ldquo;PC-map&rdquo; approach essentially implies inserting exception handlers at various places, and finalizing objects based on where the exception was raised.<br />

<MarginText>24.s_7.6.1</MarginText>
The PC-map approach is for the compiler/linker to create a map of code addresses; when an exception is raised, or abort occurs, the map can be consulted to see where the task was executing, and what finalization needs to be performed. This approach was given in the Ada 83 Rationale as a possible implementation strategy for exception handling &mdash; the map is consulted to determine which exception handler applies.<br />

<MarginText>24.t_7.6.1</MarginText>
If the PC-map approach is used, the implementation must take care in the case of arrays. The generated code will generally contain a loop to initialize an array. If an exception is raised part way through the array, the components that have been initialized must be finalized, and the others must not be finalized.<br />

<MarginText>24.u_7.6.1</MarginText>
It is our intention that both of these implementation methods should be possible. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>24.v_7.6.1</MarginText>
Finalization depends on the concepts of completion and leaving, and on the concept of a master. Therefore, we have moved the definitions of these concepts here, from where they used to be in Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>. These concepts also needed to be generalized somewhat. Task waiting is closely related to user-defined finalization; the rules here refer to the task-waiting rules of Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 95

<MarginText>24.v.1/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0066-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Ada 2012 </b> Changed the definition of the master of an anonymous object used to directly initialize an object, so it can be finalized immediately rather than having to hang around as long as the object. In this case, the Ada 2005 definition was inconsistent with Ada 95, and Ada 2012 changes it back. It is unlikely that many compilers implemented the rule as written in Amendment 1, so an inconsistency is unlikely to arise in practice. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>24.w/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00182-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0021</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Fixed the wording to say that anonymous objects aren't finalized until the object can't be used anymore.<br />

<MarginText>24.x/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00169-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0023</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added wording to clarify what happens when Adjust or Finalize raises an exception; some cases had been omitted.<br />

<MarginText>24.y/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00193-01", "AI95-00256-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0024</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Stated that if Adjust raises an exception during initialization, nothing further is required. This is corrected in Ada 2005 to include all kinds of assignment other than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>24.z/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00162-01", "AI95-00416-01"]} />
Revised the definition of master to include <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>s, in order to cleanly define what happens for tasks and controlled objects created as part of a subprogram call. Having done that, all of the special wording to cover those cases is eliminated (at least until the Ada comments start rolling in).<br />

<MarginText>24.aa/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00280-01"]} />
We define <i>finalization of the collection</i> here, so as to be able to conveniently refer to it in other rules (especially in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">4.8</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8">Allocators</a>&rdquo;).<br />

<MarginText>24.bb/2_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00416-01"]} />
Clarified that a coextension is finalized at the same time as the outer object. (This was intended for Ada 95, but since the concept did not have a name, it was overlooked.) <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2005

<MarginText>24.cc/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0051-1", "AI05-0190-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Better defined when objects allocated from anonymous access types are finalized. This could be inconsistent if objects are finalized in a different order than in an Ada 2005 implementation and that order caused different program behavior; however programs that depend on the order of finalization within a single master are already fragile and hopefully are rare. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>24.dd/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0064-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Removed a redundant rule, which is now covered by the additional places where masters are defined.<br />

<MarginText>24.ee/4_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0099-1", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified the finalization rules so that there is no doubt that privacy is ignored, and to ensure that objects of class-wide interface types are finalized based on their specific concrete type.<br />

<MarginText>24.ff/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0107-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Allowed premature finalization of parts of failed <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s. This could be an inconsistency, but the previous behavior is still allowed and there is no requirement that implementations take advantage of the permission.<br />

<MarginText>24.gg/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0111-3"]} />
Added a permission to finalize an object allocated from a subpool later than usual.<br />

<MarginText>24.hh/3_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
Added text to specially define the master of anonymous objects which are passed as explicitly aliased parameters (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>) of functions. The model for these parameters is explained in detail in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#Subclause_6.4.1">6.4.1</a>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>24.ii/5_7.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0406-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined the term &ldquo;master construct&rdquo;, so as to put static accessibility rules on a firmer basis, including ensuring that those rules apply inside of generic bodies. <br />

# 7. Packages

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.mdx

sidebar_position:  59

# 7. Packages

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[Packages are program units that allow the specification of groups of logically related entities. Typically, a package contains the declaration of a type (often a private type or private extension) along with the declarations of primitive subprograms of the type, which can be called from outside the package, while their inner workings remain hidden from outside users. ]<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>package</b> &mdash; program unit that defines the interface to a group of logically related entities, along with their implementation<br />Note: Typically, a package contains the declaration of a type (often a private type or private extension) along with the declarations of primitive subprograms of the type, which can be called from outside the package, while their inner workings remain hidden from outside users.<br />

---

# 8.1. Declarative Region

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  67

# 8.1. Declarative Region

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>For each of the following constructs, there is a portion of the program text called its <i>declarative region</i>, [within which nested declarations can occur]: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>any declaration, other than that of an enumeration type, that is not a completion [of a previous declaration];<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0094-1"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0061-1"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0119">iterated_component_association</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0308-1"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0255-1", "AI12-0308-1"]} />
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0153">quantified_expression</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>2.5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0236-1"]} />
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0255-1", "AI12-0308-1"]} />
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
<MarginText>4.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">extended_return_statement</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The declarative region includes the text of the construct together with additional text determined [(recursively)], as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If a declaration is included, so is its completion, if any.<br /></li>
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<li>If the declaration of a library unit [(including Standard &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">10.1.1</a>)] is included, so are the declarations of any child units [(and their completions, by the previous rule)]. The child declarations occur after the declaration.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<li>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0297">body_stub</a></code> is included, so is the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0302">subunit</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<li>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code> is included, then so is a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code>, if any. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is so that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>s can be directly visible in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>The declarative region of a declaration is also called the <i>declarative region</i> of any view or entity declared by the declaration. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The constructs that have declarative regions are the constructs that can have declarations nested inside them. Nested declarations are declared in that declarative region. The one exception is for enumeration literals; although they are nested inside an enumeration type declaration, they behave as if they were declared at the same level as the type. <br />

<MarginText>12.b</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>A declarative region does not include <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>12.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A declarative region does not include <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>A declaration occurs <i>immediately within</i> a declarative region if this region is the innermost declarative region that encloses the declaration (the <i>immediately enclosing</i> declarative region), not counting the declarative region (if any) associated with the declaration itself. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Don't confuse the declarative region of a declaration with the declarative region in which it immediately occurs. <br />

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>[ A declaration is <i>local</i> to a declarative region if the declaration occurs immediately within the declarative region.] [An entity is <i>local</i> to a declarative region if the entity is declared by a declaration that is local to the declarative region.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>"Occurs immediately within" and "local to" are synonyms (when referring to declarations).<br />

<MarginText>14.b</MarginText>
Thus, &ldquo;local to&rdquo; applies to both declarations and entities, whereas &ldquo;occurs immediately within&rdquo; only applies to declarations. We use this term only informally; for cases where precision is required, we use the term "occurs immediately within", since it is less likely to cause confusion. <br />

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p>A declaration is <i>global</i> to a declarative region if the declaration occurs immediately within another declarative region that encloses the declarative region. An entity is <i>global</i> to a declarative region if the entity is declared by a declaration that is global to the declarative region. <br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
NOTE 1   The children of a parent library unit are inside the parent's declarative region, even though they do not occur inside the parent's declaration or body. This implies that one can use (for example) "P.Q" to refer to a child of P whose defining name is Q, and that after "<b>use</b> P;" Q can refer (directly) to that child.<br />

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
NOTE 2   As explained above and in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">10.1.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">Compilation Units - Library Units</a>&rdquo;, all library units are descendants of Standard, and so are contained in the declarative region of Standard. They are <i>not</i> inside the declaration or body of Standard, but they <i>are</i> inside its declarative region.<br />

<MarginText>18/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 3   For a declarative region that comes in multiple parts, the text of the declarative region does not include any of the text that appears between the parts. Thus, when a portion of a declarative region is said to extend from one place to another in the declarative region, the portion does not contain any of the text that appears between the parts of the declarative region. <br />

<MarginText>18.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>It is necessary for the things that have a declarative region to include anything that contains declarations (except for enumeration type declarations). This includes any declaration that has a profile (that is, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0242">subprogram_renaming_declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6#S0335">formal_subprogram_declaration</a></code>, access-to-subprogram <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>), anything that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0059">discriminant_part</a></code> (that is, various kinds of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>), anything that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0068">component_list</a></code> (that is, record <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code> and record extension <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>), and finally the declarations of task and protected units and packages. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>18.b</MarginText>
It was necessary to extend Ada 83's definition of declarative region to take the following Ada 95 features into account: <br />

<MarginText>18.c</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Child library units.<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.d</MarginText>
<li>Derived types/type extensions &mdash; we need a declarative region for inherited components and also for new components.<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.e</MarginText>
<li>All the kinds of types that allow discriminants.<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.f</MarginText>
<li>Protected units.<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.g</MarginText>
<li>Entries that have bodies instead of accept statements.<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.h</MarginText>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0306">choice_parameter_specification</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.i</MarginText>
<li>The formal parameters of access-to-subprogram types.<br /></li>
<MarginText>18.j</MarginText>
<li>Renamings-as-body. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.k</MarginText>
Discriminated and access-to-subprogram type declarations need a declarative region. Enumeration type declarations cannot have one, because you don't have to say "Color.Red" to refer to the literal Red of Color. For other type declarations, it doesn't really matter whether or not there is an associated declarative region, so for simplicity, we give one to all types except enumeration types.<br />

<MarginText>18.l</MarginText>
We now say that an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> has its own declarative region, rather than being part of the declarative region of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>, so that declarative regions are properly nested regions of text, so that it makes sense to talk about "inner declarative regions", and "...extends to the end of a declarative region". Inside an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of one of the parameters denotes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter_specification</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, not that of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is nested within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code>, these <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter_specification</a></code>s can hide declarations of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code>. The semantics of such cases was unclear in RM83. <br />

<MarginText>18.m</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Unfortunately, we have the same problem for the entry name itself &mdash; it should denote the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, but <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s are not declarations. They should be, and they should hide the entry from all visibility within themselves. <br />

<MarginText>18.n</MarginText>
Note that we can't generalize this to <code>entry{"_"}bodies</code>, or other bodies, because the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a body is not supposed to contain (explicit) homographs of things in the declaration. It works for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s only because an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> does not have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>18.o</MarginText>
To avoid confusion, we use the term &ldquo;local to&rdquo; only informally in Ada 95. Even RM83 used the term incorrectly (see, for example, RM83-12.3(13)).<br />

<MarginText>18.p</MarginText>
In Ada 83, (root) library units were inside Standard; it was not clear whether the declaration or body of Standard was meant. In Ada 95, they are children of Standard, and so occur immediately within Standard's declarative region, but not within either the declaration or the body. (See RM83-8.6(2) and RM83-10.1.1(5).) <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>18.q/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#S0225">Extended_return_statement</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a>) is added to the list of constructs that have a declarative region. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>18.r/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0094-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is added to the list of constructs that have a declarative region. This allows parameter names declared in anonymous access type subprogram types to be the same as other names declared outside. For instance: <br />

<MarginText>18.s/4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Foo is record{"\n"}   A : Natural;{"\n"}   B : access procedure (A : Boolean);{"\n"}end record;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>18.t/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
This is now legal, as one would expect; it was illegal in previous versions of Ada as the parameter A and the component A were homographs in the same declarative region (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3">8.3</a>). Note that some implementations already allow this common sense interpretation, so this extension might in fact already be used in existing code. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>18.u/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0061-1", "AI12-0236-1", "AI12-0308-1"]} />
Added <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0119">iterated_component_association</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0131">iterated_element_association</a></code>, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0156">declare_expression</a></code> to the rapidly expanding list of constructs that have a declarative region. <br />

# 8.2. Scope of Declarations

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  68

# 8.2. Scope of Declarations

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[For each declaration, the language rules define a certain portion of the program text called the <i>scope</i> of the declaration. The scope of a declaration is also called the scope of any view or entity declared by the declaration. Within the scope of an entity, and only there, there are places where it is legal to refer to the declared entity. These places are defined by the rules of visibility and overloading.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The <i>immediate scope</i> of a declaration is a portion of the declarative region immediately enclosing the declaration. The immediate scope starts at the beginning of the declaration, except in the case of an overloadable declaration, in which case the immediate scope starts just after the place where the profile of the callable entity is determined (which is at the end of the <code>{"_"}specification</code> for the callable entity, or at the end of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code> if an instance). The immediate scope extends to the end of the declarative region, with the following exceptions: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The reason for making overloadable declarations with profiles special is to simplify compilation: until the compiler has determined the profile, it doesn't know which other declarations are homographs of this one, so it doesn't know which ones this one should hide. Without this rule, two passes over the <code>{"_"}specification</code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic_instantiation</a></code> would be required to resolve names that denote things with the same name as this one. <br />

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The immediate scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> includes only its semantic dependents. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>3.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/">10</a> defines only a partial ordering of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s. Therefore, it is a good idea to restrict the immediate scope (and the scope, defined below) to semantic dependents.<br />

<MarginText>3.b</MarginText>
Consider also examples like this: <br />

<MarginText>3.c</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package P is end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>3.d</MarginText>
package P.Q is{"\n"}    I : Integer := 0;{"\n"}end P.Q;{"\n"}
<MarginText>3.e/1</MarginText>
with P;{"\n"}package R is{"\n"}    package X renames P;{"\n"}    J : Integer := X.Q.I; -- Illegal!{"\n"}end R;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.f</MarginText>
The scope of P.Q does not contain R. Hence, neither P.Q nor X.Q are visible within R. However, the name R.X.Q would be visible in some other library unit where both R and P.Q are visible (assuming R were made legal by removing the offending declaration). <br />

<MarginText>3.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule applies to limited views as well as &ldquo;normal&rdquo; library items. In that case, the semantic dependents are the units that have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code> for the limited view. <br />

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The immediate scope of a declaration in the private part of a library unit does not include the visible part of any public descendant of that library unit. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In other words, a declaration in the private part can be visible within the visible part, private part and body of a private child unit. On the other hand, such a declaration can be visible within only the private part and body of a public child unit. <br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The purpose of this rule is to prevent children from giving private information to clients. <br />

<MarginText>4.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For a public child subprogram, this means that the parent's private part is not visible in the profile of the declaration and of the body. This is true even for <code>subprogram{"_"}bodies</code> that are not completions. For a public child generic unit, it means that the parent's private part is not visible in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code>, as well as in the first list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s (for a generic package), or the (syntactic) profile (for a generic subprogram). <br />

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>[The <i>visible part</i> of (a view of) an entity is a portion of the text of its declaration containing declarations that are visible from outside.] The <i>private part</i> of (a view of) an entity that has a visible part contains all declarations within the declaration of (the view of) the entity, except those in the visible part; [these are not visible from outside. Visible and private parts are defined only for these kinds of entities: callable entities, other program units, and composite types.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The visible part of a view of a callable entity is its profile.<br /></li>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<li>The visible part of a composite type other than a task or protected type consists of the declarations of all components declared [(explicitly or implicitly)] within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<li>The visible part of a generic unit includes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code>. For a generic package, it also includes the first list of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0088">basic_declarative_item</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>. For a generic subprogram, it also includes the profile. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Although there is no way to reference anything but the formals from outside a generic unit, they are still in the visible part in the sense that the corresponding declarations in an instance can be referenced (at least in some cases). In other words, these declarations have an effect on the outside world. The visible part of a generic unit needs to be defined this way in order to properly support the rule that makes a parent's private part invisible within a public child's visible part. <br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The visible part of an instance of a generic unit is as defined for packages and subprograms; it is not defined in terms of the visible part of a generic unit. <br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>[The visible part of a package, task unit, or protected unit consists of declarations in the program unit's declaration other than those following the reserved word <b>private</b>, if any; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1">7.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7">12.7</a> for packages, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1">9.1</a> for task units, and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4">9.4</a> for protected units.] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>The scope of a declaration always contains the immediate scope of the declaration. In addition, for a given declaration that occurs immediately within the visible part of an outer declaration, or is a public child of an outer declaration, the scope of the given declaration extends to the end of the scope of the outer declaration, except that the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> includes only its semantic dependents. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note the recursion. If a declaration appears in the visible part of a library unit, its scope extends to the end of the scope of the library unit, but since that only includes dependents of the declaration of the library unit, the scope of the inner declaration also only includes those dependents. If X renames library package P, which has a child Q, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> mentioning P.Q is necessary to be able to refer to X.Q, even if P.Q is visible at the place where X is declared. <br />

<MarginText>10.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00408-01", "AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>The scope of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> is identical to the scope of a declaration that would occur at the point of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>. The scope of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is identical to the scope of the associated declaration.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>The immediate scope of a declaration is also the immediate scope of the entity or view declared by the declaration. Similarly, the scope of a declaration is also the scope of the entity or view declared by the declaration. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The rule for immediate scope implies the following: <br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
<ul>
