<li>If the declaration is that of a library unit, then the immediate scope includes the declarative region of the declaration itself, but not other places, unless they are within the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> that mentions the library unit.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.c</MarginText>
<li>It is necessary to attach the semantics of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>s to [immediate] scopes (as opposed to visibility), in order for various rules to work properly. A library unit should hide a homographic implicit declaration that appears in its parent, but only within the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> that mentions the library unit. Otherwise, we would violate the "legality determinable via semantic dependences" rule of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/">10</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/">Program Structure and Compilation Issues</a>&rdquo;. The declaration of a library unit should be allowed to be a homograph of an explicit declaration in its parent's body, so long as that body does not mention the library unit in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.d</MarginText>
<li>This means that one cannot denote the declaration of the library unit, but one might still be able to denote the library unit via another view.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.e</MarginText>
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> does not make the declaration of a library unit visible; the lack of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> prevents it from being visible. Even if a library unit is mentioned in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>, its declaration can still be hidden.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.f</MarginText>
<li>The completion of the declaration of a library unit (assuming that's also a declaration) is not visible, neither directly nor by selection, outside that completion.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.g</MarginText>
<li>The immediate scope of a declaration immediately within the body of a library unit does not include any child of that library unit.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.h</MarginText>
<li>This is needed to prevent children from looking inside their parent's body. The children are in the declarative region of the parent, and they might be after the parent's body. Therefore, the scope of a declaration that occurs immediately within the body might include some children. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0003-1"]} />
<p>The immediate scope of a pragma that is not used as a configuration pragma is defined to be the region extending from immediately after the pragma to the end of the declarative region immediately enclosing the pragma. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
NOTE   There are notations for denoting visible declarations that are not directly visible. For example, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code>s are in the visible part of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> so that they can be used in named-notation calls appearing outside the called subprogram. For another example, declarations of the visible part of a package can be denoted by expanded names appearing outside the package, and can be made directly visible by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>13.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There are some obscure cases involving generics in which there is no such notation. See Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/">12</a>. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>13.b</MarginText>
The fact that the immediate scope of an overloadable declaration does not include its profile is new to Ada 95. It replaces RM83-8.3(16), which said that within a subprogram specification and within the formal part of an entry declaration or accept statement, all declarations with the same designator as the subprogram or entry were hidden from all visibility. The RM83-8.3(16) rule seemed to be overkill, and created both implementation difficulties and unnecessary semantic complexity. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>13.c</MarginText>
We no longer need to talk about the scope of notations, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>s.<br />

<MarginText>13.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
The notion of "visible part" has been extended in Ada 95. The syntax of task and protected units now allows private parts, thus requiring us to be able to talk about the visible part as well. It was necessary to extend the concept to subprograms and to generic units, in order for the visibility rules related to child library units to work properly. It was necessary to define the concept separately for generic formal packages, since their visible part is slightly different from that of a normal package. Extending the concept to composite types made the definition of scope slightly simpler. We define visible part for some things elsewhere, since it makes a big difference to the user for those things. For composite types and subprograms, however, the concept is used only in arcane visibility rules, so we localize it to this subclause.<br />

<MarginText>13.e</MarginText>
In Ada 83, the semantics of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>s was described in terms of visibility. It is now described in terms of [immediate] scope.<br />

<MarginText>13.f</MarginText>
We have clarified that the following is illegal (where Q and R are library units): <br />

<MarginText>13.g</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Q is{"\n"}    I : Integer := 0;{"\n"}end Q;{"\n"}
<MarginText>13.h</MarginText>
package R is{"\n"}    package X renames Standard;{"\n"}    X.Q.I := 17; -- Illegal!{"\n"}end R;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13.i</MarginText>
even though Q is declared in the declarative region of Standard, because R does not mention Q in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>13.j/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00408-01"]} />
The scope of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> is defined so that it can be used to define the visibility of such a clause, so <i>that</i> can be used by the stream attribute availability rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>13.k/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
The scope of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is defined for similar reasons that it was defined for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>s. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>13.l/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0003-1"]} />
The immediate scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> is defined as it is used in other rules in the Reference Manual. <br />

---

# 8.3. Visibility

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  69

# 8.3. Visibility

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[ The <i>visibility rules</i>, given below, determine which declarations are visible and directly visible at each place within a program. The visibility rules apply to both explicit and implicit declarations.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>A declaration is defined to be <i>directly visible</i> at places where a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> consisting of only an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> is sufficient to denote the declaration; that is, no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code> notation or special context (such as preceding ={">"} in a named association) is necessary to denote the declaration. A declaration is defined to be <i>visible</i> wherever it is directly visible, as well as at other places where some <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> (such as a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>) can denote the declaration.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> is used to indicate contexts where direct visibility is required. The syntactic category <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> is used to indicate contexts where visibility, but not direct visibility, is required.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>There are two kinds of direct visibility: <i>immediate visibility</i> and <i>use-visibility</i>. A declaration is immediately visible at a place if it is directly visible because the place is within its immediate scope. A declaration is use-visible if it is directly visible because of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4">8.4</a>). Both conditions can apply.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>A declaration can be <i>hidden</i>, either from direct visibility, or from all visibility, within certain parts of its scope. Where <i>hidden from all visibility</i>, it is not visible at all (neither using a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> nor a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>). Where <i>hidden from direct visibility</i>, only direct visibility is lost; visibility using a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> is still possible.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>[ Two or more declarations are <i>overloaded</i> if they all have the same defining name and there is a place where they are all directly visible.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> can have more than one possible interpretation even if it denotes a nonoverloadable entity. For example, if there are two functions F that return records, both containing a component called C, then the name F.C has two possible interpretations, even though component declarations are not overloadable. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The declarations of callable entities [(including enumeration literals)] are <i>overloadable</i>[, meaning that overloading is allowed for them]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0310">generic_declaration</a></code> is not overloadable within its own <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code>. This follows from the rules about when a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denotes a current instance. See AI83-00286. This implies that within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code>, outer declarations with the same defining name are hidden from direct visibility. It also implies that if a generic formal parameter has the same defining name as the generic itself, the formal parameter hides the generic from direct visibility. <br />

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>Two declarations are <i>homographs</i> if they have the same defining name, and, if both are overloadable, their profiles are type conformant. [An inner declaration hides any outer homograph from direct visibility.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>overriding operation</b> &mdash; operation that replaces an inherited primitive operation<br />Note: Operations can be marked explicitly as overriding or not overriding.<br />

<MarginText>9/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00044-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0025</i>{"}"} [Two homographs are not generally allowed immediately within the same declarative region unless one <i>overrides</i> the other (see Legality Rules below).] The only declarations that are <i>overridable</i> are the implicit declarations for predefined operators and inherited primitive subprograms. A declaration overrides another homograph that occurs immediately within the same declarative region in the following cases: <br /></p>

<MarginText>10/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00044-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0025</i>{"}"} A declaration that is not overridable overrides one that is overridable, [regardless of which declaration occurs first]; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00044-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0025</i>{"}"} And regardless of whether the nonoverridable declaration is overloadable or not. For example, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0172">statement_identifier</a></code>s are covered by this rule.<br />

<MarginText>10.b</MarginText>
The &ldquo;regardless of which declaration occurs first&rdquo; is there because the explicit declaration could be a primitive subprogram of a partial view, and then the full view might inherit a homograph. We are saying that the explicit one wins (within its scope), even though the implicit one comes later.<br />

<MarginText>10.c</MarginText>
If the overriding declaration is also a subprogram, then it is a primitive subprogram.<br />

<MarginText>10.d</MarginText>
As explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">7.3.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">Private Operations</a>&rdquo;, some inherited primitive subprograms are never declared. Such subprograms cannot be overridden, although they can be reached by dispatching calls in the case of a tagged type. <br />

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The implicit declaration of an inherited operator overrides that of a predefined operator; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In a previous version of Ada 9X, we tried to avoid the notion of predefined operators, and say that they were inherited from some magical root type. However, this seemed like too much mechanism. Therefore, a type can have a predefined "+" as well as an inherited "+". The above rule says the inherited one wins.<br />

<MarginText>11.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
The &ldquo;regardless of which declaration occurs first&rdquo; applies here as well, in the case where <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code> in the visible part of a public library unit derives from a private type declared in the parent unit, and the full view of the parent type has additional predefined operators, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">7.3.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">Private Operations</a>&rdquo;. Those predefined operators can be overridden by inherited subprograms implicitly declared earlier. <br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>An implicit declaration of an inherited subprogram overrides a previous implicit declaration of an inherited subprogram.<br /></li>
<MarginText>12.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<li>If two or more homographs are implicitly declared at the same place:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>If at least one is a subprogram that is neither a null procedure nor an abstract subprogram, and does not require overriding (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.3">3.9.3</a>), then they override those that are null procedures, abstract subprograms, or require overriding. If more than one such homograph remains that is not thus overridden, then they are all hidden from all visibility.<br /></li>
<MarginText>12.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01", "AI12-0183-1"]} />
<li>Otherwise (all are null procedures, abstract subprograms, or require overriding), then any null procedure overrides all abstract subprograms and all subprograms that require overriding; if more than one such homograph remains that is not thus overridden, then if the profiles of the remaining homographs are all fully conformant with one another, one is chosen arbitrarily; if not, they are all hidden from all visibility. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In the case where the implementation arbitrarily chooses one overrider from among a group of inherited subprograms, users should not be able to determine which member was chosen, as the set of inherited subprograms which are chosen from must be fully conformant. This rule is needed in order to allow<br />

<MarginText>12.b/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Outer is{"\n"}   package P1 is{"\n"}      type Ifc1 is interface;{"\n"}      procedure Null{"_"}Procedure (X : Ifc1) is null;{"\n"}      procedure Abstract{"_"}Subp  (X : Ifc1) is abstract;{"\n"}   end P1;{"\n"}
<MarginText>12.c/2</MarginText>
   package P2 is{"\n"}      type Ifc2 is interface;{"\n"}      procedure Null{"_"}Procedure (X : Ifc2) is null;{"\n"}      procedure Abstract{"_"}Subp  (X : Ifc2) is abstract;{"\n"}   end P2;{"\n"}
<MarginText>12.d/2</MarginText>
   type T is abstract new P1.Ifc1 and P2.Ifc2 with null record;{"\n"}end Outer;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12.e/2</MarginText>
without requiring that T explicitly override any of its inherited operations.<br />

<MarginText>12.f/2</MarginText>
Full conformance is required here, as we cannot allow the parameter names to differ. If they did differ, the routine which was selected for overriding could be determined by using named parameter notation in a call.<br />

<MarginText>12.g/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
When the subprograms do not conform, we chose not to adopt the &ldquo;use clause&rdquo; rule which would make them all visible resulting in likely ambiguity. If we had used such a rule, any successful calls would be confusing; and the fact that there are no Beaujolais-like effects to worry about means we can consider other rules. The hidden-from-all-visibility homographs are still inherited by further derivations, which avoids order-of-declaration dependencies and other anomalies.<br />

<MarginText>12.h/2</MarginText>
We have to be careful to not include arbitrary selection if the routines have real bodies. (This can happen in generics, see the example in the incompatibilities section below.) We don't want the ability to successfully call routines where the body executed depends on the compiler or a phase of the moon.<br />

<MarginText>12.i/2</MarginText>
Note that if the type is concrete, abstract subprograms are inherited as subprograms that require overriding. We include functions that require overriding as well; these don't have real bodies, so they can use the more liberal rules. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>[For an implicit declaration of a primitive subprogram in a generic unit, there is a copy of this declaration in an instance.] However, a whole new set of primitive subprograms is implicitly declared for each type declared within the visible part of the instance. These new declarations occur immediately after the type declaration, and override the copied ones. [The copied ones can be called only from within the instance; the new ones can be called only from outside the instance, although for tagged types, the body of a new one can be executed by a call to an old one.] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In addition, this is also stated redundantly (again), and is repeated, in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">Generic Instantiation</a>&rdquo;. The rationale for the rule is explained there. <br />

<MarginText>13.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0042-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>The implicit subprograms declared when an operation of a progenitor is implemented by an entry or subprogram also override the appropriate implicitly declared inherited operations of the progenitor. <br />

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>A declaration is visible within its scope, except where hidden from all visibility, as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>An overridden declaration is hidden from all visibility within the scope of the overriding declaration. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We have to talk about the scope of the overriding declaration, not its visibility, because it hides even when it is itself hidden.<br />

<MarginText>15.b</MarginText>
Note that the scope of an explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> does not start until after its profile. <br />

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A declaration is hidden from all visibility until the end of the declaration, except: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For a record type or record extension, the declaration is hidden from all visibility only until the reserved word <b>record</b>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>18/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01", "AI05-0177-1"]} />
<li>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0312">generic{"_"}package{"_"}declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram{"_"}body</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code>, the declaration is hidden from all visibility only until the reserved word <b>is</b> of the declaration; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We're talking about the <b>is</b> of the construct itself, here, not some random <b>is</b> that might appear in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>18.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>For a task declaration or protected declaration, the declaration is hidden from all visibility only until the reserved word <b>with</b> of the declaration if there is one, or the reserved word <b>is</b> of the declaration if there is no <b>with</b>.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.b/2</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>If there is neither a <b>with</b> nor <b>is</b>, then the exception does not apply and the name is hidden from all visibility until the end of the declaration. This oddity was inherited from Ada 95. <br />

<MarginText>18.c/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We need the &ldquo;<b>with</b> or <b>is</b>&rdquo; rule so that the visibility within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0078">interface_list</a></code> does not vary by construct. That would make it harder to complete private extensions and would complicate implementations. <br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the completion of a declaration is a declaration, then within the scope of the completion, the first declaration is hidden from all visibility. Similarly, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant{"_"}specification</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code> is hidden within the scope of a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0062">discriminant{"_"}specification</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter{"_"}specification</a></code> of a corresponding completion, or of a corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>19.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule means, for example, that within the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> that completes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#S0232">private_type_declaration</a></code>, the name of the type will denote the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>, and therefore the full view of the type. On the other hand, if the completion is not a declaration, then it doesn't hide anything, and you can't denote it. <br />

<MarginText>20/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI95-00412-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The declaration of a library unit (including a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0289">library_unit_renaming_declaration</a></code>) is hidden from all visibility at places outside its declarative region that are not within the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0296">nonlimited_with_clause</a></code> that mentions it. The limited view of a library package is hidden from all visibility at places that are not within the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0295">limited_with_clause</a></code> that mentions it; in addition, the limited view is hidden from all visibility within the declarative region of the package, as well as within the scope of any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0296">nonlimited_with_clause</a></code> that mentions the package. Where the declaration of the limited view of a package is visible, any name that denotes the package denotes the limited view, including those provided by a package renaming.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This is the rule that prevents <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>s from being transitive; the [immediate] scope includes indirect semantic dependents. This rule also prevents the limited view of a package from being visible in the same place as the full view of the package, which prevents various ripple effects. <br />

<MarginText>20.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI95-00412-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>[For each declaration or renaming of a generic unit as a child of some parent generic package, there is a corresponding declaration nested immediately within each instance of the parent.] Such a nested declaration is hidden from all visibility except at places that are within the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> that mentions the child.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p>A declaration with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0203">defining_operator_symbol</a></code> is immediately visible [(and hence directly visible)] within its immediate scope except where hidden from direct visibility, as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A declaration is hidden from direct visibility within the immediate scope of a homograph of the declaration, if the homograph occurs within an inner declarative region;<br /></li>
<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<li>A declaration is also hidden from direct visibility where hidden from all visibility. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>23.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00195-01", "AI95-00408-01", "AI05-0183-1"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is <i>visible</i> everywhere within its scope.<br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> shall resolve to denote a directly visible declaration whose defining name is the same as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> shall resolve to denote a visible declaration whose defining name is the same as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>"The same as" has the obvious meaning here, so for +, the possible interpretations are declarations whose defining name is "+" (an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>). <br />

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p>These rules on visibility and direct visibility do not apply in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0291">parent_unit_name</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> that appears at the place of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0286">compilation_unit</a></code>. For those contexts, see the rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.6">10.1.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.6">Environment-Level Visibility Rules</a>&rdquo;. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Direct visibility is irrelevant for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s. In terms of overload resolution <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s are similar to other literals, like <b>null</b> &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2">4.2</a>. For <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s, there is no need to worry about hiding, since there is no way to declare homographs. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>26/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00044-01", "AI95-00150-01", "AI95-00377-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0025</i>{"}"} {"{"}<i>8652/0026</i>{"}"} A nonoverridable declaration is illegal if there is a homograph occurring immediately within the same declarative region that is visible at the place of the declaration, and is not hidden from all visibility by the nonoverridable declaration. In addition, a type extension is illegal if somewhere within its immediate scope it has two visible components with the same name. Similarly, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code> for a compilation unit is illegal if it mentions (in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>) some library unit, and there is a homograph of the library unit that is visible at the place of the compilation unit, and the homograph and the mentioned library unit are both declared immediately within the same declarative region. These rules also apply to dispatching operations declared in the visible part of an instance of a generic unit. However, they do not apply to other overloadable declarations in an instance[; such declarations may have type conformant profiles in the instance, so long as the corresponding declarations in the generic were not type conformant]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Normally, these rules just mean you can't explicitly declare two homographs immediately within the same declarative region. The wording is designed to handle the following special cases: <br />

<MarginText>26.b</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the second declaration completes the first one, the second declaration is legal.<br /></li>
<MarginText>26.c</MarginText>
<li>If the body of a library unit contains an explicit homograph of a child of that same library unit, this is illegal only if the body mentions the child in its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>, or if some subunit mentions the child. Here's an example: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>26.d</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package P is{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.e</MarginText>
package P.Q is{"\n"}end P.Q;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.f</MarginText>
package body P is{"\n"}    Q : Integer; -- OK; we cannot see package P.Q here.{"\n"}    procedure Sub is separate;{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.g</MarginText>
with P.Q;{"\n"}separate(P){"\n"}procedure Sub is -- Illegal.{"\n"}begin{"\n"}    null;{"\n"}end Sub;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>26.h</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If package body P said "<b>with</b> P.Q;", then it would be illegal to declare the homograph Q: Integer. But it does not, so the body of P is OK. However, the subunit would be able to see both P.Q's, and is therefore illegal.<br /></li>
<MarginText>26.i</MarginText>
<li>A previous version of Ada 9X allowed the subunit, and said that references to P.Q would tend to be ambiguous. However, that was a bad idea, because it requires overload resolution to resolve references to directly visible nonoverloadable homographs, which is something compilers have never before been required to do.<br /></li>
<MarginText>26.i.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00150-01", "AI95-00157-01"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0026</i>{"}"} {"{"}<i>8652/0102</i>{"}"} If a type extension contains a component with the same name as a component in an ancestor type, there must be no place where both components are visible. For instance: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>26.i.2/1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package A is{"\n"}   type T is tagged private;{"\n"}   package B is{"\n"}      type NT is new T with record{"\n"}         I: Integer; -- Illegal because T.I is visible in the body.{"\n"}      end record; -- T.I is not visible here.{"\n"}   end B;{"\n"}private{"\n"}   type T is tagged record{"\n"}      I: Integer; -- Illegal because T.I is visible in the body.{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}end A;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.3/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
package body A is{"\n"}   package body B is{"\n"}      -- T.I becomes visible here.{"\n"}   end B;{"\n"}end A;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.4/1</MarginText>
package A.C is{"\n"}   type NT2 is new A.T with record{"\n"}      I: Integer; -- Illegal because T.I is visible in the private part.{"\n"}   end record; -- T.I is not visible here.{"\n"}private{"\n"}    -- T.I is visible here.{"\n"}end A.C;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.5/1</MarginText>
with A;{"\n"}package D is{"\n"}   type NT3 is new A.T with record{"\n"}      I: Integer; -- Legal because T.I is never visible in this package.{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}end D;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.6/1</MarginText>
with D;{"\n"}package A.E is{"\n"}   type NT4 is new D.NT3 with null record;{"\n"}   X : NT4;{"\n"}   I1 : Integer := X.I;        -- D.NT3.I{"\n"}   I2 : Integer := D.NT3(X).I; -- D.NT3.I{"\n"}   I3 : Integer := A.T(X).I;   -- A.T.I{"\n"}end A.E;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>26.i.7/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00157-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0102</i>{"}"} D.NT3 can have a component I because the component I of the parent type is never visible. The parent component exists, of course, but is never declared for the type D.NT3. In the child package A.E, the component I of A.T is visible, but that does not change the fact that the A.T.I component was never declared for type D.NT3. Thus, A.E.NT4 does not (visibly) inherit the component I from A.T, while it does inherit the component I from D.NT3. Of course, both components exist, and can be accessed by a type conversion as shown above. This behavior stems from the fact that every characteristic of a type (including components) must be declared somewhere in the innermost declarative region containing the type &mdash; if the characteristic is never visible in that declarative region, it is never declared. Therefore, such characteristics do not suddenly become available even if they are in fact visible in some other scope. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">7.3.1</a> for more on the rules.<br /></li>
<MarginText>26.i.8/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00377-01"]} />
<li>It is illegal to mention both an explicit child of an instance, and a child of the generic from which the instance was instantiated. This is easier to understand with an example: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>26.i.9/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}package G1 is{"\n"}end G1;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.10/2</MarginText>
generic{"\n"}package G1.G2 is{"\n"}end G1.G2;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.11/2</MarginText>
with G1;{"\n"}package I1 is new G1;{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.12/2</MarginText>
package I1.G2 renames ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>26.i.13/2</MarginText>
with G1.G2;{"\n"}with I1.G2;             -- Illegal{"\n"}package Bad is ...{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>26.i.14/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0300-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The context clause for Bad is illegal as I1 has an implicit declaration of I1.G2 based on the generic child G1.G2, as well as the mention of the explicit child I1.G2. As in the previous cases, this is illegal only if the context clause makes both children visible; the explicit child can be mentioned as long as the generic child is not (and vice versa). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>26.j</MarginText>
Note that we need to be careful which things we make "hidden from all visibility" versus which things we make simply illegal for names to denote. The distinction is subtle. The rules that disallow names denoting components within a type declaration (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7">3.7</a>) do not make the components invisible at those places, so that the above rule makes components with the same name illegal. The same is true for the rule that disallows names denoting formal parameters within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0206">formal_part</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>). <br />

<MarginText>26.k</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The part about instances is from AI83-00012. The reason it says &ldquo;overloadable declarations&rdquo; is because we don't want it to apply to type extensions that appear in an instance; components are not overloadable. <br />

<MarginText>27</MarginText>
NOTE 1   Visibility for compilation units follows from the definition of the environment in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.4">10.1.4</a>, except that it is necessary to apply a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> to obtain visibility to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library_unit_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0289">library_unit_renaming_declaration</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>28</MarginText>
NOTE 2   In addition to the visibility rules given above, the meaning of the occurrence of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> at a given place in the text can depend on the overloading rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.6">8.6</a>).<br />

<MarginText>29</MarginText>
NOTE 3   Not all contexts where an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> are allowed require visibility of a corresponding declaration. Contexts where visibility is not required are identified by using one of these three syntactic categories directly in a syntax rule, rather than using <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>29.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> that occurs in one of the following contexts is not required to denote a visible or directly visible declaration: <br />

<MarginText>29.b</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>A defining name.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29.c</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> that appear after the reserved word <b>end</b> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0090">proper_body</a></code>. Similarly for &ldquo;<b>end loop</b>&rdquo;, etc.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29.d</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0101">attribute_designator</a></code>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29.e</MarginText>
<dt><br/>4.</dt>
<dd>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29.f</MarginText>
<dt><br/>5.</dt>
<dd>A <i>pragma{"_"}argument{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29.g</MarginText>
<dt><br/>6.</dt>
<dd>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> specific to a pragma used in a pragma argument.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29.g.1/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>7.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<dd>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0347">aspect_mark</a></code>;<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29.g.2/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>8.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
<dd>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> specific to an aspect used in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>29.h</MarginText>
The visibility rules have nothing to do with the above cases; the meanings of such things are defined elsewhere. Reserved words are not <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s; the visibility rules don't apply to them either.<br />

<MarginText>29.i</MarginText>
Because of the way we have defined "declaration", it is possible for a usage name to denote a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, either within that body, or (for a nonlibrary unit) after it (since the body hides the corresponding declaration, if any). Other bodies do not work that way. Completions of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0023">type_declaration</a></code>s and deferred constant declarations do work that way. <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">Accept_statement</a></code>s are never denoted, although the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0207">parameter_specification</a></code>s in their profiles can be.<br />

<MarginText>29.j</MarginText>
The scope of a subprogram does not start until after its profile. Thus, the following is legal: <br />

<MarginText>29.k</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X : constant Integer := 17;{"\n"}...{"\n"}package P is{"\n"}    procedure X(Y : in Integer := X);{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>29.l</MarginText>
The body of the subprogram will probably be illegal, however, since the constant X will be hidden by then.<br />

<MarginText>29.m</MarginText>
The rule is different for generic subprograms, since they are not overloadable; the following is illegal: <br />

<MarginText>29.n</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X : constant Integer := 17;{"\n"}package P is{"\n"}    generic{"\n"}      Z : Integer := X; -- Illegal!{"\n"}    procedure X(Y : in Integer := X); -- Illegal!{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>29.o</MarginText>
The constant X is hidden from direct visibility by the generic declaration. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>29.p</MarginText>
Declarations with the same defining name as that of a subprogram or entry being defined are nevertheless visible within the subprogram specification or entry declaration. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>29.q</MarginText>
The term &ldquo;visible by selection&rdquo; is no longer defined. We use the terms &ldquo;directly visible&rdquo; and &ldquo;visible&rdquo; (among other things). There are only two regions of text that are of interest, here: the region in which a declaration is visible, and the region in which it is directly visible.<br />

<MarginText>29.r</MarginText>
Visibility is defined only for declarations. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>29.s/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00251-01"]} />
Added rules to handle the inheritance and overriding of multiple homographs for a single type declaration, in order to support multiple inheritance from interfaces. The new rules are intended to be compatible with the existing rules so that programs that do not use interfaces do not change their legality. However, there is a very rare case where this is not true: <br />

<MarginText>29.t/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type T1 is private;{"\n"}   type T2 is private;{"\n"}package G is{"\n"}   type T is null record;{"\n"}   procedure P (X : T; Y : T1);{"\n"}   procedure P (X : T; Z : T2);{"\n"}end G;]{"\n"}
<MarginText>29.u/2</MarginText>
package I is new G (Integer, Integer); -- Exports homographs of P.{"\n"}
<MarginText>29.v/2</MarginText>
type D is new I.T; -- Both Ps are inherited.{"\n"}
<MarginText>29.w/2</MarginText>
Obj : D;{"\n"}
<MarginText>29.x/2</MarginText>
P (Obj, Z ={">"} 10); -- Legal in Ada 95, illegal in Ada 2005.{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>29.y/2</MarginText>
The call to P would resolve in Ada 95 by using the parameter name, while the procedures P would be hidden from all visibility in Ada 2005 and thus would not resolve. This case doesn't seem worth making the rules any more complex than they already are.<br />

<MarginText>29.z/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00377-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> is illegal if it would create a homograph of an implicitly declared generic child (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">10.1.1</a>). An Ada 95 compiler could have allowed this, but which unit of the two units involved would be denoted wasn't specified, so any successful use isn't portable. Removing one of the two <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>s involved will fix the problem. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>29.aa/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00044-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0025</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified the overriding rules so that "/=" and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0172">statement_identifier</a></code>s are covered.<br />

<MarginText>29.bb/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00150-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0026</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that is it never possible for two components with the same name to be visible; any such program is illegal.<br />

<MarginText>29.cc/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00195-01", "AI95-00408-01"]} />
The visibility of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> is defined so that it can be used by the stream attribute availability rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>).<br />

<MarginText>29.dd/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
The visibility of a limited view of a library package is defined (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.1">10.1.1</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>29.ee/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0177-1", "AI12-0157-1"]} />
Added wording so that the parameters of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code> are visible in the return expression of the function. (It would be pretty useless without such a rule.)<br />

<MarginText>29.ff/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0183-1"]} />
The visibility of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> is defined so that it can be used in various other rules. <br />

<a id="Subclause_8.3.1"></a>

## 8.3.1  Overriding Indicators

<MarginText>1/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03"]} />
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> is used to declare that an operation is intended to override (or not override) an inherited operation. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>overriding{"_"}indicator</code><a id="S0234"></a><code> ::= </code>[<b>not</b>] <b>overriding</b><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/3_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03", "AI95-00348-01", "AI95-00397-01", "AI05-0177-1"]} />
<p>If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0076">abstract{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.7#S0227">null{"_"}procedure{"_"}declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8#S0228">expression{"_"}function{"_"}declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0298">subprogram{"_"}body{"_"}stub</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0242">subprogram{"_"}renaming{"_"}declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic{"_"}instantiation</a></code> of a subprogram, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code> other than a protected subprogram has an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding{"_"}indicator</a></code>, then:<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the operation shall be a primitive operation for some type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> is <b>overriding</b>, then the operation shall override a homograph at the place of the declaration or body;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.a/3_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>This doesn't require that the overriding happen at precisely the place of the declaration or body; it only requires that the region in  which the overriding is known to have happened includes this place. That is, the overriding can happen at or before the place of the declaration or body. <br />

<MarginText>6/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> is <b>not overriding</b>, then the operation shall not override any homograph (at any place). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply, these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The <b>overriding</b> and <b>not overriding</b> rules differ slightly. For <b>overriding</b>, we want the indicator to reflect the overriding state at the place of the declaration; otherwise the indicator would be &ldquo;lying&rdquo;. Whether a homograph is implicitly declared after the declaration (see 7.3.1 to see how this can happen) has no impact on this check. However, <b>not overriding</b> is different; &ldquo;lying&rdquo; would happen if a homograph declared later actually is overriding. So, we require this check to take into account later overridings. That can be implemented either by looking ahead, or by rechecking when additional operations are declared.<br />

<MarginText>7.b/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
The &ldquo;no lying&rdquo; rules are needed to prevent a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> from having contradictory <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>8/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00397-01"]} />
NOTE   Rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>s of task and protected entries and of protected subprograms are found in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.2">9.5.2</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4">9.4</a>, respectively. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>9/5_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00433-01", "AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of use of an overriding indicator when declaring a security queue derived from the Queue interface of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.4">3.9.4</a>:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>10/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Security{"_"}Queue is new Queue with record ...;{"\n"}
<MarginText>11/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
overriding{"\n"}procedure Append(Q : in out Security{"_"}Queue; Person : in Person{"_"}Name);{"\n"}
<MarginText>12/5_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1"]} />
overriding{"\n"}procedure Remove{"_"}First(Q : in out Security{"_"}Queue; Person : out Person{"_"}Name);{"\n"}
<MarginText>13/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
overriding{"\n"}function Cur{"_"}Count(Q : in Security{"_"}Queue) return Natural;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
overriding{"\n"}function Max{"_"}Count(Q : in Security{"_"}Queue) return Natural;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
not overriding{"\n"}procedure Arrest(Q : in out Security{"_"}Queue; Person : in Person{"_"}Name);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16/5_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0429-1"]} />
<p><i>The first four subprogram declarations guarantee that these subprograms will override the four subprograms inherited from the Queue interface. A misspelling in one of these subprograms will be detected at compile time by the implementation. Conversely, the declaration of Arrest guarantees that this is a new operation.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In this case, the subprograms are abstract, so misspellings will get detected anyway. But for other subprograms (especially when deriving from concrete types), the error might never be detected, and a body other than the one the programmer intended might be executed without warning. Thus our new motto: &ldquo;Overriding indicators &mdash; don't derive a type without them!&rdquo; <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>16.b/2_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00218-03"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">Overriding_indicator</a></code>s are new. These let the programmer state her overriding intentions to the compiler; if the compiler disagrees, an error will be produced rather than a hard to find bug. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>16.c/3_8.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-0177-1"]} />
Expression functions can have overriding indicators. <br />

---

# 8.4. Use Clauses

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  70

# 8.4. Use Clauses

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0236">use_package_clause</a></code> achieves direct visibility of declarations that appear in the visible part of a package; a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> achieves direct visibility of the primitive operators of a type.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
If and only if the visibility rules allow P.A, "<b>use</b> P;" should make A directly visible (barring name conflicts). This means, for example, that child library units, and generic formals of a formal package whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.7#S0341">formal_package_actual_part</a></code> is ({"<"}{">"}), should be made visible by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> for the appropriate package.<br />

<MarginText>1.b</MarginText>
The rules for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>s were carefully constructed to avoid so-called <i>Beaujolais</i> effects, where the addition or removal of a single <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, or a single declaration in a "use"d package, would change the meaning of a program from one legal interpretation to another. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>use{"_"}clause</code><a id="S0235"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0236">use_package_clause</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>use{"_"}package{"_"}clause</code><a id="S0236"></a><code> ::= </code><b>use</b> <i>package{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> {"{"}, <i>package{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"}"};<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0150-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>use{"_"}type{"_"}clause</code><a id="S0237"></a><code> ::= </code><b>use</b> [<b>all</b>] <b>type</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> {"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>{"}"};<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
<p>A <i>package{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0236">use_package_clause</a></code> shall denote a nonlimited view of a package. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This includes formal packages. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>For each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, there is a certain region of text called the <i>scope</i> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>. For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library{"_"}unit{"_"}declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0289">library{"_"}unit{"_"}renaming{"_"}declaration</a></code>, the scope is the entire declarative region of the declaration. For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code> of a body, the scope is the entire body [and any subunits (including multiply nested subunits). The scope does not include <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0292">context_clause</a></code>s themselves.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> immediately within a declarative region, the scope is the portion of the declarative region starting just after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> and extending to the end of the declarative region. However, the scope of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> in the private part of a library unit does not include the visible part of any public descendant of that library unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The exception echoes the similar exception for &ldquo;immediate scope (of a declaration)&rdquo; (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.2">8.2</a>). It makes <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>s work like this: <br />

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package P is{"\n"}    type T is range 1..10;{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7.c</MarginText>
with P;{"\n"}package Parent is{"\n"}private{"\n"}    use P;{"\n"}    X : T;{"\n"}end Parent;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7.d</MarginText>
package Parent.Child is{"\n"}    Y : T; -- Illegal!{"\n"}    Z : P.T;{"\n"}private{"\n"}    W : T;{"\n"}end Parent.Child;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.e</MarginText>
The declaration of Y is illegal because the scope of the &ldquo;<b>use</b> P&rdquo; does not include that place, so T is not directly visible there. The declarations of X, Z, and W are legal. <br />

<MarginText>7.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
<p>A package is <i>named</i> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0236">use_package_clause</a></code> if it is denoted by a <i>package{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of that clause. A type is <i>named</i> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> if it is determined by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> of that clause.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06", "AI05-0150-1"]} />
<p>For each package named in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0236">use_package_clause</a></code> whose scope encloses a place, each declaration that occurs immediately within the declarative region of the package is <i>potentially use-visible</i> at this place if the declaration is visible at this place. For each type <i>T</i> or <i>T</i>'Class named in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> whose scope encloses a place, the declaration of each primitive operator of type <i>T</i> is potentially use-visible at this place if its declaration is visible at this place. If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> whose scope encloses a place includes the reserved word <b>all</b>, then the following entities are also potentially use-visible at this place if the declaration of the entity is visible at this place: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0150-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Each primitive subprogram of <i>T</i> including each enumeration literal (if any);<br /></li>
<MarginText>8.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0150-1"]} />
<li>Each subprogram that is declared immediately within the declarative region in which an ancestor type of <i>T</i> is declared and that operates on a class-wide type that covers <i>T</i>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0150-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Primitive subprograms whose defining name is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> are <i>not</i> made potentially visible by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> unless reserved word <b>all</b> is included. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> without <b>all</b> is only for operators.<br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
The semantics described here should be similar to the semantics for expanded names given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">Selected Components</a>&rdquo; so as to achieve the effect requested by the &ldquo;principle of equivalence of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected_component</a></code>s&rdquo;. Thus, child library units and generic formal parameters of a formal package are potentially use-visible when their enclosing package is use'd.<br />

<MarginText>8.c</MarginText>
The "visible at that place" part implies that applying a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> to a parent unit does not make all of its children use-visible &mdash; only those that have been made visible by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>. It also implies that we don't have to worry about hiding in the definition of "directly visible" &mdash; a declaration cannot be use-visible unless it is visible.<br />

<MarginText>8.d</MarginText>
Note that "<b>use type</b> T'Class;" is equivalent to "<b>use type</b> T;", which helps avoid breaking the generic contract model. <br />

<MarginText>8.3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0131-1"]} />
<p>Certain implicit declarations may become potentially use-visible in certain contexts as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.6">12.6</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>A declaration is <i>use-visible</i> if it is potentially use-visible, except in these naming-conflict cases: <br /></p>

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A potentially use-visible declaration is not use-visible if the place considered is within the immediate scope of a homograph of the declaration.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<li>Potentially use-visible declarations that have the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> are not use-visible unless each of them is an overloadable declaration. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Overloadable declarations don't cancel each other out, even if they are homographs, though if they are not distinguishable by formal parameter names or the presence or absence of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0063">default_expression</a></code>s, any use will be ambiguous. We only mention <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s here, because declarations named by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code>s are always overloadable, and hence never cancel each other. Direct visibility is irrelevant for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.5#S0015">character_literal</a></code>s. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> has no effect. <br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a use clause in a context clause:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Calendar; use Ada;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a use type clause:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
use type Rational{"_"}Numbers.Rational; -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1">7.1</a>{"\n"}Two{"_"}Thirds: Rational{"_"}Numbers.Rational := 2/3;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In &ldquo;<b>use</b> X, Y;&rdquo;, Y cannot refer to something made visible by the &ldquo;<b>use</b>&rdquo; of X. Thus, it's not (quite) equivalent to &ldquo;<b>use</b> X; <b>use</b> Y;&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>16.b</MarginText>
If a given declaration is already immediately visible, then a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code> that makes it potentially use-visible has no effect. Therefore, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> for a type whose declaration appears in a place other than the visible part of a package has no effect; it cannot make a declaration use-visible unless that declaration is already immediately visible.<br />

<MarginText>16.c</MarginText>
"<b>Use</b> <b>type</b> S1;" and "<b>use</b> <b>type</b> S2;" are equivalent if S1 and S2 are both subtypes of the same type. In particular, "<b>use</b> <b>type</b> S;" and "<b>use</b> <b>type</b> S'Base;" are equivalent. <br />

<MarginText>16.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We considered adding a rule that prevented several declarations of views of the same entity that all have the same semantics from cancelling each other out. For example, if a (possibly implicit) <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> for "+" is potentially use-visible, and a fully conformant renaming of it is also potentially use-visible, then they (annoyingly) cancel each other out; neither one is use-visible. The considered rule would have made just one of them use-visible. We gave up on this idea due to the complexity of the rule. It would have had to account for both overloadable and nonoverloadable <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code>s, the case where the rule should apply only to some subset of the declarations with the same defining name, and the case of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0026">subtype_declaration</a></code>s (since they are claimed to be sufficient for renaming of subtypes). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>16.e</MarginText>
The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> is new to Ada 95. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>16.f</MarginText>
The phrase &ldquo;omitting from this set any packages that enclose this place&rdquo; is no longer necessary to avoid making something visible outside its scope, because we explicitly state that the declaration has to be visible in order to be potentially use-visible. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>16.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00217-06"]} />
Limited views of packages are not allowed in use clauses. Defined <i>named in a use clause</i> for use in other limited view rules (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.2">10.1.2</a>). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>16.h/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0150-1"]} />
The <b>use all type</b> version of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0237">use_type_clause</a></code> is new to Ada 2012. It works similarly to prefixed views. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>16.i/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0131-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording to allow other declarations to be potentially use-visible, to support corrections to formal subprograms. <br />

---

# 8.5. Renaming Declarations

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5.mdx

sidebar_position:  71

# 8.5. Renaming Declarations

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> declares another name for an entity, such as an object, exception, package, subprogram, entry, or generic unit. Alternatively, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0242">subprogram_renaming_declaration</a></code> can be the completion of a previous <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>renaming</b> &mdash; declaration that does not define a new entity, but instead defines a new view of an existing entity<br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>renaming{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0238"></a><code> ::= </code><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object_renaming_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0240">exception_renaming_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0241">package_renaming_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0242">subprogram_renaming_declaration</a></code><br />   | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0243">generic_renaming_declaration</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> evaluates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that follows the reserved word <b>renames</b> and thereby determines the view and entity denoted by this name (the <i>renamed view</i> and <i>renamed entity</i>). [A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that denotes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming_declaration</a></code> denotes (a new view of) the renamed entity.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 1   Renaming can be used to resolve name conflicts and to act as a shorthand. Renaming with a different <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0202">operator_symbol</a></code> does not hide the old <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>; the new <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> and the old <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> can be visible at different places.<br />

<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0427-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
NOTE 2   A subtype defined without any additional constraint can be used to achieve the effect of renaming another subtype (including a task or protected subtype) as in <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   subtype Mode is Ada.Text{"_"}IO.File{"_"}Mode;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
The second sentence of RM83-8.5(3), &ldquo;At any point where a renaming declaration is visible, the identifier, or operator symbol of this declaration denotes the renamed entity.&rdquo; is incorrect. It doesn't say directly visible. Also, such an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> might resolve to something else.<br />

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
The verbiage about renamings being legal &ldquo;only if exactly one...&rdquo;, which appears in RM83-8.5(4) (for objects) and RM83-8.5(7) (for subprograms) is removed, because it follows from the normal rules about overload resolution. For language lawyers, these facts are obvious; for programmers, they are irrelevant, since failing these tests is highly unlikely. <br />

<a id="Subclause_8.5.1"></a>

## 8.5.1  Object Renaming Declarations

<MarginText>1/5_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0383-1"]} />
<p>[An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object_renaming_declaration</a></code> is used to rename an object or value.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00423-01", "AI05-0183-1", "AI12-0275-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>object{"_"}renaming{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0239"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> [: [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>] <b>renames</b> <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> : <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> <b>renames</b> <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code><br />        [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/5_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00230-01", "AI95-00254-01", "AI95-00409-01", "AI12-0275-1"]} />
<p>The type of the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall resolve to the type determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>, if present. If no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> is present, the expected type of the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is any type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.1/5_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0275-1"]} />
<p>In the case where the type is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, the type of the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall resolve to an anonymous access type. If the anonymous access type is an access-to-object type, the type of the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall have the same designated type as that of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>. If the anonymous access type is an access-to-subprogram type, the type of the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall have a designated profile that is type conformant with that of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a_8.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A previous version of Ada 9X used the usual &ldquo;expected type&rdquo; wording:<br />&ldquo;The expected type for the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is that determined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code>.&rdquo;<br />We changed it so that this would be illegal: <br />

<MarginText>3.b_8.5.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
X: T;{"\n"}Y: T'Class renames X; -- Illegal!{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.c_8.5.1</MarginText>
When the above was legal, it was unclear whether Y was of type T or T'Class. Note that we still allow this: <br />

<MarginText>3.d_8.5.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Z: T'Class := ...;{"\n"}W: T renames F(Z);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.e_8.5.1</MarginText>
where F is a function with a controlling parameter and result. This is admittedly a bit odd.<br />

<MarginText>3.f_8.5.1</MarginText>
Note that the matching rule for generic formal parameters of mode <b>in out</b> was changed to keep it consistent with the rule for renaming. That makes the rule different for <b>in</b> vs. <b>in out</b>.<br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0383-1"]} />
<p>The renamed entity shall be an object or value.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.1/5_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI95-00409-01", "AI12-0383-1"]} />
<p>In the case where the type is defined by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>, the type of the renamed entity and the type defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code>: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.2/2_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00231-01", "AI95-00409-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>shall both be access-to-object types with statically matching designated subtypes and with both or neither being access-to-constant types; or <br /></li>
<MarginText>4.3/2_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00409-01"]} />
<li>shall both be access-to-subprogram types with subtype conformant designated profiles. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4.4/5_8.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00423-01", "AI12-0287-1"]} />
<p>For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object_renaming_declaration</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0084">access_definition</a></code> that has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0083">null_exclusion</a></code>, the subtype of the <i>object{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall exclude null. In addition, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0239">object_renaming_declaration</a></code> occurs within the body of a generic unit <i>G</i> or within the body of a generic unit declared within the declarative region of generic unit <i>G</i>, then:<br /></p>
