<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00397-01", "AI05-0183-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>entry{"_"}declaration</code><a id="S0257"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>]<br />   <b>entry</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> [(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>)] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0204">parameter_profile</a></code><br />      [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_9.5.2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>accept{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0258"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <b>accept</b> <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> [(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0259">entry_index</a></code>)] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0204">parameter_profile</a></code> [<b>do</b><br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />   <b>end</b> [<i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>]];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We cannot use <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s. Although an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is sort of like a body, it can appear nested within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.6#S0191">block_statement</a></code>, and therefore be hidden from its own entry by an outer homograph. <br />

<MarginText>4_9.5.2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>entry{"_"}index</code><a id="S0259"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0169-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>entry{"_"}body</code><a id="S0260"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>entry</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0261">entry_body_formal_part</a></code><br />       [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>]<br />    <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> <b>is</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code><br />    <b>begin</b><br />       <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />    <b>end</b> [<i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>];<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.a/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00397-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We don't allow an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> on an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> because entries always implement procedures at the point of the type declaration; there is no late implementation. And we don't want to have to think about <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>s on <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>6_9.5.2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>entry{"_"}body{"_"}formal{"_"}part</code><a id="S0261"></a><code> ::= </code>[(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry_index_specification</a></code>)] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0204">parameter_profile</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7_9.5.2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>entry{"_"}barrier</code><a id="S0262"></a><code> ::= </code><b>when</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0398-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>entry{"_"}index{"_"}specification</code><a id="S0263"></a><code> ::= </code><br />    <b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> <b>in</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>] <br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">If an <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> appears at the end of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, it shall repeat the <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct{"_"}name</a></code>. If an <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> appears at the end of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry{"_"}body</a></code>, it shall repeat the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining{"_"}identifier</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">[An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> is allowed only in a protected or task declaration.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This follows from the BNF. <br />

<MarginText>10.1/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00397-01"]} />
<p class="Indented2">An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> is not allowed in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> that includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a.1/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>An entry family can never implement something, so allowing an indicator is felt by the majority of the ARG to be redundant. <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>11_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>In an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, the expected profile for the <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> is that of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code>; the expected type for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0259">entry_index</a></code> is that of the subtype defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code> of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>Within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, if a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected{"_"}component</a></code> has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> that denotes the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code>, then the entity denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> is the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code>, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected{"_"}component</a></code> is interpreted as an expanded name (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.3">4.1.3</a>)[; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0099">selector_name</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0098">selected{"_"}component</a></code> has to be the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> for some formal parameter of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code>]. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The only declarations that occur immediately within the declarative region of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> are those for its formal parameters. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>13_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> in a task declaration shall not contain a specification for an access parameter (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10">3.10</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Access parameters for task entries would require a complex implementation. For example: <br />

<MarginText>13.b_9.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
task T is{"\n"}   entry E(Z : access Integer); -- Illegal!{"\n"}end T;{"\n"}
<MarginText>13.c_9.5.2</MarginText>
task body T is{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   declare{"\n"}      type A is access all Integer;{"\n"}      X : A;{"\n"}      Int : aliased Integer;{"\n"}      task Inner;{"\n"}      task body Inner is{"\n"}      begin{"\n"}         T.E(Int'Access);{"\n"}      end Inner;{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      accept E(Z : access Integer) do{"\n"}         X := A(Z); -- Accessibility{"_"}Check{"\n"}      end E;{"\n"}   end;{"\n"}end T;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13.d_9.5.2</MarginText>
Implementing the Accessibility{"_"}Check inside the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> for E is difficult, since one does not know whether the entry caller is calling from inside the immediately enclosing declare block or from outside it. This means that the lexical nesting level associated with the designated object is not sufficient to determine whether the Accessibility{"_"}Check should pass or fail.<br />

<MarginText>13.e_9.5.2</MarginText>
Note that such problems do not arise with protected entries, because <code>entry{"_"}bodies</code> are always nested immediately within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code>; they cannot be further nested as can <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s, nor can they be called from within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code> (since no entry calls are permitted inside a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected_body</a></code>). <br />

<MarginText>13.1/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00397-01"]} />
<p>If an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> has an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code>, then at the point of the declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.2/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> is <b>overriding</b>, then the entry shall implement an inherited subprogram;<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.3/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<li>if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#S0234">overriding_indicator</a></code> is <b>not overriding</b>, then the entry shall not implement any inherited subprogram.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.4/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.f/2_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>These rules are subtly different than those for subprograms (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.3#Subclause_8.3.1">8.3.1</a>) because there cannot be &ldquo;late&rdquo; inheritance of primitives from interfaces. Hidden (that is, private) interfaces are prohibited explicitly (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3">7.3</a>), as are hidden primitive operations (as private operations of public abstract types are prohibited &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.3">3.9.3</a>). <br />

<MarginText>14_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, the innermost enclosing body shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>, and the <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct{"_"}name</a></code> shall denote an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> in the corresponding task declaration; the profile of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code> shall conform fully to that of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code>. An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code> shall have a parenthesized <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0259">entry{"_"}index</a></code> if and only if the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> shall not be within another <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> that corresponds to the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code>, nor within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous{"_"}select</a></code> inner to the enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">Accept_statement</a></code>s are required to be immediately within the enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code> (as opposed to being in a nested subprogram) to ensure that a nested task does not attempt to accept the entry of its enclosing task. We considered relaxing this restriction, either by making the check a run-time check, or by allowing a nested task to accept an entry of its enclosing task. However, neither change seemed to provide sufficient benefit to justify the additional implementation burden.<br />

<MarginText>15.b_9.5.2</MarginText>
Nested <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s for the same entry (or entry family) are prohibited to ensure that there is no ambiguity in the resolution of an expanded name for a formal parameter of the entry. This could be relaxed by allowing the inner one to hide the outer one from all visibility, but again the small added benefit didn't seem to justify making the change for Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>15.c_9.5.2</MarginText>
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">Accept_statement</a></code>s are not permitted within <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> statements to simplify the semantics and implementation: an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> could result in Tasking{"_"}Error being propagated from an entry call even though the target task was still callable; implementations that use multiple tasks implicitly to implement an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> might have trouble supporting "up-level" accepts. Furthermore, if <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s were permitted in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code>, a task could call its own entry and then accept it in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code>, leading to rather unusual and possibly difficult-to-specify semantics. <br />

<MarginText>16_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> of a protected unit requires a completion[, which shall be an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>,] and every <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry{"_"}body</a></code> shall be the completion of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> of a protected unit. The profile of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry{"_"}body</a></code> shall conform fully to that of the corresponding declaration. <br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>, unlike a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>, cannot be completed with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0238">renaming{"_"}declaration</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>16.b/3_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>If the implementation supports it, the entry body can be imported (using aspect Import, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>), in which case no explicit <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> is allowed. <br />

<MarginText>16.c_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The above applies only to protected entries, which are the only ones completed with <code>entry{"_"}bodies</code>. Task entries have corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s instead of having <code>entry{"_"}bodies</code>, and we do not consider an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> to be a &ldquo;completion,&rdquo; because a task <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> is allowed to have zero, one, or more than one corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>17_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0261">entry_body_formal_part</a></code> shall have an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry{"_"}index{"_"}specification</a></code> if and only if the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> has a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>. In this case, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>s of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry{"_"}index{"_"}specification</a></code> shall fully conform to one another (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>18_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>A name that denotes a formal parameter of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> is not allowed within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>.<br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>19_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>The parameter modes defined for parameters in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0204">parameter_profile</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> are the same as for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> and have the same meaning (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.2">6.2</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Note that access parameters are not allowed for task entries (see above). <br />

<MarginText>20_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>) declares a <i>family</i> of distinct entries having the same profile, with one such entry for each value of the <i>entry index subtype</i> defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>. [A name for an entry of a family takes the form of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>, where the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> denotes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> for the family, and the index value identifies the entry within the family.] The term <i>single entry</i> is used to refer to any entry other than an entry of an entry family.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>In the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> for an entry family, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry_index_specification</a></code> declares a named constant whose subtype is the entry index subtype defined by the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>; the value of the <i>named entry index</i> identifies which entry of the family was called. <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0263">entry_index_specification</a></code> is not elaborated; the subtype of the named constant declared is defined by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete_subtype_definition</a></code> of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>, which is elaborated, either when the type is declared, or when the object is created, if its constraint is per-object. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>22/1_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00171-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0002</i>{"}"} The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> for an entry family consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#S0055">discrete{"_"}subtype{"_"}definition</a></code>, as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8">3.8</a>. The elaboration of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry{"_"}declaration</a></code> for a single entry has no effect. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The elaboration of the declaration of a protected subprogram has no effect, as specified in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>. The default initialization of an object of a task or protected type is covered in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>23_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>[The actions to be performed when an entry is called are specified by the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept{"_"}statement</a></code>s (if any) for an entry of a task unit, and by the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry{"_"}body</a></code> for an entry of a protected unit.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>23.1/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0193-1"]} />
<p>The interaction between a task that calls an entry and an accepting task is called a <i>rendezvous</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>24/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0193-1"]} />
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0259">entry_index</a></code>, if any, is first evaluated and converted to the entry index subtype; this index value identifies which entry of the family is to be accepted. Further execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is then blocked until a caller of the corresponding entry is selected (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>), whereupon the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>, if any, of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is executed, with the formal parameters associated with the corresponding actual parameters of the selected entry call. Execution of the rendezvous consists of the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code>, performance of any postcondition or type invariant checks associated with the entry, and any initialization or finalization associated with these checks, as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#Subclause_6.1.1">6.1.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.2">7.3.2</a>. After execution of the rendezvous, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> completes and is left. [The two tasks then proceed independently.] When an exception is propagated from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, the same exception is also raised by the execution of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0264">entry_call_statement</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This is in addition to propagating it to the construct containing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>. In other words, for a rendezvous, the raising splits in two, and continues concurrently in both tasks.<br />

<MarginText>24.b_9.5.2</MarginText>
The caller gets a new occurrence; this isn't considered propagation.<br />

<MarginText>24.c_9.5.2</MarginText>
Note that we say &ldquo;propagated from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>&rdquo;, not &ldquo;propagated from an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>&rdquo;. The latter would be wrong &mdash; we don't want exceptions propagated by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0259">entry_index</a></code> to be sent to the caller (there is none yet!).<br />

<MarginText>24.d/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0193-1"]} />
Execution of the rendezvous does not include any checks associated with parameter copy back or any post-call subtype predicate check for a parameter which is passed by reference. These checks are performed by the caller after the execution of the rendezvous. <br />

<MarginText>25/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0193-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>26_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p>[An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> is executed when the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> evaluates to True and a caller of the corresponding single entry, or entry of the corresponding entry family, has been selected (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>).] For the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry{"_"}body</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry{"_"}body</a></code> is elaborated, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the body is executed, as for the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. The value of the named entry index, if any, is determined by the value of the entry index specified in the <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> of the selected entry call (or intermediate <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0265">requeue{"_"}statement</a></code> &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.4">9.5.4</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>If the entry had been renamed as a subprogram, and the call was a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">procedure_call_statement</a></code> using the name declared by the renaming, the entry index (if any) comes from the entry <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> specified in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#S0242">subprogram_renaming_declaration</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>27_9.5.2</MarginText>
NOTE 1   A task entry has corresponding accept{"_"}statements (zero or more), whereas a protected entry has a corresponding entry{"_"}body (exactly one).<br />

<MarginText>28_9.5.2</MarginText>
NOTE 2   A consequence of the rule regarding the allowed placements of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s is that a task can execute <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>s only for its own entries.<br />

<MarginText>29/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00318-02", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 3   A return statement (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5">6.5</a>) or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0265">requeue_statement</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.4">9.5.4</a>) can be used to complete the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>29.a_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> need not have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> even if the corresponding entry has parameters. Equally, it can have a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled_sequence_of_statements</a></code> even if the corresponding entry has no parameters. <br />

<MarginText>29.b_9.5.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A single entry overloads a subprogram, an enumeration literal, or another single entry if they have the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code>. Overloading is not allowed for entry family names. A single entry or an entry of an entry family can be renamed as a procedure as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.5#Subclause_8.5.4">8.5.4</a>. <br />

<MarginText>30/5_9.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 4   The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> can reference anything visible except the formal parameters of the entry. This includes the entry index (if any), the components (including discriminants) of the protected object, the Count attribute of an entry of that protected object, and data global to the protected unit.<br />

<MarginText>31_9.5.2</MarginText>
The restriction against referencing the formal parameters within an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> ensures that all calls of the same entry see the same barrier value. If it is necessary to look at the parameters of an entry call before deciding whether to handle it, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> can be &ldquo;<b>when</b> True&rdquo; and the caller can be requeued (on some private entry) when its parameters indicate that it cannot be handled immediately. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>32_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of entry declarations:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>33_9.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
entry Read(V : out Item);{"\n"}entry Seize;{"\n"}entry Request(Level)(D : Item);  --  a family of entries{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>34_9.5.2</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of accept statements:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>35_9.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
accept Shut{"_"}Down;{"\n"}
<MarginText>36_9.5.2</MarginText>
accept Read(V : out Item) do{"\n"}   V := Local{"_"}Item;{"\n"}end Read;{"\n"}
<MarginText>37_9.5.2</MarginText>
accept Request(Low)(D : Item) do{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}end Request;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
