<MarginText>70/3_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI95-00427-01", "AI05-0238-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Splits Seconds into Hour, Minute, Second and Sub{"_"}Second in such a way that the resulting values all belong to their respective subtypes. The value returned in the Sub{"_"}Second parameter is always less than 1.0. If Seconds = 86400.0, Split propagates Time{"_"}Error.<br /></p>

<MarginText>70.a/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is only one way to do the split which meets all of the requirements. <br />

<MarginText>70.b/3_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0238-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>If Seconds = 86400.0, one of the returned values would have to be out of its defined range (either Sub{"_"}Second = 1.0 or Hour = 24 with the other value being 0). This doesn't seem worth breaking the invariants. <br />

<MarginText>71/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Time{"_"}Of (Year       : Year{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Month      : Month{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Day        : Day{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Hour       : Hour{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Minute     : Minute{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Second     : Second{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Sub{"_"}Second : Second{"_"}Duration := 0.0;{"\n"}                  Leap{"_"}Second: Boolean := False;{"\n"}                  Time{"_"}Zone  : Time{"_"}Zones.Time{"_"}Offset := 0){"\n"}                          return Time;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>72/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI95-00427-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Leap{"_"}Second is False, returns a Time built from the date and time values, relative to the specified time zone offset. If Leap{"_"}Second is True, returns the Time that represents the time within the leap second that is one second later than the time specified by the other parameters. Time{"_"}Error is raised if the parameters do not form a proper date or time. If Time{"_"}Of is called with a Sub{"_"}Second value of 1.0, the value returned is equal to the value of Time{"_"}Of for the next second with a Sub{"_"}Second value of 0.0. <br /></p>

<MarginText>72.a/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Time{"_"}Error should be raised if Leap{"_"}Second is True, and the date and time values do not represent the second before a leap second. A leap second always occurs at midnight UTC, and is 23:59:60 UTC in ISO notation. So, if the time zone is UTC and Leap{"_"}Second is True, if any of Hour /= 23, Minute /= 59, or Second /= 59, then Time{"_"}Error should be raised. However, we do not say that, because other time zones will have different values where a leap second is allowed. <br />

<MarginText>73/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Time{"_"}Of (Year       : Year{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Month      : Month{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Day        : Day{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                  Seconds    : Day{"_"}Duration := 0.0;{"\n"}                  Leap{"_"}Second: Boolean := False;{"\n"}                  Time{"_"}Zone  : Time{"_"}Zones.Time{"_"}Offset := 0){"\n"}                          return Time;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>74/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI95-00427-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Leap{"_"}Second is False, returns a Time built from the date and time values, relative to the specified time zone offset. If Leap{"_"}Second is True, returns the Time that represents the time within the leap second that is one second later than the time specified by the other parameters. Time{"_"}Error is raised if the parameters do not form a proper date or time. If Time{"_"}Of is called with a Seconds value of 86{"_"}400.0, the value returned is equal to the value of Time{"_"}Of for the next day with a Seconds value of 0.0.<br /></p>

<MarginText>75/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Split (Date       : in Time;{"\n"}                 Year       : out Year{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Month      : out Month{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Day        : out Day{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Hour       : out Hour{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Minute     : out Minute{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Second     : out Second{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Sub{"_"}Second : out Second{"_"}Duration;{"\n"}                 Leap{"_"}Second: out Boolean;{"\n"}                 Time{"_"}Zone  : in Time{"_"}Zones.Time{"_"}Offset := 0);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>76/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI95-00427-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Date does not represent a time within a leap second, splits Date into its constituent parts (Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Sub{"_"}Second), relative to the specified time zone offset, and sets Leap{"_"}Second to False. If Date represents a time within a leap second, set the constituent parts to values corresponding to a time one second earlier than that given by Date, relative to the specified time zone offset, and sets Leap{"_"}Seconds to True. The value returned in the Sub{"_"}Second parameter is always less than 1.0.<br /></p>

<MarginText>77/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Split (Date       : in Time;{"\n"}                 Year       : out Year{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Month      : out Month{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Day        : out Day{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Hour       : out Hour{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Minute     : out Minute{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Second     : out Second{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Sub{"_"}Second : out Second{"_"}Duration;{"\n"}                 Time{"_"}Zone  : in Time{"_"}Zones.Time{"_"}Offset := 0);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>78/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI95-00427-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Splits Date into its constituent parts (Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Sub{"_"}Second), relative to the specified time zone offset. The value returned in the Sub{"_"}Second parameter is always less than 1.0.<br /></p>

<MarginText>79/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Split (Date       : in Time;{"\n"}                 Year       : out Year{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Month      : out Month{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Day        : out Day{"_"}Number;{"\n"}                 Seconds    : out Day{"_"}Duration;{"\n"}                 Leap{"_"}Second: out Boolean;{"\n"}                 Time{"_"}Zone  : in Time{"_"}Zones.Time{"_"}Offset := 0);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>80/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI95-00427-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Date does not represent a time within a leap second, splits Date into its constituent parts (Year, Month, Day, Seconds), relative to the specified time zone offset, and sets Leap{"_"}Second to False. If Date represents a time within a leap second, set the constituent parts to values corresponding to a time one second earlier than that given by Date, relative to the specified time zone offset, and sets Leap{"_"}Seconds to True. The value returned in the Seconds parameter is always less than 86{"_"}400.0.<br /></p>

<MarginText>81/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Image (Date : Time;{"\n"}                Include{"_"}Time{"_"}Fraction : Boolean := False;{"\n"}                Time{"_"}Zone  : Time{"_"}Zones.Time{"_"}Offset := 0) return String;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>82/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns a string form of the Date relative to the given Time{"_"}Zone. The format is "Year-Month-Day Hour:Minute:Second", where the Year is a 4-digit value, and all others are 2-digit values, of the functions defined in Calendar and Calendar.Formatting, including a leading zero, if needed. The separators between the values are a minus, another minus, a colon, and a single space between the Day and Hour. If Include{"_"}Time{"_"}Fraction is True, the integer part of Sub{"_"}Seconds{"*"}100 is suffixed to the string as a point followed by a 2-digit value. <br /></p>

<MarginText>82.a/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The Image provides a string in ISO 8601 format, the international standard time format. Alternative representations allowed in ISO 8601 are not supported here.<br />

<MarginText>82.b/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
ISO 8601 allows 24:00:00 for midnight; and a seconds value of 60 for leap seconds. These are not allowed here (the routines mentioned above cannot produce those results). <br />

<MarginText>82.c/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The fractional part is truncated, not rounded. It would be quite hard to define the result with proper rounding, as it can change all of the values of the image. Values can be rounded up by adding an appropriate constant (0.5 if Include{"_"}Time{"_"}Fraction is False, 0.005 otherwise) to the time before taking the image. <br />

<MarginText>83/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Value (Date : String;{"\n"}                Time{"_"}Zone  : Time{"_"}Zones.Time{"_"}Offset := 0) return Time;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>84/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns a Time value for the image given as Date, relative to the given time zone. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if the string is not formatted as described for Image, or the function cannot interpret the given string as a Time value.<br /></p>

<MarginText>84.a/3_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The intent is that the implementation enforce the same range rules on the string as the appropriate function Time{"_"}Of, except for the hour, so &ldquo;cannot interpret the given string as a Time value&rdquo; happens when one of the values is out of the required range. For example, "2005-08-31 24:00:00" should raise Constraint{"_"}Error (the hour is out of range). <br />

<MarginText>85/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Image (Elapsed{"_"}Time : Duration;{"\n"}                Include{"_"}Time{"_"}Fraction : Boolean := False) return String;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>86/5_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns a string form of the Elapsed{"_"}Time. The format is "Hour:Minute:Second", where all values are 2-digit values, including a leading zero, if necessary. The separators between the values are colons. If Include{"_"}Time{"_"}Fraction is True, the integer part of Sub{"_"}Seconds{"*"}100 is suffixed to the string as a point followed by a 2-digit value. If Elapsed{"_"}Time {"<"} 0.0, the result is Image (<b>abs</b> Elapsed{"_"}Time, Include{"_"}Time{"_"}Fraction) prefixed with a minus sign. If <b>abs</b> Elapsed{"_"}Time represents 100 hours or more, the result is implementation-defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>86.a/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The result of Calendar.Formatting.Image if its argument represents more than 100 hours.<br />

<MarginText>86.b/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This cannot be implemented (directly) by calling Calendar.Formatting.Split, since it may be out of the range of Day{"_"}Duration, and thus the number of hours may be out of the range of Hour{"_"}Number.<br />

<MarginText>86.c_9.6.1</MarginText>
If a Duration value can represent more then 100 hours, the implementation will need to define a format for the return of Image. <br />

<MarginText>87/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Value (Elapsed{"_"}Time : String) return Duration;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>88/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns a Duration value for the image given as Elapsed{"_"}Time. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if the string is not formatted as described for Image, or the function cannot interpret the given string as a Duration value. <br /></p>

<MarginText>88.a/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The intent is that the implementation enforce the same range rules on the string as the appropriate function Time{"_"}Of, except for the hour, so &ldquo;cannot interpret the given string as a Time value&rdquo; happens when one of the values is out of the required range. For example, "10:23:60" should raise Constraint{"_"}Error (the seconds value is out of range). <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>89/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01"]} />
<p>An implementation should support leap seconds if the target system supports them. If leap seconds are not supported, Difference should return zero for Leap{"_"}Seconds, Split should return False for Leap{"_"}Second, and Time{"_"}Of should raise Time{"_"}Error if Leap{"_"}Second is True. <br /></p>

<MarginText>89.a/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Leap seconds should be supported if the target system supports them. Otherwise, operations in Calendar.Formatting should return results consistent with no leap seconds.<br />

<MarginText>89.b/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>An implementation can always support leap seconds when the target system does not; indeed, this isn't particularly hard (all that is required is a table of when leap seconds were inserted). As such, leap second support isn't &ldquo;impossible or impractical&rdquo; in the sense of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>. However, for some purposes, it may be important to follow the target system's lack of leap second support (if the target is a GPS satellite, which does not use leap seconds, leap second support would be a handicap to work around). Thus, this  should be read as giving permission to not support leap seconds on target systems that don't support leap seconds. Implementers should use the needs of their customers to determine whether or not support leap seconds on such targets. <br />

<MarginText>90/5_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI12-0336-1", "AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 1   The implementation-defined time zone of package Calendar can be the local time zone. Local{"_"}Time{"_"}Offset always returns the difference relative to the implementation-defined time zone of package Calendar. If Local{"_"}Time{"_"}Offset does not raise Unknown{"_"}Zone{"_"}Error, UTC time can be safely calculated (within the accuracy of the underlying time-base).<br />

<MarginText>90.a/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The time in the time zone known as Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is generally very close to UTC time; for most purposes they can be treated the same. GMT is the time based on the rotation of the Earth; UTC is the time based on atomic clocks, with leap seconds periodically inserted to realign with GMT (because most human activities depend on the rotation of the Earth). At any point in time, there will be a sub-second difference between GMT and UTC. <br />

<MarginText>91/5_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI12-0336-1"]} />
NOTE 2   Calling Split on the results of subtracting Duration(Local{"_"}Time{"_"}Offset{"*"}60) from Clock provides the components (hours, minutes, and so on) of the UTC time. In the United States, for example, Local{"_"}Time{"_"}Offset will generally be negative. <br />

<MarginText>91.a/5_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0336-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This is an illustration to help specify the value of Local{"_"}Time{"_"}Offset. A user should pass zero as the Time{"_"}Zone parameter of Split, rather than trying to make the above calculation. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>91.b/2_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00351-01", "AI95-00428-01"]} />
Packages Calendar.Time{"_"}Zones, Calendar.Arithmetic, and Calendar.Formatting are new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2005

<MarginText>91.c/3_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0238-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Defined that Split for Seconds raises Time{"_"}Error for a value of exactly 86400.0, rather than breaking some invariant or raising some other exception. Ada 2005 left this unspecified; a program that depended on what some implementation does might break, but such a program is not portable anyway. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>91.d/3_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0119-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified the sign of UTC{"_"}Time{"_"}Offset. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>91.e/5_9.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0336-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Changed the definition of Time{"_"}Offset to be compatible with most compilers. Also added Local{"_"}Time{"_"}Offset and Local{"_"}Image to better describe the intent. A program that expects the Ada 2012 definition of Time{"_"}Offset would get incorrect answers. However, most compilers tested use the revised definition, so the likelihood of a program breaking is quite low. Additionally, the new definitions could cause a use clause conflict; see the introduction of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a> for more on this topic. <br />

# 9.7. Select Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7.mdx

sidebar_position:  80

# 9.7. Select Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[There are four forms of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select_statement</a></code>. One form provides a selective wait for one or more <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0272">select_alternative</a></code>s. Two provide timed and conditional entry calls. The fourth provides asynchronous transfer of control.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>select{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0269"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0276">timed_entry_call</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0279">conditional_entry_call</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Examples

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a select statement:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
select{"\n"}   accept Driver{"_"}Awake{"_"}Signal;{"\n"}or{"\n"}   delay 30.0{"*"}Seconds;{"\n"}   Stop{"_"}The{"_"}Train;{"\n"}end select;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">Asynchronous_select</a></code> is new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_9.7.1"></a>

## 9.7.1  Selective Accept

<MarginText>1_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p>[This form of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select_statement</a></code> allows a combination of waiting for, and selecting from, one or more alternatives. The selection may depend on conditions associated with each alternative of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code>. ]<br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_9.7.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>selective{"_"}accept</code><a id="S0270"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <b>select</b><br />   [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0271">guard</a></code>]<br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0272">select_alternative</a></code><br />{"{"} <b>or</b><br />   [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0271">guard</a></code>]<br />     <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0272">select_alternative</a></code> {"}"}<br />[ <b>else</b><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> ]<br />  <b>end select</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_9.7.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>guard</code><a id="S0271"></a><code> ::= </code><b>when</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> ={">"}<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4_9.7.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>select{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0272"></a><code> ::= </code><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code><br />  | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5_9.7.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>accept{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0273"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6_9.7.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>delay{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0274"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7_9.7.1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>terminate{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0275"></a><code> ::= </code><b>terminate</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> shall contain at least one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code>. In addition, it can contain: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9_9.7.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code> (only one); or<br /></li>
<MarginText>10_9.7.1</MarginText>
<li>one or more <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code>s; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>11_9.7.1</MarginText>
<li>an <i>else part</i> (the reserved word <b>else</b> followed by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">These three possibilities are mutually exclusive. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>13_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> contains more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code>, then all shall be <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0268">delay{"_"}relative{"_"}statement</a></code>s, or all shall be <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0267">delay{"_"}until{"_"}statement</a></code>s for the same time type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a_9.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This simplifies the implementation and the description of the semantics. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>14_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0272">select_alternative</a></code> is said to be <i>open</i> if it is not immediately preceded by a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0271">guard</a></code>, or if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0271">guard</a></code> evaluates to True. It is said to be <i>closed</i> otherwise.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code>, any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0271">guard</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>s are evaluated; open alternatives are thus determined. For an open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code>, the <i>delay{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is also evaluated. Similarly, for an open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code> for an entry of a family, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0259">entry_index</a></code> is also evaluated. These evaluations are performed in an arbitrary order, except that a <i>delay{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0259">entry_index</a></code> is not evaluated until after evaluating the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code>, if any. Selection and execution of one open alternative, or of the else part, then completes the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code>; the rules for this selection are described below.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p>Open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code>s are first considered. Selection of one such alternative takes place immediately if the corresponding entry already has queued calls. If several alternatives can thus be selected, one of them is selected according to the entry queuing policy in effect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.4">D.4</a>). When such an alternative is selected, the selected call is removed from its entry queue and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0304">handled{"_"}sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> (if any) of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> is executed; after the rendezvous completes any subsequent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the alternative is executed. If no selection is immediately possible (in the above sense) and there is no else part, the task blocks until an open alternative can be selected.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p>Selection of the other forms of alternative or of an else part is performed as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>18_9.7.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>An open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code> is selected when its expiration time is reached if no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept{"_"}alternative</a></code> or other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay{"_"}alternative</a></code> can be selected prior to the expiration time. If several <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay{"_"}alternative</a></code>s have this same expiration time, one of them is selected according to the queuing policy in effect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.4">D.4</a>); the default queuing policy chooses arbitrarily among the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay{"_"}alternative</a></code>s whose expiration time has passed.<br /></li>
<MarginText>19_9.7.1</MarginText>
<li>The else part is selected and its <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> is executed if no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code> can immediately be selected; in particular, if all alternatives are closed.<br /></li>
<MarginText>20/5_9.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<li>An open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code> is selected if the conditions stated at the end of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.3">9.3</a> are satisfied. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a_9.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In the absence of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0265">requeue_statement</a></code>, the conditions stated are such that a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code> cannot be selected while there is a queued entry call for any entry of the task. In the presence of requeues from a task to one of its subtasks, it is possible that when a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code> of the subtask is selected, requeued calls (for closed entries only) might still be queued on some entry of the subtask. Tasking{"_"}Error will be propagated to such callers, as is usual when a task completes while queued callers remain. <br />

<MarginText>21_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The exception Program{"_"}Error is raised if all alternatives are closed and there is no else part.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22/5_9.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0447-1"]} />
NOTE   A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> can have several open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code>s. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> can have several open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code>s for the same entry.<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>23_9.7.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a task body with a selective accept:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>24_9.7.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
task body Server is{"\n"}   Current{"_"}Work{"_"}Item : Work{"_"}Item;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   loop{"\n"}      select{"\n"}         accept Next{"_"}Work{"_"}Item(WI : in Work{"_"}Item) do{"\n"}            Current{"_"}Work{"_"}Item := WI;{"\n"}         end;{"\n"}         Process{"_"}Work{"_"}Item(Current{"_"}Work{"_"}Item);{"\n"}      or{"\n"}         accept Shut{"_"}Down;{"\n"}         exit;       -- Premature shut down requested{"\n"}      or{"\n"}         terminate;  -- Normal shutdown at end of scope{"\n"}      end select;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}end Server;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>24.a_9.7.1</MarginText>
The name of <code>selective{"_"}wait</code> was changed to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> to better describe what is being waited for. We kept <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0272">select_alternative</a></code> as is, because <code>selective{"_"}accept{"_"}alternative</code> was too easily confused with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code>. <br />

<a id="Subclause_9.7.2"></a>

## 9.7.2  Timed Entry Calls

<MarginText>1/5_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0276">timed_entry_call</a></code> issues an entry call that is cancelled if the call (or a requeue-with-abort of the call) is not selected before the expiration time is reached. A procedure call may appear rather than an entry call for cases where the procedure can be implemented by an entry. ]<br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_9.7.2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>timed{"_"}entry{"_"}call</code><a id="S0276"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <b>select</b><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0277">entry_call_alternative</a></code><br />  <b>or</b><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code><br />  <b>end select</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/2_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>entry{"_"}call{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0277"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0278">procedure_or_entry_call</a></code> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.1/2_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>procedure{"_"}or{"_"}entry{"_"}call</code><a id="S0278"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">procedure_call_statement</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0264">entry_call_statement</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3.2/2_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">procedure_call_statement</a></code> is used for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0278">procedure_or_entry_call</a></code>, the <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> or <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0217">procedure_call_statement</a></code> shall statically denote an entry renamed as a procedure or (a view of) a primitive subprogram of a limited interface whose first parameter is a controlling parameter (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.2">3.9.2</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/2_9.7.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This would be a confusing way to call a procedure, so we only allow it when it is possible that the procedure is actually an entry. We could have allowed formal subprograms here, but we didn't because we'd have to allow all formal subprograms, and it would increase the difficulty of generic code sharing.<br />

<MarginText>3.b/2_9.7.2</MarginText>
We say &ldquo;statically denotes&rdquo; because an access-to-subprogram cannot be primitive, and we don't have anything like access-to-entry. So only names of entries or procedures are possible. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>4/2_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<p>For the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0276">timed_entry_call</a></code>, the <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, or <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>, and any actual parameters are evaluated, as for a simple entry call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>) or procedure call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4">6.4</a>). The expiration time (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6">9.6</a>) for the call is determined by evaluating the <i>delay{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code>. If the call is an entry call or a call on a procedure implemented by an entry, the entry call is then issued. Otherwise, the call proceeds as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4">6.4</a> for a procedure call, followed by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0277">entry{"_"}call{"_"}alternative</a></code>; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay{"_"}alternative</a></code> is ignored.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5_9.7.2</MarginText>
<p>If the call is queued (including due to a requeue-with-abort), and not selected before the expiration time is reached, an attempt to cancel the call is made. If the call completes due to the cancellation, the optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay{"_"}alternative</a></code> is executed; if the entry call completes normally, the optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0277">entry{"_"}call{"_"}alternative</a></code> is executed. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/2_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>6_9.7.2</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a timed entry call:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>7_9.7.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
select{"\n"}   Controller.Request(Medium)(Some{"_"}Item);{"\n"}or{"\n"}   delay 45.0;{"\n"}   --  controller too busy, try something else{"\n"}end select;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>7.a/3_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause comes before the one for Conditional Entry Calls, so we can define conditional entry calls in terms of timed entry calls. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>7.b/3_9.7.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01", "AI05-0005-1"]} />
A procedure call can be used as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0277">entry_call_alternative</a></code> in a timed or conditional entry call, if the procedure might actually be an entry. Since the fact that something is an entry could be used in resolving these calls in Ada 95, it is possible for timed or conditional entry calls that resolved in Ada 95 to be ambiguous in Ada 2005. That could happen if both an entry and procedure with the same name and profile exist, which should be rare. <br />

<a id="Subclause_9.7.3"></a>

## 9.7.3  Conditional Entry Calls

<MarginText>1/5_9.7.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>[A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0279">conditional_entry_call</a></code> issues an entry call that is then cancelled if it is not selected immediately (or if a requeue-with-abort of the call is not selected immediately). A procedure call may appear rather than an entry call for cases where the procedure can be implemented by an entry.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a_9.7.3</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>In the case of an entry call on a protected object, it is OK if the entry is closed at the start of the corresponding protected action, so long as it opens and the call is selected before the end of that protected action (due to changes in the Count attribute). <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_9.7.3</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>conditional{"_"}entry{"_"}call</code><a id="S0279"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <b>select</b><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0277">entry_call_alternative</a></code><br />  <b>else</b><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />  <b>end select</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>3_9.7.3</MarginText>
<p>The execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0279">conditional_entry_call</a></code> is defined to be equivalent to the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0276">timed{"_"}entry{"_"}call</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay{"_"}alternative</a></code> specifying an immediate expiration time and the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> as given after the reserved word <b>else</b>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/5_9.7.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE   A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0279">conditional_entry_call</a></code> can briefly increase the Count attribute of the entry, even if the conditional call is not selected.<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>5_9.7.3</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a conditional entry call:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>6/5_9.7.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Spin(R : in out Resource) is  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4">9.4</a>{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   loop{"\n"}      select{"\n"}         R.Seize;{"\n"}         return;{"\n"}      else{"\n"}         null;  --  busy waiting{"\n"}      end select;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>6.a/3_9.7.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause comes after the one for Timed Entry Calls, so we can define conditional entry calls in terms of timed entry calls. We do that so that an "expiration time" is defined for both, thereby simplifying the definition of what happens on a requeue-with-abort. <br />

<a id="Subclause_9.7.4"></a>

## 9.7.4  Asynchronous Transfer of Control

<MarginText>1_9.7.4</MarginText>
<p>[An asynchronous <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select_statement</a></code> provides asynchronous transfer of control upon completion of an entry call or the expiration of a delay.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2_9.7.4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>asynchronous{"_"}select</code><a id="S0280"></a><code> ::= </code><br />  <b>select</b><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0281">triggering_alternative</a></code><br />  <b>then abort</b><br />   <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code><br />  <b>end select</b>;<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_9.7.4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>triggering{"_"}alternative</code><a id="S0281"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering_statement</a></code> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/2_9.7.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>triggering{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0282"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0278">procedure_or_entry_call</a></code> | <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5_9.7.4</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>abortable{"_"}part</code><a id="S0283"></a><code> ::= </code><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code><br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6/2_9.7.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0278">procedure_or_entry_call</a></code>, the <i>entry{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, or <i>procedure{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code>, and actual parameters are evaluated as for a simple entry call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>) or procedure call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4">6.4</a>). If the call is an entry call or a call on a procedure implemented by an entry, the entry call is issued. If the entry call is queued (or requeued-with-abort), then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> is executed. [If the entry call is selected immediately, and never requeued-with-abort, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> is never started.] If the call is on a procedure that is not implemented by an entry, the call proceeds as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4">6.4</a>, followed by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0281">triggering{"_"}alternative</a></code>[; the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> is never started].<br /></p>

<MarginText>7_9.7.4</MarginText>
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code>, the <i>delay{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is evaluated and the expiration time is determined, as for a normal <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code>. If the expiration time has not already passed, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> is executed.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8_9.7.4</MarginText>
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> completes and is left prior to completion of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code>, an attempt to cancel the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code> is made. If the attempt to cancel succeeds (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6">9.6</a>), the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> is complete.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9_9.7.4</MarginText>
<p>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code> completes other than due to cancellation, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> is aborted (if started but not yet completed &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8">9.8</a>). If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code> completes normally, the optional <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0281">triggering{"_"}alternative</a></code> is executed after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> is left. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a_9.7.4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We currently don't specify when the by-copy [<b>in</b>] <b>out</b> parameters are assigned back into the actuals. We considered requiring that to happen after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> is left. However, that doesn't seem useful enough to justify possibly overspecifying the implementation approach, since some of the parameters are passed by reference anyway.<br />

<MarginText>9.b_9.7.4</MarginText>
In an earlier description, we required that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0281">triggering{"_"}alternative</a></code> execute after aborting the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code>, but before waiting for it to complete and finalize, to provide more rapid response to the triggering event in case the finalization was unbounded. However, various reviewers felt that this created unnecessary complexity in the description, and a potential for undesirable concurrency (and nondeterminism) within a single task. We have now reverted to simpler, more deterministic semantics, but anticipate that further discussion of this issue might be appropriate during subsequent reviews. One possibility is to leave this area implementation defined, so as to encourage experimentation. The user would then have to assume the worst about what kinds of actions are appropriate for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0281">triggering{"_"}alternative</a></code> to achieve portability. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>10_9.7.4</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a main command loop for a command interpreter:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>11_9.7.4</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
loop{"\n"}   select{"\n"}      Terminal.Wait{"_"}For{"_"}Interrupt;{"\n"}      Put{"_"}Line("Interrupted");{"\n"}   then abort{"\n"}      -- This will be abandoned upon terminal interrupt{"\n"}      Put{"_"}Line("-{">"} ");{"\n"}      Get{"_"}Line(Command, Last);{"\n"}      Process{"_"}Command(Command(1..Last));{"\n"}   end select;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12_9.7.4</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of a time-limited calculation:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5_9.7.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
select{"\n"}   delay 5.0;{"\n"}   Put{"_"}Line("Calculation does not converge");{"\n"}then abort{"\n"}   -- This calculation is expected to finish in 5.0 seconds;{"\n"}   --  if not, it is assumed to diverge.{"\n"}   Horribly{"_"}Complicated{"_"}Recursive{"_"}Function(X, Y);{"\n"}end select;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14/5_9.7.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0098-1", "AI12-0418-1"]} />
<p>Note that these examples presume that there are abort completion points (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8">9.8</a>) within the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>14.a_9.7.4</MarginText>
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">Asynchronous_select</a></code> is new. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>14.b/2_9.7.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
A procedure can be used as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>, if the procedure might actually be an entry. <br />

# 9.8. Abort of a Task - Abort of a Sequence of Statements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8.mdx

sidebar_position:  81

# 9.8. Abort of a Task - Abort of a Sequence of Statements

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> causes one or more tasks to become abnormal, thus preventing any further interaction with such tasks. The completion of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering{"_"}statement</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> causes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> to be aborted.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>abort{"_"}statement</code><a id="S0284"></a><code> ::= </code><b>abort</b> <i>task{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> {"{"}, <i>task{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"}"};<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>Each <i>task{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is expected to be of any task type[; each can be of a different task type.]<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>For the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code>, the given <i>task{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s are evaluated in an arbitrary order. Each named task is then <i>aborted</i>, which consists of making the task <i>abnormal</i> and aborting the execution of the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>, unless it is already completed. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that aborting those tasks is not defined to be an abort-deferred operation. Therefore, if one of the named tasks is the task executing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code>, or if the task executing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> depends on one of the named tasks, then it is possible for the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> to be aborted, thus leaving some of the tasks unaborted. This allows the implementation to use either a sequence of calls to an &ldquo;abort task&rdquo; run-time system primitive, or a single call to an &ldquo;abort list of tasks&rdquo; run-time system primitive. <br />

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>When the execution of a construct is <i>aborted</i> (including that of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task{"_"}body</a></code> or of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code>), the execution of every construct included within the aborted execution is also aborted, except for executions included within the execution of an <i>abort-deferred</i> operation; the execution of an abort-deferred operation continues to completion without being affected by the abort; the following are the abort-deferred operations: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a protected action;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<li>waiting for an entry call to complete (after having initiated the attempt to cancel it &mdash; see below);<br /></li>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<li>waiting for the termination of dependent tasks;<br /></li>
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<li>the execution of an Initialize procedure as the last step of the default initialization of a controlled object;<br /></li>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<li>the execution of a Finalize procedure as part of the finalization of a controlled object;<br /></li>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<li>an assignment operation to an object with a controlled part. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>[The last three of these are discussed further in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Deferring abort during Initialize and finalization allows, for example, the result of an allocator performed in an Initialize operation to be assigned into an access object without being interrupted in the middle, which would cause storage leaks. For an object with several controlled parts, each individual Initialize is abort-deferred. Note that there is generally no semantic difference between making each Finalize abort-deferred, versus making a group of them abort-deferred, because if the task gets aborted, the first thing it will do is complete any remaining finalizations. Individual objects are finalized prior to an assignment operation (if nonlimited controlled) and as part of Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation. <br />

<MarginText>12.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Abort is deferred during the entire assignment operation to an object with a controlled part, even if only some subcomponents are controlled. Note that this says "assignment operation", not "<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>". Explicit calls to Initialize, Finalize, or Adjust are not abort-deferred. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>When a master is aborted, all tasks that depend on that master are aborted.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>The order in which tasks become abnormal as the result of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> or the abort of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> is not specified by the language.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p>If the execution of an entry call is aborted, an immediate attempt is made to cancel the entry call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>). If the execution of a construct is aborted at a time when the execution is blocked, other than for an entry call, at a point that is outside the execution of an abort-deferred operation, then the execution of the construct completes immediately. For an abort due to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code>, these immediate effects occur before the execution of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> completes. Other than for these immediate cases, the execution of a construct that is aborted does not necessarily complete before the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> completes. However, the execution of the aborted construct completes no later than its next <i>abort completion point</i> (if any) that occurs outside of an abort-deferred operation; the following are abort completion points for an execution: <br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the point where the execution initiates the activation of another task;<br /></li>
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<li>the end of the activation of a task;<br /></li>
<MarginText>17.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<li>a point within a parallel construct where a new logical thread of control is created;<br /></li>
<MarginText>17.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<li>the end of a parallel construct;<br /></li>
<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<li>the start or end of the execution of an entry call, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>18.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Although the abort completion point doesn't occur until the end of the entry call or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code>, these operations might be cut short because an abort attempts to cancel them. <br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the start of the execution of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select_statement</a></code>, or of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence{"_"}of{"_"}statements</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>19.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The start of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.2#S0305">exception_handler</a></code> is considered an abort completion point simply because it is easy for an implementation to check at such points. <br />

<MarginText>19.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Implementations may of course check for abort more often than at each abort completion point; ideally, a fully preemptive implementation of abort will be provided. If preemptive abort is not supported in a given environment, then supporting the checking for abort as part of subprogram calls and loop iterations might be a useful option. <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>20/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>An attempt to execute an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> as part of the execution of an abort-deferred operation is a bounded error. Similarly, an attempt to create a task that depends on a master that is included entirely within the execution of an abort-deferred operation is a bounded error. In both cases, Program{"_"}Error is raised if the error is detected by the implementation; otherwise, the operations proceed as they would outside an abort-deferred operation, except that an abort of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> or the created task does not necessarily have an effect. <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> relies on an abort of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code> to effect the asynchronous transfer of control. For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> within an abort-deferred operation, the abort might have no effect.<br />

<MarginText>20.b</MarginText>
Creating a task dependent on a master included within an abort-deferred operation is considered an error, because such tasks could be aborted while the abort-deferred operation was still progressing, undermining the purpose of abort-deferral. Alternatively, we could say that such tasks are abort-deferred for their entire execution, but that seems too easy to abuse. Note that task creation is already a bounded error in protected actions, so this additional rule only applies to local task creation as part of Initialize, Finalize, or Adjust. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<p>If an assignment operation completes prematurely due to an abort, the assignment is said to be <i>disrupted</i>; the target of the assignment or its parts can become abnormal, and certain subsequent uses of the object can be erroneous, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9#Subclause_13.9.1">13.9.1</a>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 1   An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> is best used only in situations requiring unconditional termination.<br />

<MarginText>23</MarginText>
NOTE 2   A task is allowed to abort any task it can name, including itself.<br />

<MarginText>24/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0449-1"]} />
NOTE 3   Additional requirements associated with abort are given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.6">D.6</a>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>24.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause has been rewritten to accommodate the concept of aborting the execution of a construct, rather than just of a task. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>24.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
Added points within parallel constructs to the list of abort completion points. <br />

---

# 9.9. Task and Entry Attributes

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.9.mdx

sidebar_position:  82

# 9.9. Task and Entry Attributes

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> T that is of a task type [(after any implicit dereference)], the following attributes are defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>T'Callable</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Yields the value True when the task denoted by T is <i>callable</i>, and False otherwise; a task is callable unless it is completed or abnormal. The value of this attribute is of the predefined type Boolean.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>T'Terminated</dt>
<dd>Yields the value True if the task denoted by T is terminated, and False otherwise. The value of this attribute is of the predefined type Boolean. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> E that denotes an entry of a task or protected unit, the following attribute is defined. This attribute is only allowed within the body of the task or protected unit, but excluding, in the case of an entry of a task unit, within any program unit that is, itself, inner to the body of the task unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>E'Count</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Yields the number of calls presently queued on the entry E of the current instance of the unit. The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
NOTE 1   For the Count attribute, the entry can be either a single entry or an entry of a family. The name of the entry or entry family can be either a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> or an expanded name.<br />

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 2   Within task units, by interrogating the attribute E'Count an algorithm can allow for the increase of the value of this attribute for incoming entry calls, and its decrease, for example with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0276">timed_entry_call</a></code>s. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0279">conditional_entry_call</a></code> can also briefly increase this value, even if the conditional call is not accepted.<br />

<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 3   Within protected units, by interrogating the attribute E'Count in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> for the entry E an algorithm can allow for the evaluation of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of the barrier both before and after queuing a given caller. <br />

# 9. Tasks and Synchronization

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.mdx

sidebar_position:  73

# 9. Tasks and Synchronization

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0330-1"]} />
<p>The execution of an Ada program consists of the execution of one or more <i>tasks</i>. Each task represents a separable activity that proceeds independently and concurrently between the points where it <i>interacts</i> with other tasks. A single task, when within the context of a parallel construct, can represent multiple <i>logical threads of control</i> which can proceed in parallel; in other contexts, each task represents one logical thread of control. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The execution of an Ada program consists of the execution of one or more partitions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>), each of which in turn consists of the execution of an environment task and zero or more subtasks. <br />

<MarginText>1.b/5</MarginText>
<b>Term entry: </b><b>logical thread of control</b> &mdash; activity within the execution of a program that can proceed in parallel with other activities of the same task, or of separate tasks<br />

<MarginText>1.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<p>The various forms of task interaction are described in this clause, and include:<br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the activation and termination of a task;<br /></li>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<li>a call on a protected subprogram of a <i>protected object</i>, providing exclusive read-write access, or concurrent read-only access to shared data;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<li>a call on an entry, either of another task, allowing for synchronous communication with that task, or of a protected object, allowing for asynchronous communication with one or more other tasks using that same protected object;<br /></li>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<li>a timed operation, including a simple delay statement, a timed entry call or accept, or a timed asynchronous select statement (see next item);<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>an asynchronous transfer of control as part of an asynchronous select statement, where a task stops what it is doing and begins execution at a different point in response to the completion of an entry call or the expiration of a delay;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<li>an abort statement, allowing one task to cause the termination of another task. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>In addition, tasks can communicate indirectly by reading and updating (unprotected) shared variables, presuming the access is properly synchronized through some other kind of task interaction.<br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>The properties of a task are defined by a corresponding task declaration and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0248">task_body</a></code>, which together define a program unit called a <i>task unit</i>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<p>Over time, tasks proceed through various <i>states</i>. A task is initially <i>inactive</i>; upon activation, and prior to its <i>termination</i> it is either <i>blocked</i> (as part of some task interaction) or <i>ready</i> to run. While ready, a task competes for the available <i>execution resources</i> that it requires to run. In the context of a parallel construct, a single task can utilize multiple processing resources simultaneously. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The means for selecting which of the ready tasks to run, given the currently available execution resources, is determined by the <i>task dispatching policy</i> in effect, which is generally implementation defined, but may be controlled by aspects, pragmas, and operations defined in the Real-Time Annex (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2">D.2</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5">D.5</a>). <br />

<MarginText>11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE   Concurrent task execution can be implemented on multicomputers, multiprocessors, or with interleaved execution on a single physical processor. On the other hand, whenever an implementation can determine that the required semantic effects can be achieved when parts of the execution of a single logical thread of control are performed by different physical processors acting in parallel, it can choose to perform them in this way.<br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
The introduction has been rewritten.<br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
We use the term "concurrent" rather than "parallel" when talking about logically independent execution of threads of control. The term "parallel" is reserved for referring to the situation where multiple physical processors run simultaneously. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>11.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
Rewrote the introduction to emphasize that threads of control can be generated by parallel constructs as well as tasks. <br />

---

# A.1. The Package Standard

# A.1. The Package Standard

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>This subclause outlines the specification of the package Standard containing all predefined identifiers in the language. The corresponding package body is not specified by the language.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The operators that are predefined for the types declared in the package Standard are given in comments since they are implicitly declared. Italics are used for pseudo-names of anonymous types (such as <i>root{"_"}real</i>) and for undefined information (such as <i>implementation-defined</i>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>All of the predefined operators are of convention Intrinsic. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The library package Standard has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The names and characteristics of the numeric subtypes declared in the visible part of package Standard.<br />

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0414-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Standard{"\n"}   with Pure is{"\n"}
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
   type Boolean is (False, True);{"\n"}
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
   -- The predefined relational operators for this type are as follows:{"\n"}
<MarginText>7/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00145-01"]} />
{"{"}8652/0028{"}"}    -- function "="   (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "/="  (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{"<"}"   (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{"<"}="  (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{">"}"   (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{">"}="  (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
   -- The predefined logical operators and the predefined logical{"\n"}   -- negation operator are as follows:{"\n"}
<MarginText>9/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00145-01"]} />
{"{"}8652/0028{"}"}    -- function "and" (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "or"  (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "xor" (Left, Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean'Base;{"\n"}
<MarginText>10/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00145-01"]} />
{"{"}8652/0028{"}"}    -- function "not" (Right : Boolean'Base) return Boolean'Base;{"\n"}
<MarginText>11/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
   -- The integer type root{"_"}integer and the{"\n"}   -- corresponding universal type universal{"_"}integer are predefined.{"\n"}
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
   type Integer is range implementation-defined;{"\n"}
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
   subtype Natural  is Integer range 0 .. Integer'Last;{"\n"}   subtype Positive is Integer range 1 .. Integer'Last;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
   -- The predefined operators for type Integer are as follows:{"\n"}
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
   -- function "="  (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "/=" (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{"<"}"  (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{"<"}=" (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{">"}"  (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}   -- function "{">"}=" (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
   -- function "+"   (Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "-"   (Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "abs" (Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
   -- function "+"   (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "-"   (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "{"*"}"   (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "/"   (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "rem" (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}   -- function "mod" (Left, Right : Integer'Base) return Integer'Base;{"\n"}
<MarginText>18</MarginText>
   -- function "{"*"}{"*"}"  (Left : Integer'Base; Right : Natural){"\n"}   --                  return Integer'Base;{"\n"}
<MarginText>19</MarginText>
   -- The specification of each operator for the type{"\n"}   -- root{"_"}integer, or for any additional predefined integer{"\n"}   -- type, is obtained by replacing Integer by the name of the type{"\n"}   -- in the specification of the corresponding operator of the type{"\n"}   -- Integer. The right operand of the exponentiation operator{"\n"}   -- remains as subtype Natural.{"\n"}
