<MarginText>85.2/5_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1", "AI05-0265-1", "AI05-0269-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Iterate returns an iterator object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.1">5.5.1</a>) that will generate a value for a loop parameter (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>) designating each element in Container, starting with the first element and moving the cursor according to the successor relation when used as a forward iterator, and processing all nodes concurrently when used as a parallel iterator. Tampering with the cursors of Container is prohibited while the iterator object exists (in particular, in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> denotes this object). The iterator object needs finalization.<br /></p>

<MarginText>86/2_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>For any element <i>E</i>, the actual function for the generic formal function Generic{"_"}Keys.Hash is expected to be such that Hash (<i>E</i>) = Generic{"_"}Keys.Hash (Key (<i>E</i>)). If the actuals for Key or Generic{"_"}Keys.Hash behave in some other manner, the behavior of Generic{"_"}Keys is unspecified. Which subprograms of Generic{"_"}Keys call Generic{"_"}Keys.Hash, and how many times they call it, is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>87/2_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>For any two elements <i>E1</i> and <i>E2</i>, the boolean values Equivalent{"_"}Elements (<i>E1</i>, <i>E2</i>) and Equivalent{"_"}Keys (Key (<i>E1</i>), Key (<i>E2</i>)) are expected to be equal. If the actuals for Key or Equivalent{"_"}Keys behave in some other manner, the behavior of Generic{"_"}Keys is unspecified. Which subprograms of Generic{"_"}Keys call Equivalent{"_"}Keys, and how many times they call it, is unspecified.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>88/2_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>If <i>N</i> is the length of a set, the average time complexity of the subprograms Insert, Include, Replace, Delete, Exclude, and Find that take an element parameter should be <i>O</i>(log <i>N</i>). The average time complexity of the subprograms that take a cursor parameter should be <i>O</i>(1). The average time complexity of Reserve{"_"}Capacity should be <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>88.a/2_A.18.8</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The average time complexity of the Insert, Include, Replace, Delete, Exclude, and Find operations of Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets that take an element parameter should be <i>O</i>(log <i>N</i>). The average time complexity of the subprograms of Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets that take a cursor parameter should be <i>O</i>(1). The average time complexity of Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets.Reserve{"_"}Capacity should be <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>).<br />

<MarginText>88.b/2_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.5">A.18.5</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.5">The Generic Package Containers.Hashed_Maps</a>&rdquo; for implementation notes regarding some of the operations of this package. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>88.c/2_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
The generic package Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets is new. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>88.d/3_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
Subprograms Assign and Copy are added to Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets. If an instance of Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets is referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, and an entity <i>E</i> with the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> as a new entity in Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets is defined in a package that is also referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, the entity <i>E</i> may no longer be use-visible, resulting in errors. This should be rare and is easily fixed if it does occur. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>88.e/3_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
Added iterator and indexing support to make hashed set containers more convenient to use. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>88.f/3_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0044-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording to require the formal function be such that equal elements are also equivalent.<br />

<MarginText>88.g/3_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0084-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a pragma Remote{"_"}Types so that containers can be used in distributed programs. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>88.h/5_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1", "AI12-0339-1"]} />
A number of new subprograms, types, and even a nested package were added to Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets to better support contracts and stable views. Therefore, a use clause conflict is possible; see the introduction of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a> for more on this topic. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>88.i/5_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0212-1"]} />
Sets now support positional container aggregates, so <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0106">aggregate</a></code> syntax can be used to create Sets.<br />

<MarginText>88.j/5_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0266-1"]} />
The iterator for the container now can return a parallel iterator which can be used to process the container in parallel. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>88.k/5_A.18.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
Added contracts to this container. This includes describing some of the semantics with pre- and postconditions, rather than English text. Note that the preconditions can be Suppressed (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.5">11.5</a>). <br />

<MarginText>78/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>Two elements <i>E1</i> and <i>E2</i> are <i>equivalent</i> if both <i>E1</i> {"<"} <i>E2</i> and <i>E2</i> {"<"} <i>E1</i> return False, using the generic formal "{"<"}" operator for elements. Function Equivalent{"_"}Elements returns True if Left and Right are equivalent, and False otherwise.<br /></p>

<MarginText>79/3_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03", "AI05-0044-1"]} />
<p>The actual function for the generic formal function "{"<"}" on Element{"_"}Type values is expected to return the same value each time it is called with a particular pair of key values. It should define a strict weak ordering relationship (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>). If the actual for "{"<"}" behaves in some other manner, the behavior of this package is unspecified. Which subprograms of this package call "{"<"}" and how many times they call it, is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>79.1/3_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0044-1"]} />
<p>If the actual function for the generic formal function "=" returns True for any pair of nonequivalent elements, then the behavior of the container function "=" is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>80/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>If the value of an element stored in a set is changed other than by an operation in this package such that at least one of "{"<"}" or "=" give different results, the behavior of this package is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>80.a/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.6">A.18.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.6">The Generic Package Containers.Ordered_Maps</a>&rdquo; for a suggested implementation, and for justification of the restrictions regarding "{"<"}" and "=". Note that sets only need to store elements, not key/element pairs. <br />

<MarginText>81/3_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>The <i>first element</i> of a nonempty set is the one which is less than all the other elements in the set. The <i>last element</i> of a nonempty set is the one which is greater than all the other elements in the set. The <i>successor</i> of an element is the smallest element that is larger than the given element. The <i>predecessor</i> of an element is the largest element that is smaller than the given element. All comparisons are done using the generic formal "{"<"}" operator for elements.<br /></p>

<MarginText>81.1/5_A.18.9</MarginText>

<MarginText>114/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>For any two elements <i>E1</i> and <i>E2</i>, the boolean values (<i>E1</i> {"<"} <i>E2</i>) and (Key(<i>E1</i>) {"<"} Key(<i>E2</i>)) are expected to be equal. If the actuals for Key or Generic{"_"}Keys."{"<"}" behave in some other manner, the behavior of this package is unspecified. Which subprograms of this package call Key and Generic{"_"}Keys."{"<"}", and how many times the functions are called, is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>115/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>In addition to the semantics described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.7">A.18.7</a>, the subprograms in package Generic{"_"}Keys named Floor and Ceiling, are equivalent to the corresponding subprograms in the parent package, with the difference that the Key subprogram parameter is compared to elements in the container using the Key and "{"<"}" generic formal functions. The function named Equivalent{"_"}Keys in package Generic{"_"}Keys returns True if both Left {"<"} Right and Right {"<"} Left return False using the generic formal "{"<"}" operator, and returns True otherwise.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>116/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>If <i>N</i> is the length of a set, then the worst-case time complexity of the Insert, Include, Replace, Delete, Exclude, and Find operations that take an element parameter should be <i>O</i>((log <i>N</i>){"*"}{"*"}2) or better. The worst-case time complexity of the subprograms that take a cursor parameter should be <i>O</i>(1). <br /></p>

<MarginText>116.a/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The worst-case time complexity of the Insert, Include, Replace, Delete, Exclude, and Find operations of Containers.Ordered{"_"}Sets that take an element parameter should be <i>O</i>((log <i>N</i>){"*"}{"*"}2). The worst-case time complexity of the subprograms of Containers.Ordered{"_"}Sets that take a cursor parameter should be <i>O</i>(1).<br />

<MarginText>116.b/2_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.6">A.18.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.6">The Generic Package Containers.Ordered_Maps</a>&rdquo; for implementation notes regarding some of the operations of this package. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>116.d/3_A.18.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
Subprograms Assign and Copy are added to Containers.Ordered{"_"}Sets. If an instance of Containers.Ordered{"_"}Sets is referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, and an entity <i>E</i> with the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> as a new entity in Containers.Ordered{"_"}Sets is defined in a package that is also referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, the entity <i>E</i> may no longer be use-visible, resulting in errors. This should be rare and is easily fixed if it does occur. <br />

<a id="Subclause_A.18.10"></a>

## A.18.10  The Generic Package Containers.Multiway_Trees

<MarginText>1/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees provides private types Tree and Cursor, and a set of operations for each type. A multiway tree container is well-suited to represent nested structures.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This tree just provides a basic structure, and make no promises about balancing or other automatic organization. In this sense, it is different than the indexed (Map, Set) forms. Rather, it provides a building block on which to construct more complex and more specialized tree containers. <br />

<MarginText>2/4_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI12-0078-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<p>A multiway tree container object manages a tree of <i>nodes</i>, consisting of a <i>root node</i> and a set of <i>internal nodes</i>; each internal node contains an element and pointers to the parent, first child, last child, next (successor) sibling, and previous (predecessor) sibling internal nodes. A cursor designates a particular node within a tree (and by extension the element contained in that node, if any). A cursor keeps designating the same node (and element) as long as the node is part of the container, even if the node is moved within the container.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/4_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0269-1", "AI12-0078-1"]} />
<p>A <i>subtree</i> is a particular node (which <i>roots the subtree</i>) and all of its child nodes (including all of the children of the child nodes, recursively). The root node is always present and has neither an associated element value nor any parent node; it has pointers to its first child and its last child, if any. The root node provides a place to add nodes to an otherwise empty tree and represents the base of the tree.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>A node that has no children is called a <i>leaf node</i>. The <i>ancestors</i> of a node are the node itself, its parent node, the parent of the parent node, and so on until a node with no parent is reached. Similarly, the <i>descendants</i> of a node are the node itself, its child nodes, the children of each child node, and so on.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>The nodes of a subtree can be visited in several different orders. For a <i>depth-first order</i>, after visiting a node, the nodes of its child list are each visited in depth-first order, with each child node visited in natural order (first child to last child).<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For the depth-first order, when each child node is visited, the child list of the child node is visited before the next sibling of the child node is visited. <br />

<MarginText>72/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>The actual function for the generic formal function "=" on Element{"_"}Type values is expected to define a reflexive and symmetric relationship and return the same result value each time it is called with a particular pair of values. If it behaves in some other manner, the functions Find, Reverse{"_"}Find, Equal{"_"}Subtree, and "=" on tree values return an unspecified value. The exact arguments and number of calls of this generic formal function by the functions Find, Reverse{"_"}Find, Equal{"_"}Subtree, and "=" on tree values are unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>73/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>The type Tree is used to represent trees. The type Tree needs finalization (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>74/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p>Empty{"_"}Tree represents the empty Tree object. It contains only the root node (Node{"_"}Count (Empty{"_"}Tree) returns 1). If an object of type Tree is not otherwise initialized, it is initialized to the same value as Empty{"_"}Tree.<br /></p>

<MarginText>75/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>No{"_"}Element represents a cursor that designates no element. If an object of type Cursor is not otherwise initialized, it is initialized to the same value as No{"_"}Element.<br /></p>

<MarginText>76/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI12-0434-1"]} />
<p>The primitive "=" operator for type Cursor returns True if both cursors are No{"_"}Element, or designate the same element in the same container.<br /></p>

<MarginText>76.a/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0434-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>&ldquo;The primitive "=" operator&rdquo; is the one with two parameters of type Cursor which returns Boolean. We're not talking about some other (hidden) primitive function named "=". <br />

<MarginText>77/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>Execution of the default implementation of the Input, Output, Read, or Write attribute of type Cursor raises Program{"_"}Error.<br /></p>

<MarginText>78/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0437-1"]} />
<p>Tree'Write for a Tree object <i>T</i> writes Node{"_"}Count(<i>T</i>) - 1 elements of the tree to the stream. It may also write additional information about the tree.<br /></p>

<MarginText>79/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>Tree'Read reads the representation of a tree from the stream, and assigns to <i>Item</i> a tree with the same elements and structure as was written by Tree'Write.<br /></p>

<MarginText>79.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Streaming more elements than the container holds is wrong. For implementation implications of this rule, see the Implementation Note in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a>. <br />

<MarginText>80/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<p>[Some operations check for &ldquo;tampering with cursors&rdquo; of a container because they depend on the set of elements of the container remaining constant, and others check for &ldquo;tampering with elements&rdquo; of a container because they depend on elements of the container not being replaced.] When tampering with cursors is <i>prohibited</i> for a particular tree object <i>T</i>, Program{"_"}Error is propagated by the finalization of <i>T</i>[, as well as by a call that passes <i>T</i> to certain of the operations of this package, as indicated by the precondition of such an operation]. Similarly, when tampering with elements is <i>prohibited</i> for <i>T</i>, Program{"_"}Error is propagated by a call that passes <i>T</i> to certain of the other operations of this package, as indicated by the precondition of such an operation.<br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraphs 81 through 90 are removed as preconditions now describe these rules.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>85.a.1/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We don't need to explicitly mention <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>, because that finalizes the target object as part of the operation, and finalization of an object is already defined as tampering with cursors. <br />

<MarginText>93/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Equal{"_"}Subtree (Left{"_"}Position : Cursor;{"\n"}                        Right{"_"}Position: Cursor) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>94/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Left{"_"}Position or Right{"_"}Position equals No{"_"}Element, propagates Constraint{"_"}Error. If the number of child nodes of the element designated by Left{"_"}Position is different from the number of child nodes of the element designated by Right{"_"}Position, the function returns False. If Left{"_"}Position designates a root node and Right{"_"}Position does not, the function returns False. If Right{"_"}Position designates a root node and Left{"_"}Position does not, the function returns False. Unless both cursors designate a root node, the elements are compared using the generic formal equality operator. If the result of the element comparison is False, the function returns False. Otherwise, it calls Equal{"_"}Subtree on a cursor designating each child element of the element designated by Left{"_"}Position and a cursor designating the corresponding child element of the element designated by Right{"_"}Position. If any such call returns False, the function returns False; otherwise, it returns True. Any exception raised during the evaluation of element equality is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>94.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Left{"_"}Position and Right{"_"}Position do not need to be from the same tree. <br />

<MarginText>94.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This wording describes the canonical semantics. However, the order and number of calls on the formal equality function is unspecified for all of the operations that use it in this package, so an implementation can call it as many or as few times as it needs to get the correct answer. Similarly, a global rule (see the introduction of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a>) says that language-defined routines are not affected by overriding of other language-defined routines. This means that no reasonable program can tell how many times Equal{"_"}Subtree is called, and thus an implementation can call it as many or as few times as it needs to get the correct answer. Specifically, there is no requirement to call the formal equality or Equal{"_"}Subtree additional times once the answer has been determined. <br />

<MarginText>95/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "=" (Left, Right : Tree) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>96/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Left and Right denote the same tree object, then the function returns True. Otherwise, it calls Equal{"_"}Subtree with cursors designating the root nodes of Left and Right; the result is returned. Any exception raised during the evaluation of Equal{"_"}Subtree is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>96.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Similar considerations apply here as apply to Equal{"_"}Subtree. The actual number of calls performed is unspecified. <br />

<MarginText>96.1/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited{"\n"}   (Container : Tree) return Boolean{"\n"}   with Nonblocking, Global ={">"} null, Use{"_"}Formal ={">"} null;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>96.2/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns True if tampering with cursors or tampering with elements is currently prohibited for Container, and returns False otherwise.<br /></p>

<MarginText>96.b/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Prohibiting tampering with elements also needs to prohibit tampering with cursors, as deleting an element is similar to replacing it. <br />

<MarginText>96.c/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Various contracts elsewhere in this specification require that this function be implemented with synchronized data. Moreover, it is possible for tampering to be prohibited by multiple operations (sequentially or in parallel). Therefore, tampering needs to be implemented with an atomic or protected counter. The counter is initialized to zero, and is incremented when tampering is prohibited, and decremented when leaving an area that prohibited tampering. Function Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited returns True if the counter is nonzero. (Note that any case where the result is not well-defined for one task is incorrect use of shared variables and would be erroneous by the rules of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10">9.10</a>, so no special protection is needed to read the counter.) <br />

procedure Move (Target : in out Tree;{"\n"}                Source : in out Tree){"\n"}   with Pre  ={">"} (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited (Target){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error) and then{"\n"}                (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited (Source){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error),{"\n"}        Post ={">"} (if not Target'Has{"_"}Same{"_"}Storage (Source) then{"\n"}               Node{"_"}Count (Target) = Node{"_"}Count (Source'Old) and then{"\n"}               Node{"_"}Count (Source) = 1);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>137/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Target denotes the same object as Source, then the operation has no effect. Otherwise, Move first calls Clear (Target). Then, the nodes other than the root node in Source are moved to Target (in the same positions). After Move completes, Node{"_"}Count (Target) is the number of nodes originally in Source, and Node{"_"}Count (Source) is 1.<br /></p>

<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Delete{"_"}Leaf (Container : in out Tree;{"\n"}                       Position  : in out Cursor){"\n"}   with Pre  ={">"} (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited (Container){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error) and then{"\n"}                (Position /= No{"_"}Element {"\n"}                   or else raise Constraint{"_"}Error) and then{"\n"}                (Has{"_"}Element (Container, Position){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error) and then{"\n"}                (Is{"_"}Leaf (Container, Position){"\n"}                   or else raise Constraint{"_"}Error),{"\n"}        Post ={">"}{"\n"}           Node{"_"}Count (Container)'Old = Node{"_"}Count (Container) + 1 and then{"\n"}           Position = No{"_"}Element;{"\n"}

<MarginText>139.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The check on Position checks that the cursor does not belong to some other Container. This check implies that a reference to the container is included in the cursor value. This wording is not meant to require detection of dangling cursors; such cursors are defined to be invalid, which means that execution is erroneous, and any result is allowed (including not raising an exception).<br />

<MarginText>139.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
The root node cannot be deleted. <br />

<MarginText>143/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Swap exchanges the values of the elements designated by I and J.<br /></p>

<MarginText>143.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>After a call to Swap, I designates the element value previously designated by J, and J designates the element value previously designated by I. The position of the elements do not change; for instance, the parent node and the first child node of I are unchanged by the operation.<br />

<MarginText>143.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
The root nodes do not contain element values, so they cannot be swapped. <br />

<MarginText>143.c/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>The implementation is not required to actually copy the elements if it can do the swap some other way. But it is allowed to copy the elements if needed. <br />

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>153/4_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0265-1", "AI12-0069-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Iterate calls Process.<b>all</b> with a cursor that designates each element in Container, starting from the root node and proceeding in a depth-first order. Tampering with the cursors of Container is prohibited during the execution of a call on Process.<b>all</b>. Any exception raised by Process.<b>all</b> is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>153.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Process is not called with the root node, which does not have an associated element. <br />

<MarginText>153.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The purpose of the tamper with cursors check is to prevent erroneous execution from the Position parameter of Process.<b>all</b> becoming invalid. This check takes place when the operations that tamper with the cursors of the container are called. The check cannot be made later (say in the body of Iterate), because that could cause the Position cursor to be invalid and potentially cause execution to become erroneous &mdash; defeating the purpose of the check.<br />

<MarginText>153.c/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
See Iterate for vectors (<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a>) for a suggested implementation of the check. <br />

<MarginText>177/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Source is equal to No{"_"}Element, then the operation has no effect. Otherwise, the subtree rooted by Source (which can be from any tree; it does not have to be a subtree of Target) is copied (new nodes are allocated to create a new subtree with the same structure as the Source subtree, with each element initialized from the corresponding element of the Source subtree) and inserted into Target as a child of Parent. If Parent already has child nodes, then the new nodes are inserted prior to the node designated by Before, or, if Before equals No{"_"}Element, the new nodes are inserted after the last existing child node of Parent. The parent of the newly created subtree is set to Parent, and the overall count of Target is incremented by Subtree{"_"}Node{"_"}Count (Source). Any exception raised during allocation of internal storage is propagated, and Container is not modified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>177.a/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We only need one routine here, as the source object is not modified, so we can use the same routine for both copying within and between containers. However, that requires a contract that allows reading of any container of the correct type, so we provide two other routines wuth more restrictive contracts. <br />

<MarginText>179.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We can't allow moving the subtree of Position to a proper descendant node of the subtree, as the descendant node will be part of the subtree being moved. The result would be a circularly linked tree, or one with inaccessible nodes. Thus we have to check Position against Parent, even though such a check is <i>O</i>(Depth(Source)). <br />

<MarginText>180/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Otherwise (if Source does not denote the same object as Target), the subtree designated by Position is removed from Source and moved to Target. The subtree is inserted as a child of Parent. If Parent already has child nodes, then the moved nodes are inserted prior to the node designated by Before, or, if Before equals No{"_"}Element, the moved nodes are inserted after the last existing child node of Parent. In each of these cases, the count of Target is incremented by Subtree{"_"}Node{"_"}Count (Position), and the count of Source is decremented by Subtree{"_"}Node{"_"}Count (Position), Position is updated to represent an element in Target.<br /></p>

<MarginText>180.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If Source is the same as Target, and Position = Before, or Next{"_"}Sibling(Position) = Before, Splice{"_"}Subtree has no effect, as the subtree does not have to move to meet the postcondition.<br />

<MarginText>180.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
We do not allow splicing a subtree that includes a root node, as that would require inserting a node with no value in the middle of the target tree. Splice the children of the root node instead.<br />

<MarginText>180.c/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
For this reason there is no operation to splice an entire tree, as that would necessarily involve splicing a root node. <br />

<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1", "AI05-0265-1", "AI12-0112-1", "AI12-0266-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Iterate{"_"}Children returns an iterator object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.1">5.5.1</a>) that will generate a value for a loop parameter (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.2">5.5.2</a>) designating each child node of Parent. When used as a forward iterator, the nodes are designated starting with the first child node and moving the cursor as per the function Next{"_"}Sibling; when used as a reverse iterator, the nodes are designated starting with the last child node and moving the cursor as per the function Previous{"_"}Sibling; when used as a parallel iterator, processing all child nodes concurrently. Tampering with the cursors of Container is prohibited while the iterator object exists (in particular, in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0178">loop_statement</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#S0183">iterator_specification</a></code> denotes this object). The iterator object needs finalization.<br /></p>

<MarginText>219.1/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<p>The nested package Multiway{"_"}Trees.Stable provides a type Stable.Tree that represents a <i>stable</i> tree, which is one that cannot grow and shrink. Such a tree can be created by calling the Copy function, or by establishing a <i>stabilized view</i> of an ordinary tree.<br /></p>

<MarginText>219.2/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<p>The subprograms of package Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees that have a parameter or result of type tree are included in the nested package Stable with the same specification, except that the following are omitted:<br /></p>

<MarginText>219.3/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited, Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited, Assign, Move, Clear, Delete{"_"}Leaf, Insert{"_"}Child, Delete{"_"}Children, Delete{"_"}Subtree, Copy{"_"}Subtree, Copy{"_"}Local{"_"}Subtree, Splice{"_"}Subtree, and Splice{"_"}Children <br /></p>

<MarginText>219.a.1/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The names Tree and Cursor mean the types declared in the nested package in these subprogram specifications. <br />

<MarginText>219.a.2/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The omitted routines are those that tamper with cursors or elements (or test that state). The model is that it is impossible to tamper with cursors or elements of a stable view since no such operations are included. Thus tampering checks are not needed for a stable view, and we omit the operations associated with those checks. <br />

<MarginText>219.4/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<p>The operations of this package are equivalent to those for ordinary trees, except that the calls to Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited and Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited that occur in preconditions are replaced by False, and any that occur in postconditions are replaced by True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>219.5/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>If a stable tree is declared with the Base discriminant designating a pre-existing ordinary tree, the stable tree represents a stabilized view of the underlying ordinary tree, and any operation on the stable tree is reflected on the underlying ordinary tree. While a stabilized view exists, any operation that tampers with elements performed on the underlying tree is prohibited. The finalization of a stable tree that provides such a view removes this restriction on the underlying ordinary tree [(though some other restriction can exist due to other concurrent iterations or stabilized views)].<br /></p>

<MarginText>219.6/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0438-1"]} />
<p>If a stable tree is declared without specifying Base, the object is necessarily initialized. The initializing expression of the stable tree, [typically a call on Copy], determines the Node{"_"}Count of the tree. The Node{"_"}Count of a stable tree never changes after initialization.<br /></p>

<MarginText>219.a/5_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0438-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Initialization is required as the type is indefinite, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#Subclause_3.3.1">3.3.1</a>. <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>220/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error for the actual function associated with a generic formal subprogram, when called as part of an operation of this package, to tamper with elements of any Tree parameter of the operation. Either Program{"_"}Error is raised, or the operation works as defined on the value of the Tree either prior to, or subsequent to, some or all of the modifications to the Tree.<br /></p>

<MarginText>221/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error to call any subprogram declared in the visible part of Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees when the associated container has been finalized. If the operation takes Container as an <b>in out</b> parameter, then it raises Constraint{"_"}Error or Program{"_"}Error. Otherwise, the operation either proceeds as it would for an empty container, or it raises Constraint{"_"}Error or Program{"_"}Error. <br /></p>

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>222/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>A Cursor value is <i>invalid</i> if any of the following have occurred since it was created: <br /></p>

<MarginText>223/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The tree that contains the element it designates has been finalized;<br /></li>
<MarginText>224/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<li>The tree that contains the element it designates has been used as the Source or Target of a call to Move;<br /></li>
<MarginText>225/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<li>The tree that contains the element it designates has been used as the Target of a call to Assign or the target of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>226/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<li>The element it designates has been removed from the tree that previously contained the element. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>226.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We talk about which tree the element was removed from in order to handle splicing nodes from one tree to another. The node still exists, but any cursors that designate it in the original tree are now invalid. This bullet covers removals caused by calls to Clear, Delete{"_"}Leaf, Delete{"_"}Subtree, Delete{"_"}Children, Splice{"_"}Children, and Splice{"_"}Subtree. <br />

<MarginText>227/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<p>The result of "=" or Has{"_"}Element is unspecified if it is called with an invalid cursor parameter. Execution is erroneous if any other subprogram declared in Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees is called with an invalid cursor parameter.<br /></p>

<MarginText>227.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The list above is intended to be exhaustive. In other cases, a cursor value continues to designate its original element (or the root node). For instance, cursor values survive the insertion and deletion of other nodes.<br />

<MarginText>227.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
While it is possible to check for these cases, in many cases the overhead necessary to make the check is substantial in time or space. Implementations are encouraged to check for as many of these cases as possible and raise Program{"_"}Error if detected. <br />

<MarginText>228/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
<p>Execution is erroneous if the tree associated with the result of a call to Reference or Constant{"_"}Reference is finalized before the result object returned by the call to Reference or Constant{"_"}Reference is finalized. <br /></p>

<MarginText>228.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Each object of Reference{"_"}Type and Constant{"_"}Reference{"_"}Type probably contains some reference to the originating container. If that container is prematurely finalized (which is only possible via Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation, as accessibility checks prevent passing a container to Reference that will not live as long as the result), the finalization of the object of Reference{"_"}Type will try to access a nonexistent object. This is a normal case of a dangling pointer created by Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation; we have to explicitly mention it here as the pointer in question is not visible in the specification of the type. (This is the same reason we have to say this for invalid cursors.) <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>229/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>No storage associated with a multiway tree object shall be lost upon assignment or scope exit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>230/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>The execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> for a tree shall have the effect of copying the elements from the source tree object to the target tree object and changing the node count of the target object to that of the source object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>230.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0298-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>An assignment of a Tree is a &ldquo;deep&rdquo; copy; that is the elements are copied as well the data structures. We say &ldquo;effect of&rdquo; in order to allow the implementation to avoid copying elements immediately if it wishes. For instance, an implementation that avoided copying until one of the containers is modified would be allowed. (Note that this implementation would require care, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a> for more.) <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>231/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees should be implemented similarly to a multiway tree. In particular, if <i>N</i> is the overall number of nodes for a particular tree, then the worst-case time complexity of Element, Parent, First{"_"}Child, Last{"_"}Child, Next{"_"}Sibling, Previous{"_"}Sibling, Insert{"_"}Child with Count=1, and Delete should be <i>O</i>(log <i>N</i>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>231.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The worst-case time complexity of the Element, Parent, First{"_"}Child, Last{"_"}Child, Next{"_"}Sibling, Previous{"_"}Sibling, Insert{"_"}Child with Count=1, and Delete operations of Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees should be <i>O</i>(log <i>N</i>).<br />

<MarginText>231.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We do not mean to overly constrain implementation strategies here. However, it is important for portability that the performance of large containers has roughly the same factors on different implementations. If a program is moved to an implementation that takes <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>) time to access elements, that program could be unusable when the trees are large. We allow <i>O</i>(log <i>N</i>) access because the proportionality constant and caching effects are likely to be larger than the log factor, and we don't want to discourage innovative implementations. <br />

<MarginText>232/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>Move should not copy elements, and should minimize copying of internal data structures. <br /></p>

<MarginText>232.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees.Move should not copy elements, and should minimize copying of internal data structures.<br />

<MarginText>232.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Usually that can be accomplished simply by moving the pointer(s) to the internal data structures from the Source container to the Target container. <br />

<MarginText>233/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0136-1"]} />
<p>If an exception is propagated from a tree operation, no storage should be lost, nor any elements removed from a tree unless specified by the operation. <br /></p>

<MarginText>233.a/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If an exception is propagated from a tree operation, no storage should be lost, nor any elements removed from a tree unless specified by the operation.<br />

<MarginText>233.b/3_A.18.10</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is important so that programs can recover from errors. But we don't want to require heroic efforts, so we just require documentation of cases where this can't be accomplished. <br />

The generic package Containers.Multiway{"_"}Trees is new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_A.18.11"></a>

## A.18.11  The Generic Package Containers.Indefinite_Vectors

<MarginText>1/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Vectors provides a private type Vector and a set of operations. It provides the same operations as the package Containers.Vectors (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a>), with the difference that the generic formal Element{"_"}Type is indefinite. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/3_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03", "AI05-0092-1"]} />
<p>The declaration of the generic library package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Vectors has the same contents and semantics as Containers.Vectors except:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The generic formal Element{"_"}Type is indefinite.<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<li>The procedures with the profiles: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Insert (Container : in out Vector;{"\n"}                  Before    : in     Extended{"_"}Index;{"\n"}                  Count     : in     Count{"_"}Type := 1);{"\n"}
<MarginText>6/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
procedure Insert (Container : in out Vector;{"\n"}                  Before    : in     Cursor;{"\n"}                  Position  :    out Cursor;{"\n"}                  Count     : in     Count{"_"}Type := 1);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>are omitted.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>These procedures are omitted because there is no way to create a default-initialized object of an indefinite type. Note that Insert{"_"}Space can be used instead of this routine in most cases. Omitting the routine completely allows any problems to be diagnosed by the compiler when converting from a definite to indefinite vector. <br />

<MarginText>8/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The actual Element parameter of access subprogram Process of Update{"_"}Element may be constrained even if Element{"_"}Type is unconstrained.<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/4_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0035-1"]} />
<li>The operations "&", Append, Insert, Prepend, Replace{"_"}Element, and To{"_"}Vector that have a formal parameter of type Element{"_"}Type perform indefinite insertion (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>).<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/5_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<li>The description of Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited is replaced by:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11/5_A.18.11</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Returns True if tampering with elements is prohibited for Container, and False otherwise. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5_A.18.11</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Complete replacement of an element can cause its memory to be deallocated while another operation is holding onto a reference to it. That can't be allowed. However, a simple modification of (part of) an element is not a problem, so Update{"_"}Element does not cause a problem. <br />

<MarginText>12/5_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited is replaced by Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited in the postcondition for the operations Reference and Constant{"_"}Reference.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/5_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<li>The operations Replace{"_"}Element, Reverse{"_"}Elements, and Swap, and the nested generic unit Generic{"_"}Sorting are omitted from the nested package Stable.<br /></li>
</ul>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>13.a/2_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
The generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Vectors is new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>13.b/4_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0035-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Defined some routines to &ldquo;perform indefinite insertion&rdquo;. This could mean that some calls to those routines would now raise Program{"_"}Error where they previously worked. However, this is extremely unlikely, as it would require that the package was not implemented in Ada (an Ada <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> would raise Program{"_"}Error in these circumstances), and that a program inserted a more nested tagged type (or access discriminant) into a container, and then used that object before its type or discriminant went out of scope. All known implementations are implemented in Ada, so we believe there is no practical incompatibility. As such, we mention this only for completeness.<br />

<MarginText>13.c/5_A.18.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
Defined the Iterator{"_"}View aspect, so that the stable view is used for container element iterators. This means that tampering with elements is prohibited during the entire loop, rather than tampering with cursors being prohibited during the loop, and tampering with elements being prohibited only during the lifetimes of references to the loop parameter. Thus, if a container element iterator does an operation that tampers with elements on the iterated container, that operation will fail a tampering check in Ada 2022 (and thus raise Program{"_"}Error), while it would have worked in Ada 2012 so long as the loop parameter is not involved. We believe this to be a dubious loop structure that should be rare. Note that this issue only occurs for the indefinite container form, the ordinary and bounded containers allow such operations at any time in Ada 2022.<br />

<a id="Subclause_A.18.12"></a>

## A.18.12  The Generic Package Containers.Indefinite_Doubly_Linked_Lists

<MarginText>1/2_A.18.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists provides private types List and Cursor, and a set of operations for each type. It provides the same operations as the package Containers.Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.3">A.18.3</a>), with the difference that the generic formal Element{"_"}Type is indefinite. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/3_A.18.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03", "AI05-0092-1"]} />
<p>The declaration of the generic library package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists has the same contents and semantics as Containers.Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists except:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/2_A.18.12</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The generic formal Element{"_"}Type is indefinite.<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/2_A.18.12</MarginText>
<li>The procedure with the profile: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5/2_A.18.12</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Insert (Container : in out List;{"\n"}                  Before    : in     Cursor;{"\n"}                  Position  :    out Cursor;{"\n"}                  Count     : in     Count{"_"}Type := 1);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6/2_A.18.12</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>is omitted.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a/2_A.18.12</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This procedure is omitted because there is no way to create a default-initialized object of an indefinite type. We considered having this routine insert an empty element similar to the empty elements of a vector, but rejected this possibility because the semantics are fairly complex and very different from the existing definite container. That would make it more error-prone to convert a container from a definite type to an indefinite type; by omitting the routine completely, any problems will be diagnosed by the compiler. <br />

<MarginText>7/2_A.18.12</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The actual Element parameter of access subprogram Process of Update{"_"}Element may be constrained even if Element{"_"}Type is unconstrained.<br /></li>
<MarginText>8/4_A.18.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0035-1"]} />
<li>The operations Append, Insert, Prepend, and Replace{"_"}Element that have a formal parameter of type Element{"_"}Type perform indefinite insertion (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>).<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/5_A.18.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<li>The description of Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited is replaced by:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10/5_A.18.12</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Returns True if tampering with elements is prohibited for Container, and False otherwise. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/5_A.18.12</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Complete replacement of an element can cause its memory to be deallocated while another operation is holding onto a reference to it. That can't be allowed. However, a simple modification of (part of) an element is not a problem. <br />

<MarginText>11/5_A.18.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited is replaced by Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited in the postcondition for the operations Reference and Constant{"_"}Reference.<br /></li>
<MarginText>12/5_A.18.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<li>The operations Replace{"_"}Element and Swap are omitted from the nested package Stable.<br /></li>
</ul>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<a id="Subclause_A.18.13"></a>

## A.18.13  The Generic Package Containers.Indefinite_Hashed_Maps

<MarginText>1/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Hashed{"_"}Maps provides a map with the same operations as the package Containers.Hashed{"_"}Maps (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.5">A.18.5</a>), with the difference that the generic formal types Key{"_"}Type and Element{"_"}Type are indefinite. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/3_A.18.13</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03", "AI05-0092-1"]} />
<p>The declaration of the generic library package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Hashed{"_"}Maps has the same contents and semantics as Containers.Hashed{"_"}Maps except:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The generic formal Key{"_"}Type is indefinite.<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<li>The generic formal Element{"_"}Type is indefinite.<br /></li>
<MarginText>5/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<li>The procedure with the profile: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Insert (Container : in out Map;{"\n"}                  Key       : in     Key{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                  Position  :    out Cursor;{"\n"}                  Inserted  :    out Boolean);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>is omitted.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This procedure is omitted because there is no way to create a default-initialized object of an indefinite type. We considered having this routine insert an empty element similar to the empty elements of a vector, but rejected this possibility because the semantics are fairly complex and very different from the existing case. That would make it more error-prone to convert a container from a definite type to an indefinite type; by omitting the routine completely, any problems will be diagnosed by the compiler. <br />

<MarginText>8/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The actual Element parameter of access subprogram Process of Update{"_"}Element may be constrained even if Element{"_"}Type is unconstrained.<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/4_A.18.13</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0035-1"]} />
<li>The operations Include, Insert, Replace, and Replace{"_"}Element that have a formal parameter of type Element{"_"}Type perform indefinite insertion (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a/4_A.18.13</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Some of the named operations also have a formal of the indefinite formal type Key{"_"}Type and perform indefinite insertion using that value, but it is sufficient to mention the formal of type Element{"_"}Type to cover those. <br />

<MarginText>10/5_A.18.13</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The description of Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited is replaced by:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11/5_A.18.13</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Returns True if tampering with elements is prohibited for Container, and False otherwise. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5_A.18.13</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Complete replacement of an element can cause its memory to be deallocated while another operation is holding onto a reference to it. That can't be allowed. However, a simple modification of (part of) an element is not a problem. <br />

<MarginText>12/5_A.18.13</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited is replaced by Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Elements{"_"}Prohibited in the postcondition for the operations Reference and Constant{"_"}Reference.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/5_A.18.13</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<li>The operations Replace and Replace{"_"}Element are omitted from the nested package Stable.<br /></li>
</ul>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>13.a/2_A.18.13</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
The generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Hashed{"_"}Maps is new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>13.b/4_A.18.13</MarginText>

This could mean that some calls to those routines would now raise Program{"_"}Error where they previously worked. However, this is extremely unlikely; see Inconsistencies With Ada 2012 in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.11">A.18.11</a> for details.<br />

## A.18.15  The Generic Package Containers.Indefinite_Hashed_Sets

<MarginText>1/2_A.18.15</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Hashed{"_"}Sets provides a set with the same operations as the package Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.8">A.18.8</a>), with the difference that the generic formal type Element{"_"}Type is indefinite. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/3_A.18.15</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03", "AI05-0092-1"]} />
<p>The declaration of the generic library package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Hashed{"_"}Sets has the same contents and semantics as Containers.Hashed{"_"}Sets except:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/2_A.18.15</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The generic formal Element{"_"}Type is indefinite.<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/2_A.18.15</MarginText>
<li>The actual Element parameter of access subprogram Process of Update{"_"}Element{"_"}Preserving{"_"}Key may be constrained even if Element{"_"}Type is unconstrained.<br /></li>
<MarginText>5/4_A.18.15</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0035-1"]} />
<li>The operations Include, Insert, Replace, Replace{"_"}Element, and To{"_"}Set that have a formal parameter of type Element{"_"}Type perform indefinite insertion (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.a/4_A.18.15</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This includes the procedure Replace declared in the nested generic package Generic{"_"}Keys, as well as the routines declared directly in the Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Hashed{"_"}Sets package. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/5_A.18.15</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Unlike the other containers, a Hashed{"_"}Set has no operations that tamper with elements without tampering with cursors. Modifying the contents of a element of a set can change its position in the set, so those operations tamper with cursors.<br />

<MarginText>5.c/5_A.18.15</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
Because of this characteristic, this subclause is missing the rules that other indefinite containers have modifying the definition and use of Tampering{"_"}with{"_"}Elements, and the definition of the Stable subpackaage is the same as the definite version. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>5.d/2_A.18.15</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>5.e/4_A.18.15</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0035-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Defined some routines to &ldquo;perform indefinite insertion&rdquo;. This could mean that some calls to those routines would now raise Program{"_"}Error where they previously worked. However, this is extremely unlikely; see Inconsistencies With Ada 2012 in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.11">A.18.11</a> for details. <br />

## A.18.18  The Generic Package Containers.Indefinite_Holders

<MarginText>1/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders provides a private type Holder and a set of operations for that type. A holder container holds a single element of an indefinite type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>A holder container allows the declaration of an object that can be used like an uninitialized variable or component of an indefinite type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>A holder container may be <i>empty</i>. An empty holder does not contain an element. <br /></p>

<MarginText>26/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>The actual function for the generic formal function "=" on Element{"_"}Type values is expected to define a reflexive and symmetric relationship and return the same result value each time it is called with a particular pair of values. If it behaves in some other manner, the function "=" on holder values returns an unspecified value. The exact arguments and number of calls of this generic formal function by the function "=" on holder values are unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the actual function for "=" is not symmetric and consistent, the result returned by any of the functions defined to use "=" cannot be predicted. The implementation is not required to protect against "=" raising an exception, or returning random results, or any other "bad" behavior. And it can call "=" in whatever manner makes sense. But note that only the results of the function "=" is unspecified; other subprograms are not allowed to break if "=" is bad. <br />

<MarginText>27/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>The type Holder is used to represent holder containers. The type Holder needs finalization (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.6">7.6</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>28/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>Empty{"_"}Holder represents an empty holder object. If an object of type Holder is not otherwise initialized, it is initialized to the same value as Empty{"_"}Holder.<br /></p>

<MarginText>29/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<p>[Some operations check for &ldquo;tampering with the element&rdquo; of a container because they depend on the element of the container not being replaced.] When tampering with the element is <i>prohibited</i> for a particular holder object <i>H</i>, Program{"_"}Error is propagated by the finalization of <i>H</i>[, as well as by a call that passes <i>H</i> to certain of the operations of this package, as indicated by the precondition of such an operation].<br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraphs 30 through 35 are removed as preconditions now describe these rules.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>34.a/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Complete replacement of an element can cause its memory to be deallocated while another operation is holding onto a reference to it. That can't be allowed. However, a simple modification of (part of) an element is not a problem, so Update{"_"}Element does not cause a problem. <br />

<MarginText>36/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function "=" (Left, Right : Holder) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>37/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Left and Right denote the same holder object, then the function returns True. Otherwise, it compares the element contained in Left to the element contained in Right using the generic formal equality operator, returning the result of that operation. Any exception raised during the evaluation of element equality is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>37.a/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This wording describes the canonical semantics. However, the order and number of calls on the formal equality <b>function</b> is unspecified, so an implementation need not call the equality function if the correct answer can be determined without doing so. <br />

<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Source is empty, returns an empty holder container; otherwise, returns To{"_"}Holder (Element (Source)).<br /></p>

<MarginText>66/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Move (Target : in out Holder; Source : in out Holder){"\n"}   with Pre  ={">"} (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}The{"_"}Element{"_"}Prohibited (Target){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error) and then{"\n"}                (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}The{"_"}Element{"_"}Prohibited (Source){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error),{"\n"}        Post ={">"} (if not Target'Has{"_"}Same{"_"}Storage (Source) then{"\n"}                   Is{"_"}Empty (Source) and then (not Is{"_"}Empty (Target)));{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>67/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Target denotes the same object as Source, then the operation has no effect. Otherwise, the element contained by Source (if any) is removed from Source and inserted into Target, replacing any preexisting content.<br /></p>

<MarginText>67.1/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Swap (Left, Right : in out Holder){"\n"}   with Pre  ={">"} (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}The{"_"}Element{"_"}Prohibited (Left){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error) and then{"\n"}                (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}The{"_"}Element{"_"}Prohibited (Right){"\n"}                   or else raise Program{"_"}Error),{"\n"}        Post ={">"} Is{"_"}Empty (Left) = Is{"_"}Empty (Right)'Old and then{"\n"}                Is{"_"}Empty (Right) = Is{"_"}Empty (Left)'Old;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>67.2/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0350-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If Left denotes the same object as Right, then the operation has no effect. Otherwise, operation exchanges the elements (if any) contained by Left and Right.<br /></p>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>68/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0022-1", "AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0248-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error for the actual function associated with a generic formal subprogram, when called as part of an operation of this package, to tamper with the element of any Holder parameter of the operation. Either Program{"_"}Error is raised, or the operation works as defined on the value of the Holder either prior to, or subsequent to, some or all of the modifications to the Holder.<br /></p>

<MarginText>69/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0027-1", "AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error to call any subprogram declared in the visible part of Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders when the associated container has been finalized. If the operation takes Container as an <b>in out</b> parameter, then it raises Constraint{"_"}Error or Program{"_"}Error. Otherwise, the operation either proceeds as it would for an empty container, or it raises Constraint{"_"}Error or Program{"_"}Error. <br /></p>

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>70/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>Execution is erroneous if the holder container associated with the result of a call to Reference or Constant{"_"}Reference is finalized before the result object returned by the call to Reference or Constant{"_"}Reference is finalized.<br /></p>

<MarginText>70.a/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Each object of Reference{"_"}Type and Constant{"_"}Reference{"_"}Type probably contains some reference to the originating container. If that container is prematurely finalized (which is only possible via Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation, as accessibility checks prevent passing a container to Reference that will not live as long as the result), the finalization of the object of Reference{"_"}Type will try to access a nonexistent object. This is a normal case of a dangling pointer created by Unchecked{"_"}Deallocation; we have to explicitly mention it here as the pointer in question is not visible in the specification of the type. (This is the same reason we have to say this for invalid cursors.) <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>71/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1"]} />
<p>No storage associated with a holder object shall be lost upon assignment or scope exit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>72/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>The execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.2#S0173">assignment_statement</a></code> for a holder container shall have the effect of copying the element (if any) from the source holder object to the target holder object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>72.a/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0298-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>An assignment of a holder container is a &ldquo;deep&rdquo; copy; that is the element is copied as well as any data structures. We say &ldquo;effect of&rdquo; in order to allow the implementation to avoid copying the element immediately if it wishes. For instance, an implementation that avoided copying until one of the containers is modified would be allowed. (Note that this implementation would require care, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a> for more.) <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>73/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0269-1", "AI12-0350-1"]} />
<p>Move and Swap should not copy any elements, and should minimize copying of internal data structures. <br /></p>

<MarginText>73.a.1/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Move and Swap in Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders should not copy any elements, and should minimize copying of internal data structures.<br />

<MarginText>73.a/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0350-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Usually that can be accomplished simply by moving the pointer(s) to the internal data structures appropriately. <br />

<MarginText>74/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>If an exception is propagated from a holder operation, no storage should be lost, nor should the element be removed from a holder container unless specified by the operation. <br /></p>

<MarginText>74.a.1/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If an exception is propagated from a holder operation, no storage should be lost, nor should the element be removed from a holder container unless specified by the operation.<br />

<MarginText>74.a/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is important so that programs can recover from errors. But we don't want to require heroic efforts, so we just require documentation of cases where this can't be accomplished. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>74.b/3_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0084-1", "AI05-0265-1"]} />
 The generic package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders is new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>74.c/4_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0035-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Defined some routines to &ldquo;perform indefinite insertion&rdquo;. This could mean that some calls to those routines would now raise Program{"_"}Error where they previously worked. However, this is extremely unlikely; see Inconsistencies With Ada 2012 in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.11">A.18.11</a> for details. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>74.d/5_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1", "AI12-0112-1", "AI12-0350-1"]} />
A number of new subprograms and types were added to Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders to better support contracts and provide additional functionality. Therefore, a use clause conflict is possible; see the introduction of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a> for more on this topic. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>74.e/4_A.18.18</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0110-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that tampering checks precede all other checks made by a subprogram (but come after those associated with the call).<br />

Added contracts to this container. This includes describing some of the semantics with pre- and postconditions, rather than English text. Note that the preconditions can be Suppressed (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.5">11.5</a>). <br />

## A.18.19  The Generic Package Containers.Bounded_Vectors

<MarginText>1/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Bounded{"_"}Vectors provides a private type Vector and a set of operations. It provides the same operations as the package Containers.Vectors (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a>), with the difference that the maximum storage is bounded. <br /></p>
