#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>10/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0160-1", "AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error to assign from a bounded vector object while tampering with elements [or cursors] of that object is prohibited. Either Program{"_"}Error is raised by the assignment, execution proceeds with the target object prohibiting tampering with elements [or cursors], or execution proceeds normally. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Tampering with elements includes tampering with cursors, so we only really need to talk about tampering with elements here; we mention cursors for clarity. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>11/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>When a bounded vector object <i>V</i> is finalized, if tampering with cursors is prohibited for <i>V</i> other than due to an assignment from another vector, then execution is erroneous. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is a tampering event, but since the implementation is not allowed to use Ada.Finalization, it is not possible in a pure Ada implementation to detect this error. (There is no Finalize routine that will be called that could make the check.) Since the check probably cannot be made, the bad effects that could occur (such as an iterator going into an infinite loop or accessing a nonexistent element) cannot be prevented and we have to allow anything. We do allow re-assigning an object that only prohibits tampering because it was copied from another object as that cannot cause any negative effects. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>12/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>For each instance of Containers.Vectors and each instance of Containers.Bounded{"_"}Vectors, if the two instances meet the following conditions, then the output generated by the Vector'Output or Vector'Write subprograms of either instance shall be readable by the Vector'Input or Vector'Read of the other instance, respectively:<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the Element{"_"}Type parameters of the two instances are statically matching subtypes of the same type; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1"]} />
<li>the output generated by Element{"_"}Type'Output or Element{"_"}Type'Write is readable by Element{"_"}Type'Input or Element{"_"}Type'Read, respectively (where Element{"_"}Type denotes the type of the two actual Element{"_"}Type parameters); and<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1"]} />
<li>the preceding two conditions also hold for the Index{"_"}Type parameters of the instances. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>16/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>Bounded vector objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation. <br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a.1/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Bounded vector objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation.<br />

<MarginText>17/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>The implementation advice for procedure Move to minimize copying does not apply. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a.1/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The implementation advice for procedure Move to minimize copying does not apply to bounded vectors.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>17.a/3_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1", "AI05-0160-1", "AI05-0184-1"]} />
 The generic package Containers.Bounded{"_"}Vectors is new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.b/5_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Tampering with elements is now defined to be equivalent to tampering with cursors for bounded containers. If a program requires tampering detection to work, it might fail in Ada 2022. Needless to say, this shouldn't happen outside of test programs. See Inconsistencies With Ada 2012 in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a> for more details. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.c/5_A.18.19</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b>A bounded vector now only has Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization (abbreviated PI in this note) when the actual for the Element{"_"}Type has PI. If an program used a vector whose actual Element{"_"}Type does not have PI in a context when PI is required (such as a library-level object in a preelaborated unit or as a component of a type with PI), the program would be illegal in Ada 2022 but legal in original Ada 2012. This situation is unlikely, especially as some existing Ada 2012 implementations reject the instance in this case. <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>14/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0160-1", "AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error to assign from a bounded list object while tampering with elements [or cursors] of that object is prohibited. Either Program{"_"}Error is raised by the assignment, execution proceeds with the target object prohibiting tampering with elements [or cursors], or execution proceeds normally. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Tampering with elements includes tampering with cursors, so we only really need to talk about tampering with elements here; we mention cursors for clarity. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>15/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>When a bounded list object <i>L</i> is finalized, if tampering with cursors is prohibited for <i>L</i> other than due to an assignment from another list, then execution is erroneous. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is a tampering event, but since the implementation is not allowed to use Ada.Finalization, it is not possible in a pure Ada implementation to detect this error. (There is no Finalize routine that will be called that could make the check.) Since the check probably cannot be made, the bad effects that could occur (such as an iterator going into an infinite loop or accessing a nonexistent element) cannot be prevented and we have to allow anything. We do allow re-assigning an object that only prohibits tampering because it was copied from another object as that cannot cause any negative effects. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>16/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>For each instance of Containers.Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists and each instance of Containers.Bounded{"_"}Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists, if the two instances meet the following conditions, then the output generated by the List'Output or List'Write subprograms of either instance shall be readable by the List'Input or List'Read of the other instance, respectively:<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the Element{"_"}Type parameters of the two instances are statically matching subtypes of the same type; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>18/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1"]} />
<li>the output generated by Element{"_"}Type'Output or Element{"_"}Type'Write is readable by Element{"_"}Type'Input or Element{"_"}Type'Read, respectively (where Element{"_"}Type denotes the type of the two actual Element{"_"}Type parameters). <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>19/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>Bounded list objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a.1/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Bounded list objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation.<br />

<MarginText>20/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>The implementation advice for procedure Move to minimize copying does not apply. <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a.1/3_A.18.20</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The implementation advice for procedure Move to minimize copying does not apply to bounded lists.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>20.a/3_A.18.20</MarginText>

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>20.b/5_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Tampering with elements is now defined to be equivalent to tampering with cursors for bounded containers. If a program requires tampering detection to work, it might fail in Ada 2022. Needless to say, this shouldn't happen outside of test programs. See Inconsistencies With Ada 2012 in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a> for more details. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>20.c/5_A.18.20</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b>A bounded list now only has Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization (abbreviated PI in this note) when the actual for the Element{"_"}Type has PI. If an program used a list whose actual Element{"_"}Type does not have PI in a context when PI is required (such as a library-level object in a preelaborated unit or as a component of a type with PI), the program would be illegal in Ada 2022 but legal in original Ada 2012. This situation is unlikely, especially as some existing Ada 2012 implementations reject the instance in this case. <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>12/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0160-1", "AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error to assign from a bounded map object while tampering with elements [or cursors] of that object is prohibited. Either Program{"_"}Error is raised by the assignment, execution proceeds with the target object prohibiting tampering with elements [or cursors], or execution proceeds normally. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Tampering with elements includes tampering with cursors, so we only really need to talk about tampering with elements here; we mention cursors for clarity. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>13/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>When a bounded map object <i>M</i> is finalized, if tampering with cursors is prohibited for <i>M</i> other than due to an assignment from another map, then execution is erroneous. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is a tampering event, but since the implementation is not allowed to use Ada.Finalization, it is not possible in a pure Ada implementation to detect this error. (There is no Finalize routine that will be called that could make the check.) Since the check probably cannot be made, the bad effects that could occur (such as an iterator going into an infinite loop or accessing a nonexistent element) cannot be prevented and we have to allow anything. We do allow re-assigning an object that only prohibits tampering because it was copied from another object as that cannot cause any negative effects. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>14/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>For each instance of Containers.Ordered{"_"}Maps and each instance of Containers.Bounded{"_"}Ordered{"_"}Maps, if the two instances meet the following conditions, then the output generated by the Map'Output or Map'Write subprograms of either instance shall be readable by the Map'Input or Map'Read of the other instance, respectively:<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the Element{"_"}Type parameters of the two instances are statically matching subtypes of the same type; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>16/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1"]} />
<li>the output generated by Element{"_"}Type'Output or Element{"_"}Type'Write is readable by Element{"_"}Type'Input or Element{"_"}Type'Read, respectively (where Element{"_"}Type denotes the type of the two actual Element{"_"}Type parameters); and<br /></li>
<MarginText>17/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1"]} />
<li>the preceding two conditions also hold for the Key{"_"}Type parameters of the instances. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>18/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>Bounded ordered map objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a.1/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Bounded ordered map objects should be implemented without implicit pointers or dynamic allocation.<br />

<MarginText>19/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>The implementation advice for procedure Move to minimize copying does not apply. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a.1/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The implementation advice for procedure Move to minimize copying does not apply to bounded ordered maps.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>19.a/3_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1", "AI05-0160-1", "AI05-0184-1"]} />
 The generic package Containers.Bounded{"_"}Ordered{"_"}Maps is new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>19.b/5_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0111-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Tampering with elements is now defined to be equivalent to tampering with cursors for bounded containers. If a program requires tampering detection to work, it might fail in Ada 2022. Needless to say, this shouldn't happen outside of test programs. See Inconsistencies With Ada 2012 in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.2">A.18.2</a> for more details. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>19.c/5_A.18.22</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b>A bounded map now only has Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization (abbreviated PI in this note) when the actuals for the Element{"_"}Type and the Key{"_"}Type have PI. If an program used a map whose actual Element{"_"}Type or Key{"_"}Type does not have PI in a context when PI is required (such as a library-level object in a preelaborated unit or as a component of a type with PI), the program would be illegal in Ada 2022 but legal in original Ada 2012. This situation is unlikely, especially as some existing Ada 2012 implementations reject the instance in this case. <br />

   Pre ={">"} (not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited (Target){"\n"}             or else raise Program{"_"}Error) and then{"\n"}          (Length (Source) {"<"}= Target.Capacity{"\n"}             or else raise Capacity{"_"}Error),{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

<ul>
<li>The function Copy is replaced with: <br /></li>

<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
  function Copy (Source   : Set;{"\n"}                 Capacity : Count{"_"}Type := 0) return Map{"\n"}     with Pre  ={">"} Capacity = 0 or else Capacity {">"}= Length (Source){"\n"}                     or else raise Capacity{"_"}Error,{"\n"}          Post ={">"} {"\n"}             Length (Copy'Result) = Length (Source) and then{"\n"}             not Tampering{"_"}With{"_"}Cursors{"_"}Prohibited (Copy'Result) and then{"\n"}             Copy'Result.Capacity = (if Capacity = 0 then{"\n"}                Length (Source) else Capacity);{"\n"}

<p class="Indented4">Returns a set with key/element pairs initialized from the values in Source. <br /></p>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>12/3_A.18.24</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0160-1", "AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error to assign from a bounded set object while tampering with elements [or cursors] of that object is prohibited. Either Program{"_"}Error is raised by the assignment, execution proceeds with the target object prohibiting tampering with elements [or cursors], or execution proceeds normally. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/3_A.18.24</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Tampering with elements includes tampering with cursors, so we only really need to talk about tampering with elements here; we mention cursors for clarity. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>13/3_A.18.24</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0265-1"]} />
<p>When a bounded set object <i>S</i> is finalized, if tampering with cursors is prohibited for <i>S</i> other than due to an assignment from another set, then execution is erroneous. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/3_A.18.24</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is a tampering event, but since the implementation is not allowed to use Ada.Finalization, it is not possible in a pure Ada implementation to detect this error. (There is no Finalize routine that will be called that could make the check.) Since the check probably cannot be made, the bad effects that could occur (such as an iterator going into an infinite loop or accessing a nonexistent element) cannot be prevented and we have to allow anything. We do allow re-assigning an object that only prohibits tampering because it was copied from another object as that cannot cause any negative effects. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>14/3_A.18.24</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>For each instance of Containers.Ordered{"_"}Sets and each instance of Containers.Bounded{"_"}Ordered{"_"}Sets, if the two instances meet the following conditions, then the output generated by the Set'Output or Set'Write subprograms of either instance shall be readable by the Set'Input or Set'Read of the other instance, respectively:<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/3_A.18.24</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>the Element{"_"}Type parameters of the two instances are statically matching subtypes of the same type; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>16/3_A.18.24</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0184-1"]} />
<li>the output generated by Element{"_"}Type'Output or Element{"_"}Type'Write is readable by Element{"_"}Type'Input or Element{"_"}Type'Read, respectively (where Element{"_"}Type denotes the type of the two actual Element{"_"}Type parameters). <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>17.a.1/3_A.18.24</MarginText>

<MarginText>18.b/5_A.18.24</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />

<b></b>A bounded set now only has Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization (abbreviated PI in this note) when the actual for the Element{"_"}Type has PI. If an program used a set whose actual Element{"_"}Type does not have PI in a context when PI is required (such as a library-level object in a preelaborated unit or as a component of a type with PI), the program would be illegal in Ada 2022 but legal in original Ada 2012. This situation is unlikely, especially as some existing Ada 2012 implementations reject the instance in this case. <br />

## A.18.26  Array Sorting

<MarginText>1/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03", "AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic procedures Containers.Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort, Containers.Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort, and Containers.Generic{"_"}Sort provide sorting on arbitrary array types. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>The generic library procedure Containers.Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type Index{"_"}Type is ({"<"}{">"});{"\n"}   type Element{"_"}Type is private;{"\n"}   type Array{"_"}Type is array (Index{"_"}Type range {"<"}{">"}) of Element{"_"}Type;{"\n"}   with function "{"<"}" (Left, Right : Element{"_"}Type){"\n"}      return Boolean is {"<"}{">"};{"\n"}procedure Ada.Containers.Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort (Container : in out Array{"_"}Type){"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking, Global ={">"} null;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3.a/5_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Global ={">"} <b>null</b> means that the only global side-effects allowed are associated with the actual generic parameters. Similarly, when Nonblocking is set to True for a generic unit, the only blocking allowed is that associated with the actual generic parameters. <br />

<MarginText>4/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Reorders the elements of Container such that the elements are sorted smallest first as determined by the generic formal "{"<"}" operator provided. Any exception raised during evaluation of "{"<"}" is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0044-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">The actual function for the generic formal function "{"<"}" of Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort is expected to return the same value each time it is called with a particular pair of element values. It should define a strict weak ordering relationship (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>); it should not modify Container. If the actual for "{"<"}" behaves in some other manner, the behavior of the instance of Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort is unspecified. The number of times Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort calls "{"<"}" is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This implies swapping the elements, usually including an intermediate copy. This of course means that the elements will be copied. Since the elements are nonlimited, this usually will not be a problem. Note that there is Implementation Advice below that the implementation should use a sort that minimizes copying of elements.<br />

<MarginText>5.b/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
The sort is not required to be stable (and the fast algorithm required will not be stable). If a stable sort is needed, the user can include the original location of the element as an extra "sort key". We considered requiring the implementation to do that, but it is mostly extra overhead -- usually there is something already in the element that provides the needed stability. <br />

<MarginText>6/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>The generic library procedure Containers.Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>7/5_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type Index{"_"}Type is ({"<"}{">"});{"\n"}   type Element{"_"}Type is private;{"\n"}   type Array{"_"}Type is array (Index{"_"}Type) of Element{"_"}Type;{"\n"}   with function "{"<"}" (Left, Right : Element{"_"}Type){"\n"}      return Boolean is {"<"}{">"};{"\n"}procedure Ada.Containers.Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort{"\n"}      (Container : in out Array{"_"}Type){"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking, Global ={">"} null;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7.a/5_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Global ={">"} <b>null</b> means that the only global side-effects allowed are associated with the actual generic parameters. Similarly, when Nonblocking is set to True for a generic unit, the only blocking allowed is that associated with the actual generic parameters. <br />

<MarginText>8/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Reorders the elements of Container such that the elements are sorted smallest first as determined by the generic formal "{"<"}" operator provided. Any exception raised during evaluation of "{"<"}" is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0044-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">The actual function for the generic formal function "{"<"}" of Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort is expected to return the same value each time it is called with a particular pair of element values. It should define a strict weak ordering relationship (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>); it should not modify Container. If the actual for "{"<"}" behaves in some other manner, the behavior of the instance of Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort is unspecified. The number of times Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort calls "{"<"}" is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.1/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1"]} />
<p>The generic library procedure Containers.Generic{"_"}Sort has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.2/5_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0056-1", "AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type Index{"_"}Type is ({"<"}{">"});{"\n"}   with function Before (Left, Right : Index{"_"}Type) return Boolean;{"\n"}   with procedure Swap (Left, Right : in Index{"_"}Type);{"\n"}procedure Ada.Containers.Generic{"_"}Sort{"\n"}      (First, Last : Index{"_"}Type'Base){"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking, Global ={">"} null;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9.a/5_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Global ={">"} <b>null</b> means that the only global side-effects allowed are associated with the actual generic parameters. Similarly, when Nonblocking is set to True for a generic unit, the only blocking allowed is that associated with the actual generic parameters. <br />

<MarginText>9.3/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Reorders the elements of an indexable structure, over the range First .. Last, such that the elements are sorted in the ordering determined by the generic formal function Before; Before should return True if Left is to be sorted before Right. The generic formal Before compares the elements having the given indices, and the generic formal Swap exchanges the values of the indicated elements. Any exception raised during evaluation of Before or Swap is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.4/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The actual function for the generic formal function Before of Generic{"_"}Sort is expected to return the same value each time it is called with index values that identify a particular pair of element values. It should define a strict weak ordering relationship (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>); it should not modify the elements. The actual function for the generic formal Swap should exchange the values of the indicated elements. If the actual for either Before or Swap behaves in some other manner, the behavior of Generic{"_"}Sort is unspecified. The number of times the Generic{"_"}Sort calls Before or Swap is unspecified.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>10/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>The worst-case time complexity of a call on an instance of Containers.Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort or Containers.Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort should be <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2) or better, and the average time complexity should be better than <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2), where <i>N</i> is the length of the Container parameter. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Containers.Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort and Containers.Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort should have an average time complexity better than <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2) and worst case no worse than <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2).<br />

<MarginText>10.b/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In other words, we're requiring the use of a sorting algorithm better than <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2), such as Quicksort. No bubble sorts allowed! <br />

<MarginText>11/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00302-03"]} />
<p>Containers.Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort and Containers.Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort should minimize copying of elements. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Containers.Generic{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort and Containers.Generic{"_"}Constrained{"_"}Array{"_"}Sort should minimize copying of elements.<br />

<MarginText>11.b/2_A.18.26</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>We do not mean &ldquo;absolutely minimize&rdquo; here; we're not intending to require a single copy for each element. Rather, we want to suggest that the sorting algorithm chosen is one that does not copy items unnecessarily. Bubble sort would not meet this advice, for instance. <br />

<MarginText>12/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p>The worst-case time complexity of a call on an instance of Containers.Generic{"_"}Sort should be <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2) or better, and the average time complexity should be better than <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2), where <i>N</i> is the difference between the Last and First parameters plus 1. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a.1/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Containers.Generic{"_"}Sort should have an average time complexity better than <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2) and worst case no worse than <i>O</i>(<i>N</i>{"*"}{"*"}2).<br />

<MarginText>13/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p>Containers.Generic{"_"}Sort should minimize calls to the generic formal Swap. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a.1/3_A.18.26</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Containers.Generic{"_"}Sort should minimize calls to the generic formal Swap.<br />

## A.18.27  The Generic Package Containers.Synchronized_Queue_Interfaces

<MarginText>1/3_A.18.27</MarginText>

<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Synchronized{"_"}Queue{"_"}Interfaces provides interface type Queue, and a set of operations for that type. Interface Queue specifies a first-in, first-out queue. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/3_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1"]} />
<p>The generic library package Containers.Synchronized{"_"}Queue{"_"}Interfaces has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.1/5_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<p>The subprogram behavior descriptions given below are the semantics for the corresponding callable entities found in the language-defined generic packages that have a formal package named Queue{"_"}Interfaces.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Enqueue{"\n"}  (Container : in out Queue;{"\n"}   New{"_"}Item  : in     Element{"_"}Type) is abstract{"\n"}   with Synchronization ={">"} By{"_"}Entry{"\n"}        Nonblocking ={">"} False,{"\n"}        Global'Class={">"} in out synchronized;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10/3_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">A queue type that implements this interface is allowed to have a bounded <i>capacity</i>. If the queue object has a bounded capacity, and the number of existing elements equals the capacity, then Enqueue blocks until storage becomes available; otherwise, Enqueue does not block. In any case, it then copies New{"_"}Item onto the queue.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Dequeue{"\n"}  (Container : in out Queue;{"\n"}   Element   :    out Element{"_"}Type) is abstract{"\n"}   with Synchronization ={">"} By{"_"}Entry{"\n"}        Nonblocking ={">"} False,{"\n"}        Global'Class={">"} in out synchronized;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>12/3_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1", "AI05-0251-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">If the queue is empty, then Dequeue blocks until an item becomes available. In any case, it then assigns the element at the head of the queue to Element, and removes it from the queue.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Current{"_"}Use (Container : Queue) return Count{"_"}Type is abstract{"\n"}   with Nonblocking, Global'Class={">"} null, Use{"_"}Formal ={">"} null;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>14/3_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns the number of elements currently in the queue.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/5_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Peak{"_"}Use (Container : Queue) return Count{"_"}Type is abstract{"\n"}   with Nonblocking, Global'Class={">"} null, Use{"_"}Formal ={">"} null,{"\n"}         Post'Class ={">"} Peak{"_"}Use'Result {">"}= Current{"_"}Use (Container);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16/3_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns the maximum number of elements that have been in the queue at any one time.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/3_A.18.27</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0251-1"]} />
NOTE   Unlike other language-defined containers, there are no queues whose element types are indefinite. Elements of an indefinite type can be handled by defining the element of the queue to be a holder container (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.18">A.18.18</a>) of the indefinite type, or to be an explicit access type that designates the indefinite type.<br />

<MarginText>17.a/3_A.18.27</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>There are no indefinite queues, as a useful definition for Dequeue is not possible. Dequeue cannot be a function, as Ada does not have entries that are functions (thus conditional and timed calls would not be possible). Moreover, protected functions do not allow modifying the queue object (thus it doesn't work even if we decided we didn't care about conditional and timed calls). If Dequeue is an entry, then the dequeued object would have to be an <b>out</b> parameter and that would require the queue client to guess the tag and constraints of the value that will be dequeued (otherwise Constraint{"_"}Error would be raised), and that is rarely going to be possible. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>17.b/3_A.18.27</MarginText>

 The generic package Containers.Synchronized{"_"}Queue{"_"}Interfaces is new. <br />

<b></b>Nested package Implementation can be used to declare the types needed to implement the protected type Queue. This nested package is necessary as types cannot be declared in the private part of a protected type, and the types have to be declared within the generic unit in order to depend on the types imported with package Queue{"_"}Interfaces. Clients should never depend on the contents of nested package Implementation. <br />

<MarginText>12/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1"]} />
<p>The type Queue is used to represent task-safe priority queues.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1"]} />
<p>The capacity for instances of type Queue is unbounded.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1"]} />
<p>Two elements <i>E1</i> and <i>E2</i> are equivalent if Before(Get{"_"}Priority(<i>E1</i>), Get{"_"}Priority(<i>E2</i>)) and Before(Get{"_"}Priority(<i>E2</i>), Get{"_"}Priority(<i>E1</i>)) both return False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p>The actual functions for Get{"_"}Priority and Before are expected to return the same value each time they are called with the same actuals, and should not modify their actuals. Before should define a strict weak ordering relationship (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18">A.18</a>). If the actual functions behave in some other manner, the behavior of Unbounded{"_"}Priority{"_"}Queues is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1"]} />
<p>Enqueue inserts an item according to the order specified by the Before function on the result of Get{"_"}Priority on the elements; Before should return True if Left is to be inserted before Right. If the queue already contains elements equivalent to New{"_"}Item, then it is inserted after the existing equivalent elements.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Enqueue never blocks; if more storage is needed for a new element, it is allocated dynamically. We don't need to explicitly specify that Queue needs finalization, because it is visibly protected. <br />

<MarginText>17/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0159-1", "AI05-0251-1", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>For a call on Dequeue{"_"}Only{"_"}High{"_"}Priority, if the head of the nonempty queue is <i>E</i>, and the function Before(At{"_"}Least, Get{"_"}Priority(<i>E</i>)) returns False, then <i>E</i> is assigned to Element and then removed from the queue, and Success is set to True; otherwise, Success is set to False and Element is unchanged.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0251-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Unlike Dequeue, Dequeue{"_"}Only{"_"}High{"_"}Priority is not blocking; it always returns immediately. <br />

<MarginText>17.b/3_A.18.30</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0251-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The use of Before is "backwards" so that it acts like "{">"}=" (it is defined similarly to "{">"}"); thus we dequeue only when it is False. <br />

## A.18.32  The Generic Package Containers.Bounded_Indefinite_Holders

<MarginText>1/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0254-1"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package Containers.Bounded{"_"}Indefinite{"_"}Holders provides a private type Holder and a set of operations for that type. It provides the same operations as the package Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.18#Subclause_A.18.18">A.18.18</a>), with the difference that the maximum storage is bounded. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0254-1"]} />
<p>The declaration of the generic library package Containers.Bounded{"_"}Indefinite{"_"}Holders has the same contents and semantics as Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders except:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The following is added to the context clause:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   with System.Storage{"_"}Elements; use System.Storage{"_"}Elements;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>An additional generic parameter follows Element{"_"}Type:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   Max{"_"}Element{"_"}Size{"_"}in{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements : Storage{"_"}Count;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.a/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This value is in Storage{"_"}Elements so that it can be used as a discriminant on a storage pool object in the implementation of the object; Ada doesn't allow discriminant dependent components to use formulas.<br />

<MarginText>6.b/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
This is a generic parameter as it is a property of the Element{"_"}Type; the largest possible object of Element{"_"}Type is unlikely to be different for different containers, so making it a discriminant (as Capacity is) provides no useful capability. <br />

<MarginText>7/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> for Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization for type Holder is changed to: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
  Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization ={">"}{"\n"}     Element{"_"}Type'Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Add to the precondition of To{"_"}Holder and Replace{"_"}Element:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
  and then (New{"_"}Item'Size {"<"}={"\n"}               Max{"_"}Element{"_"}Size{"_"}in{"_"}Storage{"_"}Elements {"*"} System.Storage{"_"}Unit{"\n"}            or else raise Program{"_"}Error){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10.a/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that an object that won't fit is not inserted into the container. <br />

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>11/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0254-1"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error to assign from a bounded holder object while tampering with elements of that object is prohibited. Either Program{"_"}Error is raised by the assignment, execution proceeds with the target object prohibiting tampering with elements, or execution proceeds normally. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>12/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0254-1"]} />
<p>For each instance of Containers.Indefinite{"_"}Holders and each instance of Containers.Bounded{"_"}Indefinite{"_"}Holders, if the two instances meet the following conditions, then the output generated by the Holder'Output or Holder'Write subprograms of either instance shall be readable by the Holder'Input or Holder'Read of the other instance, respectively:<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the Element{"_"}Type parameters of the two instances are statically matching subtypes of the same type; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<li>the output generated by Element{"_"}Type'Output or Element{"_"}Type'Write is readable by Element{"_"}Type'Input or Element{"_"}Type'Read, respectively (where Element{"_"}Type denotes the type of the two actual Element{"_"}Type parameters). <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>15/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0254-1"]} />
<p>Bounded holder objects should be implemented without dynamic allocation and any finalization should be trivial unless Element{"_"}Type needs finalization. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a.1/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Bounded holder objects should be implemented without dynamic allocation.<br />

<MarginText>15.a/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Implementation of this container in Ada will probably require the use of a special storage pool. When we say "without dynamic allocation", we mean that this pool does not use heap memory and has a trivial finalization routine (that is, procedures Adjust and Finalize are null procedures). All storage pools are controlled, so we can't reasonably say that a bounded holder will not need finalization. <br />

<MarginText>15.b/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>If the implementation supports discontiguous objects that require multiple calls to Allocate in a storage pool, the storage pool will need to support such allocations. The storage pool implementation can assume that all Allocate calls occur together, and similarly for Deallocate calls, thus simplifying the pool implementation so that allocation only occurs at a high-water mark location. <br />

<MarginText>16/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0350-1", "AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>The  about the Move and Swap operations is deleted for bounded holders; these operations can copy elements as necessary.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The memory of a bounded indefinite holder belongs directly to the container, so it cannot be moved with the element. If the element type contains any internal pointers, moving it without calling Adjust would leave such pointers pointing to the wrong holder object. Thus, a full copy is needed, including any associated finalization and adjustments. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>16.b/5_A.18.32</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0254-1"]} />
 The generic package Containers.Bounded{"_"}Indefinite{"_"}Holders is new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_A.18.33"></a>

## A.18.33  Example of Container Use

#### Examples

<MarginText>1/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
<p>The following example is an implementation of Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm in a directed graph with positive distances. The graph is represented by a map from nodes to sets of edges.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Containers.Vectors;{"\n"}with Ada.Containers.Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists;{"\n"}use Ada.Containers;{"\n"}generic{"\n"}   type Node is range {"<"}{">"};{"\n"}package Shortest{"_"}Paths is{"\n"}   type Distance is new Float range 0.0 .. Float'Last;{"\n"}   type Edge is record{"\n"}      To, From : Node;{"\n"}      Length   : Distance;{"\n"}   end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>3/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
   package Node{"_"}Maps is new Vectors (Node, Node);{"\n"}   -- The algorithm builds a map to indicate the node used to reach a given{"\n"}   -- node in the shortest distance.{"\n"}
<MarginText>4/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
   package Adjacency{"_"}Lists is new Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists (Edge);{"\n"}   use Adjacency{"_"}Lists;{"\n"}
<MarginText>5/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
   package Graphs is new Vectors (Node, Adjacency{"_"}Lists.List);{"\n"}
<MarginText>6/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
   package Paths is new Doubly{"_"}Linked{"_"}Lists (Node);{"\n"}
<MarginText>7/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
   function Shortest{"_"}Path{"\n"}     (G : Graphs.Vector; Source : Node; Target : Node) return Paths.List{"\n"}      with Pre ={">"} G (Source) /= Adjacency{"_"}Lists.Empty{"_"}List;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
end Shortest{"_"}Paths;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9/5_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1"]} />
package body Shortest{"_"}Paths is{"\n"}   function Shortest{"_"}Path{"\n"}     (G : Graphs.Vector; Source : Node; Target : Node) return Paths.List{"\n"}   is{"\n"}      use Node{"_"}Maps, Paths, Graphs;{"\n"}      Reached  : array (Node) of Boolean := (others ={">"} False);{"\n"}      -- The set of nodes whose shortest distance to the source is known.{"\n"}
<MarginText>10/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
      Reached{"_"}From : array (Node) of Node;{"\n"}      So{"_"}Far   : array (Node) of Distance := (others ={">"} Distance'Last);{"\n"}      The{"_"}Path : Paths.List := Paths.Empty{"_"}List;{"\n"}      Nearest{"_"}Distance : Distance;{"\n"}      Next     : Node;{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      So{"_"}Far(Source)  := 0.0;{"\n"}
<MarginText>11/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
      while not Reached(Target) loop{"\n"}         Nearest{"_"}Distance := Distance'Last;{"\n"}
<MarginText>12/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
         -- Find closest node not reached yet, by iterating over all nodes.{"\n"}         -- A more efficient algorithm uses a priority queue for this step.{"\n"}
<MarginText>13/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
         Next := Source;{"\n"}         for N in Node'First .. Node'Last loop{"\n"}            if not Reached(N){"\n"}              and then So{"_"}Far(N) {"<"} Nearest{"_"}Distance then{"\n"}                 Next := N;{"\n"}                 Nearest{"_"}Distance := So{"_"}Far(N);{"\n"}            end if;{"\n"}         end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
         if Nearest{"_"}Distance = Distance'Last then{"\n"}            -- No next node found, graph is not connected{"\n"}            return Paths.Empty{"_"}List;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
         else{"\n"}            Reached(Next) := True;{"\n"}         end if;{"\n"}
<MarginText>16/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
         -- Update minimum distance to newly reachable nodes.{"\n"}
<MarginText>17/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
         for E of G (Next) loop{"\n"}            if not Reached(E.To) then{"\n"}               Nearest{"_"}Distance := E.Length + So{"_"}Far(Next);{"\n"}
<MarginText>18/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
               if Nearest{"_"}Distance {"<"} So{"_"}Far(E.To) then{"\n"}                  Reached{"_"}From(E.To) := Next;{"\n"}                  So{"_"}Far(E.To) := Nearest{"_"}Distance;{"\n"}               end if;{"\n"}            end if;{"\n"}         end loop;{"\n"}      end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>19/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
      -- Rebuild path from target to source.{"\n"}
<MarginText>20/5_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0386-1"]} />
      declare{"\n"}         N : Node := Target;{"\n"}      begin{"\n"}         Prepend (The{"_"}Path, N);{"\n"}         while N /= Source loop{"\n"}            N := Reached{"_"}From(N);{"\n"}            Prepend (The{"_"}Path, N);{"\n"}         end loop;{"\n"}      end;{"\n"}
<MarginText>21/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
      return The{"_"}Path;{"\n"}   end;{"\n"}end Shortest{"_"}Paths;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>22/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
<p>Note that the effect of the Constant{"_"}Indexing aspect (on type Vector) and the Implicit{"_"}Dereference aspect (on type Reference{"_"}Type) is that<br /></p>

<MarginText>23/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
G (Next){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>24/5_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1", "AI12-0426-1"]} />
<p>is a convenient shorthand for<br /></p>

<MarginText>25/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
G.Constant{"_"}Reference (Next).Element.all{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>26/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
<p>Similarly, the effect of the loop:<br /></p>

<MarginText>27/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for E of G (Next) loop{"\n"}   if not Reached(E.To) then{"\n"}      ...{"\n"}   end if;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>28/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
<p>is the same as:<br /></p>

<MarginText>29/4_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0080-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for C in G (Next).Iterate loop{"\n"}   declare{"\n"}      E : Edge renames G (Next)(C);{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      if not Reached(E.To) then{"\n"}         ...{"\n"}      end if;{"\n"}   end;{"\n"}end loop;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>30/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
<p>which is the same as:<br /></p>

<MarginText>31/4_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0080-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
declare{"\n"}   L : Adjacency{"_"}Lists.List renames G (Next);{"\n"}   C : Adjacency{"_"}Lists.Cursor := L.First;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   while Has{"_"}Element (C) loop{"\n"}      declare{"\n"}         E : Edge renames L(C);{"\n"}      begin{"\n"}         if not Reached(E.To) then{"\n"}            ...{"\n"}         end if;{"\n"}      end;{"\n"}      C := L.Next (C);{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>31.a/3_A.18.33</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0212-1"]} />
This example of container use is new. <br />

# A.19. The Package Locales

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.19.mdx

sidebar_position:  139

# A.19. The Package Locales

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<p>A <i>locale</i> identifies a geopolitical place or region and its associated language, which can be used to determine other internationalization-related characteristics. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2"]} />
<p>The library package Locales has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0414-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Locales{"\n"}   with Preelaborate, Remote{"_"}Types is{"\n"}
<MarginText>4/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0037-1"]} />
   type Language{"_"}Code is new String (1 .. 3){"\n"}      with Dynamic{"_"}Predicate ={">"}{"\n"}         (for all E of Language{"_"}Code ={">"} E in 'a' .. 'z');{"\n"}   type Country{"_"}Code is new String (1 .. 2){"\n"}      with Dynamic{"_"}Predicate ={">"}{"\n"}         (for all E of Country{"_"}Code  ={">"} E in 'A' .. 'Z');{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4.a/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0037-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>These types are derived from type String so that they can easily be converted to or from type String. That's important if one of these values needs to be input or displayed (via Text{"_"}IO, perhaps). We use the predicate to ensure that only possible component values are used. Ada does not allow converting between unrelated types with components that don't statically match, so we cannot declare new types with constrained components if we want conversions to or from type String. <br />

<MarginText>5/3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
   Language{"_"}Unknown : constant Language{"_"}Code := "und";{"\n"}   Country{"_"}Unknown : constant Country{"_"}Code := "ZZ";{"\n"}
<MarginText>6/3</MarginText>
   function Language return Language{"_"}Code;{"\n"}   function Country return Country{"_"}Code;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7/3</MarginText>
end Ada.Locales;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2", "AI05-0233-1"]} />
<p>The <i>active locale</i> is the locale associated with the partition of the current task.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0233-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Some environments define both a system locale and the locale of the current user. For such environments, the active locale is that of current user if any; otherwise (as in a partition running on a server without a user), the system locale should be used. <br />

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2", "AI12-0446-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2", "AI12-0446-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2", "AI05-0248-1", "AI12-0446-1"]} />
<p>Function Language returns the code of the language associated with the active locale. If the Language{"_"}Code associated with the active locale cannot be determined from the environment, then Language returns Language{"_"}Unknown. Otherwise, the result is a lower-case string representation of an ISO 639-3:2007 alpha-3 code that identifies a language.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Some common language codes are: "eng" &ndash; English; "fra" &ndash; French; "deu" &ndash; German; "zho" &ndash; Chinese. These are the same codes as used by POSIX systems. We considered including constants for the most common languages, but that was rejected as the likely source of continual arguments about the constant names and which languages are important enough to include. <br />

<MarginText>12/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2", "AI05-0248-1", "AI12-0446-1", "AI12-0450-1"]} />
<p>Function Country returns the code of the country associated with the active locale. If the Country{"_"}Code associated with the active locale cannot be determined from the environment, then Country returns Country{"_"}Unknown. Otherwise, the result is an upper-case string representation of an ISO 3166-1:2020 alpha-2 code that identifies a country.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Some common country codes are: "CA" &ndash; Canada; "FR" &ndash; France; "DE" &ndash; Germany; "IT" &ndash; Italy; "ES" &ndash; Spain; "GB" &ndash; United Kingdom; "US" &ndash; United States. These are the same codes as used by POSIX systems. We didn't include any country constants for the same reasons that we didn't include any language constants. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>12.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0127-2", "AI05-0233-1"]} />
Package Locales is new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>12.c/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0037-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Types Language{"_"}Code and Country{"_"}Code are defined with predicates rather than constrained components so that they can be converted to/from type String. This changes the exception raised from Constraint{"_"}Error to Assertion{"_"}Error if an assignment is attempted with an incorrect value. This could only matter if there is a handler specifically for Constraint{"_"}Error surrounding this assignment; as this exception raise is certainly caused by a bug (why would anyone want to use invalid language or country codes?), such a handler seems very unlikely. (In addition, this is a new Ada 2012 package, so there is not likely to be a lot of code using it.) <br />

---

# A.2. The Package Ada

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  122

# A.2. The Package Ada

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0414-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada{"\n"}   with Pure is{"\n"}end Ada;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0414-1"]} />
<p>Ada serves as the parent of most of the other language-defined library units; its declaration is empty. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>In the standard mode, it is illegal to compile a child of package Ada. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The intention is that mentioning, say, Ada.Text{"_"}IO in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> is guaranteed (at least in the standard mode) to refer to the standard version of Ada.Text{"_"}IO. The user can compile a root library unit Text{"_"}IO that has no relation to the standard version of Text{"_"}IO. <br />

<MarginText>4.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that Ada can have non-language-defined grandchildren, assuming the implementation allows it. Also, packages System and Interfaces can have children, assuming the implementation allows it. <br />

<MarginText>4.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>An implementation will typically support a nonstandard mode in which compiling the language defined library units is allowed. Whether or not this mode is made available to users is up to the implementer.<br />

<MarginText>4.d</MarginText>
An implementation could theoretically have private children of Ada, since that would be semantically neutral. However, a programmer cannot compile such a library unit. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>4.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new to Ada 95. <br />

---

# A.3. Character Handling

# A.3. Character Handling

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01", "AI05-0243-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>This subclause presents the packages related to character processing: an empty declared pure package Characters and child packages Characters.Handling and Characters.Latin{"_"}1. The package Characters.Handling provides classification and conversion functions for Character data, and some simple functions for dealing with Wide{"_"}Character and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Character data. The child package Characters.Latin{"_"}1 declares a set of constants initialized to values of type Character. <br /></p>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>1.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new to Ada 95. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>1.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
Included Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Character in this description; the individual changes are documented as extensions as needed. <br />

<a id="Subclause_A.3.1"></a>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>7/3_A.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00395-01", "AI05-0185-1"]} />
<p>If an implementation chooses to provide implementation-defined operations on Wide{"_"}Character or Wide{"_"}String (such as collating and sorting, etc.) it should do so by providing child units of Wide{"_"}Characters. Similarly if it chooses to provide implementation-defined operations on Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Character or Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String it should do so by providing child units of Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Characters. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2_A.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Implementation-defined operations on Wide{"_"}Character, Wide{"_"}String, Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Character, and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String should be child units of Wide{"_"}Characters or Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Characters.<br />

<MarginText>19.a/2_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00395-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code> for Ada.Characters.Conversions is needed for the definition of the obsolescent functions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.14">J.14</a>). It would be odd to put this clause into <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.14">J.14</a> as it was not present in Ada 95, and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0294">with_clause</a></code>s are semantically neutral to clients anyway. <br />

<MarginText>20_A.3.2</MarginText>
<p>In the description below for each function that returns a Boolean result, the effect is described in terms of the conditions under which the value True is returned. If these conditions are not met, then the function returns False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21_A.3.2</MarginText>
<p>Each of the following classification functions has a formal Character parameter, Item, and returns a Boolean result. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Control </dt>
<dl>
<dd>True if Item is a control character. A <i>control character</i> is a character whose position is in one of the ranges 0..31 or 127..159.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>23_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Graphic </dt>
<dd>True if Item is a graphic character. A <i>graphic character</i> is a character whose position is in one of the ranges 32..126 or 160..255.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>24_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Letter </dt>
<dd>True if Item is a letter. A <i>letter</i> is a character that is in one of the ranges 'A'..'Z' or 'a'..'z', or whose position is in one of the ranges 192..214, 216..246, or 248..255.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>25_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Lower </dt>
<dd>True if Item is a lower-case letter. A <i>lower-case letter</i> is a character that is in the range 'a'..'z', or whose position is in one of the ranges 223..246 or 248..255.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>26_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Upper</dt>
<dd>True if Item is an upper-case letter. An <i>upper-case letter</i> is a character that is in the range 'A'..'Z' or whose position is in one of the ranges 192..214 or 216.. 222.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>27_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Basic </dt>
<dd>True if Item is a basic letter. A <i>basic letter</i> is a character that is in one of the ranges 'A'..'Z' and 'a'..'z', or that is one of the following: 'Æ', 'æ', 'Ð', 'ð', 'Þ', 'þ', or 'ß'.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>28_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Digit </dt>
<dd>True if Item is a decimal digit. A <i>decimal digit</i> is a character in the range '0'..'9'.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>29_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Decimal{"_"}Digit </dt>
<dd>A renaming of Is{"_"}Digit.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>30_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Hexadecimal{"_"}Digit </dt>
<dd>True if Item is a hexadecimal digit. A <i>hexadecimal digit</i> is a character that is either a decimal digit or that is in one of the ranges 'A' .. 'F' or 'a' .. 'f'.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>31_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Alphanumeric </dt>
<dd>True if Item is an alphanumeric character. An <i>alphanumeric character</i> is a character that is either a letter or a decimal digit.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Special </dt>
<dd>True if Item is a special graphic character. A <i>special graphic character</i> is a graphic character that is not alphanumeric.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32.1/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0185-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Line{"_"}Terminator</dt>
<dd>True if Item is a character with position 10 .. 13 (Line{"_"}Feed, Line{"_"}Tabulation, Form{"_"}Feed, Carriage{"_"}Return) or 133 (Next{"_"}Line).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32.2/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0185-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Mark</dt>
<dd>Never True (no value of type Character has categories Mark, Non-Spacing or Mark, Spacing Combining).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32.3/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0185-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Other{"_"}Format</dt>
<dd>True if Item is a character with position 173 (Soft{"_"}Hyphen).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32.4/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0185-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Punctuation{"_"}Connector</dt>
<dd>True if Item is a character with position 95 ('{"_"}', known as Low{"_"}Line or Underscore).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32.5/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0185-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}Space</dt>
<dd>True if Item is a character with position 32 (' ') or 160 (No{"_"}Break{"_"}Space).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32.6/5_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0004-1", "AI12-0263-1", "AI12-0439-1", "AI12-0450-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}NFKC</dt>
<dd>True if Item can be present in a string normalized to Normalization Form KC (as defined by Clause 22 of ISO/IEC 10646:2020); this includes all characters except those with positions 160, 168, 170, 175, 178, 179, 180, 181, 184, 185, 186, 188, 189, and 190. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>33_A.3.2</MarginText>
<p>Each of the names To{"_"}Lower, To{"_"}Upper, and To{"_"}Basic refers to two functions: one that converts from Character to Character, and the other that converts from String to String. The result of each Character-to-Character function is described below, in terms of the conversion applied to Item, its formal Character parameter. The result of each String-to-String conversion is obtained by applying to each element of the function's String parameter the corresponding Character-to-Character conversion; the result is the null String if the value of the formal parameter is the null String. The lower bound of the result String is 1. <br /></p>

<MarginText>34_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>To{"_"}Lower</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Returns the corresponding lower-case value for Item if Is{"_"}Upper(Item), and returns Item otherwise.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>35_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>To{"_"}Upper</dt>
<dd>Returns the corresponding upper-case value for Item if Is{"_"}Lower(Item) and Item has an upper-case form, and returns Item otherwise. The lower case letters 'ß' and 'ÿ' do not have upper case forms.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>36_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>To{"_"}Basic</dt>
<dd>Returns the letter corresponding to Item but with no diacritical mark, if Item is a letter but not a basic letter; returns Item otherwise. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>37_A.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The following set of functions test for membership in the ISO 646 character range, or convert between ISO 646 and Character. <br /></p>

<MarginText>38_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}ISO{"_"}646</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The function whose formal parameter, Item, is of type Character returns True if Item is in the subtype ISO{"_"}646.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>39_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Is{"_"}ISO{"_"}646</dt>
<dd>The function whose formal parameter, Item, is of type String returns True if Is{"_"}ISO{"_"}646(Item(I)) is True for each I in Item'Range.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>40_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>To{"_"}ISO{"_"}646</dt>
<dd>The function whose first formal parameter, Item, is of type Character returns Item if Is{"_"}ISO{"_"}646(Item), and returns the Substitute ISO{"_"}646 character otherwise.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>41_A.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>To{"_"}ISO{"_"}646</dt>
<dd>The function whose first formal parameter, Item, is of type String returns the String whose Range is 1..Item'Length and each of whose elements is given by To{"_"}ISO{"_"}646 of the corresponding element in Item. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<p><i>Paragraphs 42 through 49 were deleted.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>50_A.3.2</MarginText>
NOTE 1   A basic letter is a letter without a diacritical mark.<br />

<MarginText>51_A.3.2</MarginText>
NOTE 2   Except for the hexadecimal digits, basic letters, and ISO{"_"}646 characters, the categories identified in the classification functions form a strict hierarchy: <br />

<MarginText>52_A.3.2</MarginText>
&mdash; Control characters<br />

<MarginText>53_A.3.2</MarginText>
&mdash; Graphic characters<br />

<MarginText>54_A.3.2</MarginText>
	&mdash; Alphanumeric characters<br />

<MarginText>55_A.3.2</MarginText>
		&mdash; Letters<br />

<MarginText>56_A.3.2</MarginText>
			&mdash; Upper-case letters<br />

<MarginText>57_A.3.2</MarginText>
			&mdash; Lower-case letters<br />

<MarginText>58_A.3.2</MarginText>
		&mdash; Decimal digits<br />

<MarginText>59_A.3.2</MarginText>
	&mdash; Special graphic characters<br />

<MarginText>59.a_A.3.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Thus each Character value is either a control character or a graphic character but not both; each graphic character is either an alphanumeric or special graphic but not both; each alphanumeric is either a letter or decimal digit but not both; each letter is either upper case or lower case but not both.<br />

<MarginText>60/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0114-1"]} />
NOTE 3   There are certain characters which are defined to be lower case letters by ISO 10646 and are therefore allowed in identifiers, but are not considered lower case letters by Ada.Characters.Handling.<br />

<MarginText>60.a/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0114-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is to maintain runtime compatibility with the Ada 95 definitions of these functions. We don't list the exact characters involved because they're likely to change in future character set standards; the list for ISO 10646:2011 can be found in . <br />

<MarginText>60.b/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>No version of Characters.Handling is intended to do portable (Ada-version independent) manipulation of Ada identifiers. The classification given by Wide{"_"}Characters.Handling will be correct for the current implementation for Ada 2012 identifiers, but it might not be correct for a different implementation or version of Ada. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>60.c/2_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00362-01"]} />
Characters.Handling is now Pure, so it can be used in pure units. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>60.d/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0185-1"]} />
Added additional classification routines so that Characters.Handling has all of the routines available in Wide{"_"}Characters.Handling. If Characters.Handling is referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, and an entity <i>E</i> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> that is the same as one of the new functions is defined in a package that is also referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, the entity <i>E</i> may no longer be use-visible, resulting in errors. This should be rare and is easily fixed if it does occur. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>60.e/2_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01", "AI95-00395-01"]} />
The conversion functions are made obsolescent; a more complete set is available in Characters.Conversions &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.3#Subclause_A.3.4">A.3.4</a>.<br />

<MarginText>60.f/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
We no longer talk about localized character sets; these are a nonstandard mode, which is none of our business. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>60.g/3_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0114-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a note to clarify that these functions don't have any relationship to the characters allowed in identifiers. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>60.h/5_A.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0004-1"]} />
Added an additional classification routine Is{"_"}NFKC. Therefore, a use clause conflict is possible; see the introduction of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a> for more on this topic. <br />

<a id="Subclause_A.3.3"></a>

## A.3.3  The Package Characters.Latin_1

<MarginText>1_A.3.3</MarginText>
<p>The package Characters.Latin{"_"}1 declares constants for characters in ISO 8859-1. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a_A.3.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The constants for the ISO 646 characters could have been declared as renamings of objects declared in package ASCII, as opposed to explicit constants. The main reason for explicit constants was for consistency of style with the upper-half constants, and to avoid emphasizing the package ASCII.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>27_A.3.3</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may provide additional packages as children of Ada.Characters, to declare names for the symbols of the local character set or other character sets. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>27.a/3_A.3.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0181-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Soft{"_"}Hyphen is not a graphic character, and thus a character literal for it is illegal. So we have to use the position value. This makes no semantic change to users of the constant. <br />

Machine-readable (and normative!) versions of this can be found as Character Decomposition Mapping, described in file <a href="http://www.unicode.org/Public/UCD/latest/ucd/UnicodeData.txt">http://www.unicode.org/Public/UCD/latest/ucd/UnicodeData.txt</a>, field 5 (which is the 6th item, Unicode counts from zero). <br />

<MarginText>51.2/5_A.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0004-1", "AI12-0263-1", "AI12-0439-1", "AI12-0450-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns True if the Wide{"_"}Character designated by Item can be present in a string normalized to Normalization Form KC (as defined by Clause 22 of ISO/IEC 10646:2020), otherwise returns False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>51.a/5_A.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Wide{"_"}Characters for which this function returns False are not allowed in identifiers (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3">2.3</a>) even if they are categorized as letters or digits. <br />

<MarginText>51.b/5_A.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>This function returns False if the Unicode property NFKC Quick Check (NFKC{"_"}QC in the files) has the value No. See the Implementation Notes in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3">2.3</a> for the source of this property. <br />

<MarginText>51.c/5_A.3.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A string for which Is{"_"}NFKC is true for every character may still not be in Normalization Form KC, as Is{"_"}NFKC returns true for characters that are dependent on characters around them as to whether they are removed by normalization. Ada does not provide a full normalization operation (it is complex and expensive). <br />

function To{"_"}Lower (Item : Wide{"_"}Character) return Wide{"_"}Character;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>55/5_A.3.5</MarginText>

If the Simple Lowercase Mapping does not exist for the Wide{"_"}Character designated by Item, then the value of Item is returned.<br /></p>

<MarginText>55.a/5_A.3.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0263-1", "AI12-0450-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The &ldquo;documents referenced&rdquo; means Unicode, Chapter 4 (specifically, section 4.2 &mdash; Case). The case mappings come from Unicode as ISO/IEC 10646:2020 does not include complete case mappings. See the Implementation Notes in subclause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.4">1.1.4</a> for machine-readable versions of both Uppercase and Lowercase mappings. <br />

The result is the null Wide{"_"}String if the value of the formal parameter is the null Wide{"_"}String. The lower bound of the result Wide{"_"}String is 1.<br /></p>
