<a id="Subclause_A.8.2"></a>

## A.8.2  File Management

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1/5_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>The procedures and functions described in this subclause provide for the control of external files; their declarations are repeated in each of the packages for sequential, direct, text, and stream input-output. For text input-output, the procedures Create, Open, and Reset have additional effects described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.10#Subclause_A.10.2">A.10.2</a>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Create(File : in out File{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                 Mode : in File{"_"}Mode := default{"_"}mode;{"\n"}                 Name : in String := "";{"\n"}                 Form : in String := "");{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3/2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00283-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Establishes a new external file, with the given name and form, and associates this external file with the given file. The given file is left open. The current mode of the given file is set to the given access mode. The default access mode is the mode Out{"_"}File for sequential, stream, and text input-output; it is the mode Inout{"_"}File for direct input-output. For direct access, the size of the created file is implementation defined.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/4_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For a direct file, the initial value of current index is 1 (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.8">A.8</a>). <br />

<MarginText>4_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">A null string for Name specifies an external file that is not accessible after the completion of the main program (a temporary file). A null string for Form specifies the use of the default options of the implementation for the external file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the given file is already open. The exception Name{"_"}Error is propagated if the string given as Name does not allow the identification of an external file. The exception Use{"_"}Error is propagated if, for the specified mode, the external environment does not support creation of an external file with the given name (in the absence of Name{"_"}Error) and form.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Open(File : in out File{"_"}Type;{"\n"}               Mode : in File{"_"}Mode;{"\n"}               Name : in String;{"\n"}               Form : in String := "");{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>7_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Associates the given file with an existing external file having the given name and form, and sets the current mode of the given file to the given mode. The given file is left open.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/4_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For a direct file, the initial value of current index is 1 (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.8">A.8</a>). <br />

<MarginText>8_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the given file is already open. The exception Name{"_"}Error is propagated if the string given as Name does not allow the identification of an external file; in particular, this exception is propagated if no external file with the given name exists. The exception Use{"_"}Error is propagated if, for the specified mode, the external environment does not support opening for an external file with the given name (in the absence of Name{"_"}Error) and form.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Close(File : in out File{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Severs the association between the given file and its associated external file. The given file is left closed. In addition, for sequential files, if the file being closed has mode Out{"_"}File or Append{"_"}File, then the last element written since the most recent open or reset is the last element that can be read from the file. If no elements have been written and the file mode is Out{"_"}File, then the closed file is empty. If no elements have been written and the file mode is Append{"_"}File, then the closed file is unchanged.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the given file is not open.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Delete(File : in out File{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Deletes the external file associated with the given file. The given file is closed, and the external file ceases to exist.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the given file is not open. The exception Use{"_"}Error is propagated if deletion of the external file is not supported by the external environment.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Reset(File : in out File{"_"}Type; Mode : in File{"_"}Mode);{"\n"}procedure Reset(File : in out File{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16/2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00085-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Resets the given file so that reading from its elements can be restarted from the beginning of the external file (for modes In{"_"}File and Inout{"_"}File), and so that writing to its elements can be restarted at the beginning of the external file (for modes Out{"_"}File and Inout{"_"}File) or after the last element of the external file (for mode Append{"_"}File). In particular, for direct access this means that the current index is set to one. If a Mode parameter is supplied, the current mode of the given file is set to the given mode. In addition, for sequential files, if the given file has mode Out{"_"}File or Append{"_"}File when Reset is called, the last element written since the most recent open or reset is the last element that can be read from the external file. If no elements have been written and the file mode is Out{"_"}File, the reset file is empty. If no elements have been written and the file mode is Append{"_"}File, then the reset file is unchanged.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the file is not open. The exception Use{"_"}Error is propagated if the external environment does not support resetting for the external file and, also, if the external environment does not support resetting to the specified mode for the external file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Mode(File : in File{"_"}Type) return File{"_"}Mode;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>19_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Returns the current mode of the given file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the file is not open.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Name(File : in File{"_"}Type) return String;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>22/2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00248-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns a string which uniquely identifies the external file currently associated with the given file (and may thus be used in an Open operation).<br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00248-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Retrieving the full path can be accomplished by passing the result of Name to Directories.Full{"_"}Name (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.16">A.16</a>). It is important to drop the requirement on Name, as the only way to accomplish this requirement given that the current directory can be changed with package Directories is to store the full path when the file is opened. That's expensive, and it's better for users that need the full path to explicitly request it. <br />

<MarginText>23_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the given file is not open. The exception Use{"_"}Error is propagated if the associated external file is a temporary file that cannot be opened by any name.<br /></p>

<MarginText>24_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Form(File : in File{"_"}Type) return String;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>25_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Returns the form string for the external file currently associated with the given file. If an external environment allows alternative specifications of the form (for example, abbreviations using default options), the string returned by the function should correspond to a full specification (that is, it should indicate explicitly all options selected, including default options).<br /></p>

<MarginText>26_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the given file is not open.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27_A.8.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Is{"_"}Open(File : in File{"_"}Type) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>28/3_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Returns True if the file is open (that is, if it is associated with an external file); otherwise, returns False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>28.1/4_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0130-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Flush(File : in File{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>28.2/4_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The Flush procedure synchronizes the external file with the internal file (by flushing any internal buffers) without closing the file. For a direct file, the current index is unchanged; for a stream file (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.12#Subclause_A.12.1">A.12.1</a>), the current position is unchanged.<br /></p>

<MarginText>28.3/4_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if the file is not open. The exception Mode{"_"}Error is propagated if the mode of the file is In{"_"}File.<br /></p>

<MarginText>28.4/5_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0021-1"]} />
<p>The nested package Wide{"_"}File{"_"}Names provides operations equivalent to the operations of the same name of the outer package except that Wide{"_"}String is used instead of String for the name and form of the external file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>28.a/5_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0021-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The expectation is that if one opens a file with this subpackage and then requests the name with Name from this subpackage, the result will include the same Wide{"_"}Characters that were used to open the file (rather than some encoded form). Since file names are completely implementation-defined, we cannot say this normatively. We have no expectations when retrieving the name of a file opened with this package using the String Name. Similar considerations apply to the nested package Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}File{"_"}Names (see below). <br />

<MarginText>28.5/5_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0021-1"]} />
<p>The nested package Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}File{"_"}Names provides operations equivalent to the operations of the same name of the outer package except that Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String is used instead of String for the name and form of the external file.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>29_A.8.2</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may propagate Name{"_"}Error or Use{"_"}Error if an attempt is made to use an I/O feature that cannot be supported by the implementation due to limitations in the external environment. Any such restriction should be documented. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>29.a/2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00085-01"]} />
Clarified that Reset affects and depends on the external file.<br />

<MarginText>29.b/2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00248-01"]} />
Removed the requirement for Name to return a full path; this is now accomplished by Directories.Full{"_"}Name(Name(File)) (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.16">A.16</a>). This is not documented as an inconsistency, because there is no requirement for implementations to change &mdash; the Ada 95 behavior is still allowed, it just is no longer required.<br />

<MarginText>29.c/2_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00283-01"]} />
Added text to specify the default mode for a stream file. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>29.d/4_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0130-1"]} />
Procedure Flush is now defined here, so it can be used for all of the I/O packages.<br />

<MarginText>29.e/5_A.8.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0021-1"]} />
The nested Wide{"_"}File{"_"}Names and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}File{"_"}Names packages are now described here. <br />

<a id="Subclause_A.8.3"></a>

## A.8.3  Sequential Input-Output Operations

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_A.8.3</MarginText>
<p>The operations available for sequential input and output are described in this subclause. The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if any of these operations is attempted for a file that is not open. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_A.8.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Read(File : in File{"_"}Type; Item : out Element{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_A.8.3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of mode In{"_"}File. Reads an element from the given file, and returns the value of this element in the Item parameter. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a_A.8.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We considered basing Sequential{"_"}IO.Read on Element{"_"}Type'Read from an implicit stream associated with the sequential file. However, Element{"_"}Type'Read is a type-related attribute, whereas Sequential{"_"}IO should take advantage of the particular constraints of the actual subtype corresponding to Element{"_"}Type to minimize the size of the external file. Furthermore, forcing the implementation of Sequential{"_"}IO to be based on Element{"_"}Type'Read would create an upward incompatibility since existing data files written by an Ada 83 program using Sequential{"_"}IO might not be readable by the identical program built with an Ada 95 implementation of Sequential{"_"}IO.<br />

<MarginText>3.b_A.8.3</MarginText>
An Ada 95 implementation might still use an implementation-defined attribute analogous to 'Read to implement the procedure Read, but that attribute will likely have to be subtype-specific rather than type-related, and it need not be user-specifiable. Such an attribute will presumably be needed to implement the generic package Storage{"_"}IO (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.9">A.9</a>). <br />

<MarginText>4_A.8.3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Mode{"_"}Error is propagated if the mode is not In{"_"}File. The exception End{"_"}Error is propagated if no more elements can be read from the given file. The exception Data{"_"}Error can be propagated if the element read cannot be interpreted as a value of the subtype Element{"_"}Type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.13">A.13</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.13">Exceptions in Input-Output</a>&rdquo;). <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a_A.8.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Data{"_"}Error need not be propagated if the check is too complex. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.13">A.13</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.13">Exceptions in Input-Output</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>5_A.8.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Write(File : in File{"_"}Type; Item : in Element{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6_A.8.3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of mode Out{"_"}File or Append{"_"}File. Writes the value of Item to the given file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7_A.8.3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Mode{"_"}Error is propagated if the mode is not Out{"_"}File or Append{"_"}File. The exception Use{"_"}Error is propagated if the capacity of the external file is exceeded.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8_A.8.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function End{"_"}Of{"_"}File(File : in File{"_"}Type) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9/3_A.8.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of mode In{"_"}File. Returns True if no more elements can be read from the given file; otherwise, returns False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10_A.8.3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Mode{"_"}Error is propagated if the mode is not In{"_"}File. <br /></p>

## A.8.5  Direct Input-Output Operations

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p>The operations available for direct input and output are described in this subclause. The exception Status{"_"}Error is propagated if any of these operations is attempted for a file that is not open. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_A.8.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Read(File : in File{"_"}Type; Item : out Element{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                                    From : in  Positive{"_"}Count);{"\n"}procedure Read(File : in File{"_"}Type; Item : out Element{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>3_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of mode In{"_"}File or Inout{"_"}File. In the case of the first form, sets the current index of the given file to the index value given by the parameter From. Then (for both forms) returns, in the parameter Item, the value of the element whose position in the given file is specified by the current index of the file; finally, increases the current index by one.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Mode{"_"}Error is propagated if the mode of the given file is Out{"_"}File. The exception End{"_"}Error is propagated if the index to be used exceeds the size of the external file. The exception Data{"_"}Error can be propagated if the element read cannot be interpreted as a value of the subtype Element{"_"}Type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.13">A.13</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>5_A.8.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Write(File : in File{"_"}Type; Item : in Element{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                                     To   : in Positive{"_"}Count);{"\n"}procedure Write(File : in File{"_"}Type; Item : in Element{"_"}Type);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of mode Inout{"_"}File or Out{"_"}File. In the case of the first form, sets the index of the given file to the index value given by the parameter To. Then (for both forms) gives the value of the parameter Item to the element whose position in the given file is specified by the current index of the file; finally, increases the current index by one.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Mode{"_"}Error is propagated if the mode of the given file is In{"_"}File. The exception Use{"_"}Error is propagated if the capacity of the external file is exceeded.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8_A.8.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Set{"_"}Index(File : in File{"_"}Type; To : in Positive{"_"}Count);{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of any mode. Sets the current index of the given file to the given index value (which may exceed the current size of the file).<br /></p>

<MarginText>10_A.8.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Index(File : in File{"_"}Type) return Positive{"_"}Count;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>11_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of any mode. Returns the current index of the given file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12_A.8.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Size(File : in File{"_"}Type) return Count;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>13_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of any mode. Returns the current size of the external file that is associated with the given file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14_A.8.5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function End{"_"}Of{"_"}File(File : in File{"_"}Type) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>15/3_A.8.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Operates on a file of mode In{"_"}File or Inout{"_"}File. Returns True if the current index exceeds the size of the external file; otherwise, returns False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16_A.8.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The exception Mode{"_"}Error is propagated if the mode of the given file is Out{"_"}File.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17_A.8.5</MarginText>
NOTE   Append{"_"}File mode is not supported for the generic package Direct{"_"}IO. <br />

# A.9. The Generic Package Storage_IO

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.9.mdx

sidebar_position:  129

# A.9. The Generic Package Storage_IO

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>The generic package Storage{"_"}IO provides for reading from and writing to an in-memory buffer. This generic package supports the construction of user-defined input-output packages. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This package exists to allow the portable construction of user-defined direct-access-oriented input-output packages. The Write procedure writes a value of type Element{"_"}Type into a Storage{"_"}Array of size Buffer{"_"}Size, flattening out any implicit levels of indirection used in the representation of the type. The Read procedure reads a value of type Element{"_"}Type from the buffer, reconstructing any implicit levels of indirection used in the representation of the type. It also properly initializes any type tags that appear within the value, presuming that the buffer was written by a different program and that tag values for the&ldquo;same&rdquo; type might vary from one executable to another. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The generic library package Storage{"_"}IO has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.IO{"_"}Exceptions;{"\n"}with System.Storage{"_"}Elements;{"\n"}generic{"\n"}   type Element{"_"}Type is private;{"\n"}package Ada.Storage{"_"}IO{"\n"}   with Preelaborate, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
   Buffer{"_"}Size : constant System.Storage{"_"}Elements.Storage{"_"}Count :={"\n"}      implementation-defined;{"\n"}   subtype Buffer{"_"}Type is{"\n"}      System.Storage{"_"}Elements.Storage{"_"}Array(1..Buffer{"_"}Size);{"\n"}
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
   -- Input and output operations{"\n"}
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
   procedure Read (Buffer : in  Buffer{"_"}Type; Item : out Element{"_"}Type);{"\n"}
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
   procedure Write(Buffer : out Buffer{"_"}Type; Item : in  Element{"_"}Type);{"\n"}
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
   -- Exceptions{"\n"}
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
   Data{"_"}Error   : exception renames IO{"_"}Exceptions.Data{"_"}Error;{"\n"}end Ada.Storage{"_"}IO;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>In each instance, the constant Buffer{"_"}Size has a value that is the size (in storage elements) of the buffer required to represent the content of an object of subtype Element{"_"}Type, including any implicit levels of indirection used by the implementation. The Read and Write procedures of Storage{"_"}IO correspond to the Read and Write procedures of Direct{"_"}IO (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.8#Subclause_A.8.4">A.8.4</a>), but with the content of the Item parameter being read from or written into the specified Buffer, rather than an external file.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>As with Direct{"_"}IO, the Element{"_"}Type formal of Storage{"_"}IO does not have an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code> so that there is a well-defined upper bound on the size of the buffer needed to hold the content of an object of the formal subtype (i.e. Buffer{"_"}Size). If there are no implicit levels of indirection, Buffer{"_"}Size will typically equal: <br />

<MarginText>10.b</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
(Element{"_"}Type'Size + System.Storage{"_"}Unit - 1) / System.Storage{"_"}Unit{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The value of Buffer{"_"}Size in Storage{"_"}IO.<br />

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
NOTE   A buffer used for Storage{"_"}IO holds only one element at a time; an external file used for Direct{"_"}IO holds a sequence of elements. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>11.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
Storage{"_"}IO is new in Ada 95. <br />

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In running text, we generally leave out the &ldquo;Ada.&rdquo; when referring to a child of Ada. <br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We had no strict rule for which of Ada, Interfaces, or System should be the parent of a given library unit. However, we have tried to place as many things as possible under Ada, except that interfacing is a separate category, and we have tried to place library units whose use is highly nonportable under System. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01", "AI12-0052-1", "AI12-0114-1", "AI12-0200-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>The implementation shall ensure that concurrent calls on any two (possibly the same) language-defined subprograms perform as specified, so long as all pairs of objects (one from each call) that are either denoted by parameters that can be passed by reference, or are designated by parameters of an access type, are nonoverlapping. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0052-1", "AI12-0114-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>So long as the parameters are disjoint, concurrent calls on the same language-defined subprogram, and concurrent calls on two different language-defined subprograms are required to work. But concurrent calls operating on overlapping objects (be they of the same or different language-defined subprograms) are <i>not</i> required to work (being an erroneous use of shared variables) unless both subprograms are required to pass the associated parameter by-copy.<br />

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
For example, simultaneous calls to Text{"_"}IO.Put will work properly, so long as they are going to two different files. On the other hand, simultaneous output to the same file constitutes erroneous use of shared variables. <br />

<MarginText>3.b</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>Here, &ldquo;language defined subprogram&rdquo; means a language defined library subprogram, a subprogram declared in the visible part of a language defined library package, an instance of a language defined generic library subprogram, or a subprogram declared in the visible part of an instance of a language defined generic library package. <br />

<MarginText>3.b.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0052-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This rule applies to all language-defined subprograms, including those defined in packages that manage some global state (like environment variables or the current directory). Unless specified above, such subprograms need to work when the explicit parameters are not overlapping; in particular, the existence of the global state is not considered.<br />

<MarginText>3.c/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0052-1"]} />
The rule implies that any data local to the private part or body of the package (including global state as described above) has to be somehow protected against simultaneous access. <br />

<MarginText>3.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0052-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<p>For the purpose of determining whether concurrent calls on text input-output subprograms are required to perform as specified above, when calling a subprogram within Text{"_"}IO or its children that implicitly operates on one of the default input-output files, the subprogram is considered to have a parameter of Current{"_"}Input or Current{"_"}Output (as appropriate).<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0048-1"]} />
<p>If a descendant of a language-defined tagged type is declared, the implementation shall ensure that each inherited language-defined subprogram behaves as described in this Reference Manual. In particular, overriding a language-defined subprogram shall not alter the effect of any inherited language-defined subprogram. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.d/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This means that internally the implementation must not do redispatching unless it is required by the Standard. So when we say that some subprogram Bar is equivalent to Foo, overriding Foo for a derived type doesn't change the semantics of Bar, and in particular it means that Bar may no longer be equivalent to Foo. The word &ldquo;equivalent&rdquo; is always a bit of a lie anyway. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>The implementation may restrict the replacement of language-defined compilation units. The implementation may restrict children of language-defined library units (other than Standard). <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, the implementation may say, &ldquo;you cannot compile a library unit called System&rdquo; or &ldquo;you cannot compile a child of package System&rdquo; or &ldquo;if you compile a library unit called System, it has to be a package, and it has to contain at least the following declarations: ...&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>4.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0112-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Implementations are of course allowed to make changes to the specifications of language-defined units, so long as those changes are semantically neutral (that is, no program could change legality or effect because of the changes). In particular, an implementation can <b>with</b> additional units (especially implementation-defined units) so long as those units do not change the elaboration of the language-defined unit.<br />

<MarginText>4.c/5</MarginText>
Similarly, an implementation can add postconditions to language-defined subprograms, so long as those postconditions always evaluate to True. This is useful if the implementation can use those postconditions for optimization. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>4.d</MarginText>
Many of Ada 83's language-defined library units are now children of Ada or System. For upward compatibility, these are renamed as root library units (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.1">J.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>4.e</MarginText>
The order and lettering of the annexes has been changed. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>4.f/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00081-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0047</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Units missing from the list of predefined units were added.<br />

<MarginText>4.g/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00424-01"]} />
Added new units to the list of predefined units. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>4.h/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0048-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added wording to ban redispatching unless it is explicitly required, in order to safeguard portability when overriding language-defined routines.<br />

<MarginText>4.i/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0060-1", "AI05-0206-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a permission to omit pragma Remote{"_"}Types from language-defined units if Annex E is not supported. This was later removed, as a better method of supporting the reason is now available. Note that this requires all implementations to provide minimal support for the Remote{"_"}Types categorization even if Annex E is not supported; being unable to compile language-defined units is not allowed.<br />

<MarginText>4.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0001-1", "AI05-0049-1", "AI05-0069-1", "AI05-0111-3", "AI05-0136-1", "AI05-0137-1", "AI05-0166-1", "AI05-0168-1"]} />
Added various new units to the list of predefined units. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>4.k/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
When a new entity <i>E</i> is added to a package <i>P</i> that is <b>use</b>d in client code, <i>use clause conflicts</i> are possible. Specifically, if <i>P</i> is referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, and an entity <i>F</i> with the same defining identifier as <i>E</i> is defined in some other package that is also referenced in a <i>use{"_"}clause</i>, the user-defined entity <i>F</i> may no longer be use-visible, resulting in errors. This is an incompatibility when the new entity is added to a language-defined package. Note that use clause conflicts are rare and easily fixed by using an expanded name. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>4.k.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0052-1", "AI12-0114-1", "AI12-0159-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> The rules requiring concurrent access of language-defined subprograms were expanded to include implicit Text{"_"}IO objects, overlapping objects designated by parameters of an access type, and simultaneous calls on different language-defined subprograms. While this might change behavior of some programs, it would do so by eliminating erroneous execution, so we don't consider this an inconsistency.<br />

<MarginText>4.k.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0200-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The rules requiring concurrent access of language-defined subprograms were clarified further.<br />

<MarginText>4.l/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0021-1", "AI12-0208-1", "AI12-0234-1", "AI12-0254-1", "AI12-0293-1", "AI12-0321-1", "AI12-0340-1"]} />
Added various new units to the list of predefined units. <br />

# B.1. Interfacing Aspects

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  141

# B.1. Interfacing Aspects

<MarginText>0.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An <i>interfacing</i> aspect is a representation aspect that is one of the aspects Import, Export, Link{"_"}Name, External{"_"}Name, or Convention.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>Specifying the Import aspect to have the value True is used to import an entity defined in a foreign language into an Ada program, thus allowing a foreign-language subprogram to be called from Ada, or a foreign-language variable to be accessed from Ada. In contrast, specifying the Export aspect to have the value True is used to export an Ada entity to a foreign language, thus allowing an Ada subprogram to be called from a foreign language, or an Ada object to be accessed from a foreign language. The Import and Export aspects are intended primarily for objects and subprograms, although implementations are allowed to support other entities. The Link{"_"}Name and External{"_"}Name aspects are used to specify the link name and external name, respectively, to be used to identify imported or exported entities in the external environment. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Import: </b>Entity is imported from another language.<br />

<MarginText>1.b/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Export: </b>Entity is exported to another language.<br />

<MarginText>1.c/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>External{"_"}Name: </b>Name used to identify an imported or exported entity.<br />

<MarginText>1.d/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Link{"_"}Name: </b>Linker symbol used to identify an imported or exported entity.<br />

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The Convention aspect is used to indicate that an Ada entity should use the conventions of another language. It is intended primarily for types and &ldquo;callback&rdquo; subprograms. For example, &ldquo;<b>with</b> Convention ={">"} Fortran&rdquo; on the declaration of an array type Matrix implies that Matrix should be represented according to the conventions of the supported Fortran implementation, namely column-major order.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Convention: </b>Calling convention or other convention used for interfacing to other languages.<br />

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Linker{"_"}Options is used to specify the system linker parameters necessary when a given compilation unit is included in a partition.<br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Linker{"_"}Options is as follows: <br /></p>

<p class="Indented2"><i>Paragraphs 5 through 7 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Linker{"_"}Options(<i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Linker{"_"}Options is allowed only at the place of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00036-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2"><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i>{"{"}<i>8652/0058</i>{"}"} <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>9.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The Import and Export aspects are of type Boolean.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The Link{"_"}Name and External{"_"}Name aspects are of type String. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is no language-defined support for external or link names of type Wide{"_"}String, or of other string types. Implementations may, of course, have additional aspects for that purpose. Note that allowing both String and Wide{"_"}String in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> would cause ambiguities. <br />

<MarginText>10.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for the <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in pragma Linker{"_"}Options is String.<br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The aspect Convention shall be specified by a <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> which shall be the name of a <i>convention</i>. The convention names are implementation defined, except for certain language-defined ones, such as Ada and Intrinsic, as explained in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">Conformance Rules</a>&rdquo;. [Additional convention names generally represent the calling conventions of foreign languages, language implementations, or specific run-time models.] The convention of a callable entity is its <i>calling convention</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined convention names.<br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We considered representing the convention names using an enumeration type declared in System. Then, <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> would be changed to <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, and we would make its expected type be the enumeration type. We didn't do this because it seems to introduce extra complexity, and because the list of available languages is better represented as the list of children of package Interfaces &mdash; a more open-ended sort of list. <br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>If <i>L</i> is a <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> for a language, then a type T is said to be <i>compatible with convention L</i>, (alternatively, is said to be an <i>L-compatible type</i>) if any of the following conditions are met: <br /></p>

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>T is declared in a language interface package corresponding to <i>L</i> and is defined to be <i>L</i>-compatible (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3">B.3</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3#Subclause_B.3.1">B.3.1</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3#Subclause_B.3.2">B.3.2</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.4">B.4</a>, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.5">B.5</a>),<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<li>Convention <i>L</i> has been specified for T, and T is <i>eligible for convention L</i>; that is: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0135-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>T is an enumeration type such that all internal codes (whether assigned by default or explicitly) are within an implementation-defined range that includes at least the range of values 0 .. 2{"*"}{"*"}15&ndash;1;<br /></li>
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<li>T is an array type with either an unconstrained or statically-constrained first subtype, and its component type is <i>L</i>-compatible,<br /></li>
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<li>T is a record type that has no discriminants and that only has components with statically-constrained subtypes, and each component type is <i>L</i>-compatible,<br /></li>
<MarginText>17/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0002-1"]} />
<li>T is an access-to-object type, its designated type is <i>L</i>-compatible, and its designated subtype is not an unconstrained array subtype,<br /></li>
<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<li>T is an access-to-subprogram type, and its designated profile's parameter and result types are all <i>L</i>-compatible. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>T is derived from an <i>L</i>-compatible type,<br /></li>
<MarginText>19.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0207-1"]} />
<li>T is an anonymous access type, and T is eligible for convention <i>L</i>,<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>19.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We say this so that the presence of an anonymous access component does not necessarily prevent a type from being eligible for convention <i>L</i>. We want the anonymous access type to take the convention from the enclosing type, but if we only said that, the definition would be circular (one can only portably apply the convention <i>L</i> to a record type R if the components of R already have convention <i>L</i>; but the anonymous components of R have to take the convention from R). We include the part of about T being eligible for convention <i>L</i> so that we don't force convention <i>L</i> on some type that is incompatible with it. <br />

<MarginText>20</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The implementation permits T as an <i>L</i>-compatible type.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For example, an implementation might permit Integer as a C-compatible type, though the C type to which it corresponds might be different in different environments. <br />

<MarginText>21/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If the Convention aspect is specified for a type, then the type shall either be compatible with or eligible for the specified convention. <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If a type is derived from an <i>L</i>-compatible type, the derived type is by default <i>L</i>-compatible, but it is also permitted to specify the Convention aspect for the derived type.<br />

<MarginText>21.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
It is permitted to specify the Convention aspect for an incomplete type, but in the complete declaration each component must be <i>L</i>-compatible.<br />

<MarginText>21.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
If each component of a record type is <i>L</i>-compatible, then the record type itself is only <i>L</i>-compatible if it has a specified Convention. <br />

<MarginText>21.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0207-1"]} />
<p>If convention <i>L</i> is specified for a type T, for each component of T that has an anonymous access type, the convention of the anonymous access type is <i>L</i>. If convention <i>L</i> is specified for an object that has an anonymous access type, the convention of the anonymous access type is <i>L</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.d/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This applies to both anonymous access-to-object and anonymous access-to-subprogram types. <br />

<MarginText>22/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>Notwithstanding any rule to the contrary, a declaration with a True Import aspect shall not have a completion. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For declarations of deferred constants and subprograms, we explicitly mention that no completion is allowed when aspect Import is True. For other declarations that require completions, we ignore the possibility of the aspect Import being True. Nevertheless, if an implementation chooses to allow specifying aspect Import to be True for the declaration of a task, protected type, incomplete type, private type, etc., it may do so, and the normal completion is then not allowed for that declaration. <br />

<MarginText>23/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An entity with a True Import aspect (or Export aspect) is said to be <i>imported</i> (respectively, <i>exported</i>). An entity shall not be both imported and exported.<br /></p>

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<p>The declaration of an imported object shall not include an explicit initialization expression. [Default initializations are not performed.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This follows from the &ldquo;Notwithstanding ...&rdquo; wording in the Dynamics Semantics paragraphs below. <br />

<MarginText>25/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The type of an imported or exported object shall be compatible with the specified Convention aspect, if any. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This implies, for example, that importing an Integer object might be illegal, whereas importing an object of type Interfaces.C.int would be permitted. <br />

<MarginText>26/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For an imported or exported subprogram, the result and parameter types shall each be compatible with the specified Convention aspect, if any.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> (if any) used to directly specify an Import, Export, External{"_"}Name, or Link{"_"}Name aspect shall be a static expression. The <i>string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Linker{"_"}Options shall be static. An External{"_"}Name or Link{"_"}Name aspect shall be specified only for an entity that is either imported or exported.<br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<p><i>Paragraphs 28 and 29 were deleted.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>30/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The Convention aspect represents the calling convention or representation convention of the entity. For an access-to-subprogram type, it represents the calling convention of designated subprograms. In addition: <br /></p>

<MarginText>31/3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A True Import aspect indicates that the entity is defined externally (that is, outside the Ada program). This aspect is never inherited; if not directly specified, the Import aspect is False.<br /></li>
<MarginText>32/3</MarginText>
<li>A True Export aspect indicates that the entity is used externally. This aspect is never inherited; if not directly specified, the Export aspect is False.<br /></li>
<MarginText>33/3</MarginText>
<li>For an entity with a True Import or Export aspect, an external name, link name, or both may also be specified. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>34</MarginText>
<p>An <i>external name</i> is a string value for the name used by a foreign language program either for an entity that an Ada program imports, or for referring to an entity that an Ada program exports.<br /></p>

<MarginText>35</MarginText>
<p>A <i>link name</i> is a string value for the name of an exported or imported entity, based on the conventions of the foreign language's compiler in interfacing with the system's linker tool.<br /></p>

<MarginText>36</MarginText>
<p>The meaning of link names is implementation defined. If neither a link name nor the Address attribute of an imported or exported entity is specified, then a link name is chosen in an implementation-defined manner, based on the external name if one is specified. <br /></p>

<MarginText>36.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The meaning of link names.<br />

<MarginText>36.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, an implementation might always prepend "{"_"}", and then pass it to the system linker. <br />

<MarginText>36.c</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The manner of choosing link names when neither the link name nor the address of an imported or exported entity is specified.<br />

<MarginText>36.d</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Normally, this will be the entity's defining name, or some simple transformation thereof. <br />

<MarginText>37</MarginText>
<p>Pragma Linker{"_"}Options has the effect of passing its string argument as a parameter to the system linker (if one exists), if the immediately enclosing compilation unit is included in the partition being linked. The interpretation of the string argument, and the way in which the string arguments from multiple Linker{"_"}Options pragmas are combined, is implementation defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>37.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The effect of pragma Linker{"_"}Options.<br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>38/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>Notwithstanding what this document says elsewhere, the elaboration of a declaration with a True Import aspect does not create the entity. Such an elaboration has no other effect than to allow the defining name to denote the external entity. <br /></p>

<MarginText>38.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This implies that default initializations are skipped. (Explicit initializations are illegal.) For example, an imported access object is <i>not</i> initialized to <b>null</b>.<br />

<MarginText>38.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>38.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This &ldquo;notwithstanding&rdquo; wording is better than saying &ldquo;unless aspect Import is True&rdquo; on every definition of elaboration. It says we recognize the contradiction, and this rule takes precedence. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>38.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00320-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0219-1"]} />
<p>It is the programmer's responsibility to ensure that the use of interfacing aspects does not violate Ada semantics; otherwise, program execution is erroneous. For example, passing an object with mode <b>in</b> to imported code that modifies it causes erroneous execution. Similarly, calling an imported subprogram that is not pure from a pure package causes erroneous execution. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>39/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If an implementation supports Export for a given language, then it should also allow the main subprogram to be written in that language. It should support some mechanism for invoking the elaboration of the Ada library units included in the system, and for invoking the finalization of the environment task. On typical systems, the recommended mechanism is to provide two subprograms whose link names are "adainit" and "adafinal". Adainit should contain the elaboration code for library units. Adafinal should contain the finalization code. These subprograms should have no effect the second and subsequent time they are called. <br /></p>

<MarginText>39.a.1/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If Export is supported for a language, the main program should be able to be written in that language. Subprograms named "adainit" and "adafinal" should be provided for elaboration and finalization of the environment task.<br />

<MarginText>39.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, if the main subprogram is written in C, it can call adainit before the first call to an Ada subprogram, and adafinal after the last. <br />

<MarginText>40/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>Automatic elaboration of preelaborated packages should be provided when specifying the Export aspect as True is supported. <br /></p>

<MarginText>40.a.1/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Automatic elaboration of preelaborated packages should be provided when specifying the Export aspect as True is supported.<br />

<MarginText>41/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0135-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>For each supported convention <i>L</i> other than Intrinsic, an implementation should support specifying the Import and Export aspects for objects of <i>L</i>-compatible types and for subprograms, and the Convention aspect for <i>L</i>-eligible types and for subprograms, presuming the other language has corresponding features. Specifying the Convention aspect should be supported for enumeration types whose internal codes fall within the range 0 .. 2{"*"}{"*"}15&ndash;1, but no recommendation is made for other scalar types. <br /></p>

<MarginText>41.a.1/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>For each supported convention <i>L</i> other than Intrinsic, specifying the aspects Import and Export should be supported for objects of <i>L</i>-compatible types and for subprograms, and aspect Convention should be supported for <i>L</i>-eligible types and for subprograms.<br />

<MarginText>41.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Specifying aspect Convention is not necessary for scalar types, since the language interface packages declare scalar types corresponding to those provided by the respective foreign languages. <br />

<MarginText>41.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>If an implementation supports interfacing to the C++ entities not supported by <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3">B.3</a>, it should do so via the convention identifier C{"_"}Plus{"_"}Plus (in additional to any C++-implementation-specific ones). <br />

<MarginText>41.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The reason for giving the advice about C++ is to encourage uniformity among implementations, given that the name of the language is not syntactically legal as an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>42/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 1   Implementations can place restrictions on interfacing aspects; for example, requiring each exported entity to be declared at the library level. <br />

<MarginText>42.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Arbitrary restrictions are allowed by <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>42.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Such a restriction might be to disallow them altogether. Alternatively, the implementation might allow them only for certain kinds of entities, or only for certain conventions. <br />

<MarginText>43/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
NOTE 2   The Convention aspect in combination with the Import aspect indicates the conventions for accessing external entities. It is possible that the actual entity is written in assembly language, but reflects the conventions of a particular language. For example, <b>with</b> Convention ={">"} Ada can be used to interface to an assembly language routine that obeys the Ada compiler's calling conventions.<br />

<MarginText>44/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 3   To obtain &ldquo;call-back&rdquo; to an Ada subprogram from a foreign language environment, the Convention aspect can be specified both for the access-to-subprogram type and the specific subprogram(s) to which 'Access is applied.<br />

<i>Paragraphs 45 and 46 were deleted.</i> <br />

<MarginText>47/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0449-1"]} />
NOTE 4   Machine code insertions can also be relevant for interfacing; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.8">13.8</a>. <br />

<MarginText>47.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The Intrinsic convention (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>) implies that the entity is somehow &ldquo;built in&rdquo; to the implementation. Thus, it generally does not make sense for users to specify Intrinsic along with specifying that the entity is imported. The intention is that only implementations will specify Intrinsic for an imported entity. The language also defines certain subprograms to be Intrinsic. <br />

<MarginText>47.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There are many imaginable interfacing aspects that don't make any sense. For example, setting the Convention of a protected procedure to Ada is probably wrong. Rather than enumerating all such cases, however, we leave it up to implementations to decide what is sensible. <br />

<MarginText>48/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
NOTE 5   If both External{"_"}Name and Link{"_"}Name are specified for a given entity, then the External{"_"}Name is ignored.<br />

<MarginText>49/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00320-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>50/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0080-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of interfacing aspects:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>51/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Fortran{"_"}Library is{"\n"}  function Sqrt (X : Float) return Float{"\n"}    with Import ={">"} True, Convention ={">"} Fortran;{"\n"}  type Matrix is array (Natural range {"<"}{">"}, Natural range {"<"}{">"}) of Float{"\n"}    with Convention ={">"} Fortran;{"\n"}  function Invert (M : Matrix) return Matrix{"\n"}    with Import ={">"} True, Convention ={">"} Fortran;{"\n"}end Fortran{"_"}Library;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>51.a</MarginText>
Interfacing pragmas are new to Ada 95. Pragma Import replaces Ada 83's pragma Interface. Existing implementations can continue to support pragma Interface for upward compatibility. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>51.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00036-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0058</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Import and Export work like a subprogram call; parameters cannot be omitted unless named notation is used. (Reordering is still not permitted, however.)<br />

<MarginText>51.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00320-01"]} />
Added wording to say all bets are off if foreign code doesn't follow the semantics promised by the Ada specifications. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>51.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0002-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Access types that designate unconstrained arrays are no longer defined to be <i>L</i>-compatible. Such access-to-arrays require bounds information, which is likely to be incompatible with a foreign language. The change will allow (but not require) compilers to reject bad uses, which probably will not work anyway. Note that implementations can still support any type that it wants as <i>L</i>-compatible; such uses will not be portable, however. As such, there should be little existing code that will be impacted (compilers probably already rejected cases that could not be translated, whether or not the language allowed doing so formally). <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>51.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
Aspects Convention, Import, Export, Link{"_"}Name, and External{"_"}Name are new; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Convention, Import, and Export are now obsolescent. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>51.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0207-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The convention of anonymous access components is that of the enclosing type (in Ada 2012, it was Ada). Similarly, the convention of the anonymous access type of an object is that of the object (again, in Ada 2012 it was Ada). While this is formally incompatible, it should be more useful in portable code; it makes little sense to have a component of an Ada access type in a record with a C convention. For most implementations, this will have no real effect as convention Ada anonymous access types were allowed as C-compatible anyway. But such code was not portable, as this was not required in Ada 2012. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>51.g/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0135-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a suggestion that convention be supported for enumeration types. This will make the use of enumeration types portable for implementations that support interfacing to a particular language. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>51.h/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0219-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added some examples to the erroneous execution text; this is a very important rule as it means that Ada compilers can assume that provided interfacing declarations reflect the actual foreign code. <br />

---

# B.2. The Package Interfaces

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  142

# B.2. The Package Interfaces

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>Package Interfaces is the parent of several library packages that declare types and other entities useful for interfacing to foreign languages. It also contains some implementation-defined types that are useful across more than one language (in particular for interfacing to assembly language). <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The contents of the visible part of package Interfaces and its language-defined descendants.<br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The library package Interfaces has the following skeletal declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0414-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Interfaces{"\n"}   with Pure is{"\n"}
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
   type Integer{"_"}n is range -2{"*"}{"*"}(n-1) .. 2{"*"}{"*"}(n-1) - 1;  --2's complement{"\n"}
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
   type Unsigned{"_"}n is mod 2{"*"}{"*"}n;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
   function Shift{"_"}Left  (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}      return Unsigned{"_"}n;{"\n"}   function Shift{"_"}Right (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}      return Unsigned{"_"}n;{"\n"}   function Shift{"_"}Right{"_"}Arithmetic (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}      return Unsigned{"_"}n;{"\n"}   function Rotate{"_"}Left  (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}      return Unsigned{"_"}n;{"\n"}   function Rotate{"_"}Right (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}      return Unsigned{"_"}n;{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}end Interfaces;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>An implementation shall provide the following declarations in the visible part of package Interfaces: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Signed and modular integer types of <i>n</i> bits, if supported by the target architecture, for each <i>n</i> that is at least the size of a storage element and that is a factor of the word size. The names of these types are of the form Integer{"_"}<i>n</i> for the signed types, and Unsigned{"_"}<i>n</i> for the modular types; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, for a typical 32-bit machine the corresponding types might be Integer{"_"}8, Unsigned{"_"}8, Integer{"_"}16, Unsigned{"_"}16, Integer{"_"}32, and Unsigned{"_"}32.<br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
The wording above implies, for example, that Integer{"_"}16'Size = Unsigned{"_"}16'Size = 16. Unchecked conversions between same-Sized types will work as expected. <br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>For each such modular type in Interfaces, shifting and rotating subprograms as specified in the declaration of Interfaces above. These subprograms are Intrinsic. They operate on a bit-by-bit basis, using the binary representation of the value of the operands to yield a binary representation for the result. The Amount parameter gives the number of bits by which to shift or rotate. For shifting, zero bits are shifted in, except in the case of Shift{"_"}Right{"_"}Arithmetic, where one bits are shifted in if Value is at least half the modulus. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We considered making shifting and rotating be primitive operations of all modular types. However, it is a design principle of Ada that all predefined operations should be operators (not functions named by identifiers). (Note that an early version of Ada had "<b>abs</b>" as an identifier, but it was changed to a reserved word operator before standardization of Ada 83.) This is important because the implicit declarations would hide nonoverloadable declarations with the same name, whereas operators are always overloadable. Therefore, we would have had to make shift and rotate into reserved words, which would have been upward incompatible, or else invent new operator symbols, which seemed like too much mechanism. <br />

<MarginText>9.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0264-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>&ldquo;Shifting&rdquo; and &ldquo;rotating&rdquo; have the conventional meaning. Neither of these terms is usefully defined by the usual normative references of the Reference Manual, so we provide pseudo-code here to describe the intended semantics of the above wording (all operations in these examples are using modular semantics).<br />

<MarginText>9.c/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Rotate{"_"}Left (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}   return Unsigned{"_"}n is{"\n"}   Result : Unsigned{"_"}n := Value;{"\n"}   Bit : Unsigned{"_"}n range 0 .. 1;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   for Count in 1 .. Amount loop{"\n"}      Bit := Result/2{"*"}{"*"}(n-1); -- High-bit of Result{"\n"}      Result := Result{"*"}2 + Bit;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}   return Result;{"\n"}end Rotate{"_"}Left;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9.d/5</MarginText>
function Rotate{"_"}Right (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}   return Unsigned{"_"}n is{"\n"}   Result : Unsigned{"_"}n := Value;{"\n"}   Bit : Unsigned{"_"}n range 0 .. 1;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   for Count in 1 .. Amount loop{"\n"}      Bit := Result mod 2; -- Low-bit of Result{"\n"}      Result := Result/2 + (Bit {"*"} 2{"*"}{"*"}(n-1));{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}   return Result;{"\n"}end Rotate{"_"}Right;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9.e/5</MarginText>
function Shift{"_"}Left (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}   return Unsigned{"_"}n is{"\n"}   Result : Unsigned{"_"}n := Value;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   for Count in 1 .. Amount loop{"\n"}      Result := Result {"*"} 2;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}   return Result;{"\n"}end Shift{"_"}Left;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9.f/5</MarginText>
function Shift{"_"}Right (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}   return Unsigned{"_"}n is{"\n"}   Result : Unsigned{"_"}n := Value;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   for Count in 1 .. Amount loop{"\n"}      Result := Result / 2;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}   return Result;{"\n"}end Shift{"_"}Right;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9.g/5</MarginText>
function Shift{"_"}Right{"_"}Arithmetic (Value : Unsigned{"_"}n; Amount : Natural){"\n"}   return Unsigned{"_"}n is{"\n"}   Result : Unsigned{"_"}n := Value;{"\n"}   Neg : constant Boolean :={"\n"}      Result/2{"*"}{"*"}(n-1) = 1; -- High-bit of Result{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   for Count in 1 .. Amount loop{"\n"}      if Neg then{"\n"}         Result := Result / 2 + 2{"*"}{"*"}(n-1);{"\n"}      else{"\n"}         Result := Result / 2;{"\n"}      end if;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}   return Result;{"\n"}end Shift{"_"}Right{"_"}Arithmetic;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9.h/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0264-1"]} />
These generally correspond to machine instructions, although there may not be an exact match in terms of boundary conditions, as Ada requires the correct result to be produced for all values of Amount. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Floating point types corresponding to each floating point format fully supported by the hardware. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The names for these floating point types are not specified. However, if IEEE arithmetic is supported, then the names should be IEEE{"_"}Float{"_"}32 and IEEE{"_"}Float{"_"}64 for single and double precision, respectively.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may provide implementation-defined library units that are children of Interfaces, and may add declarations to the visible part of Interfaces in addition to the ones defined above. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined children of package Interfaces.<br />

<MarginText>11.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00204-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>A child package of package Interfaces with the name of a convention may be provided independently of whether the convention is supported by the Convention aspect and vice versa. Such a child package should contain any declarations that would be useful for interfacing to the language (implementation) represented by the convention. Any declarations useful for interfacing to any language on the given hardware architecture should be provided directly in Interfaces. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.b/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, package Interfaces.XYZ{"_"}Pascal might contain declarations of types that match the data types provided by the XYZ implementation of Pascal, so that it will be more convenient to pass parameters to a subprogram whose convention is XYZ{"_"}Pascal. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>12/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00204-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>13/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>An implementation supporting an interface to C, COBOL, or Fortran should provide the corresponding package or packages described in the following subclauses. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If an interface to C, COBOL, or Fortran is provided, the corresponding package or packages described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/">Annex B</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/">Interface to Other Languages</a>&rdquo; should also be provided.<br />

<MarginText>13.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The intention is that an implementation might support several implementations of the foreign language: Interfaces.This{"_"}Fortran and Interfaces.That{"_"}Fortran might both exist. The &ldquo;default&rdquo; implementation, overridable by the user, should be declared as a renaming: <br />

<MarginText>13.b</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Interfaces.Fortran renames Interfaces.This{"_"}Fortran;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>13.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00204-01"]} />
Clarified that interfacing to foreign languages is optional and has the same restrictions as a Specialized Needs Annex. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>13.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
Move the restrictions on implementations of optional features to the start of this Annex. <br />

# B.3. Interfacing with C and C++

# B.3. Interfacing with C and C++

<MarginText>1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00131-01", "AI95-00376-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0028-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0059</i>{"}"} The facilities relevant to interfacing with the C language and the corresponding subset of the C++ language are the package Interfaces.C and its children, and support for specifying the Convention aspect with <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s C, C{"_"}Pass{"_"}By{"_"}Copy, and any of the C{"_"}Variadic{"_"}<i>n</i> conventions described below.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00376-01", "AI95-0262-1", "AI95-0299-1"]} />
<p>The package Interfaces.C contains the basic types, constants, and subprograms that allow an Ada program to pass scalars and strings to C and C++ functions. When this subclause mentions a C entity, the reference also applies to the corresponding entity in C++. <br /></p>
