private{"\n"}   ... -- not specified by the language{"\n"}end Interfaces.COBOL;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>50.a/1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The types Floating, Long{"_"}Floating, Binary, Long{"_"}Binary, Decimal{"_"}Element, and COBOL{"_"}Character; and the initializations of the variables Ada{"_"}To{"_"}COBOL and COBOL{"_"}To{"_"}Ada, in Interfaces.COBOL.<br />

<MarginText>51</MarginText>
<p>Each of the types in Interfaces.COBOL is COBOL-compatible.<br /></p>

<MarginText>52</MarginText>
<p>The types Floating and Long{"_"}Floating correspond to the native types in COBOL for data items with computational usage implemented by floating point. The types Binary and Long{"_"}Binary correspond to the native types in COBOL for data items with binary usage, or with computational usage implemented by binary.<br /></p>

<MarginText>53</MarginText>
<p>Max{"_"}Digits{"_"}Binary is the largest number of decimal digits in a numeric value that is represented as Binary. Max{"_"}Digits{"_"}Long{"_"}Binary is the largest number of decimal digits in a numeric value that is represented as Long{"_"}Binary.<br /></p>

<MarginText>54</MarginText>
<p>The type Packed{"_"}Decimal corresponds to COBOL's packed-decimal usage.<br /></p>

<MarginText>55</MarginText>
<p>The type COBOL{"_"}Character defines the run-time character set used in the COBOL implementation. Ada{"_"}To{"_"}COBOL and COBOL{"_"}To{"_"}Ada are the mappings between the Ada and COBOL run-time character sets. <br /></p>

<MarginText>55.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The character mappings are visible variables, since the user needs the ability to modify them at run time. <br />

<MarginText>56</MarginText>
<p>Type Alphanumeric corresponds to COBOL's alphanumeric data category.<br /></p>

<MarginText>57</MarginText>
<p>Each of the functions To{"_"}COBOL and To{"_"}Ada converts its parameter based on the mappings Ada{"_"}To{"_"}COBOL and COBOL{"_"}To{"_"}Ada, respectively. The length of the result for each is the length of the parameter, and the lower bound of the result is 1. Each component of the result is obtained by applying the relevant mapping to the corresponding component of the parameter.<br /></p>

<MarginText>58</MarginText>
<p>Each of the procedures To{"_"}COBOL and To{"_"}Ada copies converted elements from Item to Target, using the appropriate mapping (Ada{"_"}To{"_"}COBOL or COBOL{"_"}To{"_"}Ada, respectively). The index in Target of the last element assigned is returned in Last (0 if Item is a null array). If Item'Length exceeds Target'Length, Constraint{"_"}Error is propagated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>59</MarginText>
<p>Type Numeric corresponds to COBOL's numeric data category with display usage.<br /></p>

<MarginText>60</MarginText>
<p>The types Display{"_"}Format, Binary{"_"}Format, and Packed{"_"}Format are used in conversions between Ada decimal type values and COBOL internal or external data representations. The value of the constant Native{"_"}Binary is either High{"_"}Order{"_"}First or Low{"_"}Order{"_"}First, depending on the implementation. <br /></p>

<MarginText>61</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Valid (Item   : in Numeric;{"\n"}                Format : in Display{"_"}Format) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>62</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The function Valid checks that the Item parameter has a value consistent with the value of Format. If the value of Format is other than Unsigned, Leading{"_"}Separate, and Trailing{"_"}Separate, the effect is implementation defined. If Format does have one of these values, the following rules apply: <br /></p>

<MarginText>63/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00071-01", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0066</i>{"}"} Format=Unsigned: if Item comprises one or more decimal digit characters, then Valid returns True, else it returns False.<br /></li>
<MarginText>64/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00071-01"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0066</i>{"}"} Format=Leading{"_"}Separate: if Item comprises a single occurrence of the plus or minus sign character, and then one or more decimal digit characters, then Valid returns True, else it returns False.<br /></li>
<MarginText>65/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00071-01"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0066</i>{"}"} Format=Trailing{"_"}Separate: if Item comprises one or more decimal digit characters and finally a plus or minus sign character, then Valid returns True, else it returns False. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>66</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Length (Format : in Display{"_"}Format) return Natural;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>67</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">The Length function returns the minimal length of a Numeric value sufficient to hold any value of type Num when represented as Format.<br /></p>

<MarginText>68</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Decimal (Item   : in Numeric;{"\n"}                     Format : in Display{"_"}Format) return Num;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>69</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Produces a value of type Num corresponding to Item as represented by Format. The number of digits after the assumed radix point in Item is Num'Scale. Conversion{"_"}Error is propagated if the value represented by Item is outside the range of Num. <br /></p>

<MarginText>69.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There is no issue of truncation versus rounding, since the number of decimal places is established by Num'Scale.<br />

<MarginText>70</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Display (Item   : in Num;{"\n"}                     Format : in Display{"_"}Format) return Numeric;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>71/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00072-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">{"{"}<i>8652/0067</i>{"}"} This function returns the Numeric value for Item, represented in accordance with Format. The length of the returned value is Length(Format), and the lower bound is 1. Conversion{"_"}Error is propagated if Num is negative and Format is Unsigned.<br /></p>

<MarginText>72</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Valid (Item   : in Packed{"_"}Decimal;{"\n"}                Format : in Packed{"_"}Format) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>73</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">This function returns True if Item has a value consistent with Format, and False otherwise. The rules for the formation of Packed{"_"}Decimal values are implementation defined.<br /></p>

<MarginText>74</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Length (Format : in Packed{"_"}Format) return Natural;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>75</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">This function returns the minimal length of a Packed{"_"}Decimal value sufficient to hold any value of type Num when represented as Format.<br /></p>

<MarginText>76</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Decimal (Item   : in Packed{"_"}Decimal;{"\n"}                     Format : in Packed{"_"}Format) return Num;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>77</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Produces a value of type Num corresponding to Item as represented by Format. Num'Scale is the number of digits after the assumed radix point in Item. Conversion{"_"}Error is propagated if the value represented by Item is outside the range of Num.<br /></p>

<MarginText>78</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Packed (Item   : in Num;{"\n"}                    Format : in Packed{"_"}Format) return Packed{"_"}Decimal;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>79/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00072-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">{"{"}<i>8652/0067</i>{"}"} This function returns the Packed{"_"}Decimal value for Item, represented in accordance with Format. The length of the returned value is Length(Format), and the lower bound is 1. Conversion{"_"}Error is propagated if Num is negative and Format is Packed{"_"}Unsigned.<br /></p>

<MarginText>80</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Valid (Item   : in Byte{"_"}Array;{"\n"}                Format : in Binary{"_"}Format) return Boolean;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>81</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">This function returns True if Item has a value consistent with Format, and False otherwise. <br /></p>

<MarginText>81.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This function returns False only when the represented value is outside the range of Num.<br />

<MarginText>82</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function Length (Format : in Binary{"_"}Format) return Natural;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>83</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">This function returns the minimal length of a Byte{"_"}Array value sufficient to hold any value of type Num when represented as Format.<br /></p>

<MarginText>84</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Decimal (Item   : in Byte{"_"}Array;{"\n"}                     Format : in Binary{"_"}Format) return Num;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>85</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">Produces a value of type Num corresponding to Item as represented by Format. Num'Scale is the number of digits after the assumed radix point in Item. Conversion{"_"}Error is propagated if the value represented by Item is outside the range of Num.<br /></p>

<MarginText>86</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Binary (Item   : in Num;{"\n"}                    Format : in Binary{"_"}Format) return Byte{"_"}Array;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>87/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00072-01"]} />
<p class="Indented4">{"{"}<i>8652/0067</i>{"}"} This function returns the Byte{"_"}Array value for Item, represented in accordance with Format. The length of the returned value is Length(Format), and the lower bound is 1.<br /></p>

<MarginText>88</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Decimal (Item : in Binary)      return Num;{"\n"}{"\n"}function To{"_"}Decimal (Item : in Long{"_"}Binary) return Num;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>89</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">These functions convert from COBOL binary format to a corresponding value of the decimal type Num. Conversion{"_"}Error is propagated if Item is too large for Num. <br /></p>

<MarginText>89.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>There is no rescaling performed on the conversion. That is, the returned value in each case is a &ldquo;bit copy&rdquo; if Num has a binary radix. The programmer is responsible for maintaining the correct scale. <br />

<MarginText>90</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function To{"_"}Binary      (Item : in Num)  return Binary;{"\n"}{"\n"}function To{"_"}Long{"_"}Binary (Item : in Num)  return Long{"_"}Binary;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>91</MarginText>
<p class="Indented4">These functions convert from Ada decimal to COBOL binary format. Conversion{"_"}Error is propagated if the value of Item is too large to be represented in the result type. <br /></p>

<MarginText>91.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>One style of interface supported for COBOL, similar to what is provided for C, is the ability to call and pass parameters to an existing COBOL program. Thus the interface package supplies types that can be used in an Ada program as parameters to subprograms whose bodies will be in COBOL. These types map to COBOL's alphanumeric and numeric data categories.<br />

<MarginText>91.b</MarginText>
Several types are provided for support of alphanumeric data. Since COBOL's run-time character set is not necessarily the same as Ada's, Interfaces.COBOL declares an implementation-defined character type COBOL{"_"}Character, and mappings between Character and COBOL{"_"}Character. These mappings are visible variables (rather than, say, functions or constant arrays), since in the situation where COBOL{"_"}Character is EBCDIC, the flexibility of dynamically modifying the mappings is needed. Corresponding to COBOL's alphanumeric data is the string type Alphanumeric.<br />

<MarginText>91.c</MarginText>
Numeric data may have either a &ldquo;display&rdquo; or &ldquo;computational&rdquo; representation in COBOL. On the Ada side, the data is of a decimal fixed point type. Passing an Ada decimal data item to a COBOL program requires conversion from the Ada decimal type to some type that reflects the representation expected on the COBOL side. <br />

<MarginText>91.d</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Computational Representation<br /></li>
<MarginText>91.e</MarginText>
<li>Floating point representation is modeled by Ada floating point types, Floating and Long{"_"}Floating. Conversion between these types and Ada decimal types is obtained directly, since the type name serves as a conversion function.<br /></li>
<MarginText>91.f</MarginText>
<li>Binary representation is modeled by an Ada integer type, Binary, and possibly other types such as Long{"_"}Binary. Conversion between, say, Binary and a decimal type is through functions from an instantiation of the generic package Decimal{"_"}Conversions.<br /></li>
<MarginText>91.g</MarginText>
<li>Packed decimal representation is modeled by the Ada array type Packed{"_"}Decimal. Conversion between packed decimal and a decimal type is through functions from an instantiation of the generic package Decimal{"_"}Conversions.<br /></li>
<MarginText>91.h</MarginText>
<li>Display Representation<br /></li>
<MarginText>91.i</MarginText>
<li>Display representation for numeric data is modeled by the array type Numeric. Conversion between display representation and a decimal type is through functions from an instantiation of the generic package Decimal{"_"}Conversions. A parameter to the conversion function indicates the desired interpretation of the data (e.g., signed leading separate, etc.) <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>91.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
The Convention of a record type may be specified as COBOL to direct the compiler to choose a COBOL-compatible representation for objects of the type.<br />

<MarginText>91.k</MarginText>
The package Interfaces.COBOL allows the Ada programmer to deal with data from files (or databases) created by a COBOL program. For data that is alphanumeric, or in display or packed decimal format, the approach is the same as for passing parameters (instantiate Decimal{"_"}Conversions to obtain the needed conversion functions). For binary data, the external representation is treated as a Byte array, and an instantiation of Decimal{"_"}IO produces a package that declares the needed conversion functions. A parameter to the conversion function indicates the desired interpretation of the data (e.g., high- versus low-order byte first). <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>92/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An implementation shall support specifying aspect Convention with a COBOL <i>convention</i>{"_"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> for a COBOL-eligible type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>92.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>An implementation supporting this package shall ensure that if the bounds of a Packed{"_"}Decimal, Alphanumeric, or Numeric variable are static, then the representation of the object comprises solely the array components (that is, there is no implicit run-time &ldquo;descriptor&rdquo; that is part of the object). <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>93</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may provide additional constants of the private types Display{"_"}Format, Binary{"_"}Format, or Packed{"_"}Format. <br /></p>

<MarginText>93.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is to allow exploitation of other external formats that may be available in the COBOL implementation.<br />

<MarginText>94</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may provide further floating point and integer types in Interfaces.COBOL to match additional native COBOL types, and may also supply corresponding conversion functions in the generic package Decimal{"_"}Conversions. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>95</MarginText>
<p>An Ada implementation should support the following interface correspondences between Ada and COBOL. <br /></p>

<MarginText>96</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>An Ada <b>access</b> T parameter is passed as a &ldquo;BY REFERENCE&rdquo; data item of the COBOL type corresponding to T.<br /></li>
<MarginText>97</MarginText>
<li>An Ada <b>in</b> scalar parameter is passed as a &ldquo;BY CONTENT&rdquo; data item of the corresponding COBOL type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>98</MarginText>
<li>Any other Ada parameter is passed as a &ldquo;BY REFERENCE&rdquo; data item of the COBOL type corresponding to the Ada parameter type; for scalars, a local copy is used if necessary to ensure by-copy semantics. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>98.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If COBOL interfacing is supported, the interface correspondences between Ada and COBOL should be supported.<br />

<MarginText>99/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
NOTE 1   An implementation is not required to support specifying aspect Convention for access types, nor is it required to support specifying aspects Import, Export, or Convention for functions. <br />

<MarginText>99.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>COBOL does not have a pointer facility, and a COBOL program does not return a value. <br />

<MarginText>100/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 2   If an Ada subprogram is exported to COBOL, then a call from COBOL call can specify either &ldquo;BY CONTENT&rdquo; or &ldquo;BY REFERENCE&rdquo;. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>101</MarginText>
<p><i>Examples of Interfaces.COBOL:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>102</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Interfaces.COBOL;{"\n"}procedure Test{"_"}Call is{"\n"}
<MarginText>103</MarginText>
   -- Calling a foreign COBOL program{"\n"}   -- Assume that a COBOL program PROG has the following declaration{"\n"}   --  in its LINKAGE section:{"\n"}   --  01 Parameter-Area{"\n"}   --     05 NAME   PIC X(20).{"\n"}   --     05 SSN    PIC X(9).{"\n"}   --     05 SALARY PIC 99999V99 USAGE COMP.{"\n"}   -- The effect of PROG is to update SALARY based on some algorithm{"\n"}
<MarginText>104</MarginText>
   package COBOL renames Interfaces.COBOL;{"\n"}
<MarginText>105</MarginText>
   type Salary{"_"}Type is delta 0.01 digits 7;{"\n"}
<MarginText>106/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
   type COBOL{"_"}Record is{"\n"}      record{"\n"}         Name   : COBOL.Numeric(1..20);{"\n"}         SSN    : COBOL.Numeric(1..9);{"\n"}         Salary : COBOL.Binary;  -- Assume Binary = 32 bits{"\n"}      end record{"\n"}      with Convention ={">"} COBOL;{"\n"}
<MarginText>107/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
   procedure Prog (Item : in out COBOL{"_"}Record){"\n"}      with Import ={">"} True, Convention ={">"} COBOL;{"\n"}
<MarginText>108</MarginText>
   package Salary{"_"}Conversions is{"\n"}      new COBOL.Decimal{"_"}Conversions(Salary{"_"}Type);{"\n"}
<MarginText>109</MarginText>
   Some{"_"}Salary : Salary{"_"}Type := 12{"_"}345.67;{"\n"}   Some{"_"}Record : COBOL{"_"}Record :={"\n"}      (Name   ={">"} "Johnson, John       ",{"\n"}       SSN    ={">"} "111223333",{"\n"}       Salary ={">"} Salary{"_"}Conversions.To{"_"}Binary(Some{"_"}Salary));{"\n"}
<MarginText>110</MarginText>
begin{"\n"}   Prog (Some{"_"}Record);{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}end Test{"_"}Call;{"\n"}
<MarginText>111</MarginText>
with Interfaces.COBOL;{"\n"}with COBOL{"_"}Sequential{"_"}IO; -- Assumed to be supplied by implementation{"\n"}procedure Test{"_"}External{"_"}Formats is{"\n"}
<MarginText>112/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
   -- Using data created by a COBOL program{"\n"}   -- Assume that a COBOL program has created a sequential file with{"\n"}   --  the following record structure, and that we want{"\n"}   --  process the records in an Ada program{"\n"}   --  01 EMPLOYEE-RECORD{"\n"}   --     05 NAME    PIC X(20).{"\n"}   --     05 SSN     PIC X(9).{"\n"}   --     05 SALARY  PIC 99999V99 USAGE COMP.{"\n"}   --     05 ADJUST  PIC S999V999 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE.{"\n"}   -- The COMP data is binary (32 bits), high-order byte first{"\n"}
<MarginText>113</MarginText>
   package COBOL renames Interfaces.COBOL;{"\n"}
<MarginText>114</MarginText>
   type Salary{"_"}Type      is delta 0.01  digits 7;{"\n"}   type Adjustments{"_"}Type is delta 0.001 digits 6;{"\n"}
<MarginText>115/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
   type COBOL{"_"}Employee{"_"}Record{"_"}Type is  -- External representation{"\n"}      record{"\n"}         Name    : COBOL.Alphanumeric(1..20);{"\n"}         SSN     : COBOL.Alphanumeric(1..9);{"\n"}         Salary  : COBOL.Byte{"_"}Array(1..4);{"\n"}         Adjust  : COBOL.Numeric(1..7);  -- Sign and 6 digits{"\n"}      end record{"\n"}      with Convention ={">"} COBOL;{"\n"}
<MarginText>116</MarginText>
   package COBOL{"_"}Employee{"_"}IO is{"\n"}      new COBOL{"_"}Sequential{"_"}IO(COBOL{"_"}Employee{"_"}Record{"_"}Type);{"\n"}   use COBOL{"_"}Employee{"_"}IO;{"\n"}
<MarginText>117</MarginText>
   COBOL{"_"}File : File{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>118</MarginText>
   type Ada{"_"}Employee{"_"}Record{"_"}Type is  -- Internal representation{"\n"}      record{"\n"}         Name    : String(1..20);{"\n"}         SSN     : String(1..9);{"\n"}         Salary  : Salary{"_"}Type;{"\n"}         Adjust  : Adjustments{"_"}Type;{"\n"}      end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>119</MarginText>
   COBOL{"_"}Record : COBOL{"_"}Employee{"_"}Record{"_"}Type;{"\n"}   Ada{"_"}Record   : Ada{"_"}Employee{"_"}Record{"_"}Type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>120</MarginText>
   package Salary{"_"}Conversions is{"\n"}      new COBOL.Decimal{"_"}Conversions(Salary{"_"}Type);{"\n"}   use Salary{"_"}Conversions;{"\n"}
<MarginText>121</MarginText>
   package Adjustments{"_"}Conversions is{"\n"}      new COBOL.Decimal{"_"}Conversions(Adjustments{"_"}Type);{"\n"}   use Adjustments{"_"}Conversions;{"\n"}
<MarginText>122</MarginText>
begin{"\n"}   Open (COBOL{"_"}File, Name ={">"} "Some{"_"}File");{"\n"}
<MarginText>123</MarginText>
   loop{"\n"}     Read (COBOL{"_"}File, COBOL{"_"}Record);{"\n"}
<MarginText>124/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0178-1"]} />
     Ada{"_"}Record.Name := COBOL.To{"_"}Ada(COBOL{"_"}Record.Name);{"\n"}     Ada{"_"}Record.SSN  := COBOL.To{"_"}Ada(COBOL{"_"}Record.SSN);{"\n"}     Ada{"_"}Record.Salary :={"\n"}        To{"_"}Decimal(COBOL{"_"}Record.Salary, COBOL.High{"_"}Order{"_"}First);{"\n"}     Ada{"_"}Record.Adjust :={"\n"}        To{"_"}Decimal(COBOL{"_"}Record.Adjust, COBOL.Leading{"_"}Separate);{"\n"}     ... -- Process Ada{"_"}Record{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}exception{"\n"}   when End{"_"}Error ={">"} ...{"\n"}end Test{"_"}External{"_"}Formats;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

# B.5. Interfacing with Fortran

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.5.mdx

sidebar_position:  145

# B.5. Interfacing with Fortran

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The facilities relevant to interfacing with the Fortran language are the package Interfaces.Fortran and support for specifying the Convention aspect with <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> Fortran.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The package Interfaces.Fortran defines Ada types whose representations are identical to the default representations of the Fortran intrinsic types Integer, Real, Double Precision, Complex, Logical, and Character in a supported Fortran implementation. These Ada types can therefore be used to pass objects between Ada and Fortran programs. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The library package Interfaces.Fortran has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0414-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types;  -- see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.1#Subclause_G.1.1">G.1.1</a>{"\n"}pragma Elaborate{"_"}All(Ada.Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types);{"\n"}package Interfaces.Fortran{"\n"}   with Pure is{"\n"}
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
   type Fortran{"_"}Integer is range implementation-defined;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
   type Real             is digits implementation-defined;{"\n"}   type Double{"_"}Precision is digits implementation-defined;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
   type Logical is new Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
   package Single{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types is{"\n"}      new Ada.Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types (Real);{"\n"}
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
   type Complex is new Single{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types.Complex;{"\n"}
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
   subtype Imaginary is Single{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types.Imaginary;{"\n"}   i : Imaginary renames Single{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types.i;{"\n"}   j : Imaginary renames Single{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types.j;{"\n"}
<MarginText>10.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
   package Double{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types is{"\n"}      new Ada.Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types (Double{"_"}Precision);{"\n"}
<MarginText>10.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
   type Double{"_"}Complex is new Double{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types.Complex;{"\n"}
<MarginText>10.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
   subtype Double{"_"}Imaginary is Double{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types.Imaginary;{"\n"}
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
   type Character{"_"}Set is implementation-defined character type;{"\n"}
<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
   type Fortran{"_"}Character is array (Positive range {"<"}{">"}) of Character{"_"}Set{"\n"}      with Pack;{"\n"}
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
   function To{"_"}Fortran (Item : in Character) return Character{"_"}Set;{"\n"}   function To{"_"}Ada (Item : in Character{"_"}Set) return Character;{"\n"}
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
   function To{"_"}Fortran (Item : in String) return Fortran{"_"}Character;{"\n"}   function To{"_"}Ada     (Item : in Fortran{"_"}Character) return String;{"\n"}
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
   procedure To{"_"}Fortran (Item       : in String;{"\n"}                         Target     : out Fortran{"_"}Character;{"\n"}                         Last       : out Natural);{"\n"}
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
   procedure To{"_"}Ada (Item     : in Fortran{"_"}Character;{"\n"}                     Target   : out String;{"\n"}                     Last     : out Natural);{"\n"}
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
end Interfaces.Fortran;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>17.a.1/1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The types Fortran{"_"}Integer, Real, Double{"_"}Precision, and Character{"_"}Set in Interfaces.Fortran.<br />

<MarginText>17.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The means by which the Complex and Double{"_"}Complex types are provided in Interfaces.Fortran creates a dependence of Interfaces.Fortran on Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.1#Subclause_G.1.1">G.1.1</a>). This dependence is intentional and unavoidable, if the Fortran-compatible Complex and Double{"_"}Complex types are to be useful in Ada code without duplicating facilities defined elsewhere. <br />

<MarginText>18/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
<p>The types Fortran{"_"}Integer, Real, Double{"_"}Precision, Logical, Complex, Double{"_"}Complex, Character{"_"}Set, and Fortran{"_"}Character are Fortran-compatible.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<p>The To{"_"}Fortran and To{"_"}Ada functions map between the Ada type Character and the Fortran type Character{"_"}Set, and also between the Ada type String and the Fortran type Fortran{"_"}Character. The To{"_"}Fortran and To{"_"}Ada procedures have analogous effects to the string conversion subprograms found in Interfaces.COBOL. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>20/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An implementation shall support specifying aspect Convention with a Fortran <i>convention</i>{"_"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> for a Fortran-eligible type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>). <br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>21/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1", "AI12-0263-1", "AI12-0450-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may add additional declarations to the Fortran interface packages. For example, declarations are permitted for the character types corresponding to Fortran character kinds 'ascii' and 'iso{"_"}10646', which in turn correspond to ISO/IEC 646:1991 and to UCS-4 as specified in ISO/IEC 10646:2020. <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Fortran compilers are required to recognize 'ascii' and 'iso{"_"}10646' as arguments to the SELECTED{"_"}CHAR{"_"}KIND intrinsic function, but are not required to support those kinds. <br />

<MarginText>21.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Implementations may add auxiliary declarations as needed to assist in the declarations of additional Fortran-compatible types. For example,  if a wide character type is defined to match a Fortran 90 wide character type (accessible in Fortran 90 with the Kind attribute), then an auxiliary character set may be declared to serve as its component type. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<p>An Ada implementation should support the following interface correspondences between Ada and Fortran: <br /></p>

<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>An Ada procedure corresponds to a Fortran subroutine.<br /></li>
<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<li>An Ada function corresponds to a Fortran function.<br /></li>
<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<li>An Ada parameter of an elementary, array, or record type T is passed as a TF argument to a Fortran procedure, where TF is the Fortran type corresponding to the Ada type T, and where the INTENT attribute of the corresponding dummy argument matches the Ada formal parameter mode; the Fortran implementation's parameter passing conventions are used. For elementary types, a local copy is used if necessary to ensure by-copy semantics.<br /></li>
<MarginText>26</MarginText>
<li>An Ada parameter of an access-to-subprogram type is passed as a reference to a Fortran procedure whose interface corresponds to the designated subprogram's specification. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>26.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If Fortran interfacing is supported, the interface correspondences between Ada and Fortran should be supported.<br />

<MarginText>27</MarginText>
NOTE 1   An object of a Fortran-compatible record type, declared in a library package or subprogram, can correspond to a Fortran common block; the type also corresponds to a Fortran &ldquo;derived type&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>28/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0224-1"]} />
NOTE 2   For Fortran facilities not addressed by this subclause, consider using the Fortran to C interoperability features defined in ISO/IEC 1594-1:2018 along with the C interfacing features defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3">B.3</a>.<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>29</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of Interfaces.Fortran:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>30</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Interfaces.Fortran;{"\n"}use Interfaces.Fortran;{"\n"}procedure Ada{"_"}Application is{"\n"}
<MarginText>31/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0178-1"]} />
   type Fortran{"_"}Matrix is {"\n"}      array (Fortran{"_"}Integer range {"<"}{">"},{"\n"}             Fortran{"_"}Integer range {"<"}{">"}) of Double{"_"}Precision{"\n"}      with Convention ={">"} Fortran;                  -- stored in Fortran's{"\n"}                                                   -- column-major order{"\n"}   procedure Invert (Rank : in Fortran{"_"}Integer; X : in out Fortran{"_"}Matrix){"\n"}      with Import ={">"} True, Convention ={">"} Fortran; -- a Fortran subroutine{"\n"}
<MarginText>32</MarginText>
   Rank      : constant Fortran{"_"}Integer := 100;{"\n"}   My{"_"}Matrix : Fortran{"_"}Matrix (1 .. Rank, 1 .. Rank);{"\n"}
<MarginText>33/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
   Precision: constant := 6;{"\n"}   type Standard{"_"}Deviation is digits Precision{"\n"}      with Convention ={">"} Fortran;{"\n"}   Deviation : Standard{"_"}Deviation;{"\n"}      -- Declarations to match the following Fortran declarations:{"\n"}      --   integer, parameter :: precision = selected{"_"}real{"_"}kind(p=6){"\n"}      --   real(precision) :: deviation{"\n"}
<MarginText>34</MarginText>
begin{"\n"}
<MarginText>35</MarginText>
   ...{"\n"}   My{"_"}Matrix := ...;{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}   Invert (Rank, My{"_"}Matrix);{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>36/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
   Deviation := ...;{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}
<MarginText>37</MarginText>
end Ada{"_"}Application;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>37.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0058-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> The package Double{"_"}Precision{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types and associated types are added to package Interfaces.Fortran. In unusual circumstances, this could cause an incompatibility; we don't document it as an incompatibility as implementations are allowed to add declarations to this package, so that risk of an incompatibility is present for any move from one version of an implementation to another (not to mention to another implementation). As such, the language-defined additions make no change in the risk of incompatibility. <br />

# Annex B. Interface to Other Languages

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.mdx

sidebar_position:  140

# Annex B. Interface to Other Languages

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>This Annex describes features for writing mixed-language programs. General interface support is presented first; then specific support for C, COBOL, and Fortran is defined, in terms of language interface packages for each of these languages. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This Annex is not a &ldquo;Specialized Needs&rdquo; annex. Every implementation must support all nonoptional features defined here (mainly the package Interfaces). <br />

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.b</MarginText>
Ada should have strong support for mixed-language programming. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0262-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>Support for interfacing to any foreign language is optional. However, an implementation shall not provide any optional aspect, attribute, library unit, or pragma having the same name as an aspect, attribute, library unit, or pragma (respectively) specified in the subclauses of this Annex unless the provided construct is either as specified in those subclauses or is more limited in capability than that required by those subclauses. A program that attempts to use an unsupported capability of this Annex shall either be identified by the implementation before run time or shall raise an exception at run time. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The intent is that the same rules apply for the optional parts of language interfacing as apply for Specialized Needs Annexes. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a> for a discussion of the purpose of these rules. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
Much of the functionality in this Annex is new to Ada 95. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>2.c</MarginText>
This Annex contains what used to be RM83-13.8. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>2.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0262-1"]} />
Moved the clarification that interfacing to foreign languages is optional and has the same restrictions as a Specialized Needs Annex here. <br />

---

# C.1. Access to Machine Operations

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  147

# C.1. Access to Machine Operations

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause specifies rules regarding access to machine instructions from within an Ada program.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined intrinsic subprograms.<br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0320-1"]} />
<p>The implementation shall support machine code insertions (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.8">13.8</a>) or intrinsic subprograms (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>) (or both). The implementation shall allow the use of Ada entities as operands for such machine code insertions or intrinsic subprograms.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0320-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Ada entities could be used as operands in machine code insertions and/or intrinsic subprograms using language-defined attributes (such as address), implementation-defined attributes, or could be directly allowed. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The machine code or intrinsics support should allow access to all operations normally available to assembly language programmers for the target environment, including privileged instructions, if any. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The machine code or intrinsics support should allow access to all operations normally available to assembly language programmers for the target environment.<br />

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Of course, on a machine with protection, an attempt to execute a privileged instruction in user mode will probably trap. Nonetheless, we want implementations to provide access to them so that Ada can be used to write systems programs that run in privileged mode. <br />

<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The support for interfacing aspects (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/">Annex B</a>) should include interface to assembler; the default assembler should be associated with the convention identifier Assembler. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Interface to assembler should be supported; the default assembler should be associated with the convention identifier Assembler.<br />

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>If an entity is exported to assembly language, then the implementation should allocate it at an addressable location, and should ensure that it is retained by the linking process, even if not otherwise referenced from the Ada code. The implementation should assume that any call to a machine code or assembler subprogram is allowed to read or update every object that is specified as exported. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If an entity is exported to assembly language, then the implementation should allocate it at an addressable location even if not otherwise referenced from the Ada code. A call to a machine code or assembler subprogram should be treated as if it can read or update every object that is specified as exported.<br />

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document the overhead associated with calling machine-code or intrinsic subprograms, as compared to a fully-inlined call, and to a regular out-of-line call. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The overhead of calling machine-code or intrinsic subprograms.<br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document the types of the package System.Machine{"_"}Code usable for machine code insertions, and the attributes to be used in machine code insertions for references to Ada entities. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The types and attributes used in machine code insertions.<br />

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The implementation shall document the subprogram calling conventions associated with the convention identifiers available for use with the Convention aspect (Ada and Assembler, at a minimum), including register saving, exception propagation, parameter passing, and function value returning. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The subprogram calling conventions for all supported convention identifiers.<br />

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>For exported and imported subprograms, the implementation shall document the mapping between the Link{"_"}Name string, if specified, or the Ada designator, if not, and the external link name used for such a subprogram. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>9.b/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The mapping between the Link{"_"}Name or Ada designator and the external link name.<br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>The implementation should ensure that little or no overhead is associated with calling intrinsic and machine-code subprograms. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Little or no overhead should be associated with calling intrinsic and machine-code subprograms.<br />

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>It is recommended that intrinsic subprograms be provided for convenient access to any machine operations that provide special capabilities or efficiency and that are not otherwise available through the language constructs. Examples of such instructions include: <br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Atomic read-modify-write operations &mdash; for example, test and set, compare and swap, decrement and test, enqueue/dequeue.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
<li>Standard numeric functions &mdash; for example, <i>sin</i>, <i>log</i>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
<li>String manipulation operations &mdash; for example, translate and test.<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
<li>Vector operations &mdash; for example, compare vector against thresholds.<br /></li>
<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<li>Direct operations on I/O ports.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Intrinsic subprograms should be provided to access any machine operations that provide special capabilities or efficiency not normally available.<br />

# C.3. Interrupt Support

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  149

# C.3. Interrupt Support

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause specifies the language-defined model for hardware interrupts in addition to mechanisms for handling interrupts.] <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>[An <i>interrupt</i> represents a class of events that are detected by the hardware or the system software.] Interrupts are said to occur. An <i>occurrence</i> of an interrupt is separable into generation and delivery. <i>Generation</i> of an interrupt is the event in the underlying hardware or system that makes the interrupt available to the program. <i>Delivery</i> is the action that invokes part of the program as response to the interrupt occurrence. Between generation and delivery, the interrupt occurrence [(or interrupt)] is <i>pending</i>. Some or all interrupts may be <i>blocked</i>. When an interrupt is blocked, all occurrences of that interrupt are prevented from being delivered. Certain interrupts are <i>reserved</i>. The set of reserved interrupts is implementation defined. A reserved interrupt is either an interrupt for which user-defined handlers are not supported, or one which already has an attached handler by some other implementation-defined means. Program units can be connected to nonreserved interrupts. While connected, the program unit is said to be <i>attached</i> to that interrupt. The execution of that program unit, the <i>interrupt handler</i>, is invoked upon delivery of the interrupt occurrence. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
<b>To be honest: </b>As an obsolescent feature, interrupts may be attached to task entries by an address clause. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#Subclause_J.7.1">J.7.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>While a handler is attached to an interrupt, it is called once for each delivered occurrence of that interrupt. While the handler executes, the corresponding interrupt is blocked.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>While an interrupt is blocked, all occurrences of that interrupt are prevented from being delivered. Whether such occurrences remain pending or are lost is implementation defined.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>Each interrupt has a <i>default treatment</i> which determines the system's response to an occurrence of that interrupt when no user-defined handler is attached. The set of possible default treatments is implementation defined, as is the method (if one exists) for configuring the default treatments for interrupts.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>An interrupt is delivered to the handler (or default treatment) that is in effect for that interrupt at the time of delivery.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>An exception propagated from a handler that is invoked by an interrupt has no effect.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>[If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) is in effect, the interrupt handler executes with the active priority that is the ceiling priority of the corresponding protected object.]<br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0445-1"]} />
<p>The implementation shall provide a mechanism to determine the minimum stack space that is necessary for each interrupt handler and to reserve that space for the execution of the handler. [This space should accommodate nested invocations of the handler where the system permits this.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>If the hardware or the underlying system holds pending interrupt occurrences, the implementation shall provide for later delivery of these occurrences to the program.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy is not in effect, the implementation shall provide means for the application to specify whether interrupts are to be blocked during protected actions.<br /></p>

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document the following items: <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This information may be different for different forms of interrupt handlers. <br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>For each interrupt, which interrupts are blocked from delivery when a handler attached to that interrupt executes (either as a result of an interrupt delivery or of an ordinary call on a procedure of the corresponding protected object).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>Any interrupts that cannot be blocked, and the effect of attaching handlers to such interrupts, if this is permitted.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>Which run-time stack an interrupt handler uses when it executes as a result of an interrupt delivery; if this is configurable, what is the mechanism to do so; how to specify how much space to reserve on that stack.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>16/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>4.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
<dd>Any implementation- or hardware-specific activity that happens before a user-defined interrupt handler gets control (for example, reading device registers, acknowledging devices).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<dt><br/>5.</dt>
<dd>Any timing or other limitations imposed on the execution of interrupt handlers.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<dt><br/>6.</dt>
<dd>The state (blocked/unblocked) of the nonreserved interrupts when the program starts; if some interrupts are unblocked, what is the mechanism a program can use to protect itself before it can attach the corresponding handlers.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<dt><br/>7.</dt>
<dd>Whether the interrupted task is allowed to resume execution before the interrupt handler returns.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>20/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>8.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
<dd>The treatment of interrupt occurrences that are generated while the interrupt is blocked; that is, whether one or more occurrences are held for later delivery, or all are lost.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>21</MarginText>
<dt><br/>9.</dt>
<dd>Whether predefined or implementation-defined exceptions are raised as a result of the occurrence of any interrupt, and the mapping between the machine interrupts (or traps) and the predefined exceptions.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<dt><br/>10.</dt>
<dd>On a multi-processor, the rules governing the delivery of an interrupt to a particular processor. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>22.a/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The treatment of interrupts.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>23/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
<p>If the underlying system or hardware does not allow interrupts to be blocked, then no blocking is required [as part of the execution of subprograms of a protected object for which one of its subprograms is an interrupt handler].<br /></p>

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<p>In a multi-processor with more than one interrupt subsystem, it is implementation defined whether (and how) interrupt sources from separate subsystems share the same Interrupt{"_"}Id type (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.2">C.3.2</a>). In particular, the meaning of a blocked or pending interrupt may then be applicable to one processor only. <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This issue is tightly related to the issue of scheduling on a multi-processor. In a sense, if a particular interrupt source is not available to all processors, the system is not truly homogeneous.<br />

<MarginText>24.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
One way to approach this problem is to assign sub-ranges within Interrupt{"_"}Id to each interrupt subsystem, such that &ldquo;similar&rdquo; interrupt sources (for example a timer) in different subsystems get a distinct id. <br />

<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<p>Implementations are allowed to impose timing or other limitations on the execution of interrupt handlers. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>These limitations are often necessary to ensure proper behavior of the implementation. <br />

<MarginText>26/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>Other forms of handlers are allowed to be supported, in which case the rules of this subclause should be adhered to.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27</MarginText>
<p>The active priority of the execution of an interrupt handler is allowed to vary from one occurrence of the same interrupt to another.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>28/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
<p>If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy is not in effect, the implementation should provide means for the application to specify which interrupts are to be blocked during protected actions, if the underlying system allows for finer-grained control of interrupt blocking. <br /></p>

<MarginText>28.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy is not in effect and the target system allows for finer-grained control of interrupt blocking, a means for the application to specify which interrupts are to be blocked during protected actions should be provided.<br />

<MarginText>29/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0447-1"]} />
NOTE 1   The default treatment for an interrupt can be to keep the interrupt pending or to deliver it to an implementation-defined handler. Examples of actions that an implementation-defined handler can perform include aborting the partition, ignoring (that is, discarding occurrences of) the interrupt, or queuing one or more occurrences of the interrupt for possible later delivery when a user-defined handler is attached to that interrupt.<br />

<MarginText>30</MarginText>
NOTE 2   It is a bounded error to call Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.7#Subclause_C.7.1">C.7.1</a>) from an interrupt handler.<br />

<MarginText>31</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The rule that an exception propagated from an interrupt handler has no effect is modeled after the rule about exceptions propagated out of task bodies.<br />

<a id="Subclause_C.3.1"></a>

## C.3.1  Protected Procedure Handlers

<p><i>Paragraphs 1 through 6 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6.1/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For a parameterless protected procedure, the following language-defined representation aspects may be specified: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.2/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Interrupt{"_"}Handler</dt>
<dl>
<dd> The type of aspect Interrupt{"_"}Handler is Boolean. If directly specified, the aspect{"_"}definition shall be a static expression. [This aspect is never inherited;] if not directly specified, the aspect is False.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.a/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Interrupt{"_"}Handler: </b>Protected procedure may be attached to interrupts.<br />

<MarginText>6.3/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Attach{"_"}Handler</dt>
<dl>
<dd> The aspect Attach{"_"}Handler is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, which shall be of type Interrupts.Interrupt{"_"}Id. [This aspect is never inherited.]<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.b/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Attach{"_"}Handler: </b>Protected procedure is attached to an interrupt.<br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01", "AI05-0033-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If either the Attach{"_"}Handler or Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspect are specified for a protected procedure, the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0249">protected{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single{"_"}protected{"_"}declaration</a></code> shall be a library-level declaration and shall not be declared within a generic body. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), this rule also applies in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0249">protected_type_declaration</a></code>, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> of an object of that type need not be at library level.<br />

<MarginText>7.b/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0033-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
We cannot allow these aspects in protected declarations in a generic body, because legality rules are not checked for instance bodies, and these should not be allowed if the instance is not at the library level. The protected types can be declared in the private part if this is desired. Note that while the 'Access to use the handler would provide the check in the case of Interrupt{"_"}Handler, there is no other check for Attach{"_"}Handler. Since these aspects are so similar, we want the rules to be the same. <br />

<MarginText>8/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00253-01", "AI95-00303-01", "AI05-0033-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>9/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If the Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspect of a protected procedure is True, then the procedure may be attached dynamically, as a handler, to interrupts (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.2">C.3.2</a>). [Such procedures are allowed to be attached to multiple interrupts.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> specified for the Attach{"_"}Handler aspect of a protected procedure <i>P</i> is evaluated as part of the creation of the protected object that contains <i>P</i>. The value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> identifies an interrupt. As part of the initialization of that object, <i>P</i> (the <i>handler</i> procedure) is attached to the identified interrupt. A check is made that the corresponding interrupt is not reserved. Program{"_"}Error is raised if the check fails, and the existing treatment for the interrupt is not affected.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) is in effect, then upon the initialization of a protected object that contains a protected procedure for which either the Attach{"_"}Handler aspect is specified or the  Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspect is True, a check is made that the initial ceiling priority of the object is in the range of System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority. If the check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00121-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0068</i>{"}"} When a protected object is finalized, for any of its procedures that are attached to interrupts, the handler is detached. If the handler was attached by a procedure in the Interrupts package or if no user handler was previously attached to the interrupt, the default treatment is restored. If the Attach{"_"}Handler aspect was specified and the most recently attached handler for the same interrupt is the same as the one that was attached at the time the protected object was initialized, the previous handler is restored. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00121-01", "AI95-00303-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0068</i>{"}"} If all protected objects for interrupt handlers are declared at the library level, the finalization discussed above occurs only as part of the finalization of all library-level packages in a partition. However, objects of a protected type containing procedures with an Attach{"_"}Handler aspect specified need not be at the library level. Thus, an implementation needs to be able to restore handlers during the execution of the program. (An object with an Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspect also need not be at the library level, but such a handler cannot be attached to an interrupt using the Interrupts package.) <br />

<MarginText>13_C.3.1</MarginText>
<p>When a handler is attached to an interrupt, the interrupt is blocked [(subject to the Implementation Permission in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3">C.3</a>)] during the execution of every protected action on the protected object containing the handler.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.1/5_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0252-1"]} />
<p>If restriction No{"_"}Dynamic{"_"}Attachment is in effect, then a check is made that the interrupt identified by an Attach{"_"}Handler aspect does not appear in any previously elaborated Attach{"_"}Handler aspect; Program{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/5_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>When No{"_"}Dynamic{"_"}Attachment is in effect, it is not possible to call any previous handler. Therefore, the only possibility is to replace the original handler, rendering it ineffective. Having an unused handler in a program is likely a bug, so we require an exception to be raised. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>14_C.3.1</MarginText>
<p>If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) is in effect and an interrupt is delivered to a handler, and the interrupt hardware priority is higher than the ceiling priority of the corresponding protected object, the execution of the program is erroneous.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14.1/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00121-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0068</i>{"}"} If the handlers for a given interrupt attached via aspect Attach{"_"}Handler are not attached and detached in a stack-like (LIFO) order, program execution is erroneous. In particular, when a protected object is finalized, the execution is erroneous if any of the procedures of the protected object are attached to interrupts via aspect Attach{"_"}Handler and the most recently attached handler for the same interrupt is not the same as the one that was attached at the time the protected object was initialized. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00121-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0068</i>{"}"} This simplifies implementation of the Attach{"_"}Handler aspect by not requiring a check that the current handler is the same as the one attached by the initialization of a protected object. <br />

#### Metrics

<MarginText>15_C.3.1</MarginText>
<p>The following metric shall be documented by the implementation: <br /></p>

<MarginText>16/2_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>The worst-case overhead for an interrupt handler that is a parameterless protected procedure, in clock cycles. This is the execution time not directly attributable to the handler procedure or the interrupted execution. It is estimated as C &ndash; (A+B), where A is how long it takes to complete a given sequence of instructions without any interrupt, B is how long it takes to complete a normal call to a given protected procedure, and C is how long it takes to complete the same sequence of instructions when it is interrupted by one execution of the same procedure called via an interrupt. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16.a_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The instruction sequence and interrupt handler used to measure interrupt handling overhead should be chosen so as to maximize the execution time cost due to cache misses. For example, if the processor has cache memory and the activity of an interrupt handler could invalidate the contents of cache memory, the handler should be written such that it invalidates all of the cache memory. <br />

<MarginText>16.b/2_C.3.1</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The metrics for interrupt handlers.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>17/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>When the aspects Attach{"_"}Handler or Interrupt{"_"}Handler are specified for a protected procedure, the implementation is allowed to impose implementation-defined restrictions on the corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0249">protected{"_"}type{"_"}declaration</a></code> and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0254">protected{"_"}body</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The restrictions may be on the constructs that are allowed within them, and on ordinary calls (i.e. not via interrupts) on protected operations in these protected objects. <br />

<MarginText>17.b/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Any restrictions on a protected procedure or its containing type when an aspect Attach{"_"}handler or Interrupt{"_"}Handler is specified.<br />

<MarginText>18_C.3.1</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may use a different mechanism for invoking a protected procedure in response to a hardware interrupt than is used for a call to that protected procedure from a task. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This is despite the fact that the priority of an interrupt handler (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>) is modeled after a hardware task calling the handler. <br />

<MarginText>19/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>Notwithstanding what this subclause says elsewhere, the Attach{"_"}Handler and Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspects are allowed to be used for other, implementation defined, forms of interrupt handlers. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, if an implementation wishes to allow interrupt handlers to have parameters, it is allowed to do so via these aspects; it need not invent implementation-defined aspects for the purpose. <br />

<MarginText>19.b/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Any other forms of interrupt handler supported by the Attach{"_"}Handler and Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspects.<br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>20_C.3.1</MarginText>
<p>Whenever possible, the implementation should allow interrupt handlers to be called directly by the hardware. <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a/2_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Interrupt handlers should be called directly by the hardware.<br />

<MarginText>21_C.3.1</MarginText>
<p>Whenever practical, the implementation should detect violations of any implementation-defined restrictions before run time. <br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a/2_C.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Violations of any implementation-defined restrictions on interrupt handlers should be detected before run time.<br />

<MarginText>22/5_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 1   The Attach{"_"}Handler aspect can provide static attachment of handlers to interrupts if the implementation supports preelaboration of protected objects. (See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.4">C.4</a>.)<br />

<MarginText>23/5_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01", "AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 2   For a protected object that has a (protected) procedure attached to an interrupt, the correct ceiling priority is at least as high as the highest processor priority at which that interrupt will ever be delivered.<br />

<MarginText>24_C.3.1</MarginText>
NOTE 3   Protected procedures can also be attached dynamically to interrupts via operations declared in the predefined package Interrupts.<br />

<MarginText>25_C.3.1</MarginText>
NOTE 4   An example of a possible implementation-defined restriction is disallowing the use of the standard storage pools within the body of a protected procedure that is an interrupt handler.<br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>25.a/2_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00253-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> Corrected the wording so that the rules for the use of Attach{"_"}Handler and Interrupt{"_"}Handler are identical. This means that uses of pragma Interrupt{"_"}Handler outside of the target protected type or single protected object are now illegal. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>25.b/2_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00121-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0068</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified the meaning of &ldquo;the previous handler&rdquo; when finalizing protected objects containing interrupt handlers.<br />

<MarginText>25.c/2_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00303-01"]} />
Dropped the requirement that an object of a type containing an Interrupt{"_"}Handler pragma must be declared at the library level. This was a generic contract model violation. This change is not an extension, as an attempt to attach such a handler with a routine in package Interrupts will fail an accessibility check anyway. Moreover, implementations can retain the rule as an implementation-defined restriction on the use of the type, as permitted by the Implementation Permissions above. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>25.d/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
Aspects Interrupt{"_"}Handler and Attach{"_"}Handler are new; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Interrupt{"_"}Handler and Attach{"_"}Handler are now obsolescent. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>25.e/3_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0033-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added missing generic contract wording for the aspects Attach{"_"}Handler and Interrupt{"_"}Handler. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>25.f/5_C.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0252-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Program{"_"}Error might be raised if two handlers are attached when restriction No{"_"}Dynamic{"_"}Attachment is in effect (including as part of the Ravenscar profile). Original Ada 2012 would have just ignored the first handler. This is almost certainly a bug rather than an intended result. <br />

<a id="Subclause_C.3.2"></a>

## C.3.2  The Package Interrupts

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The following language-defined packages exist: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with System;{"\n"}with System.Multiprocessors;{"\n"}package Ada.Interrupts{"\n"}   with Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}   type Interrupt{"_"}Id is implementation-defined;{"\n"}   type Parameterless{"_"}Handler is{"\n"}      access protected procedure{"\n"}      with Nonblocking ={">"} False;{"\n"}
<MarginText>3/1_C.3.2</MarginText>
This paragraph was deleted.{"\n"}
<MarginText>4_C.3.2</MarginText>
   function Is{"_"}Reserved (Interrupt : Interrupt{"_"}Id){"\n"}      return Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>5_C.3.2</MarginText>
   function Is{"_"}Attached (Interrupt : Interrupt{"_"}Id){"\n"}      return Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6_C.3.2</MarginText>
   function Current{"_"}Handler (Interrupt : Interrupt{"_"}Id){"\n"}      return Parameterless{"_"}Handler;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7_C.3.2</MarginText>
   procedure Attach{"_"}Handler{"\n"}      (New{"_"}Handler : in Parameterless{"_"}Handler;{"\n"}       Interrupt   : in Interrupt{"_"}Id);{"\n"}
<MarginText>8_C.3.2</MarginText>
   procedure Exchange{"_"}Handler{"\n"}      (Old{"_"}Handler : out Parameterless{"_"}Handler;{"\n"}       New{"_"}Handler : in Parameterless{"_"}Handler;{"\n"}       Interrupt   : in Interrupt{"_"}Id);{"\n"}
