#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>13_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The Interrupt{"_"}Id type is an implementation-defined discrete type used to identify interrupts.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The Is{"_"}Reserved function returns True if and only if the specified interrupt is reserved.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The Is{"_"}Attached function returns True if and only if a user-specified interrupt handler is attached to the interrupt.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16/1_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00166-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0069</i>{"}"} The Current{"_"}Handler function returns a value that represents the attached handler of the interrupt. If no user-defined handler is attached to the interrupt, Current{"_"}Handler returns <b>null</b>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/3_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The Attach{"_"}Handler procedure attaches the specified handler to the interrupt, overriding any existing treatment (including a user handler) in effect for that interrupt. If New{"_"}Handler is <b>null</b>, the default treatment is restored. If New{"_"}Handler designates a protected procedure for which the aspect Interrupt{"_"}Handler is False, Program{"_"}Error is raised. In this case, the operation does not modify the existing interrupt treatment.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/1_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00166-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0069</i>{"}"} The Exchange{"_"}Handler procedure operates in the same manner as Attach{"_"}Handler with the addition that the value returned in Old{"_"}Handler designates the previous treatment for the specified interrupt. If the previous treatment is not a user-defined handler, <b>null</b> is returned. <br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a_C.3.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Calling Attach{"_"}Handler or Exchange{"_"}Handler with this value for New{"_"}Handler restores the previous handler.<br />

<MarginText>18.a.1/1_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00166-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0069</i>{"}"} If the application uses only parameterless procedures as handlers (other types of handlers may be provided by the implementation, but are not required by the standard), then if Old{"_"}Handler is not <b>null</b>, it may be called to execute the previous handler. This provides a way to cascade application interrupt handlers. However, the default handler cannot be cascaded this way (Old{"_"}Handler must be <b>null</b> for the default handler). <br />

<MarginText>19_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The Detach{"_"}Handler procedure restores the default treatment for the specified interrupt.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>For all operations defined in this package that take a parameter of type Interrupt{"_"}Id, with the exception of Is{"_"}Reserved and Reference, a check is made that the specified interrupt is not reserved. Program{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21/3_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If, by using the Attach{"_"}Handler, Detach{"_"}Handler, or Exchange{"_"}Handler procedures, an attempt is made to detach a handler that was attached statically (using the aspect Attach{"_"}Handler), the handler is not detached and Program{"_"}Error is raised.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22/2_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
<p>The Reference function returns a value of type System.Address that can be used to attach a task entry via an address clause (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#Subclause_J.7.1">J.7.1</a>) to the interrupt specified by Interrupt. This function raises Program{"_"}Error if attaching task entries to interrupts (or to this particular interrupt) is not supported.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22.1/3_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0153-3"]} />
<p>The function Get{"_"}CPU returns the processor on which the handler for Interrupt is executed. If the handler can execute on more than one processor the value System.Multiprocessors.Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU is returned.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>23_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>At no time during attachment or exchange of handlers shall the current handler of the corresponding interrupt be undefined.<br /></p>

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>24/5_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0320-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>The implementation shall document, when the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) is in effect, the default ceiling priority assigned to a protected object that contains a protected procedure that specifies either the Attach{"_"}Handler or Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspects, but does not specify the Interrupt{"_"}Priority aspect. [This default can be different for different interrupts.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>24.a.1/3_C.3.2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy is in effect, the default ceiling priority for a protected object that specifies an interrupt handler aspect.<br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>25_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p>If implementation-defined forms of interrupt handler procedures are supported, such as protected procedures with parameters, then for each such form of a handler, a type analogous to Parameterless{"_"}Handler should be specified in a child package of Interrupts, with the same operations as in the predefined package Interrupts.<br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a/2_C.3.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If implementation-defined forms of interrupt handler procedures are supported, then for each such form of a handler, a type analogous to Parameterless{"_"}Handler should be specified in a child package of Interrupts, with the same operations as in the predefined package Interrupts.<br />

<MarginText>26_C.3.2</MarginText>
NOTE   The package Interrupts.Names contains implementation-defined names (and constant values) for the interrupts that are supported by the implementation.<br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>27_C.3.2</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of interrupt handlers:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>28/5_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0178-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Device{"_"}Priority : constant{"\n"}  array (Ada.Interrupts.Interrupt{"_"}Id range 1..5) of{"\n"}    System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority := ( ... );{"\n"}protected type Device{"_"}Interface{"\n"}  (Int{"_"}Id : Ada.Interrupts.Interrupt{"_"}Id) {"\n"}     with Interrupt{"_"}Priority ={">"} Device{"_"}Priority(Int{"_"}Id) is{"\n"}  procedure Handler{"\n"}     with Attach{"_"}Handler ={">"} Int{"_"}Id;{"\n"}  ...{"\n"}end Device{"_"}Interface;{"\n"}  ...{"\n"}Device{"_"}1{"_"}Driver : Device{"_"}Interface(1);{"\n"}  ...{"\n"}Device{"_"}5{"_"}Driver : Device{"_"}Interface(5);{"\n"}  ...{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>28.a/2_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00166-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0069</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that the value returned by Current{"_"}Handler and Exchange{"_"}Handler for the default treatment is null. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>28.b/3_C.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
Function Get{"_"}CPU is added to Interrupts. If Interrupts is referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, and an entity <i>E</i> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> of Get{"_"}CPU is defined in a package that is also referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, the entity <i>E</i> may no longer be use-visible, resulting in errors. This should be rare and is easily fixed if it does occur. <br />

# C.4. Preelaboration Requirements

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  150

# C.4. Preelaboration Requirements

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause specifies additional implementation and documentation requirements for the Preelaborate aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>).] <br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall not incur any run-time overhead for the elaboration checks of subprograms and <code>protected{"_"}bodies</code> declared in preelaborated library units. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall not execute any memory write operations after load time for the elaboration of constant objects declared immediately within the declarative region of a preelaborated library package, so long as the subtype and initial expression (or default initial expressions if initialized by default) of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> satisfy the following restrictions. The meaning of <i>load time</i> is implementation defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>On systems where the image of the partition is initially copied from disk to RAM, or from ROM to RAM, prior to starting execution of the partition, the intention is that &ldquo;load time&rdquo; consist of this initial copying step. On other systems, load time and run time might actually be interspersed. <br />

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes a statically constrained subtype, with statically constrained subcomponents, if any;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01"]} />
<li>no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> denotes a controlled type, a private type, a private extension, a generic formal private type, a generic formal derived type, or a descendant of such a type;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>For an implementation that uses the registration method of finalization, a controlled object will require some code executed to register the object at the appropriate point. The other types are those that <i>might</i> have a controlled component. None of these types were allowed in preelaborated units in Ada 95. These types are covered by the , of course, so they should still execute as little code as possible. <br />

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0029">constraint</a></code> is a static constraint;<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> is for an access-to-constant type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<li>any uses of predefined operators appear only within static expressions;<br /></li>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<li>any <code>primaries</code> that are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s, other than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>s for the Access or Address attributes, appear only within static expressions; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This cuts out <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code>s that are not static, except for Access and Address. <br />

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0368-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> that is not part of a static expression is an expanded name or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> that statically names some entity; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.a/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0368-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This cuts out <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.4#S0218">function_call</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6#S0162">type_conversion</a></code>s that are not static, including calls on attribute functions like 'Image and 'Value. We do allow components if those components don't require any evaluation or checks. <br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>any <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0074">discrete_choice</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#S0113">array_aggregate</a></code> is static;<br /></li>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<li>no language-defined check associated with the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> can fail. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The intent is that aggregates all of whose scalar subcomponents are static and all of whose access subcomponents are <b>null</b>, allocators for access-to-constant types, or X'Access, will be supported with no run-time code generated. <br />

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document any circumstances under which the elaboration of a preelaborated package causes code to be executed at run time. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>Any circumstances when the elaboration of a preelaborated package causes code to be executed.<br />

<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document whether the method used for initialization of preelaborated variables allows a partition to be restarted without reloading. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a.1/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>Whether a partition can be restarted without reloading.<br />

<MarginText>13.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>13.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This covers the issue of the run-time system itself being restartable, so that need not be a separate Documentation Requirement. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>It is recommended that preelaborated packages be implemented in such a way that there should be little or no code executed at run time for the elaboration of entities not already covered by the Implementation Requirements.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Preelaborated packages should be implemented such that little or no code is executed at run time for the elaboration of entities.<br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>14.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01"]} />
Added wording to exclude the additional kinds of types allowed in preelaborated units from the Implementation Requirements. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>14.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0368-1"]} />
Added wording to allow components so long as no evaluation or checks are required for the reference. <br />

# C.5. Aspect Discard_Names

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.5.mdx

sidebar_position:  151

# C.5. Aspect Discard_Names

<MarginText>1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0072-1"]} />
<p>[Specifying the aspect Discard{"_"}Names can be used to request a reduction in storage used for the names of entities with runtime name text.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0072-1"]} />
<p>An entity with <i>runtime name text</i> is a nonderived enumeration first subtype, a tagged first subtype, or an exception.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.2/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0072-1"]} />
<p>For an entity with runtime name text, the following language-defined representation aspect may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.3/4</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Discard{"_"}Names</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Discard{"_"}Names is Boolean. If directly specified, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a static expression. If not specified (including by inheritance), the aspect is False.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>1.a.1/4</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Discard{"_"}Names: </b>Requests a reduction in storage for names associated with an entity.<br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Discard{"_"}Names is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Discard{"_"}Names[([On ={">"} ] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>)];<br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Discard{"_"}Names is allowed only immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>, immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, or as a configuration pragma. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>5/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0072-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> (if present) shall denote an entity with runtime name text. The pragma specifies that the aspect Discard{"_"}Names for the type or exception has the value True. Without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>, the pragma specifies that all entities with runtime name text declared after the pragma, within the same declarative region have the value True for aspect Discard{"_"}Names. Alternatively, the pragma can be used as a configuration pragma. If the configuration pragma Discard{"_"}Names applies to a compilation unit, all entities with runtime name text declared in the compilation unit have the value True for the aspect Discard{"_"}Names.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0072-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the aspect is specified for a type, then it is inherited by all descendants of the type. The aspect cannot be specified as False on a derived type (because specifying the aspect is not allowed on derived enumeration types, and by rule applying to all aspects for other types (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>)). <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> is given, then a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Discard{"_"}Names is a representation pragma.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0072-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>7/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01", "AI95-00400-01", "AI12-0072-1"]} />
<p>If the aspect Discard{"_"}Names is True for an enumeration type, then the semantics of the Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value attributes are implementation defined for that type[; the semantics of Image, Wide{"_"}Image, Value, and Wide{"_"}Value are still defined in terms of Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value]. In addition, the semantics of Text{"_"}IO.Enumeration{"_"}IO are implementation defined. If the aspect Discard{"_"}Names is True for a tagged type, then the semantics of the Tags.Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Expanded{"_"}Name function are implementation defined for that type[; the semantics of Tags.Expanded{"_"}Name and Tags.Wide{"_"}Expanded{"_"}Name are still defined in terms of Tags.Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Expanded{"_"}Name]. If the aspect Discard{"_"}Names is True for an exception, then the semantics of the Exceptions.Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Exception{"_"}Name function are implementation defined for that exception[; the semantics of Exceptions.Exception{"_"}Name and Exceptions.Wide{"_"}Exception{"_"}Name are still defined in terms of Exceptions.Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Exception{"_"}Name].<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The semantics of some attributes and functions of an entity for which aspect Discard{"_"}Names is True.<br />

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The Width attribute is still defined in terms of Image.<br />

<MarginText>7.c/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01", "AI12-0072-1"]} />
The semantics of S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image and S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value are implementation defined for any subtype of an enumeration type for which the aspect is True. (The pragma, if used, actually names the first subtype, of course.) <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>8/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0072-1"]} />
<p>If the aspect Discard{"_"}Names is True for an entity, then the implementation should reduce the amount of storage used for storing names associated with that entity. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If aspect Discard{"_"}Names is True for an entity, then the amount of storage used for storing names associated with that entity should be reduced.<br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A typical implementation of the Image attribute for enumeration types is to store a table containing the names of all the enumeration literals. Aspect Discard{"_"}Names allows the implementation to avoid storing such a table without having to prove that the Image attribute is never used (which can be difficult in the presence of separate compilation).<br />

<MarginText>8.c</MarginText>
We did not specify the semantics of the Image attribute when aspect Discard{"_"}Names is True because different semantics might be desirable in different situations. In some cases, it might make sense to use the Image attribute to print out a useful value that can be used to identify the entity given information in compiler-generated listings. In other cases, it might make sense to get an error at compile time or at run time. In cases where memory is plentiful, the simplest implementation makes sense: ignore the aspect. Implementations that are capable of avoiding the extra storage in cases where the Image attribute is never used might also wish to ignore the aspect.<br />

<MarginText>8.d</MarginText>
The same applies to the Tags.Expanded{"_"}Name and Exceptions.Exception{"_"}Name functions. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>8.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01", "AI95-00400-01"]} />
Updated the wording to reflect that the double wide image and value functions are now the master versions that the others are defined from. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>8.f/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0072-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Defined the pragma in terms of the aspect Discard{"_"}Names, and added a missing definition of the meaning of the configuration pragma. This is not intended to make any semantic change (Ada 2012 has an aspect Discard{"_"}Names defined via blanket rules for representation pragmas in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>), just to clarify the meaning. <br />

# C.6. Shared Variable Control

# C.6. Shared Variable Control

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause defines representation aspects that control the use of shared variables.] <br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraphs 2 through 6 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0282-1"]} />
<p>For an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#S0321">formal_complete_type_declaration</a></code>, the following representation aspects may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.2/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Atomic</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Atomic is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.a/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Atomic: </b>Declare that a type, object, or component is atomic.<br />

<MarginText>6.3/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Independent</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Independent is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.b/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Independent: </b>Declare that a type, object, or component is independently addressable.<br />

<MarginText>6.4/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Volatile</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Volatile is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.c/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Volatile: </b>Declare that a type, object, or component is volatile.<br />

<MarginText>6.5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<dt><br/>Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.c.1/5</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only: </b>Declare that a volatile type, object, or component is full access.<br />

<MarginText>6.6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0282-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> of an array type, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> for an object of an anonymous array type, or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#S0321">formal_complete_type_declaration</a></code> of a formal array type, the following representation aspects may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.7/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Atomic{"_"}Components</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Atomic{"_"}Components is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.d/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Atomic{"_"}Components: </b>Declare that the components of an array type or object are atomic.<br />

<MarginText>6.8/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Volatile{"_"}Components</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Volatile{"_"}Components is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.e/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Volatile{"_"}Components: </b>Declare that the components of an array type or object are volatile.<br />

<MarginText>6.9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0282-1"]} />
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code> of a composite type, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> for an object of an anonymous composite type, or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#S0321">formal_complete_type_declaration</a></code> of a formal composite type, the following representation aspect may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.10/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Independent{"_"}Components</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Independent{"_"}Components is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.f/3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Independent{"_"}Components: </b>Declare that the components of an array or record type, or an array object, are independently addressable.<br />

<MarginText>6.11/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0363-1"]} />
<p>If any of these aspects are directly specified, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a static expression. If not specified for a type (including by inheritance), the Atomic, Atomic{"_"}Components, and Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only aspects are False. If any of these aspects are specified True for a type, then the corresponding aspect is True for all objects of the type. If the Atomic aspect is specified True, then the aspects Volatile, Independent, and Volatile{"_"}Component (if defined) are True; if the Atomic{"_"}Components aspect is specified True, then the aspects Volatile, Volatile{"_"}Components, and Independent{"_"}Components are True. If the Volatile aspect is specified True, then the Volatile{"_"}Components aspect (if defined) is True, and vice versa. When not determined by one of the other aspects, or for an object by its type, the Volatile, Volatile{"_"}Components, Independent, and Independent{"_"}Components aspects are False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.g/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Aspects Volatile and Volatile{"_"}Components (when defined) are equivalent. We provide the Volatile{"_"}Components aspect only to give symmetry with Atomic{"_"}Components and Independent{"_"}Components aspects. <br />

<MarginText>7/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00272-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An <i>atomic</i> type is one for which the aspect Atomic is True. An <i>atomic</i> object (including a component) is one for which the aspect Atomic is True, or a component of an array for which the aspect Atomic{"_"}Components is True for the associated type, or any object of an atomic type, other than objects obtained by evaluating a slice. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00272-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A slice of an atomic array object is not itself atomic. That's necessary as executing a read or write of a dynamic number of components in a single instruction is not possible on many targets. <br />

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>A <i>volatile</i> type is one for which the aspect Volatile is True. A <i>volatile</i> object (including a component) is one for which the aspect Volatile is True, or a component of an array for which the aspect Volatile{"_"}Components is True for the associated type, or any object of a volatile type. In addition, every atomic type or object is also defined to be volatile. Finally, if an object is volatile, then so are all of its subcomponents [(the same does not apply to atomic)].<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.1/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0001-1"]} />
<p>When True, the aspects Independent and Independent{"_"}Components <i>specify as independently addressable</i> the named object or component(s), or in the case of a type, all objects or components of that type. All atomic objects and aliased objects are considered to be specified as independently addressable.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the compiler cannot guarantee that an object (including a component) for which aspect Independent or aspect Independent{"_"}Components is True is independently addressable from any other nonoverlapping object, then the aspect specification must be rejected.<br />

<MarginText>8.b/3</MarginText>
Similarly, an atomic object (including atomic components) is always independently addressable from any other nonoverlapping object. Any representation item which would prevent this from being true should be rejected, notwithstanding what this Standard says elsewhere (specifically, in the Recommended Level of Support). <br />

<MarginText>8.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<p>The Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only aspect shall not be specified unless the associated type or object is volatile [(or atomic)]. A <i>full access</i> type is any atomic type, or a volatile type for which the aspect Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only is True. A <i>full access</i> object (including a component) is any atomic object, or a volatile object for which the aspect Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only is True for the object[ or its type]. A Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only aspect is illegal if any subcomponent of the object or type is a full access object or is of a generic formal type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This last rule breaks privacy, but that is considered OK for representation clauses when there is no clear alternative. Note that atomic objects may be nested, so long as the outer atomic object does not have the Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only aspect True. <br />

<MarginText>8.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We disallow subcomponents of a generic formal type in a Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only object or type as the actual to a formal type can be a full access type. We could have had a less restrictive rule, but such a use is unlikely as full access only objects are intended to be used to access memory-mapped devices with access restrictions, and those will need a concrete mapping not possible for generic formal types. <br />

<p><i>Paragraph 9 was moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>9.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If aspect Independent{"_"}Components is specified for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>, the declaration shall be that of an array or record type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0001-1"]} />
<p>It is illegal to specify either of the aspects Atomic or Atomic{"_"}Components to have the value True for an object or type if the implementation cannot support the indivisible and independent reads and updates required by the aspect (see below).<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0001-1"]} />
<p>It is illegal to specify the Size attribute of an atomic object, the Component{"_"}Size attribute for an array type with atomic components, or the layout attributes of an atomic component, in a way that prevents the implementation from performing the required indivisible and independent reads and updates.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4", "AI05-0218-1", "AI12-0282-1", "AI12-0363-1"]} />
<p>If an atomic object is passed as a parameter, then the formal parameter shall either have an atomic type or allow pass by copy. If an atomic object is used as an actual for a generic formal object of mode <b>in out</b>, then the type of the generic formal object shall be atomic. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> for an Access attribute denotes an atomic object [(including a component)], then the designated type of the resulting access type shall be atomic. Corresponding rules apply to volatile objects and to full access objects.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A formal parameter allows pass by copy if it is not <b>aliased</b> and it is of a type that allows pass by copy (that is, is not a by-reference type). <br />

<MarginText>12.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0128-1", "AI12-0363-1"]} />
<p>If a nonatomic subcomponent of a full access object is passed as an actual parameter in a call then the formal parameter shall allow pass by copy (and, at run time, the parameter shall be passed by copy). A nonatomic subcomponent of a full access object shall not be used as an actual for a generic formal of mode <b>in out</b>. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> for an Access attribute shall not denote a nonatomic subcomponent of a full access object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12.2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0218-1", "AI12-0282-1", "AI12-0363-1"]} />
<p>If the Atomic, Atomic{"_"}Components, Volatile, Volatile{"_"}Components, Independent, Independent{"_"}Components, or Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only aspect is True for a generic formal type, then that aspect shall be True for the actual type. If an atomic type is used as an actual for a generic formal derived type, then the ancestor of the formal type shall be atomic. A corresponding rule applies to volatile types and similarly to full access types.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12.3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<p>If a type with volatile components is used as an actual for a generic formal array type, then the components of the formal type shall be volatile. Furthermore, if the actual type has atomic components and the formal array type has aliased components, then the components of the formal array type shall also be atomic. A corresponding rule applies when the actual type has volatile full access components.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The limitations on formal array types are separate for volatile and atomic because of the fact that only volatility is carried down to all subcomponents of a volatile object, while atomicity is not. The goal of both limitations is that we don't want 'Access for an access type to produce a value that designates an object whose atomicity and volatility don't agree with that of the designated type of the access type. The above rules ensure that the generic &ldquo;sees&rdquo; the relevant volatility and atomicity. <br />

<MarginText>13/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If an aspect Volatile, Volatile{"_"}Components, Atomic, or Atomic{"_"}Components is directly specified to have the value True for a stand-alone constant object, then the aspect Import shall also be specified as True for it. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Hence, no initialization expression is allowed for such a constant. Note that a constant that is atomic or volatile because of its type is allowed. <br />

<MarginText>13.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Stand-alone constants that are explicitly specified as Atomic or Volatile only make sense if they are being manipulated outside the Ada program. From the Ada perspective the object is read-only. Nevertheless, if imported and atomic or volatile, the implementation should presume it might be altered externally. For an imported stand-alone constant that is not atomic or volatile, the implementation can assume that it will not be altered. <br />

<MarginText>13.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0218-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>Volatile{"_"}Components and Atomic{"_"}Components actually are aspects of the anonymous array type; this rule only applies when the aspect is specified directly on the constant object and not when the (named) array type has the aspect. <br />

<MarginText>13.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>It is illegal to specify the aspect Independent or Independent{"_"}Components as True for a component, object or type if the implementation cannot provide the independent addressability required by the aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10">9.10</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>It is illegal to specify a representation aspect for a component, object or type for which the aspect Independent or Independent{"_"}Components is True, in a way that prevents the implementation from providing the independent addressability required by the aspect.<br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraph 14 was moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>15</MarginText>
<p>For an atomic object (including an atomic component) all reads and updates of the object as a whole are indivisible.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0117-1", "AI05-0275-1"]} />
<p>All tasks of the program (on all processors) that read or update volatile variables see the same order of updates to the variables. A use of an atomic variable or other mechanism may be necessary to avoid erroneous execution and to ensure that access to nonatomic volatile variables is sequential (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10">9.10</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0117-1", "AI05-0275-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>To ensure this, on a multiprocessor, any read or update of an atomic object may require the use of an appropriate memory barrier. <br />

<MarginText>16.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0275-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>From <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10">9.10</a> it follows that (in non-erroneous programs) accesses to variables, including those shared by multiple tasks, are always sequential. This guarantees that no task will ever see partial updates of any variable. For volatile variables (including atomic variables), the above rule additionally specifies that all tasks see the same order of updates.<br />

<MarginText>16.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0275-1"]} />
If for a shared variable <i>X</i>, a read of <i>X</i> occurs sequentially after an update of <i>X</i>, then the read will return the updated value if <i>X</i> is volatile or atomic, but may or or may not return the updated value if <i>X</i> is nonvolatile. For nonvolatile accesses, a signaling action is needed in order to share the updated value.<br />

<MarginText>16.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0275-1"]} />
Because accesses to the same atomic variable by different tasks establish a sequential order between the actions of those tasks, implementations may be required to emit memory barriers around such updates or use atomic instructions that imply such barriers. <br />

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p>Two actions are sequential (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.10">9.10</a>) if each is the read or update of the same atomic object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<p>If a type is atomic or volatile and it is not a by-copy type, then the type is defined to be a by-reference type. If any subcomponent of a type is atomic or volatile, then the type is defined to be a by-reference type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<p>If an actual parameter is atomic or volatile, and the corresponding formal parameter is not, then the parameter is passed by copy. <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Note that in the case where such a parameter is normally passed by reference, a copy of the actual will have to be produced at the call-site, and a pointer to the copy passed to the formal parameter. If the actual is atomic, any copying has to use indivisible read on the way in, and indivisible write on the way out. <br />

<MarginText>19.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>It has to be known at compile time whether an atomic or a volatile parameter is to be passed by copy or by reference. For some types, it is unspecified whether parameters are passed by copy or by reference. The above rules further specify the parameter passing rules involving atomic and volatile types and objects. <br />

<MarginText>19.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0128-1", "AI12-0347-1"]} />
<p>All reads of or writes to any nonatomic subcomponent of a full access object are performed by reading and/or writing all of the nearest enclosing full access object.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0128-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>{"}"} For example, if a 32-bit record object has four nonatomic components, each occupying one byte, then an assignment to one of those components might normally be implemented on some target machines via some sort of store{"_"}byte instruction; if the record object is an atomic full access object then instead a 32-bit read-modify-write must be performed. That read-modify-write need not be atomic, although the read and the write must each separately be atomic. Note that it doesn't matter whether the store{"_"}byte instruction would have executed atomically. This rule is needed in some cases for memory-mapped device registers. <br />

<MarginText>19.d/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The atomic reads and writes associated with accesses to nonatomic components of a full access object that is atomic are normal atomic operations &mdash; all of the rules that apply to other atomic operations apply to these as well. In particular, these atomic reads and writes are sequential if they apply to the same object. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>20/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0128-1", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>The external effect of a program (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>) is defined to include each read and update of a volatile or atomic object. The implementation shall not generate any memory reads or updates of atomic or volatile objects other than those specified by the program. However, there may be target-dependent cases where reading or writing a volatile but nonatomic object (typically a component) necessarily involves reading and/or writing neighboring storage, and that neighboring storage can overlap a volatile object. <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The presumption is that volatile or atomic objects might reside in an &ldquo;active&rdquo; part of the address space where each read has a potential side effect, and at the very least might deliver a different value.<br />

<MarginText>20.b</MarginText>
The rule above and the definition of external effect are intended to prevent (at least) the following incorrect optimizations, where V is a volatile variable: <br />

<MarginText>20.c</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>X:= V; Y:=V; cannot be allowed to be translated as Y:=V; X:=V;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.d</MarginText>
<li>Deleting redundant loads: X:= V; X:= V; shall read the value of V from memory twice.<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.e</MarginText>
<li>Deleting redundant stores: V:= X; V:= X; shall write into V twice.<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.f</MarginText>
<li>Extra stores: V:= X+Y; should not translate to something like V:= X; V:= V+Y;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.g</MarginText>
<li>Extra loads: X:= V; Y:= X+Z; X:=X+B; should not translate to something like Y:= V+Z; X:= V+B;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.h</MarginText>
<li>Reordering of loads from volatile variables: X:= V1; Y:= V2; (whether or not V1 = V2) should not translate to Y:= V2; X:= V1;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20.i</MarginText>
<li>Reordering of stores to volatile variables: V1:= X; V2:= X; should not translate to V2:=X; V1:= X; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>20.j/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0128-1"]} />
The part about &ldquo;target-dependent cases&rdquo; is intended to let compilers use a read-modify-write operation when a volatile component has a size that cannot be directly read or written with the available machine instructions. (For instance, writing a Boolean component with size 1 in a volatile packed array of Boolean requires a pre-read on most existing machines.) <br />

<MarginText>21/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0001-1"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI12-0001-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>21.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0282-1"]} />
<p>Within the body of an instance of a generic unit that has a formal type <i>T</i> that is not atomic and an actual type that is atomic, if an object <i>O</i> of type <i>T</i> is declared and explicitly specified as atomic, the implementation may introduce an additional copy on passing <i>O</i> to a subprogram with a parameter of type <i>T</i> that is normally passed by reference. A corresponding permission applies to volatile parameter passing. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00259-01", "AI12-0128-1"]} />
<p>A load or store of a volatile object whose size is a multiple of System.Storage{"_"}Unit and whose alignment is nonzero, should be implemented by accessing exactly the bits of the object and no others, except in the case of a volatile but nonatomic subcomponent of an atomic object. <br /></p>

<MarginText>22.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>A load or store of a volatile object whose size is a multiple of System.Storage{"_"}Unit and whose alignment is nonzero, should be implemented by accessing exactly the bits of the object and no others.<br />

<MarginText>22.b/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0128-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Since any object can be a volatile object, including packed array components and bit-mapped record components, we require the above only when it is reasonable to assume that the machine can avoid accessing bits outside of the object. The exception is needed so this advice doesn't conflict with other rules of this subclauase. <br />

<MarginText>22.c/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>This implies that the load or store of a volatile object that meets the above requirement should not be combined with that of any other object, nor should it access any bits not belonging to any other object. This means that the suitability of the implementation for memory-mapped I/O can be determined from its documentation, as any cases where the implementation does not follow  must be documented. <br />

<MarginText>23/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00259-01"]} />
<p>A load or store of an atomic object should, where possible, be implemented by a single load or store instruction. <br /></p>

<MarginText>23.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>A load or store of an atomic object should be implemented by a single load or store instruction.<br />

<MarginText>24</MarginText>
NOTE 1   An imported volatile or atomic constant behaves as a constant (i.e. read-only) with respect to other parts of the Ada program, but can still be modified by an &ldquo;external source&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>25/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0001-1"]} />
NOTE 2   Specifying the Pack aspect cannot override the effect of specifying an Atomic or Atomic{"_"}Components aspect.<br />

<MarginText>26/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0128-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 3   When mapping an Ada object to a memory-mapped hardware register, the Ada object can be declared atomic to ensure that the compiler will read and write exactly the bits of the register as specified in the source code and no others.<br />

<MarginText>26.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This is especially important for a write-only hardware register, as in such a case a read-modify-write cycle will not work. The only time the language guarantees such a cycle will not happen is when writing an entire atomic object. If one wants to write individual components of a write-only hardware register (assuming the hardware supports that), those also need to be declared atomic. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>26.b</MarginText>
Pragma Atomic replaces Ada 83's pragma Shared. The name &ldquo;Shared&rdquo; was confusing, because the pragma was not used to mark variables as shared. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>26.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00259-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
Added  to clarify the meaning of Atomic and Volatile in machine terms. The documentation that this advice applies will make the use of Ada implementations more predictable for low-level (such as device register) programming.<br />

<MarginText>26.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00272-01"]} />
Added wording to clarify that a slice of an object of an atomic type is not atomic, just like a component of an atomic type is not (necessarily) atomic. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0218-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Plugged a hole involving volatile components of formal types when the formal type's component has a nonvolatile type. This was done by making certain actual types illegal for formal derived and formal array types; these types were allowed for Ada 95 and Ada 2005. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.f/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
Aspects Independent and Independent{"_"}Components are new; they eliminate ambiguity about independent addressability.<br />

<MarginText>26.g/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
Aspects Atomic, Atomic{"_"}Components, Volatile, and Volatile{"_"}Components are new; <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Atomic, Atomic{"_"}Components, Volatile, and Volatile{"_"}Components are now obsolescent. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>26.h/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0117-1", "AI05-0275-1"]} />
Revised the definition of volatile to eliminate overspecification and simply focus on the root requirement (that all tasks see the same view of volatile objects). This is not an inconsistency; "memory" arguably includes on-chip caches so long as those are kept consistent. Moreover, it is difficult to imagine a program that could tell the difference.<br />

<MarginText>26.i/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0142-4"]} />
Added wording to take explicitly aliased parameters (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1">6.1</a>) into account when determining the legality of parameter passing of volatile and atomic objects. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.j/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0128-1"]} />
 Required that nonatomic components of a atomic object use a read-modify-write cycle, as well as clarifying that such a cycle is allowed for volatile objects that aren't exactly the size of a machine scalar. That can introduce a read-modify-write cycle where one was not used previously (for instance, if the components are exactly byte-sized on most machines); it is thought that this will more often fix bugs with access to hardware than it will cause them. If this is an issue, declaring the components themselves as atomic will restore the previous behavior. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.k/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0282-1"]} />
These aspects now can be specified for generic formal types.<br />

<MarginText>26.l/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0363-1"]} />
Aspect Full{"_"}Access{"_"}Only is new; it can be used to guarantee access to a complete device register for any operation even when the register is mapped to a number of components. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>26.m/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0001-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that aliased objects are considered to be specified as independently addressable, and also eliminated an unnecessary rule. <br />

<a id="Subclause_C.6.1"></a>

## C.6.1  The Package System.Atomic_Operations

<MarginText>1/5_C.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>The language-defined package System.Atomic{"_"}Operations is the parent of a set of child units that provide facilities for manipulating objects of atomic types and for supporting lock-free synchronization. The subprograms of this subsystem are Intrinsic subprograms (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.1">6.3.1</a>) in order to provide convenient access to machine operations that can provide these capabilities if they are available in the target environment. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/5_C.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>The library package System.Atomic{"_"}Operations has the following declaration:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_C.6.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package System.Atomic{"_"}Operations{"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking is{"\n"}end System.Atomic{"_"}Operations;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4/5_C.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>System.Atomic{"_"}Operations serves as the parent of other language-defined library units that manipulate atomic objects; its declaration is empty.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/5_C.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>A call to a subprogram is said to be <i>lock-free</i> if the subprogram is guaranteed to return from the call while keeping the processor of the logical thread of control busy for the duration of the call.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/5_C.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>In each child package, a function Is{"_"}Lock{"_"}Free(...) is provided to check whether the operations of the child package can all be provided lock-free for a given object. Is{"_"}Lock{"_"}Free returns True if operations defined in the child package are lock-free when applied to the object denoted by Item, and Is{"_"}Lock{"_"}Free returns False otherwise.<br /></p>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>6.a/5_C.6.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
This package is new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_C.6.2"></a>

## C.6.2  The Package System.Atomic_Operations.Exchange

<MarginText>1/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>The language-defined generic package System.Atomic{"_"}Operations.Exchange provides the following operations:<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>To atomically compare the value of two atomic objects, and update the first atomic object with a desired value if both objects were found to be equal, or otherwise update the second object with the value of the first object.<br /></li>
<MarginText>3/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<li>To atomically update the value of an atomic object, and then return the value that the atomic object had just prior to the update.<br /></li>
</ul>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>4/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>The generic library package System.Atomic{"_"}Operations.Exchange has the following declaration:<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
generic{"\n"}   type Atomic{"_"}Type is private with Atomic;{"\n"}package System.Atomic{"_"}Operations.Exchange{"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking is{"\n"}
<MarginText>6/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
   function Atomic{"_"}Exchange (Item  : aliased in out Atomic{"_"}Type;{"\n"}                             Value : Atomic{"_"}Type) return Atomic{"_"}Type{"\n"}      with Convention ={">"} Intrinsic;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
   function Atomic{"_"}Compare{"_"}And{"_"}Exchange {"\n"}     (Item    : aliased in out Atomic{"_"}Type;{"\n"}      Prior   : aliased in out Atomic{"_"}Type;{"\n"}      Desired : Atomic{"_"}Type) return Boolean{"\n"}      with Convention ={">"} Intrinsic;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
   function Is{"_"}Lock{"_"}Free (Item : aliased Atomic{"_"}Type) return Boolean{"\n"}      with Convention ={">"} Intrinsic;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
end System.Atomic{"_"}Operations.Exchange;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>Atomic{"_"}Exchange atomically assigns the value of Value to Item, and returns the previous value of Item.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>Atomic{"_"}Compare{"_"}And{"_"}Exchange first evaluates the value of Prior. Atomic{"_"}Compare{"_"}And{"_"}Exchange then performs the following steps as part of a single indivisible operation:<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>evaluates the value of Item;<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<li>compares the value of Item with the value of Prior;<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<li>if equal, assigns Item the value of Desired;<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, makes no change to the value of Item.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p>After these steps, if the value of Item and Prior did not match, Prior is assigned the original value of Item, and the function returns False. Otherwise, Prior is unaffected and the function returns True.<br /></p>

#### Examples

<MarginText>17/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
<p><i>Example of a spin lock using Atomic{"_"}Exchange:</i><br /></p>

<MarginText>18/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
type Atomic{"_"}Boolean is new Boolean with Atomic;{"\n"}package Exchange is new{"\n"}   Atomic{"_"}Operations.Exchange (Atomic{"_"}Type ={">"} Atomic{"_"}Boolean);{"\n"}
<MarginText>19/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
Lock : aliased Atomic{"_"}Boolean := False;{"\n"}
<MarginText>20/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
...{"\n"}
<MarginText>21/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
begin -- Some critical section, trying to get the lock:{"\n"}
<MarginText>22/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
   -- Obtain the lock{"\n"}   while Exchange.Atomic{"_"}Exchange (Item ={">"} Lock, Value ={">"} True) loop{"\n"}      null;{"\n"}   end loop;{"\n"}
<MarginText>23/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
   ... -- Do stuff{"\n"}
<MarginText>24/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
   Lock := False; -- Release the lock{"\n"}end;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>24.a/5_C.6.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0234-1"]} />
This package is new. <br />

## C.6.4  The Package System.Atomic_Operations.Integer_Arithmetic

# C.7. Task Information
