private{"\n"}   ... -- not specified by the language{"\n"}end System.Multiprocessors.Dispatching{"_"}Domains;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>16/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0082-1"]} />
<p>A <i>dispatching domain</i> represents a set of processors on which a task may execute. Each processor is contained within exactly one dispatching domain. An object of type Dispatching{"_"}Domain identifies a dispatching domain. System{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain identifies a domain that contains the processor or processors on which the environment task executes. At program start-up all processors are contained within this domain.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>For a task type (including the anonymous type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single_task_declaration</a></code>), the following language-defined representation aspect may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Dispatching{"_"}Domain</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The value of aspect Dispatching{"_"}Domain is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, which shall be of type Dispatching{"_"}Domains.Dispatching{"_"}Domain. This aspect is the domain to which the task (or all objects of the task type) are assigned.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>18.a/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Dispatching{"_"}Domain: </b>Domain (group of processors) on which a given task should run.<br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>19/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>The Dispatching{"_"}Domain aspect shall not be specified for a task interface.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>20/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0033-1"]} />
<p>The expression specified for the Dispatching{"_"}Domain aspect of a task type is evaluated each time an object of the task type is created (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1">9.1</a>). If the identified dispatching domain is empty, then Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error is raised; otherwise the newly created task is assigned to the domain identified by the value of the expression.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>If a task is not explicitly assigned to any domain, it is assigned to that of the activating task. A task always executes on some CPU in its domain.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0082-1"]} />
<p>If both the dispatching domain and CPU are specified for a task, and the CPU value is not contained within the set of processors for the domain (and is not Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU), the activation of the task is defined to have failed, and it becomes a completed task (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.2">9.2</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>23/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0033-1"]} />
<p>The function Create with First and Last parameters creates and returns a dispatching domain containing all the processors in the range First .. Last. The function Create with a Set parameter creates and returns a dispatching domain containing the processors for which Set(I) is True. These processors are removed from System{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain. A call of Create will raise Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error if any designated processor is not currently in System{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain, or if the system cannot support a distinct domain over the processors identified, or if a processor has a task assigned to it, or if the allocation would leave System{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain empty. A call of Create will raise Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error if the calling task is not the environment task, or if Create is called after the call to the main subprogram.<br /></p>

<MarginText>24/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0033-1"]} />
<p>The function Get{"_"}First{"_"}CPU returns the first CPU in Domain, or CPU'First if Domain is empty; Get{"_"}Last{"_"}CPU returns the last CPU in Domain, or CPU{"_"}Range'First if Domain is empty. The function Get{"_"}CPU{"_"}Set(D) returns an array whose low bound is Get{"_"}First{"_"}CPU(D), whose high bound is Get{"_"}Last{"_"}CPU(D), with True values in the Set corresponding to the CPUs that are in the given Domain.<br /></p>

<MarginText>25/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0082-1"]} />
<p>The function Get{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain returns the dispatching domain on which the task is assigned.<br /></p>

<MarginText>26/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI05-0278-1", "AI12-0033-1"]} />
<p>A call of the procedure Assign{"_"}Task assigns task T to the CPU within the dispatching domain Domain. Task T can now execute only on CPU, unless CPU designates Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU in which case it can execute on any processor within Domain. The exception Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error is propagated if Domain is empty, T is already assigned to a dispatching domain other than System{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain, or if CPU is not one of the processors of Domain (and is not Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU). A call of Assign{"_"}Task is a task dispatching point for task T unless T is inside of a protected action, in which case the effect on task T is delayed until its next task dispatching point. If T is the Current{"_"}Task the effect is immediate if T is not inside a protected action, otherwise the effect is as soon as practical. Assigning a task already assigned to System{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain to that domain has no effect.<br /></p>

<MarginText>27/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI05-0278-1", "AI12-0082-1"]} />
<p>A call of procedure Set{"_"}CPU assigns task T to the CPU. Task T can now execute only on CPU, unless CPU designates Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU, in which case it can execute on any processor within its dispatching domain. The exception Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error is propagated if CPU is not one of the processors of the dispatching domain on which T is assigned (and is not Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU). A call of Set{"_"}CPU is a task dispatching point for task T unless T is inside of a protected action, in which case the effect on task T is delayed until its next task dispatching point. If T is the Current{"_"}Task the effect is immediate if T is not inside a protected action, otherwise the effect is as soon as practical.<br /></p>

<MarginText>28/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>The function Get{"_"}CPU returns the processor assigned to task T, or Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU if the task is not assigned to a processor.<br /></p>

<MarginText>29/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI12-0082-1"]} />
<p>A call of Delay{"_"}Until{"_"}And{"_"}Set{"_"}CPU delays the calling task for the designated time and then assigns the task to the specified processor when the delay expires. The exception Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error is propagated if P is not one of the processors of the calling task's dispatching domain (and is not Not{"_"}A{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU).<br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>30/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>The implementation shall perform the operations Assign{"_"}Task, Set{"_"}CPU, Get{"_"}CPU and Delay{"_"}Until{"_"}And{"_"}Set{"_"}CPU atomically with respect to any of these operations on the same dispatching{"_"}domain, processor or task.<br /></p>

<MarginText>30.1/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0048-1"]} />
<p>Any task that belongs to the system dispatching domain can execute on any CPU within that domain, unless the assignment of the task has been specified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>30.a/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This ensures that priorities and deadlines are respected within the system dispatching domain. There is no such guarantee between different domains.<br />

<MarginText>30.b/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
We only need to talk about the system dispatching domain here, because Assign{"_"}Task and Set{"_"}CPU already have such wording for tasks that are assigned explicitly to a dispatching domain and specify Not{"_"}a{"_"}Specific{"_"}CPU. <br />

<MarginText>30.c/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If no dispatching domains are created, all tasks can execute on all processors. (As always, implementation-defined dispatching policies may have other rules, so a partition that does not specify any language-defined dispatching policy may do anything at all and in particular does not need to follow this rule. <br />

<MarginText>30.d/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>A task can be assigned to a specific CPU by specifying the aspect CPU for a task, or by calling a dynamic operation like Set{"_"}CPU or Assign{"_"}Task. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>31/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>Each dispatching domain should have separate and disjoint ready queues.<br /></p>

<MarginText>31.a/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Each dispatching domain should have separate and disjoint ready queues.<br />

<MarginText>31.b/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0048-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>&ldquo;Ready queue&rdquo; here doesn't mean the conceptual "ready queue" as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.1">D.2.1</a> (one per processor); this rule is talking about the ready queues used by the implementation. <br />

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>32/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>The implementation shall document the processor(s) on which the clock interrupt is handled and hence where delay queue and ready queue manipulations occur. For any Interrupt{"_"}Id whose handler can execute on more than one processor the implementation shall also document this set of processors.<br /></p>

<MarginText>32.a/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The processor(s) on which the clock interrupt is handled; the processors on which each Interrupt{"_"}Id can be handled.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>33/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may limit the number of dispatching domains that can be created and raise Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error if an attempt is made to exceed this number.<br /></p>

<MarginText>34/5_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<p>The implementation may defer the effect of a Set{"_"}CPU or an Assign{"_"}Task operation until the specified task leaves an ongoing parallel construct.<br /></p>

<MarginText>34.a/5_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>These operations can change the set of CPUs that a parallel operation is allowed to use. This could require the ability to move or suspend one or more threads to execute them on a different CPU. However, parallel constructs are primarily intended to improve performance of code, and the overhead needed to support such a rarely used operation could be substantial. Therefore, rather than requiring support we allow the implementation to wait to implement these operations until the parallel construct (and thus the extra threads) have completed. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>34.b/3_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0167-1", "AI05-0278-1"]} />
The package System.Multiprocessors.Dispatching{"_"}Domains and the aspect Dispatching{"_"}Domains are new. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>34.c/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0033-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> We now explicitly allow empty dispatching domains, as it would be difficult to avoid declaring them when a system is configured at runtime. Therefore, assigning a task to an empty domain now raises Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error; creating such a domain should not raise Dispatching{"_"}Domain{"_"}Error. If an implementation does something different in these cases, and a program depends on that difference, the program could malfunction. This seems very unlikely (if no exception is ever raised, the task assigned to the empty domain could never run; if the exception is raised earlier, the program can't do anything useful). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>34.d/5_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1", "AI05-0033-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> The subtypes of the parameter or result of several routines were changed to support empty domains. These changes will cause rules requiring subtype conformance to fail on these routines (such as 'Access). We believe such uses are unlikely. In addition, type CPU{"_"}Set and function Get{"_"}CPU{"_"}Set, along with an overloaded Create are newly added to this package. As such, a use clause conflict is possible; see the introduction of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a> for more on this topic. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>34.e/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0048-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added wording to clarify that all tasks can execute on all CPUs of the system dispatching domain by default.<br />

<MarginText>34.f/4_D.16.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0082-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Added a definition to clarify that a "dispatching domain" is a concept which is identified by an object of type Dispatching{"_"}Domain; more than one object might identify the same dispatching domain (for instance, the result of function Get{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Domain is a different object but identifies the same dispatching domain). <br />

# D.2. Priority Scheduling

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause describes the rules that determine which task is selected for execution when more than one task is ready (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>).] <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>1.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This introduction is simplified in order to reflect the rearrangement and expansion of this subclause. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.2.1"></a>

## D.2.1  The Task Dispatching Model

<MarginText>1/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p>[The task dispatching model specifies task scheduling, based on conceptual priority-ordered ready queues.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1.1/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.2/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1", "AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Dispatching{"\n"}  with Preelaborate, Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}
<MarginText>1.3/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1", "AI12-0241-1"]} />
  procedure Yield{"\n"}   with Nonblocking ={">"} False;{"\n"}
<MarginText>1.4/3_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1"]} />
  Dispatching{"_"}Policy{"_"}Error : exception;{"\n"}end Ada.Dispatching;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>1.5/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<p>Dispatching serves as the parent of other language-defined library units concerned with task dispatching.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.6/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0279-1"]} />
<p>For a noninstance subprogram (including a generic formal subprogram), a generic subprogram, or an entry, the following language-defined aspect may be specified with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>):<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.7/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Yield</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Yield is Boolean.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>1.a/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Yield: </b>Ensures that a callable entity includes a task dispatching point.<br />

<MarginText>1.8/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>If directly specified, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a static expression. If not specified (including by inheritance), the aspect is False.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>1.9/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0279-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
<dd>If a Yield aspect is specified True for a primitive subprogram <i>S</i> of a type <i>T</i>, then the aspect is inherited by the corresponding primitive subprogram of each descendant of <i>T</i>. <br /></dd>
</dl>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>1.10/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0279-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
<p>If the Yield aspect is specified for a dispatching subprogram that inherits the aspect, the specified value shall be confirming.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.11/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0279-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
<p>If the Nonblocking aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>) of the associated callable entity is statically True, the Yield aspect shall not be specified as True. For a callable entity that is declared within a generic body, this rule is checked assuming that any nonstatic Nonblocking attributes in the expression of the Nonblocking aspect of the entity are statically True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.b/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0294-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The second sentence here is an assume-the-worst rule. The only Nonblocking attributes that are nonstatic are those that depend, directly or indirectly, on the nonblocking aspect of a generic formal parameter. We have to assume these might in fact have the value True if given an appropriate actual entity. <br />

<MarginText>1.12/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0294-1"]} />
<p>In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>2/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI12-0454-1"]} />
<p>A task can become a <i>running task</i> only if it is ready (see Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a>) and the execution resources required by that task are available. Processors are allocated to tasks based on each task's active priority.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3_D.2.1</MarginText>
<p>It is implementation defined whether, on a multiprocessor, a task that is waiting for access to a protected object keeps its processor busy. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a_D.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Whether, on a multiprocessor, a task that is waiting for access to a protected object keeps its processor busy.<br />

<MarginText>4/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI12-0119-1"]} />
<p><i>Task dispatching</i> is the process by which a logical thread of control associated with a ready task is selected for execution on a processor. This selection is done during the execution of such a logical thread of control, at certain points called <i>task dispatching points</i>. Such a logical thread of control reaches a task dispatching point whenever it becomes blocked, and when its associated task terminates. [Other task dispatching points are defined throughout this Annex for specific policies.] Below we talk in terms of tasks, but in the context of a parallel construct, a single task can be represented by multiple logical threads of control, each of which can appear separately on a ready queue. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a_D.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>On multiprocessor systems, more than one task can be chosen, at the same time, for execution on more than one processor, as explained below. <br />

<MarginText>5/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p><i>Task dispatching policies</i> are specified in terms of conceptual <i>ready queues</i> and task states. A ready queue is an ordered list of ready tasks. The first position in a queue is called the <i>head of the queue</i>, and the last position is called the <i>tail of the queue</i>. A task is <i>ready</i> if it is in a ready queue, or if it is running. Each processor has one ready queue for each priority value. At any instant, each ready queue of a processor contains exactly the set of tasks of that priority that are ready for execution on that processor, but are not running on any processor; that is, those tasks that are ready, are not running on any processor, and can be executed using that processor and other available resources. A task can be on the ready queues of more than one processor. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a_D.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The core language defines a ready task as one that is not blocked. Here we refine this definition and talk about ready queues. <br />

<MarginText>6/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p>Each processor also has one <i>running task</i>, which is the task currently being executed by that processor. Whenever a task running on a processor reaches a task dispatching point it goes back to one or more ready queues; a task (possibly the same task) is then selected to run on that processor. The task selected is the one at the head of the highest priority nonempty ready queue; this task is then removed from all ready queues to which it belongs. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a_D.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There is always at least one task to run, if we count the idle task. <br />

<MarginText>7/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI05-0166-1", "AI12-0241-1"]} />
<p>A call of Yield and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code> are task dispatching points for all language-defined policies.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>8/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI12-0279-1"]} />
<p>If the Yield aspect has the value True, then a call to procedure Yield is included within the body of the associated callable entity, and invoked immediately prior to returning from the body if and only if no other task dispatching points were encountered during the execution of the body. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>9/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p>An implementation is allowed to define additional resources as execution resources, and to define the corresponding allocation policies for them. Such resources may have an implementation-defined effect on task dispatching. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The effect of implementation-defined execution resources on task dispatching.<br />

<MarginText>10_D.2.1</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may place implementation-defined restrictions on tasks whose active priority is in the Interrupt{"_"}Priority range. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/3_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For example, on some operating systems, it might be necessary to disallow them altogether. This permission applies to tasks whose priority is set to interrupt level for any reason: via an aspect, via a call to Dynamic{"_"}Priorities.Set{"_"}Priority, or via priority inheritance. <br />

<MarginText>10.1/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI12-0299-1"]} />
<p>Unless otherwise specified for a task dispatching policy, an implementation may add additional points at which task dispatching may occur, in an implementation-defined manner.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.b/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This permission is intended to allow the implementation of Ada tasks in terms of target system threads, which may have additional conditions that cause task dispatching. For instance, for Linux threads, page faults are task dispatching points. <br />

<MarginText>10.c/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities task dispatching policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.4">D.2.4</a>) does not allow additional task dispatching points. <br />

<MarginText>11_D.2.1</MarginText>
NOTE 1   Clause <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/">9</a> specifies under which circumstances a task becomes ready. The ready state is affected by the rules for task activation and termination, delay statements, and entry calls. When a task is not ready, it is said to be blocked.<br />

<MarginText>12/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 2   An example of a possible implementation-defined execution resource is a page of physical memory, which must be loaded with a particular page of virtual memory before a task can continue execution.<br />

<MarginText>13_D.2.1</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The ready queues are purely conceptual; there is no requirement that such lists physically exist in an implementation.<br />

<MarginText>14_D.2.1</MarginText>
NOTE 4   While a task is running, it is not on any ready queue. Any time the task that is running on a processor is added to a ready queue, a new running task is selected for that processor.<br />

<MarginText>15_D.2.1</MarginText>
NOTE 5   In a multiprocessor system, a task can be on the ready queues of more than one processor. At the extreme, if several processors share the same set of ready tasks, the contents of their ready queues is identical, and so they can be viewed as sharing one ready queue, and can be implemented that way. [Thus, the dispatching model covers multiprocessors where dispatching is implemented using a single ready queue, as well as those with separate dispatching domains.]<br />

<MarginText>16_D.2.1</MarginText>
NOTE 6   The priority of a task is determined by rules specified in this subclause, and under <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">Task Priorities</a>&rdquo;, <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">Priority Ceiling Locking</a>&rdquo;, and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5">D.5</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5">Dynamic Priorities</a>&rdquo;.<br />

<MarginText>17/2_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
NOTE 7   The setting of a task's base priority as a result of a call to Set{"_"}Priority does not always take effect immediately when Set{"_"}Priority is called. The effect of setting the task's base priority is deferred while the affected task performs a protected action.<br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>17.a/3_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI05-0005-1"]} />
This description is simplified to describe only the parts of the dispatching model common to all policies. In particular, rules about preemption are moved elsewhere. This makes it easier to add other policies (which might not involve preemption). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>17.b/3_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1"]} />
Procedure Yield is added to Dispatching. If Dispatching is referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, and an entity <i>E</i> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.1#S0022">defining_identifier</a></code> of Yield is defined in a package that is also referenced in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-8/AA-8.4#S0235">use_clause</a></code>, the entity <i>E</i> may no longer be use-visible, resulting in errors. This should be rare and is easily fixed if it does occur.<br />

<MarginText>17.c/4_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
Package Dispatching was a Pure package, but now is Preelaborated with the addition of Yield. This is incompatible as Dispatching can no longer be depended upon from a Pure package. This should happen rarely in practice as the only contents was the exception Dispatching{"_"}Policy{"_"}Error and none of the child packages that could raise that exception are pure. <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.d/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Substantially reduced the Implementation Permission that used to allow &ldquo;altering&rdquo; task dispatching points to only allow adding task dispatching points. If an implementation was using this permission to remove task dispatching points, and a program depended on that behavior to work, it could fail when used with Ada 2022. We are not aware of any such implementations, and such behavior was never portable to other implementations, so we do not expect this to matter in practice. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.e/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0279-1", "AI12-0294-1"]} />
Aspect Yield is new. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>17.f/5_D.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0119-1"]} />
Redid the description of task dispatching to include the separate threads of control that can be started by a parallel construct. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.2.2"></a>

## D.2.2  Task Dispatching Pragmas

<MarginText>0.1/3_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause allows a single task dispatching policy to be defined for all priorities, or the range of priorities to be split into subranges that are assigned individual dispatching policies.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1_D.2.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy(<i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.1/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.2/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching (<br />     <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, <i>first{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, <i>last{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>);<br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>2.3/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The expected type for <i>first{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and <i>last{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is Integer. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy shall be the name of a task dispatching policy. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>3.1/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> used in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching shall be the name of a task dispatching policy.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.2/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>Both <i>first{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and <i>last{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall be static expressions in the range of System.Any{"_"}Priority; <i>last{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall have a value greater than or equal to <i>first{"_"}priority{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>.<br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3.3/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy specifies the single task dispatching policy.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.4/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching specifies the task dispatching policy for the specified range of priorities. Tasks with base priorities within the range of priorities specified in a Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragma have their active priorities determined according to the specified dispatching policy. Tasks with active priorities within the range of priorities specified in a Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragma are dispatched according to the specified dispatching policy. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.b/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Each ready queue is managed by exactly one policy. Anything else would be chaos. The ready queue is determined by the active priority. However, how the active priority is calculated is determined by the policy; in order to break out of this circle, we have to say that the active priority is calculated by the method determined by the policy of the base priority. <br />

<MarginText>3.5/3_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>If a partition contains one or more Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragmas, the dispatching policy for priorities not covered by any Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragmas is FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities.<br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>4/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>A Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy pragma is a configuration pragma. A Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragma is a configuration pragma. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.1/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The priority ranges specified in more than one Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragma within the same partition shall not be overlapping.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.2/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>If a partition contains one or more Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragmas it shall not contain a Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy pragma.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00333-01"]} />
<p><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>[A <i>task dispatching policy</i> specifies the details of task dispatching that are not covered by the basic task dispatching model. These rules govern when tasks are inserted into and deleted from the ready queues.] A single task dispatching policy is specified by a Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy pragma. Pragma Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching assigns distinct dispatching policies to subranges of System.Any{"_"}Priority.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.1/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>If neither <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies to any of the program units comprising a partition, the task dispatching policy for that partition is unspecified.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.2/3_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI05-0262-1"]} />
<p>If a partition contains one or more Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragmas, a task dispatching point occurs for the currently running task of a processor whenever there is a nonempty ready queue for that processor with a higher priority than the priority of the running task.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/3_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>If we have priority specific dispatching then we want preemption across the entire range of priorities. That prevents higher priority tasks from being blocked by lower priority tasks that have a different policy. On the other hand, if we have a single policy for the entire partition, we want the characteristics of that policy to apply for preemption; specifically, we might not require any preemption. Note that policy Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is not allowed in a priority specific dispatching pragma. <br />

<MarginText>6.3/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>A task that has its base priority changed may move from one dispatching policy to another. It is immediately subject to the new dispatching policy.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.b/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Once subject to the new dispatching policy, it may be immediately preempted or dispatched, according the rules of the new policy. <br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 7 through 13 were moved to D.2.3.</i> <br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>13.1/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00333-01", "AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>An implementation shall allow, for a single partition, both the locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) to be specified as Ceiling{"_"}Locking and also one or more Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragmas to be given. <br /></p>

#### Documentation Requirements

<p><i>Paragraphs 14 through 16 were moved to D.2.3.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>17/5_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>Implementations are allowed to define other task dispatching policies, but are not required to support specifying more than one task dispatching policy per partition.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/5_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>An implementation is not required to support <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching if it is infeasible to support it in the target environment.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18.a/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation defined task dispatching policies.<br />

<i>Paragraphs 19 through 21 were deleted.</i> <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>21.a/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00333-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> It is no longer required to specify Ceiling{"_"}Locking with the language-defined task dispatching policies; we only require that implementations <i>allow</i> them to be used together.<br />

<MarginText>21.b/3_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI05-0005-1"]} />
<b>Pragma</b> Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching is new; it allows the specification of different policies for different priorities. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>21.c/2_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01"]} />
Clarified that an implementation need support only one task dispatching policy (of any kind, language-defined or otherwise) per partition.<br />

<MarginText>21.d/3_D.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI05-0005-1"]} />
This description is simplified to describe only the rules for the Task{"_"}Dispatching{"_"}Policy pragma that are common to all policies. In particular, rules about preemption are moved elsewhere. This makes it easier to add other policies (which might not involve preemption). <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.2.3"></a>

## D.2.3  Preemptive Dispatching

<MarginText>1/3_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause defines a preemptive task dispatching policy.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is a task dispatching policy.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>3/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p>When FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is in effect, modifications to the ready queues occur only as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>When a blocked task becomes ready, it is added at the tail of the ready queue for its active priority.<br /></li>
<MarginText>5/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<li>When the active priority of a ready task that is not running changes, or the setting of its base priority takes effect, the task is removed from the ready queue for its old active priority and is added at the tail of the ready queue for its new active priority, except in the case where the active priority is lowered due to the loss of inherited priority, in which case the task is added at the head of the ready queue for its new active priority.<br /></li>
<MarginText>6/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<li>When the setting of the base priority of a running task takes effect, the task is added to the tail of the ready queue for its active priority.<br /></li>
<MarginText>7/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<li>When a task executes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code> that does not result in blocking, it is added to the tail of the ready queue for its active priority. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the delay does result in blocking, the task moves to the &ldquo;delay queue&rdquo;, not to the ready queue. <br />

<MarginText>8/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p>Each of the events specified above is a task dispatching point (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.1">D.2.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p>A task dispatching point occurs for the currently running task of a processor whenever there is a nonempty ready queue for that processor with a higher priority than the priority of the running task. The currently running task is said to be <i>preempted</i> and it is added at the head of the ready queue for its active priority.<br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>10/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00333-01"]} />
<p>An implementation shall allow, for a single partition, both the task dispatching policy to be specified as FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities and also the locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) to be specified as Ceiling{"_"}Locking. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is the preferred combination of the FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities policy with a locking policy, and we want that combination to be portable. <br />

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>11/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
<p><i>Priority inversion</i> is the duration for which a task remains at the head of the highest priority nonempty ready queue while the processor executes a lower priority task. The implementation shall document:<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The maximum priority inversion a user task can experience due to activity of the implementation (on behalf of lower priority tasks), and <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The maximum priority inversion a user task can experience from the implementation.<br />

<MarginText>13/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>whether execution of a task can be preempted by the implementation processing of delay expirations for lower priority tasks, and if so, for how long. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The amount of time that a task can be preempted for processing on behalf of lower-priority tasks.<br />

<MarginText>14/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
NOTE 1   If the active priority of a running task is lowered due to loss of inherited priority (as it is on completion of a protected operation) and there is a ready task of the same active priority that is not running, the running task continues to run (provided that there is no higher priority task).<br />

<MarginText>15/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
NOTE 2   Setting the base priority of a ready task causes the task to move to the tail of the queue for its active priority, regardless of whether the active priority of the task actually changes.<br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>15.a/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
This subclause is new; it mainly consists of text that was found in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.1">D.2.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.2">D.2.2</a> in Ada 95. This was separated out so the definition of additional policies was easier.<br />

<MarginText>15.b/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00333-01"]} />
We require that implementations allow this policy and Ceiling{"_"}Locking together.<br />

<MarginText>15.c/2_D.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
We explicitly defined FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities to be a task dispatching policy. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.2.4"></a>

## D.2.4  Non-Preemptive Dispatching

<MarginText>1/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00298-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause defines a non-preemptive task dispatching policy.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00298-01", "AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is a task dispatching policy.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.1/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1"]} />
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.2/5_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Dispatching.Non{"_"}Preemptive{"\n"}  with Preelaborate, Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}  procedure Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Higher;{"\n"}  procedure Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Same{"_"}Or{"_"}Higher renames Yield;{"\n"}end Ada.Dispatching.Non{"_"}Preemptive;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.3/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>A call of Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Higher is a task dispatching point for this policy. If the task at the head of the highest priority ready queue has a higher active priority than the calling task, then the calling task is preempted.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>For language-defined policies other than Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities, a higher priority task should never be on a ready queue while a lower priority task is executed. Thus, for such policies, Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Higher does nothing.<br />

<MarginText>2.b/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Higher is <i>not</i> a potentially blocking operation; it can be used during a protected operation. That is allowed, as under the predefined Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy any task with a higher priority than the protected operation cannot call the operation (that would violate the locking policy). An implementation-defined locking policy may need to define the semantics of Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Higher differently. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities shall not be specified as the <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.2">D.2.2</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The non-preemptive nature of this policy could cause the policies of higher priority tasks to malfunction, missing deadlines and having unlimited priority inversion. That would render the use of such policies impotent and misleading. As such, this policy only makes sense for a complete system. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>4/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00298-01"]} />
<p>When Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is in effect, modifications to the ready queues occur only as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00298-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>When a blocked task becomes ready, it is added at the tail of the ready queue for its active priority.<br /></li>
<MarginText>6/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<li>When the active priority of a ready task that is not running changes, or the setting of its base priority takes effect, the task is removed from the ready queue for its old active priority and is added at the tail of the ready queue for its new active priority.<br /></li>
<MarginText>7/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<li>When the setting of the base priority of a running task takes effect, the task is added to the tail of the ready queue for its active priority.<br /></li>
<MarginText>8/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<li>When a task executes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code> that does not result in blocking, it is added to the tail of the ready queue for its active priority. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If the delay does result in blocking, the task moves to the &ldquo;delay queue&rdquo;, not to the ready queue. <br />

<MarginText>9/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1"]} />
<p>For this policy, blocking or termination of a task, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code>, a call to Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Higher, and a call to Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Same{"_"}Or{"_"}Higher or Yield are the only task dispatching points (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.1">D.2.1</a>). <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0266">delay_statement</a></code> is always a task dispatching point even if it is not blocking. Similarly, a call to Yield{"_"}To{"_"}Higher is never blocking, but it is a task dispatching point In each of these cases, they can cause the current task to stop running (it is still ready). Otherwise, the running task continues to run until it is blocked.<br />

<MarginText>9.b/5_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0299-1"]} />
This rule supersedes the Implementation Permission of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.1">D.2.1</a>; an implementation that adds additional task dispatching points to this policy is incorrect. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>10/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00333-01"]} />
<p>An implementation shall allow, for a single partition, both the task dispatching policy to be specified as Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities and also the locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) to be specified as Ceiling{"_"}Locking. <br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is the preferred combination of the Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities policy with a locking policy, and we want that combination to be portable. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>11/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00298-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>Since implementations are allowed to round all ceiling priorities in subrange System.Priority to System.Priority'Last (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>), an implementation may allow a task of a partition using the Non{"_"}Premptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities policy to execute within a protected object without raising its active priority provided the associated protected unit does not contain any subprograms with aspects Interrupt{"_"}Handler or Attach{"_"}Handler specified, nor does the unit have aspect Interrupt{"_"}Priority specified. When the locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) is Ceiling{"_"}Locking, an implementation taking advantage of this permission shall ensure that a call to Yield{"_"}to{"_"}Higher that occurs within a protected action uses the ceiling priority of the protected object (rather than the active priority of the task) when determining whether to preempt the task. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a.1/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0269-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We explicitly require that the ceiling priority be used in calls to Yield{"_"}to{"_"}Higher in order to prevent a risk of priority inversion and consequent loss of mutual exclusion when Yield{"_"}to{"_"}Higher is used in a protected object. This requirement might lessen the value of the permission (as the current Ceiling{"_"}Priority will have to be maintained in the TCB), but loss of mutual exclusion cannot be tolerated. The primary benefit of the permission (eliminating the need for preemption at the end of a protected action) is still available. As noted above, an implementation-defined locking policy will need to specify the semantics of Yield{"_"}to{"_"}Higher, including this case. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>11.a/2_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00298-01", "AI95-00355-01"]} />
Policy Non{"_"}Preemptive{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is new. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>11.b/3_D.2.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0166-1"]} />
Package Dispatching.Non{"_"}Preemptive is new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.2.5"></a>

## D.2.5  Round Robin Dispatching

<MarginText>1/3_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause defines the task dispatching policy Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities and the package Round{"_"}Robin.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The <i>policy</i>{"_"}<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is a task dispatching policy.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/5_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with System;{"\n"}with Ada.Real{"_"}Time;{"\n"}package Ada.Dispatching.Round{"_"}Robin{"\n"}  with Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}  Default{"_"}Quantum : constant Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span :={"\n"}             implementation-defined;{"\n"}  procedure Set{"_"}Quantum (Pri     : in System.Priority;{"\n"}                         Quantum : in Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span);{"\n"}  procedure Set{"_"}Quantum (Low, High : in System.Priority;{"\n"}                         Quantum   : in Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span);{"\n"}  function Actual{"_"}Quantum (Pri : System.Priority){"\n"}             return Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span;{"\n"}  function Is{"_"}Round{"_"}Robin (Pri : System.Priority) return Boolean;{"\n"}end Ada.Dispatching.Round{"_"}Robin;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4.a.1/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The value of Default{"_"}Quantum in Dispatching.Round{"_"}Robin.<br />

<MarginText>5/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>When task dispatching policy Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is the single policy in effect for a partition, each task with priority in the range of System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority is dispatched according to policy FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The procedures Set{"_"}Quantum set the required Quantum value for a single priority level Pri or a range of priority levels Low .. High. If no quantum is set for a Round Robin priority level, Default{"_"}Quantum is used.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>The function Actual{"_"}Quantum returns the actual quantum used by the implementation for the priority level Pri.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/3_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>The function Is{"_"}Round{"_"}Robin returns True if priority Pri is covered by task dispatching policy Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities; otherwise, it returns False.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>A call of Actual{"_"}Quantum or Set{"_"}Quantum raises exception Dispatching.Dispatching{"_"}Policy{"_"}Error if a predefined policy other than Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities applies to the specified priority or any of the priorities in the specified range.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>For Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities, the dispatching rules for FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities apply with the following additional rules:<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>When a task is added or moved to the tail of the ready queue for its base priority, it has an execution time budget equal to the quantum for that priority level. This will also occur when a blocked task becomes executable again.<br /></li>
<MarginText>12/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<li>When a task is preempted (by a higher priority task) and is added to the head of the ready queue for its priority level, it retains its remaining budget.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<li>While a task is executing, its budget is decreased by the amount of execution time it uses. The accuracy of this accounting is the same as that for execution time clocks (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.14">D.14</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that this happens even when the task is executing at a higher, inherited priority, and even if that higher priority is dispatched by a different policy than round robin. <br />

<MarginText>14/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>When a task has exhausted its budget and is without an inherited priority (and is not executing within a protected operation), it is moved to the tail of the ready queue for its priority level. This is a task dispatching point.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>In this case, it will be given a budget as described in the first bullet.<br />

<MarginText>14.b/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
The rules for FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priority (to which these bullets are added) say that a task that has its base priority set to a Round Robin priority is moved to the tail of the ready queue for its new priority level, and then will be given a budget as described in the first bullet. That happens whether or not the task's original base priority was a Round Robin priority. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>15/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00333-01", "AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>An implementation shall allow, for a single partition, both the task dispatching policy to be specified as Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities and also the locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) to be specified as Ceiling{"_"}Locking. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is the preferred combination of the Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities policy with a locking policy, and we want that combination to be portable. <br />

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>16/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>An implementation shall document the quantum values supported. <br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a.1/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The quantum values supported for round robin dispatching.<br />

<MarginText>17/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
<p>An implementation shall document the accuracy with which it detects the exhaustion of the budget of a task. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a.1/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The accuracy of the detection of the exhaustion of the budget of a task for round robin dispatching.<br />

<MarginText>18/5_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 1   Due to implementation constraints, the quantum value returned by Actual{"_"}Quantum can differ from that set with Set{"_"}Quantum.<br />

<MarginText>19/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
NOTE 2   A task that executes continuously with an inherited priority will not be subject to round robin dispatching.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>19.a/2_D.2.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
Policy Round{"_"}Robin{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities and package Dispatching.Round{"_"}Robin are new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.2.6"></a>

## D.2.6  Earliest Deadline First Dispatching

<MarginText>1/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0439-1"]} />
<p>The deadline of a task is an indication of the urgency of the task; it represents a point on an ideal physical time line. The deadline can affect how resources are allocated to the task.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause presents Dispatching.EDF, a package for representing the deadline of a task and a dispatching policy that defines Earliest Deadline First (EDF) dispatching. The Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect is provided to assign an initial deadline to a task. A configuration pragma Generate{"_"}Deadlines is provided to specify that a task's deadline is recomputed whenever it is made ready.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>2.b/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 3 through 6 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>7/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is a task dispatching policy.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/2_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01"]} />
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1", "AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with Ada.Real{"_"}Time;{"\n"}with Ada.Task{"_"}Identification;{"\n"}package Ada.Dispatching.EDF{"\n"}  with Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}  subtype Deadline is Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time;{"\n"}  subtype Relative{"_"}Deadline is Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span;{"\n"}  Default{"_"}Deadline : constant Deadline :={"\n"}              Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Last;{"\n"}  Default{"_"}Relative{"_"}Deadline : constant Relative{"_"}Deadline :={"\n"}              Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span{"_"}Last;{"\n"}  procedure Set{"_"}Deadline{"\n"}     (D : in Deadline;{"\n"}      T : in Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Task{"_"}Id :={"\n"}      Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task);{"\n"}  function Get{"_"}Deadline{"\n"}     (T : Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Task{"_"}Id :={"\n"}      Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task) return Deadline;{"\n"}  procedure Set{"_"}Relative{"_"}Deadline{"\n"}     (D : in Relative{"_"}Deadline;{"\n"}      T : in Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Task{"_"}Id :={"\n"}      Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task);{"\n"}  function Get{"_"}Relative{"_"}Deadline{"\n"}     (T : Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Task{"_"}Id :={"\n"}      Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task){"\n"}      return Relative{"_"}Deadline;{"\n"}  procedure Delay{"_"}Until{"_"}And{"_"}Set{"_"}Deadline{"\n"}     (Delay{"_"}Until{"_"}Time : in Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time;{"\n"}      Deadline{"_"}Offset : in Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span){"\n"}     with Nonblocking ={">"} False;{"\n"}  function Get{"_"}Last{"_"}Release{"_"}Time{"\n"}     (T : Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Task{"_"}Id :={"\n"}      Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task){"\n"}      return Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time;{"\n"}end Ada.Dispatching.EDF;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>9.1/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>For a subprogram, a task type (including the anonymous type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single_task_declaration</a></code>), or a protected type (including the anonymous type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single_protected_declaration</a></code>), the following language-defined representation aspect may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.2/3_D.2.6</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Relative{"_"}Deadline</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The aspect Relative{"_"}Deadline is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>, which shall be of type Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>9.a/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Relative{"_"}Deadline: </b>Task or protected type parameter used in Earliest Deadline First Dispatching.<br />

<MarginText>9.3/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The form of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Generate{"_"}Deadlines is as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.4/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<p>  <b>pragma</b> Generate{"_"}Deadlines;<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.5/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The Generate{"_"}Deadlines <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> is a configuration pragma.<br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>9.6/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect shall not be specified on a task or protected interface type. If the Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect is specified for a subprogram, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0348">aspect_definition</a></code> shall be a static expression.<br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>10/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>If the EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities policy is specified for a partition, then the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) shall also be specified for the partition.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>If the EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities policy appears in a Priority{"_"}Specific{"_"}Dispatching pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.2">D.2.2</a>) in a partition, then the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) shall also be specified for the partition.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Unlike the other language-defined dispatching policies, the semantic description of EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities assumes Ceiling{"_"}Locking (and a ceiling priority) in order to make the mapping between deadlines and priorities work. Thus, we require both policies to be specified if EDF is used in the partition. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>12/3_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect has no effect if it is specified for a subprogram other than the main subprogram.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12.1/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>If pragma Generate{"_"}Deadlines is in effect, the deadline of a task is recomputed each time it becomes ready. The new deadline is the value of Real{"_"}Time.Clock at the time the task is added to a ready queue plus the value returned by Get{"_"}Relative{"_"}Deadline.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The initial absolute deadline for a task with a specified Relative{"_"}Deadline is the result of adding the value returned by a call of Real{"_"}Time.Clock to the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> specified as the Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect, where this entire computation, including the call of Real{"_"}Time.Clock, is performed between task creation and the start of its activation. If the aspect Relative{"_"}Deadline is not specified, then the initial absolute deadline of a task is the value of Default{"_"}Deadline (Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Last). The environment task is also given an initial deadline by this rule, using the value of the Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect of the main subprogram (if any).<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/2_D.2.6</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>The environment task is a normal task by <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>, so of course this rule applies to it. <br />

<MarginText>13.1/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The effect of specifying a Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect for a protected type or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single_protected_declaration</a></code> is discussed in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>A task has both an <i>active</i> and a <i>base</i> absolute deadline. These are the same except when the task is inheriting a relative deadline during activation or a rendezvous (see below) or within a protected action (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>). The procedure Set{"_"}Deadline changes the (base) absolute deadline of the task to D. The function Get{"_"}Deadline returns the (base) absolute deadline of the task.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14.1/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The procedure Set{"_"}Relative{"_"}Deadline changes the relative deadline of the task to D. The function Get{"_"}Relative{"_"}Deadline returns the relative deadline of the task.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14.2/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The function Get{"_"}Last{"_"}Release{"_"}Time returns the time, as provided by Real{"_"}Time.Clock, when the task was last made ready (that is, was added to a ready queue).<br /></p>

<MarginText>15/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The procedure Delay{"_"}Until{"_"}And{"_"}Set{"_"}Deadline delays the calling task until time Delay{"_"}Until{"_"}Time. When the task becomes ready again it will have deadline Delay{"_"}Until{"_"}Time + Deadline{"_"}Offset.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>On a system with a single processor, the setting of the deadline of a task to the new value occurs immediately at the first point that is outside the execution of a protected action. If the task is currently on a ready queue it is removed and re-entered onto the ready queue determined by the rules defined below.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>When EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities is specified for a priority, the ready queue for that priority is ordered by deadline. The task at the head of a queue is the one with the earliest deadline.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>A task dispatching point occurs for the currently running task <i>T</i> to which policy EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities applies:<br /></p>

<MarginText>19/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>when a change to the base (absolute) deadline of <i>T</i> occurs;<br /></li>
<MarginText>20/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
<MarginText>21/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<li>there is a nonempty ready queue for that processor with a higher priority than the active priority of the running task;<br /></li>
<MarginText>21.1/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<li>there is a ready task with the same priority as <i>T</i> but with an earlier absolute deadline.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>22/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>In these cases, the currently running task is said to be preempted and is returned to the ready queue for its active priority, at a position determined by its active (absolute) deadline.<br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraphs 23 through 27 were deleted.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>28/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>When the setting of the base priority of a ready task takes effect and the new priority is specified as EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities, the task is added to the ready queue, at a position determined by its active deadline.<br /></p>

<MarginText>29/2_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01"]} />
<p>For all the operations defined in Dispatching.EDF, Tasking{"_"}Error is raised if the task identified by T has terminated. Program{"_"}Error is raised if the value of T is Null{"_"}Task{"_"}Id.<br /></p>

<MarginText>29.1/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>If two tasks with priority designated as EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities rendezvous then the deadline for the execution of the accept statement is the earlier of the deadlines of the two tasks.<br /></p>

<MarginText>29.2/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>During activation, a task being activated inherits the deadline that its activator (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.2">9.2</a>) had at the time the activation was initiated.<br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraph 30 was deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>31/2_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01"]} />
<p>If a value of Task{"_"}Id is passed as a parameter to any of the subprograms of this package and the corresponding task object no longer exists, the execution of the program is erroneous.<br /></p>

<MarginText>32/2_D.2.6</MarginText>

<MarginText>32.a.1/2_D.2.6</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>Any conditions that cause the completion of the setting of the deadline of a task to be delayed for a multiprocessor.<br />

<MarginText>33/5_D.2.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00357-01", "AI05-0264-1", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
NOTE   If two distinct priorities are specified to have policy EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities, then tasks from the higher priority always run before tasks of the lower priority, regardless of deadlines.<br />
