# D.3. Priority Ceiling Locking

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  157

# D.3. Priority Ceiling Locking

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause specifies the interactions between priority task scheduling and protected object ceilings. This interaction is based on the concept of the <i>ceiling priority</i> of a protected object.] <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Locking{"_"}Policy is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Locking{"_"}Policy(<i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall either be Ceiling{"_"}Locking or an implementation-defined <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>s allowed in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Locking{"_"}Policy.<br />

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>A Locking{"_"}Policy pragma is a configuration pragma.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00091-01", "AI95-00327-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0073</i>{"}"} [A locking policy specifies the details of protected object locking. All protected objects have a priority. The locking policy specifies the meaning of the priority of a protected object, and the relationships between these priorities and task priorities. In addition, the policy specifies the state of a task when it executes a protected action, and how its active priority is affected by the locking.] The <i>locking policy</i> is specified by a Locking{"_"}Policy pragma. For implementation-defined locking policies, the meaning of the priority of a protected object is implementation defined. If no Locking{"_"}Policy pragma applies to any of the program units comprising a partition, the locking policy for that partition, as well as the meaning of the priority of a protected object, are implementation defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The locking policy if no Locking{"_"}Policy pragma applies to any unit of a partition.<br />

<MarginText>6.1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> specified for the Priority or Interrupt{"_"}Priority aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>) is evaluated as part of the creation of the corresponding protected object and converted to the subtype System.Any{"_"}Priority or System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority, respectively. The value of the expression is the initial priority of the corresponding protected object. If no Priority or Interrupt{"_"}Priority aspect is specified for a protected object, the initial priority is specified by the locking policy. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>There is one predefined locking policy, Ceiling{"_"}Locking; this policy is defined as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>Every protected object has a <i>ceiling priority</i>, which is determined by either a Priority or Interrupt{"_"}Priority aspect as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>, or by assignment to the Priority attribute as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5#Subclause_D.5.2">D.5.2</a>. The ceiling priority of a protected object (or ceiling, for short) is an upper bound on the active priority a task can have when it calls protected operations of that protected object.<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01"]} />
<li>The initial ceiling priority of a protected object is equal to the initial priority for that object.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0051-1"]} />
<li>If an Interrupt{"_"}Handler or Attach{"_"}Handler aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>) is specified for a protected subprogram of a protected type that does not have either the Priority or Interrupt{"_"}Priority aspect specified, the initial priority of protected objects of that type is implementation defined, but in the range of the subtype System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Default ceiling priorities.<br />

<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>If neither aspect Priority nor Interrupt{"_"}Priority is specified for a protected type, and no protected subprogram of the type has aspect Interrupt{"_"}Handler or Attach{"_"}Handler specified, then the initial priority of the corresponding protected object is System.Priority'Last.<br /></li>
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<li>While a task executes a protected action, it inherits the ceiling priority of the corresponding protected object.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<li>When a task calls a protected operation, a check is made that its active priority is not higher than the ceiling of the corresponding protected object; Program{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1", "AI12-0404-1"]} />
<p>If the task dispatching policy specified for the ceiling priority of a protected object is EDF{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities, the following additional rules apply:<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.2/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Every protected object has a <i>relative deadline</i>, which is determined by a Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.6">D.2.6</a>, or by assignment to the Relative{"_"}Deadline attribute as described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5#Subclause_D.5.2">D.5.2</a>. The relative deadline of a protected object represents a lower bound on the relative deadline a task may have when it calls a protected operation of that protected object.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.3/5</MarginText>
<li>If aspect Relative{"_"}Deadline is not specified for a protected type then the initial relative deadline of the corresponding protected object is Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span{"_"}Zero.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.4/5</MarginText>
<li>While a task executes a protected action on a protected object <i>P</i>, it inherits the relative deadline of <i>P</i>. In this case, let <i>DF</i> be 'now' ('now' is obtained via a call on Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Clock at the start of the action) plus the deadline floor of <i>P</i>. If the active deadline of the task is later than <i>DF</i>, its active deadline is reduced to <i>DF</i>[; the active deadline is unchanged otherwise].<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.5/5</MarginText>
<li>When a task calls a protected operation, a check is made that its active deadline minus its last release time is not less than the relative deadline of the corresponding protected object; Program{"_"}Error is raised if this check fails. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>13.6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>Following any change of priority, it is a bounded error for the active priority of any task with a call queued on an entry of a protected object to be higher than the ceiling priority of the protected object. In this case one of the following applies:<br /></p>

<MarginText>13.7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0404-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>at any time prior to executing the entry body, Program{"_"}Error is raised in the calling task;<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0404-1"]} />
<li>when the entry is open, the entry body is executed at the ceiling priority of the protected object;<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0404-1"]} />
<li>when the entry is open, the entry body is executed at the ceiling priority of the protected object and then Program{"_"}Error is raised in the calling task; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.10/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0404-1"]} />
<li>when the entry is open, the entry body is executed at the ceiling priority of the protected object that was in effect when the entry call was queued. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a.1/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that the error is &ldquo;blamed&rdquo; on the task that did the entry call, not the task that changed the priority of the task or protected object. This seems to make sense for the case of changing the priority of a task blocked on a call, since if the Set{"_"}Priority had happened a little bit sooner, before the task queued a call, the entry-calling task would get the error. Similarly, there is no reason not to raise the priority of a task that is executing in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code>, so long as its priority is lowered before it gets to the end and needs to cancel the call. The priority might need to be lowered to allow it to remove the call from the entry queue, in order to avoid violating the ceiling. This seems relatively harmless, since there is an error, and the task is about to start raising an exception anyway. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>The implementation is allowed to round all ceilings in a certain subrange of System.Priority or System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority up to the top of that subrange, uniformly. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For example, an implementation might use Priority'Last for all ceilings in Priority, and Interrupt{"_"}Priority'Last for all ceilings in Interrupt{"_"}Priority. This would be equivalent to having two ceiling priorities for protected objects, &ldquo;nonpreemptible&rdquo; and &ldquo;noninterruptible&rdquo;, and is an allowed behavior.<br />

<MarginText>14.b</MarginText>
Note that the implementation cannot choose a subrange that crosses the boundary between normal and interrupt priorities. <br />

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>Implementations are allowed to define other locking policies, but are not required to support specifying more than one locking policy per partition.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<p>[Since implementations are allowed to place restrictions on code that runs at an interrupt-level active priority (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.1">D.2.1</a>), the implementation may implement a language feature in terms of a protected object with an implementation-defined ceiling, but the ceiling shall be no less than Priority'Last.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The ceiling of any protected object used internally by the implementation.<br />

<MarginText>16.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This permission follows from the fact that the implementation can place restrictions on interrupt handlers and on any other code that runs at an interrupt-level active priority.<br />

<MarginText>16.c</MarginText>
The implementation might protect a storage pool with a protected object whose ceiling is Priority'Last, which would cause <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s to fail when evaluated at interrupt priority. Note that the ceiling of such an object has to be at least Priority'Last, since there is no permission for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code>s to fail when evaluated at a noninterrupt priority. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<p>The implementation should use names that end with &ldquo;{"_"}Locking&rdquo; for implementation-defined locking policies.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Names that end with &ldquo;{"_"}Locking&rdquo; should be used for implementation-defined locking policies.<br />

<MarginText>18</MarginText>
NOTE 1   While a task executes in a protected action, it can be preempted only by tasks whose active priorities are higher than the ceiling priority of the protected object.<br />

<MarginText>19</MarginText>
NOTE 2   If a protected object has a ceiling priority in the range of Interrupt{"_"}Priority, certain interrupts are blocked while protected actions of that object execute. In the extreme, if the ceiling is Interrupt{"_"}Priority'Last, all blockable interrupts are blocked during that time.<br />

<MarginText>20/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0447-1"]} />
NOTE 3   As described in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>, whenever an interrupt is handled by one of the protected procedures of a protected object, a check is made that its ceiling priority is in the Interrupt{"_"}Priority range.<br />

<MarginText>21/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 4   When specifying the ceiling of a protected object, a correct value is one that is at least as high as the highest active priority at which tasks can be executing when they call protected operations of that object. In determining this value the following factors, which can affect active priority, are relevant: the effect of Set{"_"}Priority, nested protected operations, entry calls, task activation, and other implementation-defined factors.<br />

<MarginText>22</MarginText>
NOTE 5   Attaching a protected procedure whose ceiling is below the interrupt hardware priority to an interrupt causes the execution of the program to be erroneous (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>).<br />

<MarginText>23</MarginText>
NOTE 6   On a single processor implementation, the ceiling priority rules guarantee that there is no possibility of deadlock involving only protected subprograms (excluding the case where a protected operation calls another protected operation on the same protected object).<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>23.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01"]} />
All protected objects now have a priority, which is the value of the Priority attribute of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5#Subclause_D.5.2">D.5.2</a>. How this value is interpreted depends on the locking policy; for instance, the ceiling priority is derived from this value when the locking policy is Ceiling{"_"}Locking. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>23.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00091-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0073</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected the wording to reflect that pragma Locking{"_"}Policy cannot be inside of a program unit.<br />

<MarginText>23.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01"]} />
Clarified that an implementation need support only one locking policy (of any kind, language-defined or otherwise) per partition.<br />

<MarginText>23.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01"]} />
The bounded error for the priority of a task being higher than the ceiling of an object it is currently in was moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5">D.5</a>, so that it applies no matter how the situation arises. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>23.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
Revised to use aspects Priority and Interrupt{"_"}Priority as <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Priority and Interrupt{"_"}Priority are now obsolescent. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>23.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
All protected objects now have a relative deadline, which is the value of the Relative{"_"}Deadline attribute of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5#Subclause_D.5.2">D.5.2</a>. How this value is interpreted depends on the locking policy. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>23.g/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0051-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that the Priority aspect can be used to set the initial ceiling priority of a protected object that contains an interrupt handler. <br />

# D.4. Entry Queuing Policies

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  158

# D.4. Entry Queuing Policies

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00068-01", "AI05-0299-1", "AI12-0324-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0074</i>{"}"} [ This subclause specifies a mechanism for a user to choose an entry <i>queuing policy</i>. It also defines three such policies. Other policies are implementation defined.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined queuing policies.<br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Queuing{"_"}Policy is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Queuing{"_"}Policy(<i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0183-1"]} />
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall be either FIFO{"_"}Queuing, Ordered{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Queuing, Priority{"_"}Queuing or an implementation-defined <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>.<br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>A Queuing{"_"}Policy pragma is a configuration pragma.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>[A <i>queuing policy</i> governs the order in which tasks are queued for entry service, and the order in which different entry queues are considered for service.] The queuing policy is specified by a Queuing{"_"}Policy pragma. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The queuing policy includes entry queuing order, the choice among open alternatives of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code>, and the choice among queued entry calls of a protected object when more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> is True. <br />

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01", "AI12-0163-1", "AI12-0183-1"]} />
<p>Three queuing policies, FIFO{"_"}Queuing, Ordered{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Queuing, and Priority{"_"}Queuing, are language defined. If no Queuing{"_"}Policy pragma applies to any of the program units comprising the partition, the queuing policy for that partition is FIFO{"_"}Queuing. The rules for the FIFO{"_"}Queuing policy are specified in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#Subclause_9.7.1">9.7.1</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0163-1"]} />
<p>The Ordered{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Queuing policy is defined as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.2/5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Calls are selected on a given entry queue in order of arrival.<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.3/5</MarginText>
<li>When more than one condition of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> of a protected object becomes True, and more than one of the respective queues is nonempty, the call that arrived first is selected.<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.4/5</MarginText>
<li>If the expiration time of two or more open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code>s is the same and no other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code>s are open, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code> that is first in textual order in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> is executed.<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.5/5</MarginText>
<li>When more than one alternative of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> is open and has queued calls, the alternative whose queue has the call that arrived first is selected. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>A possible implementation for this policy would be to assign a sequence number to each queued entry call, where the sequence number is incremented globally across all queues associated with the protected object or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>7.b/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>It would have been marginally easier to use textual order for the case when multiple queues are selectable. But textual order can lead to unfair queue servicing, since the queues in earlier textual order will end up starving the later ones if calls arrive fast enough. Applying arrival first as the selector provides fairness for this policy. <br />

<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<p>The Priority{"_"}Queuing policy is defined as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The calls to an entry [(including a member of an entry family)] are queued in an order consistent with the priorities of the calls. The <i>priority of an entry call</i> is initialized from the active priority of the calling task at the time the call is made, but can change later. Within the same priority, the order is consistent with the calling (or requeuing, or priority setting) time (that is, a FIFO order).<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00205-01"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0075</i>{"}"} After a call is first queued, changes to the active priority of a task do not affect the priority of the call, unless the base priority of the task is set while the task is blocked on an entry call.<br /></li>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<li>When the base priority of a task is set (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5">D.5</a>), if the task is blocked on an entry call, and the call is queued, the priority of the call is updated to the new active priority of the calling task. This causes the call to be removed from and then reinserted in the queue at the new active priority. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A task is blocked on an entry call if the entry call is simple, conditional, or timed. If the call came from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering_statement</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>, or a requeue thereof, then the task is not blocked on that call; such calls do not have their priority updated. Thus, there can exist many queued calls from a given task (caused by many nested ATC's), but a task can be blocked on only one call at a time.<br />

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
A previous version of Ada 9X required queue reordering in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> case as well. If the call corresponds to a &ldquo;synchronous&rdquo; entry call, then the task is blocked while queued, and it makes good sense to move it up in the queue if its priority is raised.<br />

<MarginText>11.c</MarginText>
However, if the entry call is &ldquo;asynchronous&rdquo;, that is, it is due to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> whose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering_statement</a></code> is an entry call, then the task is not waiting for this entry call, so the placement of the entry call on the queue is irrelevant to the rate at which the task proceeds.<br />

<MarginText>11.d</MarginText>
Furthermore, when an entry is used for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>s, it is almost certain to be a &ldquo;broadcast&rdquo; entry or have only one caller at a time. For example, if the entry is used to notify tasks of a mode switch, then all tasks on the entry queue would be signaled when the mode changes. Similarly, if it is indicating some interrupting event such as a control-C, all tasks sensitive to the interrupt will want to be informed that the event occurred. Hence, the order on such a queue is essentially irrelevant.<br />

<MarginText>11.e</MarginText>
Given the above, it seems an unnecessary semantic and implementation complexity to specify that asynchronous queued calls are moved in response to dynamic priority changes. Furthermore, it is somewhat inconsistent, since the call was originally queued based on the active priority of the task, but dynamic priority changes are changing the base priority of the task, and only indirectly the active priority. We say explicitly that asynchronous queued calls are not affected by normal changes in active priority during the execution of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0283">abortable_part</a></code>. Saying that, if a change in the base priority affects the active priority, then we do want the calls reordered, would be inconsistent. It would also require the implementation to maintain a readily accessible list of all queued calls which would not otherwise be necessary.<br />

<MarginText>11.f</MarginText>
Several rules were removed or simplified when we changed the rules so that calls due to <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>s are never moved due to intervening changes in active priority, be they due to protected actions, some other priority inheritance, or changes in the base priority. <br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>When more than one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> of a protected object becomes True, and more than one of the respective queues is nonempty, the call with the highest priority is selected. If more than one such call has the same priority, the call that is queued on the entry whose declaration is first in textual order in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code> is selected. For members of the same entry family, the one with the lower family index is selected.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<li>If the expiration time of two or more open <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code>s is the same and no other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code>s are open, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0166">sequence_of_statements</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0274">delay_alternative</a></code> that is first in textual order in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> is executed.<br /></li>
<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<li>When more than one alternative of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> is open and has queued calls, an alternative whose queue has the highest-priority call at its head is selected. If two or more open alternatives have equal-priority queued calls, then a call on the entry in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code> that is first in textual order in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0270">selective_accept</a></code> is selected.<br /></li>
</ul>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>Implementations are allowed to define other queuing policies, but are not required to support specifying more than one queuing policy per partition. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00069-01", "AI95-00256-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0116</i>{"}"} This rule is really redundant, as <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.5">10.1.5</a> allows an implementation to limit the use of configuration pragmas to an empty environment. In that case, there would be no way to have multiple policies in a partition. <br />

<MarginText>15.1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00188-02"]} />
<p>Implementations are allowed to defer the reordering of entry queues following a change of base priority of a task blocked on the entry call if it is not practical to reorder the queue immediately. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15.a.2/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Priority change is immediate, but the effect of the change on entry queues can be deferred. That is necessary in order to implement priority changes on top of a non-Ada kernel. <br />

<MarginText>15.a.3/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The reordering should occur as soon as the blocked task can itself perform the reinsertion into the entry queue. <br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
<p>The implementation should use names that end with &ldquo;{"_"}Queuing&rdquo; for implementation-defined queuing policies.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Names that end with &ldquo;{"_"}Queuing&rdquo; should be used for implementation-defined queuing policies.<br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>17/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0164-1"]} />
<p>For a task type (including the anonymous type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single_task_declaration</a></code>), protected type (including the anonymous type of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single_protected_declaration</a></code>), or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>, the following language-defined representation aspect may be specified:<br /></p>

<MarginText>18/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The type of aspect Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length is Integer.<br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>18.a/5</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length: </b>The maximum entry queue length for a task type, protected type, or entry.<br />

<MarginText>19/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/></dt>
<dl>
<dd>If directly specified, the aspect{"_"}definition shall be a static expression no less than -1. If not specified, the aspect has value -1 (representing no additional restriction on queue length). <br /></dd>
</dl>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>20/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0164-1", "AI12-0388-1"]} />
<p>If the Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length aspect for a type has a nonnegative value, the Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length aspect for every individual entry of that type shall not be greater than the value of the aspect for the type. The Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length aspect of a type is nonoverridable (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Aspect Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length can specify less than the partition-wide or type-wide default, but it can't expand the length of a queue. <br />

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>21/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0164-1"]} />
<p>If a restriction Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length applies to a partition, any value specified for the Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length aspect specified for the declaration of a type or entry in the partition shall not be greater than the value of the restriction.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>13.12(6) says that the restriction value has to be static, so this is statically checkable. But the restriction does not have to be in the same compilation as the aspect, so the check cannot, in general, be done until link time. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>22/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0164-1"]} />
<p>If a nonconfirming value is specified for Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length for a type, and an entry call or requeue would cause the queue for any entry of the type to become longer than the specified value, then Program{"_"}Error is raised at the point of the call or requeue.<br /></p>

<MarginText>23/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0164-1"]} />
<p>If a nonconfirming value is specified for Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length for an entry, and an entry call or requeue would cause the queue for an entry to become longer than the specified value, then Program{"_"}Error is raised at the point of the call or requeue. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>23.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00068-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0074</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected the number of queuing policies defined.<br />

<MarginText>23.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00205-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0075</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected so that a call of Set{"_"}Priority in an abortable part does not change the priority of the triggering entry call.<br />

<MarginText>23.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00188-02"]} />
Added a permission to defer queue reordering when the base priority of a task is changed. This is a counterpart to stronger requirements on the implementation of priority change.<br />

<MarginText>23.d/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00256-01"]} />
Clarified that an implementation need support only one queuing policy (of any kind, language-defined or otherwise) per partition.<br />

<MarginText>23.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00355-01"]} />
Fixed wording to make clear that <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> never appears inside of a unit; rather it &ldquo;applies to&rdquo; the unit. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>23.f/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0163-1"]} />
Defined the new queuing policy Ordered{"_"}FIFO{"_"}Queuing.<br />

<MarginText>23.g/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0164-1"]} />
Defined the new aspect Max{"_"}Entry{"_"}Queue{"_"}Length. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.4.1"></a>

## D.4.1  Admission Policies

<MarginText>1/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause specifies a mechanism for a user to choose an admission policy. It also defines one such policy. Other policies are implementation defined.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a.1/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Implementation-defined admission policies.<br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Admission{"_"}Policy is as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Admission{"_"}Policy (<i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1"]} />
<p>The <i>policy{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall be either FIFO{"_"}Spinning or an implementation-defined identifier. <br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>5/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1"]} />
<p>An Admission{"_"}Policy pragma is a configuration pragma.<br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1"]} />
<p>An admission policy governs the order in which competing tasks are evaluated for acquiring the execution resource associated with a protected object. The admission policy is specified by an Admission{"_"}Policy pragma.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1"]} />
<p>One admission policy, FIFO{"_"}Spinning, is language defined. If FIFO{"_"}Spinning is in effect, and starting a protected action on a protected object involves busy-waiting, then calls are selected for acquiring the execution resource of the protected object in the order in which the busy-wait was initiated; otherwise the FIFO{"_"}Spinning policy has no effect. If no Admission{"_"}Policy pragma applies to any of the program units in the partition, the admission policy for that partition is implementation defined.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Busy-waiting might be used for protected objects that can be called from tasks running on other processors than the one the protected object is on. It is unnecessary if all of the tasks that can call a protected object are on the same processor as the object; in particular, it would not be used on a monoprocessor. Aspect CPU (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.16">D.16</a>) can be used to ensure that busy-waiting is not needed. <br />

<MarginText>7.b/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>A possible implementation for this policy would be to apply the abstraction of a ticketing system by assigning two sequence number values to each protected object. One sequence number represents the next available ticket number, and the other sequence number represents the ticket number currently being serviced by the protected object. The next available ticket number is incremented and assigned to a task when the task initiates a busy-wait for acquiring the execution resource associated with the protected object. The ticket number currently being serviced is incremented when a task releases this execution resource. As part of acquiring the execution resource, a task busy-waits until its assigned ticket number equals the protected object's value for the ticket number currently being serviced. While a task busy-waits, it monitors the active priority of the protected object in order to inherit any modifications to the protected object's active priority. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>8/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>Implementations are allowed to define other admission policies, but are not required to support specifying more than one admission policy per partition.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This rule is in fact redundant, as <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.5">10.1.5</a> allows an implementation to limit the use of configuration pragmas to an empty environment. In that case, there would be no way to have multiple policies in a partition. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>8.b/5_D.4.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0276-1"]} />
Admission Policies and the specific policy FIFO{"_"}Spinning are new. <br />

---

# D.5. Dynamic Priorities

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5.mdx

sidebar_position:  159

# D.5. Dynamic Priorities

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause describes how the priority of an entity can be modified or queried at run time.] <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>1.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is turned into two subclauses. This subclause introduction is new. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.5.1"></a>

## D.5.1  Dynamic Priorities for Tasks

<MarginText>1/3_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause describes how the base priority of a task can be modified or queried at run time.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<p>The following language-defined library package exists: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00362-01", "AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
with System;{"\n"}with Ada.Task{"_"}Identification; -- See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.7#Subclause_C.7.1">C.7.1</a>{"\n"}package Ada.Dynamic{"_"}Priorities{"\n"}    with Preelaborate, Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}
<MarginText>4_D.5.1</MarginText>
    procedure Set{"_"}Priority(Priority : in System.Any{"_"}Priority;{"\n"}                           T : in Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Task{"_"}Id :={"\n"}                           Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task);{"\n"}
<MarginText>5_D.5.1</MarginText>
    function Get{"_"}Priority (T : Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Task{"_"}Id :={"\n"}                           Ada.Task{"_"}Identification.Current{"_"}Task){"\n"}                           return System.Any{"_"}Priority;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6_D.5.1</MarginText>
end Ada.Dynamic{"_"}Priorities;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7_D.5.1</MarginText>
<p>The procedure Set{"_"}Priority sets the base priority of the specified task to the specified Priority value. Set{"_"}Priority has no effect if the task is terminated.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8_D.5.1</MarginText>
<p>The function Get{"_"}Priority returns T's current base priority. Tasking{"_"}Error is raised if the task is terminated. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a_D.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>There is no harm in setting the priority of a terminated task. A previous version of Ada 9X made this a run-time error. However, there is little difference between setting the priority of a terminated task, and setting the priority of a task that is about to terminate very soon; neither case should be an error. Furthermore, the runtime check is not necessarily feasible to implement on all systems, since priority changes might be deferred due to inter-processor communication overhead, so the error might not be detected until after Set{"_"}Priority has returned.<br />

<MarginText>8.b_D.5.1</MarginText>
However, we wish to allow implementations to avoid storing &ldquo;extra&rdquo; information about terminated tasks. Therefore, we make Get{"_"}Priority of a terminated task raise an exception; the implementation need not continue to store the priority of a task that has terminated. <br />

<MarginText>9_D.5.1</MarginText>
<p>Program{"_"}Error is raised by Set{"_"}Priority and Get{"_"}Priority if T is equal to Null{"_"}Task{"_"}Id.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00188-02"]} />
<p>On a system with a single processor, the setting of the base priority of a task <i>T</i> to the new value occurs immediately at the first point when <i>T</i> is outside the execution of a protected action.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00188-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>The priority change is immediate if the target task is on a delay queue or a ready queue outside of a protected action. However, consider when Set{"_"}Priority is called by a task T1 to set the priority of T2, if T2 is blocked, waiting on an entry call queued on a protected object, the entry queue needs to be reordered. Since T1 might have a priority that is higher than the ceiling of the protected object, T1 cannot, in general, do the reordering. One way to implement this is to wake T2 up and have T2 do the work. This is similar to the disentangling of queues that needs to happen when a high-priority task aborts a lower-priority task, which might have a call queued on a protected object with a low ceiling. We have an Implementation Permission in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.4">D.4</a> to allow this implementation. We could have required an immediate priority change if on a ready queue during a protected action, but that would have required extra checks for ceiling violations to meet Bounded (Run-Time) Error requirements of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a> and potentially could cause a protected action to be abandoned in the middle (by raising Program{"_"}Error). That seems bad. <br />

<MarginText>10.b_D.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A previous version of Ada 9X made it a run-time error for a high-priority task to set the priority of a lower-priority task that has a queued call on a protected object with a low ceiling. This was changed because: <br />

<MarginText>10.c_D.5.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The check was not feasible to implement on all systems, since priority changes might be deferred due to inter-processor communication overhead. The calling task would continue to execute without finding out whether the operation succeeded or not.<br /></li>
<MarginText>10.d_D.5.1</MarginText>
<li>The runtime check would tend to cause intermittent system failures &mdash; how is the caller supposed to know whether the other task happens to have a queued call at any given time? Consider for example an interrupt that needs to trigger a priority change in some task. The interrupt handler could not safely call Set{"_"}Priority without knowing exactly what the other task is doing, or without severely restricting the ceilings used in the system. If the interrupt handler wants to hand the job off to a third task whose job is to call Set{"_"}Priority, this won't help, because one would normally want the third task to have high priority. <br /></li>
</ul>
<p><i>Paragraph 11 was deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>12_D.5.1</MarginText>
<p>If any subprogram in this package is called with a parameter T that specifies a task object that no longer exists, the execution of the program is erroneous. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a_D.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that this rule overrides the above rule saying that Program{"_"}Error is raised on Get{"_"}Priority of a terminated task. If the task object still exists, and the task is terminated, Get{"_"}Priority raises Program{"_"}Error. However, if the task object no longer exists, calling Get{"_"}Priority causes erroneous execution. <br />

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>12.1/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00188-02"]} />
<p>On a multiprocessor, the implementation shall document any conditions that cause the completion of the setting of the priority of a task to be delayed later than what is specified for a single processor. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a.1/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>Any conditions that cause the completion of the setting of the priority of a task to be delayed for a multiprocessor.<br />

#### Metrics

<MarginText>13_D.5.1</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document the following metric: <br /></p>

<MarginText>14_D.5.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The execution time of a call to Set{"_"}Priority, for the nonpreempting case, in processor clock cycles. This is measured for a call that modifies the priority of a ready task that is not running (which cannot be the calling one), where the new base priority of the affected task is lower than the active priority of the calling task, and the affected task is not on any entry queue and is not executing a protected operation. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The metrics for Set{"_"}Priority.<br />

<MarginText>15/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
NOTE 1   Setting a task's base priority affects task dispatching. First, it can change the task's active priority. Second, under the FIFO{"_"}Within{"_"}Priorities policy it always causes the task to move to the tail of the ready queue corresponding to its active priority, even if the new base priority is unchanged.<br />

<MarginText>16_D.5.1</MarginText>
NOTE 2   Under the priority queuing policy, setting a task's base priority has an effect on a queued entry call if the task is blocked waiting for the call. That is, setting the base priority of a task causes the priority of a queued entry call from that task to be updated and the call to be removed and then reinserted in the entry queue at the new priority (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.4">D.4</a>), unless the call originated from the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0282">triggering_statement</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>.<br />

<MarginText>17_D.5.1</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The effect of two or more Set{"_"}Priority calls executed in parallel on the same task is defined as executing these calls in some serial order.<br />

<MarginText>17.a_D.5.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>This follows from the general reentrancy requirements stated near the beginning of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Predefined Language Environment</a>&rdquo;. <br />

<MarginText>18/5_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0092-1", "AI12-0447-1"]} />
NOTE 4   The rule for when Tasking{"_"}Error is raised for Set{"_"}Priority or Get{"_"}Priority is different from the rule for when Tasking{"_"}Error is raised on an entry call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.3">9.5.3</a>). In particular, the priority of a completed or an abnormal task can be queried so long as the task is not yet terminated, and the priority of a task can be set in any task state (including for terminated tasks).<br />

<MarginText>19/5_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 5   Changing the priorities of a set of tasks can be performed by a series of calls to Set{"_"}Priority for each task separately. This can be done reliably within a protected operation that has high enough ceiling priority to guarantee that the operation completes without being preempted by any of the affected tasks.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>19.a/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00188-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> Priority changes are now required to be done immediately so long as the target task is not on an entry queue.<br />

<MarginText>19.b/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00362-01"]} />
Dynamic{"_"}Priorities is now Preelaborated, so it can be used in preelaborated units. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>19.c/3_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This Ada 95 subclause was moved down a level. The paragraph numbers are the same as those for <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5">D.5</a> in Ada 95.<br />

<MarginText>19.d/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00321-01"]} />
There is no &ldquo;standard&rdquo; policy anymore, so that phrase was replaced by the name of a specific policy in the notes.<br />

<MarginText>19.e/2_D.5.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01"]} />
The bounded error for the priority of a task being higher than the ceiling of an object it is currently in was moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>, so that it applies no matter how the situation arises. <br />

<a id="Subclause_D.5.2"></a>

## D.5.2  Dynamic Priorities for Protected Objects

<MarginText>1/3_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>This subclause specifies how the priority of a protected object can be modified or queried at run time. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2/5_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The following attributes are defined for a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> P that denotes a protected object:<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>P'Priority</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01"]} />
<dl>
<dd>Denotes a non-aliased component of the protected object P. This component is of type System.Any{"_"}Priority and its value is the priority of P. P'Priority denotes a variable if and only if P denotes a variable. A reference to this attribute shall appear only within the body of P.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>3.1/5_D.5.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>P'Relative{"_"}Deadline</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
<dd>Denotes a non-aliased component of the protected object P. This component is of type Ada.Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span and its value is the relative deadline of P. P'Relative{"_"}Deadline denotes a variable if and only if P denotes a variable. A reference to this attribute shall appear only within the body of P. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>4/5_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI12-0230-1"]} />
<p>The initial value of the attribute Priority is determined by the initial value of the priority of the protected object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>)[, and can be changed by an assignment]. The initial value of the attribute Relative{"_"}Deadline is determined by the initial value of the relative deadline of the protected object (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>)[, and can be changed by an assignment]. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>5/3_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p>If the locking policy Ceiling{"_"}Locking (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.3">D.3</a>) is in effect, then the ceiling priority of a protected object <i>P</i> is set to the value of <i>P</i>'Priority at the end of each protected action of <i>P</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00445-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If the locking policy Ceiling{"_"}Locking is in effect, then for a protected object <i>P</i> with either an Attach{"_"}Handler or Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspect specified for one of its procedures, a check is made that the value to be assigned to <i>P</i>'Priority is in the range System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority. If the check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

#### Metrics

<MarginText>7/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01"]} />
<p>The implementation shall document the following metric:<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The difference in execution time of calls to the following procedures in protected object P:<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
protected P is{"\n"}   procedure Do{"_"}Not{"_"}Set{"_"}Ceiling (Pr : System.Any{"_"}Priority);{"\n"}   procedure Set{"_"}Ceiling (Pr : System.Any{"_"}Priority);{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}
<MarginText>10/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
protected body P is{"\n"}   procedure Do{"_"}Not{"_"}Set{"_"}Ceiling (Pr : System.Any{"_"}Priority) is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      null;{"\n"}   end;{"\n"}   procedure Set{"_"}Ceiling (Pr : System.Any{"_"}Priority) is{"\n"}   begin{"\n"}      P'Priority := Pr;{"\n"}   end;{"\n"}end P;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>10.a/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The metrics for setting the priority of a protected object.<br />

<MarginText>11/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01"]} />
NOTE   Since P'Priority is a normal variable, the value following an assignment to the attribute immediately reflects the new value even though its impact on the ceiling priority of P is postponed until completion of the protected action in which it is executed. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>11.a/2_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00327-01", "AI95-00445-01"]} />
The ability to dynamically change and query the priority of a protected object is new. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2012

<MarginText>11.b/5_D.5.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0230-1"]} />
The ability to dynamically change and query the relative deadline of a protected object is new. <br />

# D.6. Preemptive Abort

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.6.mdx

sidebar_position:  160

# D.6. Preemptive Abort

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[This subclause specifies requirements on the immediacy with which an aborted construct is completed.] <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>On a system with a single processor, an aborted construct is completed immediately at the first point that is outside the execution of an abort-deferred operation.<br /></p>

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>On a multiprocessor, the implementation shall document any conditions that cause the completion of an aborted construct to be delayed later than what is specified for a single processor. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>3.b/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>On a multiprocessor, any conditions that cause the completion of an aborted construct to be delayed later than what is specified for a single processor.<br />

#### Metrics

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document the following metrics: <br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The execution time, in processor clock cycles, that it takes for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> to cause the completion of the aborted task. This is measured in a situation where a task T2 preempts task T1 and aborts T1. T1 does not have any finalization code. T2 shall verify that T1 has terminated, by means of the Terminated attribute.<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>On a multiprocessor, an upper bound in seconds, on the time that the completion of an aborted task can be delayed beyond the point that it is required for a single processor.<br /></li>
<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<li>An upper bound on the execution time of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>, in processor clock cycles. This is measured between a point immediately before a task T1 executes a protected operation Pr.Set that makes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5#S0150">condition</a></code> of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code> Pr.Wait True, and the point where task T2 resumes execution immediately after an entry call to Pr.Wait in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>. T1 preempts T2 while T2 is executing the abortable part, and then blocks itself so that T2 can execute. The execution time of T1 is measured separately, and subtracted.<br /></li>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<li>An upper bound on the execution time of an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code>, in the case that no asynchronous transfer of control takes place. This is measured between a point immediately before a task executes the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0280">asynchronous_select</a></code> with a nonnull abortable part, and the point where the task continues execution immediately after it. The execution time of the abortable part is subtracted. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The metrics for aborts.<br />

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<p>Even though the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> is included in the list of potentially blocking operations (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#Subclause_9.5.1">9.5.1</a>), it is recommended that this statement be implemented in a way that never requires the task executing the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> to block.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.8#S0284">abort_statement</a></code> should not require the task executing the statement to block.<br />

<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<p>On a multi-processor, the delay associated with aborting a task on another processor should be bounded; the implementation should use periodic polling, if necessary, to achieve this.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>On a multi-processor, the delay associated with aborting a task on another processor should be bounded.<br />

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
NOTE 1   Abortion does not change the active or base priority of the aborted task.<br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
NOTE 2   Abortion cannot be more immediate than is allowed by the rules for deferral of abortion during finalization and in protected actions.<br />
