# Annex D. Real-Time Systems

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.mdx

sidebar_position:  154

# Annex D. Real-Time Systems

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0404-1"]} />
<p>This Annex specifies additional characteristics of Ada implementations intended for real-time systems software. To conform to this Annex, an implementation shall also conform to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/">Annex C</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/">Systems Programming</a>&rdquo;. <br /></p>

#### Metrics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>The metrics are documentation requirements; an implementation shall document the values of the language-defined metrics for at least one configuration [of hardware or an underlying system] supported by the implementation, and shall document the details of that configuration. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/2</MarginText>
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

<MarginText>2.a.1/2</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The details of the configuration used to generate the values of all metrics.<br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The actual values of the metrics are likely to depend on hardware configuration details that are variable and generally outside the control of a compiler vendor. <br />

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>The metrics do not necessarily yield a simple number. [For some, a range is more suitable, for others a formula dependent on some parameter is appropriate, and for others, it may be more suitable to break the metric into several cases.] Unless specified otherwise, the metrics in this annex are expressed in processor clock cycles. For metrics that require documentation of an upper bound, if there is no upper bound, the implementation shall report that the metric is unbounded. <br /></p>

<MarginText>3.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>There are several good reasons to specify metrics in seconds; there are however equally good reasons to specify them in processor clock cycles. In defining the metrics, we have tried to strike a balance on a case-by-case basis.<br />

<MarginText>3.b</MarginText>
It has been suggested that all metrics should be given names, so that &ldquo;data-sheets&rdquo; could be formulated and published by vendors. However the paragraph number can serve that purpose. <br />

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
NOTE 1   The specification of the metrics makes a distinction between upper bounds and simple execution times. Where something is just specified as &ldquo;the execution time of&rdquo; a piece of code, this leaves one the freedom to choose a nonpathological case. This kind of metric is of the form &ldquo;there exists a program such that the value of the metric is V&rdquo;. Conversely, the meaning of upper bounds is &ldquo;there is no program such that the value of the metric is greater than V&rdquo;. This kind of metric can only be partially tested, by finding the value of V for one or more test programs.<br />

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
NOTE 2   The metrics do not cover the whole language; they are limited to features that are specified in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/">Annex C</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/">Systems Programming</a>&rdquo; and in this Annex. The metrics are intended to provide guidance to potential users as to whether a particular implementation of such a feature is going to be adequate for a particular real-time application. As such, the metrics are aimed at known implementation choices that can result in significant performance differences.<br />

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
NOTE 3   The purpose of the metrics is not necessarily to provide fine-grained quantitative results or to serve as a comparison between different implementations on the same or different platforms. Instead, their goal is rather qualitative; to define a standard set of approximate values that can be measured and used to estimate the general suitability of an implementation, or to evaluate the comparative utility of certain features of an implementation for a particular real-time application.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
This Annex is new to Ada 95. <br />

---

# E.1. Partitions

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  172

# E.1. Partitions

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[The partitions of a distributed program are classified as either active or passive.] <br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>An <i>active partition</i> is a partition as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>. A <i>passive partition</i> is a partition that has no thread of control of its own, whose library units are all preelaborated, and whose data and subprograms are accessible to one or more active partitions. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In most situations, a passive partition does not execute, and does not have a &ldquo;real&rdquo; environment task. Any execution involved in its elaboration and initialization occurs before it comes into existence in a distributed program (like most preelaborated entities). Likewise, there is no concrete meaning to passive partition termination. <br />

<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<p>A passive partition shall include only <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s that either are declared pure or are shared passive (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a> and <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2#Subclause_E.2.1">E.2.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>An active partition shall be configured on a processing node. A passive partition shall be configured either on a storage node or on a processing node.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>The configuration of the partitions of a program onto a distributed system shall be consistent with the possibility for data references or calls between the partitions implied by their semantic dependences. Any reference to data or call of a subprogram across partitions is called a <i>remote access</i>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>For example, an active partition that includes a unit with a semantic dependence on the declaration of another RCI package of some other active partition has to be connected to that other partition by some sort of a message passing mechanism.<br />

<MarginText>5.b</MarginText>
A passive partition that is accessible to an active partition should have its storage addressable to the processor(s) of the active partition. The processor(s) should be able to read and write from/to that storage, as well as to perform &ldquo;read-modify-write&rdquo; operations (in order to support entry-less protected objects).<br />

<MarginText>5.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0359-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A passive partition has no execution resources of its own, so while a call of a subprogram in a passive partition is a remote access to that subprogram, it is <i>not</i> a remote subprogram call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.4">E.4</a>). The calling active partition executes the body of the subprogram of the passive partition. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> is elaborated as part of the elaboration of each partition that includes it. If a normal library unit (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2">E.2</a>) has state, then a separate copy of the state exists in each active partition that elaborates it. [The state evolves independently in each such partition.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Normal library units cannot be included in passive partitions. <br />

<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<p>[An active partition <i>terminates</i> when its environment task terminates.] A partition becomes <i>inaccessible</i> if it terminates or if it is <i>aborted</i>. An active partition is aborted when its environment task is aborted. In addition, if a partition fails during its elaboration, it becomes inaccessible to other partitions. Other implementation-defined events can also result in a partition becoming inaccessible. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>Any events that can result in a partition becoming inaccessible.<br />

<MarginText>8/1</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> D that denotes a library-level declaration, excepting a declaration of or within a declared-pure library unit, the following attribute is defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<dt><br/>D'Partition{"_"}Id</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Denotes a value of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i> that identifies the partition in which D was elaborated. If D denotes the declaration of a remote call interface library unit (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2#Subclause_E.2.3">E.2.3</a>) the given partition is the one where the body of D was elaborated. <br /></dd>
</dl>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>10/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00226-01"]} />
<p>It is a bounded error for there to be cyclic elaboration dependences between the active partitions of a single distributed program. The possible effects, in each of the partitions involved, are deadlock during elaboration, or the raising of Communication{"_"}Error or Program{"_"}Error. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may allow multiple active or passive partitions to be configured on a single processing node, and multiple passive partitions to be configured on a single storage node. In these cases, the scheduling policies, treatment of priorities, and management of shared resources between these partitions are implementation defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The scheduling policies, treatment of priorities, and management of shared resources between partitions in certain cases.<br />

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may allow separate copies of an active partition to be configured on different processing nodes, and to provide appropriate interactions between the copies to present a consistent state of the partition to other active partitions. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The language does not specify the nature of these interactions, nor the actual level of consistency preserved. <br />

<MarginText>13/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>In an implementation, the partitions of a distributed program may be loaded and elaborated at different times; they may be loaded and elaborated one at a time over an extended period of time. An implementation may provide facilities to abort and reload a partition during the execution of a distributed program.<br /></p>

<MarginText>14</MarginText>
<p>An implementation may allow the state of some of the partitions of a distributed program to persist while other partitions of the program terminate and are later reinvoked. <br /></p>

<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
NOTE 1   Library units are grouped into partitions after compile time, but before run time. At compile time, only the relevant library unit properties are identified using categorization aspects.<br />

<MarginText>16</MarginText>
NOTE 2   The value returned by the Partition{"_"}Id attribute can be used as a parameter to implementation-provided subprograms in order to query information about the partition.<br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>16.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00226-01"]} />
Corrected wording so that a partition that has an elaboration problem will either deadlock or raise an exception. While an Ada 95 implementation could allow some partitions to continue to execute, they could be accessing unelaborated data, which is very bad (and erroneous in a practical sense). Therefore, this isn't listed as an inconsistency. <br />

---

# E.2. Categorization of Library Units

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  173

# E.2. Categorization of Library Units

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>[Library units can be categorized according to the role they play in a distributed program. Certain restrictions are associated with each category to ensure that the semantics of a distributed program remain close to the semantics for a nondistributed program.]<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>A <i>categorization aspect</i> restricts the declarations, child units, or semantic dependences of the library unit to which it applies. A <i>categorized library unit</i> is a library unit that has a categorization aspect that is True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>The aspects Shared{"_"}Passive, Remote{"_"}Types, and Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface are categorization aspects. In addition, for the purposes of this Annex, the aspect Pure (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>) is considered a categorization aspect.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01", "AI05-0243-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} [ A library package or generic library package is called a <i>shared passive</i> library unit if the Shared{"_"}Passive aspect of the unit is True. A library package or generic library package is called a <i>remote types</i> library unit if the Remote{"_"}Types aspect of the unit is True.  A library unit is called a <i>remote call interface</i> if the Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface aspect of the unit is True.] A <i>normal library unit</i> is one for which no categorization aspect is True. <br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>These terms (other than &ldquo;normal library unit&rdquo;) are really defined in the following subclauses. <br />

<MarginText>4.a.1/1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} A library subprogram can be a remote call interface, but it cannot be a remote types or shared passive library unit. <br />

<MarginText>5/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0206-1", "AI05-0243-1", "AI05-0269-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>[The various categories of library units and the associated restrictions are described in this and the following subclauses. The categories are related hierarchically in that the library units of one category can depend semantically only on library units of that category or an earlier one in the hierarchy, except that the body of a remote types or remote call interface library unit is unrestricted, the declaration of a remote types or remote call interface library unit may depend on preelaborated normal library units that are mentioned only in private with clauses, and all categories can depend on limited views.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<p>The overall hierarchy (including declared pure) is as follows, with a lower-numbered category being &ldquo;earlier in the hierarchy&rdquo; in the sense of the previous paragraph: <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.1/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Declared Pure<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.2/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>Shared Passive<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.3/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>Remote Types<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.4/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>4.</dt>
<dd>Remote Call Interface<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6.5/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>5.</dt>
<dd>Normal (no restrictions) <br /></dd>
</dl>
<p><i>Paragraphs 7 through 11 were deleted.</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<p>Declared pure and shared passive library units are preelaborated. The declaration of a remote types or remote call interface library unit is required to be preelaborable. ]<br /></p>

<p><i>Paragraph 13 and 14 were deleted.</i> <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>14.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that a library subprogram can be a remote call interface unit.<br />

<MarginText>14.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00208-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0079</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Removed the requirement that types be represented the same in all partitions, because it prevents the definition of heterogeneous distributed systems and goes much further than required. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>14.c/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0206-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
We now allow private withs of preelaborated units in Remote Types and Remote Call Interface units; this is documented as an extension in the subclauses where this is defined normatively.<br />

<MarginText>14.d/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
We have introduced categorization aspects; these are documented as extensions in the subclauses where they actually are defined. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>14.e/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
Categorization pragmas are now obsolescent. <br />

<a id="Subclause_E.2.1"></a>

## E.2.1  Shared Passive Library Units

<MarginText>1_E.2.1</MarginText>
<p>[A shared passive library unit is used for managing global data shared between active partitions. The restrictions on shared passive library units prevent the data or tasks of one active partition from being accessible to another active partition through references implicit in objects declared in the shared passive library unit.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a_E.2.1</MarginText>
The restrictions governing a shared passive library unit are designed to ensure that objects and subprograms declared in the package can be used safely from multiple active partitions, even though the active partitions live in different address spaces, and have separate run-time systems. <br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 2 and 3 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>When the library unit aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>) Shared{"_"}Passive of a library unit is True, the library unit is a <i>shared passive library unit</i>. The following restrictions apply to such a library unit:<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/3_E.2.1</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Shared{"_"}Passive: </b>A given package is used to represent shared memory in a distributed system.<br />

<MarginText>5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>[it shall be preelaborable (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>);] <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.a_E.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>It cannot contain library-level declarations of protected objects with entries, nor of task objects. Task objects are disallowed because passive partitions don't have any threads of control of their own, nor any run-time system of their own. Protected objects with entries are disallowed because an entry queue contains references to calling tasks, and that would require in effect a pointer from a passive partition back to a task in some active partition. <br />

<MarginText>6/3_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>it shall depend semantically only upon declared pure or shared passive <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a_E.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Shared passive packages cannot depend semantically upon remote types packages because the values of an access type declared in a remote types package refer to the local heap of the active partition including the remote types package. <br />

<MarginText>6.b/3_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We say <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> here, so that limited views are allowed; those are not library units, but they are <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>7/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00003-01", "AI12-0038-1", "AI12-0320-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0080</i>{"}"} it shall not contain a library-level declaration:<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.1/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0320-1"]} />
<li>of an access type that designates a class-wide type; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a_E.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>These kinds of access types are disallowed because the object designated by an access value of such a type could contain an implicit reference back to the active partition on whose behalf the designated object was created. <br />

<MarginText>7.2/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0320-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>of a type with a part that is of a task type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.3/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0320-1"]} />
<li>of a type with a part that is of a protected type with <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>s; or<br /></li>
<MarginText>7.4/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0038-1", "AI12-0320-1"]} />
<li>that contains a name that denotes a type declared within a declared-pure package, if that type has a part that is of an access type; for the purposes of this rule, the parts considered include those of the full views of any private types or private extensions.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.b/4_E.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This rule breaks privacy by looking into the full views of private types. Avoiding privacy breakage here would have required disallowing the use in a shared passive package of any private type declared in a declared-pure package, which would have been severely incompatible. <br />

<MarginText>8_E.2.1</MarginText>
<p>Notwithstanding the definition of accessibility given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>, the declaration of a library unit P1 is not accessible from within the declarative region of a shared passive library unit P2, unless the shared passive library unit P2 depends semantically on P1. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a_E.2.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We considered a more complex rule, but dropped it. This is the simplest rule that recognizes that a shared passive package may outlive some other library package, unless it depends semantically on that package. In a nondistributed program, all library packages are presumed to have the same lifetime.<br />

<MarginText>8.b/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
Implementations may define additional aspects or pragmas that force two library packages to be in the same partition, or to have the same lifetime, which would allow this rule to be relaxed in the presence of such aspects or pragmas. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9_E.2.1</MarginText>
<p>A shared passive library unit is preelaborated.<br /></p>

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>10_E.2.1</MarginText>
<p>A shared passive library unit shall be assigned to at most one partition within a given program.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11_E.2.1</MarginText>
<p>Notwithstanding the rule given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>, a compilation unit in a given partition does not <i>need</i> (in the sense of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>) the shared passive library units on which it depends semantically to be included in that same partition; they will typically reside in separate passive partitions.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0359-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>This rule is necessary so that the shared data of a shared passive partition is not duplicated in each partition. It does not imply a particular implementation; in particular, code can be replicated in each active partition. <br />

<MarginText>11.b/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0359-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>One possible implementation for a shared passive partition is as a shared library that is mapped into the address space of of each active partition. In such case, both the code and the data of the passive partition would be mapped into the active partitions and directly called/accessed from each active partition. For instance, on Microsoft Windows a DLL has the correct semantics.<br />

<MarginText>11.c/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
Alternatively, the shared data can be represented as a file or persistent memory, with the shared code being replicated in each active partition. Code replication is an as-if optimization; it should be impossible to tell where the code lives since no elaboration is necessary. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>11.d/2_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00003-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0080</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Corrected the wording to allow access types in blocks in shared passive generic packages. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>11.e/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
Shared{"_"}Passive is now a categorization aspect, so it can be specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>11.f/4_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0038-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Uses of access types declared in declared-pure units are not allowed in library-level shared passive packages. These were allowed by Ada 2005 and Ada 2012, but it is unlikely that they work properly, as active partitions could disappear before the shared-passive partition. As such, the new errors are more likely to catch bugs than to cause them. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>11.g/5_E.2.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
The pragma Shared{"_"}Passive is now obsolescent. <br />

<a id="Subclause_E.2.2"></a>

## E.2.2  Remote Types Library Units

<MarginText>1_E.2.2</MarginText>
<p>[A remote types library unit supports the definition of types intended for use in communication between active partitions.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a_E.2.2</MarginText>
The restrictions governing a remote types package are similar to those for a declared pure package. However, the restrictions are relaxed deliberately to allow such a package to contain declarations that violate the stateless property of pure packages, though it is presumed that any state-dependent properties are essentially invisible outside the package. <br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 2 and 3 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>When the library unit aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>) Remote{"_"}Types of a library unit is True, the library unit is a <i>remote types library unit</i>. The following restrictions apply to such a library unit:<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Remote{"_"}Types: </b>Types in a given package may be used in remote procedure calls.<br />

<MarginText>5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>[it shall be preelaborable;]<br /></li>
<MarginText>6/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0206-1", "AI05-0243-1"]} />
<li>it shall depend semantically only on declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s, shared passive library units, other remote types library units, or preelaborated normal library units that are mentioned only in private with clauses;<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We say declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> here, so that (all) limited views are allowed; those are not library units, but they are declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>7_E.2.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>it shall not contain the declaration of any variable within the visible part of the library unit; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>7.a_E.2.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is essentially a &ldquo;methodological&rdquo; restriction. A separate copy of a remote types package is included in each partition that references it, just like a normal package. Nevertheless, a remote types package is thought of as an &ldquo;essentially pure&rdquo; package for defining types to be used for interpartition communication, and it could be misleading to declare visible objects when no remote data access is actually being provided. <br />

<MarginText>8/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00240-01", "AI95-00366-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>the full view of each type declared in the visible part of the library unit that has any available stream attributes shall support external streaming (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>8.a_E.2.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is to prevent the use of the predefined Read and Write attributes of an access type as part of the Read and Write attributes of a visible type. <br />

<MarginText>8.b/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Types that do not have available stream attributes are excluded from this rule; that means that attributes do not need to be specified for most limited types. It is only necessary to specify attributes for nonlimited types that have a part that is of any access type, and for extensions of limited types with available stream attributes where the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#S0075">record_extension_part</a></code> includes a subcomponent of an access type, where the access type does not have specified attributes. <br />

<MarginText>9/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00164-01", "AI05-0060-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0082</i>{"}"} A named access type declared in the visible part of a remote types or remote call interface library unit is called a <i>remote access type</i>. Such a type shall be:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.1/1_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00164-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0082</i>{"}"} an access-to-subprogram type, or<br /></li>
<MarginText>9.2/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00164-01", "AI05-0060-1"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0082</i>{"}"} a general access type that designates a class-wide limited private type, a class-wide limited interface type, or a class-wide private extension all of whose ancestors are either private extensions, limited interface types, or limited private types. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9.3/1_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00004-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0081</i>{"}"} A type that is derived from a remote access type is also a remote access type.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.4/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0283-1"]} />
<p>A remote access-to-subprogram type shall not be nonblocking (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>All calls on remote subprograms are considered potentially blocking, so they cannot statically be allowed in nonblocking code. <br />

<MarginText>9.b/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The type declaration of a remote type is illegal if the Nonblocking aspect is True, either implicitly by inheritance or by explicit specification. <br />

<MarginText>10_E.2.2</MarginText>
<p>The following restrictions apply to the use of a remote access-to-subprogram type: <br /></p>

<MarginText>11/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00431-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>A value of a remote access-to-subprogram type shall be converted only to or from another (subtype-conformant) remote access-to-subprogram type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>12_E.2.2</MarginText>
<li>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> of an Access <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0100">attribute_reference</a></code> that yields a value of a remote access-to-subprogram type shall statically denote a (subtype-conformant) remote subprogram. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13_E.2.2</MarginText>
<p>The following restrictions apply to the use of a remote access-to-class-wide type: <br /></p>

<MarginText>14/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00047-01", "AI95-00240-01", "AI95-00366-01", "AI05-0060-1", "AI05-0101-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0083</i>{"}"} The primitive subprograms of the corresponding specific type shall only have access parameters if they are controlling formal parameters. The primitive functions of the corresponding specific type shall only have an access result if it is a controlling access result. Each noncontrolling formal parameter and noncontrolling result type shall support external streaming (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>14.1/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0060-1", "AI05-0215-1", "AI05-0269-1"]} />
<li>The corresponding specific type shall not have a primitive procedure with the Synchronization aspect specified unless the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0256">synchronization_kind</a></code> is Optional (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>);<br /></li>
<MarginText>15_E.2.2</MarginText>
<li>A value of a remote access-to-class-wide type shall be explicitly converted only to another remote access-to-class-wide type;<br /></li>
<MarginText>16/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0034-1"]} />
<li>A value of a remote access-to-class-wide type shall be dereferenced (or implicitly converted to an anonymous access type) only as part of a dispatching call to a primitive operation of the designated type where the value designates a controlling operand of the call (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.4">E.4</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.4">Remote Subprogram Calls</a>&rdquo;); <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>16.a/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0034-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Stream attributes of the designated type are not primitive operations of the designated type, and thus remote calls to them are prohibited by this rule. This is good, as the access parameter of a stream attribute does not have external streaming, and thus cannot be a parameter of a remote call. <br />

<MarginText>16.1/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0101-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A controlling access result value for a primitive function with any controlling operands of the corresponding specific type shall either be explicitly converted to a remote access-to-class-wide type or be part of a dispatching call where the value designates a controlling operand of the call;<br /></li>
<MarginText>17/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01", "AI12-0085-1"]} />
<li>The Storage{"_"}Pool attribute is not defined for a remote access-to-class-wide type; the expected type for an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.8#S0164">allocator</a></code> shall not be a remote access-to-class-wide type. A remote access-to-class-wide type shall not be an actual parameter for a generic formal access type. The Storage{"_"}Size attribute of a remote access-to-class-wide type yields 0. The Storage{"_"}Pool and Storage{"_"}Size aspects shall not be specified for a remote access-to-class-wide type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17.a/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>All of these restrictions are because there is no storage pool associated with a remote access-to-class-wide type. The Storage{"_"}Size is defined to be 0 so that there is no conflict with the rules for pure units. <br />

<MarginText>17.b/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0085-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The prohibition against specifying the Storage{"_"}Size aspect for an access-to-class-wide type applies to any method of doing that, including via either an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> or an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>. <br />

#### Erroneous Execution

<MarginText>17.1/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0076-1"]} />
<p>Execution is erroneous if some operation (other than the initialization or finalization of the object) modifies the value of a constant object declared in the visible part of a remote types package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17.c/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This could be accomplished via a self-referencing pointer or via squirrelling away a writable pointer to a controlled object. <br />

<MarginText>18/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
NOTE 1   A remote types library unit is not necessarily pure, and the types it defines can include levels of indirection implemented by using access types. User-specified Read and Write attributes (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>) provide for sending values of such a type between active partitions, with Write marshalling the representation, and Read unmarshalling any levels of indirection.<br />

<MarginText>19/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0060-1"]} />
NOTE 2   The value of a remote access-to-class-wide limited interface can designate an object of a nonlimited type derived from the interface.<br />

<MarginText>20/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0060-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE 3   A remote access type can designate a class-wide synchronized, protected, or task interface type. <br />

<MarginText>20.a/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="proof">
<b></b>Synchronized, protected, and task interfaces are all considered limited interfaces, see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9#Subclause_3.9.4">3.9.4</a>. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>20.b/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00240-01", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> The wording was changed from &ldquo;user-specified&rdquo; to &ldquo;available&rdquo; read and write attributes. (This was then further changed, see below.) This means that an access type with the attributes specified in the private part would originally have been sufficient to allow the access type to be used in a remote type, but that is no longer allowed. Similarly, the attributes of a remote type that has access components have to be specified in the visible part. These changes were made so that the rules were consistent with the rules introduced for the Corrigendum for stream attributes; moreover, legality should not depend on the contents of the private part. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>20.c/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01", "AI05-0005-1"]} />
Remote types that cannot be streamed (that is, have no available stream attributes) do not require the specification of stream attributes. This is necessary so that most extensions of Limited{"_"}Controlled do not need stream attributes defined (otherwise there would be a significant incompatibility, as Limited{"_"}Controlled would need stream attributes, and then all extensions of it also would need stream attributes). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>20.d/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00004-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0081</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added missing wording so that a type derived from a remote access type is also a remote access type.<br />

<MarginText>20.e/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00047-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0083</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that user-defined Read and Write attributes are required for the primitive subprograms corresponding to a remote access-to-class-wide type.<br />

<MarginText>20.f/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00164-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0082</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Added missing wording so that a remote access type can designate an appropriate private extension.<br />

<MarginText>20.g/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
Changed the wording to use the newly defined term <i>type that supports external streaming</i>, so that various issues with access types in pure units and implicitly declared attributes for type extensions are properly handled.<br />

<MarginText>20.h/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
Defined Storage{"_"}Size to be 0 for remote access-to-class-wide types, rather than having it undefined. This eliminates issues with pure units requiring a defined storage size.<br />

<MarginText>20.i/2_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00431-01"]} />
Corrected the wording so that a value of a local access-to-subprogram type cannot be converted to a remote access-to-subprogram type, as intended (and required by the ACATS). <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>20.j/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0101-1", "AI12-0005-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added rules about the returning of remote access-to-class-wide types; this had been missed in the past. While programs that returned unstreamable types from RCI functions were legal, it is not clear what they could have done (as the results could not be marshalled). Similarly, RCI functions that return remote controlling access types could try to save those values, but it is unlikely that a compiler would know how to do that usefully. Thus, it seems unlikely that any real programs will be impacted by these changes. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>20.k/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0060-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Clarified that anonymous access types are never remote access types (and can be used in remote types units subject to the normal restrictions). Added wording to allow limited class-wide interfaces to be designated by remote access types.<br />

<MarginText>20.l/3_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0206-1"]} />
Added wording to allow private withs of preelaborated normal units in the specification of a remote types unit.<br />

<MarginText>20.m/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
Remote{"_"}Types is now a categorization aspect, so it can be specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>20.n/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0034-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that dispatching remote stream attribute calls are prohibited. We don't document this as an incompatibility, as the stream parameter cannot be marshalled for a remote call (it doesn't have external streaming), so it's impossible that any working program depends on this functionality.<br />

<MarginText>20.o/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0076-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Explicitly stated that modifying a visible constant in a remote types package is erroneous. We don't document this as inconsistent as implementations certainly can still do whatever they were previously doing (no change is required); moreover, this case (and many more) were erroneous in Ada 2005 and before, so we're just restoring the previous semantics.<br />

<MarginText>20.p/4_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0085-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Clarified that specifying the Storage{"_"}Pool or Storage{"_"}Size aspect for an access-to-class-wide type is not allowed. The intent is clear, and no implementation has ever allowed specifying the aspects (the attributes already cannot be specified), so we don't document this as an incompatibility.<br />

<MarginText>20.q/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0283-1"]} />
Added a rule to ensure that potentially blocking remote calls are not considered nonblocking.<br />

<MarginText>20.r/5_E.2.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
The pragma Remote{"_"}Types is now obsolescent.<br />

<a id="Subclause_E.2.3"></a>

## E.2.3  Remote Call Interface Library Units

<MarginText>1_E.2.3</MarginText>
<p>[A remote call interface library unit can be used as an interface for remote procedure calls (RPCs) (or remote function calls) between active partitions.] <br /></p>

#### Language Design Principles

<MarginText>1.a_E.2.3</MarginText>
The restrictions governing a remote call interface library unit are intended to ensure that the values of the actual parameters in a remote call can be meaningfully sent between two active partitions. <br />

<p><i>Paragraphs 2 through 6 were moved to <a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Annex J</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/">Obsolescent Features</a>&rdquo;.</i> <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01", "AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} When the library unit aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#Subclause_13.1.1">13.1.1</a>) Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface of a library unit is True, the library unit is a <i>remote call interface (RCI)</i>. A subprogram declared in the visible part of such a library unit, or declared by such a library unit, is called a <i>remote subprogram</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface: </b>Subprograms in a given package may be used in remote procedure calls.<br />

<MarginText>8/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0206-1", "AI05-0243-1"]} />
<p>The declaration of an RCI library unit shall be preelaborable (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>), and shall depend semantically only upon declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s, shared passive library units, remote types library units, other remote call interface library units, or preelaborated normal library units that are mentioned only in private with clauses.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8.a/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>We say declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code> here, so that (all) limited views are allowed; those are not library units, but they are declared pure <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>9/1_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} In addition, the following restrictions apply to an RCI library unit: <br /></p>

<MarginText>10/1_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} its visible part shall not contain the declaration of a variable; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>10.a/1_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} Remote call interface units do not provide remote data access. A shared passive package has to be used for that. <br />

<MarginText>11/1_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} its visible part shall not contain the declaration of a limited type; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>11.a/2_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00240-01", "AI95-00366-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>We disallow the declaration of task and protected types, since calling an entry or a protected subprogram implicitly passes an object of a limited type (the target task or protected object). We disallow other limited types since we require that such types have available Read and Write attributes, but we certainly don't want the Read and Write attributes themselves to involve remote calls (thereby defeating their purpose of marshalling the value for remote calls). <br />

<MarginText>12/1_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} its visible part shall not contain a nested <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0310">generic_declaration</a></code>; <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12.a_E.2.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is disallowed because the body of the nested generic would presumably have access to data inside the body of the RCI package, and if instantiated in a different partition, remote data access might result, which is not supported. <br />

<MarginText>13/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} it shall not be, nor shall its visible part contain, the declaration of a subprogram for which aspect Inline is True;<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.1/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0283-1"]} />
<li>it shall not be, nor shall its visible part contain, the declaration of a subprogram that is nonblocking (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>);<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>13.a/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>All such subprograms are remote subprograms, and all calls on remote subprograms are considered potentially blocking, so they cannot statically be allowed in nonblocking code. <br />

<MarginText>13.b/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The type declaration of a remote subprogram is illegal if the Nonblocking aspect is True, either implicitly by inheritance or by explicit specification. <br />

<MarginText>14/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01", "AI95-00240-01", "AI95-00366-01", "AI05-0101-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} it shall not be, nor shall its visible part contain, a subprogram (or access-to-subprogram) declaration whose profile has a parameter or result of a type that does not support external streaming (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>);<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14.a/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0101-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>No anonymous access types support external streaming, so they are never allowed as parameters or results of RCI subprograms. <br />

<MarginText>15_E.2.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>any public child of the library unit shall be a remote call interface library unit. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>15.a/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>No restrictions apply to the private part of an RCI package, and since a public child can &ldquo;see&rdquo; the private part of its parent, such a child must itself have a Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface aspect, and be assigned to the same partition (see below). <br />

<MarginText>15.b/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We considered making the public child of an RCI package implicitly RCI, but it seemed better to require an explicit aspect to avoid any confusion.<br />

<MarginText>15.c_E.2.3</MarginText>
Note that there is no need for a private child to be an RCI package, since it can only be seen from the body of its parent or its siblings, all of which are required to be in the same active partition. <br />

<MarginText>15.1/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0002-1"]} />
<p>Specification of a stream-oriented attribute is illegal in the specification of a remote call interface library unit. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), this rule applies also in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15.d/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This applies whether the stream-oriented attribute is specified with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> or with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>15.e/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Stream-oriented attributes are intended to be used locally (to marshall values), while subprograms in a remote call interface are intended to be used remotely. We resolve the conflict by banning the local use routines. The type should be included in a remote types package and imported into the remote call interface package. <br />

<MarginText>16/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote is a library unit aspect. If the All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote aspect of a library unit is True, the library unit shall be a remote call interface.<br /></p>

<MarginText>16.a/4_E.2.3</MarginText>
<b>Aspect Description for </b><b>All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote: </b>All indirect or dispatching remote subprogram calls, and all direct remote subprogram calls, should use the Partition Communication Subsystem.<br />

#### Post-Compilation Rules

<MarginText>17_E.2.3</MarginText>
<p>A remote call interface library unit shall be assigned to at most one partition of a given program. A remote call interface library unit whose parent is also an RCI library unit shall be assigned only to the same partition as its parent. <br /></p>

<MarginText>17.a/1_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} The declaration of an RCI unit, with a calling-stub body, is automatically included in all active partitions with compilation units that depend on it. However the whole RCI library unit, including its (non-stub) body, will only be in one of the active partitions. <br />

<MarginText>18_E.2.3</MarginText>
<p>Notwithstanding the rule given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>, a compilation unit in a given partition that semantically depends on the declaration of an RCI library unit, <i>needs</i> (in the sense of <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2">10.2</a>) only the declaration of the RCI library unit, not the body, to be included in that same partition. [Therefore, the body of an RCI library unit is included only in the partition to which the RCI library unit is explicitly assigned.]<br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>19/4_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0031-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} If aspect All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote is True for a given RCI library unit, then the implementation shall route any of the following calls through the Partition Communication Subsystem (PCS); see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.5">E.5</a>: <br /></p>

<MarginText>19.1/4_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0031-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>A direct call to a subprogram of the RCI unit from outside the declarative region of the unit;<br /></li>
<MarginText>19.2/4_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0031-1"]} />
<li>An indirect call through a remote access-to-subprogram value that designates a subprogram of the RCI unit;<br /></li>
<MarginText>19.3/4_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0031-1"]} />
<li>A dispatching call with a controlling operand designated by a remote access-to-class-wide value whose tag identifies a type declared in the RCI unit. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>19.a/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01", "AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0031-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} When this aspect is False (or not used), it is presumed that most implementations will not make calls through the PCS if the call originates in the same partition as that of the RCI unit. When this aspect is True, all indirect or dispatching remote subprogram calls to the RCI unit, and all direct calls from outside the subsystem rooted at the RCI unit, are treated like calls from outside the partition, ensuring that the PCS is involved in all such calls (for debugging, redundancy, etc.). <br />

<MarginText>19.b/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0005-1", "AI12-0031-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>There is no point in forcing local direct calls (including calls from children) to go through the PCS, since on the target system these calls are always local, and all the units are in the same active partition. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>20/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1", "AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may omit support for the Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface aspect or the All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote aspect. [Explicit message-based communication between active partitions can be supported as an alternative to RPC.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>20.a/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Of course, it is pointless to support the All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote aspect if the Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface aspect (or some approximate equivalent) is not supported. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 95

<MarginText>20.b/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00240-01", "AI05-0248-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> The wording was changed from &ldquo;user-specified&rdquo; to &ldquo;available&rdquo; read and write attributes. (This was then further changed, see below.) This means that a type with the attributes specified in the private part would originally have been allowed as a formal parameter of an RCI subprogram, but that is no longer allowed. This change was made so that the rules were consistent with the rules introduced for the Corrigendum for stream attributes; moreover, legality should not depend on the contents of the private part. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>20.c/2_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00048-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0078</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> Changed the wording to allow a library subprogram to be a remote call interface unit.<br />

<MarginText>20.d/2_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00366-01"]} />
Changed the wording to use the newly defined term <i>type that supports external streaming</i>, so that various issues with access types in pure units and implicitly declared attributes for type extensions are properly handled. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>20.e/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0101-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added a rule to ensure that function results are streamable; this was missing in previous versions of Ada. While programs that returned unstreamable types from RCI functions were legal, it is not clear what they could have done (as the results could not be marshalled). Thus, it seems unlikely that any real programs will be impacted by this change. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>20.f/3_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0206-1"]} />
Added wording to allow private withs of preelaborated normal units in the specification of a remote call interface unit.<br />

<MarginText>20.g/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote is now a representation aspect, so it can be specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code><br />

<MarginText>20.h/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0243-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface is now a categorization aspect, so it can be specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> <br />

#### Inconsistencies With Ada 2012

<MarginText>20.i/4_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0031-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Redefined when indirect and dispatching remote calls have to be remote for a unit for which the aspect All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote is True. With the new rules, a local target called indirectly or via dispatching will be routed through the PCS, while that was not necessarily true in earlier Ada. If a program depended on local targets not being routed through the PCS even when All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote is used, then it might behave differently or fail in Ada 2012 as corrected with this refinement. This is highly unlikely as the PCS is going to be able to communicate with any partition of the program, including the local partition. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2012

<MarginText>20.j/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0002-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Specifying user-defined stream-oriented attributes is now illegal in an RCI unit. If a program contains such attributes, they and their associated type will need to be moved to a remote types package (which is then imported into the RCI unit). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>20.k/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0283-1"]} />
Added a rule to ensure that potentially blocking remote calls are not considered nonblocking.<br />

<MarginText>20.l/5_E.2.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
The pragmas Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface and All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote are now obsolescent. <br />
