<MarginText>39_F.3.1</MarginText>
<p>The following composition constraints apply to a picture String: <br /></p>

<MarginText>40_F.3.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code> does not have occurrences of different <code>LHS{"_"}Sign</code> Character values.<br /></li>
<MarginText>41_F.3.1</MarginText>
<li>If a picture String has '{"<"}' as <code>fixed{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code>, then it has '{">"}' as <code>RHS{"_"}sign</code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>42_F.3.1</MarginText>
<li>If a picture String has '{"<"}' in a <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code> or in an <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number</code>, then it has an occurrence of '{">"}'.<br /></li>
<MarginText>43/1_F.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00153"]} />
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0088</i>{"}"} If a picture String has '+' or '&ndash;' as <code>fixed{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code>, in a <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code>, or in an <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number</code>, then it has no <code>RHS{"_"}sign</code> or '{">"}' character.<br /></li>
<MarginText>44_F.3.1</MarginText>
<li>An instance of <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number</code> does not have occurrences of different <code>sign{"_"}char</code> Character values.<br /></li>
<MarginText>45_F.3.1</MarginText>
<li>An instance of <code>all{"_"}currency{"_"}number</code> does not have occurrences of different <code>currency{"_"}char</code> Character values.<br /></li>
<MarginText>46_F.3.1</MarginText>
<li>An instance of <code>all{"_"}zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}number</code> does not have occurrences of different <code>zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}char</code> Character values, except for possible case differences between 'Z' and 'z'. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>47_F.3.1</MarginText>
<p>A <i>replicable Character</i> is a Character that, by the above rules, can occur in two consecutive positions in a picture String.<br /></p>

<MarginText>48_F.3.1</MarginText>
<p>A <i>Character replication</i> is a String <br /></p>

<MarginText>49_F.3.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
char & '(' & spaces & count{"_"}string & ')'{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>50_F.3.1</MarginText>
<p>where <i>char</i> is a replicable Character, <i>spaces</i> is a String (possibly empty) comprising only space Character values, and <i>count{"_"}string</i> is a String of one or more decimal digit Character values. A Character replication in a picture String has the same effect as (and is said to be <i>equivalent to</i>) a String comprising <i>n</i> consecutive occurrences of <i>char</i>, where <i>n</i>=Integer'Value(<i>count{"_"}string</i>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>51_F.3.1</MarginText>
<p>An <i>expanded picture String</i> is a picture String containing no Character replications. <br /></p>

<MarginText>51.a_F.3.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Since 'B' is not allowed after a RHS sign, there is no need for a special rule to disallow "9.99DB(2)" as an abbreviation for "9.99DBB" <br />

<MarginText>52_F.3.1</MarginText>
NOTE   Although a sign to the left of the number can float, a sign to the right of the number is in a fixed position. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>52.a/2_F.3.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00153-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0088</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> The picture string rules for numbers were tightened. <br />

<a id="Subclause_F.3.2"></a>

## F.3.2  Edited Output Generation

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>1_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The contents of an edited output string are based on: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A value, Item, of some decimal type Num,<br /></li>
<MarginText>3_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>An expanded picture String Pic{"_"}String,<br /></li>
<MarginText>4_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>A Boolean value, Blank{"_"}When{"_"}Zero,<br /></li>
<MarginText>5_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>A Currency string,<br /></li>
<MarginText>6_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>A Fill character,<br /></li>
<MarginText>7_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>A Separator character, and<br /></li>
<MarginText>8_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>A Radix{"_"}Mark character. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>9_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The combination of a True value for Blank{"_"}When{"_"}Zero and a '{"*"}' character in Pic{"_"}String is inconsistent; no edited output string is defined. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/2_F.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Such a Pic{"_"}String is invalid, and any attempt to use such a string will raise Picture{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>10_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>A layout error is identified in the rules below if leading nonzero digits of Item, character values of the Currency string, or a negative sign would be truncated; in such cases no edited output string is defined.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>The edited output string has lower bound 1 and upper bound N where N = Pic{"_"}String'Length + Currency{"_"}Length{"_"}Adjustment &ndash; Radix{"_"}Adjustment, and <br /></p>

<MarginText>12_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Currency{"_"}Length{"_"}Adjustment = Currency'Length &ndash; 1 if there is some occurrence of '{"$"}' in Pic{"_"}String, and 0 otherwise.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>Radix{"_"}Adjustment = 1 if there is an occurrence of 'V' or 'v' in Pic{"_"}Str, and 0 otherwise. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>14_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>Let the magnitude of Item be expressed as a base-10 number Ip···I1.F1···Fq, called the <i>displayed</i> <i>magnitude</i> of Item, where: <br /></p>

<MarginText>15_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>q = Min(Max(Num'Scale, 0), n) where n is 0 if Pic{"_"}String has no <code>radix</code> and is otherwise the number of digit positions following <code>radix</code> in Pic{"_"}String, where a digit position corresponds to an occurrence of '9', a <code>zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}char</code> (for an <code>all{"_"}zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}number</code>), a <code>currency{"_"}char</code> (for an <code>all{"_"}currency{"_"}number</code>), or a <code>sign{"_"}char</code> (for an <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number</code>).<br /></li>
<MarginText>16_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>Ip /= 0 if p{">"}0. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>17_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>If n {"<"} Num'Scale, then the above number is the result of rounding (away from 0 if exactly midway between values).<br /></p>

<MarginText>18_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>If Blank{"_"}When{"_"}Zero = True and the displayed magnitude of Item is zero, then the edited output string comprises all space character values. Otherwise, the picture String is treated as a sequence of instances of syntactic categories based on the rules in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-F/AA-F.3#Subclause_F.3.1">F.3.1</a>, and the edited output string is the concatenation of string values derived from these categories according to the following mapping rules.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19/5_F.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0451-1"]} />
<p>Table F.1 shows the mapping from a sign control symbol to a corresponding character or string in the edited output. In the columns showing the edited output, a lower-case 'b' represents the space character. If there is no sign control symbol but the value of Item is negative, a layout error occurs and no edited output string is produced.<br /></p>

<MarginText>20/5_F.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0451-1"]} />
<p><b>Table F.1: Edited Output for Sign Control Symbols</b><b>Sign Control Symbol</b><b>Edited Output for <br />Nonnegative Number</b><b>Edited Output for <br />Negative Number</b>'+''+''&ndash;''&ndash;''b''&ndash;''{"<"}''b''(''{">"}''b'')'"CR""bb""CR""DB""bb""DB"An instance of <code>fixed{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code> maps to a character as shown in Table F.1.<br /></p>

<MarginText>21_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>fixed{"_"}{"$"}{"_"}char</code> maps to Currency.<br /></p>

<MarginText>22_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>direct{"_"}insertion</code> maps to Separator if <code>direct{"_"}insertion</code> = '{"_"}', and to the <code>direct{"_"}insertion</code> Character otherwise.<br /></p>

<MarginText>23_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>number</code> maps to a string <i>integer{"_"}part</i> & <i>radix{"_"}part</i> & <i>fraction{"_"}part</i> where: <br /></p>

<MarginText>24_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The string for <i>integer{"_"}part</i> is obtained as follows: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>25_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Occurrences of '9' in <code>fore{"_"}digits</code> of <code>number</code> are replaced from right to left with the decimal digit character values for I1, ..., Ip, respectively.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>26_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>Each occurrence of '9' in <code>fore{"_"}digits</code> to the left of the leftmost '9' replaced according to rule 1 is replaced with '0'.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>27_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>If p exceeds the number of occurrences of '9' in <code>fore{"_"}digits</code> of <code>number</code>, then the excess leftmost digits are eligible for use in the mapping of an instance of <code>zero{"_"}suppression</code>, <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code>, <code>floating{"_"}{"$"}{"_"}currency</code>, or <code>floating{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> to the left of <code>number</code>; if there is no such instance, then a layout error occurs and no edited output string is produced. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>28_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The <i>radix{"_"}part</i> is: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>29_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>"" if <code>number</code> does not include a <code>radix</code>, if <code>radix</code> = 'V', or if <code>radix</code> = 'v'<br /></li>
<MarginText>30_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>Radix{"_"}Mark if <code>number</code> includes '.' as <code>radix</code> <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>31_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The string for <i>fraction{"_"}part</i> is obtained as follows: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>32_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Occurrences of '9' in <code>aft{"_"}digits</code> of <code>number</code> are replaced from left to right with the decimal digit character values for F1, ... Fq.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>33_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>Each occurrence of '9' in <code>aft{"_"}digits</code> to the right of the rightmost '9' replaced according to rule 1 is replaced by '0'. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>34_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>zero{"_"}suppression</code> maps to the string obtained as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>35_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>The rightmost 'Z', 'z', or '{"*"}' Character values are replaced with the excess digits (if any) from the <i>integer{"_"}part</i> of the mapping of the <code>number</code> to the right of the <code>zero{"_"}suppression</code> instance,<br /></dd>
<MarginText>36_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>A <code>context{"_"}sensitive{"_"}insertion</code> Character is replaced as though it were a <code>direct{"_"}insertion</code> Character, if it occurs to the right of some 'Z', 'z', or '{"*"}' in <code>zero{"_"}suppression</code> that has been mapped to an excess digit,<br /></dd>
<MarginText>37_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>Each Character to the left of the leftmost Character replaced according to rule 1 above is replaced by: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>38_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>the space character if the zero suppression Character is 'Z' or 'z', or<br /></li>
<MarginText>39_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>the Fill character if the zero suppression Character is '{"*"}'. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>40_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>4.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>A layout error occurs if some excess digits remain after all 'Z', 'z', and '{"*"}' Character values in <code>zero{"_"}suppression</code> have been replaced via rule 1; no edited output string is produced. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>41/5_F.3.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0451-1"]} />
<p>An instance of <code>RHS{"_"}sign</code> maps to a character or string as shown in Table F.1.<br /></p>

<MarginText>42_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code> maps to the string obtained as follows. <br /></p>

<MarginText>43_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Up to all but one of the rightmost <code>LHS{"_"}Sign</code> Character values are replaced by the excess digits (if any) from the <i>integer{"_"}part</i> of the mapping of the <code>number</code> to the right of the <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code> instance.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>44/5_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0451-1"]} />
<dd>The next Character to the left is replaced with the character given by the entry in Table F.1 corresponding to the <code>LHS{"_"}Sign</code> Character.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>45_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>A <code>context{"_"}sensitive{"_"}insertion</code> Character is replaced as though it were a <code>direct{"_"}insertion</code> Character, if it occurs to the right of the leftmost <code>LHS{"_"}Sign</code> character replaced according to rule 1.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>46_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>4.</dt>
<dd>Any other Character is replaced by the space character.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>47_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>5.</dt>
<dd>A layout error occurs if some excess digits remain after replacement via rule 1; no edited output string is produced. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>48_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>fixed{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> maps to the Currency string with n space character values concatenated on the left (if the instance does not follow a <code>radix</code>) or on the right (if the instance does follow a <code>radix</code>), where n is the difference between the length of the <code>fixed{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> instance and Currency'Length. A layout error occurs if Currency'Length exceeds the length of the <code>fixed{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> instance; no edited output string is produced.<br /></p>

<MarginText>49_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>floating{"_"}{"$"}{"_"}currency</code> maps to the string obtained as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>50_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Up to all but one of the rightmost '{"$"}' Character values are replaced with the excess digits (if any) from the <i>integer{"_"}part</i> of the mapping of the <code>number</code> to the right of the <code>floating{"_"}{"$"}{"_"}currency</code> instance.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>51_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>The next Character to the left is replaced by the Currency string.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>52_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>A <code>context{"_"}sensitive{"_"}insertion</code> Character is replaced as though it were a <code>direct{"_"}insertion</code> Character, if it occurs to the right of the leftmost '{"$"}' Character replaced via rule 1.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>53_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>4.</dt>
<dd>Each other Character is replaced by the space character.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>54_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>5.</dt>
<dd>A layout error occurs if some excess digits remain after replacement by rule 1; no edited output string is produced. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>55_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>floating{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> maps to the string obtained as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>56_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>1.</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Up to all but one of the rightmost '{"#"}' Character values are replaced with the excess digits (if any) from the <i>integer{"_"}part</i> of the mapping of the <code>number</code> to the right of the <code>floating{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> instance.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>57_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>2.</dt>
<dd>The substring whose last Character occurs at the position immediately preceding the leftmost Character replaced via rule 1, and whose length is Currency'Length, is replaced by the Currency string.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>58_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>3.</dt>
<dd>A <code>context{"_"}sensitive{"_"}insertion</code> Character is replaced as though it were a <code>direct{"_"}insertion</code> Character, if it occurs to the right of the leftmost '{"#"}' replaced via rule 1.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>59_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>4.</dt>
<dd>Any other Character is replaced by the space character.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>60_F.3.2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>5.</dt>
<dd>A layout error occurs if some excess digits remain after replacement rule 1, or if there is no substring with the required length for replacement rule 2; no edited output string is produced. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>61_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>all{"_"}zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}number</code> maps to: <br /></p>

<MarginText>62_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a string of all spaces if the displayed magnitude of Item is zero, the <code>zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}char</code> is 'Z' or 'z', and the instance of <code>all{"_"}zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}number</code> does not have a <code>radix</code> at its last character position;<br /></li>
<MarginText>63_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>a string containing the Fill character in each position except for the character (if any) corresponding to <code>radix</code>, if <code>zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}char</code> = '{"*"}' and the displayed magnitude of Item is zero;<br /></li>
<MarginText>64_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, the same result as if each <code>zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}char</code> in <code>all{"_"}zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}aft</code> were '9', interpreting the instance of <code>all{"_"}zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}number</code> as either <code>zero{"_"}suppression</code> <code>number</code> (if a <code>radix</code> and <code>all{"_"}zero{"_"}suppression{"_"}aft</code> are present), or as <code>zero{"_"}suppression</code> otherwise. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>65_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number</code> maps to: <br /></p>

<MarginText>66_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a string of all spaces if the displayed magnitude of Item is zero and the instance of <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number</code> does not have a <code>radix</code> at its last character position;<br /></li>
<MarginText>67_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, the same result as if each <code>sign{"_"}char</code> in <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number{"_"}aft</code> were '9', interpreting the instance of <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number</code> as either <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code> <code>number</code> (if a <code>radix</code> and <code>all{"_"}sign{"_"}number{"_"}aft</code> are present), or as <code>floating{"_"}LHS{"_"}sign</code> otherwise. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>68_F.3.2</MarginText>
<p>An instance of <code>all{"_"}currency{"_"}number</code> maps to: <br /></p>

<MarginText>69_F.3.2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>a string of all spaces if the displayed magnitude of Item is zero and the instance of <code>all{"_"}currency{"_"}number</code> does not have a <code>radix</code> at its last character position;<br /></li>
<MarginText>70_F.3.2</MarginText>
<li>otherwise, the same result as if each <code>currency{"_"}char</code> in <code>all{"_"}currency{"_"}number{"_"}aft</code> were '9', interpreting the instance of <code>all{"_"}currency{"_"}number</code> as <code>floating{"_"}{"$"}{"_"}currency</code> <code>number</code> or <code>floating{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> <code>number</code> (if a <code>radix</code> and <code>all{"_"}currency{"_"}number{"_"}aft</code> are present), or as <code>floating{"_"}{"$"}{"_"}currency</code> or <code>floating{"_"}{"#"}{"_"}currency</code> otherwise. <br /></li>
</ul>

<a id="Subclause_F.3.3"></a>

## F.3.3  The Package Text_IO.Editing

<MarginText>1_F.3.3</MarginText>
<p>The package Text{"_"}IO.Editing provides a private type Picture with associated operations, and a generic package Decimal{"_"}Output. An object of type Picture is composed from a well-formed picture String (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-F/AA-F.3#Subclause_F.3.1">F.3.1</a>) and a Boolean item indicating whether a zero numeric value will result in an edited output string of all space characters. The package Decimal{"_"}Output contains edited output subprograms implementing the effects defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-F/AA-F.3#Subclause_F.3.2">F.3.2</a>. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2_F.3.3</MarginText>
<p>The library package Text{"_"}IO.Editing has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1", "AI12-0302-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package Ada.Text{"_"}IO.Editing{"\n"}   with Nonblocking, Global ={">"} in out synchronized is{"\n"}
<MarginText>4_F.3.3</MarginText>
   type Picture is private;{"\n"}
<MarginText>5_F.3.3</MarginText>
   function Valid (Pic{"_"}String      : in String;{"\n"}                   Blank{"_"}When{"_"}Zero : in Boolean := False) return Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>6_F.3.3</MarginText>
   function To{"_"}Picture (Pic{"_"}String      : in String;{"\n"}                        Blank{"_"}When{"_"}Zero : in Boolean := False){"\n"}      return Picture;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7_F.3.3</MarginText>
   function Pic{"_"}String      (Pic : in Picture) return String;{"\n"}   function Blank{"_"}When{"_"}Zero (Pic : in Picture) return Boolean;{"\n"}
<MarginText>8_F.3.3</MarginText>
   Max{"_"}Picture{"_"}Length  : constant := implementation{"_"}defined;{"\n"}
<MarginText>9_F.3.3</MarginText>

<MarginText>43_F.3.3</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure Put (To         : out String;{"\n"}               Item       : in Num;{"\n"}               Pic        : in Picture;{"\n"}               Currency   : in String    := Default{"_"}Currency;{"\n"}               Fill       : in Character := Default{"_"}Fill;{"\n"}               Separator  : in Character := Default{"_"}Separator;{"\n"}               Radix{"_"}Mark : in Character := Default{"_"}Radix{"_"}Mark);{"\n"}

<MarginText>44/3_F.3.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0264-1"]} />
<p class="Indented4">Put copies Image(Item, Pic, Currency, Fill, Separator, Radix{"_"}Mark) to the given string, right justified. Otherwise, unassigned Character values in To are assigned the space character. If To'Length is less than the length of the string resulting from Image, then Layout{"_"}Error is raised. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>45_F.3.3</MarginText>
<p>Max{"_"}Picture{"_"}Length shall be at least 30. The implementation shall support currency strings of length up to at least 10, both for Default{"_"}Currency in an instantiation of Decimal{"_"}Output, and for Currency in an invocation of Image or any of the Put procedures. <br /></p>

<MarginText>45.a_F.3.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This implies that a picture string with character replications need not be supported (i.e., To{"_"}Picture will raise Picture{"_"}Error) if its expanded form exceeds 30 characters. <br />

<MarginText>52.a/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0450-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The rules for edited output were based on the 1985 version of COBOL (ANSI X3.23:1985, endorsed by ISO as ISO 1989-1985), with the following differences: <br />

<MarginText>52.b/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The COBOL provisions for picture string localization and for 'P' format are absent from Ada.<br /></li>
<MarginText>52.c/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<li>The following Ada facilities are not in the 1985 version of COBOL: <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>52.d/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>currency symbol placement after the number;<br /></li>
<MarginText>52.e/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<li>localization of edited output string for multi-character currency string values, including support for both length-preserving and length-expanding currency symbols in picture strings;<br /></li>
<MarginText>52.f/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<li>localization of the radix mark, digits separator, and fill character; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>52.g/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<li>parenthesization of negative values. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>52.h/5_F.3.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0450-1"]} />
The value of 30 for Max{"_"}Picture{"_"}Length is the same limit as in COBOL. <br />

<MarginText>52.i_F.3.3</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>There are several reasons we have not adopted the COBOL-style permission to provide a single-character replacement in the picture string for the `{"$"}' as currency symbol, or to interchange the roles of `.' and `,' in picture strings <br />

<MarginText>52.j_F.3.3</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>It would have introduced considerable complexity into Ada, as well as confusion between run-time and compile-time character interpretation, since picture Strings are dynamically computable in Ada, in contrast with COBOL<br /></li>
<MarginText>52.k_F.3.3</MarginText>
<li>Ada's rules for real literals provide a natural interpretation of `{"_"}' as digits separator and `.' for radix mark; it is not essential to allow these to be localized in picture strings, since Ada does not allow them to be localized in real literals.<br /></li>
<MarginText>52.l_F.3.3</MarginText>
<li>The COBOL restriction for the currency symbol in a picture string to be replaced by a single character currency symbol is a compromise solution. For general international usage a mechanism is needed to localize the edited output to be a multi-character currency string. Allowing a single-Character localization for the picture Character, and a multiple-character localization for the currency string, would be an unnecessary complication. <br /></li>
<a id="Subclause_F.3.4"></a>
</ul>

## F.3.4  The Package Wide_Text_IO.Editing

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_F.3.4</MarginText>

<MarginText>2_F.3.4</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>each occurrence of Character is replaced by Wide{"_"}Character,<br /></li>
<MarginText>3_F.3.4</MarginText>
<li>each occurrence of Text{"_"}IO is replaced by Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO,<br /></li>
<MarginText>4_F.3.4</MarginText>
<li>the subtype of Default{"_"}Currency is Wide{"_"}String rather than String, and<br /></li>
<MarginText>5_F.3.4</MarginText>
<li>each occurrence of String in the generic package Decimal{"_"}Output is replaced by Wide{"_"}String. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.a_F.3.4</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The value of Max{"_"}Picture{"_"}Length in the package Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO.Editing<br />

<MarginText>6_F.3.4</MarginText>
NOTE   Each of the functions Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO.Editing.Valid, To{"_"}Picture, and Pic{"_"}String has String (versus Wide{"_"}String) as its parameter or result subtype, since a picture String is not localizable. <br />

# Annex F. Information Systems

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-F/AA-F.mdx

sidebar_position:  177

# Annex F. Information Systems

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>This Annex provides a set of facilities relevant to Information Systems programming. These fall into several categories: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>an attribute definition clause specifying Machine{"_"}Radix for a decimal subtype;<br /></li>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<li>the package Decimal, which declares a set of constants defining the implementation's capacity for decimal types, and a generic procedure for decimal division; and<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
<li>the child packages Text{"_"}IO.Editing, Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO.Editing, and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO.Editing, which support formatted and localized output of decimal data, based on &ldquo;picture String&rdquo; values. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01", "AI12-0449-1"]} />
<p>Other relevant facilities can be found in: <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.9">3.5.9</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.9">Fixed Point Types</a>&rdquo;; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.10">3.5.10</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.10">Operations of Fixed Point Types</a>&rdquo;; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">4.6</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.6">Type Conversions</a>&rdquo;; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">Operational and Representation Attributes</a>&rdquo;; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.10#Subclause_A.10.9">A.10.9</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.10#Subclause_A.10.9">Input-Output for Real Types</a>&rdquo;; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3">B.3</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3">Interfacing with C and C++</a>&rdquo;; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.4">B.4</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.4">Interfacing with COBOL</a>&rdquo;; <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/">Annex G</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/">Numerics</a>&rdquo;.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>The character and string handling packages in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Annex A</a>, &ldquo;<a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/">Predefined Language Environment</a>&rdquo; are also relevant for Information Systems. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>7/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If COBOL (respectively, C) is widely supported in the target environment, implementations supporting the Information Systems Annex should provide the child package Interfaces.COBOL (respectively, Interfaces.C) specified in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/">Annex B</a> and should support a <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of COBOL (respectively, C) for the Convention aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/">Annex B</a>), thus allowing Ada programs to interface with programs written in that language. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If COBOL (respectively, C) is supported in the target environment, then interfacing to COBOL (respectively, C) should be supported as specified in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/">Annex B</a>.<br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>7.b</MarginText>
This Annex is new to Ada 95. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>7.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
Added a mention of Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO.Editing, part of the support for 32-bit characters. <br />

# G.1. Complex Arithmetic

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.1.mdx

sidebar_position:  182

# G.1. Complex Arithmetic

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>Types and arithmetic operations for complex arithmetic are provided in Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, which is defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.1#Subclause_G.1.1">G.1.1</a>. Implementation-defined approximations to the complex analogs of the mathematical functions known as the &ldquo;elementary functions&rdquo; are provided by the subprograms in Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Elementary{"_"}Functions, which is defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.1#Subclause_G.1.2">G.1.2</a>. Both of these library units are generic children of the predefined package Numerics (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5">A.5</a>). Nongeneric equivalents of these generic packages for each of the predefined floating point types are also provided as children of Numerics. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The accuracy actually achieved by the complex elementary functions and by other complex arithmetic operations.<br />

<MarginText>1.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Complex arithmetic is defined in the Numerics Annex, rather than in the core, because it is considered to be a specialized need of (some) numeric applications. <br />

<a id="Subclause_G.1.1"></a>

## G.1.1  Complex Types

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>The generic library package Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types has the following declaration: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00126-01", "AI12-0241-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
{"{"}8652/0020{"}"} generic{"\n"}   type Real is digits {"<"}{">"};{"\n"}package Ada.Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types{"\n"}   with Pure, Nonblocking is{"\n"}
<MarginText>3_G.1.1</MarginText>
   type Complex is{"\n"}      record{"\n"}         Re, Im : Real'Base;{"\n"}      end record;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01", "AI95-0399-1"]} />
   type Imaginary is private{"\n"}      with Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization;{"\n"}
<MarginText>5_G.1.1</MarginText>

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>25/1_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00126-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0020</i>{"}"} The library package Numerics.Complex{"_"}Types is declared pure and defines the same types, constants, and subprograms as Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, except that the predefined type Float is systematically substituted for Real'Base throughout. Nongeneric equivalents of Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types for each of the other predefined floating point types are defined similarly, with the names Numerics.Short{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, Numerics.Long{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, etc. <br /></p>

<MarginText>25.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The nongeneric equivalents are provided to allow the programmer to construct simple mathematical applications without being required to understand and use generics. <br />

<MarginText>25.b_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The nongeneric equivalents all export the types Complex and Imaginary and the constants i and j (rather than uniquely named types and constants, such as Short{"_"}Complex, Long{"_"}Complex, etc.) to preserve their equivalence to actual instantiations of the generic package and to allow the programmer to change the precision of an application globally by changing a single context clause. <br />

<MarginText>25.c/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0241-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>A pure unit is always nonblocking, so we don't need to talk about the Nonblocking aspect of these packages. Similarly, a pure unit always has the Global aspect set to <b>null</b>, so we don't need to talk about that, either. <br />

<MarginText>26/2_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
<p>[Complex is a visible type with Cartesian components.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>26.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The Cartesian representation is far more common than the polar representation, in practice. The accuracy of the results of the complex arithmetic operations and of the complex elementary functions is dependent on the representation; thus, implementers need to know that representation. The type is visible so that complex &ldquo;literals&rdquo; can be written in aggregate notation, if desired. <br />

<MarginText>27_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>[Imaginary is a private type; its full type is derived from Real'Base.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>27.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The Imaginary type and the constants i and j are provided for two reasons: <br />

<MarginText>27.b_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>They allow complex &ldquo;literals&rdquo; to be written in the alternate form of <i>a</i> + <i>b</i>{"*"}i (or <i>a</i> + <i>b</i>{"*"}j), if desired. Of course, in some contexts the sum will need to be parenthesized.<br /></li>
<MarginText>27.c/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0437-1", "AI12-0453-1"]} />
<li>When an Ada binding to ISO/IEC 60559:2020 that provides (signed) infinities as the result of operations that overflow becomes available, it will be important to allow arithmetic between pure-imaginary and complex operands without requiring the former to be represented as (or promoted to) complex values with a real component of zero. For example, the multiplication of <i>a</i> + <i>b</i>{"*"}i by <i>d</i>{"*"}i should yield &ndash;<i>b</i>· <i>d</i> + <i>a</i>· <i>d</i>{"*"}i, but if one cannot avoid representing the pure-imaginary value <i>d</i>{"*"}i as the complex value 0.0 + <i>d</i>{"*"}i, then a NaN ("Not-a-Number") could be produced as the result of multiplying <i>a</i> by 0.0 (for example, when <i>a</i> is infinite); the NaN could later trigger an exception. Providing the Imaginary type and overloadings of the arithmetic operators for mixtures of Imaginary and Complex operands gives the programmer the same control over avoiding premature coercion of pure-imaginary values to complex as is already provided for pure-real values. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>27.d_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The Imaginary type is private, rather than being visibly derived from Real'Base, for two reasons: <br />

<MarginText>27.e_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>to preclude implicit conversions of real literals to the Imaginary type (such implicit conversions would make many common arithmetic expressions ambiguous); and<br /></li>
<MarginText>27.f_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>to suppress the implicit derivation of the multiplication, division, and absolute value operators with Imaginary operands and an Imaginary result (the result type would be incorrect). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>27.g/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0453-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The base subtype Real'Base is used for the component type of Complex, the parent type of Imaginary, and the parameter and result types of some of the subprograms to maximize the chances of being able to pass meaningful values into the subprograms and receive meaningful results back. The generic formal parameter Real therefore plays only one role, that of providing the precision to be maintained in complex arithmetic calculations. Thus, the subprograms in Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types share with those in Numerics.Generic{"_"}Elementary{"_"}Functions, and indeed even with the predefined arithmetic operations (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.5">4.5</a>), the property of being free of range checks on input and output, that is, of being able to exploit the base range of the relevant floating point type fully. As a result, the user loses the ability to impose application-oriented bounds on the range of values that the components of a complex variable can acquire; however, it can be argued that few, if any, applications have a naturally square domain (as opposed to a circular domain) anyway. <br />

<MarginText>28_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>The arithmetic operations and the Re, Im, Modulus, Argument, and Conjugate functions have their usual mathematical meanings. When applied to a parameter of pure-imaginary type, the &ldquo;imaginary-part&rdquo; function Im yields the value of its parameter, as the corresponding real value. The remaining subprograms have the following meanings: <br /></p>

<MarginText>28.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The middle case can be understood by considering the parameter of pure-imaginary type to represent a complex value with a zero real part. <br />

<MarginText>29_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The Set{"_"}Re and Set{"_"}Im procedures replace the designated component of a complex parameter with the given real value; applied to a parameter of pure-imaginary type, the Set{"_"}Im procedure replaces the value of that parameter with the imaginary value corresponding to the given real value.<br /></li>
<MarginText>30_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>The Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Cartesian function constructs a complex value from the given real and imaginary components. If only one component is given, the other component is implicitly zero.<br /></li>
<MarginText>31_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>The Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Polar function constructs a complex value from the given modulus (radius) and argument (angle). When the value of the parameter Modulus is positive (resp., negative), the result is the complex value represented by the point in the complex plane lying at a distance from the origin given by the absolute value of Modulus and forming an angle measured counterclockwise from the positive (resp., negative) real axis given by the value of the parameter Argument. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>32_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>When the Cycle parameter is specified, the result of the Argument function and the parameter Argument of the Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Polar function are measured in units such that a full cycle of revolution has the given value; otherwise, they are measured in radians.<br /></p>

<MarginText>33_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>The computed results of the mathematically multivalued functions are rendered single-valued by the following conventions, which are meant to imply the principal branch: <br /></p>

<MarginText>34_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The result of the Modulus function is nonnegative.<br /></li>
<MarginText>35_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>The result of the Argument function is in the quadrant containing the point in the complex plane represented by the parameter X. This may be any quadrant (I through IV); thus, the range of the Argument function is approximately &ndash;&pi; to &pi; (&ndash;Cycle/2.0 to Cycle/2.0, if the parameter Cycle is specified). When the point represented by the parameter X lies on the negative real axis, the result approximates <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>36_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>&pi; (resp., &ndash;&pi;) when the sign of the imaginary component of X is positive (resp., negative), if Real'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True;<br /></li>
<MarginText>37_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>&pi;, if Real'Signed{"_"}Zeros is False. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>38_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Because a result lying on or near one of the axes may not be exactly representable, the approximation inherent in computing the result may place it in an adjacent quadrant, close to but on the wrong side of the axis. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>39_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>The exception Numerics.Argument{"_"}Error is raised by the Argument and Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Polar functions with specified cycle, signaling a parameter value outside the domain of the corresponding mathematical function, when the value of the parameter Cycle is zero or negative.<br /></p>

<MarginText>40_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>The exception Constraint{"_"}Error is raised by the division operator when the value of the right operand is zero, and by the exponentiation operator when the value of the left operand is zero and the value of the exponent is negative, provided that Real'Machine{"_"}Overflows is True; when Real'Machine{"_"}Overflows is False, the result is unspecified. [Constraint{"_"}Error can also be raised when a finite result overflows (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.6">G.2.6</a>).] <br /></p>

<MarginText>40.a/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0437-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>It is anticipated that an Ada binding to ISO/IEC 60559:2020 will be developed in the future. As part of such a binding, the Machine{"_"}Overflows attribute of a conformant floating point type will be specified to yield False, which will permit implementations of the complex arithmetic operations to deliver results with an infinite component (and set the overflow flag defined by the binding) instead of raising Constraint{"_"}Error in overflow situations, when traps are disabled. Similarly, it is appropriate for the complex arithmetic operations to deliver results with infinite components (and set the zero-divide flag defined by the binding) instead of raising Constraint{"_"}Error in the situations defined above, when traps are disabled. Finally, such a binding should also specify the behavior of the complex arithmetic operations, when sensible, given operands with infinite components. <br />

#### Implementation Requirements

<MarginText>41_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>In the implementation of Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, the range of intermediate values allowed during the calculation of a final result shall not be affected by any range constraint of the subtype Real. <br /></p>

<MarginText>41.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>Implementations of Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types written in Ada should therefore avoid declaring local variables of subtype Real; the subtype Real'Base should be used instead. <br />

<MarginText>42_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>In the following cases, evaluation of a complex arithmetic operation shall yield the <i>prescribed result</i>, provided that the preceding rules do not call for an exception to be raised: <br /></p>

<MarginText>43_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The results of the Re, Im, and Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Cartesian functions are exact.<br /></li>
<MarginText>44_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>The real (resp., imaginary) component of the result of a binary addition operator that yields a result of complex type is exact when either of its operands is of pure-imaginary (resp., real) type. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>44.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The result of the addition operator is exact when one of its operands is of real type and the other is of pure-imaginary type. In this particular case, the operator is analogous to the Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Cartesian function; it performs no arithmetic. <br />

<MarginText>45_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The real (resp., imaginary) component of the result of a binary subtraction operator that yields a result of complex type is exact when its right operand is of pure-imaginary (resp., real) type.<br /></li>
<MarginText>46_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>The real component of the result of the Conjugate function for the complex type is exact.<br /></li>
<MarginText>47_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>When the point in the complex plane represented by the parameter X lies on the nonnegative real axis, the Argument function yields a result of zero. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>47.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Argument(X + i{"*"}Y) is analogous to <i>EF</i>.Arctan(Y, X), where <i>EF</i> is an appropriate instance of Numerics.Generic{"_"}Elementary{"_"}Functions, except when X and Y are both zero, in which case the former yields the value zero while the latter raises Numerics.Argument{"_"}Error. <br />

<MarginText>48_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>When the value of the parameter Modulus is zero, the Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Polar function yields a result of zero.<br /></li>
<MarginText>49_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>When the value of the parameter Argument is equal to a multiple of the quarter cycle, the result of the Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Polar function with specified cycle lies on one of the axes. In this case, one of its components is zero, and the other has the magnitude of the parameter Modulus.<br /></li>
<MarginText>50_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>Exponentiation by a zero exponent yields the value one. Exponentiation by a unit exponent yields the value of the left operand. Exponentiation of the value one yields the value one. Exponentiation of the value zero yields the value zero, provided that the exponent is nonzero. When the left operand is of pure-imaginary type, one component of the result of the exponentiation operator is zero. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>51_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>When the result, or a result component, of any operator of Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types has a mathematical definition in terms of a single arithmetic or relational operation, that result or result component exhibits the accuracy of the corresponding operation of the type Real.<br /></p>

<MarginText>52_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>Other accuracy requirements for the Modulus, Argument, and Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Polar functions, and accuracy requirements for the multiplication of a pair of complex operands or for division by a complex operand, all of which apply only in the strict mode, are given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.6">G.2.6</a>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>53_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>The sign of a zero result or zero result component yielded by a complex arithmetic operation or function is implementation defined when Real'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True. <br /></p>

<MarginText>53.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-defined">
<b></b>The sign of a zero result (or a component thereof) from any operator or function in Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, when Real'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>54/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0444-1"]} />
<p>The nongeneric equivalent packages can be actual instantiations of the generic package for the appropriate predefined type, though that is not required.<br /></p>

<MarginText>55/2_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00434-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0091</i>{"}"} Implementations may obtain the result of exponentiation of a complex or pure-imaginary operand by repeated complex multiplication, with arbitrary association of the factors and with a possible final complex reciprocation (when the exponent is negative). Implementations are also permitted to obtain the result of exponentiation of a complex operand, but not of a pure-imaginary operand, by converting the left operand to a polar representation; exponentiating the modulus by the given exponent; multiplying the argument by the given exponent; and reconverting to a Cartesian representation. Because of this implementation freedom, no accuracy requirement is imposed on complex exponentiation (except for the prescribed results given above, which apply regardless of the implementation method chosen). <br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>56/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0437-1"]} />
<p>Because the usual mathematical meaning of multiplication of a complex operand and a real operand is that of the scaling of both components of the former by the latter, an implementation should not perform this operation by first promoting the real operand to complex type and then performing a full complex multiplication. In systems that, in the future, support an Ada binding to ISO/IEC 60559:2020, the latter technique will not generate the required result when one of the components of the complex operand is infinite. (Explicit multiplication of the infinite component by the zero component obtained during promotion yields a NaN that propagates into the final result.) Analogous advice applies in the case of multiplication of a complex operand and a pure-imaginary operand, and in the case of division of a complex operand by a real or pure-imaginary operand. <br /></p>

<MarginText>56.a/2_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>Mixed real and complex operations (as well as pure-imaginary and complex operations) should not be performed by converting the real (resp. pure-imaginary) operand to complex.<br />

<MarginText>57/5_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0437-1"]} />
<p>Likewise, because the usual mathematical meaning of addition of a complex operand and a real operand is that the imaginary operand remains unchanged, an implementation should not perform this operation by first promoting the real operand to complex type and then performing a full complex addition. In implementations in which the Signed{"_"}Zeros attribute of the component type is True (and which therefore conform to ISO/IEC 60559:2020 in regard to the handling of the sign of zero in predefined arithmetic operations), the latter technique will not generate the required result when the imaginary component of the complex operand is a negatively signed zero. (Explicit addition of the negative zero to the zero obtained during promotion yields a positive zero.) Analogous advice applies in the case of addition of a complex operand and a pure-imaginary operand, and in the case of subtraction of a complex operand and a real or pure-imaginary operand.<br /></p>

<MarginText>58_G.1.1</MarginText>
<p>Implementations in which Real'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True should attempt to provide a rational treatment of the signs of zero results and result components. As one example, the result of the Argument function should have the sign of the imaginary component of the parameter X when the point represented by that parameter lies on the positive real axis; as another, the sign of the imaginary component of the Compose{"_"}From{"_"}Polar function should be the same as (resp., the opposite of) that of the Argument parameter when that parameter has a value of zero and the Modulus parameter has a nonnegative (resp., negative) value. <br /></p>

<MarginText>58.a.1/3_G.1.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>If Real'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True for Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, a rational treatment of the signs of zero results and result components should be provided.<br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>58.a_G.1.1</MarginText>
The semantics of Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types differs from Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types as defined in ISO/IEC CD 13813 (for Ada 83) in the following ways: <br />

<MarginText>58.b_G.1.1</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The generic package is a child of the package defining the Argument{"_"}Error exception.<br /></li>
<MarginText>58.c_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>The nongeneric equivalents export types and constants with the same names as those exported by the generic package, rather than with names unique to the package.<br /></li>
<MarginText>58.d_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>Implementations are not allowed to impose an optional restriction that the generic actual parameter associated with Real be unconstrained. (In view of the ability to declare variables of subtype Real'Base in implementations of Numerics.Generic{"_"}Complex{"_"}Types, this flexibility is no longer needed.)<br /></li>
<MarginText>58.e_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>The dependence of the Argument function on the sign of a zero parameter component is tied to the value of Real'Signed{"_"}Zeros.<br /></li>
<MarginText>58.f_G.1.1</MarginText>
<li>Conformance to accuracy requirements is conditional. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>58.g/2_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00161-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> Added a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization to type Imaginary, so that it can be used in preelaborated units. <br />

<MarginText>58.h/2_G.1.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00126-01"]} />
