# Annex H. High Integrity Systems

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-H/AA-H.mdx

sidebar_position:  185

# Annex H. High Integrity Systems

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00347-01"]} />
<p>This Annex addresses requirements for high integrity systems (including safety-critical systems and security-critical systems). It provides facilities and specifies documentation requirements that relate to several needs: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Understanding program execution;<br /></li>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<li>Reviewing object code;<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0439-1"]} />
<li>Restricting language constructs whose usage can complicate the demonstration of program correctness <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4.1</MarginText>
<p>Execution understandability is supported by pragma Normalize{"_"}Scalars, and also by requirements for the implementation to document the effect of a program in the presence of a bounded error or where the language rules leave the effect unspecified. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Reviewable and Restrictions relate to the other requirements addressed by this Annex. <br /></p>

<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE   The Valid attribute (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.9#Subclause_13.9.2">13.9.2</a>) is also useful in addressing these needs, to avoid problems that can otherwise arise from scalars that have values outside their declared range constraints.<br />

<MarginText>6.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The Annex tries to provide high assurance rather than language features. However, it is not possible, in general, to test for high assurance. For any specific language feature, it is possible to demonstrate its presence by a functional test, as in the ACVC. One can also check for the presence of some documentation requirements, but it is not easy to determine objectively that the documentation is &ldquo;adequate&rdquo;. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>6.b</MarginText>
This Annex is new to Ada 95. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>6.c/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00347-01"]} />
The title of this annex was changed to better reflect its purpose and scope. High integrity systems has become the standard way of identifying systems that have high reliability requirements; it subsumes terms such as safety and security. Moreover, the annex does not include any security specific features and as such the previous title is somewhat misleading. <br />

---

<MarginText>1</MarginText>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>

with Ada.Unchecked{"_"}Conversion;{"\n"}generic function Unchecked{"_"}Conversion renames Ada.Unchecked{"_"}Conversion;{"\n"}

<MarginText>4</MarginText>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
with Ada.Text{"_"}IO;{"\n"}package Text{"_"}IO renames Ada.Text{"_"}IO;{"\n"}
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
with Ada.IO{"_"}Exceptions;{"\n"}package IO{"_"}Exceptions renames Ada.IO{"_"}Exceptions;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

<MarginText>10</MarginText>

# J.10. Specific Suppression of Checks

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.10.mdx

sidebar_position:  203

# J.10. Specific Suppression of Checks

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01"]} />
<p>Pragma Suppress can be used to suppress checks on specific entities. <br /></p>

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a specific Suppress <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/2</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Suppress(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, [On ={">"}] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> shall be the name of a check (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.5">11.5</a>). The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall statically denote some entity.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01"]} />
<p>For a specific Suppress <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> that is immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall denote an entity (or several overloaded subprograms) declared immediately within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package{"_"}specification</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01"]} />
<p>A specific Suppress <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies to the named check from the place of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> to the end of the innermost enclosing declarative region, or, if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> is given in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, to the end of the scope of the named entity. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies only to the named entity, or, for a subtype, on objects and values of its type. A specific Suppress <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> suppresses the named check for any entities to which it applies (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.5">11.5</a>). Which checks are associated with a specific entity is not defined by this document.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>The language doesn't specify exactly which entities control whether a check is performed. For example, in <br />

<MarginText>6.b</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
pragma Suppress (Range{"_"}Check, On ={">"} A);{"\n"}A := B;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>6.c</MarginText>
whether or not the range check is performed is not specified. The compiler may require that checks are suppressed on B or on the type of A in order to omit the range check. <br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01"]} />
<p>An implementation is allowed to place restrictions on specific Suppress <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s. <br /></p>

<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE   An implementation can support a similar On parameter on <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Unsuppress (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.5">11.5</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>8.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00224-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. This feature was moved here because it is important for pragma Unsuppress that there be an unambiguous meaning for each checking pragma. For instance, in the example <br />

<MarginText>8.b</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
pragma Suppress (Range{"_"}Check);{"\n"}pragma Unsuppress (Range{"_"}Check, On ={">"} A);{"\n"}A := B;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>8.c</MarginText>
the user needs to be able to depend on the range check being made on the assignment. But a compiler survey showed that the interpretation of this feature varied widely; trying to define this carefully was likely to cause a lot of user and implementer pain. Thus the feature was moved here, to emphasize that its use is not portable. <br />

---

# J.11. The Class Attribute of Untagged Incomplete Types

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.11.mdx

sidebar_position:  204

# J.11. The Class Attribute of Untagged Incomplete Types

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<p>For the first subtype S of a type <i>T</i> declared by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code> that is not tagged, the following attribute is defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<dt><br/>S'Class </dt>
<dl>
<dd>Denotes the first subtype of the incomplete class-wide type rooted at <i>T</i>. The completion of <i>T</i> shall declare a tagged type. Such an attribute reference shall occur in the same library unit as the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#S0085">incomplete_type_declaration</a></code>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>2.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This must occur in the same unit to prevent children from imposing requirements on their ancestor library units for deferred incomplete types. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>2.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. This feature was moved here because the tagged incomplete type provides a better way to provide this capability (it doesn't put requirements on the completion based on uses that could be anywhere). Pity we didn't think of it in 1994. <br />

---

# J.12. Pragma Interface

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.12.mdx

sidebar_position:  205

# J.12. Pragma Interface

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00284-02"]} />
<p class="Indented2">In addition to an identifier, the reserved word <b>interface</b> is allowed as a pragma name, to provide compatibility with a prior edition of this Reference Manual. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00284-02"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-note">
<b></b>All implementations need to at least recognize and ignore this pragma. A syntax error is not an acceptable implementation of this pragma. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>1.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00326-01", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. This is necessary as <b>interface</b> is now a reserved word, which would prevent pragma Interface from being an implementation-defined pragma. We don't define any semantics for this pragma, as we expect that implementations will continue to use whatever they currently implement - requiring any changes would be counter-productive. <br />

# J.15. Aspect-related Pragmas

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.15.mdx

sidebar_position:  208

# J.15. Aspect-related Pragmas

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>Pragmas can be used as an alternative to aspect{"_"}specifications to specify certain aspects. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>2/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>Certain <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s are defined to be <i>program unit pragmas</i>. A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> given as the argument of a program unit pragma shall resolve to denote the declarations or renamings of one or more program units that occur immediately within the declarative region or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0285">compilation</a></code> in which the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> immediately occurs, or it shall resolve to denote the declaration of the immediately enclosing program unit (if any); the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies to the denoted program unit(s). If there are no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>s given as arguments, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies to the immediately enclosing program unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The fact that this is a Name Resolution Rule means that the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> will not apply to declarations from outer declarative regions. <br />

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>A program unit pragma shall appear in one of these places: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>At the place of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0286">compilation_unit</a></code>, in which case the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> shall immediately follow in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0285">compilation</a></code> (except for other <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s) a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library{"_"}unit{"_"}declaration</a></code> that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0311">generic{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic{"_"}instantiation</a></code>, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> shall have an argument that is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> denoting that declaration. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>4.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> has to denote the immediately preceding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0288">library_unit_declaration</a></code>. <br />

<MarginText>5/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00136-01", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>{"{"}<i>8652/0033</i>{"}"} Immediately within the visible part of a program unit and before any nested declaration (but not within a generic formal part), in which case the argument, if any, shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> that denotes the immediately enclosing program unit declaration. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>The argument is optional in this case. <br />

<MarginText>6/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<ul>
<li>At the place of a declaration other than the first, of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> or program unit declaration, in which case the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> shall have an argument, which shall be a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> that denotes one or more of the following (and nothing else): a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0311">generic{"_"}subprogram{"_"}declaration</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3#S0315">generic{"_"}instantiation</a></code>, of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative{"_"}part</a></code> or program unit declaration. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>6.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>If you want to denote a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> that is not a completion, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code>, for example, you have to put the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> inside. <br />

<MarginText>7/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0132-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>Certain program unit pragmas are defined to be <i>library unit pragmas</i>. If a library unit pragma applies to a program unit, the program unit shall be a library unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>This, together with the rules for program unit pragmas above, implies that if a library unit pragma applies to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code> (and similar things), it has to appear immediately after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0286">compilation_unit</a></code>, whereas if the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0229">package_declaration</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> that is not a completion (and similar things), it has to appear inside, as the first <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0087">declarative_item</a></code>. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>8/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00041-01", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0034</i>{"}"} A library unit pragma that applies to a generic unit does not apply to its instances, unless a specific rule for the pragma specifies the contrary. <br /></p>

#### Implementation Advice

<MarginText>9/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00041-01", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0034</i>{"}"} When applied to a generic unit, a program unit pragma that is not a library unit pragma should apply to each instance of the generic unit for which there is not an overriding pragma applied directly to the instance. <br /></p>

<MarginText>9.a/5</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="implementation-advice">
<b></b>When applied to a generic unit, a program unit pragma that is not a library unit pragma should apply to each instance of the generic unit for which there is not an overriding pragma applied directly to the instance.<br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>9.b/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Many existing pragmas have been converted into aspects; the pragmas have moved here.<br />

<MarginText>9.c/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0132-1", "AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> A library unit pragma must apply directly to a library unit, even if no name is given in the pragma. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>9.d/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
The terms &ldquo;program unit pragma&rdquo; and &ldquo;library unit pragma&rdquo; were moved here as all of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s that use these terms are now in this annex. <br />

<a id="Subclause_J.15.1"></a>

## J.15.1  Pragma Inline

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Inline, which is a program unit pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#Subclause_10.1.5">10.1.5</a>), is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Inline (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"{"}, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>{"}"}); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> shall apply to one or more callable entities or generic subprograms. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Inline specifies that the Inline aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.2">6.3.2</a>) for each entity denoted by each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> has the value True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>4.a/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Note that inline expansion is desired no matter what <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> is used in the call. This allows one to request inlining for only one of several overloaded subprograms as follows:<br />

<MarginText>4.b/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
package IO is{"\n"}   procedure Put(X : in Integer);{"\n"}   procedure Put(X : in String);{"\n"}   procedure Put(X : in Character);{"\n"}private{"\n"}   procedure Character{"_"}Put(X : in Character) renames Put;{"\n"}   pragma Inline(Character{"_"}Put);{"\n"}end IO;{"\n"}
<MarginText>4.c/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
with IO; use IO;{"\n"}procedure Main is{"\n"}   I : Integer;{"\n"}   C : Character;{"\n"}begin{"\n"}   ...{"\n"}   Put(C); -- Inline expansion is desired.{"\n"}   Put(I); -- Inline expansion is NOT desired.{"\n"}end Main;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An implementation may allow a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Inline that has an argument which is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> denoting a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> of the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>This is allowed for Ada 83 compatibility. This is only a permission as this usage was considered obsolescent even for Ada 95. <br />

<MarginText>5.b/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>We only need to allow this in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>s, because a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0089">body</a></code> is only allowed in another <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0089">body</a></code>, and these all have <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>s. <br />

<MarginText>6/5_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0440-1"]} />
NOTE   The name in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Inline can denote more than one entity in the case of overloading. Such a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> applies to all of the denoted entities. <br />

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 83

<MarginText>6.a/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00309-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
A pragma Inline cannot refer to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> outside of that body. The pragma can be given inside of the subprogram body. Ada 2005 adds an Implementation Permission to allow this usage for compatibility (and Ada 95 implementations also can use this permission), but implementations do not have to allow such <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>6.b/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Inline is allowed inside a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code> if there is no corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#S0195">subprogram_declaration</a></code>. This is for uniformity with other program unit pragmas. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 95

<MarginText>6.c/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00309-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b>Amendment </b> Implementations are allowed to let <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Inline apply to a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>6.d/3_J.15.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragma Inline was moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#Subclause_6.3.2">6.3.2</a>; aspect Inline lives there now. <br />

## J.15.2  Pragma No_Return

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> No{"_"}Return, which is a representation pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>), is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/5_J.15.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> No{"_"}Return (<i>subprogram{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>{"{"}, <i>subprogram{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>{"}"}); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/5_J.15.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p>Each <i>subprogram{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> shall denote one or more subprograms or generic subprograms. [The <i>subprogram{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> shall not denote a null procedure nor an instance of a generic unit.] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>4/5_J.15.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0269-1"]} />
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> No{"_"}Return specifies that the No{"_"}Return aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#Subclause_6.5.1">6.5.1</a>) for each subprogram denoted by each <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> has the value True. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>4.a/3_J.15.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragma No{"_"}Return was moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#Subclause_6.5.1">6.5.1</a>; aspect No{"_"}Return lives there now. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>4.b/5_J.15.2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0269-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragma No{"_"}Return was moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.5#Subclause_6.5.1">6.5.1</a>; aspect No{"_"}Return lives there now. <br />

## J.15.3  Pragma Pack

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Pack, which is a representation pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>), is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.3</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Pack (<i>first{"_"}subtype{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <i>first{"_"}subtype{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Pack shall denote a composite subtype. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Pack specifies that the Pack aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.2">13.2</a>) for the type denoted by <i>first{"_"}subtype{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> has the value True. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>4.a/3_J.15.3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragma Pack was moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.2">13.2</a>; aspect Pack lives there now. <br />

## J.15.4  Pragma Storage_Size

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Storage{"_"}Size is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.4</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Storage{"_"}Size (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Storage{"_"}Size is allowed only immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Storage{"_"}Size is expected to be of any integer type. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Storage{"_"}Size sets the Storage{"_"}Size aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>) of the type defined by the immediately enclosing <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code> to the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>5.a/3_J.15.4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragma Storage{"_"}Size was moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>; aspect Storage{"_"}Size lives there now. <br />

<a id="Subclause_J.15.5"></a>

## J.15.5  Interfacing Pragmas

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">An <i>interfacing pragma</i> is a representation pragma that is one of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Import, Export, or Convention. Their forms are as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Import(<br />     [Convention ={">"}] <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, [Entity ={">"}] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code><br />  [, [External{"_"}Name ={">"}] <i>external{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]<br />  [, [Link{"_"}Name ={">"}] <i>link{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]);<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Export(<br />     [Convention ={">"}] <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>, [Entity ={">"}] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code><br />  [, [External{"_"}Name ={">"}] <i>external{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]<br />  [, [Link{"_"}Name ={">"}] <i>link{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>]);<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Convention([Convention ={">"}] <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>,[Entity ={">"}] <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">For <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s Import and Export, the argument for Link{"_"}Name shall not be given without the <i>pragma{"_"}argument{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> unless the argument for External{"_"}Name is given. <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>6/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p> The expected type for an <i>external{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and a <i>link{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in an interfacing pragma is String. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code> of an interfacing pragma shall be the name of a convention (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import shall be the completion of a declaration. Notwithstanding any rule to the contrary, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import may serve as the completion of any kind of (explicit) declaration if supported by an implementation for that kind of declaration. If a completion is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import, then it shall appear in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code> as the declaration. For a library unit, it shall appear in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0285">compilation</a></code>, before any subsequent <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0286">compilation_unit</a></code>s other than <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> denotes more than one entity, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import is the completion of all of them.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <i>external{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> and <i>link{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import or Export shall be static.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> of each of these pragmas shall denote a declaration that may have the similarly named aspect specified. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>11/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>An interfacing pragma specifies various aspects of the entity denoted by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>12/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The Convention aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>) is <i>convention{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.3#S0002">identifier</a></code>.<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import specifies that the Import aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>) is True.<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<li>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Export specifies that the Export aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>) is True.<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<li>For both <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Import and Export, if an external name is given in the pragma, the External{"_"}Name aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>) is specified to be <i>external{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. If a link name is given in the pragma, the Link{"_"}Name aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>) is specified to be the <i>link{"_"}name{"_"}string{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. <br /></li>
</ul>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>15.a/3_J.15.5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragmas Import, Export, and Convention were moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>; aspects Import, Export, Convention, Link{"_"}Name, and External{"_"}Name live there now. <br />

<a id="Subclause_J.15.6"></a>

## J.15.6  Pragma Unchecked_Union

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Unchecked{"_"}Union, which is a representation pragma (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>), is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.6</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Unchecked{"_"}Union (<i>first{"_"}subtype{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>); <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <i>first{"_"}subtype{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Unchecked{"_"}Union shall denote an unconstrained discriminated record subtype having a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0071">variant_part</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Unchecked{"_"}Union specifies that the Unchecked{"_"}Union aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3#Subclause_B.3.3">B.3.3</a>) for the type denoted by <i>first{"_"}subtype{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> has the value True. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>4.a/3_J.15.6</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragma Unchecked{"_"}Union was moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3#Subclause_B.3.3">B.3.3</a>; aspect Unchecked{"_"}Union lives there now. <br />

<a id="Subclause_J.15.7"></a>

## J.15.7  Pragmas Interrupt_Handler and Attach_Handler

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Interrupt{"_"}Handler is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Interrupt{"_"}Handler (<i>handler{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Attach{"_"}Handler is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Attach{"_"}Handler (<i>handler{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>); <br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For the Interrupt{"_"}Handler and Attach{"_"}Handler pragmas, the <i>handler{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> shall resolve to denote a protected procedure with a parameterless profile.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For the Attach{"_"}Handler pragma, the expected type for the expression is Interrupts.Interrupt{"_"}Id (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.2">C.3.2</a>). <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>7/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0033-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The Attach{"_"}Handler and Interrupt{"_"}Handler pragmas are only allowed immediately within the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code> where the corresponding subprogram is declared. The corresponding <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0249">protected_type_declaration</a></code> or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single_protected_declaration</a></code> shall be a library-level declaration, and shall not be declared within a generic body. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>In the case of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0249">protected_type_declaration</a></code>, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code> of an object of that type need not be at library level.<br />

<MarginText>7.b/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0033-1"]} />
We cannot allow these pragmas in a generic body, because legality rules are not checked for instance bodies, and these should not be allowed if the instance is not at the library level. The protected types can be declared in the private part if this is desired. Note that while the 'Access to use the handler would provide the check in the case of Interrupt{"_"}Handler, there is no other check for Attach{"_"}Handler. Since these pragmas are so similar, we want the rules to be the same. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>8/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For an implementation that supports Annex C, a pragma Interrupt{"_"}Handler specifies the Interrupt{"_"}Handler aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>) for the protected procedure <i>handler{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> to have the value True. For an implementation that supports Annex C, a pragma Attach{"_"}Handler specifies the Attach{"_"}Handler aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>) for the protected procedure <i>handler{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code> to have the value of the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>[ as evaluated at object creation time]. <br /></p>

#### Incompatibilities With Ada 2005

<MarginText>8.a/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0033-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="correction">
<b></b> Added missing generic contract wording for the pragma Attach{"_"}Handler and Interrupt{"_"}Handler. This means that nested instances with these pragmas in the private part are now illegal. This is not likely to occur in practice. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>8.b/3_J.15.7</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragmas Interrupt{"_"}Handler and Attach{"_"}Handler were moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>; aspects Interrupt{"_"}Handler and Attach{"_"}Handler live there now. <br />

<a id="Subclause_J.15.8"></a>

## J.15.8  Shared Variable Pragmas

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/5_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0425-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The following <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s are defined with the given forms: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Atomic (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Volatile (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Independent (<i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Atomic{"_"}Components (<i>array{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Volatile{"_"}Components (<i>array{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Independent{"_"}Components (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Pragmas Independent and Independent{"_"}Components are born obsolescent; they are defined to provide consistency with the existing shared variable pragmas. As with all obsolescent features, these pragmas are not optional; all Ada implementations need to implement them. Also note that these pragmas were defined as a <b>Correction</b>; as such, they are expected to be implemented as part of Ada 2005 implementations (and they would not be obsolescent there). <br />

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>8/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> in an Atomic or Volatile pragma shall resolve to denote either an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.3#S0032">object_declaration</a></code>, a noninherited <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>, or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0024">full_type_declaration</a></code>. The <i>component{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> in an Independent pragma shall resolve to denote a noninherited <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.8#S0070">component_declaration</a></code>. The <i>array{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> in an Atomic{"_"}Components or Volatile{"_"}Components pragma shall resolve to denote the declaration of an array type or an array object of an anonymous type. The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> in an Independent{"_"}Components pragma shall resolve to denote the declaration of an array or record type or an array object of an anonymous type. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>9/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>These <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s are representation pragmas (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1">13.1</a>). Each of these <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s specifies that the similarly named aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>) of the type, object, or component denoted by its argument is True. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>10/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0345">local_name</a></code> of each of these <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s shall denote a declaration that may have the similarly named aspect specified. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>10.a/3_J.15.8</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. These pragmas were moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>; various aspects live there now. <br />

## J.15.9  Pragma CPU

<MarginText>0.a/3_J.15.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This pragma is born obsolescent; it is defined to provide consistency with existing real-time pragmas. As with all obsolescent features, this pragma is not optional; all Ada implementations need to implement it. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> CPU is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.9</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> CPU (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>);<br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> CPU is System.Multiprocessors.CPU{"_"}Range. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/5_J.15.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0281-1"]} />
<p>A CPU pragma is allowed only immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code>, or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For a CPU pragma that appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall be static. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>6/5_J.15.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI12-0281-1"]} />
<p>For an implementation that supports Annex D, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> CPU specifies the value of the CPU aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.16">D.16</a>). If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> appears in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the task type or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single_task_declaration</a></code> that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>. If the pragma appears in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the protected type or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single_protected_declaration</a></code> that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>. Otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the subprogram that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Extensions to Ada 2005

<MarginText>6.a/3_J.15.9</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0009-1"]} />
Pragma CPU is new. <br />

## J.15.11  Pragmas Priority and Interrupt_Priority

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Priority (<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Interrupt{"_"}Priority is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Interrupt{"_"}Priority [(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>);]<br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in a Priority or Interrupt{"_"}Priority pragma is Integer. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>6/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>A Priority pragma is allowed only immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code>, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code>, or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. An Interrupt{"_"}Priority pragma is allowed only immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For a Priority pragma that appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> shall be static, and its value shall be in the range of System.Priority. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>8/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For an implementation that supports Annex D, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Priority specifies the value of the Priority aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>) and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Interrupt{"_"}Priority specifies the value of the Interrupt{"_"}Priority aspect as follows:<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> appears in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the task type or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single_task_declaration</a></code> that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> appears in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0251">protected_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the protected type or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.4#S0250">single_protected_declaration</a></code> that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>;<br /></li>
<MarginText>11/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<li>If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> appears in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the subprogram that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>.<br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>12/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>If there is no <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> in an Interrupt{"_"}Priority pragma, the Interrupt{"_"}Priority aspect has the value Interrupt{"_"}Priority'Last. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>12.a/3_J.15.11</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
This subclause is new. Pragmas Interrupt{"_"}Priority and Priority were moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>; aspects Interrupt{"_"}Priority and Priority live there now. <br />

## J.15.12  Pragma Relative_Deadline

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1/3_J.15.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The form of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Relative{"_"}Deadline is as follows: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3_J.15.12</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Relative{"_"}Deadline (<i>relative{"_"}deadline{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>);<br /></p>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/3_J.15.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>The expected type for a <i>relative{"_"}deadline{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is Real{"_"}Time.Time{"_"}Span. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/3_J.15.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>A Relative{"_"}Deadline pragma is allowed only immediately within a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code> or the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.11#S0086">declarative_part</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.3#S0216">subprogram_body</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>5/3_J.15.12</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<p>For an implementation that supports Annex D, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Relative{"_"}Deadline specifies the value of the Relative{"_"}Deadline aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.6">D.2.6</a>). If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> appears in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0246">task_definition</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the task type or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.1#S0245">single_task_declaration</a></code> that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>; otherwise, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> is associated with the aspect for the subprogram that contains the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

## J.15.14  Elaboration Control Pragmas

<MarginText>1/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>This subclause defines pragmas that specify aspects that help control the elaboration order of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s.<br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>Pragmas that do not have associated aspects still appear in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>. These pragmas are presented in the order that the aspects are defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2">The following <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code>s are defined with the given forms: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Preelaborate[(<i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>)];<br /></p>

<MarginText>4/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization(<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code>);<br /></p>

<MarginText>5/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Pure[(<i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>)];<br /></p>

<MarginText>6/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">  <b>pragma</b> Elaborate{"_"}Body[(<i>library{"_"}unit{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0091">name</a></code>)];<br /></p>

<MarginText>7/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p class="Indented2"><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code>s Preelaborate, Pure, and Elaborate{"_"}Body are library unit pragmas. <br /></p>

<MarginText>7.a/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization is <b>not</b> a library unit pragma. <br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>8/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Preelaborate specifies that a library unit is preelaborated, namely that the Preelaborate aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>) of the library unit is True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Pure specifies that a library unit is declared pure, namely that the Pure aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>) of the library unit is True.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0417-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Elaborate{"_"}Body specifies that [a library unit requires a completion, namely that] the Elaborate{"_"}Body aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>) of the library unit is True. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>11/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">pragma</a></code> Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization specifies that the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>) for a composite type is True. This pragma shall appear in the visible part of a package or generic package.<br /></p>

<MarginText>12/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>If the pragma appears in the first declaration list of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.1#S0230">package_specification</a></code>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> shall denote the first subtype of a composite type, and the type shall be declared immediately within the same package as the pragma. The composite type shall be one for which the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect can be directly specified as True. In addition to the places where Legality Rules normally apply (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.3">12.3</a>), these rules also apply in the private part of an instance of a generic unit.<br /></p>

<MarginText>13/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
<p>If the pragma appears in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code>, then the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> shall denote a type declared in the same <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.1#S0313">generic_formal_part</a></code> as the pragma, and be one for which the Preelaborable{"_"}Initialization aspect can be directly specified as True. <br /></p>

<MarginText>14/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
NOTE   Pragmas Elaborate and Elaborate{"_"}All, which do not have associated aspects, are found in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>14.a/5_J.15.14</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0409-1"]} />
This subclause is new. These pragmas were moved here from <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>. <br />

# J.2. Allowed Replacements of Characters

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  195

# J.2. Allowed Replacements of Characters

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">The following replacements are allowed for the vertical line, number sign, and quotation mark characters: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>A vertical line character (|) can be replaced by an exclamation mark (!) where used as a delimiter.<br /></li>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<li>The number sign characters ({"#"}) of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.4#S0011">based_literal</a></code> can be replaced by colons (:) provided that the replacement is done for both occurrences. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>3.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00285-01"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>The intent is that such a replacement works in the Value, Wide{"_"}Value, and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value attributes, and in the Get procedures of Text{"_"}IO (and Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO and Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Text{"_"}IO as well){"}"}, so that things like &ldquo;16:.123:&rdquo; is acceptable. <br />

<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The quotation marks (") used as string brackets at both ends of a string literal can be replaced by percent signs (%) provided that the enclosed sequence of characters contains no quotation mark, and provided that both string brackets are replaced. Any percent sign within the sequence of characters shall then be doubled and each such doubled percent sign is interpreted as a single percent sign character value. <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p class="Indented2">These replacements do not change the meaning of the program. <br /></p>

<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The original purpose of this feature was to support hardware (for example, teletype machines) that has long been obsolete. The feature is no longer necessary for that reason. Another use of the feature has been to replace the vertical line character (|) when using certain hardware that treats that character as a (non-English) letter. The feature is no longer necessary for that reason, either, since Ada 95 has full support for international character sets. Therefore, we believe this feature is no longer necessary.<br />

<MarginText>5.b</MarginText>
Users of equipment that still uses | to represent a letter will continue to do so. Perhaps by next the time Ada is revised, such equipment will no longer be in use.<br />

<MarginText>5.c</MarginText>
Note that it was never legal to use this feature as a convenient method of including double quotes in a string without doubling them &mdash; the string literal: <br />

<MarginText>5.d</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
%"This is quoted."%{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.e/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0248-1"]} />
is not legal in Ada (and never was legal). One has to write: <br />

<MarginText>5.f</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
"""This is quoted."""{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

---

# J.3. Reduced Accuracy Subtypes

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  196

# J.3. Reduced Accuracy Subtypes

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> may be used to define a floating point subtype with a new value for its requested decimal precision, as reflected by its Digits attribute. Similarly, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> may be used to define an ordinary fixed point subtype with a new value for its <i>delta</i>, as reflected by its Delta attribute. <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>It might be more direct to make these attributes specifiable via an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>, and eliminate the syntax for these <code>{"_"}constraint</code>s. <br />

#### Syntax

<MarginText>2/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />

<CodeBlock>
<code>delta{"_"}constraint</code><a id="S0367"></a><code> ::= </code><b>delta</b> <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> [<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range_constraint</a></code>]<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Name Resolution Rules

<MarginText>3/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> is expected to be of any real type. <br /></p>

#### Legality Rules

<MarginText>4/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>The <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> shall be static.<br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> shall denote an ordinary fixed point subtype.<br /></p>

<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<p>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code>, the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> shall denote either a decimal fixed point subtype or a floating point subtype (notwithstanding the rule given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.9">3.5.9</a> that only allows a decimal fixed point subtype). <br /></p>

<MarginText>6.a/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
<i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br />

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>7/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> that denotes an ordinary fixed point subtype and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> defines an ordinary fixed point subtype with a <i>delta</i> given by the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code>. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range{"_"}constraint</a></code>, then the ordinary fixed point subtype is constrained by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range{"_"}constraint</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0027">subtype_indication</a></code> with a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#S0028">subtype_mark</a></code> that denotes a floating point subtype and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> defines a floating point subtype with a requested decimal precision (as reflected by its Digits attribute) given by the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code>. If the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> includes a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range{"_"}constraint</a></code>, then the floating point subtype is constrained by the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range{"_"}constraint</a></code>. <br /></p>

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>9/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> is <i>compatible</i> with an ordinary fixed point subtype if the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is no less than the <i>delta</i> of the subtype, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range_constraint</a></code>, if any, is compatible with the subtype.<br /></p>

<MarginText>10/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> is <i>compatible</i> with a floating point subtype if the value of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code> is no greater than the requested decimal precision of the subtype, and the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range_constraint</a></code>, if any, is compatible with the subtype.<br /></p>

<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<p>The elaboration of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> consists of the elaboration of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range_constraint</a></code>, if any. <br /></p>

<MarginText>11.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>A numeric subtype is considered &ldquo;constrained&rdquo; only if a range constraint applies to it. The only effect of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> or a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> without a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0036">range_constraint</a></code> is to specify the value of the corresponding Digits or Delta attribute in the new subtype. The set of values of the subtype is not &ldquo;constrained&rdquo; in any way by such <code>{"_"}constraint</code>s. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>11.b</MarginText>
In Ada 83, a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> is called a fixed{"_"}point{"_"}constraint, and a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> is called a floating{"_"}point{"_"}constraint. We have adopted other terms because <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code>s apply primarily to decimal fixed point types now (they apply to floating point types only as an obsolescent feature). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2012

<MarginText>11.c/4</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0152-1"]} />
<b>Corrigendum:</b> Changed the syntax so that the value following <b>delta</b> in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.3#S0367">delta_constraint</a></code> is a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0138">simple_expression</a></code>. This is compatible as any expressions that would require extra parentheses are already illegal. The change is necessary to eliminate syntax ambguities in <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.4#S0035">derived_type_definition</a></code>s. The similar change for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#S0050">digits_constraint</a></code> is documented in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.9">3.5.9</a>. <br />

---

# J.4. The Constrained Attribute

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.4.mdx

sidebar_position:  197

# J.4. The Constrained Attribute

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>For every private subtype S, the following attribute is defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This includes generic formal private subtypes. <br />

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Constrained</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Yields the value False if S denotes an unconstrained nonformal private subtype with discriminants; also yields the value False if S denotes a generic formal private subtype, and the associated actual subtype is either an unconstrained subtype with discriminants or an unconstrained array subtype; yields the value True otherwise. The value of this attribute is of the predefined subtype Boolean. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Because Ada 95 has <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#S0060">unknown_discriminant_part</a></code>s, the Constrained attribute of private subtypes is obsolete. This is fortunate, since its Ada 83 definition was confusing, as explained below. Because this attribute is obsolete, we do not bother to extend its definition to private extensions.<br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
The Constrained attribute of an object is <i>not</i> obsolete.<br />

<MarginText>2.c</MarginText>
Note well: S'Constrained matches the Ada 95 definition of &ldquo;constrained&rdquo; only for composite subtypes. For elementary subtypes, S'Constrained is always true, whether or not S is constrained. (The Constrained attribute of an object does not have this problem, as it is only defined for objects of a discriminated type.) So one should think of its designator as being 'Constrained{"_"}Or{"_"}Elementary. <br />

# J.6. Numeric_Error

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.6.mdx

sidebar_position:  199

# J.6. Numeric_Error

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>The following declaration exists in the declaration of package Standard: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
Numeric{"_"}Error : exception renames Constraint{"_"}Error;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="discussion">
<b></b>This is true even though it is not shown in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.1">A.1</a>. <br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>In Ada 83, it was unclear which situations should raise Numeric{"_"}Error, and which should raise Constraint{"_"}Error. The permissions of RM83-11.6 could often be used to allow the implementation to raise Constraint{"_"}Error in a situation where one would normally expect Numeric{"_"}Error. To avoid this confusion, all situations that raise Numeric{"_"}Error in Ada 83 are changed to raise Constraint{"_"}Error in Ada 95. Numeric{"_"}Error is changed to be a renaming of Constraint{"_"}Error to avoid most of the upward compatibilities associated with this change.<br />

<MarginText>2.c</MarginText>
In new code, Constraint{"_"}Error should be used instead of Numeric{"_"}Error. <br />
