# J.7. At Clauses

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7.mdx

sidebar_position:  200

# J.7. At Clauses

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>at{"_"}clause</code><a id="S0368"></a><code> ::= </code><b>for</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0092">direct_name</a></code> <b>use</b> <b>at</b> <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>;<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>An <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code> of the form &ldquo;for <i>x</i> use at <i>y</i>;&rdquo; is equivalent to an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> of the form &ldquo;for <i>x</i>'Address use <i>y</i>;&rdquo;. <br /></p>

<MarginText>2.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The preferred syntax for specifying the address of an entity is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> specifying the Address attribute. Therefore, the special-purpose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code> syntax is now obsolete.<br />

<MarginText>2.b</MarginText>
The above equivalence implies, for example, that only one <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code> is allowed for a given entity. Similarly, it is illegal to give both an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code> and an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> specifying the Address attribute. <br />

#### Extensions to Ada 83

<MarginText>2.c</MarginText>
We now allow to define the address of an entity using an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>. This is because Ada 83's <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code> is so hard to remember: programmers often tend to write &ldquo;for X'Address use...;&rdquo;. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>2.d</MarginText>
Ada 83's <code>address{"_"}clause</code> is now called an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code> to avoid confusion with the new term &ldquo;Address clause&rdquo; (that is, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> for the Address attribute). <br />

<a id="Subclause_J.7.1"></a>

## J.7.1  Interrupt Entries

<MarginText>1_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>[Implementations are permitted to allow the attachment of task entries to interrupts via the address clause. Such an entry is referred to as an <i>interrupt entry</i>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The address of the task entry corresponds to a hardware interrupt in an implementation-defined manner. (See Ada.Interrupts.Reference in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.2">C.3.2</a>.)] <br /></p>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>3_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The following attribute is defined:<br /></p>

<MarginText>4_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>For any task entry X: <br /></p>

<MarginText>5_J.7.1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Address </dt>
<dl>
<dd>For a task entry whose address is specified (an <i>interrupt entry</i>), the value refers to the corresponding hardware interrupt. For such an entry, as for any other task entry, the meaning of this value is implementation defined. The value of this attribute is of the type of the subtype System.Address.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6_J.7.1</MarginText>
<dd>Address may be specified for single entries via an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>6.a_J.7.1</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>Because of the equivalence of <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.7#S0368">at_clause</a></code>s and <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>s, an interrupt entry may be specified via either notation. <br />

#### Dynamic Semantics

<MarginText>7_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>As part of the initialization of a task object, the address clause for an interrupt entry is elaborated[, which evaluates the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> of the address clause]. A check is made that the address specified is associated with some interrupt to which a task entry may be attached. If this check fails, Program{"_"}Error is raised. Otherwise, the interrupt entry is attached to the interrupt associated with the specified address.<br /></p>

<MarginText>8_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>Upon finalization of the task object, the interrupt entry, if any, is detached from the corresponding interrupt and the default treatment is restored.<br /></p>

<MarginText>9_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>While an interrupt entry is attached to an interrupt, the interrupt is reserved (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3">C.3</a>).<br /></p>

<MarginText>10_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>An interrupt delivered to a task entry acts as a call to the entry issued by a hardware task whose priority is in the System.Interrupt{"_"}Priority range. It is implementation defined whether the call is performed as an ordinary entry call, a timed entry call, or a conditional entry call; which kind of call is performed can depend on the specific interrupt.<br /></p>

#### Bounded (Run-Time) Errors

<MarginText>11_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>It is a bounded error to evaluate E'Caller (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.7#Subclause_C.7.1">C.7.1</a>) in an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> for an interrupt entry. The possible effects are the same as for calling Current{"_"}Task from an entry body. <br /></p>

#### Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>12_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document to which interrupts a task entry may be attached. <br /></p>

<MarginText>12.a/2_J.7.1</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The interrupts to which a task entry may be attached.<br />

<MarginText>13_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The implementation shall document whether the invocation of an interrupt entry has the effect of an ordinary entry call, conditional call, or a timed call, and whether the effect varies in the presence of pending interrupts. <br /></p>

<MarginText>13.a/2_J.7.1</MarginText>
<b>Documentation Requirement: </b>The type of entry call invoked for an interrupt entry.<br />

#### Implementation Permissions

<MarginText>14_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The support for this subclause is optional.<br /></p>

<MarginText>15_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>Interrupts to which the implementation allows a task entry to be attached may be designated as reserved for the entire duration of program execution[; that is, not just when they have an interrupt entry attached to them].<br /></p>

<MarginText>16/1_J.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00111-01"]} />
<p>{"{"}<i>8652/0077</i>{"}"} Interrupt entry calls may be implemented by having the hardware execute directly the appropriate <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>. Alternatively, the implementation is allowed to provide an internal interrupt handler to simulate the effect of a normal task calling the entry.<br /></p>

<MarginText>17_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>The implementation is allowed to impose restrictions on the specifications and bodies of tasks that have interrupt entries.<br /></p>

<MarginText>18_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>It is implementation defined whether direct calls (from the program) to interrupt entries are allowed.<br /></p>

<MarginText>19_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p>If a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0269">select_statement</a></code> contains both a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code> and an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0273">accept_alternative</a></code> for an interrupt entry, then an implementation is allowed to impose further requirements for the selection of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.7#S0275">terminate_alternative</a></code> in addition to those given in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.3">9.3</a>. <br /></p>

<MarginText>20/1_J.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00111-01"]} />
NOTE 1   {"{"}<i>8652/0077</i>{"}"} Queued interrupts correspond to ordinary entry calls. Interrupts that are lost if not immediately processed correspond to conditional entry calls. It is a consequence of the priority rules that an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code> executed in response to an interrupt can be executed with the active priority at which the hardware generates the interrupt, taking precedence over lower priority tasks, without a scheduling action.<br />

<MarginText>21_J.7.1</MarginText>
NOTE 2   Control information that is supplied upon an interrupt can be passed to an associated interrupt entry as one or more parameters of mode <b>in</b>. <br />

#### Examples

<MarginText>22_J.7.1</MarginText>
<p><i>Example of an interrupt entry:</i> <br /></p>

<MarginText>23_J.7.1</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
task Interrupt{"_"}Handler is{"\n"}  entry Done;{"\n"}  for Done'Address use Ada.Interrupts.Reference(Ada.Interrupts.Names.Device{"_"}Done);{"\n"}end Interrupt{"_"}Handler;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>23.a/2_J.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00114-01"]} />
RM83-13.5.1 did not adequately address the problems associated with interrupts. This feature is now obsolescent and is replaced by the Ada 95 interrupt model as specified in the Systems Programming Annex. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>23.b/2_J.7.1</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00111-01"]} />
{"{"}<i>8652/0077</i>{"}"} <b>Corrigendum:</b> The undefined term <i>accept body</i> was replaced by <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>. <br />

---

# J.8. Mod Clauses

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8.mdx

sidebar_position:  201

# J.8. Mod Clauses

#### Syntax

<MarginText>1</MarginText>

<CodeBlock>
<code>mod{"_"}clause</code><a id="S0369"></a><code> ::= </code><b>at</b> <b>mod</b> <i>static{"_"}</i><code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>;<br />

</CodeBlock>

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<p>A <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code> of the form: <br /></p>

<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0092-1"]} />
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for r use{"\n"}    record at mod a;{"\n"}        ...{"\n"}    end record;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<p>is equivalent to: <br /></p>

<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
for r'Alignment use a;{"\n"}for r use{"\n"}    record{"\n"}        ...{"\n"}    end record;{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>5.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="reason">
<b></b>The preferred syntax for specifying the alignment of an entity is an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> specifying the Alignment attribute. Therefore, the special-purpose <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8#S0369">mod_clause</a></code> syntax is now obsolete.<br />

<MarginText>5.b</MarginText>
The above equivalence implies, for example, that it is illegal to give both a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8#S0369">mod_clause</a></code> and an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> specifying the Alignment attribute for the same type. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>5.c</MarginText>
Ada 83's <code>alignment{"_"}clause</code> is now called a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.8#S0369">mod_clause</a></code> to avoid confusion with the new term &ldquo;Alignment clause&rdquo; (that is, an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code> for the Alignment attribute). <br />

---

# J.9. The Storage_Size Attribute

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.9.mdx

sidebar_position:  202

# J.9. The Storage_Size Attribute

#### Static Semantics

<MarginText>1</MarginText>
<p>For any task subtype T, the following attribute is defined: <br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>T'Storage{"_"}Size </dt>
<dl>
<dd>Denotes an implementation-defined value of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i> representing the number of storage elements reserved for a task of the subtype T. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>2.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<b>To be honest: </b>T'Storage{"_"}Size cannot be particularly meaningful in the presence of the specification of the aspect Storage{"_"}Size, especially when the expression is dynamic, or depends on a discriminant of the task, because the Storage{"_"}Size will be different for different objects of the type. Even without such a specification, the Storage{"_"}Size can be different for different objects of the type, and in any case, the value is implementation defined. Hence, it is always implementation defined. <br />

<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01", "AI05-0229-1"]} />
<dl>
<dd>Storage{"_"}Size may be specified for a task first subtype that is not an interface via an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>. When the attribute is specified, the Storage{"_"}Size aspect is specified to be the value of the given <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code>. <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>3.a/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>When this attribute is specified with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>, the associated aspect is set to the <i>value</i> of the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> given in the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3#S0349">attribute_definition_clause</a></code>, rather than the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.4#S0132">expression</a></code> itself. This value is therefore the same for all objects of the type; in particular, it is not re-evaluated when objects are created. This is different than when the aspect is specified with an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code> (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>). <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>3.b/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00345-01"]} />
We don't allow specifying Storage{"_"}Size on task interfaces. We don't need to mention class-wide task types, because these cannot be a first subtype. <br />

---

# Annex J. Obsolescent Features

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-J/AA-J.mdx

sidebar_position:  193

# Annex J. Obsolescent Features

<MarginText>1/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00368-01"]} />
<p>[ This Annex contains descriptions of features of the language whose functionality is largely redundant with other features defined by this Reference Manual. Use of these features is not recommended in newly written programs. Use of these features can be prevented by using pragma Restrictions (No{"_"}Obsolescent{"_"}Features), see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.12#Subclause_13.12.1">13.12.1</a>.] <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>These features are still part of the language, and have to be implemented by conforming implementations. The primary reason for putting these descriptions here is to get redundant features out of the way of most readers. The designers of the next version of Ada will have to assess whether or not it makes sense to drop these features from the language. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 83

<MarginText>1.b</MarginText>
The following features have been removed from the language, rather than declared to be obsolescent: <br />

<MarginText>1.c</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The package Low{"_"}Level{"_"}IO (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.6">A.6</a>).<br /></li>
<MarginText>1.d</MarginText>
<li>The Epsilon, Mantissa, Emax, Small, Large, Safe{"_"}Emax, Safe{"_"}Small, and Safe{"_"}Large attributes of floating point types (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>).<br /></li>
<MarginText>1.e/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00284-02"]} />
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
<MarginText>1.f</MarginText>
<li>The pragmas System{"_"}Name, Storage{"_"}Unit, and Memory{"_"}Size (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.7">13.7</a>).<br /></li>
<MarginText>1.g</MarginText>
<li>The pragma Shared (see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>). <br /></li>
</ul>
<MarginText>1.h</MarginText>
Implementations can continue to support the above features for upward compatibility. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 95

<MarginText>1.i/2</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI95-00368-01"]} />
A mention of the No{"_"}Obsolescent{"_"}Features restriction was added. <br />

#### Wording Changes from Ada 2005

<MarginText>1.j/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1"]} />
<code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8#S0019">Pragma</a></code> Controlled has been removed from the language, rather than declared to be obsolescent. No existing implementation gives it any effect. An implementation could continue to support the pragma as an implementation-defined pragma for upward compatibility. <br />

# K.1. Language-Defined Aspects

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-K/AA-K.1.mdx

# K.1. Language-Defined Aspects

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>This subclause summarizes the definitions given elsewhere of the language-defined aspects. Aspects are properties of entities that can be specified by the Ada program; unless otherwise specified below, aspects can be specified using an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Address</dt>
<dl>
<dd>Machine address of an entity. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>2.1/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Aggregate</dt>
<dd>Mechanism to define user-defined aggregates. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.3#Subclause_4.3.5">4.3.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>3/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Alignment (object)</dt>
<dd>Alignment of an object. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>4/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Alignment (subtype)</dt>
<dd>Alignment of a subtype. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>5/4</MarginText>
<dt><br/>All{"_"}Calls{"_"}Remote</dt>
<dd>All indirect or dispatching remote subprogram calls, and all direct remote subprogram calls, should use the Partition Communication Subsystem. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2#Subclause_E.2.3">E.2.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>5.1/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Allows{"_"}Exit</dt>
<dd>An indication of whether a subprogram will operate correctly for arbitrary transfers of control. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.5#Subclause_5.5.3">5.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Asynchronous</dt>
<dd>Remote procedure calls are asynchronous; the caller continues without waiting for the call to return. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.4#Subclause_E.4.1">E.4.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>7/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Atomic</dt>
<dd>Declare that a type, object, or component is atomic. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>8/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Atomic{"_"}Components</dt>
<dd>Declare that the components of an array type or object are atomic. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>9/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Attach{"_"}Handler</dt>
<dd>Protected procedure is attached to an interrupt. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>10/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Bit{"_"}Order</dt>
<dd>Order of bit numbering in a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#S0352">record_representation_clause</a></code>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#Subclause_13.5.3">13.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>11/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Coding</dt>
<dd>Internal representation of enumeration literals. Specified by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.4#S0350">enumeration_representation_clause</a></code>, not by an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.1#S0346">aspect_specification</a></code>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.4">13.4</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Component{"_"}Size</dt>
<dd>Size in bits of a component of an array type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>13/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Constant{"_"}Indexing</dt>
<dd>Defines function(s) to implement user-defined <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>s. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.6">4.1.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>14/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Convention</dt>
<dd>Calling convention or other convention used for interfacing to other languages. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.1">B.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>15/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>CPU</dt>
<dd>Processor on which a given task, or calling task for a protected operation, should run. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.16">D.16</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>16/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Default{"_"}Component{"_"}Value</dt>
<dd>Default value for the components of an array-of-scalar subtype. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6">3.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>16.1/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Default{"_"}Initial{"_"}Condition</dt>

<MarginText>17/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Default{"_"}Iterator</dt>

<MarginText>18/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Default{"_"}Storage{"_"}Pool</dt>

<MarginText>19/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Default{"_"}Value</dt>

<MarginText>19.1/4</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Discard{"_"}Names</dt>
<dd>Requests a reduction in storage for names associated with an entity. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.5">C.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>19.2/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Dispatching</dt>

<MarginText>45/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Preelaborate</dt>
<dd>Code execution during elaboration is avoided for a given package. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>46/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Priority</dt>
<dd>Priority of a task object or type, or priority of a protected object or type; the priority is not in the interrupt range. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.1">D.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>47/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Pure</dt>
<dd>Side effects are avoided in the subprograms of a given package. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>47.1/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Put{"_"}Image</dt>
<dd>Procedure to define the image of a given type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.10">4.10</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>48/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Read</dt>
<dd>Procedure to read a value from a stream for a given type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>48.1/4</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Read'Class</dt>
<dd>Procedure to read a value from a stream for the class-wide type associated with a given type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>48.2/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Real{"_"}Literal</dt>
<dd>Defines a function or functions to implement user-defined real literals. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>49/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Record layout</dt>
<dd>See Layout. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#Subclause_13.5.1">13.5.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>50/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Relative{"_"}Deadline</dt>
<dd>Task or protected type parameter used in Earliest Deadline First Dispatching. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.6">D.2.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>51/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Remote{"_"}Call{"_"}Interface</dt>
<dd>Subprograms in a given package may be used in remote procedure calls. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2#Subclause_E.2.3">E.2.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>52/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Remote{"_"}Types</dt>
<dd>Types in a given package may be used in remote procedure calls. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2#Subclause_E.2.2">E.2.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>53/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Shared{"_"}Passive</dt>
<dd>A given package is used to represent shared memory in a distributed system. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.2#Subclause_E.2.1">E.2.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>54/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Size (object)</dt>
<dd>Size in bits of an object. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>55/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Size (subtype)</dt>
<dd>Size in bits of a subtype. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>56/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Small</dt>
<dd>Scale factor for a fixed point type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.10">3.5.10</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>56.1/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Stable{"_"}Properties</dt>
<dd>A list of functions describing characteristics that usually are unchanged by primitive operations of the type or an individual primitive subprogram. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.4">7.3.4</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>56.2/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Stable{"_"}Properties'Class</dt>
<dd>A list of functions describing characteristics that usually are unchanged by primitive operations of a class of types or a primitive subprogram for such a class. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.4">7.3.4</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>56.3/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Static</dt>
<dd>Specifies that an associated expression function can be used in static expressions. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.8">6.8</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>57/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Static{"_"}Predicate</dt>
<dd>Condition that will hold true for objects of a given subtype; the subtype may be static. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.2#Subclause_3.2.4">3.2.4</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>58/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Storage{"_"}Pool</dt>
<dd>Pool of memory from which <b>new</b> will allocate for a given access type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>59/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Storage{"_"}Size (access)</dt>
<dd>Sets memory size for allocations for an access type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>60/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Storage{"_"}Size (task)</dt>
<dd>Size in storage elements reserved for a task type or single task object. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>61/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Stream{"_"}Size</dt>
<dd>Size in bits used to represent elementary objects in a stream. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>61.1/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>String{"_"}Literal</dt>
<dd>Defines a function to implement user-defined string literals. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.2#Subclause_4.2.1">4.2.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>62/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Synchronization</dt>
<dd>Defines whether a given primitive operation of a synchronized interface will be implemented by an entry or protected procedure. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5">9.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>63/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Type{"_"}Invariant</dt>
<dd>A condition that will hold true for all objects of a type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.2">7.3.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>64/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Type{"_"}Invariant'Class</dt>
<dd>A condition that will hold true for all objects in a class of types. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.2">7.3.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>65/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Unchecked{"_"}Union</dt>
<dd>Type is used to interface to a C union type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-B/AA-B.3#Subclause_B.3.3">B.3.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>65.1/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Use{"_"}Formal</dt>
<dd>Generic formal parameters used in the implementation of an entity. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-H/AA-H.7#Subclause_H.7.1">H.7.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>66/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Variable{"_"}Indexing</dt>
<dd>Defines function(s) to implement user-defined <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0096">indexed_component</a></code>s. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#Subclause_4.1.6">4.1.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>67/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Volatile</dt>
<dd>Declare that a type, object, or component is volatile. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>68/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Volatile{"_"}Components</dt>
<dd>Declare that the components of an array type or object are volatile. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.6">C.6</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>69/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Write</dt>
<dd>Procedure to write a value to a stream for a given type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>69.1/4</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Write'Class</dt>
<dd>Procedure to write a value to a stream for a the class-wide type associated with a given type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>69.2/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>Yield</dt>
<dd>Ensures that a callable entity includes a task dispatching point. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.1">D.2.1</a>.<br /></dd>
</dl>

# K.2. Language-Defined Attributes

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-K/AA-K.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  211

# K.2. Language-Defined Attributes

<MarginText>1/3</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI05-0229-1", "AI05-0299-1"]} />
<p>This subclause summarizes the definitions given elsewhere of the language-defined attributes. Attributes are properties of entities that can be queried by an Ada program.<br /></p>

<MarginText>2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>P'Access</dt>
<dl>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> P that denotes a subprogram:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<dd>P'Access yields an access value that designates the subprogram denoted by P. The type of P'Access is an access-to-subprogram type (<i>S</i>), as determined by the expected type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Access</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X that denotes an aliased view of an object:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<dd>X'Access yields an access value that designates the object denoted by X. The type of X'Access is an access-to-object type, as determined by the expected type. The expected type shall be a general access type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.10#Subclause_3.10.2">3.10.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>6/1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Address</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X that denotes an object, program unit, or label:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>7</MarginText>
<dd>Denotes the address of the first of the storage elements allocated to X. For a program unit or label, this value refers to the machine code associated with the corresponding body or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-5/AA-5.1#S0167">statement</a></code>. The value of this attribute is of type System.Address. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Adjacent</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a floating point type <i>T</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<dd>S'Adjacent denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Adjacent (X, Towards : T){"\n"}  return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>If <i>Towards</i> = <i>X</i>, the function yields <i>X</i>; otherwise, it yields the machine number of the type <i>T</i> adjacent to <i>X</i> in the direction of <i>Towards</i>, if that machine number exists. If the result would be outside the base range of S, Constraint{"_"}Error is raised. When <i>T</i>'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True, a zero result has the sign of <i>X</i>. When <i>Towards</i> is zero, its sign has no bearing on the result. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>12</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Aft</dt>
<dd>For every fixed point subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>13</MarginText>
<dd>S'Aft yields the number of decimal digits needed after the decimal point to accommodate the <i>delta</i> of the subtype S, unless the <i>delta</i> of the subtype S is greater than 0.1, in which case the attribute yields the value one. (S'Aft is the smallest positive integer N for which (10{"*"}{"*"}N){"*"}S'Delta is greater than or equal to one.) The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.10">3.5.10</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>13.1/2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Alignment</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>13.2/2</MarginText>
<dd>The value of this attribute is of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>, and nonnegative.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>13.3/2</MarginText>
<dd>For an object X of subtype S, if S'Alignment is not zero, then X'Alignment is a nonzero integral multiple of S'Alignment unless specified otherwise by a representation item. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>14/1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Alignment</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X that denotes an object:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>15/2</MarginText>
<dd>The value of this attribute is of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>, and nonnegative; zero means that the object is not necessarily aligned on a storage element boundary. If X'Alignment is not zero, then X is aligned on a storage unit boundary and X'Address is an integral multiple of X'Alignment (that is, the Address modulo the Alignment is zero).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>16/2</MarginText>
<dt><br/></dt>
<dd><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i> See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>17</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Base</dt>
<dd>For every scalar subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>18</MarginText>
<dd>S'Base denotes an unconstrained subtype of the type of S. This unconstrained subtype is called the <i>base subtype</i> of the type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>19</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Bit{"_"}Order</dt>
<dd>For every specific record subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>20</MarginText>
<dd>Denotes the bit ordering for the type of S. The value of this attribute is of type System.Bit{"_"}Order. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.5#Subclause_13.5.3">13.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>21/1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>P'Body{"_"}Version</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> P that statically denotes a program unit:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>22</MarginText>
<dd>Yields a value of the predefined type String that identifies the version of the compilation unit that contains the body (but not any subunits) of the program unit. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-E/AA-E.3">E.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>23</MarginText>
<dt><br/>T'Callable</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> T that is of a task type (after any implicit dereference):<br /></dd>
<MarginText>24</MarginText>
<dd>Yields the value True when the task denoted by T is <i>callable</i>, and False otherwise; See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.9">9.9</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>25</MarginText>
<dt><br/>E'Caller</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> E that denotes an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>26/3</MarginText>
<dd>Yields a value of the type Task{"_"}Id that identifies the task whose call is now being serviced. Use of this attribute is allowed only inside an <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0258">accept_statement</a></code>, or <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0260">entry_body</a></code> after the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0262">entry_barrier</a></code>, corresponding to the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.5#S0257">entry_declaration</a></code> denoted by E. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.7#Subclause_C.7.1">C.7.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>27</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Ceiling</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a floating point type <i>T</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>28</MarginText>
<dd>S'Ceiling denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>29</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Ceiling (X : T){"\n"}  return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>30/5</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>The function yields the value &lceil;<i>X</i>&rceil;, that is, the smallest (most negative) integral value greater than or equal to <i>X</i>. When <i>X</i> is zero, the result has the sign of <i>X</i>; a zero result otherwise has a negative sign when S'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>31</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Class</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a tagged type <i>T</i> (specific or class-wide):<br /></dd>
<MarginText>32</MarginText>
<dd>S'Class denotes a subtype of the class-wide type (called <i>T</i>'Class in this document) for the class rooted at <i>T</i> (or if S already denotes a class-wide subtype, then S'Class is the same as S).<br /></dd>
<MarginText>33</MarginText>
<dd>S'Class is unconstrained. However, if S is constrained, then the values of S'Class are only those that when converted to the type <i>T</i> belong to S. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9">3.9</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>34</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Class</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of an untagged private type whose full view is tagged:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>35</MarginText>
<dd>Denotes the class-wide subtype corresponding to the full view of S. This attribute is allowed only from the beginning of the private part in which the full view is declared, until the declaration of the full view. After the full view, the Class attribute of the full view can be used. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-7/AA-7.3#Subclause_7.3.1">7.3.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>36/1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Component{"_"}Size</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X that denotes an array subtype or array object (after any implicit dereference):<br /></dd>
<MarginText>37</MarginText>
<dd>Denotes the size in bits of components of the type of X. The value of this attribute is of type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.3">13.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>38</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Compose</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a floating point type <i>T</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>39</MarginText>
<dd>S'Compose denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>40</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Compose (Fraction : T;{"\n"}                    Exponent : universal{"_"}integer){"\n"}  return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>41</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>Let <i>v</i> be the value <i>Fraction</i> · <i>T</i>'Machine{"_"}Radix<i>Exponent</i>&ndash;<i>k</i>, where <i>k</i> is the normalized exponent of <i>Fraction</i>. If <i>v</i> is a machine number of the type <i>T</i>, or if |<i>v</i>| &ge; <i>T</i>'Model{"_"}Small, the function yields <i>v</i>; otherwise, it yields either one of the machine numbers of the type <i>T</i> adjacent to <i>v</i>. Constraint{"_"}Error is optionally raised if <i>v</i> is outside the base range of S. A zero result has the sign of <i>Fraction</i> when S'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>42</MarginText>
<dt><br/>A'Constrained</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> A that is of a discriminated type (after any implicit dereference):<br /></dd>
<MarginText>43/5</MarginText>
<dd>Yields the value True if A denotes a constant, a value, a tagged object, or a constrained variable, and False otherwise. The value of this attribute is of the predefined type Boolean. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.7#Subclause_3.7.2">3.7.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>44</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Copy{"_"}Sign</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a floating point type <i>T</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>45</MarginText>
<dd>S'Copy{"_"}Sign denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>46</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Copy{"_"}Sign (Value, Sign : T){"\n"}  return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>47</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>If the value of <i>Value</i> is nonzero, the function yields a result whose magnitude is that of <i>Value</i> and whose sign is that of <i>Sign</i>; otherwise, it yields the value zero. Constraint{"_"}Error is optionally raised if the result is outside the base range of S. A zero result has the sign of <i>Sign</i> when S'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>48</MarginText>
<dt><br/>E'Count</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> E that denotes an entry of a task or protected unit:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>49</MarginText>
<dd>Yields the number of calls presently queued on the entry E of the current instance of the unit. The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.9">9.9</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>50/1</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Definite</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> S that denotes a formal indefinite subtype:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>51/3</MarginText>
<dd>S'Definite yields True if the actual subtype corresponding to S is definite; otherwise, it yields False. The value of this attribute is of the predefined type Boolean. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-12/AA-12.5#Subclause_12.5.1">12.5.1</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>52</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Delta</dt>
<dd>For every fixed point subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>53</MarginText>
<dd>S'Delta denotes the <i>delta</i> of the fixed point subtype S. The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}real</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.10">3.5.10</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>54</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Denorm</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a floating point type <i>T</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>55</MarginText>

<MarginText>136.4/2</MarginText>

<MarginText>199</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Remainder</dt>

<dd>S'Remainder denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>201</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Remainder (X, Y : T){"\n"}  return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>202</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>For nonzero <i>Y</i>, let <i>v</i> be the value <i>X</i> &ndash; <i>n</i> · <i>Y</i>, where <i>n</i> is the integer nearest to the exact value of <i>X</i>/<i>Y</i>; if |<i>n</i> &ndash; <i>X</i>/<i>Y</i>| = 1/2, then <i>n</i> is chosen to be even. If <i>v</i> is a machine number of the type <i>T</i>, the function yields <i>v</i>; otherwise, it yields zero. Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if <i>Y</i> is zero. A zero result has the sign of <i>X</i> when S'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>202.1/3</MarginText>
<dt><br/>F'Result</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> F that denotes a function declaration or an access-to-function type:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>202.2/5</MarginText>
<dd>Within a postcondition expression for F, denotes the return object of the function call for which the postcondition expression is evaluated. The type of this attribute is that of the result subtype of the function or access-to-function type except within a Post'Class postcondition expression for a function with a controlling result or with a controlling access result; in those cases the type of the attribute is described above as part of the Name Resolution Rules for Post'Class. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-6/AA-6.1#Subclause_6.1.1">6.1.1</a>.<br /></dd>

If the Numerics Annex is not supported, the value of this attribute is implementation defined; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.2">G.2.2</a> for the definition that applies to implementations supporting the Numerics Annex. If the Numerics Annex is not supported, the value of this attribute is implementation defined; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-G/AA-G.2#Subclause_G.2.2">G.2.2</a> for the definition that applies to implementations supporting the Numerics Annex. <MarginText>216</MarginText>

The scale indicates the position of the point relative to the rightmost significant digits of values of subtype S. The value of this attribute is of the type <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.10">3.5.10</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>217</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Scaling</dt>

<MarginText>218</MarginText>

</dl>
<MarginText>219</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Scaling (X : T;{"\n"}                    Adjustment : universal{"_"}integer){"\n"}  return T{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>220</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>Let <i>v</i> be the value <i>X</i> · <i>T</i>'Machine{"_"}Radix<i>Adjustment</i>. If <i>v</i> is a machine number of the type <i>T</i>, or if |<i>v</i>| &ge; <i>T</i>'Model{"_"}Small, the function yields <i>v</i>; otherwise, it yields either one of the machine numbers of the type <i>T</i> adjacent to <i>v</i>. Constraint{"_"}Error is optionally raised if <i>v</i> is outside the base range of S. A zero result has the sign of <i>X</i> when S'Signed{"_"}Zeros is True. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>221</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Signed{"_"}Zeros</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a floating point type <i>T</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>222</MarginText>
<dd>Yields the value True if the hardware representation for the type <i>T</i> has the capability of representing both positively and negatively signed zeros, these being generated and used by the predefined operations of the type <i>T</i> as specified in IEC 559:1989; yields the value False otherwise. The value of this attribute is of the predefined type Boolean. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.3">A.5.3</a>.<br /></dd>

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>241</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>For an enumeration type, the function returns the value whose position number is one more than that of the value of <i>Arg</i>; Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if there is no such value of the type. For an integer type, the function returns the result of adding one to the value of <i>Arg</i>. For a fixed point type, the function returns the result of adding <i>small</i> to the value of <i>Arg</i>. For a floating point type, the function returns the machine number (as defined in <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.7">3.5.7</a>) immediately above the value of <i>Arg</i>; Constraint{"_"}Error is raised if there is no such machine number. <dd>This function returns a value given an image of the value as a Wide{"_"}String, ignoring any leading or trailing spaces. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.1/2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a type T:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.2/5</MarginText>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>277.3/5</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image(Arg : S'Base){"\n"}  return Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>277.4/5</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image calls S'Put{"_"}Image passing <i>Arg</i> (which will typically store a sequence of character values in a text buffer) and then returns the result of retrieving the contents of that buffer with function Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Get. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.10">4.10</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.5/5</MarginText>
<dt><br/>X'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image</dt>
<dd>For a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.1#S0093">prefix</a></code> X of a type T other than <i>universal{"_"}real</i> or <i>universal{"_"}fixed</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.6/5</MarginText>
<dd>X'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image denotes the result of calling function S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image with <i>Arg</i> being X, where S is the nominal subtype of X. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.10">4.10</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.7/2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value</dt>
<dd>For every scalar subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.8/2</MarginText>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value denotes a function with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>277.9/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
function S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Value(Arg : Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String){"\n"}  return S'Base{"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>277.10/2</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>This function returns a value given an image of the value as a Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String, ignoring any leading or trailing spaces. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.11/2</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Width</dt>
<dd>For every scalar subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>277.12/5</MarginText>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Width denotes the maximum length of a Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}String returned by S'Wide{"_"}Wide{"_"}Image over all values of the subtype S, assuming a default implementation of S'Put{"_"}Image. It denotes zero for a subtype that has a null range. Its type is <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>278</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Wide{"_"}Width</dt>
<dd>For every scalar subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>279/5</MarginText>
<dd>S'Wide{"_"}Width denotes the maximum length of a Wide{"_"}String returned by S'Wide{"_"}Image over all values of the subtype S, assuming a default implementation of S'Put{"_"}Image. It denotes zero for a subtype that has a null range. Its type is <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>280</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Width</dt>
<dd>For every scalar subtype S:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>281/5</MarginText>
<dd>S'Width denotes the maximum length of a String returned by S'Image over all values of the subtype S, assuming a default implementation of S'Put{"_"}Image. It denotes zero for a subtype that has a null range. Its type is <i>universal{"_"}integer</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5">3.5</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>282</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Class'Write</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S'Class of a class-wide type <i>T</i>'Class:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>283</MarginText>
<dd>S'Class'Write denotes a procedure with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>284/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure S'Class'Write({"\n"}   Stream : not null access Ada.Streams.Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type'Class;{"\n"}   Item   : in T'Class){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>285</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>Dispatches to the subprogram denoted by the Write attribute of the specific type identified by the tag of Item. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br /></dd>
<MarginText>286</MarginText>
<dt><br/>S'Write</dt>
<dd>For every subtype S of a specific type <i>T</i>:<br /></dd>
<MarginText>287</MarginText>
<dd>S'Write denotes a procedure with the following specification: <br /></dd>
</dl>
<MarginText>288/2</MarginText>
<CodeBlock language="ada">
procedure S'Write({"\n"}   Stream : not null access Ada.Streams.Root{"_"}Stream{"_"}Type'Class;{"\n"}   Item : in T){"\n"}

</CodeBlock>
<MarginText>289</MarginText>
<dl>
<dd>S'Write writes the value of <i>Item</i> to <i>Stream</i>. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.13#Subclause_13.13.2">13.13.2</a>.<br /></dd>
</dl>

# M.1. Specific Documentation Requirements

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
<p>In addition to implementation-defined characteristics, each Ada implementation is required to document various properties of the implementation: <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Most of the items in this list require documentation only for implementations that conform to Specialized Needs Annexes. <br />

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>The behavior of implementations in implementation-defined situations shall be documented &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-M/AA-M.2">M.2</a> for a listing. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>(19).<br /></li>
<MarginText>3/2</MarginText>
<li>The set of values that a user-defined Allocate procedure needs to accept for the Alignment parameter. How the standard storage pool is chosen, and how storage is allocated by standard storage pools. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.11">13.11</a>(22).<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<li>The algorithm used for random number generation, including a description of its period. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.2">A.5.2</a>(44).<br /></li>
<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<li>The minimum time interval between calls to the time-dependent Reset procedure that is guaranteed to initiate different random number sequences. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.5#Subclause_A.5.2">A.5.2</a>(45).<br /></li>
<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<li>The conditions under which Io{"_"}Exceptions.Name{"_"}Error, Io{"_"}Exceptions.Use{"_"}Error, and Io{"_"}Exceptions.Device{"_"}Error are propagated. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.13">A.13</a>(15).<br /></li>
<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<li>The behavior of package Environment{"_"}Variables when environment variables are changed by external mechanisms. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-A/AA-A.17">A.17</a>(30/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>8/2</MarginText>
<li>The overhead of calling machine-code or intrinsic subprograms. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.1">C.1</a>(6).<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/2</MarginText>
<li>The types and attributes used in machine code insertions. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.1">C.1</a>(7).<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/2</MarginText>
<li>The subprogram calling conventions for all supported convention identifiers. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.1">C.1</a>(8/3).<br /></li>
<MarginText>11/2</MarginText>
<li>The mapping between the Link{"_"}Name or Ada designator and the external link name. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.1">C.1</a>(9).<br /></li>
<MarginText>12/2</MarginText>
<li>The treatment of interrupts. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3">C.3</a>(22).<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/2</MarginText>
<li>The metrics for interrupt handlers. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.1">C.3.1</a>(16).<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/3</MarginText>
<li>If the Ceiling{"_"}Locking policy is in effect, the default ceiling priority for a protected object that specifies an interrupt handler aspect. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.3#Subclause_C.3.2">C.3.2</a>(24/5).<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/2</MarginText>
<li>Any circumstances when the elaboration of a preelaborated package causes code to be executed. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.4">C.4</a>(12).<br /></li>
<MarginText>16/2</MarginText>
<li>Whether a partition can be restarted without reloading. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.4">C.4</a>(13).<br /></li>
<MarginText>17/2</MarginText>
<li>The effect of calling Current{"_"}Task from an entry body or interrupt handler. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.7#Subclause_C.7.1">C.7.1</a>(19).<br /></li>
<MarginText>18/2</MarginText>
<li>For package Task{"_"}Attributes, limits on the number and size of task attributes, and how to configure any limits. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.7#Subclause_C.7.2">C.7.2</a>(19).<br /></li>
<MarginText>19/2</MarginText>
<li>The metrics for the Task{"_"}Attributes package. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-C/AA-C.7#Subclause_C.7.2">C.7.2</a>(27).<br /></li>
<MarginText>20/2</MarginText>
<li>The details of the configuration used to generate the values of all metrics. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/">D</a>(2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>21/2</MarginText>
<li>The maximum priority inversion a user task can experience from the implementation. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.3">D.2.3</a>(12/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>22/2</MarginText>
<li>The amount of time that a task can be preempted for processing on behalf of lower-priority tasks. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.3">D.2.3</a>(13/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>23/2</MarginText>
<li>The quantum values supported for round robin dispatching. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.5">D.2.5</a>(16/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>24/2</MarginText>
<li>The accuracy of the detection of the exhaustion of the budget of a task for round robin dispatching. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.5">D.2.5</a>(17/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>25/2</MarginText>
<li>Any conditions that cause the completion of the setting of the deadline of a task to be delayed for a multiprocessor. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.2#Subclause_D.2.6">D.2.6</a>(32/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>26/2</MarginText>
<li>Any conditions that cause the completion of the setting of the priority of a task to be delayed for a multiprocessor. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5#Subclause_D.5.1">D.5.1</a>(12.1/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>27/2</MarginText>
<li>The metrics for Set{"_"}Priority. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5#Subclause_D.5.1">D.5.1</a>(14).<br /></li>
<MarginText>28/2</MarginText>
<li>The metrics for setting the priority of a protected object. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.5#Subclause_D.5.2">D.5.2</a>(10).<br /></li>
<MarginText>29/2</MarginText>
<li>On a multiprocessor, any conditions that cause the completion of an aborted construct to be delayed later than what is specified for a single processor. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.6">D.6</a>(3).<br /></li>
<MarginText>30/2</MarginText>
<li>The metrics for aborts. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.6">D.6</a>(8).<br /></li>
<MarginText>31/2</MarginText>
<li>The values of Time{"_"}First, Time{"_"}Last, Time{"_"}Span{"_"}First, Time{"_"}Span{"_"}Last, Time{"_"}Span{"_"}Unit, and Tick for package Real{"_"}Time. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.8">D.8</a>(33).<br /></li>
<MarginText>32/2</MarginText>
<li>The properties of the underlying time base used in package Real{"_"}Time. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.8">D.8</a>(34).<br /></li>
<MarginText>33/2</MarginText>
<li>Any synchronization of package Real{"_"}Time with external time references. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.8">D.8</a>(35).<br /></li>
<MarginText>34/5</MarginText>
<li>Any aspects of the external environment that can interfere with package Real{"_"}Time. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.8">D.8</a>(36/5).<br /></li>
<MarginText>35/2</MarginText>
<li>The metrics for package Real{"_"}Time. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.8">D.8</a>(45).<br /></li>
<MarginText>36/2</MarginText>
<li>The minimum value of the delay expression of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0268">delay_relative_statement</a></code> that causes a task to actually be blocked. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.9">D.9</a>(7).<br /></li>
<MarginText>37/2</MarginText>
<li>The minimum difference between the value of the delay expression of a <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0267">delay_until_statement</a></code> and the value of Real{"_"}Time.Clock, that causes the task to actually be blocked. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.9">D.9</a>(8).<br /></li>
<MarginText>38/2</MarginText>
<li>The metrics for delay statements. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.9">D.9</a>(13).<br /></li>
<MarginText>39/2</MarginText>
<li>The upper bound on the duration of interrupt blocking caused by the implementation. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-D/AA-D.12">D.12</a>(5).<br /></li>

# M.2. Implementation-Defined Characteristics

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-M/AA-M.2.mdx

sidebar_position:  215

# M.2. Implementation-Defined Characteristics

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
<p>The Ada language allows for certain machine dependences in a controlled manner. Each Ada implementation is required to document all implementation-defined characteristics: <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>It need not document unspecified characteristics.<br />

<MarginText>1.b</MarginText>
Some of the items in this list require documentation only for implementations that conform to Specialized Needs Annexes. <br />

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Whether or not each recommendation given in  is followed &mdash; see <a href="/docs/arm/AA-M/AA-M.3">M.3</a> for a listing. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.2">1.1.2</a>(37).<br /></li>
<MarginText>3</MarginText>
<li>Capacity limitations of the implementation. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>(3).<br /></li>
<MarginText>4</MarginText>
<li>Variations from the standard that are impractical to avoid given the implementation's execution environment. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>(6).<br /></li>
<MarginText>5</MarginText>
<li>Which <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-13/AA-13.8#S0357">code_statement</a></code>s cause external interactions. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>(10).<br /></li>
<MarginText>6</MarginText>
<li>The coded representation for the text of an Ada program. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.1">2.1</a>(4/5).<br /></li>
<MarginText>6.1/5</MarginText>
<li>The semantics of an Ada program whose text is not in Normalization Form C. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.1">2.1</a>(4.1/5).<br /></li>
<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
<MarginText>8</MarginText>
<li>The representation for an end of line. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.2">2.2</a>(2/3).<br /></li>
<MarginText>9</MarginText>
<li>Maximum supported line length and lexical element length. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.2">2.2</a>(14).<br /></li>
<MarginText>10</MarginText>
<li>Implementation-defined pragmas. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8">2.8</a>(14).<br /></li>
<MarginText>11</MarginText>
<li>Effect of pragma Optimize. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8">2.8</a>(27).<br /></li>
<MarginText>11.1/4</MarginText>

# M.3. Implementation Advice

Source: https://github.com/ada-lang-io/ada-lang-io/blob/main/docs/arm/AA-M/AA-M.3.mdx

sidebar_position:  216

# M.3. Implementation Advice

<MarginText>1/5</MarginText>
<MarginInfo items={["AI12-0442-1"]} />
<p>This Reference Manual sometimes gives advice about handling certain target machine dependences. Each Ada implementation is required to document whether that advice is followed: <br /></p>

<MarginText>1.a/2</MarginText>
<Admonition type="aarm" aarm="ramification">
<b></b>Some of the items in this list require documentation only for implementations that conform to Specialized Needs Annexes. <br />

<MarginText>2/2</MarginText>
<ul>
<li>Program{"_"}Error should be raised when an unsupported Specialized Needs Annex feature is used at run time. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>(20).<br /></li>
<MarginText>3/2</MarginText>
<li>Implementation-defined extensions to the functionality of a language-defined library unit should be provided by adding children to the library unit. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.3">1.1.3</a>(21).<br /></li>
<MarginText>4/2</MarginText>
<li>If a bounded error or erroneous execution is detected, Program{"_"}Error should be raised. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-1/AA-1.1#Subclause_1.1.5">1.1.5</a>(12).<br /></li>
<MarginText>5/2</MarginText>
<li>Implementation-defined pragmas should have no semantic effect for error-free programs. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8">2.8</a>(16/3).<br /></li>
<MarginText>6/2</MarginText>
<li>Implementation-defined pragmas should not make an illegal program legal, unless they complete a declaration or configure the <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.1#S0287">library_item</a></code>s in an environment. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-2/AA-2.8">2.8</a>(19).<br /></li>
<MarginText>7/2</MarginText>
<li>Long{"_"}Integer should be declared in Standard if the target supports 32-bit arithmetic. No other named integer subtypes should be declared in Standard. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.4">3.5.4</a>(28).<br /></li>
<MarginText>8/2</MarginText>
<li>For a two's complement target, modular types with a binary modulus up to System.Max{"_"}Int{"*"}2+2 should be supported. A nonbinary modulus up to Integer'Last should be supported. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.4">3.5.4</a>(29).<br /></li>
<MarginText>9/2</MarginText>
<li>Program{"_"}Error should be raised for the evaluation of S'Pos for an enumeration type, if the value of the operand does not correspond to the internal code for any enumeration literal of the type. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.5">3.5.5</a>(8).<br /></li>
<MarginText>10/2</MarginText>
<li>Long{"_"}Float should be declared in Standard if the target supports 11 or more digits of precision. No other named float subtypes should be declared in Standard. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.5#Subclause_3.5.7">3.5.7</a>(17).<br /></li>
<MarginText>11/2</MarginText>
<li>Multidimensional arrays should be represented in row-major order, unless the array has convention Fortran. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.6#Subclause_3.6.2">3.6.2</a>(11/3).<br /></li>
<MarginText>12/3</MarginText>
<li>Tags.Internal{"_"}Tag should return the tag of a type, if one exists, whose innermost master is a master of the point of the function call. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-3/AA-3.9">3.9</a>(26.1/3).<br /></li>
<MarginText>13/2</MarginText>
<li>A real static expression with a nonformal type that is not part of a larger static expression should be rounded the same as the target system. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.9">4.9</a>(38.1/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>13.1/5</MarginText>
<li>For each language-defined private type T, T'Image should generate an image that would be meaningful based only on the relevant public interfaces. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-4/AA-4.10">4.10</a>(56).<br /></li>
<MarginText>14/2</MarginText>
<li>The value of Duration'Small should be no greater than 100 microseconds. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6">9.6</a>(30).<br /></li>
<MarginText>15/2</MarginText>
<li>The time base for <code><a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#S0268">delay_relative_statement</a></code>s should be monotonic. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6">9.6</a>(31/5).<br /></li>
<MarginText>16/2</MarginText>
<li>Leap seconds should be supported if the target system supports them. Otherwise, operations in Calendar.Formatting should return results consistent with no leap seconds. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-9/AA-9.6#Subclause_9.6.1">9.6.1</a>(89/2).<br /></li>
<MarginText>17/5</MarginText>
<li><i>This paragraph was deleted.</i><br /></li>
<MarginText>18/2</MarginText>
<li>A type declared in a preelaborated package should have the same representation in every elaboration of a given version of the package. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-10/AA-10.2#Subclause_10.2.1">10.2.1</a>(12).<br /></li>
<MarginText>19/2</MarginText>
<li>Exception{"_"}Information should provide information useful for debugging, and should include the Exception{"_"}Name and Exception{"_"}Message. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4#Subclause_11.4.1">11.4.1</a>(19).<br /></li>
<MarginText>20/2</MarginText>
<li>Exception{"_"}Message by default should be short, provide information useful for debugging, and should not include the Exception{"_"}Name. See <a href="/docs/arm/AA-11/AA-11.4#Subclause_11.4.1">11.4.1</a>(19).<br /></li>

<MarginText>79.13/3</MarginText>
